13.2 Local Bergman kernels and ideal generators In this section $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, is a bounded pseudoconvex open set, $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and integrals are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure unless another measure is specified. For an integer $m\geq 1$ we put \[  H_ m=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| _ m^2 =\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad K_ m(z)=\sup _{\| F\| _ m\leq 1}|F(z)|^2.  \] Thus $H_ m$ is the space $\mathcal H_{mu}(\Omega )$ of theorem 12.2.7 , for the complex manifold $\Omega $ and the weight $mu$, and the function $K_ m$ is the Bergman kernel of $H_ m$ on the diagonal. We need that $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space of holomorphic functions that generates the multiplier ideal $\mathcal I(mu)$, with bounded coefficients near each point. These facts were proved in chapter 12 on bounded pseudoconvex open sets, also for measures $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ comparable with Lebesgue measure (theorem 12.2.7 , lemma 12.2.8 ), and the next lemma restates them in the notation of this section. Throughout this section, $\varrho $ denotes a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Such measures arise in section 13.3 , where the kernels are computed with the volume form of a Kähler form. Lemma 13.2.1 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, be a bounded pseudoconvex open set, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and let $\varrho $ be a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Put \[  \mathcal H=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| ^2=\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad \langle F,Gangle =\int _\Omega F ar G\, \mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV.  \] For every compact set $K\subset \Omega $ there is a constant $C_ K$ such that $|F(z)|\leq C_ K\| F\| $ for all $F\in \mathcal H$ and $z\in K$. The space $\mathcal H$ is a separable Hilbert space, and it has an orthonormal basis, that is, an orthonormal family $(e_\ell )$, finite or countable, whose linear span is dense. For every such family and every $F\in \mathcal H$, the partial sums of $\sum _\ell \langle F,e_\ell angle e_\ell $ converge to $F$ in norm and locally uniformly on $\Omega $, and $\sum _\ell |\langle F,e_\ell angle |^2=\| F\| ^2$. The germs of the elements of $\mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ at every point of $\Omega $, and near each point finitely many elements of $\mathcal H$ already generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$. Let $x\in \Omega $, and let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s\in \mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then there are a neighborhood $V$ of $x$ and a constant $C$ such that every $F\in \mathcal H$ can be written as $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ with $h_ i\in \mathcal O(V)$ and $\sup _ V|h_ i|\leq C\| F\| $. Proof. We regard $\Omega $ as a complex manifold, with the single chart given by the identity map. Then $\psi $ is a weight on $\Omega $ in the sense of section 12.2 , the set $\Omega $ satisfies the hypotheses of theorem 12.2.7 , and $\mathcal H$ is the space $\mathcal H_\psi (\Omega ,\varrho )$ of that theorem, with the same inner product. Hence (1) is contained in theorem 12.2.7 (1) and (2), and (2) follows from theorem 12.2.7 (3), because an initial segment of an enumerated orthonormal basis is a finite family of elements of $\mathcal H$. Finally, (3) is the first assertion of lemma 12.2.8 , applied to the weight $\psi $ on $\Omega $. $\square$ By lemma 13.2.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$ and $\varrho =1$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space on which evaluation at each point is a bounded linear functional; in particular $K_ m$ is finite. Let $(e_\ell )$ be an orthonormal basis of $H_ m$. Then 13.2  egin{equation} \label{eq:bergman-kernel-basis} K_ m=\sum _\ell |e_\ell |^2. \end{equation} Indeed, let $F$ lie in the unit ball of $H_ m$ and put $c_\ell =\langle F,e_\ell angle $. By lemma 13.2.1 (1), $F(z)=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell (z)$ and $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2=\| F\| _ m^2\leq 1$, so the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|F(z)|^2\leq \sum _\ell |e_\ell (z)|^2$. Conversely, for each $N$ the function $F_ N=\sum _{\ell \leq N}\overline{e_\ell (z)}e_\ell $ satisfies $F_ N(z)=\| F_ N\| _ m^2=\sum _{\ell \leq N}|e_\ell (z)|^2$; if this number is positive, then $F_ N/\| F_ N\| _ m$ lies in the unit ball, and $\sum _{\ell \leq N}|e_\ell (z)|^2=|F_ N(z)|^2/\| F_ N\| _ m^2\leq K_ m(z)$. The same argument applies to the kernel of the space defined with $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in place of Lebesgue measure, for an orthonormal basis of that space. Lemma 13.2.2 . The function $K_ m$ is real analytic on $\Omega $. Near each point of $\Omega $ it is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, where $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ are finitely many generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$ near that point. If $\pi \colon Y	o \Omega $ is a holomorphic map from a complex manifold $Y$ such that $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)=\mathcal O_ Y(-D)$ for an effective divisor $D$ on $Y$, for instance a log resolution of $\mathcal I(mu)$, then locally on $Y$ \[  K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m,\qquad b_ m	ext{ smooth and strictly positive},  \] where $s_ D$ is a local equation of $D$. The same conclusions hold if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$. Proof. We give the proof for the measure $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; Lebesgue measure is the case $\varrho =1$. By lemma 13.2.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space with an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$, evaluation is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Omega $, and ( 13.2 ) holds. We show that the map $z\mapsto (e_\ell (z))_\ell $ into $\ell ^2$ is given locally by a convergent power series with coefficients in $\ell ^2$. Fix a point $z_0$ and a polydisc $P$ of multiradius $ho $ about $z_0$ with $\overline P\subset \Omega $, and let $C$ be the evaluation bound on $\overline P$. For a finitely supported sequence $(c_\ell )$ with $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2\leq 1$, the function $F=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell $ has norm at most one, so $|F|\leq C$ on $P$, and the Cauchy estimates give $|\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !|\leq Cho ^{-\alpha }$. Since $\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !=\sum _\ell c_\ell A_{\alpha ,\ell }$ with $A_{\alpha ,\ell }=\partial ^\alpha e_\ell (z_0)/\alpha !$, taking the supremum over such sequences shows that the sequence $A_\alpha =(A_{\alpha ,\ell })_\ell $ has $\ell ^2$ norm $\| A_\alpha \| \leq Cho ^{-\alpha }$. Let $0<\lambda <1$, and let $P_\lambda $ be the concentric polydisc of multiradius $\lambda ho $. For $z\in P_\lambda $ we have $\sum _\alpha \| A_\alpha \| |(z-z_0)^\alpha |\leq C\sum _\alpha \lambda ^{|\alpha |}<\infty $, so the $\ell ^2$-valued series $\sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha $ converges absolutely, and its $\ell $th component is the Taylor series of $e_\ell $, which converges to $e_\ell (z)$. By ( 13.2 ), \[  K_ m(z)=\Bigl \| \sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha \Bigr \| ^2=\sum _{\alpha , eta }\langle A_\alpha ,A_ eta angle (z-z_0)^\alpha \overline{(z-z_0)^ eta },\qquad z\in P_\lambda ,  \] where $|\langle A_\alpha ,A_ eta angle |\leq C^2ho ^{-\alpha - eta }$. Hence this double power series, and each series obtained from it by differentiating term by term, converge uniformly on $P_{\lambda '}$ for every $\lambda '<\lambda $, since a derivative of order $k$ only introduces factors bounded by a polynomial of degree $k$ in $|\alpha |+| eta |$. Therefore $K_ m$ is real analytic, in particular smooth. Next choose members $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ of $H_ m$ generating $\mathcal I(mu)$ near a given point, by lemma 13.2.1 (2); by the remark following definition 13.1.5 , any other finite system of generators gives a comparable sum of squares. By the definition of $K_ m$, $|g_ i|^2\leq \| g_ i\| _ m^2K_ m$, so $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq  igl (\sum _ i\| g_ i\| _ m^2 igr )K_ m$. Conversely, lemma 13.2.1 (3) gives, on a fixed smaller neighborhood, a representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ with $|h_ i|\leq C'$ for every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|F|^2\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, and hence $K_ m\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ there. These constants may depend on $m$, $u$ and $\varrho $. Let $\pi $ and $D$ be as in the statement, let $y\in Y$, let $V$ be a neighborhood of $\pi (y)$ on which the bounded representation of the previous paragraph holds, and let $s_ D$ be a local equation of $D$ on a neighborhood $W\subset \pi ^{-1}(V)$ of $y$. Since $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $s_ D$ on $W$, we may write $g_ i\circ \pi =s_ Dk_ i$ and $s_ D=\sum _ il_ i\, (g_ i\circ \pi )$ with holomorphic $k_ i$ and $l_ i$, after shrinking $W$; since $s_ D$ does not vanish identically on any open set, $\sum _ il_ ik_ i=1$. For $F\in H_ m$, the representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ gives $F\circ \pi =s_ D\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )k_ i$ on $W$, so \[   rac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}=\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )\, k_ i,\qquad \Bigl | rac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}\Bigr |\leq C'\| F\| _ m\sum _ i|k_ i|.  \] Hence evaluation of $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ is bounded on each compact subset of $W$, uniformly for $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The power-series argument above therefore applies, in local coordinates on $Y$, to the holomorphic functions $(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and shows that $b_ m=\sum _\ell |(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D|^2$ is smooth; by ( 13.2 ), $K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m$. To see that $b_ m$ is strictly positive, let $F$ lie in the unit ball of $H_ m$, with coefficients $c_\ell =\langle F,e_\ell angle $ and partial sums $S_ N$. The estimate in the last display, applied to $F-S_ N$, shows that $(S_ N\circ \pi )/s_ D	o (F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ pointwise on $W$; hence $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D=\sum _\ell c_\ell (e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|(F\circ \pi )/s_ D|^2\leq b_ m$. Taking $F=g_ i/\| g_ i\| _ m$ for the indices with $g_ i
eq 0$, we obtain $b_ m\geq |k_ i|^2/\| g_ i\| _ m^2$, and the functions $k_ i$ have no common zero. $\square$ Theorem 13.2.3 . Let $\Omega $ have diameter at most $L$, and put $u_ m=m^{-1}\log K_ m$. Then $u_ m$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ and has analytic singularities of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(mu))$. There are constants $C_1,C_2>0$, depending only on $n$ and $L$, such that 13.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:local-bergman-bounds} u(z)- rac{\log C_1}{m}\leq u_ m(z) \leq \sup _{B(z,r)}u+ rac1m\log  rac{C_2}{r^{2n}} \end{equation} for all $z\in \Omega $ and $r>0$ with $B(z,r)\Subset \Omega $. As $m	o \infty $, $u_ m	o u$ pointwise and in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$. For every $z\in \Omega $, 13.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:local-bergman-lelong}

u (u,z). \end{equation} Finally, for each fixed $m$, the function $\exp (m(u_ m-u))$ is locally integrable on $\Omega $. All these assertions remain true if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$, provided $C_1$ and $C_2$ are replaced by $C_\varrho C_1$ and $C_2/c_\varrho $. Proof. Let $\Omega _0$ be a connected component of $\Omega $, and choose $a\in \Omega _0$ with $u(a)>-\infty $. By corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega $ to the weight $mu$, some element of $H_ m$ takes the value $1$ at $a$, so $H_ m$ contains a function that does not vanish identically on $\Omega _0$. For every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$ that is not identically zero on $\Omega _0$, $\log |F|^2$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega _0$ by proposition 8.3.3 , and $\log K_ m$ is the supremum of these functions on $\Omega _0$. Since $K_ m$ is continuous by lemma 13.2.2 , this family is locally uniformly bounded above, and $\log K_ m$ is upper semicontinuous with values in $[-\infty ,\infty )$, so it equals its upper semicontinuous regularization. Hence theorem 8.3.2 shows that $u_ m$ is plurisubharmonic. The comparison in lemma 13.2.2 gives $u_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ locally, with generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(mu)$; this is the asserted type. For the lower bound in ( 13.3 ), let $u(z)>-\infty $; at points of the pole set of $u$ there is nothing to prove. By corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega $ to the weight $mu$, there is $F\in H_ m$ with $F(z)=1$ and $\| F\| _ m^2\leq C_1\mathrm e^{-mu(z)}$, where $C_1$ depends only on $n$ and $L$. Hence $K_ m(z)\geq |F(z)|^2/\| F\| _ m^2\geq C_1^{-1}\mathrm e^{mu(z)}$. For the upper bound, let $\| F\| _ m\leq 1$. The mean-value inequality ( 12.9 ) of lemma 12.2.6 for $|F|^2$ on $B(z,r)$, where $|B(z,r)|=\pi ^ nr^{2n}/n!$, gives  egin{align*}  |F(z)|^2& \leq C_2r^{-2n}\int _{B(z,r)}|F|^2\ & \leq C_2r^{-2n}\exp \Bigl (m\sup _{B(z,r)}u\Bigr )\int _{B(z,r)}|F|^2\mathrm e^{-mu} \leq C_2r^{-2n}\exp \Bigl (m\sup _{B(z,r)}u\Bigr ), \end{align*} with $C_2=n!/\pi ^ n$, and taking the supremum over $F$ proves the upper bound. Now fix $z$ and $r$, and let $m	o \infty $ in ( 13.3 ): we obtain $u(z)\leq \varliminf _ mu_ m(z)\leq \varlimsup _ mu_ m(z)\leq \sup _{B(z,r)}u$. Letting $r\downarrow 0$ and using the upper semicontinuity of $u$ gives $u_ m(z)	o u(z)$, also at points of the pole set. On a compact set $K\subset \Omega $, a fixed $r<\operatorname {dist}(K,\partial \Omega )$ in the upper bound gives a uniform upper bound for all $u_ m$, while $u_ m\geq u-|\log C_1|$. Since $u\in L^1(K)$, dominated convergence gives $u_ m	o u$ in $L^1(K)$. For the Lelong numbers, let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$ near $z$. The stalk $\mathcal I(mu)_ z$ is not zero: by the first paragraph, applied to the component of $\Omega $ containing $z$, it contains the germ of an element of $H_ m$ that does not vanish identically on that component, and this germ is not zero by the identity theorem. Since $u_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ near $z$, lemma 13.1.6 gives $
u (u_ m,z)=m^{-1}\operatorname {ord}_ z\mathcal I(mu)$, and ( 13.4 ) follows from lemma 12.3.1 . Finally, near each point $K_ m\leq C\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ with $g_ i\in H_ m$, by lemma 13.2.2 , and each $|g_ i|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is integrable on $\Omega $. Hence $\exp (m(u_ m-u))=K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. Now replace Lebesgue measure by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$, and let $K^\varrho _ m$ be the corresponding kernel. The space of holomorphic functions is the same, and the two norms satisfy $c_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2\leq \| F\| _{m,\varrho }^2\leq C_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2$. If $\| F\| _ m\leq 1$, then $F/C_\varrho ^{1/2}$ lies in the unit ball for $\varrho $, and if $\| F\| _{m,\varrho }\leq 1$, then $c_\varrho ^{1/2}F$ lies in the unit ball for Lebesgue measure; hence \[  C_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\leq K^\varrho _ m\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m.  \] The proof of plurisubharmonicity applies verbatim to $m^{-1}\log K^\varrho _ m$, with the unit ball taken for $\varrho $ and the continuity of $K^\varrho _ m$ given by lemma 13.2.2 . The lower and upper bounds follow from the last display, with the constants $C_\varrho C_1$ and $C_2/c_\varrho $. The convergence and the Lelong numbers then follow as before, since lemma 13.2.2 applies to $K^\varrho _ m$. Finally, $K^\varrho _ m\mathrm e^{-mu}\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. $\square$ The kernels at the scales $m$ and $2m$ are compared by extending a function from the diagonal of $\Omega 	imes \Omega $. Lemma 13.2.4 . Suppose that the spaces $H_ m$ are defined with respect to $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; for instance $\varrho =1$. There is a constant $C_\Omega >0$, depending only on $n$, on a bound $L$ for the diameter of $\Omega $ and on $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $, and in particular independent of $m$ and $u$, such that \[  K_{2m}\leq C_\Omega K_ m^2\qquad 	ext{on }\Omega .  \] Proof. We write $\| \cdot \| _ m$ for the norm of $H_ m$. By the definition of $K_ m$, every $h\in H_ m$ satisfies $|h(\zeta )|^2\leq \| h\| _ m^2K_ m(\zeta )$ for all $\zeta \in \Omega $; if $\| h\| _ m=0$, then $h$ vanishes almost everywhere, hence identically. Let $F\in H_{2m}$. We first extend $F$ from the diagonal to $\Omega 	imes \Omega $. By corollary 11.2.5 , $\Omega 	imes \Omega $ is a bounded pseudoconvex open set in $\mathbb C^{2n}$, of diameter at most $\sqrt2L$, and the function $p(z,w)=mu(z)+mu(w)$ is plurisubharmonic on it (proposition 8.2.3 , proposition 8.2.5 ). The diagonal $\Lambda =\{ (z,w)\in \mathbb C^{2n}:z=w\} $ is a complex linear subspace of codimension $n$, and the map $z\mapsto (z,z)$ multiplies Euclidean lengths by $\sqrt2$, so Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda $ corresponds to $2^ n$ times Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb C^ n$. On $\Lambda \cap (\Omega 	imes \Omega )$, identified with $\Omega $, the weight $p$ restricts to $2mu$, so \[  \int _{\Lambda \cap (\Omega 	imes \Omega )}|F|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}=2^ n\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-2mu}\, \mathrm dV\leq 2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2.  \] The extension statement of corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega 	imes \Omega $ to the weight $p$ and the subspace $\Lambda $, gives $G\in \mathcal O(\Omega 	imes \Omega )$ with $G(z,z)=F(z)$ and $\int _{\Omega 	imes \Omega }|G|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{4n}\leq C^ n(\sqrt2L)^{2n}2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2$, where $C$ is the constant of theorem 11.4.4 . Hence \[  \| G\| ^2=\int _{\Omega 	imes \Omega }|G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)-mu(w)}\varrho (z)\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(z)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2  \] with $C_\Omega =4^ nC^ nL^{2n}C_\varrho ^2/c_\varrho $. We now bound $G$ on the diagonal by $K_ m$. For $w\in \Omega $ put \[  N(w)=\int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)}\varrho (z)\, \mathrm dV(z)\in [0,\infty ].  \] By Tonelli's theorem, $N$ is measurable and $\int _\Omega N(w)\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)=\| G\| ^2<\infty $; since $\mathrm e^{-mu}\varrho >0$ almost everywhere, $N(w)<\infty $ for almost every $w$. For such $w$, the function $G(\cdot ,w)$ belongs to $H_ m$ with $\| G(\cdot ,w)\| _ m^2=N(w)$, so $|G(z,w)|^2\leq N(w)K_ m(z)$ for every $z$. Fix $z\in \Omega $. Integrating this inequality in $w$, we obtain \[  \int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2,  \] so $G(z,\cdot )\in H_ m$ with $\| G(z,\cdot )\| _ m^2\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2$, and therefore $|G(z,w)|^2\leq K_ m(z)K_ m(w)\| G\| ^2$ for every $w$. Taking $w=z$, \[  |F(z)|^2=|G(z,z)|^2\leq K_ m(z)^2\| G\| ^2\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2K_ m(z)^2.  \] Taking the supremum over the unit ball of $H_{2m}$ proves the lemma. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.2.1
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.2.1 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, be a bounded pseudoconvex open set, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and let $\varrho $ be a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Put \[  \mathcal H=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| ^2=\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad \langle F,G\rangle =\int _\Omega F\bar G\, \mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV.  \] For every compact set $K\subset \Omega $ there is a constant $C_ K$ such that $|F(z)|\leq C_ K\| F\| $ for all $F\in \mathcal H$ and $z\in K$. The space $\mathcal H$ is a separable Hilbert space, and it has an orthonormal basis, that is, an orthonormal family $(e_\ell )$, finite or countable, whose linear span is dense. For every such family and every $F\in \mathcal H$, the partial sums of $\sum _\ell \langle F,e_\ell \rangle e_\ell $ converge to $F$ in norm and locally uniformly on $\Omega $, and $\sum _\ell |\langle F,e_\ell \rangle |^2=\| F\| ^2$. The germs of the elements of $\mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ at every point of $\Omega $, and near each point finitely many elements of $\mathcal H$ already generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$. Let $x\in \Omega $, and let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s\in \mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then there are a neighborhood $V$ of $x$ and a constant $C$ such that every $F\in \mathcal H$ can be written as $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ with $h_ i\in \mathcal O(V)$ and $\sup _ V|h_ i|\leq C\| F\| $. Proof. We regard $\Omega $ as a complex manifold, with the single chart given by the identity map. Then $\psi $ is a weight on $\Omega $ in the sense of section 12.2 , the set $\Omega $ satisfies the hypotheses of theorem 12.2.7 , and $\mathcal H$ is the space $\mathcal H_\psi (\Omega ,\varrho )$ of that theorem, with the same inner product. Hence (1) is contained in theorem 12.2.7 (1) and (2), and (2) follows from theorem 12.2.7 (3), because an initial segment of an enumerated orthonormal basis is a finite family of elements of $\mathcal H$. Finally, (3) is the first assertion of lemma 12.2.8 , applied to the weight $\psi $ on $\Omega $. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.2.2
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.2.2 . The function $K_ m$ is real analytic on $\Omega $. Near each point of $\Omega $ it is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, where $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ are finitely many generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$ near that point. If $\pi \colon Y\to \Omega $ is a holomorphic map from a complex manifold $Y$ such that $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)=\mathcal O_ Y(-D)$ for an effective divisor $D$ on $Y$, for instance a log resolution of $\mathcal I(mu)$, then locally on $Y$ \[  K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m,\qquad b_ m\text{ smooth and strictly positive},  \] where $s_ D$ is a local equation of $D$. The same conclusions hold if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$. Proof. We give the proof for the measure $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; Lebesgue measure is the case $\varrho =1$. By lemma 13.2.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space with an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$, evaluation is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Omega $, and ( 13.2 ) holds. We show that the map $z\mapsto (e_\ell (z))_\ell $ into $\ell ^2$ is given locally by a convergent power series with coefficients in $\ell ^2$. Fix a point $z_0$ and a polydisc $P$ of multiradius $\rho $ about $z_0$ with $\overline P\subset \Omega $, and let $C$ be the evaluation bound on $\overline P$. For a finitely supported sequence $(c_\ell )$ with $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2\leq 1$, the function $F=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell $ has norm at most one, so $|F|\leq C$ on $P$, and the Cauchy estimates give $|\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !|\leq C\rho ^{-\alpha }$. Since $\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !=\sum _\ell c_\ell A_{\alpha ,\ell }$ with $A_{\alpha ,\ell }=\partial ^\alpha e_\ell (z_0)/\alpha !$, taking the supremum over such sequences shows that the sequence $A_\alpha =(A_{\alpha ,\ell })_\ell $ has $\ell ^2$ norm $\| A_\alpha \| \leq C\rho ^{-\alpha }$. Let $0<\lambda <1$, and let $P_\lambda $ be the concentric polydisc of multiradius $\lambda \rho $. For $z\in P_\lambda $ we have $\sum _\alpha \| A_\alpha \| |(z-z_0)^\alpha |\leq C\sum _\alpha \lambda ^{|\alpha |}<\infty $, so the $\ell ^2$-valued series $\sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha $ converges absolutely, and its $\ell $th component is the Taylor series of $e_\ell $, which converges to $e_\ell (z)$. By ( 13.2 ), \[  K_ m(z)=\Bigl \| \sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha \Bigr \| ^2=\sum _{\alpha ,\beta }\langle A_\alpha ,A_\beta \rangle (z-z_0)^\alpha \overline{(z-z_0)^\beta },\qquad z\in P_\lambda ,  \] where $|\langle A_\alpha ,A_\beta \rangle |\leq C^2\rho ^{-\alpha -\beta }$. Hence this double power series, and each series obtained from it by differentiating term by term, converge uniformly on $P_{\lambda '}$ for every $\lambda '<\lambda $, since a derivative of order $k$ only introduces factors bounded by a polynomial of degree $k$ in $|\alpha |+|\beta |$. Therefore $K_ m$ is real analytic, in particular smooth. Next choose members $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ of $H_ m$ generating $\mathcal I(mu)$ near a given point, by lemma 13.2.1 (2); by the remark following definition 13.1.5 , any other finite system of generators gives a comparable sum of squares. By the definition of $K_ m$, $|g_ i|^2\leq \| g_ i\| _ m^2K_ m$, so $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq \bigl (\sum _ i\| g_ i\| _ m^2\bigr )K_ m$. Conversely, lemma 13.2.1 (3) gives, on a fixed smaller neighborhood, a representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ with $|h_ i|\leq C'$ for every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|F|^2\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, and hence $K_ m\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ there. These constants may depend on $m$, $u$ and $\varrho $. Let $\pi $ and $D$ be as in the statement, let $y\in Y$, let $V$ be a neighborhood of $\pi (y)$ on which the bounded representation of the previous paragraph holds, and let $s_ D$ be a local equation of $D$ on a neighborhood $W\subset \pi ^{-1}(V)$ of $y$. Since $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $s_ D$ on $W$, we may write $g_ i\circ \pi =s_ Dk_ i$ and $s_ D=\sum _ il_ i\, (g_ i\circ \pi )$ with holomorphic $k_ i$ and $l_ i$, after shrinking $W$; since $s_ D$ does not vanish identically on any open set, $\sum _ il_ ik_ i=1$. For $F\in H_ m$, the representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ gives $F\circ \pi =s_ D\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )k_ i$ on $W$, so \[  \frac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}=\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )\, k_ i,\qquad \Bigl |\frac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}\Bigr |\leq C'\| F\| _ m\sum _ i|k_ i|.  \] Hence evaluation of $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ is bounded on each compact subset of $W$, uniformly for $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The power-series argument above therefore applies, in local coordinates on $Y$, to the holomorphic functions $(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and shows that $b_ m=\sum _\ell |(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D|^2$ is smooth; by ( 13.2 ), $K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m$. To see that $b_ m$ is strictly positive, let $F$ lie in the unit ball of $H_ m$, with coefficients $c_\ell =\langle F,e_\ell \rangle $ and partial sums $S_ N$. The estimate in the last display, applied to $F-S_ N$, shows that $(S_ N\circ \pi )/s_ D\to (F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ pointwise on $W$; hence $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D=\sum _\ell c_\ell (e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|(F\circ \pi )/s_ D|^2\leq b_ m$. Taking $F=g_ i/\| g_ i\| _ m$ for the indices with $g_ i\neq 0$, we obtain $b_ m\geq |k_ i|^2/\| g_ i\| _ m^2$, and the functions $k_ i$ have no common zero. $\square$

Theorem 13.2.3 . Let $\Omega $ have diameter at most $L$, and put $u_ m=m^{-1}\log K_ m$. Then $u_ m$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ and has analytic singularities of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(mu))$. There are constants $C_1,C_2>0$, depending only on $n$ and $L$, such that 13.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:local-bergman-bounds} u(z)- rac{\log C_1}{m}\leq u_ m(z) \leq \sup _{B(z,r)}u+ rac1m\log  rac{C_2}{r^{2n}} \end{equation} for all $z\in \Omega $ and $r>0$ with $B(z,r)\Subset \Omega $. As $m	o \infty $, $u_ m	o u$ pointwise and in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$. For every $z\in \Omega $, 13.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:local-bergman-lelong}

All these assertions remain true if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$, provided $C_1$ and $C_2$ are replaced by $C_\varrho C_1$ and $C_2/c_\varrho $. Proof. Let $\Omega _0$ be a connected component of $\Omega $, and choose $a\in \Omega _0$ with $u(a)>-\infty $. By corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega $ to the weight $mu$, some element of $H_ m$ takes the value $1$ at $a$, so $H_ m$ contains a function that does not vanish identically on $\Omega _0$. For every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$ that is not identically zero on $\Omega _0$, $\log |F|^2$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega _0$ by proposition 8.3.3 , and $\log K_ m$ is the supremum of these functions on $\Omega _0$. Since $K_ m$ is continuous by lemma 13.2.2 , this family is locally uniformly bounded above, and $\log K_ m$ is upper semicontinuous with values in $[-\infty ,\infty )$, so it equals its upper semicontinuous regularization. Hence theorem 8.3.2 shows that $u_ m$ is plurisubharmonic. The comparison in lemma 13.2.2 gives $u_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ locally, with generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(mu)$; this is the asserted type. For the lower bound in ( 13.3 ), let $u(z)>-\infty $; at points of the pole set of $u$ there is nothing to prove. By corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega $ to the weight $mu$, there is $F\in H_ m$ with $F(z)=1$ and $\| F\| _ m^2\leq C_1\mathrm e^{-mu(z)}$, where $C_1$ depends only on $n$ and $L$. Hence $K_ m(z)\geq |F(z)|^2/\| F\| _ m^2\geq C_1^{-1}\mathrm e^{mu(z)}$. For the upper bound, let $\| F\| _ m\leq 1$. The mean-value inequality ( 12.9 ) of lemma 12.2.6 for $|F|^2$ on $B(z,r)$, where $|B(z,r)|=\pi ^ nr^{2n}/n!$, gives  egin{align*}  |F(z)|^2& \leq C_2r^{-2n}\int _{B(z,r)}|F|^2\ & \leq C_2r^{-2n}\exp \Bigl (m\sup _{B(z,r)}u\Bigr )\int _{B(z,r)}|F|^2\mathrm e^{-mu} \leq C_2r^{-2n}\exp \Bigl (m\sup _{B(z,r)}u\Bigr ), \end{align*} with $C_2=n!/\pi ^ n$, and taking the supremum over $F$ proves the upper bound. Now fix $z$ and $r$, and let $m	o \infty $ in ( 13.3 ): we obtain $u(z)\leq \varliminf _ mu_ m(z)\leq \varlimsup _ mu_ m(z)\leq \sup _{B(z,r)}u$. Letting $r\downarrow 0$ and using the upper semicontinuity of $u$ gives $u_ m(z)	o u(z)$, also at points of the pole set. On a compact set $K\subset \Omega $, a fixed $r<\operatorname {dist}(K,\partial \Omega )$ in the upper bound gives a uniform upper bound for all $u_ m$, while $u_ m\geq u-|\log C_1|$. Since $u\in L^1(K)$, dominated convergence gives $u_ m	o u$ in $L^1(K)$. For the Lelong numbers, let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$ near $z$. The stalk $\mathcal I(mu)_ z$ is not zero: by the first paragraph, applied to the component of $\Omega $ containing $z$, it contains the germ of an element of $H_ m$ that does not vanish identically on that component, and this germ is not zero by the identity theorem. Since $u_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ near $z$, lemma 13.1.6 gives $
u (u_ m,z)=m^{-1}\operatorname {ord}_ z\mathcal I(mu)$, and ( 13.4 ) follows from lemma 12.3.1 . Finally, near each point $K_ m\leq C\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ with $g_ i\in H_ m$, by lemma 13.2.2 , and each $|g_ i|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is integrable on $\Omega $. Hence $\exp (m(u_ m-u))=K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. Now replace Lebesgue measure by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$, and let $K^\varrho _ m$ be the corresponding kernel. The space of holomorphic functions is the same, and the two norms satisfy $c_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2\leq \| F\| _{m,\varrho }^2\leq C_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2$. If $\| F\| _ m\leq 1$, then $F/C_\varrho ^{1/2}$ lies in the unit ball for $\varrho $, and if $\| F\| _{m,\varrho }\leq 1$, then $c_\varrho ^{1/2}F$ lies in the unit ball for Lebesgue measure; hence \[  C_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\leq K^\varrho _ m\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m.  \] The proof of plurisubharmonicity applies verbatim to $m^{-1}\log K^\varrho _ m$, with the unit ball taken for $\varrho $ and the continuity of $K^\varrho _ m$ given by lemma 13.2.2 . The lower and upper bounds follow from the last display, with the constants $C_\varrho C_1$ and $C_2/c_\varrho $. The convergence and the Lelong numbers then follow as before, since lemma 13.2.2 applies to $K^\varrho _ m$. Finally, $K^\varrho _ m\mathrm e^{-mu}\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.2.4
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.2.4 . Suppose that the spaces $H_ m$ are defined with respect to $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; for instance $\varrho =1$. There is a constant $C_\Omega >0$, depending only on $n$, on a bound $L$ for the diameter of $\Omega $ and on $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $, and in particular independent of $m$ and $u$, such that \[  K_{2m}\leq C_\Omega K_ m^2\qquad \text{on }\Omega .  \] Proof. We write $\| \cdot \| _ m$ for the norm of $H_ m$. By the definition of $K_ m$, every $h\in H_ m$ satisfies $|h(\zeta )|^2\leq \| h\| _ m^2K_ m(\zeta )$ for all $\zeta \in \Omega $; if $\| h\| _ m=0$, then $h$ vanishes almost everywhere, hence identically. Let $F\in H_{2m}$. We first extend $F$ from the diagonal to $\Omega \times \Omega $. By corollary 11.2.5 , $\Omega \times \Omega $ is a bounded pseudoconvex open set in $\mathbb C^{2n}$, of diameter at most $\sqrt2L$, and the function $p(z,w)=mu(z)+mu(w)$ is plurisubharmonic on it (proposition 8.2.3 , proposition 8.2.5 ). The diagonal $\Lambda =\{ (z,w)\in \mathbb C^{2n}:z=w\} $ is a complex linear subspace of codimension $n$, and the map $z\mapsto (z,z)$ multiplies Euclidean lengths by $\sqrt2$, so Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda $ corresponds to $2^ n$ times Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb C^ n$. On $\Lambda \cap (\Omega \times \Omega )$, identified with $\Omega $, the weight $p$ restricts to $2mu$, so \[  \int _{\Lambda \cap (\Omega \times \Omega )}|F|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}=2^ n\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-2mu}\, \mathrm dV\leq 2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2.  \] The extension statement of corollary 11.4.5 , applied on $\Omega \times \Omega $ to the weight $p$ and the subspace $\Lambda $, gives $G\in \mathcal O(\Omega \times \Omega )$ with $G(z,z)=F(z)$ and $\int _{\Omega \times \Omega }|G|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{4n}\leq C^ n(\sqrt2L)^{2n}2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2$, where $C$ is the constant of theorem 11.4.4 . Hence \[  \| G\| ^2=\int _{\Omega \times \Omega }|G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)-mu(w)}\varrho (z)\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(z)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2  \] with $C_\Omega =4^ nC^ nL^{2n}C_\varrho ^2/c_\varrho $. We now bound $G$ on the diagonal by $K_ m$. For $w\in \Omega $ put \[  N(w)=\int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)}\varrho (z)\, \mathrm dV(z)\in [0,\infty ].  \] By Tonelli's theorem, $N$ is measurable and $\int _\Omega N(w)\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)=\| G\| ^2<\infty $; since $\mathrm e^{-mu}\varrho >0$ almost everywhere, $N(w)<\infty $ for almost every $w$. For such $w$, the function $G(\cdot ,w)$ belongs to $H_ m$ with $\| G(\cdot ,w)\| _ m^2=N(w)$, so $|G(z,w)|^2\leq N(w)K_ m(z)$ for every $z$. Fix $z\in \Omega $. Integrating this inequality in $w$, we obtain \[  \int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2,  \] so $G(z,\cdot )\in H_ m$ with $\| G(z,\cdot )\| _ m^2\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2$, and therefore $|G(z,w)|^2\leq K_ m(z)K_ m(w)\| G\| ^2$ for every $w$. Taking $w=z$, \[  |F(z)|^2=|G(z,z)|^2\leq K_ m(z)^2\| G\| ^2\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2K_ m(z)^2.  \] Taking the supremum over the unit ball of $H_{2m}$ proves the lemma. $\square$

title: 13.3 Overlap interpolation and quantitative patching
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization

title: Lemma 13.3.1
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.3.1 . Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $a\geq 0$, and let $v_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(B_ j,\theta )$ for $j=1,\ldots ,J$ satisfy $v_ j\leq v_ l+a$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ for all $j,l$. Then the function \[  v(x)=\max _{j:\, x\in \overline{U'_ j}}\bigl (v_ j(x)+a\chi _ j(x)\bigr )  \] is quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$ and satisfies $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq -aC_\chi \omega $ and $v_ j\leq v\leq v_ j+2a$ on $U_ j$. Proof. Since the $U_ i$ cover $X$, the maximum is taken over a nonempty set at every point. Fix $x_0\in X$ and choose $i$ with $x_0\in U_ i$. Indices $j$ with $x_0\notin \overline{U'_ j}$ do not occur near $x_0$. If $x_0\in \partial U'_ j$, then $\chi _ j=0$ near $x_0$, because $\chi _ j$ has compact support in $U'_ j$; so near $x_0$ the $j$th term, where it is defined, equals $v_ j\leq v_ i+a=v_ i+a\chi _ i$, since $\chi _ i=1$ on the neighborhood $U_ i$ of $x_0$. Such a term never exceeds the $i$th term and can be omitted. Hence on a small neighborhood of $x_0$, $v$ is the maximum of $v_ j+a\chi _ j$ over the fixed set of indices $j$ with $x_0\in U'_ j$. Each of these functions satisfies $\theta +aC_\chi \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ j+a\chi _ j)\geq 0$. Adding a local potential of the closed form $\theta +aC_\chi \omega $ on a coordinate ball about $x_0$ (lemma 13.1.2 ), which makes these functions plurisubharmonic by lemma 13.1.4 (2), and applying proposition 8.2.5 , we obtain that $v$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic near $x_0$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq -aC_\chi \omega $. On $U_ j$ the $j$th term is $v_ j+a\geq v_ j$, and every term with index $l$ is at most $v_ l+a\leq v_ j+2a$. This proves the two bounds, also at points of the pole sets. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.3.2
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.3.2 . There is a constant $C_ B\geq 0$, depending only on the fixed geometry and in particular independent of $\theta $, $\varphi $ and $m$, such that \[  a_{j,m}\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}a_{l,m}\qquad \text{on }\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}  \] for all $j,l$. In particular $a_{j,m}$ and $a_{l,m}$ have the same zeros on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, and $|v_{j,m}-v_{l,m}|\leq C_ B/m$ there outside these common zeros. Proof. Fix $j,l$ with $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}\neq \varnothing $, and work in the coordinates of the ball $\mathcal B_{jl}$. By lemma 13.1.2 choose a smooth function $g$ on $\mathcal B_{jl}$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=\theta $. The functions $h_ j-g$ and $h_ l-g$ are pluriharmonic on the coordinate balls $B_ j^+$ and $B_ l^+$, so by the same lemma $h_ j-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ and $h_ l-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ l$ with $b_ j,b_ l$ holomorphic on these balls (the constants are absorbed into $b_ j,b_ l$). Put $u=\varphi +g$, a plurisubharmonic function on $\mathcal B_{jl}$. Since $|\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}|^2=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}$, multiplication by $\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}$ is an isometry from the weighted space defining $K_{j,m}$ onto the space of holomorphic functions on $B_ j$ with weight $mu$ and volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$. If $K^{mu}_{B_ j}$ denotes the Bergman kernel of the latter space, then $K^{mu}_{B_ j}=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}K_{j,m}$, and therefore \[  a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}K^{mu}_{B_ j},\qquad a_{l,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}K^{mu}_{B_ l}.  \] Hence it suffices to prove $K^{mu}_{B_ j}\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ with $C_0\geq 1$ depending only on the fixed geometry. Choose a smooth function $\rho \colon X\to [0,1]$ with compact support in $B_ j\cap B_ l$, equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact set $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ (proposition 7.1.3 ); this choice belongs to the fixed geometry. Let $r>0$ be the distance, in the coordinates of $\mathcal B_{jl}$, from $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ to the support of $\bar\partial \rho $, and let $c>0$ and $C''$ be lower and upper bounds for the density of $\omega ^ n/n!$ with respect to Lebesgue measure on $B_ j\cup B_ l$ in these coordinates. The ball $B_ l$ is pseudoconvex also in the coordinates of $\mathcal B_{jl}$, since a biholomorphism transports a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function (proposition 8.2.3 ). To compare the kernels at a point $x\in \overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, we correct $\rho f$, for $f$ holomorphic on $B_ j$, to a holomorphic function on $B_ l$ with the same value at $x$. Let $f$ be holomorphic on $B_ j$ with norm at most one in the weighted space, and extend $\rho f$ by zero to a smooth function on $B_ l$. We apply theorem 11.3.4 on $B_ l$ to the smooth $\bar\partial $-closed form $f\bar\partial \rho $, with the plurisubharmonic function $p=mu+n\log |z-x|^2$ and the smooth function $q=|z|^2$, whose complex Hessian matrix is the identity. On the support of $\bar\partial \rho $ we have $|z-x|^{-2n}\leq r^{-2n}$, so \[  \int _{B_ l}|f\bar\partial \rho |^2\mathrm e^{-p-q}\, \mathrm dV\leq r^{-2n}\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2\int _{B_ j}|f|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}\, \mathrm dV\leq \frac{\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2}{cr^{2n}}.  \] Hence there is a solution of $\bar\partial w=f\bar\partial \rho $ on $B_ l$ with \[  \int _{B_ l}|w|^2|z-x|^{-2n}\mathrm e^{-mu-|z|^2}\, \mathrm dV\leq C=\frac{\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2}{cr^{2n}},  \] and $C$ depends only on the fixed geometry. The function $|z-x|^{2n}\mathrm e^{|z|^2}$ is bounded on the bounded set $B_ l$ by a constant of the same kind, and the density of $\omega ^ n/n!$ is at most $C''$. Hence the squared weighted norm of $w$, for the weight $mu$ and the volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$, is at most a constant $C'$ depending only on the fixed geometry. Near $x$ we have $\bar\partial w=f\bar\partial \rho =0$, because $\rho =1$ there; hence $\Delta w=0$ near $x$, and by theorem 2.1.4 $w$ is smooth, hence holomorphic, near $x$. Suppose that $w(x)\neq 0$. Then $|w|^2\geq |w(x)|^2/4$ on a ball $B(x,\delta )$ on which $u\leq M$ for some constant $M$, since $u$ is upper semicontinuous, and the last integral is at least \[  \frac{|w(x)|^2}4\, \mathrm e^{-mM-\sup _{B_ l}|z|^2}\int _{B(x,\delta )}|z-x|^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV=\infty ,  \] because $\int _{B(x,\delta )}|z-x|^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV=s_{2n-1}\int _0^\delta t^{-1}\, \mathrm dt$ in polar coordinates ( 2.1 ). Hence $w(x)=0$. The function $F=\rho f-w$ satisfies $\bar\partial F=0$ on $B_ l$, so it is holomorphic by theorem 2.1.4 , and $F(x)=f(x)$. Since $0\leq \rho \leq 1$ and $\rho $ vanishes outside $B_ j$, the weighted norm of $F$ on $B_ l$ is at most $1+C'^{1/2}=C_0$. By the definition of the kernel, $|f(x)|^2=|F(x)|^2\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}(x)$, and taking the supremum over $f$ gives $K^{mu}_{B_ j}(x)\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}(x)$. No bound on $u$, $\theta $ or $m$ enters these constants. Taking $C_ B$ to be the maximum of $2\log C_0$ over the finitely many pairs $(j,l)$, with the roles of $j$ and $l$ also exchanged, proves the lemma. $\square$

title: Theorem 13.3.3
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Theorem 13.3.3 . There is a constant $c>0$, depending only on $(X,\omega )$ through the fixed geometry, with the following property. Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $m\geq 1$ be an integer. Then there is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi _ m$ on $X$ such that \[  \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ m\geq -\frac cm\omega , \qquad \varphi _ m\geq \frac1m\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)\quad \text{locally},  \] where the $g_ i$ are local generators of $\mathcal I(m\varphi )$. The bounded term may depend on $m$, $\theta $, $\varphi $ and the point. Proof. By lemma 13.3.2 , the functions $v_{j,m}\in \mathrm{PSH}(B_ j,\theta )$ satisfy $v_{j,m}\leq v_{l,m}+C_ B/m$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, also at their common zeros. Hence lemma 13.3.1 with $a=C_ B/m$ gives a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi _ m$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ m\geq -(C_ BC_\chi /m)\omega $, so the first conclusion holds with $c=C_ BC_\chi $, increased if necessary to make it positive. On $U_ j$ the function $\varphi _ m$ dominates $v_{j,m}=m^{-1}\log K_{j,m}-h_ j$. Since $h_ j$ is smooth, $\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ j))=\mathcal I(m\varphi )$, and the comparison of lemma 13.2.2 gives $v_{j,m}\geq m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ near each point of $U_ j$. This proves the second conclusion. $\square$

13.4 Smooth cutoff sums and decreasing approximation The maximum in theorem 13.3.3 destroys smoothness, and that theorem does not compare the functions $\varphi _ m$ for different values of $m$. To obtain the regularity required of gentle singularities and, later, a decreasing sequence, we glue the local kernels instead by a sum with smooth cutoffs and control the curvature of its logarithm by a direct computation. We keep the notation of the previous section. Lemma 13.4.1 . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, let $m\geq 1$ be an integer, and put \[  R_ m=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2a_{j,m},\qquad G_ m=m^{-1}\log R_ m,  \] each summand being extended by zero outside the support of $\chi _ j$. There is a constant $c'>0$, depending only on the fixed geometry, such that $	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}G_ m\geq -(c'/m)\omega $. Moreover $R_ m$ is smooth on $X$, and $G_ m$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(m\varphi ))$. Proof. Step 1: proof of (2). Let $w_ j$, $\chi _ j$, $S$ and $\alpha _ j$ be as in (2), and put $f_ j=\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$, so that $S=\sum _ jf_ j$. Then $\partial f_ j=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}(\chi _ j\partial w_ j+2\partial \chi _ j)=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j$, so that $\partial S=\sum _ j\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j$. Since $\chi _ j$ and $w_ j$ are real, $ ar\partial f_ j=\overline{\partial f_ j}=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j} ar\alpha _ j$ with $ ar\alpha _ j=\chi _ j ar\partial w_ j+2 ar\partial \chi _ j$, and \[   egin{aligned}  \partial  ar\partial f_ j& =\partial (\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j})\wedge  ar\alpha _ j+\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\, \partial  ar\alpha _ j\ & =\mathrm e^{w_ j} igl ((\partial \chi _ j+\chi _ j\partial w_ j)\wedge (\chi _ j ar\partial w_ j+2 ar\partial \chi _ j)\ & \qquad +\chi _ j\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+\chi _ j^2\partial  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial  ar\partial \chi _ j igr )\ & =\mathrm e^{w_ j} igl (\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j+\chi _ j^2\partial  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial  ar\partial \chi _ j-2\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j igr ), \end{aligned}  \] where the last line follows by expanding $\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j=\chi _ j^2\partial w_ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial w_ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j+2\chi _ j\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+4\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j$. Next, $\partial  ar\partial \log S=\partial  ar\partial S/S-\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S/S^2$, and since $\sum _ l\chi _ l^2\mathrm e^{w_ l}=S$, \[  \sum _ j rac{\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j}S- rac{\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S}{S^2} = rac1{S^2}\sum _{j,l}\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l} igl (\chi _ l^2\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j-\chi _ j\chi _ l\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ l igr ).  \] In the last sum the terms with $j=l$ vanish, and for $j<l$ the terms with indices $(j,l)$ and $(l,j)$ add up to $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)\wedge \overline{(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)}$. Multiplying by $\mathrm i/2\pi $ and using $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}= rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial  ar\partial $, we obtain ( 13.5 ). The first term on the right of ( 13.5 ) is semipositive, because the coefficients $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}/(2\pi S^2)$ are positive and, for a $(1,0)$-form $\gamma =\sum _ k\gamma _ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$, the coefficient matrix $(\gamma _ k ar\gamma _{k'})$ of $\mathrm i\gamma \wedge  ar\gamma $ is positive semidefinite. We now prove (1) in three steps. Step 2: a curvature estimate. By lemma 13.1.1 , applied on the compact manifold $X$ to the finitely many smooth forms below, there is a constant $A>0$, depending only on the fixed geometry, such that $\chi _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j- rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j\geq -A\omega $ for every $j$. Let $W\subset X$ be open, and for the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ let $w_ j$ be smooth real functions on $W$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j\geq -m	heta \quad 	ext{on }W,\qquad \mathrm e^{w_ j}\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}\mathrm e^{w_ i}\quad 	ext{on }W\cap U_ i\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j  \] for all such $i,j$. We claim that $S=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$ is positive on $W$ and that \[  	heta + rac1m\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log S\geq - rac{2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}}m\omega \qquad 	ext{on }W.  \] Let $x\in W$ and choose $i$ with $x\in U_ i$. Then $\chi _ i(x)=1$, so $S(x)\geq \mathrm e^{w_ i(x)}>0$, and $\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}$ at $x$ for every $j$ with $\chi _ j(x)
eq 0$. Since $S>0$ on $W$, the identity ( 13.5 ) of (2) holds on $W$. If $\chi _ j(x)=0$, the $j$th summand of the last term in ( 13.5 ) vanishes at $x$, because the nonnegative function $\chi _ j$ attains its minimum at $x$, so that $\partial \chi _ j(x)=0$. Hence the last term is at least $-2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}\omega $ at $x$. The coefficients $\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S$ are nonnegative with sum one, so the middle term is at least $-m	heta $, and the first term is semipositive. This proves the claim. Step 3: $G_ m$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and satisfies the curvature bound. Since the kernels $a_{j,m}$ may vanish, we apply Step 2 to smooth approximations of $\log a_{j,m}$ and pass to the limit. Fix $x_0\in X$ and a small coordinate ball $W$ about $x_0$ such that $W\subset U'_ j$ whenever $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$, and $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j=\varnothing $ otherwise; then the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ are those with $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$. Choose a smooth function $g$ on $W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=	heta $, and for each such $j$ write $h_ j-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$ with $b_ j$ holomorphic, by lemma 13.1.2 . Since $h_ j=g+\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$, we have $a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mh_ j}K_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}k_ j$ on $W$, where, by ( 13.2 ) and since $|\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}|^2=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}$, $k_ j=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}K_{j,m}=\sum _\ell |\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}e_\ell |^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$ of the space defining $K_{j,m}$. For $\delta >0$ the function $\log (k_ j+\delta )$ is smooth, by lemma 13.2.2 , and plurisubharmonic: it is the increasing limit of the logarithms of the finite partial sums of these squared moduli together with $|\sqrt\delta |^2$, which are plurisubharmonic by proposition 8.3.3 , and since the limit is continuous, theorem 8.3.2 applies. Put $w_ j^\delta =\log (k_ j+\delta )-mg$, so that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j^\delta \geq -m	heta $. On $W\cap U_ i\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$, which lies in $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ i}$, lemma 13.3.2 and the identities $a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}k_ j$, $a_{i,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}k_ i$ give $k_ j\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}k_ i$, and since $\mathrm e^{C_ B}\geq 1$ also $k_ j+\delta \leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}(k_ i+\delta )$. Thus the functions $w_ j^\delta $ satisfy the hypotheses of Step 2 on $W$, and the function \[   rac1m\log \sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j^\delta }+g'  \] is plurisubharmonic on $W$, where $g'$ is a smooth function on $W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g'=	heta +(2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}/m)\omega $, given by lemma 13.1.2 . Indeed, by Step 2 this function is smooth with positive semidefinite complex Hessian, so proposition 8.2.2 (1) applies. As $\delta \downarrow 0$, the sums $\sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j^\delta }=\mathrm e^{-mg}\sum _ j\chi _ j^2(k_ j+\delta )$ decrease to $R_ m$, so these functions decrease to $G_ m+g'$, which is not identically $-\infty $, since $G_ m\geq v_{i,m}$ on $U_ i$. By theorem 8.3.1 , $G_ m+g'$ is plurisubharmonic on $W$. Hence $G_ m$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, and the curvature bound holds with $c'=2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}$, which depends only on the fixed geometry. Step 4: the singularities of $G_ m$ are gentle. Each summand of $R_ m$ is smooth by lemma 13.2.2 . On $U_ i$ we have $a_{i,m}\leq R_ m\leq J\mathrm e^{C_ B}a_{i,m}$ by lemma 13.3.2 , and $a_{i,m}$ is comparable with $\sum _ k|g_ k|^2$ for local generators $g_ k$ of $\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ i))=\mathcal I(m\varphi )$. Thus $G_ m$ has analytic singularities of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(m\varphi ))$, and $\exp (mG_ m)=R_ m$ is smooth on $X$. Now let $\pi \colon Y	o X$ be any log resolution of $\mathcal I(m\varphi )$, with $\pi ^*\mathcal I(m\varphi )=\mathcal O(-D)$. Its restriction $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)	o B_ j$ satisfies $\pi ^*\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ j))=\mathcal O(-D)$ on $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$, so by lemma 13.2.2 , applied with the volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$, the pulled-back kernel $K_{j,m}\circ \pi $ is locally $|s_ D|^2$ times a smooth strictly positive function on $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$. The factors $\mathrm e^{-mh_ j}\circ \pi $ and $\chi _ j^2\circ \pi $ are smooth, and the latter vanishes outside the closed set $\pi ^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j)\subset \pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$; hence $(R_ m\circ \pi )/|s_ D|^2$ is smooth on $Y$, and it is strictly positive because at every point some $\chi _ i\circ \pi $ equals one. Therefore $G_ m\circ \pi $ is locally the sum of $m^{-1}\log |s_ D|^2$ and a smooth function. These are exactly the requirements of definition 13.1.11 . $\square$ Lemma 13.4.2 . Consequently \[  R_{2m}\leq C_*\sum _ j\chi _ j^2a_{j,m}^2 \leq C_*J\mathrm e^{2C_ B}R_ m^2  \] at $x$, also when both sides vanish. Taking logarithms and dividing by $2m$ gives $G_{2m}\leq G_ m+D/m$ with $D= rac12\log \max (1,C_*J\mathrm e^{2C_ B})$. $\square$ To obtain inclusions of multiplier ideals from an integrability estimate, we use the following elementary lemma. Lemma 13.4.3 . Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic near a point $x$ of a complex manifold, and let $m>0$ be such that $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$ is integrable near $x$. If $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ and $m\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then \[  \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x.  \] Proof. After shrinking the neighborhood we may subtract a constant from $v$ and assume $v\leq 0$; this changes neither the ideals nor the integrability of $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Put $p=\lambda '/\lambda >1$, and note that $m\geq \lambda p/(p-1)>\lambda $. Let $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x$, defined on a small neighborhood on which $|f|^2\leq C$ for a constant $C$. All the following inequalities are taken outside the pole sets of $u$ and $v$, which have measure zero. Where $u\geq pv$, we have $\lambda u\geq \lambda 'v$ and hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq |f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda 'v}$. Where $u<pv$, since $m-\lambda >0$, $v\leq 0$ and $(m-\lambda )p-m=m(p-1)-\lambda p\geq 0$, \[  (m-\lambda )u-mv\leq ((m-\lambda )p-m)v\leq 0,  \] that is, $-\lambda u\leq m(v-u)$; hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq C\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Both bounds are integrable near $x$, so $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x$. $\square$ Definition 13.4.4 . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. A quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ is a sequence $(\Phi _ j)_{j\geq 1}$ of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions with analytic singularities, decreasing pointwise to $\varphi $, such that $	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -\varepsilon _ j\omega $ for some numbers $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, and such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad 	ext{for every sufficiently large }j.  \] Theorem 13.4.5 . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Every $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ admits a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\Phi _ j)$ in which each $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$, and which can be chosen with $\varepsilon _ j=c'2^{-j}$, where $c'$ is the constant of lemma 13.4.1 (1). Moreover $\Phi _ j	o \varphi $ in $L^1(X)$, and the Lelong numbers of $\Phi _ j$ satisfy the bounds of lemma 13.4.2 with $m=2^ j$. Proof. Put $\Phi _ j=G_{2^ j}+2D/2^ j$, with $D$ as in lemma 13.4.2 . The doubling inequality gives \[  \Phi _{j+1}=G_{2\cdot 2^ j}+ rac D{2^ j}\leq G_{2^ j}+ rac D{2^ j}+ rac D{2^ j}=\Phi _ j,  \] so the sequence is decreasing, and by lemma 13.4.2 its pointwise and $L^1$ limit is $\varphi $. Adding a constant changes neither the curvature, nor the analytic type, nor the Lelong numbers. Moreover $\exp (2^ j\Phi _ j)=\mathrm e^{2D}R_{2^ j}$ is smooth, and the remainder on a log resolution changes only by a constant. Hence $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$ by lemma 13.4.1 (1), and $	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -c'2^{-j}\omega $. It remains to prove the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Let $0<\lambda <\lambda '$. The function $\exp (2^ j(\Phi _ j-\varphi ))=\mathrm e^{2D}\mathrm e^{2^ j(G_{2^ j}-\varphi )}$ is integrable on $X$ by lemma 13.4.2 . If $j$ is so large that $2^ j\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then lemma 13.4.3 , with $u=\varphi $, $v=\Phi _ j$ and $m=2^ j$, gives $\mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi )_ x$ at every point $x\in X$. Since this threshold for $j$ depends only on $\lambda $ and $\lambda '$, the inclusion holds as an inclusion of sheaves on $X$ for all such $j$. $\square$

Lemma 13.4.1 . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, let $m\geq 1$ be an integer, and put \[  R_ m=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2a_{j,m},\qquad G_ m=m^{-1}\log R_ m,  \] each summand being extended by zero outside the support of $\chi _ j$. Let $W$ be an open subset of a complex manifold, let $N\geq 1$, and let $w_1,\ldots ,w_ N$ and $\chi _1,\ldots ,\chi _ N$ be smooth real functions on $W$ such that $S=\sum _{j=1}^ N\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$ is positive on $W$. Proof. Step 1: proof of (2). Let $w_ j$, $\chi _ j$, $S$ and $\alpha _ j$ be as in (2), and put $f_ j=\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$, so that $S=\sum _ jf_ j$. Next, $\partial  ar\partial \log S=\partial  ar\partial S/S-\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S/S^2$, and since $\sum _ l\chi _ l^2\mathrm e^{w_ l}=S$, \[  \sum _ j rac{\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j}S- rac{\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S}{S^2} = rac1{S^2}\sum _{j,l}\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l} igl (\chi _ l^2\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j-\chi _ j\chi _ l\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ l igr ).  \] In the last sum the terms with $j=l$ vanish, and for $j<l$ the terms with indices $(j,l)$ and $(l,j)$ add up to $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)\wedge \overline{(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)}$. Multiplying by $\mathrm i/2\pi $ and using $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}= rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial  ar\partial $, we obtain ( 13.5 ). The first term on the right of ( 13.5 ) is semipositive, because the coefficients $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}/(2\pi S^2)$ are positive and, for a $(1,0)$-form $\gamma =\sum _ k\gamma _ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$, the coefficient matrix $(\gamma _ k ar\gamma _{k'})$ of $\mathrm i\gamma \wedge  ar\gamma $ is positive semidefinite. We now prove (1) in three steps. Step 2: a curvature estimate. By lemma 13.1.1 , applied on the compact manifold $X$ to the finitely many smooth forms below, there is a constant $A>0$, depending only on the fixed geometry, such that $\chi _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j- rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j\geq -A\omega $ for every $j$. Let $W\subset X$ be open, and for the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ let $w_ j$ be smooth real functions on $W$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j\geq -m	heta \quad 	ext{on }W,\qquad \mathrm e^{w_ j}\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}\mathrm e^{w_ i}\quad 	ext{on }W\cap U_ i\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j  \] for all such $i,j$. We claim that $S=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$ is positive on $W$ and that \[  	heta + rac1m\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log S\geq - rac{2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}}m\omega \qquad 	ext{on }W.  \] Let $x\in W$ and choose $i$ with $x\in U_ i$. Then $\chi _ i(x)=1$, so $S(x)\geq \mathrm e^{w_ i(x)}>0$, and $\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}$ at $x$ for every $j$ with $\chi _ j(x)
eq 0$. Since $S>0$ on $W$, the identity ( 13.5 ) of (2) holds on $W$. If $\chi _ j(x)=0$, the $j$th summand of the last term in ( 13.5 ) vanishes at $x$, because the nonnegative function $\chi _ j$ attains its minimum at $x$, so that $\partial \chi _ j(x)=0$. Hence the last term is at least $-2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}\omega $ at $x$. The coefficients $\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S$ are nonnegative with sum one, so the middle term is at least $-m	heta $, and the first term is semipositive. This proves the claim. Step 3: $G_ m$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and satisfies the curvature bound. Since the kernels $a_{j,m}$ may vanish, we apply Step 2 to smooth approximations of $\log a_{j,m}$ and pass to the limit. Fix $x_0\in X$ and a small coordinate ball $W$ about $x_0$ such that $W\subset U'_ j$ whenever $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$, and $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j=\varnothing $ otherwise; then the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ are those with $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$. Choose a smooth function $g$ on $W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=	heta $, and for each such $j$ write $h_ j-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$ with $b_ j$ holomorphic, by lemma 13.1.2 . Since $h_ j=g+\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$, we have $a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mh_ j}K_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}k_ j$ on $W$, where, by ( 13.2 ) and since $|\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}|^2=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}$, $k_ j=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}K_{j,m}=\sum _\ell |\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}e_\ell |^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$ of the space defining $K_{j,m}$. For $\delta >0$ the function $\log (k_ j+\delta )$ is smooth, by lemma 13.2.2 , and plurisubharmonic: it is the increasing limit of the logarithms of the finite partial sums of these squared moduli together with $|\sqrt\delta |^2$, which are plurisubharmonic by proposition 8.3.3 , and since the limit is continuous, theorem 8.3.2 applies. Thus the functions $w_ j^\delta $ satisfy the hypotheses of Step 2 on $W$, and the function \[   rac1m\log \sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j^\delta }+g'  \] is plurisubharmonic on $W$, where $g'$ is a smooth function on $W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g'=	heta +(2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}/m)\omega $, given by lemma 13.1.2 . Indeed, by Step 2 this function is smooth with positive semidefinite complex Hessian, so proposition 8.2.2 (1) applies. On $U_ i$ we have $a_{i,m}\leq R_ m\leq J\mathrm e^{C_ B}a_{i,m}$ by lemma 13.3.2 , and $a_{i,m}$ is comparable with $\sum _ k|g_ k|^2$ for local generators $g_ k$ of $\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ i))=\mathcal I(m\varphi )$. Now let $\pi \colon Y	o X$ be any log resolution of $\mathcal I(m\varphi )$, with $\pi ^*\mathcal I(m\varphi )=\mathcal O(-D)$. Its restriction $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)	o B_ j$ satisfies $\pi ^*\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ j))=\mathcal O(-D)$ on $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$, so by lemma 13.2.2 , applied with the volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$, the pulled-back kernel $K_{j,m}\circ \pi $ is locally $|s_ D|^2$ times a smooth strictly positive function on $\pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$. The factors $\mathrm e^{-mh_ j}\circ \pi $ and $\chi _ j^2\circ \pi $ are smooth, and the latter vanishes outside the closed set $\pi ^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j)\subset \pi ^{-1}(B_ j)$; hence $(R_ m\circ \pi )/|s_ D|^2$ is smooth on $Y$, and it is strictly positive because at every point some $\chi _ i\circ \pi $ equals one. Therefore $G_ m\circ \pi $ is locally the sum of $m^{-1}\log |s_ D|^2$ and a smooth function. These are exactly the requirements of definition 13.1.11 . $\square$

title: Lemma 13.4.3
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Lemma 13.4.3 . Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic near a point $x$ of a complex manifold, and let $m>0$ be such that $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$ is integrable near $x$. If $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ and $m\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then \[  \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x.  \] Proof. After shrinking the neighborhood we may subtract a constant from $v$ and assume $v\leq 0$; this changes neither the ideals nor the integrability of $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Put $p=\lambda '/\lambda >1$, and note that $m\geq \lambda p/(p-1)>\lambda $. Let $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x$, defined on a small neighborhood on which $|f|^2\leq C$ for a constant $C$. All the following inequalities are taken outside the pole sets of $u$ and $v$, which have measure zero. Where $u\geq pv$, we have $\lambda u\geq \lambda 'v$ and hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq |f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda 'v}$. Where $u<pv$, since $m-\lambda >0$, $v\leq 0$ and $(m-\lambda )p-m=m(p-1)-\lambda p\geq 0$, \[  (m-\lambda )u-mv\leq ((m-\lambda )p-m)v\leq 0,  \] that is, $-\lambda u\leq m(v-u)$; hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq C\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Both bounds are integrable near $x$, so $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x$. $\square$

title: Definition 13.4.4
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Definition 13.4.4 . Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. A quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ is a sequence $(\Phi _ j)_{j\geq 1}$ of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions with analytic singularities, decreasing pointwise to $\varphi $, such that $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -\varepsilon _ j\omega $ for some numbers $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, and such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }j.  \] Definition 1.6.8 . Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Consider $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. A sequence $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}$ in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ is quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ if $\varphi _ j$ has analytic singularities for each $j$; $\varphi _ j$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $; there is a decreasing sequence $\epsilon _ j\geq 0$ with limit $0$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$; for each $\lambda '>\lambda >0$, there is $j>0$ such that 1.40 \begin{equation} \label{eq:quasi_eq_prop} \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ). \end{equation} We also say $(\theta _{\varphi _ j})_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\theta _{\varphi }$.

title: Theorem 13.4.5
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Theorem 13.4.5 . Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Every $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ admits a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\Phi _ j)$ in which each $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$, and which can be chosen with $\varepsilon _ j=c'2^{-j}$, where $c'$ is the constant of lemma 13.4.1 (1). Moreover $\Phi _ j\to \varphi $ in $L^1(X)$, and the Lelong numbers of $\Phi _ j$ satisfy the bounds of lemma 13.4.2 with $m=2^ j$. Proof. Put $\Phi _ j=G_{2^ j}+2D/2^ j$, with $D$ as in lemma 13.4.2 . The doubling inequality gives \[  \Phi _{j+1}=G_{2\cdot 2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}\leq G_{2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}=\Phi _ j,  \] so the sequence is decreasing, and by lemma 13.4.2 its pointwise and $L^1$ limit is $\varphi $. Adding a constant changes neither the curvature, nor the analytic type, nor the Lelong numbers. Moreover $\exp (2^ j\Phi _ j)=\mathrm e^{2D}R_{2^ j}$ is smooth, and the remainder on a log resolution changes only by a constant. Hence $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$ by lemma 13.4.1 (1), and $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -c'2^{-j}\omega $. It remains to prove the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Let $0<\lambda <\lambda '$. The function $\exp (2^ j(\Phi _ j-\varphi ))=\mathrm e^{2D}\mathrm e^{2^ j(G_{2^ j}-\varphi )}$ is integrable on $X$ by lemma 13.4.2 . If $j$ is so large that $2^ j\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then lemma 13.4.3 , with $u=\varphi $, $v=\Phi _ j$ and $m=2^ j$, gives $\mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi )_ x$ at every point $x\in X$. Since this threshold for $j$ depends only on $\lambda $ and $\lambda '$, the inclusion holds as an inclusion of sheaves on $X$ for all such $j$. $\square$

title: 13.5 Comparison of analytic singularities
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: 13.5 Comparison of analytic singularities For functions $u,v\colon X\to [-\infty ,\infty )$ we write $u\preceq v$, and say that $u$ is more singular than $v$, if $u\leq v+C$ on $X$ for some constant $C$. Since $X$ is compact, it suffices that every point have a neighborhood on which such an inequality holds. We now show that two quasi-equisingular approximations of the same function are comparable for $\preceq $, up to an arbitrarily small loss in the coefficient. The key is a growth estimate for the members of the multiplier ideals of a function with analytic singularities. Lemma 13.5.1 . Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function with analytic singularities on a compact complex manifold $X$, and let $0<\eta <1$. There is $t_0>0$ such that for every real $t\geq t_0$ and every germ $f\in \mathcal I(tv)_ x$, $x\in X$, \[  \log |f|^2\leq t(1-\eta )v+O(1)  \] near $x$, where the bounded term may depend on $f$. Moreover, for every quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ and every $t>0$, local generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(tu)$ satisfy \[  u\leq t^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1).  \] Proof. For the first assertion we pull $v$ back to log resolutions of its local presentations, where theorem 12.6.5 bounds the vanishing orders of $f$ along the components of the divisor from below. Cover $X$ by finitely many open sets $V_\kappa ^+$ on which $v$ has a presentation ( 13.1 ), and choose open sets $V_\kappa \Subset V_\kappa ^+$ that still cover $X$. By theorem A.5.5 , the ideal generated by the presentation on $V_\kappa ^+$ has a log resolution $\pi _\kappa \colon Y_\kappa \to V_\kappa ^+$, a sequence of blowups that is finite over $V_\kappa $; it is proper and surjective, so $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$ and the fibers of $\pi _\kappa $ are compact. On $Y_\kappa $ we have locally $v\circ \pi _\kappa =\sum _ Ea_ E\log |s_ E|^2+O(1)$, where $\pi _\kappa ^*(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r)=\mathcal O(-\sum _ Ed_ EE)$, $E$ runs over the components of this divisor, $s_ E$ is a local equation of $E$, and $a_ E=cd_ E>0$. Let $A_ E$ be the log discrepancy of $E$ (definition 12.6.3 ). Only finitely many components $E$ meet the compact set $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$, so altogether there are finitely many pairs $(a_ E,A_ E)$ with $E$ meeting one of these sets. Choose $t_0>0$ with $t_0\eta a_ E\geq A_ E$ for all of them. Now let $x\in V_\kappa $, let $t\geq t_0$, and let $f\in \mathcal I(tv)_ x$ be defined on an open neighborhood $V'\subset V_\kappa $ of $x$. Near $x$ the function $tv$ differs by a smooth function from a plurisubharmonic function with the same multiplier ideal and of the form required in theorem 12.6.5 , with coefficient $tc$. We apply that theorem over $V'$, shrunk if necessary, to the log resolution obtained by restricting $\pi _\kappa $. Each component $E'$ of the restricted divisor is a connected component of $E\cap \pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$ for a component $E$ as above, and it has the same coefficient $d_ E$ and the same log discrepancy $A_ E$, as we show below. Since $tc\, d_ E=ta_ E$, the theorem gives \[  \operatorname {ord}_{E'}f>ta_ E-A_ E\geq t(1-\eta )a_ E  \] for every component $E'$ of the restricted divisor that meets $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$; the second inequality holds because $t\geq t_0$ and $E$ meets $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$. The coefficient and the log discrepancy of $E'$ are those of $E$ because the vanishing orders along $E$ of a local generator of $\pi _\kappa ^*(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r)$ and of a local Jacobian determinant of $\pi _\kappa $ do not depend on the point of $E$ at which they are computed. Indeed, two local generators of this invertible ideal, like two local Jacobian determinants, differ by a unit, which has order zero along $E$; since orders add under products, they have the same order along $E$ at every point of $E$ where both are defined (lemma 12.6.1 (2),(4)). Moreover, the order along $E$ of a holomorphic function is locally constant on $E_{\mathrm{reg}}$, by the last assertion of lemma 12.6.1 (2), and $E_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is connected (corollary A.2.13 ); here $E_{\mathrm{reg}}=E$, since the components of a simple normal crossings divisor are smooth. If $f=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $f\neq 0$. Shrinking $V'$, we may assume that $V'$ is connected; then $f$ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $V'$. Hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$, because $\pi _\kappa $ is a biholomorphism off the nowhere dense set $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r))$; in particular, the orders of $f$ along the components of the restricted divisor are finite. Let $p\in \pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and choose coordinates $w$ on a neighborhood of $p$ in $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$ in which the components of the divisor through $p$ are $\{ w_ k=0\} $, $k=1,\ldots ,\ell $, with coefficients $a_ k=a_ E$ for the corresponding components $E$. Then $v\circ \pi _\kappa =\sum _ ka_ k\log |w_ k|^2+O(1)$ near $p$. For each $k$, let $E'_ k$ be the component of the restricted divisor that contains $\{ w_ k=0\} $ near $p$, and put $o_ k=\operatorname {ord}_{E'_ k}f$, an integer with $o_ k>t(1-\eta )a_ k$ by the inequality above. Since $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is holomorphic on a neighborhood of $E'_ k$, its order along $E'_ k$ is the same at all points of the connected submanifold $E'_ k$, by lemma 12.6.1 (3); hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is divisible by $w_ k^{o_ k}$ near $p$, by lemma 12.6.1 (1),(2). By the last assertion of lemma 12.6.2 , divisibility by each $w_ k^{o_ k}$ separately implies divisibility by their product: $f\circ \pi _\kappa =\prod _ kw_ k^{o_ k}\cdot h$ with $h$ holomorphic near $p$, hence bounded on a smaller neighborhood of $p$. Since $|w_ k|\leq 1$ there, we obtain $|f\circ \pi _\kappa |^2\leq C\prod _ k|w_ k|^{2t(1-\eta )a_ k}\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v\circ \pi _\kappa )$. Finitely many such neighborhoods cover the compact fiber $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and since $\pi _\kappa $ is proper, their union contains the inverse image of a neighborhood of $x$. As $\pi _\kappa $ is surjective, the inequality $|f|^2\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v)$ holds near $x$. For the second assertion, fix a point and write $u=u_0-\sigma $ near it, with $u_0$ plurisubharmonic and $\sigma $ smooth. Then $\mathcal I(tu)=\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point. On a bounded polydisc $\Omega $ about the point on which $u_0$ is bounded above, theorem 12.2.7 (3) provides finitely many elements of $\mathcal H_{tu_0}(\Omega )$ that generate $\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point, and ( 12.11 ) of lemma 12.2.8 , applied with $m=t$ to the weight $u_0$, gives $u_0\leq t^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ for these generators. Since $\sigma $ is bounded near the point, and any two finite systems of local generators give comparable sums of squares (the remark following definition 13.1.5 ), the assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 13.5.2 . Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, let $\varphi $ and $\Phi $ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ with $\varphi \leq \Phi $, where $\Phi $ has analytic singularities, and let $(\Psi _ k)_{k\geq 1}$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Psi _ k)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] Then for each $0<\varepsilon <1$, \[  \Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] In particular, if $(X,\omega )$ is a compact Kähler manifold, $\theta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $(\Phi _ j)$ and $(\Psi _ k)$ are quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $, then for each $j$ and each $0<\varepsilon <1$ we have $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi _ j$ for every sufficiently large $k$. Proof. Choose $0<\eta <\varepsilon $ and $\delta >0$ so small that $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $. Fix $t\geq t_0$, where $t_0$ is given by lemma 13.5.1 for $v=\Phi $ and $\eta $. By the hypothesis on $(\Psi _ k)$, applied with $\lambda =t$ and $\lambda '=t(1+\delta )$, and since $\varphi \leq \Phi $, \[  \mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k) \subseteq \mathcal I(t\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal I(t\Phi )  \] for every sufficiently large $k$. Fix such a $k$ and choose local generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k)$ near a point of $X$. They belong to $\mathcal I(t\Phi )$, so the first part of lemma 13.5.1 gives $\log |g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$ near the point, and hence $\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$. Its second part, applied to $u=\Psi _ k$ and $t(1+\delta )$, then gives \[  \Psi _ k\leq \frac1{t(1+\delta )}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1) \leq \frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }\Phi +O(1).  \] The upper semicontinuous function $\Phi $ is bounded above on the compact space $X$, say by $M$. Since $\Phi -M\leq 0$ and $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $, we have $\frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }(\Phi -M)\leq (1-\varepsilon )(\Phi -M)$, and therefore $\Psi _ k\leq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi +O(1)$ near every point. By compactness $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi $; the constant may depend on $k$. For the last assertion, recall from definition 13.4.4 that each $\Phi _ j$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic with analytic singularities and that $\varphi \leq \Phi _ j$, since the sequence decreases to $\varphi $; and $(\Psi _ k)$ satisfies the hypothesis on the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Hence the first part applies with $\Phi =\Phi _ j$. $\square$ Example 13.5.3 . Let $u=c\log |z|^2$ on a disc about $0\in \mathbb C$, with $c>0$. A germ $z^ kh$ with $h(0)\neq 0$ lies in $\mathcal I(mu)_0$ if and only if $|z|^{2k-2mc}$ is integrable near $0$, that is, $k>mc-1$; hence $\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $z^{\lfloor mc\rfloor }$ (example 12.5.5 ). A potential of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(mu))$, such as the Bergman potential $u_ m$ of theorem 13.2.3 , is therefore $(\lfloor mc\rfloor /m)\log |z|^2+O(1)$ near $0$. Its coefficient $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m$ need not equal $c$ for any $m$, and then such an approximation does not reproduce the multiplier ideals of $u$ at a fixed scale. For instance, let $c$ be irrational, so that $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m<c$ for every $m$, and take the scale $1/c$. Since $u_ m/c$ differs by a bounded function from $c_ m\log |z|^2$ with $c_ m=\lfloor mc\rfloor /(mc)<1$, the same computation gives $\mathcal I(u_ m/c)_0=\mathcal O_0$ for every $m$, whereas $\mathcal I(u/c)_0=\mathcal I(\log |z|^2)_0$ is generated by $z$. This is why definition 13.4.4 compares two different scales $\lambda '>\lambda $ instead of requiring equality of multiplier ideals.
