title: Theorem 14.8.7
section: 9.1 Global potentials and positive cohomology classes
text: Theorem 14.8.7 . Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, and let $A\subset X$ be pluripolar (definition 10.1.1 ). Then there is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\Phi $ on $X$ with $A\subset \{ \Phi =-\infty \} $; that is, $A$ is globally pluripolar. Proof. The compact manifold $X$ has finitely many connected components, which are open, and it suffices to construct $\Phi $ on each of them, since the intersection of $A$ with a component is pluripolar in that component. On a component of dimension zero, which is a point, pluripolar sets are empty and $\Phi =0$ works. We may therefore assume that $X$ is connected of dimension $n\geq 1$, and we fix a Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$ (one exists by section 7.5 ), so that the notation of this section applies. Every point of $X$ has a coordinate ball $U$ and a plurisubharmonic function on $U$ whose pole set contains $A\cap U$, by definition 10.1.1 ; choose a smaller ball $U_1\Subset U$ around the point. By compactness finitely many of the balls $U_1$ cover $X$. By the last assertion of lemma 14.8.4 it therefore suffices to prove the following: if $U$ is a coordinate ball, $\varphi $ is plurisubharmonic on $U$ and $U_1\Subset U$ is a smaller ball, then $E=\{ \varphi =-\infty \} \cap U_1$ is globally pluripolar. If $E$ is empty, there is nothing to prove, so let $E\neq \varnothing $. Choose balls $U_1\Subset U_2\Subset U_3\Subset U$ and subtract a constant from $\varphi $ so that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $U_3$. Suppose, to reach a contradiction, that $E$ is not globally pluripolar. By lemma 14.8.4 , there is a constant $C$ with $0\leq T_ E^*\leq C$. From the extremal functions of compact sublevel sets of regularizations of $\varphi $, which have small capacity, we shall obtain a bounded function in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with zero Monge–Ampère mass. Step 1. Sublevel sets and their extremal functions. Convolution with radial mollifiers of radii decreasing to zero and smaller than the distance from $U_2$ to $\partial U_3$ gives smooth plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi _ j$ on $U_2$ that decrease to $\varphi $ as $j\to \infty $, by proposition 8.2.2 (2). Since $\varphi \leq 0$ on $U_3$, we have $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j\leq 0$ on $U_2$, so $\| \varphi _ j\| _{L^1(U_2)}\leq \| \varphi \| _{L^1(U_2)}<\infty $. For integers $N,j\geq 1$ put \[  K_{j,N}=\{ \varphi _ j\leq -N\} \cap \overline{U_1},\qquad O_{j,N}=\{ \varphi _ j<-N\} \cap U_1.  \] Then $K_{j,N}$ is compact and contains the open set $O_{j,N}$. Fix $x_0\in E$. Since $\varphi _ j(x_0)\downarrow -\infty $, there is $j_0(N)$ such that $x_0\in O_{j,N}$ for $j\geq j_0(N)$; we choose $j_0(N)$ nondecreasing in $N$. For these $j$ the set $K_{j,N}$ has nonempty interior, so $u_{j,N}=T_{K_{j,N}}^*$ is a bounded nonnegative function in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ by lemma 14.8.4 . Every competitor for $T_{K_{j,N}}$ is nonpositive on the open set $O_{j,N}$; hence so is $T_{K_{j,N}}$, and its upper semicontinuous regularization satisfies $u_{j,N}=0$ on $O_{j,N}$. For fixed $N$, the sets $K_{j,N}$ increase with $j$, because $\varphi _ j$ decreases. A competitor for $T_{K_{j+1,N}}$ is a competitor for $T_{K_{j,N}}$, so $u_{j,N}$ decreases with $j\geq j_0(N)$; let $u_ N$ be its limit. By lemma 14.8.1 (3), $u_ N\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, and $0\leq u_ N\leq u_{j_0(N),N}$ is bounded. If $x\in U_1$ and $\varphi (x)<-N$, then $x\in O_{j,N}$ for all large $j$, so $u_ N(x)=0$. In particular $u_ N=0$ on $E$, so $u_ N$ is a competitor for $T_ E$, and \[  0\leq u_ N\leq T_ E^*\leq C.  \] For fixed $j$, the sets $K_{j,N}$ decrease as $N$ increases, so $u_{j,N}\leq u_{j,N+1}$ for $j\geq j_0(N+1)$; letting $j\to \infty $ gives $u_ N\leq u_{N+1}$. Let $u_\infty $ be the upper semicontinuous regularization of $\lim _ Nu_ N$. By lemma 14.8.1 (1), $u_\infty \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $0\leq u_\infty \leq C$. Step 2. Convergence of the masses. By lemma 14.8.1 (3), applied to the uniformly bounded decreasing sequence $(u_{j,N})_{j\geq j_0(N)}$ and to the uniformly bounded increasing sequence $(u_ N)_{N\geq 1}$, and testing the weak convergence with the constant function $1$ on the compact manifold $X$, we obtain \[  \int _ X\omega _{u_{j,N}}^ n\longrightarrow \int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\quad (j\to \infty ),\qquad \int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\longrightarrow \int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n\quad (N\to \infty ).  \] Moreover $\int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n>0$ by proposition 14.8.3 , since $u_\infty $ is bounded. Step 3. The capacity of $K_{j,N}$. Choose a smooth function $h$ on $U_2$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\geq \omega $ and $\sup _{U_2}|h|<\infty $, for instance a large multiple of $|z|^2$. If $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $0\leq v\leq 1$, then $v+h$ is plurisubharmonic on $U_2$ with $|v+h|\leq 1+\sup _{U_2}|h|$, and $\omega _ v^ n\leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+h))^ n$ on $U_2$ by lemma 14.8.1 (2). Since $K_{j,N}\subset \overline{U_1}$ and $-\varphi _ j\geq N$ on $K_{j,N}$, while $-\varphi _ j\geq 0$ on $U_2$, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg inequality (theorem 9.3.1 ), applied in $U_2$ to $\varphi _ j$, the compact set $\overline{U_1}$ and a compact neighborhood $L\subset U_2$ of $\overline{U_1}$, gives \[  \int _{K_{j,N}}\omega _ v^ n \leq \frac1N\int _{\overline{U_1}}(-\varphi _ j)\, (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+h))^ n \leq \frac{C'}N.  \] The constant $C'$ depends on $\| \varphi _ j\| _{L^1(L)}\leq \| \varphi \| _{L^1(U_2)}$ and on the bound for $|v+h|$, but not on $v$, $j$ or $N$. Taking the supremum over $v$, we obtain $c_\omega (K_{j,N})\leq C'/N$. Step 4. Conclusion. By proposition 14.8.6 , \[  \int _ X\omega _{u_{j,N}}^ n\leq \max \{ 1,\sup _ Xu_{j,N}\} ^ n\, \frac{C'}N\qquad (j\geq j_0(N)).  \] For fixed $N$, the uniformly bounded functions $u_{j,N}$ decrease to $u_ N$, so $u_{j,N}\to u_ N$ in $L^1(X)$ by dominated convergence, and $\sup _ Xu_{j,N}\to \sup _ Xu_ N$ by lemma 14.8.1 (4). Letting $j\to \infty $ and using $u_ N\leq C$, we obtain $\int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\leq \max \{ 1,C\} ^ nC'/N$. Letting $N\to \infty $ gives $\int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n=0$, which contradicts Step 2. Hence $E$ is globally pluripolar, and the theorem is proved. $\square$

title: 15 Non-pluripolar products
text: 15 Non-pluripolar products In chapter 9 we multiplied the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1,\ldots ,\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p$ of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions by the Bedford–Taylor recursion $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1T)$. The potentials that arise in global geometry are often unbounded: by corollary 14.1.9 , a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on a compact Kähler manifold is $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ with $\theta $ a smooth form and $\varphi $ quasi-plurisubharmonic, and $\varphi =-\infty $ wherever the current has a positive Lelong number, for instance along a hypersurface carrying a current of integration. Indeed, at a point where $\varphi $ is finite, the spherical means of a local potential are bounded below by its value at that point, so the Lelong number vanishes there by ( 12.5 ). For such potentials the recursion breaks down, since it multiplies the measure coefficients of a current by an unbounded function. In this chapter we construct a product for arbitrary plurisubharmonic potentials which keeps positivity, closedness, multilinearity and locality, at the price of ignoring everything that happens on pluripolar sets. The construction truncates the potentials and discards their poles. We replace each $u_ j$ by $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $, take the Bedford–Taylor product, and keep only its restriction to the set where all $u_ j>-k$, on which the truncated potentials coincide with the original ones. Since bounded products are local in the plurifine topology (theorem 10.4.3 ), the restrictions obtained for different $k$ are compatible and increase with $k$. Their limit is the non-pluripolar product $\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p\rangle $, which by construction gives no mass to pluripolar sets. Two phenomena without counterpart in the bounded theory appear. The limit may have infinite mass on compact sets (example 15.1.6 ). And the mass carried by the poles is lost: in degree one, $\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\rangle $ is the restriction of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ to $\{ u>-\infty \} $ (proposition 15.3.6 ), so the current of integration at a point of $\mathbb P^1$ has zero non-pluripolar product, and even a potential with zero Lelong numbers and trivial multiplier ideals can have zero non-pluripolar mass (example 15.3.8 ). When the local masses are finite, the product is a closed positive current (theorem 15.2.1 ). On a compact Kähler manifold $X$ the local masses are always finite: every tuple of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents has a non-pluripolar product, and its total mass is bounded by a cohomological quantity (theorem 15.4.3 ). The total mass is, however, no longer determined by the cohomology classes of the factors; it depends on the singularities of the potentials. The central result of the second half of the chapter is that it is monotone in the singularities: if $\theta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form, $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\psi $ is more singular than $\varphi $ in the sense of definition 14.2.6 , then the mass of $\varphi $ is at least that of $\psi $ (theorem 15.7.4 ). When all potentials are locally bounded outside the closed pole set of a fixed quasi-plurisubharmonic function, this follows from Stokes' formula; arbitrary singularities are reduced to this case by an auxiliary potential on $X\times \mathbb P^ N$, whose total mass is an average of the masses along a segment of potentials. Along the way we prove that non-pluripolar products are lower semicontinuous under convergence in capacity, and continuous when no mass is lost in the limit (theorem 15.6.5 ). Monotonicity has several consequences that are used in the rest of the book. Mixed masses do not change under bounded perturbations of the potentials, and in a big class the potentials with minimal singularities have the largest masses; these maximal masses define the positive intersection numbers and the volume of pseudo-effective classes. The full-mass classes and the comparison and domination principles at the end of the chapter are basic tools for the envelopes of chapter 16 , and the fiber formula of section 15.5 is used for relative energy in chapter 17 . Historical remarks and references for this chapter are collected in section B.15 .

title: 15.1 Truncation and plurifine locality
text:
15.1 Truncation and plurifine locality Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$, let $U\subset X$ be a coordinate domain, and fix an integer $1\leq p\leq n$. Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ be plurisubharmonic functions on $U$, and recall that $\{ u_ j=-\infty \} $ is the pole set of $u_ j$. For each integer $k\geq 1$ put \[   egin{gathered} u_{j,k}=\max \{ u_ j,-k\} ,\qquad O_ k= igcap _{j=1}^ p\{ u_ j>-k\} ,\ S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,k}. \end{gathered}  \] The functions $u_{j,k}$ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic, so the product in $S_ k$ is the Bedford–Taylor product of definition 9.1.1 , and multiplication by $\mathbf1_{O_ k}$ restricts its coefficient measures to $O_ k$, where every $u_{j,k}$ coincides with $u_ j$. By proposition 10.4.4 , the trace measures of the currents $S_ k$ increase with $k$ to a Borel measure $\mu $ for which every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero, but $\mu $ may be infinite on compact sets (example 15.1.6 below). The set $O_ k$ is Borel, because plurisubharmonic functions are upper semicontinuous, and it is plurifine open, because they are plurifine continuous; it need not be open in the ordinary topology. For instance, the countable set $A$ of points with rational coordinates in the unit disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb C$ is polar, each point $a$ being the pole of $\log |z-a|$, so by proposition 4.2.3 there is a finite positive measure $
u $ with compact support such that the fundamental potential $E_2*
u $ equals $-\infty $ on $A$. The function $u_1(z)=(E_2*
u )(z_1)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\mathbb C^ n$ by proposition 3.2.1 , proposition 8.2.3 , and its pole set contains the dense subset $A	imes \mathbb C^{n-1}$ of $\Delta 	imes \mathbb C^{n-1}$. For $p=1$ and large $k$, the set $O_ k\cap (\Delta 	imes \mathbb C^{n-1})$ is nonempty, because $E_2*
u $ is locally integrable, but it has empty interior, so $O_ k$ is not open. We shall often restrict positive currents to Borel sets such as $O_ k$, and we first note that this preserves positivity. Lemma 15.1.1 . Let $R$ be a positive current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on an open set $W\subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $E\subset W$ be a Borel set. Then the current $\mathbf1_ ER$, obtained by multiplying the coefficient measures of $R$ by $\mathbf1_ E$, is positive. If $R$ is strongly positive, that is, $R(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every test form $\varphi $ that is weakly positive at every point, then so is $\mathbf1_ ER$. Proof. By theorem 7.2.5 , $R$ has measure coefficients. Let $\varphi $ be a test form of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$ that is strongly positive, respectively weakly positive, at every point. The complex measure $R\wedge \varphi $, whose integral against a test function $\chi $ is $R(\chi \varphi )$, defines a positive distribution, because $\chi \varphi $ has the same positivity as $\varphi $ whenever $\chi \geq 0$; by the uniqueness in theorem 1.4.5 , it is a positive measure. Hence $(\mathbf1_ ER)(\varphi )=(R\wedge \varphi )(E)\geq 0$. $\square$ The next lemma shows that local finiteness of $\mu $ is exactly what is needed for the currents $S_ k$ to converge. Lemma 15.1.2 . For $l\geq k$ the current $S_ l-S_ k$ is positive, and $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. The currents $S_ k$ converge weakly to a positive current $S$ if and only if 15.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-local-mass-condition} \sup _ k\int _ K S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}<\infty \quad 	ext{for every compact set }K\subset U, \end{equation} where $ eta $ is the Euclidean Kähler form ( 7.4 ) of the coordinates. In that case $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$ for every $k$, the coefficient measures of $S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ in total variation on compact subsets of $U$, and the trace measure of $S$ is the measure $\mu $ above. Every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero for $\mu $ and for the total variations of the coefficient measures of $S$; consequently every plurifine open subset of $U$ is measurable for the completions of these measures. Moreover, if $E_ k\subset O_ k$ are Borel sets such that $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ almost everywhere for the trace measure of $S$, then the coefficient measures of $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ when integrated against any bounded Borel function with compact support in $U$. This is the case, in particular, if the sets $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus  igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Proof. Let $l\geq k$. By proposition 10.4.4 , the level-$l$ and level-$k$ Bedford–Taylor products have the same restriction to $O_ k$; since $O_ k\subset O_ l$, this is the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. Consequently $S_ l-S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ l\setminus O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,l}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,l}$, and this current is positive by lemma 15.1.1 . Suppose that ( 15.1 ) holds. The trace measures $S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and, by ( 15.1 ), converge to a locally finite measure. Hence the trace mass of the positive current $S_ l-S_ k$ on a compact set $K$ tends to zero as $k,l	o \infty $. By theorem 7.2.5 , the total variation on $K$ of each coefficient measure of $S_ l-S_ k$ is at most a fixed multiple of this trace mass. Therefore each coefficient measure of $S_ k$ is a Cauchy sequence in total variation on compact sets, and the limits are the coefficients of a current $S$, which is positive as a weak limit of positive currents. Conversely, suppose that $S_ k	o S$ weakly for a positive current $S$. For every smooth compactly supported $\chi \geq 0$, the numbers $\int \chi S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and converge to $\int \chi S\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$, which therefore bounds them; choosing $\chi =1$ on $K$ gives ( 15.1 ). Assume now that ( 15.1 ) holds. Letting $l	o \infty $ in $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ gives $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$. By the convergence in total variation, the trace measure of $S$ is the increasing limit of the trace measures of the $S_ k$, which is $\mu $. By proposition 10.4.4 , every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer $\mu $-measure zero. The total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is at most $C_{n,p}\mu $ (theorem 7.2.5 ), so pluripolar sets have outer measure zero for these total variations as well, and theorem 10.4.1 (2), applied to $\mu $ and to these total variations, shows that plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for their completions. In particular $S$ vanishes on $U\setminus  igcup _ kO_ k$, the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, which is a pluripolar Borel set. Finally, let $E_ k$ be as in the statement. Since $E_ k\subset O_ k$, we have $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k=\mathbf1_{E_ k}S$. By theorem 7.2.5 , the total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is locally finite and absolutely continuous with respect to the trace measure. Hence $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ almost everywhere for each of these variations, and dominated convergence proves the assertion. If the $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus  igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar, then $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ outside this pluripolar Borel set, which $S$ does not charge. $\square$ Definition 15.1.3 . If ( 15.1 ) holds, we say that the non-pluripolar product of $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite , and we call the limit $S$ of lemma 15.1.2 the non-pluripolar product \[  \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle =S.  \] The angle brackets distinguish this construction from a product that retains mass on pluripolar sets. The empty product ($p=0$) is $1$. If all $u_ j$ are locally bounded, then every relatively compact open subset of $U$ is contained in $O_ k$ for large $k$. In this case the non-pluripolar product is locally finite and coincides with the Bedford–Taylor product, and we omit the brackets. Proposition 15.1.4 . Every locally finite non-pluripolar product $S$ is strongly positive: $S(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every compactly supported smooth weakly positive form $\varphi $ of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$. Proof. First let all potentials be locally bounded. Near each point they are limits of decreasing sequences of smooth plurisubharmonic functions, for instance of their mollifications (proposition 8.2.2 (2)). The complex Hessians of these functions are semipositive $(1,1)$-forms (proposition 8.2.2 (1)), hence strongly positive, since the two notions of positivity coincide in bidegree $(1,1)$; by proposition 7.2.1 , their exterior products are strongly positive, and the product of such a product with a weakly positive form of complementary bidegree is a nonnegative multiple of the volume form. Thus the smooth products pair nonnegatively with every smooth compactly supported weakly positive form. By theorem 9.2.5 , the Bedford–Taylor product is their weak limit, and therefore it pairs nonnegatively with these forms as well. By lemma 15.1.1 , applied to the bounded products in the definition of $S_ k$, every $S_ k$ is strongly positive. Since $S_ k	o S$ weakly by lemma 15.1.2 , so is $S$. $\square$ Proposition 15.1.5 . Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ and $v_1,\ldots ,v_ p$ be plurisubharmonic on $U$. If $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$, then the non-pluripolar product of the $u_ j$ is locally finite if and only if that of the $v_ j$ is, and then the two products are equal; thus local finiteness and the product depend only on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. The product is symmetric in its factors and local in the plurifine topology: if $u_ j=v_ j$ on a plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$ and both products are locally finite, then they have the same restriction to $O$. Finally, the product is multilinear: if $u_1'$ is plurisubharmonic on $U$, then the product of $u_1+u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite if and only if the products of $u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ and of $u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ are, and in that case \[   egin{aligned}  \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1+u_1')\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle & =\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle \ & \quad +\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1'\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle . \end{aligned}  \] Similarly, for real $c>0$ the product of $cu_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite if and only if that of $u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is, and then it is $c$ times the latter. Proof. In this proof we write $P^{(m)}(w_1,\ldots ,w_ p)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_1,-m\} \wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_ p,-m\} $ for plurisubharmonic $w_1,\ldots ,w_ p$ and an integer $m\geq 1$. Symmetry and locality. Each truncated product $S_ k$ is symmetric in its factors, hence so is the limit. Suppose that $u_ j=v_ j$ on the plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$, and that both products are locally finite. By lemma 15.1.2 , plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for the completions of the total variations of the coefficient measures of both products, so the restrictions of the products to $O$ and to the plurifine open sets $W_ k=O\cap  igcap _ j\{ u_ j>-k\} =O\cap  igcap _ j\{ v_ j>-k\} $ are well defined; the sets $W_ k$ increase with $k$. On $W_ k$ the truncations $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ coincide, so the two level-$k$ products agree on $W_ k$ by theorem 10.4.3 . Since $W_ k$ is contained in the level-$k$ sets of both tuples, lemma 15.1.2 shows that the two non-pluripolar products also agree on $W_ k$. The union of the $W_ k$ is $O$ minus the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, a pluripolar set, which has outer measure zero for these total variations by the same lemma. Letting $k	o \infty $, we conclude that the two products have the same restriction to $O$. Dependence on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. Suppose that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$. The distribution $v_ j-u_ j$ then has zero Laplacian, so by Weyl's lemma (theorem 2.1.4 ) it is a smooth function $w_ j$, and its complex Hessian vanishes: $w_ j$ is pluriharmonic. The plurisubharmonic functions $v_ j$ and $u_ j+w_ j$ agree almost everywhere, hence everywhere, since both are subharmonic (theorem 8.2.1 , theorem 3.2.2 ). Fix a relatively compact open set $V\subset U$ and an integer $C$ such that $|w_ j|\leq C$ on $V$ for all $j$. Write $O_ k(u),S_ k(u)$ and $O_ k(v),S_ k(v)$ for the level sets and truncated products of the two tuples. On $V\cap O_ k(v)$ we have $u_ j=v_ j-w_ j>-k-C$, hence \[  \max \{ v_ j,-k\} =v_ j=\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j .  \] The functions $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j$ are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $V$ and coincide on $V\cap O_ k(v)$. Moreover, adding the pluriharmonic function $w_ j$ to a factor does not change Bedford–Taylor products. Indeed, by additivity (proposition 9.1.2 ) and symmetry (theorem 9.2.5 ), the difference is a sum of products having $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j$ as first factor; by proposition 9.1.2 (1), such a product is the exterior product of the remaining closed positive current with the smooth form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j=0$. As $V\cap O_ k(v)\subset O_{k+C}(u)$, plurifine locality gives on $V$ \[  S_ k(v)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}P^{(k+C)}(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}S_{k+C}(u)\leq S_{k+C}(u).  \] Thus ( 15.1 ) for the $u_ j$ implies ( 15.1 ) for the $v_ j$ on compact subsets of $V$, and exchanging the two tuples (that is, replacing $w_ j$ by $-w_ j$) gives the converse. If both products are locally finite, the display and lemma 15.1.2 give $\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ pangle =\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle $ on $V$ for every $k$. The sets $O_ k(v)$ exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets, which are the same for the two tuples and carry no mass for either product. Hence the two products coincide. Additivity. Let $u_1'$ be plurisubharmonic and put \[  E_ k=\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ u_1'>-k\}  \cap  igcap _{j=2}^ p\{ u_ j>-k\} .  \] These plurifine open sets increase with $k$ and exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets of $u_1,u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$. On $E_ k$ we have $\max \{ u_1+u_1',-2k\} =u_1+u_1'=\max \{ u_1,-k\} +\max \{ u_1',-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-2k\} =\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ for $j\geq 2$. Plurifine locality and the additivity of bounded products (proposition 9.1.2 ) therefore give 15.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-additivity-on-levels}  egin{aligned}  \mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(2k)}(u_1+u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p) & =\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p)\ & \quad +\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Before local finiteness is known we argue with trace measures. By proposition 10.4.4 , for each of the three tuples the trace measures of the truncated products increase to a Borel measure, possibly infinite on compact sets, for which every pluripolar set has outer measure zero; for a locally finite product it is the trace measure of the product. The set $E_ k$ is contained in the level-$2k$ set of the first tuple and in the level-$k$ sets of the other two, so by the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ of lemma 15.1.2 , the restriction of each limit measure to $E_ k$ is the restriction of the corresponding trace measure in ( 15.4 ). Hence, on $E_ k$, the limit measure of the first tuple is the sum of those of the other two. Letting $k	o \infty $, monotone convergence gives this equality on every Borel subset of $ igcup _ kE_ k$, and hence everywhere, because the complement of $ igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Since all three measures are positive, the first is locally finite if and only if the other two are; this is the asserted equivalence of local finiteness. When the products are locally finite, ( 15.4 ) and lemma 15.1.2 give the additivity identity on each $E_ k$, and letting $k	o \infty $ proves it. For $c>0$ the same argument applies to the sets $\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ cu_1>-k\} \cap  igcap _{j\geq 2}\{ u_ j>-k\} $, on which $\max \{ cu_1,-k\} =c\max \{ u_1,-k\} $, and proves the homogeneity assertion. $\square$ Let now $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on the complex manifold $X$. By theorem 7.3.2 , every point of $X$ has a coordinate neighborhood on which $T_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ with $u_ j$ plurisubharmonic. By proposition 15.1.5 , local finiteness and the local non-pluripolar product do not depend on the choice of these potentials, and the construction is compatible with restriction to smaller open sets. They do not depend on the coordinates either. Indeed, let $F$ be a biholomorphism between coordinate domains. Then $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} \circ F=\max \{ u_ j\circ F,-k\} $ and $O_ k(u\circ F)=F^{-1}(O_ k(u))$. Since $F$ is a submersion, the pullback $F^*$ of proposition 7.5.2 satisfies $F^*(\mathbf1_ ES)=\mathbf1_{F^{-1}(E)}F^*S$ for every current $S$ of order zero and every Borel set $E$ (corollary 7.5.3 (2)), so proposition 9.1.2 (5) gives $F^*S_ k(u)=S_ k(u\circ F)$ for the truncated products. To compare trace measures, note that if $\alpha $ and $\alpha '$ are smooth semipositive $(1,1)$-forms on an open set with $\alpha '\leq c\alpha $, then \[  (c\alpha )^{n-p}-\alpha '^{n-p}=(c\alpha -\alpha ')\wedge \sum _{i=0}^{n-p-1}(c\alpha )^ i\wedge \alpha '^{n-p-1-i}  \] is a sum of products of semipositive $(1,1)$-forms, hence strongly positive (proposition 7.2.1 ). Since the product of a positive current with a smooth strongly positive form of complementary bidegree is a positive measure, it follows that 15.7  egin{equation} \label{eq:trace-measure-form-comparison} R\wedge \alpha '^{n-p}\leq c^{n-p}R\wedge \alpha ^{n-p} \end{equation} on that open set, for every positive current $R$ of bidegree $(p,p)$. On a neighborhood of a compact set, the Euclidean forms $ eta $ and $ eta '$ of the two coordinate systems satisfy $ eta '\leq c eta $ for some $c$ (lemma 13.1.1 ), so by ( 15.7 ) the trace measures of a positive current in the two coordinate systems are comparable on compact sets, and local finiteness does not depend on the coordinates. Since $F^*$ is weakly continuous, $F^*\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle =\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1\circ F)\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ p\circ F)angle $. We say that the non-pluripolar product of $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ is locally finite if this holds near every point; the local products then glue to a positive current $\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ pangle $ on $X$, which is closed by theorem 15.2.1 below. When $X$ is compact we also say simply that the product is finite . Repeated factors are written as powers, as in $\langle T^ j\wedge S^{r-j}angle $, and for $T_ j=	heta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ we also write $\langle (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ p+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p)angle $. The assertions of proposition 15.1.5 carry over to these products, with multilinearity in the factors $T_ j$. Example 15.1.6 . Let $U=\{ (x,y)\in \mathbb C^2:|x|^2<1/2,\  |y|<\mathrm e^{-1}\} $, put $L=-\log |y|$, and define \[  u(x,y)=(|x|^2-1)\sqrt L\quad (y
e 0),\qquad u(x,0)=-\infty .  \] On $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $ we have $L>1$, the function $u$ is smooth, and its complex second derivatives are \[  u_{x ar x}=\sqrt L,\qquad u_{y ar y}= rac{1-|x|^2}{16|y|^2L^{3/2}},\qquad u_{x ar y}=- rac{ ar x}{4 ar y\sqrt L},\qquad \det (u_{j ar k})= rac{1-2|x|^2}{16|y|^2L}.  \] Since $u_{x ar x}>0$ and $\det (u_{j ar k})>0$, the complex Hessian is positive definite, so $u$ is plurisubharmonic off the axis $\{ y=0\} $ (proposition 8.2.2 (1)). Moreover $u<-\sqrt L/2$ is bounded above and tends to $-\infty $ at the axis. By theorem 8.4.1 , the plurisubharmonic extension across the axis takes the value $\varlimsup u=-\infty $ there, which is the displayed value; hence $u$ is plurisubharmonic on $U$. Off the axis, $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$ is the smooth measure with density a fixed positive multiple of $\det (u_{j ar k})$, by ( 9.2 ). The sets $O_ k=\{ u>-k\} $ are open, since $u$ is continuous as an extended-real function, and they increase to $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $; on $O_ k$ the truncation $\max \{ u,-k\} $ equals $u$, so $S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$. Take $K=\{ |x|^2\leq 1/4,\  |y|\leq r\} $ with $0<r<\mathrm e^{-1}$. On $K$ we have $1-2|x|^2\geq 1/2$, and polar coordinates in $y$ give \[  \int _{|y|\leq r} rac{\mathrm dA(y)}{|y|^2L}=2\pi \int _0^ r rac{\mathrm dt}{t(-\log t)}=\infty .  \] Hence $\sup _ k\int _ KS_ k=\int _{K\setminus \{ y=0\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2=\infty $, and ( 15.1 ) fails. Thus the non-pluripolar product of an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function need not be locally finite.

title: Lemma 15.1.1
text: Lemma 15.1.1 . Let $R$ be a positive current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on an open set $W\subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $E\subset W$ be a Borel set. Then the current $\mathbf1_ ER$, obtained by multiplying the coefficient measures of $R$ by $\mathbf1_ E$, is positive. If $R$ is strongly positive, that is, $R(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every test form $\varphi $ that is weakly positive at every point, then so is $\mathbf1_ ER$. Proof. By theorem 7.2.5 , $R$ has measure coefficients. Let $\varphi $ be a test form of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$ that is strongly positive, respectively weakly positive, at every point. The complex measure $R\wedge \varphi $, whose integral against a test function $\chi $ is $R(\chi \varphi )$, defines a positive distribution, because $\chi \varphi $ has the same positivity as $\varphi $ whenever $\chi \geq 0$; by the uniqueness in theorem 1.4.5 , it is a positive measure. Hence $(\mathbf1_ ER)(\varphi )=(R\wedge \varphi )(E)\geq 0$. $\square$

title: Lemma 15.1.2
text: Lemma 15.1.2 . For $l\geq k$ the current $S_ l-S_ k$ is positive, and $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. The currents $S_ k$ converge weakly to a positive current $S$ if and only if 15.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-local-mass-condition} \sup _ k\int _ K S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}<\infty \quad \text{for every compact set }K\subset U, \end{equation} where $\beta $ is the Euclidean Kähler form ( 7.4 ) of the coordinates. In that case $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$ for every $k$, the coefficient measures of $S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ in total variation on compact subsets of $U$, and the trace measure of $S$ is the measure $\mu $ above. Every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero for $\mu $ and for the total variations of the coefficient measures of $S$; consequently every plurifine open subset of $U$ is measurable for the completions of these measures. Moreover, if $E_ k\subset O_ k$ are Borel sets such that $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ almost everywhere for the trace measure of $S$, then the coefficient measures of $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ when integrated against any bounded Borel function with compact support in $U$. This is the case, in particular, if the sets $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus \bigcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Proof. Let $l\geq k$. By proposition 10.4.4 , the level-$l$ and level-$k$ Bedford–Taylor products have the same restriction to $O_ k$; since $O_ k\subset O_ l$, this is the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. Consequently $S_ l-S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ l\setminus O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,l}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,l}$, and this current is positive by lemma 15.1.1 . Suppose that ( 15.1 ) holds. The trace measures $S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and, by ( 15.1 ), converge to a locally finite measure. Hence the trace mass of the positive current $S_ l-S_ k$ on a compact set $K$ tends to zero as $k,l\to \infty $. By theorem 7.2.5 , the total variation on $K$ of each coefficient measure of $S_ l-S_ k$ is at most a fixed multiple of this trace mass. Therefore each coefficient measure of $S_ k$ is a Cauchy sequence in total variation on compact sets, and the limits are the coefficients of a current $S$, which is positive as a weak limit of positive currents. Conversely, suppose that $S_ k\to S$ weakly for a positive current $S$. For every smooth compactly supported $\chi \geq 0$, the numbers $\int \chi S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and converge to $\int \chi S\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$, which therefore bounds them; choosing $\chi =1$ on $K$ gives ( 15.1 ). Assume now that ( 15.1 ) holds. Letting $l\to \infty $ in $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ gives $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$. By the convergence in total variation, the trace measure of $S$ is the increasing limit of the trace measures of the $S_ k$, which is $\mu $. By proposition 10.4.4 , every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer $\mu $-measure zero. The total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is at most $C_{n,p}\mu $ (theorem 7.2.5 ), so pluripolar sets have outer measure zero for these total variations as well, and theorem 10.4.1 (2), applied to $\mu $ and to these total variations, shows that plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for their completions. In particular $S$ vanishes on $U\setminus \bigcup _ kO_ k$, the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, which is a pluripolar Borel set. Finally, let $E_ k$ be as in the statement. Since $E_ k\subset O_ k$, we have $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k=\mathbf1_{E_ k}S$. By theorem 7.2.5 , the total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is locally finite and absolutely continuous with respect to the trace measure. Hence $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ almost everywhere for each of these variations, and dominated convergence proves the assertion. If the $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus \bigcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar, then $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ outside this pluripolar Borel set, which $S$ does not charge. $\square$
15.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-local-mass-condition} \sup _ k\int _ K S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}<\infty \quad \text{for every compact set }K\subset U, \end{equation}

title: Definition 15.1.3
text: Definition 15.1.3 . If ( 15.1 ) holds, we say that the non-pluripolar product of $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite , and we call the limit $S$ of lemma 15.1.2 the non-pluripolar product \[  \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p\rangle =S.  \] The angle brackets distinguish this construction from a product that retains mass on pluripolar sets. The empty product ($p=0$) is $1$.

title: Proposition 15.1.4
text: Proposition 15.1.4 . Every locally finite non-pluripolar product $S$ is strongly positive: $S(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every compactly supported smooth weakly positive form $\varphi $ of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$. Proof. First let all potentials be locally bounded. Near each point they are limits of decreasing sequences of smooth plurisubharmonic functions, for instance of their mollifications (proposition 8.2.2 (2)). The complex Hessians of these functions are semipositive $(1,1)$-forms (proposition 8.2.2 (1)), hence strongly positive, since the two notions of positivity coincide in bidegree $(1,1)$; by proposition 7.2.1 , their exterior products are strongly positive, and the product of such a product with a weakly positive form of complementary bidegree is a nonnegative multiple of the volume form. Thus the smooth products pair nonnegatively with every smooth compactly supported weakly positive form. By theorem 9.2.5 , the Bedford–Taylor product is their weak limit, and therefore it pairs nonnegatively with these forms as well. By lemma 15.1.1 , applied to the bounded products in the definition of $S_ k$, every $S_ k$ is strongly positive. Since $S_ k\to S$ weakly by lemma 15.1.2 , so is $S$. $\square$

title: Proposition 15.1.5
text: Proposition 15.1.5 . Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ and $v_1,\ldots ,v_ p$ be plurisubharmonic on $U$. If $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$, then the non-pluripolar product of the $u_ j$ is locally finite if and only if that of the $v_ j$ is, and then the two products are equal; thus local finiteness and the product depend only on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. The product is symmetric in its factors and local in the plurifine topology: if $u_ j=v_ j$ on a plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$ and both products are locally finite, then they have the same restriction to $O$. Proof. In this proof we write $P^{(m)}(w_1,\ldots ,w_ p)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_1,-m\} \wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_ p,-m\} $ for plurisubharmonic $w_1,\ldots ,w_ p$ and an integer $m\geq 1$. Symmetry and locality. Each truncated product $S_ k$ is symmetric in its factors, hence so is the limit. Suppose that $u_ j=v_ j$ on the plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$, and that both products are locally finite. By lemma 15.1.2 , plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for the completions of the total variations of the coefficient measures of both products, so the restrictions of the products to $O$ and to the plurifine open sets $W_ k=O\cap \bigcap _ j\{ u_ j>-k\} =O\cap \bigcap _ j\{ v_ j>-k\} $ are well defined; the sets $W_ k$ increase with $k$. On $W_ k$ the truncations $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ coincide, so the two level-$k$ products agree on $W_ k$ by theorem 10.4.3 . Since $W_ k$ is contained in the level-$k$ sets of both tuples, lemma 15.1.2 shows that the two non-pluripolar products also agree on $W_ k$. The union of the $W_ k$ is $O$ minus the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, a pluripolar set, which has outer measure zero for these total variations by the same lemma. Letting $k\to \infty $, we conclude that the two products have the same restriction to $O$. Dependence on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. Suppose that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$. The distribution $v_ j-u_ j$ then has zero Laplacian, so by Weyl's lemma (theorem 2.1.4 ) it is a smooth function $w_ j$, and its complex Hessian vanishes: $w_ j$ is pluriharmonic. Fix a relatively compact open set $V\subset U$ and an integer $C$ such that $|w_ j|\leq C$ on $V$ for all $j$. Write $O_ k(u),S_ k(u)$ and $O_ k(v),S_ k(v)$ for the level sets and truncated products of the two tuples. On $V\cap O_ k(v)$ we have $u_ j=v_ j-w_ j>-k-C$, hence \[  \max \{ v_ j,-k\} =v_ j=\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j .  \] The functions $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j$ are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $V$ and coincide on $V\cap O_ k(v)$. As $V\cap O_ k(v)\subset O_{k+C}(u)$, plurifine locality gives on $V$ \[  S_ k(v)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}P^{(k+C)}(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}S_{k+C}(u)\leq S_{k+C}(u).  \] Thus ( 15.1 ) for the $u_ j$ implies ( 15.1 ) for the $v_ j$ on compact subsets of $V$, and exchanging the two tuples (that is, replacing $w_ j$ by $-w_ j$) gives the converse. If both products are locally finite, the display and lemma 15.1.2 give $\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ p\rangle =\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p\rangle $ on $V$ for every $k$. The sets $O_ k(v)$ exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets, which are the same for the two tuples and carry no mass for either product. Hence the two products coincide. Additivity. Let $u_1'$ be plurisubharmonic and put \[  E_ k=\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ u_1'>-k\}  \cap \bigcap _{j=2}^ p\{ u_ j>-k\} .  \] These plurifine open sets increase with $k$ and exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets of $u_1,u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$. On $E_ k$ we have $\max \{ u_1+u_1',-2k\} =u_1+u_1'=\max \{ u_1,-k\} +\max \{ u_1',-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-2k\} =\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ for $j\geq 2$. Plurifine locality and the additivity of bounded products (proposition 9.1.2 ) therefore give 15.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-additivity-on-levels} \begin{aligned}  \mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(2k)}(u_1+u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p) & =\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p)\\ & \quad +\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Before local finiteness is known we argue with trace measures. By proposition 10.4.4 , for each of the three tuples the trace measures of the truncated products increase to a Borel measure, possibly infinite on compact sets, for which every pluripolar set has outer measure zero; for a locally finite product it is the trace measure of the product. The set $E_ k$ is contained in the level-$2k$ set of the first tuple and in the level-$k$ sets of the other two, so by the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ of lemma 15.1.2 , the restriction of each limit measure to $E_ k$ is the restriction of the corresponding trace measure in ( 15.4 ). Hence, on $E_ k$, the limit measure of the first tuple is the sum of those of the other two. Letting $k\to \infty $, monotone convergence gives this equality on every Borel subset of $\bigcup _ kE_ k$, and hence everywhere, because the complement of $\bigcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. When the products are locally finite, ( 15.4 ) and lemma 15.1.2 give the additivity identity on each $E_ k$, and letting $k\to \infty $ proves it. For $c>0$ the same argument applies to the sets $\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ cu_1>-k\} \cap \bigcap _{j\geq 2}\{ u_ j>-k\} $, on which $\max \{ cu_1,-k\} =c\max \{ u_1,-k\} $, and proves the homogeneity assertion. $\square$

title: Example 15.1.6
text: Example 15.1.6 . Let $U=\{ (x,y)\in \mathbb C^2:|x|^2<1/2,\  |y|<\mathrm e^{-1}\} $, put $L=-\log |y|$, and define \[  u(x,y)=(|x|^2-1)\sqrt L\quad (y\ne 0),\qquad u(x,0)=-\infty .  \] On $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $ we have $L>1$, the function $u$ is smooth, and its complex second derivatives are \[  u_{x\bar x}=\sqrt L,\qquad u_{y\bar y}=\frac{1-|x|^2}{16|y|^2L^{3/2}},\qquad u_{x\bar y}=-\frac{\bar x}{4\bar y\sqrt L},\qquad \det (u_{j\bar k})=\frac{1-2|x|^2}{16|y|^2L}.  \] Since $u_{x\bar x}>0$ and $\det (u_{j\bar k})>0$, the complex Hessian is positive definite, so $u$ is plurisubharmonic off the axis $\{ y=0\} $ (proposition 8.2.2 (1)). Moreover $u<-\sqrt L/2$ is bounded above and tends to $-\infty $ at the axis. By theorem 8.4.1 , the plurisubharmonic extension across the axis takes the value $\varlimsup u=-\infty $ there, which is the displayed value; hence $u$ is plurisubharmonic on $U$. Off the axis, $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$ is the smooth measure with density a fixed positive multiple of $\det (u_{j\bar k})$, by ( 9.2 ). The sets $O_ k=\{ u>-k\} $ are open, since $u$ is continuous as an extended-real function, and they increase to $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $; on $O_ k$ the truncation $\max \{ u,-k\} $ equals $u$, so $S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$. Take $K=\{ |x|^2\leq 1/4,\  |y|\leq r\} $ with $0<r<\mathrm e^{-1}$. On $K$ we have $1-2|x|^2\geq 1/2$, and polar coordinates in $y$ give \[  \int _{|y|\leq r}\frac{\mathrm dA(y)}{|y|^2L}=2\pi \int _0^ r\frac{\mathrm dt}{t(-\log t)}=\infty .  \] Hence $\sup _ k\int _ KS_ k=\int _{K\setminus \{ y=0\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2=\infty $, and ( 15.1 ) fails. Thus the non-pluripolar product of an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function need not be locally finite.

title: 15.2 Closedness and cutoff gradients
text: 15.2 Closedness and cutoff gradients The indicators $\mathbf1_{O_ k}$ cannot be differentiated, so closedness of the non-pluripolar product does not follow directly from closedness of the truncated products. We replace the indicators by bounded plurisubharmonic cutoff functions and control the resulting error with the gradient estimates of section 9.13 . Here $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ is the real operator of ( 7.6 ), so that $\mathrm d\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$. Theorem 15.2.1 . Every locally finite non-pluripolar product is closed. Proof. Closedness is a local property, so we may shrink $U$ and subtract constants to assume that $u_ j\leq 0$ for every $j$. If $p=n$ the product has top degree and is closed for degree reasons, so let $p<n$. Fix a constant strongly positive $(n-p-1,n-p-1)$-form $\gamma $ and put \[  \Theta _ k=\gamma \wedge \bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j,k},\qquad S_\gamma =\gamma \wedge \Bigl \langle \bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\Bigr \rangle .  \] The $\Theta _ k$ are closed positive currents of bidimension $(1,1)$. By lemma 15.1.2 , $\mathbf1_{O_ k}\Theta _ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_\gamma $ increases to $S_\gamma $, and in particular these restrictions have uniformly bounded mass on compact sets. We shall prove that $\mathrm dS_\gamma =0$. Cutoff functions. Put $u=\sum _ ju_ j\leq 0$ and $w_ k=\max \{ 1+u/k,0\} $. By proposition 8.2.5 , $w_ k$ is plurisubharmonic, and $0\leq w_ k\leq 1$. As $k\to \infty $, $w_ k$ increases to $1$ at every point where $u>-\infty $, because $u/k$ increases to $0$ there, while $w_ k=0$ on the pole set of $u$. Moreover $w_ k=0$ outside $O_ k$: if $u_ j\leq -k$ for some $j$, then $u\leq u_ j\leq -k$, since all $u_ i\leq 0$. Choose a smooth function $\zeta $ on $\mathbb R$ with $0\leq \zeta \leq 1$, $\zeta =0$ on $(-\infty ,1/2]$ and $\zeta =1$ near $1$. Then $\zeta (w_ k)$ and $\zeta '(w_ k)$ vanish outside $O_ k$, so that $\zeta (w_ k)\Theta _ k=\zeta (w_ k)S_\gamma $. At every point where $u>-\infty $ we have $\zeta (w_ k)\to 1$ and $\zeta '(w_ k)\to 0$, and $S_\gamma $ gives the pole set of $u$ zero mass. Dominated convergence therefore gives \[  \zeta (w_ k)\Theta _ k\longrightarrow S_\gamma , \qquad \zeta '(w_ k)\longrightarrow 0 \quad S_\gamma \text{-almost everywhere}.  \] Gradient bound. Let $\eta $ be a compactly supported smooth real one-form, and let $\tau \geq 0$ be a smooth compactly supported function equal to one near $\operatorname{Supp}\eta $. By ( 9.84 ), the gradient measure of $w_ k$ with respect to $\Theta _ k$ is $E_{\Theta _ k}(w_ k)=\frac12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w_ k^2\Theta _ k)-w_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ k\wedge \Theta _ k$, and the last term is a positive measure because $w_ k\geq 0$. Hence \[  \int \tau E_{\Theta _ k}(w_ k) \leq \tfrac 12\int w_ k^2\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\tau \wedge \Theta _ k \leq C\int _{\operatorname{Supp}\tau } \mathbf1_{O_ k}\Theta _ k\wedge \beta \leq C'.  \] The second inequality uses $w_ k=0$ outside $O_ k$, $w_ k\leq 1$, and the bound of the coefficients of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\tau \wedge \Theta _ k$ by a constant times the trace measure (theorem 7.2.5 ). The constant $C'$ is independent of $k$ because $\mathbf1_{O_ k}\Theta _ k\leq S_\gamma $ and $S_\gamma $ is locally finite. Conclusion. By the chain rule ( 9.85 ), $\mathrm d(\zeta (w_ k)\Theta _ k)=\zeta '(w_ k)\, \mathrm dw_ k\wedge \Theta _ k$. We apply ( 9.86 ) with $a=\zeta '(w_ k)$. The constant $C_\eta $ there depends only on $\eta $, so it is the same for every $k$. The first factor on the right is bounded by the gradient bound, and the second tends to zero, since \[  |\zeta '(w_ k)|^2\Theta _ k\wedge \beta =|\zeta '(w_ k)|^2\mathbf1_{O_ k}\Theta _ k\wedge \beta \leq |\zeta '(w_ k)|^2 S_\gamma \wedge \beta  \] and the right side tends to zero on $\operatorname{Supp}\eta $ by dominated convergence. Hence the pairing of $\mathrm d(\zeta (w_ k)\Theta _ k)$ with $\eta $ tends to zero. Since $\zeta (w_ k)\Theta _ k\to S_\gamma $, the pairing of $\mathrm dS_\gamma $ with $\eta $ vanishes, so $\mathrm dS_\gamma =0$. Finally, $\gamma \wedge \mathrm d\langle \bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\rangle =\mathrm dS_\gamma =0$ for every constant strongly positive $\gamma $. These forms span the constant real $(n-p-1,n-p-1)$-forms (proposition 7.2.1 ), and their products with smooth functions and the coordinate one-forms $\mathrm dz_ i,\mathrm d\bar z_ i$ span the test forms of the two bidegrees against which $\mathrm d\langle \bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\rangle $ is evaluated. Therefore the non-pluripolar product is closed. $\square$
