The assertion is local, so we may work on a polydisc $P$ such that $u\leq 0$ is plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline P$. Fix one of the coordinates, denote it by $x$, and write $z\in \mathbb C^{n-1}$ for the others, so that $P=\Delta 	imes Z$ with a disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb C$ and a polydisc $Z\subset \mathbb C^{n-1}$. Let $\mathrm dV_ z$ be the Euclidean volume form of the $z$-coordinates, viewed as an $(n-1,n-1)$-form, and $\mathrm dA$ the area measure on $\Delta $. We disintegrate $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z$ along the fibers $\Delta 	imes \{ z\} $ and apply the one-variable case on each fiber. Since $u$ is integrable on $\Delta 	imes Z$, Fubini's theorem (proposition 1.1.7 ) shows that $G=\{ z\in Z:\int _\Delta |u(x,z)|\, \mathrm dA(x)<\infty \} $ is a Borel set of full measure in $Z$. For $z\in G$ the function $u_ z=u(\, \cdot \, ,z)$ is integrable, hence not identically $-\infty $, so it is subharmonic on $\Delta $ by proposition 8.2.3 ; let $\mu _ z=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ xu_ z$ be its Hessian measure. For a test function $a$ on $\Delta $, we have $\int a\, \mathrm d\mu _ z=\int _\Delta u_ z\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ xa$, and Fubini's theorem, applied to the positive and negative parts of the integrand, shows that this is a Borel function of $z\in G$. Uniform approximation by test functions supported in a fixed compact set extends this to continuous functions $a$ with compact support, since each $\mu _ z$ is finite on compact sets. Hence lemma 15.3.4 , with $f=1$, gives a measure $\lambda $ on $\Delta 	imes Z$ with $\int h\, \mathrm d\lambda =\int _ G(\int h(\, \cdot \, ,z)\, \mathrm d\mu _ z)\, \mathrm dV(z)$ for nonnegative Borel $h$. If $\chi \in C_ c^\infty (\Delta )$ satisfies $0\leq \chi \leq 1$ and equals one on a disc $\Delta '\Subset \Delta $, then $\mu _ z(\Delta ')\leq \int u_ z\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x\chi \leq C_\chi \int _\Delta |u_ z|\, \mathrm dA$, which is integrable over $G$; so $\lambda $ is finite on compact sets. For a test function $\varphi $ on $\Delta 	imes Z$, only the derivative $\partial _ x\partial _{ ar x}\varphi $ survives in $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \mathrm dV_ z$, and Fubini's theorem gives \[  \int \varphi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\int u\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\int _ G\Bigl (\int _\Delta u_ z\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x\varphi (\, \cdot \, ,z)\Bigr )\mathrm dV(z)=\int \varphi \, \mathrm d\lambda .  \] By the uniqueness in theorem 1.4.5 , the positive measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z$ equals $\lambda $, that is, 15.12  egin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-fibre-disintegration} \int g\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\int _ G\Bigl (\int g(\, \cdot \, ,z)\, \mathrm d\mu _ z\Bigr )\mathrm dV(z) \end{equation} for every nonnegative Borel function $g$ on $\Delta 	imes Z$. Now let $g\geq 0$ be a bounded Borel function with compact support in $\Delta 	imes Z$, and apply lemma 15.3.5 , with $r=1$, $Q=\Delta $, $D=Z$ and $\eta =\mathrm dV_ z$, to the bounded function $u_ k=\max \{ u,-k\} $ and the weight $g\mathbf1_{\{ u>-k\} }$: \[  \int g\mathbf1_{\{ u>-k\} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k\wedge \mathrm dV_ z =\int \Bigl (\int g\mathbf1_{\{ u_ z>-k\} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ x\max \{ u_ z,-k\} \Bigr )\mathrm dV_ z.  \] As $k	o \infty $, the left side increases to $\int gS\wedge \mathrm dV_ z$ by lemma 15.1.2 , since $\mathbf1_{\{ u>-k\} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ is the truncated product $S_ k$ of $u$. For $z\in G$, the inner integral on the right is the integral of $g(\, \cdot \, ,z)$ against the truncated product of $u_ z$ at level $k$; by lemma 15.1.2 and the one-variable case, it increases to $\int g\, \mathrm d\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}_ xu_ zangle =\int g\mathbf1_{\{ u_ z>-\infty \} }\, \mathrm d\mu _ z$. Since $Z\setminus G$ is a null set, monotone convergence in $z$ and ( 15.12 ), applied to $g\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }$, give $\int gS\wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\int g\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z$, so that $S\wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z$. Since $ eta ^{n-1}=(n-1)!\sum _{j=1}^ n\mathrm dV_{(j)}$, where $\mathrm dV_{(j)}$ is the volume form of the coordinates other than the $j$th, summing over the $n$ coordinate directions shows that the trace measures of $S$ and of $\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ coincide. Thus $\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u-S$ is a positive current with zero trace measure, and it vanishes by theorem 7.2.5 . This proves ( 15.11 ); closedness follows from theorem 15.2.1 . $\square$
15.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:nonpluripolar-degree-one-restriction} \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\rangle =\mathbf1_{\{ u>-\infty \} }\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u, \end{equation}

15.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-fibre-disintegration} \int g\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \mathrm dV_ z=\int _ G\Bigl (\int g(\, \cdot \, ,z)\, \mathrm d\mu _ z\Bigr )\mathrm dV(z) \end{equation}

title: Proposition 15.3.7
text: Proposition 15.3.7 . Let $\mu $ be a probability measure supported on a compact set $K\subset \mathbb C\subset \mathbb P^1$, and let $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$ be the Fubini–Study form of example 14.5.6 , which has total mass one on $\mathbb P^1$. Then \[  q(z)=\int _ K\log \frac{|z-a|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|a|^2)}\, \mathrm d\mu (a)  \] defines a nonpositive $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$-plurisubharmonic function on $\mathbb P^1$ with $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=\mu $. Its Lelong number at every point $x\in \mathbb P^1$ is $\mu (\{ x\} )$, where $\mu $ is regarded as a measure on $\mathbb P^1$. Proof. In the affine chart put $\rho (z)=\log (1+|z|^2)$, so that $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho $. The integrand is nonpositive, since $|z-a|^2\leq (|z|+|a|)^2\leq (1+|z|^2)(1+|a|^2)$ by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. On the affine chart, \[  q+\rho =p_\mu -c,\qquad p_\mu (z)=\int _ K\log |z-a|^2\, \mathrm d\mu (a),\qquad c=\int _ K\log (1+|a|^2)\, \mathrm d\mu (a).  \] Since $\log |z-a|^2=4\pi E_2(z-a)$ with the fundamental solution $E_2$ of ( 2.9 ), the function $p_\mu =4\pi E_2*\mu $ is subharmonic and locally integrable with $\Delta p_\mu =4\pi \mu $, by proposition 3.2.1 . Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}=\Delta /(4\pi )$ on functions of one complex variable, as planar measures, this gives $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_\mu =\mu $ on the affine chart, and $q=p_\mu -c-\rho $ is quasi-plurisubharmonic there. Near infinity use the coordinate $w=1/z$, in which the integrand becomes \[  \log |1-aw|^2-\log (1+|w|^2)-\log (1+|a|^2).  \] Let $R_ K=\max _{a\in K}|a|$. For $|w|<1/(2R_ K+2)$ we have $|1-aw|\geq 1/2$, so this expression is a smooth function of $(a,w)$ on $K\times \{ |w|<1/(2R_ K+2)\} $ whose derivatives in $w$ of every order are bounded uniformly in $a\in K$; at $w=0$ it takes the value $-\log (1+|a|^2)$. Differentiating under the integral sign, we see that $q$ extends to a smooth function near infinity, and that $q+\log (1+|w|^2)=\int _ K\log |1-aw|^2\, \mathrm d\mu (a)-c$ is harmonic there, because each $\log |1-aw|^2$ is harmonic in $w$. Since $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log (1+|w|^2)$ in this chart and $\mu $ vanishes near infinity, $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=0=\mu $ there. Hence $q$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on $\mathbb P^1$, $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=\mu \geq 0$ globally, and $q$ is a nonpositive $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$-plurisubharmonic function. At infinity both the Lelong number and the point mass vanish, because $q$ is smooth there and $K\subset \mathbb C$. At an affine point $x$, the Lelong number of $q$ is that of the local subharmonic function $q+\rho $ (corollary 12.3.2 ), and by ( 12.5 ) and ( 12.3 ) it equals $\lim _{r\downarrow 0}\mu (B(x,r))=\mu (\{ x\} )$. $\square$

title: Example 15.3.8
text: Example 15.3.8 . Let $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$ be the Fubini–Study form on $\mathbb P^1$, as in proposition 15.3.7 . There is a nonpositive $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$-plurisubharmonic function $q$ on $\mathbb P^1$ such that \[  \nu (q,x)=0\quad \text{for every }x,\qquad \mathcal I(tq)=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\quad (t>0),\qquad \langle \omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\rangle =0.  \] Let $\mu $ be the atom-free probability measure on the compact polar set $K$ of proposition 4.2.4 , and let $q$ be its potential from proposition 15.3.7 . Since $\mu $ has no atoms, all Lelong numbers of $q$ vanish, and corollary 12.3.2 gives the assertion on multiplier ideals. On the affine chart, $q$ differs from the function $p(z)=\int _ K\log |z-a|^2\, \mathrm d\mu (a)$ of proposition 4.2.4 by the smooth function $-\log (1+|z|^2)$ and a constant, and $p=-\infty $ on $K$; hence $q=-\infty $ on $K$. Applying proposition 15.3.6 to local potentials of $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q$, we obtain \[  \langle \omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\rangle =\mathbf1_{\{ q>-\infty \} }\mu =0,  \] because $\mu $ is carried by $K$. By contrast, the potential $0$ has the same multiplier ideals and non-pluripolar mass one. Thus exponential integrability at every scale does not determine the non-pluripolar mass.

title: 15.4 Global finiteness and bounded cohomological mass
search_title: Global finiteness and bounded cohomological mass
text: 15.4 Global finiteness and bounded cohomological mass From now on, $X$ is a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$ with a fixed Kähler form $\omega $, and $\theta $ and $\theta _ j$ always denote smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. (We exclude dimension zero, where the only product is the empty one.) If $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ (definition 13.1.3 ) is locally bounded, then near each point $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(h+\varphi )$, where $h$ is a smooth local potential of $\theta $ and $h+\varphi $ is bounded and plurisubharmonic. By proposition 15.1.5 , the Bedford–Taylor products of such local potentials do not depend on the choice of $h$; hence they glue to closed positive currents $\bigwedge _ j(\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)$ on $X$, which can be multiplied by smooth forms. We first prove Stokes' formula for these products and then show that non-pluripolar products on $X$ are always finite. Proposition 15.4.1 . Let $1\leq p\leq n$, let $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ be locally bounded for $1\leq j\leq p$, and let $\eta $ be a smooth closed $(n-p,n-p)$-form on $X$. Then \[  \int _ X\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p(\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge \eta =\int _ X\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _ p\wedge \eta .  \] Proof. Fix $j$, let $R$ be the closed positive current $\bigwedge _{i>j}(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)$, and let $\eta '$ be a smooth closed form of pure complementary bidegree. Locally $\theta _ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j$ with $h_ j$ smooth, and since $R$ is closed, the recursion gives \[  (\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}((h_ j+\varphi _ j)R)=\theta _ j\wedge R+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ jR).  \] Here $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(h_ jR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j\wedge R$ because $h_ j$ is smooth and $R$ is closed of pure bidegree, so that $\partial R=\bar\partial R=0$. Both sides are globally defined, because $\varphi _ j$ is a global bounded function. Moreover $\int _ X\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ jR)\wedge \eta '=\int _ X\varphi _ jR\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta '=0$, since $\eta '$ is closed of pure bidegree, so that $\partial \eta '=\bar\partial \eta '=0$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta '=0$. Hence $\int _ X(\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge R\wedge \eta '=\int _ X\theta _ j\wedge R\wedge \eta '$. Apply this successively for $j=1,2,\ldots ,p$, with $\eta '=\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j-1}\wedge \eta $ at the $j$th step, which is smooth and closed. After $p$ steps the integral becomes $\int _ X\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _ p\wedge \eta $. $\square$ Lemma 15.4.2 . Let $R$ be a closed positive current of bidimension $(1,1)$ on $X$, and let $a,b$ be bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, or differences of such functions. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(aR)$ are finite signed measures, and \[  \int _ X a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R =\int _ X b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R =-\int _ X\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R.  \] Here the mixed gradient \[  \mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R=\tfrac 12\bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)-a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R-b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R\bigr )  \] is a finite signed measure on $X$, symmetric in $a$ and $b$. It is the exterior product of $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b$ with $R$ when $a$ and $b$ are smooth, and on an open set where $a=b$ is plurisubharmonic it is the gradient measure $E_ R(a)$ of ( 9.84 ). Proof. The measures. Near each point of $X$, a bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic function $b$ is the difference $b_1-b_2$ of two bounded plurisubharmonic functions: if $b+g$ is plurisubharmonic on a coordinate ball with $g$ smooth, and $q=C|z|^2$ with $C$ so large that $g+q$ is plurisubharmonic on a smaller ball, take $b_1=b+g+q$ and $b_2=g+q$. Hence $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_1\wedge R-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_2\wedge R$ is locally the difference of two Bedford–Taylor products, which are positive measures. Covering the compact manifold $X$ by finitely many such neighborhoods, we see that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ is a finite signed measure; the same holds for $a$. For bounded plurisubharmonic functions $A$ and $B$ on an open set, additivity of Bedford–Taylor products (proposition 9.1.2 ) and the formula ( 9.84 ) give, after expanding $(A+B)^2$, \[  E_ R(A+B)=E_ R(A)+E_ R(B)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ABR)-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}B\wedge R-B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R,  \] so that $\frac12(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ABR)-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}B\wedge R-B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R)=\frac12(E_ R(A+B)-E_ R(A)-E_ R(B))$ is a signed measure, by lemma 9.13.1 . Since the expression defining the mixed gradient is bilinear in $(a,b)$, writing $a=a_1-a_2$ and $b=b_1-b_2$ locally shows that the mixed gradient is a signed measure near each point, hence a finite signed measure on $X$. It is symmetric by definition. For $a=b$ plurisubharmonic it equals $\frac12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a^2R)-a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=E_ R(a)$. For smooth $a$ and $b$ we have $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ab)=a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b+b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a+\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b+\mathrm db\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a$, and the $(1,1)$-parts of $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b$ and $\mathrm db\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a$ both equal $\frac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }(\partial a\wedge \bar\partial b+\partial b\wedge \bar\partial a)$; since only $(1,1)$-parts contribute in products with $R$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ab)\wedge R$, the mixed gradient is $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R$. A local identity. Let $\chi $ be a test function with support in a coordinate ball $W$, and let $A$ and $B$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a neighborhood of $\overline W$. We claim that 15.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:local-symmetry-defect} \int \chi A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)-\int \chi B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(AR)=-\int AB\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge R-2\, \mathrm d(BR)(A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi ), \end{equation} where $\mathrm d(BR)$ is the current of order zero of lemma 9.13.1 and its value on the bounded Borel one-form $A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi $ with compact support is computed with its coefficient measures. Suppose first that $A$ is smooth. Then $\int \chi A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)=(BR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi A))$ and \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi A)=\chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A+A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi +\mathrm d\chi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}A+\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi .  \] The first term contributes $\int \chi B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R$. Since $BR$ has bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$, it sees only the $(1,1)$-parts of the last two terms, which agree as above; so these terms contribute $2(BR)(\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi )$. Finally $\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi =\mathrm d(A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi )-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $, and $(BR)(\mathrm d\psi )=-\mathrm d(BR)(\psi )$ for one-forms $\psi $, because $BR$ has even degree. Collecting terms gives ( 15.13 ). In general, let $A_ l$ be smooth plurisubharmonic functions decreasing to $A$ on a neighborhood of $\overline W$, for instance mollifications (proposition 8.2.2 (2)). Then ( 15.13 ) holds for $A_ l$, and every term converges to the corresponding term for $A$. For the first, third and last terms this follows by dominated convergence against the fixed signed measures $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge R$ and the coefficient measures of $\mathrm d(BR)$, since the $A_ l$ are uniformly bounded on $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $ and converge pointwise to $A$. For the second term it follows from the weighted form of theorem 9.2.5 , with the constant sequence of weights $B$. This proves the claim. Since both sides of ( 15.13 ) are bilinear in $(A,B)$, the identity also holds for differences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and in particular for $A=a$ and $B=b$ near $\overline W$. Conclusion. Let $(\chi _ i)$ be a finite smooth partition of unity on $X$ subordinate to coordinate balls as above (proposition 7.1.3 ). Summing ( 15.13 ) for $\chi =\chi _ i$, $A=a$ and $B=b$ over $i$, and using that $abR$, $\mathrm d(bR)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(aR)$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ are global currents, we obtain \[  \int _ Xa\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R-\int _ Xb\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=-\int _ Xab\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Bigl (\sum _ i\chi _ i\Bigr )\wedge R-2\, \mathrm d(bR)\Bigl (a\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\sum _ i\chi _ i\Bigr )=0,  \] because $\sum _ i\chi _ i=1$. This is the first equality. For the second, note that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)$ is a finite signed measure, being a combination of the mixed gradient and the measures $a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R$ and $b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R$, and that its total integral is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)(1)=(abR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}1)=0$, because the constant function $1$ is a test function on the compact manifold $X$. Integrating the definition of the mixed gradient over $X$ and using the first equality, we get $\int _ X\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R=-\int _ Xa\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R$. $\square$ Theorem 15.4.3 . Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$, $1\leq p\leq n$, be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on the compact Kähler manifold $X$. Then their non-pluripolar product is finite. More precisely, write $T_ j=\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$, and choose $C\geq 0$ such that the forms $\tau _ j=\theta _ j+C\omega $ are semipositive. Then 15.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:shifted-cohomological-mass-bound} \int _ X\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle \wedge \omega ^{n-p} \leq \int _ X\tau _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \tau _ p\wedge \omega ^{n-p}. \end{equation} In particular, if the forms $\theta _ j$ are semipositive, we may take $C=0$. Proof. The decomposition $T_ j=\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ exists by theorem 14.1.7 . Since $\tau _ j\geq \theta _ j$ and $\tau _ j\geq 0$, $\varphi _ j$ is $\tau _ j$-plurisubharmonic, and so is every constant; hence $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} $ is a bounded $\tau _ j$-plurisubharmonic function, and \[  R_{j,k}=\tau _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\}   \] is a closed positive current. By proposition 15.4.1 , the total mass $\int _ XR_{1,k}\wedge \cdots \wedge R_{p,k}\wedge \omega ^{n-p}$ equals the right side of ( 15.14 ) for every $k$. Local finiteness. Let $W$ be a relatively compact coordinate chart, and choose smooth functions $h_ j$ and $h$ near $\overline W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j=\theta _ j$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h=\omega $. Then $u_ j=\varphi _ j+h_ j$ is a plurisubharmonic potential of $T_ j$ on $W$. Let $B$ be an integer with $h_ j\leq B$ on $W$ for all $j$, fix an integer $l\geq 1$, and put $O_ l(u)=\bigcap _ j\{ u_ j>-l\} $. On $W\cap O_ l(u)$ we have $\varphi _ j>-l-B$, so for every integer $k\geq l+B$ the bounded plurisubharmonic functions $\max \{ u_ j,-l\} +Ch$ and $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} +h_ j+Ch$ both equal $u_ j+Ch$ there; the second is a local potential of $R_{j,k}$. By plurifine locality, \[  \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ u_ j,-l\} +C\omega )=\mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}\quad \text{on }W.  \] Expanding the left side into positive terms gives \[  \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ u_ j,-l\}  \leq \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j R_{j,k}\leq \bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}.  \] Let $K\subset W$ be compact. On a neighborhood of $K$ in $W$ we have $\beta \leq c\, \omega $ for some $c>0$ (lemma 13.1.1 ), so by the last display and ( 15.7 ), the trace masses on $K$ of the truncated local products are at most $c^{n-p}$ times the right side of ( 15.14 ), uniformly in $l$. Hence the non-pluripolar product is locally finite everywhere, and $\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle $ is a closed positive current by theorem 15.2.1 . Mass bound. By the same argument, the currents $T_ j+C\omega =\tau _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$, with local potentials $u_ j+Ch$, have a locally finite non-pluripolar product. The sets $G_ k=\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j>-k\} $ increase and exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets of the $\varphi _ j$. On $G_ k$ the global truncations $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} $ coincide with $\varphi _ j$. If $B'$ is an integer with $h_ j+Ch\geq -B'$ on $W$ for all $j$, then on $G_ k\cap W$ all local potentials satisfy $u_ j+Ch>-k-B'$, so they coincide there with their truncations at level $k+B'$, and also with the local potentials $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} +h_ j+Ch$ of $R_{j,k}$. By plurifine locality and lemma 15.1.2 , $\mathbf1_{G_ k}\bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}=\mathbf1_{G_ k}\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $, and these restrictions increase to $\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $. Their total masses against $\omega ^{n-p}$ are at most the right side of ( 15.14 ), hence so is that of the limit. Finally, expanding $\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $ by multilinearity (proposition 15.1.5 ) into a sum of positive currents, one of which is $\langle \bigwedge _ jT_ j\rangle $, we obtain $\langle \bigwedge _ j T_ j\rangle \leq \langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $, which proves ( 15.14 ). $\square$ Example 15.4.4 . On $\mathbb P^1$, the current of integration $[0]$ at the point $0$ satisfies $\langle [0]\rangle =0$. Indeed, near $0$ it has the potential $\log |z|^2$ (theorem 7.4.5 ), whose pole set is $\{ 0\} $, so $\langle [0]\rangle =\mathbf1_{\{ z\neq 0\} }[0]=0$ there by proposition 15.3.6 ; away from $0$ the current vanishes. Thus $[0]$ has mass one while $\langle [0]\rangle $ has mass zero: discarding the poles can change the cohomology class, even in degree one.

title: Proposition 15.4.1
text: Proposition 15.4.1 . Let $1\leq p\leq n$, let $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ be locally bounded for $1\leq j\leq p$, and let $\eta $ be a smooth closed $(n-p,n-p)$-form on $X$. Then \[  \int _ X\bigwedge _{j=1}^ p(\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge \eta =\int _ X\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _ p\wedge \eta .  \] Proof. Fix $j$, let $R$ be the closed positive current $\bigwedge _{i>j}(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)$, and let $\eta '$ be a smooth closed form of pure complementary bidegree. Locally $\theta _ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j$ with $h_ j$ smooth, and since $R$ is closed, the recursion gives \[  (\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}((h_ j+\varphi _ j)R)=\theta _ j\wedge R+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ jR).  \] Here $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(h_ jR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j\wedge R$ because $h_ j$ is smooth and $R$ is closed of pure bidegree, so that $\partial R=\bar\partial R=0$. Both sides are globally defined, because $\varphi _ j$ is a global bounded function. Moreover $\int _ X\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi _ jR)\wedge \eta '=\int _ X\varphi _ jR\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta '=0$, since $\eta '$ is closed of pure bidegree, so that $\partial \eta '=\bar\partial \eta '=0$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta '=0$. Hence $\int _ X(\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\wedge R\wedge \eta '=\int _ X\theta _ j\wedge R\wedge \eta '$. Apply this successively for $j=1,2,\ldots ,p$, with $\eta '=\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j-1}\wedge \eta $ at the $j$th step, which is smooth and closed. After $p$ steps the integral becomes $\int _ X\theta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _ p\wedge \eta $. $\square$

title: Lemma 15.4.2
text: Lemma 15.4.2 . Let $R$ be a closed positive current of bidimension $(1,1)$ on $X$, and let $a,b$ be bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, or differences of such functions. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(aR)$ are finite signed measures, and \[  \int _ X a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R =\int _ X b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R =-\int _ X\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R.  \] Here the mixed gradient \[  \mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R=\tfrac 12\bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)-a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R-b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R\bigr )  \] is a finite signed measure on $X$, symmetric in $a$ and $b$. It is the exterior product of $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b$ with $R$ when $a$ and $b$ are smooth, and on an open set where $a=b$ is plurisubharmonic it is the gradient measure $E_ R(a)$ of ( 9.84 ). Proof. The measures. Near each point of $X$, a bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic function $b$ is the difference $b_1-b_2$ of two bounded plurisubharmonic functions: if $b+g$ is plurisubharmonic on a coordinate ball with $g$ smooth, and $q=C|z|^2$ with $C$ so large that $g+q$ is plurisubharmonic on a smaller ball, take $b_1=b+g+q$ and $b_2=g+q$. Hence $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_1\wedge R-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_2\wedge R$ is locally the difference of two Bedford–Taylor products, which are positive measures. Covering the compact manifold $X$ by finitely many such neighborhoods, we see that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ is a finite signed measure; the same holds for $a$. For bounded plurisubharmonic functions $A$ and $B$ on an open set, additivity of Bedford–Taylor products (proposition 9.1.2 ) and the formula ( 9.84 ) give, after expanding $(A+B)^2$, \[  E_ R(A+B)=E_ R(A)+E_ R(B)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ABR)-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}B\wedge R-B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R,  \] so that $\frac12(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ABR)-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}B\wedge R-B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R)=\frac12(E_ R(A+B)-E_ R(A)-E_ R(B))$ is a signed measure, by lemma 9.13.1 . Since the expression defining the mixed gradient is bilinear in $(a,b)$, writing $a=a_1-a_2$ and $b=b_1-b_2$ locally shows that the mixed gradient is a signed measure near each point, hence a finite signed measure on $X$. It is symmetric by definition. For $a=b$ plurisubharmonic it equals $\frac12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a^2R)-a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=E_ R(a)$. For smooth $a$ and $b$ we have $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ab)=a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b+b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a+\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b+\mathrm db\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a$, and the $(1,1)$-parts of $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b$ and $\mathrm db\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a$ both equal $\frac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }(\partial a\wedge \bar\partial b+\partial b\wedge \bar\partial a)$; since only $(1,1)$-parts contribute in products with $R$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(ab)\wedge R$, the mixed gradient is $\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R$. A local identity. Let $\chi $ be a test function with support in a coordinate ball $W$, and let $A$ and $B$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a neighborhood of $\overline W$. We claim that 15.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:local-symmetry-defect} \int \chi A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)-\int \chi B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(AR)=-\int AB\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge R-2\, \mathrm d(BR)(A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi ), \end{equation} where $\mathrm d(BR)$ is the current of order zero of lemma 9.13.1 and its value on the bounded Borel one-form $A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi $ with compact support is computed with its coefficient measures. Suppose first that $A$ is smooth. Then $\int \chi A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)=(BR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi A))$ and \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi A)=\chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A+A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi +\mathrm d\chi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}A+\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi .  \] The first term contributes $\int \chi B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}A\wedge R$. Since $BR$ has bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$, it sees only the $(1,1)$-parts of the last two terms, which agree as above; so these terms contribute $2(BR)(\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi )$. Finally $\mathrm dA\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi =\mathrm d(A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi )-A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $, and $(BR)(\mathrm d\psi )=-\mathrm d(BR)(\psi )$ for one-forms $\psi $, because $BR$ has even degree. Collecting terms gives ( 15.13 ). In general, let $A_ l$ be smooth plurisubharmonic functions decreasing to $A$ on a neighborhood of $\overline W$, for instance mollifications (proposition 8.2.2 (2)). Then ( 15.13 ) holds for $A_ l$, and every term converges to the corresponding term for $A$. For the first, third and last terms this follows by dominated convergence against the fixed signed measures $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge R$ and the coefficient measures of $\mathrm d(BR)$, since the $A_ l$ are uniformly bounded on $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $ and converge pointwise to $A$. For the second term it follows from the weighted form of theorem 9.2.5 , with the constant sequence of weights $B$. This proves the claim. Since both sides of ( 15.13 ) are bilinear in $(A,B)$, the identity also holds for differences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and in particular for $A=a$ and $B=b$ near $\overline W$. Conclusion. Let $(\chi _ i)$ be a finite smooth partition of unity on $X$ subordinate to coordinate balls as above (proposition 7.1.3 ). Summing ( 15.13 ) for $\chi =\chi _ i$, $A=a$ and $B=b$ over $i$, and using that $abR$, $\mathrm d(bR)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(aR)$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(bR)$ are global currents, we obtain \[  \int _ Xa\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R-\int _ Xb\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R=-\int _ Xab\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Bigl (\sum _ i\chi _ i\Bigr )\wedge R-2\, \mathrm d(bR)\Bigl (a\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\sum _ i\chi _ i\Bigr )=0,  \] because $\sum _ i\chi _ i=1$. This is the first equality. For the second, note that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)$ is a finite signed measure, being a combination of the mixed gradient and the measures $a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R$ and $b\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\wedge R$, and that its total integral is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(abR)(1)=(abR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}1)=0$, because the constant function $1$ is a test function on the compact manifold $X$. Integrating the definition of the mixed gradient over $X$ and using the first equality, we get $\int _ X\mathrm da\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}b\wedge R=-\int _ Xa\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge R$. $\square$

15.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:local-symmetry-defect} \int \chi A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(BR)-\int \chi B\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(AR)=-\int AB\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge R-2\, \mathrm d(BR)(A\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi ), \end{equation}

title: Theorem 15.4.3
text: Theorem 15.4.3 . Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$, $1\leq p\leq n$, be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on the compact Kähler manifold $X$. Then their non-pluripolar product is finite. Let $W$ be a relatively compact coordinate chart, and choose smooth functions $h_ j$ and $h$ near $\overline W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ j=\theta _ j$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h=\omega $. By plurifine locality, \[  \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ u_ j,-l\} +C\omega )=\mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}\quad \text{on }W.  \] Expanding the left side into positive terms gives \[  \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ u_ j,-l\}  \leq \mathbf1_{O_ l(u)}\bigwedge _ j R_{j,k}\leq \bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}.  \] Let $K\subset W$ be compact. On a neighborhood of $K$ in $W$ we have $\beta \leq c\, \omega $ for some $c>0$ (lemma 13.1.1 ), so by the last display and ( 15.7 ), the trace masses on $K$ of the truncated local products are at most $c^{n-p}$ times the right side of ( 15.14 ), uniformly in $l$. Hence the non-pluripolar product is locally finite everywhere, and $\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle $ is a closed positive current by theorem 15.2.1 . Mass bound. By the same argument, the currents $T_ j+C\omega =\tau _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$, with local potentials $u_ j+Ch$, have a locally finite non-pluripolar product. The sets $G_ k=\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j>-k\} $ increase and exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets of the $\varphi _ j$. On $G_ k$ the global truncations $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} $ coincide with $\varphi _ j$. If $B'$ is an integer with $h_ j+Ch\geq -B'$ on $W$ for all $j$, then on $G_ k\cap W$ all local potentials satisfy $u_ j+Ch>-k-B'$, so they coincide there with their truncations at level $k+B'$, and also with the local potentials $\max \{ \varphi _ j,-k\} +h_ j+Ch$ of $R_{j,k}$. By plurifine locality and lemma 15.1.2 , $\mathbf1_{G_ k}\bigwedge _ jR_{j,k}=\mathbf1_{G_ k}\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $, and these restrictions increase to $\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $. Their total masses against $\omega ^{n-p}$ are at most the right side of ( 15.14 ), hence so is that of the limit. Finally, expanding $\langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $ by multilinearity (proposition 15.1.5 ) into a sum of positive currents, one of which is $\langle \bigwedge _ jT_ j\rangle $, we obtain $\langle \bigwedge _ j T_ j\rangle \leq \langle \bigwedge _ j(T_ j+C\omega )\rangle $, which proves ( 15.14 ). $\square$

15.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:shifted-cohomological-mass-bound} \int _ X\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle \wedge \omega ^{n-p} \leq \int _ X\tau _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \tau _ p\wedge \omega ^{n-p}. \end{equation}

title: Example 15.4.4
text: Example 15.4.4 . On $\mathbb P^1$, the current of integration $[0]$ at the point $0$ satisfies $\langle [0]\rangle =0$. Indeed, near $0$ it has the potential $\log |z|^2$ (theorem 7.4.5 ), whose pole set is $\{ 0\} $, so $\langle [0]\rangle =\mathbf1_{\{ z\neq 0\} }[0]=0$ there by proposition 15.3.6 ; away from $0$ the current vanishes. title: Proposition 15.4.5
text:

title: 15.5 Fiber integration and modifications
text: 15.5 Fiber integration and modifications We now pass the fiber formula of lemma 15.3.5 through the truncations that define non-pluripolar products on a product of compact Kähler manifolds. The resulting identity, weighted by a bounded difference of potentials, is the form needed for relative energy in chapter 17 . We also show that non-pluripolar products commute with modifications. Corollary 15.5.1 . Let $X$ and $Z$ be connected compact Kähler manifolds of dimensions $r$ and $m$, with projections $p_ X,p_ Z$ from $X\times Z$. Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $\gamma \geq 0$ be a smooth closed $(1,1)$-form on $Z$. Put \[  \Theta =p_ X^*\theta +p_ Z^*\gamma ,\qquad \Phi =p_ X^*\varphi ,\qquad T=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}W,\quad S=\Theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi ,  \] where $W\in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times Z,\Theta )$ satisfies $\Phi -C\leq W\leq \Phi +C$ for a constant $C\geq 0$. Then for every $z\in Z$ the function $W_ z=W(\, \cdot \, ,z)$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and for every integer $0\leq j\leq r$ and every smooth real $(m,m)$-form $\eta $ on $Z$, 15.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:compact-nonpluripolar-fibre-fubini} \begin{aligned} & \int _{X\times Z}(W-\Phi )\, p_ Z^*\eta \wedge \langle T^ j\wedge S^{r-j}\rangle \\ & \qquad =\int _ Z\left(\int _ X(W_ z-\varphi ) \langle (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}W_ z)^ j\wedge (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^{r-j}\rangle \right)\eta (z). \end{aligned} \end{equation} The same identity holds with both difference weights replaced by $1$. The weights are undefined only on the common pole set of the two potentials involved, where they may be given any bounded values. Proof. In product charts choose smooth local potentials $a(x)$ of $\theta $ and $b(z)$ of $\gamma $. Then $W+a+b$ is plurisubharmonic, so by proposition 8.2.3 its restriction $W_ z+a+b(z)$ to a fiber is plurisubharmonic in $x$ or identically $-\infty $; the second alternative is excluded, because $W_ z\geq \varphi -C$ and $\varphi $ is not identically $-\infty $ on any open set. Hence $W_ z$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}W_ z\geq 0$, that is, $W_ z\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. All the products in ( 15.16 ) are finite by theorem 15.4.3 , and ( 15.14 ) bounds the fiber masses uniformly in $z$, because the shifted background can be chosen from the fixed form $\theta $, independently of $W_ z$. Put $w=W+a+b$, $v=\Phi +a+b$ and $O_ k=\{ w>-k\} \cap \{ v>-k\} $ in a product chart. Let $\rho \geq 0$ be a smooth function with compact support in the chart, let $G\geq 0$ be bounded and Borel, and let $\eta \geq 0$. Apply ( 15.10 ) to the bounded functions $\max \{ w,-k\} $ and $\max \{ v,-k\} $, with multiplicities $j$ and $r-j$, and to the weight $\rho G\mathbf1_{O_ k}$. The set $O_ k$ is contained in the level-$k$ set of the tuple formed by $j$ copies of $w$ and $r-j$ copies of $v$ (if $j=0$ or $j=r$, one of the two conditions defining $O_ k$ concerns a potential that does not occur in the tuple). Hence, by lemma 15.1.2 , the restriction to $O_ k$ of the bounded mixed product equals the restriction to $O_ k$ of the non-pluripolar product, on the total space and, with $(O_ k)_ z$ in place of $O_ k$, on every fiber. These restrictions increase with $k$, and they increase to the non-pluripolar products, because the complements of $\bigcup _ kO_ k$ and of $\bigcup _ k(O_ k)_ z$ are contained in the pole sets of $w,v$ and of $w_ z,v_ z$, which are pluripolar and carry no mass. Monotone convergence, on the total space and in $z$, therefore gives the fiber formula for the non-pluripolar products with weight $\rho G$. Taking $G=1$ gives the unweighted identity. Since $\Phi -C\leq W\leq \Phi +C$, the potentials $W$ and $\Phi $ have the same pole set, and so do $W_ z$ and $\varphi $; take $G=W-\Phi +C\in [0,2C]$ off this set and $G=C$ on it, and subtract $C$ times the unweighted identity. Summing over a finite partition of unity by such functions $\rho $ (proposition 7.1.3 ), and writing a signed $\eta $ as a difference of nonnegative forms, gives ( 15.16 ). All integrals are finite by the uniform mass bound and $|W-\Phi |\leq C$, and the values assigned on the common pole set do not matter, because this set is pluripolar and carries no mass for any of the products. $\square$ Proposition 15.5.2 . Let $\pi \colon \widetilde X\to X$ be a modification between compact Kähler manifolds, that is, a proper bimeromorphic holomorphic map, and let $1\leq p\leq \dim X$. For closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ on $X$, \[  \pi _*\langle \pi ^*T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \pi ^*T_ p\rangle =\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle ,  \] and for closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $R_1,\ldots ,R_ p$ on $\widetilde X$, \[  \pi _*\langle R_1\wedge \cdots \wedge R_ p\rangle =\langle \pi _*R_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \pi _*R_ p\rangle .  \] In particular, in top degree the corresponding total masses agree. Proof. The pullback $\pi ^*T_ j$ is the closed positive current of proposition 7.5.4 , defined by pulling back local plurisubharmonic potentials; a pulled-back potential is not identically $-\infty $ on any open set, because $\pi $ is biholomorphic over a dense open set whose preimage is dense (proposition A.7.3 and the definition of bimeromorphic maps in section A.3 ). The pushforward $\pi _*R$ of a closed positive current is closed and positive, since pullback of smooth forms commutes with $\mathrm d$ and preserves strong positivity (proposition 7.2.1 ). All products in the statement are therefore defined, and they are finite by theorem 15.4.3 . Choose a nowhere dense analytic subset $A\subset X$ such that $\pi ^{-1}(A)$ is nowhere dense and $\pi $ restricts to a biholomorphism $\pi ^{-1}(X\setminus A)\to X\setminus A$. Both $A$ and $\pi ^{-1}(A)$ are pluripolar: near each point, a nowhere dense analytic set is contained in the zero set of a holomorphic function $f$ that does not vanish identically on a connected neighborhood, hence in the pole set of $\log |f|^2$. For a point $\widetilde x\in \pi ^{-1}(X\setminus A)$, use on a neighborhood of $\widetilde x$ the coordinates $z\circ \pi $, where $z$ are coordinates near $\pi (\widetilde x)$. In these coordinates $\pi $ is the identity, and the local potentials $u_ j\circ \pi $ of $\pi ^*T_ j$ are the local potentials $u_ j$ of $T_ j$. Since non-pluripolar products do not depend on the choice of coordinates or of local potentials, the two sides of the first identity agree on $X\setminus A$. It remains to show that neither side charges $A$. The right side gives the pluripolar set $A$ zero mass. The product $S=\langle \pi ^*T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \pi ^*T_ p\rangle $ gives $\pi ^{-1}(A)$ zero mass, and hence $\pi _*S$ gives $A$ zero mass. Indeed, in a chart of $X$, the trace measure of $\pi _*S$ is the image under $\pi $ of the positive measure $S\wedge \pi ^*\beta ^{n-p}$, which does not charge $\pi ^{-1}(A)$, and the coefficient measures of $\pi _*S$ are bounded by a multiple of this trace measure (theorem 7.2.5 ). Hence the two sides of the first identity have the same coefficient measures on $X\setminus A$ and on $A$, and they are equal. The same argument on $X\setminus A$, where now the local potentials of $\pi _*R_ j$ are those of $R_ j$ in the coordinates $z\circ \pi $, proves the second identity. In top degree, the total mass of $\pi _*S$ is $(\pi _*S)(1)=S(\pi ^*1)=S(1)$, which proves the assertion on masses. $\square$

title: 15.6 Capacity convergence and loss of mass
search_title: Capacity convergence and loss of mass
text: 15.6 Capacity convergence and loss of mass Bedford–Taylor products of locally uniformly bounded potentials are continuous under convergence in capacity (theorem 9.4.8 ). For unbounded potentials this fails, because mass can escape into the poles in the limit (example 15.6.6 ). What survives is a lower semicontinuity statement, which becomes continuity when the total masses do not drop in the limit. Throughout, capacities are the local Monge–Ampère capacities $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ of definition 9.3.2 , used in coordinate charts as in definition 9.4.5 , and not the global capacity $c_\omega $ of section 14.8 . Accordingly, a Borel function on $X$ is quasi-continuous (definition 9.4.1 ), and a net of Borel functions on $X$ converges locally in capacity (definition 9.4.5 ), if this holds in the charts of a finite atlas whose charts have bounded images; by the following lemma, this does not depend on the atlas. We then extend convergence in capacity to functions with poles. Lemma 15.6.1 . Let $(W,z)$ and $(W',z')$ be holomorphic charts of a complex manifold whose images $D=z(W)$ and $D'=z'(W')$ are bounded, and let $K\subset W\cap W'$ be compact. Then there is a constant $C$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_{D'}^*(z'(E))\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(z(E))\qquad \text{for every set }E\subset K,  \] and $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(z'(E))\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(z(E))$ for every Borel set $E\subset K$. Consequently, for a net of Borel functions on a complex manifold, convergence locally in capacity in the charts of an atlas whose charts have bounded images implies the same in every chart with bounded image; similarly for quasi-continuity of a Borel function. Proof. For every $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ such that the closed ball $\overline{B(z(x),2r_ x)}$ lies in $z(W\cap W')$. Finitely many of the sets $z^{-1}(B(z(x_ i),r_ i))$, $r_ i=r_{x_ i}$, cover $K$; put $B_ i=B(z(x_ i),2r_ i)$ and $K_ i=K\cap z^{-1}(\overline{B(z(x_ i),r_ i)})$. The map $F_ i=z'\circ z^{-1}$ is a biholomorphism from $B_ i$ onto the bounded open set $B_ i'=F_ i(B_ i)\subset D'$. Let $E\subset K$ and $E_ i=E\cap K_ i$. Every competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}$ restricts to a competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{B_ i'}$, so $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G)\leq \operatorname {Cap}_{B_ i'}(G)$ for Borel sets $G\subset B_ i'$, and taking infima over open sets, $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}\leq \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i'}$ on subsets of $B_ i'$. By proposition 9.3.3 (5) and (4), applied to the ball $B_ i\Subset D$ and the compact set $\overline{B(z(x_ i),r_ i)}\subset B_ i$, there is a constant $C_ i$ with \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}(z'(E_ i))& \leq \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i'}(z'(E_ i))=\operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i}(z(E_ i))\\ & \leq C_ i\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(z(E_ i))\leq C_ i\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(z(E)). \end{aligned}  \] By subadditivity of $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}$ (proposition 9.3.3 ), the assertion holds with $C=\sum _ iC_ i$. If $E$ is a Borel set, then so are $E_ i$, $z(E_ i)$ and $z'(E_ i)$, because $z$ and $z'$ are homeomorphisms onto their images. The restriction argument above and proposition 9.3.3 (4),(5) also apply to the capacities of Borel sets, so the same chain of inequalities holds with $\operatorname {Cap}$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}^*$, and the subadditivity of $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}$ gives the second assertion with the same constant. For the consequences, let $(W',z')$ be a chart with bounded image and $K'\subset W'$ compact. Cover $K'$ by finitely many compact sets $K_ i'\subset W'\cap W_ i$, where the $(W_ i,z_ i)$ are charts of the given atlas. Suppose that $(f_ a)$ converges to $f$ locally in capacity in the charts $W_ i$. By subadditivity, the outer capacity in $D'=z'(W')$ of the image of $K'\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} $ is at most the sum over $i$ of the outer capacities of the images of $K_ i'\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} $. By the first part, each of these is at most a constant times the corresponding outer capacity in $z_ i(W_ i)$, which tends to zero; similarly for $\{ f_ a<f-\delta \} $. If $f$ is quasi-continuous in the charts $W_ i$ and $\varepsilon >0$, choose open sets $G_ i\subset z_ i(W_ i)$ of small capacity such that $f$ is continuous on $K_ i'\setminus z_ i^{-1}(G_ i)$. By the first part, $z'(K_ i'\cap z_ i^{-1}(G_ i))$ has outer capacity at most $C_ i\operatorname {Cap}_{z_ i(W_ i)}(G_ i)$ in $D'$, so it is contained in an open set $G_ i'\subset D'$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G_ i')<\varepsilon /N$, where $N$ is the number of sets $K_ i'$, provided the $G_ i$ are chosen small enough. Then $G'=\bigcup _ iG_ i'$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G')<\varepsilon $, and the set $F=K'\setminus z'^{-1}(G')$ is the union of the finitely many relatively closed sets $F\cap K_ i'$, on each of which $f$ is continuous; hence $f$ is continuous on $F$. $\square$ Definition 15.6.2 . For $s,t\in [-\infty ,\infty )$ put $d_*(s,t)=|\arctan s-\arctan t|$, where $\arctan (-\infty )=-\pi /2$. A net $(u_ a)$ of plurisubharmonic functions on a bounded open set $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ converges in extended capacity to a plurisubharmonic function $u$ if, for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\delta >0$, the outer capacity of $K\cap \{ d_*(u_ a,u)>\delta \} $ tends to zero, the capacity being taken as in definition 9.4.5 . A net of $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions on a compact manifold converges in extended capacity if the local plurisubharmonic functions obtained by adding smooth local potentials of $\theta $ do so on the charts of a finite coordinate cover by charts with bounded images. This does not depend on the choice of the local potentials or of the cover, by lemma 15.6.3 below. Lemma 15.6.3 . Let $(u_ k)$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on a bounded open set $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ that is locally uniformly bounded above, and let $u$ be plurisubharmonic on $D$. Then $u_ k\to u$ in extended capacity if and only if $\max \{ u_ k,-C\} \to \max \{ u,-C\} $ locally in capacity for every $C>0$. A decreasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions with plurisubharmonic limit converges to it in extended capacity. Extended capacity convergence of $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions on a compact manifold does not depend on the choices made in definition 15.6.2 . If a sequence $(u_ k)$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ converges in extended capacity to an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, then the suprema $\sup _ Xu_ k$ are bounded above. Proof. Fix a compact set $K$ and let $M$ be an upper bound for all $u_ k$ and $u$ on $K$. On $[-\infty ,M]$, the function $\max \{ s,-C\} $ is a Lipschitz function of $\arctan s$: it is constant for $\arctan s\leq \arctan (-C)$, and the derivative of the tangent is bounded on the compact interval $[\arctan (-C),\arctan M]$. Hence extended capacity convergence implies capacity convergence of the truncations. Conversely, $|\arctan s-\arctan \max \{ s,-C\} |\leq \pi /2-\arctan C$ for all $s$, so that \[  d_*(u_ k,u)\leq |\max \{ u_ k,-C\} -\max \{ u,-C\} |+2(\pi /2-\arctan C),  \] where we also used $|\arctan s-\arctan t|\leq |s-t|$ for finite $s,t$. Choosing $C$ with $2(\pi /2-\arctan C)<\delta /2$, the set $\{ d_*(u_ k,u)>\delta \} $ is contained in $\{ |\max \{ u_ k,-C\} -\max \{ u,-C\} |>\delta /2\} $, which proves the equivalence. Adding the same bounded real function $h$ to $s$ and $t$ changes $d_*$ by at most a bounded factor: since $1+\sigma ^2\leq 2(1+h^2)(1+(\sigma +h)^2)$, the formula $\arctan t-\arctan s=\int _ s^ t\mathrm d\sigma /(1+\sigma ^2)$ gives $d_*(s+h,t+h)\leq 2(1+h^2)d_*(s,t)$. Now let $(W_ i,h_ i)$ and $(W'_ l,h'_ l)$ be two choices of a finite cover of $X$ by charts with bounded images and of smooth local potentials $h_ i$ of $\theta $ on $W_ i$ and $h'_ l$ on $W'_ l$, and suppose that $u_ k+h_ i\to u+h_ i$ in extended capacity on every $W_ i$. Fix $l$, a compact set $K\subset W'_ l$ and $\delta >0$, and cover $K$ by finitely many compact sets $K_ i\subset W_ i\cap W'_ l$. The smooth function $h'_ l-h_ i$ is bounded on $K_ i$, say by $H_ i$, so the inequality just proved, applied with $h=h'_ l-h_ i$, gives \[  K_ i\cap \{ d_*(u_ k+h'_ l,u+h'_ l)>\delta \} \subset K_ i\cap \{ d_*(u_ k+h_ i,u+h_ i)>\delta /(2+2H_ i^2)\} .  \] By lemma 15.6.1 , the outer capacity of the left side, computed in the chart $W'_ l$, is at most a constant times the outer capacity of the right side, computed in $W_ i$, which tends to zero. By subadditivity of outer capacity, the outer capacity of $K\cap \{ d_*(u_ k+h'_ l,u+h'_ l)>\delta \} $ in $W'_ l$ tends to zero. Thus extended capacity convergence does not depend on the choice of the cover or of the local potentials. If $u_ k$ decreases to $u$, then for every $C$ the truncations decrease to the bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-C\} $, so they converge in capacity by proposition 9.4.6 ; the equivalence just proved gives extended capacity convergence. For the global assertion, put $m_ k=\sup _ Xu_ k$ and $v_ k=u_ k-m_ k$. By proposition 14.2.1 , $\int _ X|v_ k|\, \omega ^ n\leq M_0$ for a constant $M_0$. Suppose that $m_ k\to +\infty $ along a subsequence, to which we pass. By Markov's inequality, the $\omega ^ n$-volume of $\{ u_ k<m_ k/2\} =\{ v_ k<-m_ k/2\} $ is at most $2M_0/m_ k$, which tends to zero. On the other hand, let $(W,z)$ be one of the charts of definition 15.6.2 , with smooth local potential $h$ of $\theta $, and let $K\subset W$ be a compact set of positive volume, with $|h|\leq H$ and $u+h\leq M$ on $K$. On $K\cap \{ u_ k\geq m_ k/2\} $ we have $u_ k+h\geq m_ k/2-H$, so for large $k$ this set is contained in $K\cap \{ d_*(u_ k+h,u+h)>\delta _0\} $, where $\delta _0=(\pi /2-\arctan M)/2$. The outer capacity in $z(W)$ of the image of the latter set tends to zero, and hence so does its Lebesgue measure, by proposition 9.3.3 (3). Since Lebesgue measure in the chart and the $\omega ^ n$-volume are comparable on $K$, the volume of $K\cap \{ u_ k\geq m_ k/2\} $ tends to zero, whereas by the first observation it tends to the volume of $K$, which is positive. This contradiction shows that the suprema are bounded above. $\square$ The lower semicontinuity of non-pluripolar products under convergence in capacity is proved with the following cutoff weights. They vanish where one of the potentials is at most $-C$, and multiplied by them, non-pluripolar products become Bedford–Taylor products of bounded potentials. Lemma 15.6.4 . Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set and $1\leq p\leq n$. For $1\leq j\leq p$ let $(v_{j,k})_{k\geq 1}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ that is locally uniformly bounded above and converges in extended capacity to a plurisubharmonic function $v_ j$, and suppose that the non-pluripolar products $R_ k=\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{1,k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{p,k}\rangle $ and $R=\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ p\rangle $ are locally finite. For $C,\varepsilon >0$ put \[  v_{j,k}^ C=\max \{ v_{j,k},-C\} ,\qquad a_{j,k}=\frac{v_{j,k}^ C+C}{v_{j,k}^ C+C+\varepsilon },\qquad a_ k=\prod _ j a_{j,k},  \] and define $v_ j^ C$, $a_ j$ and $a$ from the $v_ j$ in the same way. Then: the functions $a_ k$ and $a$ are Borel and take values in $[0,1]$, the function $a$ is quasi-continuous, and $a_ k\to a$ locally in capacity as $k\to \infty $; $a_ kR_ k=a_ k\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{1,k}^ C\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{p,k}^ C$ and $aR=a\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1^ C\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ p^ C$, where the products on the right are Bedford–Taylor products; for fixed $C$, the weight $a$ increases to the indicator function of $\bigcap _ j\{ v_ j>-C\} $ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$, and these indicator functions increase to the indicator function of the complement of the union of the pole sets of the $v_ j$ as $C\to \infty $. Proof. (1) The weights are Borel functions of the Borel functions $v_{j,k}$ and $v_ j$, and they take values in $[0,1]$ because $v_{j,k}^ C+C\geq 0$ and $v_ j^ C+C\geq 0$. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\delta >0$. By theorem 9.4.2 there are open sets $G_ j\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ j)<\delta /p$ such that $v_ j$ is continuous on $K\setminus G_ j$. Then $a$, a continuous function of $v_1^ C,\ldots ,v_ p^ C$, is continuous on $K\setminus \bigcup _ jG_ j$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(\bigcup _ jG_ j)<\delta $ by subadditivity; thus $a$ is quasi-continuous. By lemma 15.6.3 , $v_{j,k}^ C\to v_ j^ C$ locally in capacity. Since $s\mapsto (s+C)/(s+C+\varepsilon )$ is Lipschitz with constant $1/\varepsilon $ on $[-C,\infty )$, and since $|\prod _ jb_ j-\prod _ jb_ j'|\leq \sum _ j|b_ j-b_ j'|$ for numbers in $[0,1]$, the set where $|a_ k-a|>\delta $ is contained in the union over $j$ of the sets where $|v_{j,k}^ C-v_ j^ C|>\varepsilon \delta /p$. By subadditivity of outer capacity, $a_ k\to a$ locally in capacity. (2) Fix $k$, and let $O=\bigcap _ j\{ v_{j,k}>-C\} $, a plurifine open set. For every integer $m\geq C$, the set $O$ is contained in the level-$m$ set $O_ m=\bigcap _ j\{ v_{j,k}>-m\} $ of the tuple $(v_{j,k})_ j$, and on $O$ the truncations $\max \{ v_{j,k},-m\} $ coincide with $v_{j,k}$, hence with $v_{j,k}^ C$. By lemma 15.1.2 , $\mathbf1_{O_ m}R_ k$ is the Bedford–Taylor product of the truncations at level $m$ restricted to $O_ m$, and by theorem 10.4.3 this product coincides on $O$ with $\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{j,k}^ C$. Hence $\mathbf1_ OR_ k=\mathbf1_ O\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{j,k}^ C$. The weight $a_ k$ vanishes outside $O$, because $a_{j,k}=0$ wherever $v_{j,k}\leq -C$, and multiplying by $a_ k$ gives the first identity. The same argument, applied to the tuple $(v_ j)_ j$, gives the second. (3) Where $v_ j>-C$ we have $v_ j^ C+C>0$, so $a_ j$ increases to $1$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$; where $v_ j\leq -C$ we have $a_ j=0$. Hence $a$ increases to the indicator function of $\bigcap _ j\{ v_ j>-C\} $, and these sets increase to $\bigcap _ j\{ v_ j>-\infty \} $ as $C\to \infty $. $\square$ Theorem 15.6.5 . Let $T_{j,k}=\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j,k}$ and $T_ j=\theta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ be closed positive currents on $X$, for $1\leq j\leq p\leq n$ and $k\geq 1$, and suppose that $u_{j,k}\to u_ j$ in extended capacity as $k\to \infty $, for every $j$. Put $R_ k=\langle T_{1,k}\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{p,k}\rangle $ and $R=\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ p\rangle $. Then for every smooth strongly positive $(n-p,n-p)$-form $\eta $ on $X$, \[  \varliminf _ k\int _ X R_ k\wedge \eta \geq \int _ X R\wedge \eta .  \] If moreover $\varlimsup _ k\int _ X R_ k\wedge \omega ^{n-p}\leq \int _ X R\wedge \omega ^{n-p}$, then $R_ k\to R$ weakly. The lower inequality also holds locally, on any complex manifold and for compactly supported $\eta $, whenever the local products are finite and the potentials converge in extended capacity and are locally uniformly bounded above. Proof. Lower inequality. Work on a coordinate ball $B$ such that $\overline B$ lies in a larger coordinate ball, add fixed smooth local potentials of the $\theta _ j$, defined near $\overline B$, and denote the resulting plurisubharmonic functions by $v_{j,k}$ and $v_ j$. By lemma 15.6.3 (including its independence assertion, which allows us to use the chart $B$), $v_{j,k}\to v_ j$ in extended capacity on $B$, and the $v_{j,k}$ are uniformly bounded above on $B$, because the suprema of the $u_{j,k}$ are bounded above. The local non-pluripolar products of the $v_{j,k}$ and of the $v_ j$ are the restrictions of $R_ k$ and $R$ to $B$, and they are finite by theorem 15.4.3 . For $C,\varepsilon >0$ let $v_{j,k}^ C$, $v_ j^ C$, $a_ k$ and $a$ be as in lemma 15.6.4 . By that lemma, the weights take values in $[0,1]$, $a$ is quasi-continuous, $a_ k\to a$ locally in capacity, and \[  a_ k R_ k=a_ k\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_{j,k}^ C,\qquad aR=a\bigwedge _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j^ C  \] on $B$. Moreover, the plurisubharmonic functions $v_{j,k}^ C\geq -C$ are uniformly bounded on $B$, and they converge to $v_ j^ C$ locally in capacity, by lemma 15.6.3 . Let $\chi \geq 0$ be a smooth function with compact support in $B$. By the weighted capacity continuity of theorem 9.4.8 , \[  \int \chi \, aR\wedge \eta =\lim _ k\int \chi \, a_ kR_ k\wedge \eta \leq \varliminf _ k\int \chi R_ k\wedge \eta ,  \] where the inequality holds because $0\leq a_ k\leq 1$ and $R_ k\wedge \chi \eta $ is a positive measure. Now let $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ and then $C\to \infty $. By lemma 15.6.4 (3), the weights $a$ increase to the indicator function of the complement of the union of the pole sets of the $v_ j$, which $R$ does not charge; so monotone convergence gives $\int \chi R\wedge \eta \leq \varliminf _ k\int \chi R_ k\wedge \eta $. This is the local lower inequality; it used only the finiteness of the local products, the extended capacity convergence and the local upper bounds. A finite partition of unity by such functions $\chi $ (proposition 7.1.3 ) gives the global inequality. Convergence. By ( 15.14 ), the masses $\int _ XR_ k\wedge \omega ^{n-p}$ are bounded, since the shifted backgrounds depend only on the fixed forms $\theta _ j$. Near a compact subset $L$ of a chart with Euclidean form $\beta $, we have $\beta \leq c\, \omega $ for some $c>0$ (lemma 13.1.1 ), and hence $R_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}\leq c^{n-p}R_ k\wedge \omega ^{n-p}$ by ( 15.7 ). Therefore the trace measures of the $R_ k$ are locally uniformly bounded, and by theorem 7.2.5 every subsequence of $(R_ k)$ has a weakly convergent subsequence. Its limit $R'$ is positive, and $R'-R$ is positive, by the lower inequality applied to all smooth strongly positive forms $\eta $ on $X$. The additional hypothesis gives $\int _ X(R'-R)\wedge \omega ^{n-p}\leq 0$, because $\omega ^{n-p}$ is a test form on the compact manifold $X$. Hence the positive measure $(R'-R)\wedge \omega ^{n-p}$ vanishes, so the trace measures of $R'-R$, which are bounded on compact subsets of charts by multiples of it, vanish as well, and $R'-R=0$ by theorem 7.2.5 . Thus every subsequence of $(R_ k)$ has a further subsequence converging weakly to $R$, which proves $R_ k\to R$. $\square$ Example 15.6.6 . On $\mathbb P^1$ let $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$ be the Fubini–Study form of example 14.5.6 , which has total mass one, and put $u=\log |z|^2-\log (1+|z|^2)$ and $u_ k=\max \{ u,-k\} $. As computed in that example, $u$ extends smoothly across infinity and $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=[0]$. Each $u_ k$ is bounded and $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$-plurisubharmonic, so $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ has mass one by proposition 15.4.1 . The sequence $u_ k$ decreases to $u$, hence converges to it in extended capacity (lemma 15.6.3 ), and the measures $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ converge weakly to $[0]$, because $u_ k\to u$ in $L^1$. However, $\langle [0]\rangle =0$ by example 15.4.4 . The weak limit retains the mass that the non-pluripolar product discards at the pole, so the mass hypothesis in theorem 15.6.5 cannot be omitted.

title: Lemma 15.6.1
text: Lemma 15.6.1 . Let $(W,z)$ and $(W',z')$ be holomorphic charts of a complex manifold whose images $D=z(W)$ and $D'=z'(W')$ are bounded, and let $K\subset W\cap W'$ be compact. Then there is a constant $C$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_{D'}^*(z'(E))\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(z(E))\qquad \text{for every set }E\subset K,  \] and $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(z'(E))\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(z(E))$ for every Borel set $E\subset K$. Consequently, for a net of Borel functions on a complex manifold, convergence locally in capacity in the charts of an atlas whose charts have bounded images implies the same in every chart with bounded image; similarly for quasi-continuity of a Borel function. Proof. For every $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ such that the closed ball $\overline{B(z(x),2r_ x)}$ lies in $z(W\cap W')$. Finitely many of the sets $z^{-1}(B(z(x_ i),r_ i))$, $r_ i=r_{x_ i}$, cover $K$; put $B_ i=B(z(x_ i),2r_ i)$ and $K_ i=K\cap z^{-1}(\overline{B(z(x_ i),r_ i)})$. The map $F_ i=z'\circ z^{-1}$ is a biholomorphism from $B_ i$ onto the bounded open set $B_ i'=F_ i(B_ i)\subset D'$. Let $E\subset K$ and $E_ i=E\cap K_ i$. Every competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}$ restricts to a competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{B_ i'}$, so $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G)\leq \operatorname {Cap}_{B_ i'}(G)$ for Borel sets $G\subset B_ i'$, and taking infima over open sets, $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}\leq \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i'}$ on subsets of $B_ i'$. By proposition 9.3.3 (5) and (4), applied to the ball $B_ i\Subset D$ and the compact set $\overline{B(z(x_ i),r_ i)}\subset B_ i$, there is a constant $C_ i$ with \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}(z'(E_ i))& \leq \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i'}(z'(E_ i))=\operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ i}(z(E_ i))\\ & \leq C_ i\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(z(E_ i))\leq C_ i\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(z(E)). \end{aligned}  \] By subadditivity of $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}$ (proposition 9.3.3 ), the assertion holds with $C=\sum _ iC_ i$. If $E$ is a Borel set, then so are $E_ i$, $z(E_ i)$ and $z'(E_ i)$, because $z$ and $z'$ are homeomorphisms onto their images. The restriction argument above and proposition 9.3.3 (4),(5) also apply to the capacities of Borel sets, so the same chain of inequalities holds with $\operatorname {Cap}$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}^*$, and the subadditivity of $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}$ gives the second assertion with the same constant. For the consequences, let $(W',z')$ be a chart with bounded image and $K'\subset W'$ compact. Cover $K'$ by finitely many compact sets $K_ i'\subset W'\cap W_ i$, where the $(W_ i,z_ i)$ are charts of the given atlas. Suppose that $(f_ a)$ converges to $f$ locally in capacity in the charts $W_ i$. By subadditivity, the outer capacity in $D'=z'(W')$ of the image of $K'\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} $ is at most the sum over $i$ of the outer capacities of the images of $K_ i'\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} $. By the first part, each of these is at most a constant times the corresponding outer capacity in $z_ i(W_ i)$, which tends to zero; similarly for $\{ f_ a<f-\delta \} $. If $f$ is quasi-continuous in the charts $W_ i$ and $\varepsilon >0$, choose open sets $G_ i\subset z_ i(W_ i)$ of small capacity such that $f$ is continuous on $K_ i'\setminus z_ i^{-1}(G_ i)$. By the first part, $z'(K_ i'\cap z_ i^{-1}(G_ i))$ has outer capacity at most $C_ i\operatorname {Cap}_{z_ i(W_ i)}(G_ i)$ in $D'$, so it is contained in an open set $G_ i'\subset D'$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G_ i')<\varepsilon /N$, where $N$ is the number of sets $K_ i'$, provided the $G_ i$ are chosen small enough. Then $G'=\bigcup _ iG_ i'$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(G')<\varepsilon $, and the set $F=K'\setminus z'^{-1}(G')$ is the union of the finitely many relatively closed sets $F\cap K_ i'$, on each of which $f$ is continuous; hence $f$ is continuous on $F$. $\square$
