Using locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we have \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n=h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n,\quad h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n=h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n.  \] Therefore, \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq &  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n & \  =&  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n & \  =&  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n &  	extup{by theorem \gerbyref{B4CE255F}{2.3.8}}\  =& \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n & \  \geq &  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} } h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n &  	extup{by }(\gerbyref{4EC9ECC1}{2.84})\  =&  \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the last equality follows from the dominated convergence theorem. By our choice of $C$, we have $h^{C,\epsilon }>0$ on $\{ \varphi =f\} $, and hence when $\epsilon 	o 0+$, $h^{C,\epsilon }	o 1$ everywhere on this set. Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, we find \[  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g \, \omega _{f}^ n  \] by the dominated convergence theorem. By the Riesz representation theorem, we conclude that \[  \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega _{f}^ n.  \] Then by 2.4.10 , the reverse inequality also holds, and ( 2.83 ) follows in this case. Step 2.2 . We no longer assume that $	heta $ is a Kähler form. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta +\omega $ is a Kähler form and $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega )$. Fix $g\in C^0(X)$ and consider, for $t\geq 0$, \[  Q(t)\coloneqq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (	heta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n - \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (	heta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ n.  \] By multilinearity of the non-pluripolar product, $Q$ is a polynomial in $t$. Step 2.1 applied to $	heta +t\omega $ for $t>1$ gives $Q(t)\equiv 0$ for $t>1$, hence $Q\equiv 0$, and in particular $Q(0)=0$. Since $g$ is arbitrary, ( 2.83 ) holds. Step 3 . We handle the general case. We no longer assume that $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta +\omega $ is a Kähler form. Then \[  \varphi \leq P_{	heta +\omega }(f)\leq f.  \] By 2.4.23 applied to $f_1=f_2=f$, we find that $f$ and $P_{	heta +\omega }(f)$ agree to the second order on the contact set $\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f \} $, so \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f ight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta +\omega }(f)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=f ight\} }\, 	heta _{f}^ n. ootnotemark  \] Note. This expression looks slightly unusual, as $P_{	heta +\omega }(f)$ is not $	heta $-psh in general, but it does make sense. However, Step 2 implies that \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=\varphi ight\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{	heta +\omega }(f)=\varphi ight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta +\omega }(f)}^ n.  \] Combining these results, we conclude ( 2.83 ). $\square$ Corollary 2.4.25 . Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )
eq \varnothing $. For any $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, we have \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ V_{	heta }=0\} }\, 	heta ^ n.  \] Proof. From theorem 2.4.24 , we find \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] By the concentration property theorem 2.4.14 , our assertion follows. $\square$ Theorem 2.4.26 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then \[  P_	heta (f)\in C^{1,\overline{1}} igl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} ) igr ).  \] In particular, $V_{	heta }\in C^{1,\overline{1}} igl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} ) igr )$. We refer to [ DNT23 ] for the proof. Politiques et scientifiques ont le sens des réalités, mais ce ne sont pas les mêmes. Il en résulte — et ce sera là un principe que le général de Gaulle fera sien que l'activité de recherche ne peut être évaluée, quant à sa qualité propre, que par des hommes qui la pratiquent eux-mêmes. 
— Pierre Lelong Note. Pierre Lelong (1912–2011) was the husband of another famous mathematician Jacqueline Ferrand. During their marriage (1947–1977), the latter published under the name of Jacqueline Lelong-Ferrand. , 1999
2.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHpos} \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}=\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n>0 \right\} . \end{equation}

title: Remark 2.4.1
text: Remark 2.4.1 . Suppose that $X$ is a connected complex manifold of dimension $0$, namely, $X$ is a single point. In this case, by definition, the non-pluripolar product $\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ is given by the current of integration at the unique point. So $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}=\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cong \mathbb {R}$ in this case and $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=1$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$.

title: Proposition 2.4.2
text: Proposition 2.4.2 . Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is non-empty. Then the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $ is big.

title: Proposition 2.4.3
text: Proposition 2.4.3 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ and $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \int _ Y (\pi ^*T_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\pi ^*T_ n)=\int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n.  \] Similarly, if $S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $Y$, then \[  \int _ Y S_1\wedge \cdots \wedge S_ n=\int _ X \left(\pi _*S_1\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\pi _*S_ n\right).  \] Proof. The assertions follow from proposition 2.2.2 1 on the Zariski open set where $\pi $ is an isomorphism. The exceptional locus is pluripolar, and the relevant non-pluripolar products put no mass on pluripolar sets by proposition 2.2.2 4 . $\square$

title: Theorem 2.4.4
text: Theorem 2.4.4 . Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the map \[  [0,1] \ni t\mapsto \log \int _ X \theta _{t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0}^ n  \] is concave. More generally, given closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$, we have \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \int _ X T_ i^ n \right)^{1/n}.  \]

title: Remark 2.4.5
text: Remark 2.4.5 . Here and in the sequel, when we write expressions like $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi $ for $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we will follow the convention that when $t=0$, the value is $\psi $ and when $t=1$, the value is $\varphi $.
2.20 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Vtheta} V_{\theta }=\sup \left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ):\varphi \leq 0 \right\} . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 2.4.6
text: Lemma 2.4.6 . Suppose that $\{ \theta \} $ is big. The potential $V_{\theta }$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Proof. By definition of $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$, it suffices to show that if $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ has analytic singularities and $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then $V_{\theta }$ is locally bounded outside $\{ \varphi =-\infty \} $. After replacing $\varphi $ by $\varphi -\sup _ X\varphi $, the function $\varphi $ is a candidate in ( 2.20 ); hence $V_{\theta }\geq \varphi $ and $V_{\theta }\leq 0$. Since $\varphi $ is locally bounded outside its pole set, so is $V_{\theta }$. $\square$

title: Theorem 2.4.7 (Semicontinuity theorem)
text: Theorem 2.4.7 (Semicontinuity theorem) . Let $\varphi _ j, \varphi _ j^ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$, $j=1,\ldots ,n$). Let $\chi _ k,\chi $ ($k\in \mathbb {N}$) be non-negative uniformly bounded quasi-continuous functions on $X$ such that $(\chi _ k)_ k$ converges to $\chi $ in capacity. Assume that for any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, as $k\to \infty $, either $\varphi _ j^ k$ decreases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ or increases to $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ almost everywhere. Then 2.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:semicon1} \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \geq \int _ X \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} If in addition, \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} =\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n},  \] then \[  \chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\rightharpoonup \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}  \] weakly as measures Note. Recall that the weak convergence of Radon measures is stronger than the weak convergence as currents in general. When the Radon measures have uniformly bounded total variation, they are equivalent. . In particular, the limit in ( 2.21 ) exists and equality holds in ( 2.21 ).

2.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:semicon1} \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X\chi _ k \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k} \geq \int _ X \chi \, \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 2.4.8 (Monotonicity theorem)
text: Theorem 2.4.8 (Monotonicity theorem) . Let $\varphi _ j,\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ j \succeq \psi _ j$ Note. See definition 1.5.2 for the notation. for every $j$, then \[  \int _{X} \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n} \geq \int _{X} \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In particular, if $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\varphi \succeq \psi $, then \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass increases as the potentials become less singular.

title: Corollary 2.4.9
text: Corollary 2.4.9 . Fix a directed set $I$. For each $j=1,\ldots ,n$, take an increasing net $(\varphi _ j^ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$, uniformly bounded from above. Set \[  \varphi _ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j^ i,\quad j=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then 2.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:increseqnppcont} \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} = \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} In particular, if the nets are indeed sequences, we have \[  \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} \rightharpoonup \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] Proof. The final assertion follows from ( 2.22 ) together with theorem 2.4.7 . It remains to establish ( 2.22 ). We may assume that $I$ is infinite as there is nothing to prove otherwise. Thanks to theorem 2.4.8 , we already know the $\leq $ inequality in ( 2.22 ). We prove the reverse inequality. When $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets, the reverse inequality follows from theorem 2.4.7 . In general, by Choquet's lemma proposition 1.2.3 , we can find a countable infinite subset $R\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{r\in R}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ r_ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi ^ i_ j  \] for all $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We fix a bijection $R\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For any $j=1,\ldots ,n$, we will then denote elements $\varphi _ j^ r$ ($r\in R$) by $\varphi _ j^1,\varphi _ j^2,\dots $. We shall write \[  \psi _ j^ a=\varphi _ j^1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ j^ a  \] for each $a\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. For every $a$ we may choose $i_ a\in I$ dominating the finitely many indices corresponding to $\varphi _ j^1,\ldots ,\varphi _ j^ a$ for all $j$. It then follows from the monotonicity theorem that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i}\geq \lim _{a\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{1,\psi _1^ a}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n^ a}.  \] From the special case mentioned above, we know that the right-hand side is exactly the right-hand side of ( 2.22 ), so we conclude. $\square$

2.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:increseqnppcont} \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ i}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ i} = \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 2.4.10
text: Lemma 2.4.10 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 2.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetavarphilorpsi1} \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, if $\varphi \leq \psi $, then \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. For each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we set \[  \psi _ k=\psi \lor (V_{\theta }-k),\quad \varphi _ k=\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-k).  \] For each $t>0$ and each $k\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\geq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\\  =& \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k<\varphi _ k+t\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality follows from the plurifine locality of non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 1 . We observe that for any $t>0$, $\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)\sim \psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k$. Therefore, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 guarantees that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n.  \] As $t\to 0+$, \[  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (\varphi _ k+t)}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n  \] by theorem 2.4.7 . Letting $t\to 0+$, we conclude that \[  \theta _{\psi _ k\lor \varphi _ k}^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k>\varphi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ k\leq \varphi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n.  \] In particular, multiplying both sides by $\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} }$ and applying proposition 2.2.2 1 again, we find that \[  \begin{split}  \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} }\, \theta _{\psi \lor \varphi }^ n\geq & \mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi \leq \varphi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n \\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >V_{\theta }-k\} \cap \{ \psi >\varphi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{split}  \] Letting $k\to \infty $, we conclude ( 2.23 ). $\square$

2.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetavarphilorpsi1} \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \geq \psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 2.4.11
text: Corollary 2.4.11 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ so that $\varphi _ i\to \varphi $ in $L^1$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\leq 0$ for all $i\in I$. Then 2.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:contact_int_usc} \varlimsup _{i\in I} \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi =0\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Observe that $\varphi \leq 0$ by proposition 1.5.4 . Step 1 . We first assume that $I\cong \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ as directed sets. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ is a sequence. For each $k>0$, let \[  \psi _ k=\operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq k}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j.  \] Then $(\psi _ k)_{k}$ is a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with limit $\varphi $, see corollary 1.2.8 for example. Thanks to 2.4.10 , for each $k>0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=\psi _ k\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Multiplying both sides with $\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }$, we find that \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n.  \] Take $b,C>0$. For each $k>0$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k}^ n\\ =\int _{\{ \psi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\psi _ k}\, \theta _{\psi _ k\lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n, \end{split}  \] where the equality part follows from proposition 2.2.2 1 . Letting $k\to \infty $ with the help of theorem 2.4.7 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\int _{\{ \varphi _ k=0\} } \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\leq \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{b\varphi }\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n.  \] Letting $b\to \infty $ and then $C\to \infty $, we conclude ( 2.28 ). Step 2 . We now handle the general net case. Fix a volume form on $X$, so that we can talk about the $L^1$-norm on $X$ in the sequel. Suppose that ( 2.28 ) fails. Then there is $\delta >0$ such that, for every $i_0\in I$, one can find $i\geq i_0$ satisfying \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n>\int _{\{ \varphi =0\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n+\delta .  \] Since $\varphi _ i\to \varphi $ in $L^1$, for every $k>0$ there is $a_ k\in I$ such that \[  \| \varphi _ i-\varphi \| _{L^1}<k^{-1},\quad i\geq a_ k.  \] We can then recursively choose an increasing sequence $(i_ k)_{k>0}$ in $I$ with $i_ k\geq a_ k$ and \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _{i_ k}=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _{i_ k}}^ n>\int _{\{ \varphi =0\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n+\delta .  \] This sequence converges to $\varphi $ in $L^1$, contradicting Step 1. $\square$
2.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:contact_int_usc} \varlimsup _{i\in I} \int _{\{ \varphi _ i=0\} }\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n\leq \int _{\{ \varphi =0\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Definition 2.4.12
text: Definition 2.4.12 . Given a function $f\colon X\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$, we define $P_{\theta }(f)$ as follows: 2.31 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafdef} P_{\theta }(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \varphi \leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere} \right\} \footnotemark . \end{equation} Note. In the original article [ DDNLsurv ] , the authors required that $\varphi \leq f$ everywhere. But in the proof of their Theorem 2.7 (theorem 2.4.14 below), they actually relied on the current definition. In the most relevant case, if $f$ is $\mathcal{F}$-upper semicontinuous (for example, if $f$ is upper semicontinuous), then these two definitions coincide. This is due to 1.3.17 and proposition 1.3.15 .

2.31 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafdef} P_{\theta }(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \varphi \leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere} \right\} \footnotemark . \end{equation}
2.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafleqfqe} P_{\theta }(f)\leq f\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 2.4.13
text: Lemma 2.4.13 . Fix a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\colon X\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a lower semicontinuous function. Assume that $P_{\theta }(f)\not\equiv \infty $. Then $P_{\theta }(f)$ is locally bounded outside $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Set $U\coloneqq \{ P_{\theta }(f)<f\} \setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$, then 2.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:bal_ddcn0} \Bigl (\theta |_ U+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }(f)|_ U\Bigr )^ n=0. \end{equation} Proof. First observe that $V_{\theta }+\inf _ X f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 2.31 ). So \[  P_{\theta }(f)\geq V_{\theta }+\inf _ X f,  \] and in particular $P_{\theta }(f)\not\equiv -\infty $. In particular, $P_{\theta }(f)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. It is therefore bounded from above. By 2.4.6 , it is locally bounded away from $\operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )$. Now fix $x\in U$, and $\epsilon >0$ so that \[  P_{\theta }(f)(x)<f(x)-\epsilon .  \] Take holomorphic balls $B\Subset B'\Subset U$ containing $x$. After shrinking $B$, we can guarantee that 2.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetafBp_temp1} \left.P_{\theta }(f)\right|_{B}<f(x)-\epsilon ,\quad f|_ B> f(x)-\epsilon . \end{equation} Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be the balayage of $P_{\theta }(f)$ on $B$, as constructed in proposition 1.5.9 . By the domination principle proposition 1.2.15 , we find that \[  \varphi |_{B}\leq f(x)-\epsilon <f|_{B}.  \] Since $\varphi =P_{\theta }(f)$ outside $B$, we conclude that \[  \varphi \leq f\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] From this it follows that $\varphi \leq P_{\theta }(f)$, and hence equality holds. But then ( 2.33 ) holds automatically on $B$ since $\varphi $ is constructed by balayage. Since $x$ and $B$ are arbitrary, we conclude ( 2.33 ). $\square$
2.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:bal_ddcn0} \Bigl (\theta |_ U+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }(f)|_ U\Bigr )^ n=0. \end{equation}
2.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetafBp_temp1} \left.P_{\theta }(f)\right|_{B}<f(x)-\epsilon ,\quad f|_ B> f(x)-\epsilon . \end{equation}

title: Theorem 2.4.14
text:
Theorem 2.4.14 . Let $f\colon Xightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a quasi-continuous function. Assume that $P_{	heta }(f)
ot\equiv \pm \infty $. Then $P_{	heta }(f)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and 2.35  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafconc} \int _{\{ P_{	heta }(f)<f\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $f$ is bounded. Step 1.1 . Reduce to the case where $f\leq 0$. Take $C\in \mathbb {R}$ so that $P_{	heta }(f)\leq C$. Then \[  P_{	heta }(f)=P_{	heta }\Bigl ( \min \{ f,C\}  \Bigr ).  \] Thus we can replace $f$ by $\min \{ f,C\} $. Replacing $f$ by $f-\sup _ X f$, we reduce easily to the case where $f\leq 0$. Step 1.2 . Reduce to the case where $f$ is bounded. Assume that in this case, the theorem is known. We prove ( 2.35 ) for $f\leq 0$. For each $j>0$, we have 2.36  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafjint0_temp1} \int _{\{ P_{	heta }(f_ j)<f_ j\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)}^ n=0, \end{equation} where $f_ j=f\lor (-j)$. Now fix $C>0$ and two open sets $G'\Subset G\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$. Fix a smooth function $\chi \colon Xightarrow [0,1]$ so that $\chi |_{G'}\equiv 1$ and $\chi $ is supported in $G$. Define \[  U_ C\coloneqq G \cap \left\{ P_{	heta }(f)>V_{	heta }-C ight\} ,\quad U'_ C\coloneqq G' \cap \left\{ P_{	heta }(f)>V_{	heta }-C ight\} .  \] Then $U_ C$ is $\mathcal{F}$-open. It follows from proposition 2.2.2 1 that for any $j>0$, \[  \mathds {1}_{U_ C}\,  	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{U_ C}\,  	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)}^ n.  \] In particular, thanks to ( 2.36 ), 2.37  egin{equation} \label{eq:intU1mexpPthetaf_temp1} \int _{U_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Note that the $P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)$'s for various $j$ are uniformly bounded from below on $U_ C$, thanks to 2.4.6 . Next we claim that $(P_{	heta }(f_ j))_ j$ is decreasing and converges to $P_{	heta }(f)$. The sequence is decreasing; let us compute its limit. In fact, $P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq f_ j$ quasi-everywhere. It follows that $\inf _ j P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and hence \[  \inf _{j>0} P_{	heta }(f_ j)\leq P_{	heta }(f).  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, and our assertion follows. Since $P_{	heta }(f)
ot\equiv -\infty $, we know that the set $\{ f=-\infty \} $ is pluripolar. It follows that $P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j$ converges to the following function $g\colon Xightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ in capacity: \[  g(x)= egin{cases}  P_{	heta }(f)(x)-f(x),& 	extup{if } f(x)
eq -\infty ;\  -\infty ,&  	extup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] Therefore, \[  1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j}\xlongrightarrow {\mathrm{C}} 1-\mathrm{e}^{g}.  \] Next we claim that 2.40  egin{equation} \label{eq:intU1mexpPthetaf_temp2} \int _{U'_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation} Since $g\leq 0$ quasi-everywhere, the left-hand side of ( 2.40 ) is non-negative. It suffices to prove the $\leq $ direction. We wish to let $j	o \infty $ directly in ( 2.37 ), but since $U_ C$ is not open in general, this cannot be done directly. In the sequel, we shall slightly enlarge $U_ C$ to get an open set and then take the limit. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find an open subset $W\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$ so that 2.41  egin{equation} \label{eq:CapCinvthetaWmusmall_temp1} \operatorname{Cap}_{C^{-1}	heta }(W\setminus U_ C)<\epsilon . \end{equation} For example, we can construct $W$ as follows. By example 2.3.5 , we can find an open set $A\subseteq G$ so that $\operatorname{Cap}_{C^{-1}	heta }(A)<\epsilon $ and $P_{	heta }(f)-V_{	heta }$ is continuous on $G\setminus A$. Then $U_ C\cap (G\setminus A)$ is relatively open in $G\setminus A$, so we may choose an open set $W_0\subseteq G$ such that \[  W_0\cap (G\setminus A)=U_ C\cap (G\setminus A).  \] Taking $W=W_0\cup A$, we get $U_ C\subseteq W$ and $W\setminus U_ C\subseteq A$, hence ( 2.41 ). Thanks to ( 2.41 ) and ( 2.37 ), we have \[  \int _ W \chi \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f_ j)-f_ j} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq C^ n\epsilon .  \] Letting $j	o \infty $ and applying theorem 2.3.8 , we find that \[  \int _{U'_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq \int _ W \chi \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)\lor (V_{	heta }-C)}^ n\leq C^ n\epsilon .  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, ( 2.40 ) follows. Now letting $C	o \infty $ in ( 2.40 ), we find \[  \int _{G'}\left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0.  \] Since $G'\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$ is arbitrary, and $\operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )\subseteq X$ is a proper analytic subset, we finally conclude \[  \int _ X \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0.  \] In other words, $P_{	heta }(f)=f$ almost everywhere with respect to $	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n$. This proves ( 2.35 ). Step 2 . We now assume that $-C'\leq f\leq 0$ for some $C'>0$. For each $j>0$, take an open subset $V_ j\subseteq X$ so that $\operatorname{Cap}_{C'^{-1}	heta }(V_ j)\leq 2^{-j-1}$, and $f|_{X\setminus V_ j}$ is continuous. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $V_ j$'s are decreasing. Take a continuous function $f_ j\colon Xightarrow [-C',0]$ extending $f|_{X\setminus V_ j}$. This is always possible thanks to Tietze's extension theorem. For each $j>0$, we let \[  h_ j\coloneqq \sup _{k\geq j} f_ k.  \] Then $h_ j$ is lower semicontinuous and $h_ j$ agrees with $f$ outside $V_ j$. Set \[  h=\inf _{j>0} h_ j.  \] Then the set $\{ h
eq f\} $ is contained in the intersection of the $V_ j$'s and hence is a pluripolar set, thanks to theorem 2.3.4 . In particular, $P_{	heta }(f)=P_{	heta }(h)$. Now we can apply 2.4.13 to conclude that \[  \int _{X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )} \left(1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(h_ j)-h_ j} ight) 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n=0  \] for each $j>0$. Fix two open subsets $G'\Subset G\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$. Note that $-C'\leq h_ j\leq 0$. In particular, \[  V_{	heta }-C'\leq P_{	heta }(h_ j)\leq V_{	heta }.  \] Hence, \[   egin{aligned} & \int _ G \left| 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(h_ j)-f}ight|\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n\  =& \int _{G\cap V_ j} \left|1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(h_ j)-f}ight|\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n+\int _{G\setminus V_ j} \left|1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(h_ j)-h_ j}ight|\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n\  =&  \int _{G\cap V_ j} \left|1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(h_ j)-f}ight|\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n\  \leq &  \int _{G\cap V_ j} \left( 1+\mathrm{e}^{C'}ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(h_ j)}^ n\  \leq &  \left( 1+\mathrm{e}^{C'}ight) \cdot 2^{-j-1} C'^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Now we can apply the same arguments as in Step 1.2 to conclude that \[  \int _{G'}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{	heta }(f)-f}ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta }(f)}^ n=0.  \] Since $G'\Subset X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ 	heta \} )$, ( 2.35 ) follows. $\square$
2.35 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafconc} \int _{\{ P_{\theta }(f)<f\} } \theta _{P_{\theta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation}
2.36 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetafjint0_temp1} \int _{\{ P_{\theta }(f_ j)<f_ j\} } \theta _{P_{\theta }(f_ j)}^ n=0, \end{equation}
2.37 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intU1mexpPthetaf_temp1} \int _{U_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{P_{\theta }(f_ j)-f_ j} \right)\, \theta _{P_{\theta }(f_ j)\lor (V_{\theta }-C)}^ n=0. \end{equation}
2.40 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intU1mexpPthetaf_temp2} \int _{U'_ C} \left( 1-\mathrm{e}^{g} \right)\, \theta _{P_{\theta }(f)}^ n=0. \end{equation}
2.41 \begin{equation} \label{eq:CapCinvthetaWmusmall_temp1} \operatorname{Cap}_{C^{-1}\theta }(W\setminus U_ C)<\epsilon . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 2.4.15
text:
Lemma 2.4.15 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, $\varphi \preceq \psi $ and $\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. Then for any 2.47  egin{equation} \label{eq:arangetemp} a\in \left( 1, \left( rac{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n}ight)^{1/n} ight) ootnotemark , \end{equation} there is $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ such that 2.48  egin{equation} \label{eq:path_env} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} Proof. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi \leq \psi \leq 0$. Step 1 . We show the existence of $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ satisfying ( 2.48 ). Step 1.1 . We first consider the case where $\psi \sim \varphi $. In this case, we can take $\eta =\varphi -C$ enough $C>0$. But since by ( 2.52 ), we also have $P_{	heta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\psi )\leq \psi $, we find that \[  P_{	heta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )\sim \varphi \sim \psi  \] in this case. Step 1.2 . We make a first reduction of the problem. Now for each $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we let \[  P_{	heta }[\gamma ]\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \eta \leq \min \{ \gamma +C,0\} 	extup{ for some }C>0 \Bigr \}  ootnotemark .  \] Note. This is precisely the $P$-envelope to be introduced later in definition 3.1.4 . Observe that due to corollary 2.4.9 and theorem 2.4.8 , we have 2.53  egin{equation} \label{eq:intthetaP_pr_mass_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\gamma ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n. \end{equation} Further, $0\geq P_{	heta }[\gamma ]\geq \gamma $ if $\gamma \leq 0$. We now define an increasing transfinite sequence $(\psi _{\alpha })_{\alpha }$ consisting of non-positive functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ as follows: $\psi _0=\psi $; $\psi _{\alpha +1}=P_{	heta }[\psi _{\alpha }]$; if $\alpha $ is a limit ordinal, we define \[  \psi _{\alpha }=\operatorname *{sup}_{ eta <\alpha }{}\! {}^{*} \psi _{ eta }.  \] Observe that \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\psi _{\alpha }}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n  \] by corollary 2.4.9 and ( 2.53 ). Since $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ is indeed a set, the transfinite sequence must stabilize, say at some $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Note that $0 \geq \phi \geq \psi $, and $P_{	heta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Note that the interval ( 2.47 ) remains the same if we replace $\psi $ by $\phi $. Take $a$ in this interval, it suffices to prove the existence of $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ so that 2.54  egin{equation} \label{eq:path_env_temp1} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\phi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} Let us record the following observation for later use. Suppose that $	au \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $	au \preceq \phi $. Then 2.55  egin{equation} \label{eq:modelpot_sup_temp1} \sup _{\{ \phi 
eq -\infty \} } (	au -\phi )=\sup _ X 	au . \end{equation} Observe that $\phi \leq 0$, so on the set $\{ \phi 
eq -\infty \} $, we have \[  	au -\phi \geq 	au .  \] So the $\geq $ direction in ( 2.55 ) follows from corollary 1.3.18 . Conversely, by assumption, we can find a constant $C>0$ so that \[  	au -\sup _ X 	au \leq \min \{ \phi +C,0 \} .  \] It follows that $	au -\sup _ X 	au \leq P_{	heta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Therefore, the reverse inequality follows, and ( 2.55 ) follows. For each $k>0$, we introduce \[  \varphi _ k=\varphi \lor \left(\phi -kight),\quad \eta _ k\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a \varphi _ k+(1-a)\phi \Bigr ).  \] Since $\varphi _ k\sim \phi $, using Step 1.1, we have $\eta _ k\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\eta _ k\sim \phi $ as well. Note that $(\eta _ k)_ k$ is decreasing in $k$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{k\in \mathbb {N}} \eta _ k.  \] Note that $\eta $ automatically satisfies ( 2.54 ). It remains to show that $\eta 
ot\equiv -\infty $. Step 1.3 . We prove that $\eta 
ot\equiv -\infty $. Suppose, for contradiction, that $\sup _ X \eta _ k	o -\infty $. For each $k>0$, let \[  \gamma _ k\coloneqq a^{-1}\eta _ k+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\phi ,\quad D_ k\coloneqq \left\{ \gamma _ k=\varphi _ kight\} .  \] We claim that 2.56  egin{equation} \label{eq:1Dkan_temp1} 	heta _{\eta _ k}^ n\leq a^ n\mathds {1}_{D_ k}\,  	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n. \end{equation} Since $\gamma _ k\leq \varphi _ k$ with equality on $D_ k$, 2.4.10 gives \[  \mathds {1}_{D_ k}\,  	heta _{\gamma _ k}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{D_ k}\,  	heta _{\varphi _ k}^ n.  \] On the other hand, \[  	heta _{\gamma _ k}=a^{-1}	heta _{\eta _ k}+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)	heta _{\phi },  \] so positivity and multilinearity of the non-pluripolar product imply \[  a^{-n}	heta _{\eta _ k}^ n\leq 	heta _{\gamma _ k}^ n.  \] Finally, it follows from theorem 2.4.14 that \[  \mathds {1}_{D_ k}\, 	heta _{\eta _ k}^ n=	heta _{\eta _ k}^ n.  \] Putting these results together, we conclude ( 2.56 ). Fix $j>k>0$. Note that 2.57  egin{equation} \label{eq:intthetavarphijn_temp1} \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n, \end{equation} where we applied theorem 2.4.8 and proposition 2.2.2 1 in the second equality. Next, we compute \[   egin{aligned}  \int _{\left\{  \eta _ j\leq \phi -ak ight\} } 	heta _{\eta _ j}^ n\leq &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  \eta _ j\leq \phi -ak ight\} } \mathds {1}_{D_ j}\,  	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n &  	extup{by (\gerbyref{49BC5178}{2.56})}\  \leq &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  a\varphi _ j+(1-a)\phi \leq \phi -ak ight\} \cap \left\{ \phi 
eq -\infty ight\}  } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  = &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  \varphi _ j\leq \phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  = &  a^ n \int _{\left\{  \varphi \leq \phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\  \leq &  a^ n\left( \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n- \int _{\left\{ \varphi >\phi -k ight\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n ight)& 	extup{ by (\gerbyref{12ED989D}{2.57})}. \end{aligned}  \] Next thanks to ( 2.55 ), \[  \sup _{ \left\{ \phi 
eq -\infty ight\}  } \left(\eta _ j-\phi ight)=\sup _ X \eta _ j	o -\infty .  \] In particular, for a fixed $k$, if $j$ is large enough, we have \[  \left\{ \eta _ j\leq \phi -ak ight\} =X.  \] Therefore, for a fixed $k$, for any large enough $j$, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ j}^ n\leq a^ n\left( \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n- \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ night).  \] Letting $k	o \infty $, we find \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n\leq a^ n \left(\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n ight).  \] This is a contradiction with our choice of $a$. Step 2 . Next we argue that $P_{	heta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\psi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Choose \[  a'\in \left( a, \left( rac{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n}ight)^{1/n} ight).  \] It follows from ( 2.49 ) that 2.63  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetalowerbdtemp1} P_{	heta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )\geq  rac{a}{a'} P_{	heta }\Bigl (a'\varphi +(1-a')\psi \Bigr )+ rac{a'-a}{a'}\varphi . \end{equation} Therefore, by theorem 2.4.8 , we have 2.64  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetalowerbdtemp2} \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }\left(a\varphi +(1-a)\psi ight)}^ n\geq  rac{(a'-a)^ n}{a'^ n}\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0. \end{equation} We conclude the proof. $\square$

2.47 \begin{equation} \label{eq:arangetemp} a\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right)\footnotemark , \end{equation}
2.48 \begin{equation} \label{eq:path_env} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation}

2.49 \begin{equation} \label{eq:perversePtheta} \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )\coloneqq & \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi \right\} \\  \in &  \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
2.52 \begin{equation} \label{eq:P_path_everywhere_ineq} a^{-1}P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )+(1-a^{-1})\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation}
2.53 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intthetaP_pr_mass_temp1} \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\gamma ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n. \end{equation}
2.54 \begin{equation} \label{eq:path_env_temp1} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\phi \leq \varphi . \end{equation}
2.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:modelpot_sup_temp1} \sup _{\{ \phi \neq -\infty \} } (\tau -\phi )=\sup _ X \tau . \end{equation}
2.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:1Dkan_temp1} \theta _{\eta _ k}^ n\leq a^ n\mathds {1}_{D_ k}\,  \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n. \end{equation}

2.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intthetavarphijn_temp1} \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -k \} } \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -k \} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n, \end{equation}

2.63 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetalowerbdtemp1} P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )\geq \frac{a}{a'} P_{\theta }\Bigl (a'\varphi +(1-a')\psi \Bigr )+\frac{a'-a}{a'}\varphi . \end{equation}

title: Corollary 2.4.16
text: Corollary 2.4.16 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\varphi \preceq \psi $. Assume that $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n$. Then for any $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, there is $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$; $\epsilon \eta +(1-\epsilon )\psi \leq \varphi $. In fact, we can take \[  \eta =P_{\theta }\left(\epsilon ^{-1}\varphi +(1-\epsilon ^{-1})\psi \right).  \] Proof. Fix $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. We define $\eta $ as in the statement of the corollary. By 2.4.15 , $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Observe that 2 is satisfied by ( 2.52 ). Thanks to ( 2.64 ), for each $a'>\epsilon ^{-1}$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\left(\frac{a'-\epsilon ^{-1}}{a'}\right)^ n\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Letting $a'\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] On the other hand, since $\eta \preceq \psi $, using the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 we find that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Hence, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, 1 holds as well. $\square$

title: Theorem 2.4.17 (Domination principle)
text: Theorem 2.4.17 (Domination principle) . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that 2.65 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphipsiPequiv} \exists \phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\quad \textup{s.t.} \quad \varphi \preceq \phi , \quad \psi \preceq \phi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n, \end{equation} and 2.66 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphilpsitheta0} \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \geq \psi $.

2.65 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphipsiPequiv} \exists \phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\quad \textup{s.t.} \quad \varphi \preceq \phi , \quad \psi \preceq \phi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n, \end{equation}
2.66 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphilpsitheta0} \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation}

title: Remark 2.4.18
text: Remark 2.4.18 . Using the terminologies to be introduced in chapter 3 , we can reformulate a special case of theorem 2.4.17 as follows: Suppose that $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is a model potential and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that ( 2.66 ) holds then $\varphi \geq \psi $. Equivalently, using the terminologies of chapter 6 , the assumption ( 2.65 ) can be reformulated as $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. Proof. Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] We may replace $\psi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. Without loss of generality, we may also assume that $\psi \leq 0$. Now fix $a>1$. We define \[  \eta _ a\coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl ( a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr ).  \] Note that $\eta _ a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by corollary 2.4.16 and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Furthermore, $\eta _ a\leq P_{\theta }(a\varphi +(1-a)\varphi )=\varphi $. Define \[  \gamma _ a\coloneqq a^{-1}\eta _ a+(1-a^{-1})\psi ,\quad D_ a\coloneqq \{ \gamma _ a=\varphi \} .  \] Then $\gamma _ a\leq \varphi $ with equality on $D_ a$. Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n\leq &  a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, \theta _{\psi }^ n& \\  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} a^{-n}\, \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n+\mathds {1}_{D_ a} (1-a^{-1})^ n \, \theta _{\psi }^ n &  \textup{ by theorem \gerbyref{DD169AC1}{2.4.14}}\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} \theta _{\gamma _ a}^ n & \\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{D_ a} \theta _{\varphi }^ n &  \textup{ by \gerbyref{6959A57D}{2.4.10}}\\  =&  \mathds {1}_{D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n &  \textup{ by (\gerbyref{07DE36DF}{2.66})}. \end{aligned}  \] Note that on $D_ a\cap \{ \varphi =\psi \} $, we have $\eta _ a=\varphi $. We deduce that \[  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\,  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n \leq \theta _{\varphi }^ n,  \] where the inequality follows from 2.4.10 . But the two ends have the same mass, and hence \[  \theta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta _ a=\varphi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\eta _ a}\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \mathrm{e}^{\varphi }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0.  \] Note that $\eta _ a$ is decreasing in $a$. The above equation shows that \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{a>1} \eta _ a\not\equiv -\infty .  \] On the other hand, if $x\in X$ is such that $\varphi (x)<\psi (x)$, we then have \[  \eta _ a(x)\leq a\varphi (x)-(a-1)\psi (x)= \psi (x)+a\Bigl ( \varphi (x)-\psi (x) \Bigr ).  \] Letting $a\to \infty $, we find that $\eta (x)=-\infty $. Therefore, $\{ \varphi \neq \psi \} $ is pluripolar, and hence empty by proposition 1.2.6 . Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Lemma 2.4.19
text: Lemma 2.4.19 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current, and $\psi \leq \varphi $. In particular, there is an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ i)_{i>0}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ converging almost everywhere to $\varphi $ such that $\theta _{\varphi _ i}$ is a Kähler current for all $i\geq 1$. Proof. Using 2.4.15 , we can find $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that \[  \epsilon V_{\theta }+(1-\epsilon )\gamma \leq \varphi .  \] We observe that the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $ is big as a consequence of proposition 2.4.2 . Therefore, we can take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\eta }$ is a Kähler current and $\eta \leq 0$. Since $\eta \leq V_{\theta }$, we may take \[  \psi \coloneqq \epsilon \eta +(1-\epsilon )\gamma .  \] Then $\psi $ clearly satisfies 1 and 2 . For the latter claim, it suffices to take \[  \varphi _ i=\left(1-(i+1)^{-1}\right)\varphi +(i+1)^{-1}\psi  \] for each $i>0$. $\square$

title: Lemma 2.4.20
text: Lemma 2.4.20 . Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$ with $\theta \in c_1(L)$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there exists $k_0>0$ such that for each $k\geq k_0$, we have \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\neq 0.  \] Proof. By 2.4.19 , there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\psi }$ a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. Since $\mathcal{I}(k\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$, it suffices to prove the assertion with $\psi $ in place of $\varphi $. In this case, the result follows from Hörmander's $L^2$-estimate ( [ Hor66 ] ), see [ Theorem 13.21 , Dem12 ] . $\square$

title: Theorem 2.4.21 (Tosatti, Chu–Zhou)
text: Theorem 2.4.21 (Tosatti, Chu–Zhou) . Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with a Kähler form $\omega $ and let $f\in C^{1,1}(X)$. Then \[  P_\omega (f)\in C^{1,1}(X),  \] and there is a constant $C=C(X,\omega ,\| f\| _{C^{1,1}})$ such that \[  \| P_\omega (f)\| _{C^{1,1}}\leq C.  \]

title: Proposition 2.4.22 (Darvas–Rubinstein)
text: Proposition 2.4.22 (Darvas–Rubinstein) . Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$.

title: Lemma 2.4.23
text: Lemma 2.4.23 . Assume that $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$ and let $f_1,f_2\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then the functions $f_1$, $f_2$ and $P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$ coincide up to second order at almost every point of the contact set $\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\} $. In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega _{f_1}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega _{f_2}^ n.  \] We also have for $j\in \{ 1,2\} $, 2.72 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_Pomega} \begin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_{P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)} = &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} \\ & - \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}\\  \geq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_ j\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Proof. Set $\varphi \coloneqq P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )$. Since $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \in C^0(X)$, we have $\varphi \leq \min \{ f_1,f_2\} $. By proposition 2.4.22 , $\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. As $f_1,f_2,\varphi \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, the measures $\omega ^ n_{f_1}$, $\omega ^ n_{f_2}$ and $\omega ^ n_\varphi $ are all absolutely continuous. Step 1 : We show that at almost every contact point, $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two. For $i\in \{ 1,2,3\} $ set \[  \Psi _1\coloneqq \varphi -f_1,\quad \Psi _2\coloneqq \varphi -f_2,\quad \Psi _3\coloneqq f_1-f_2.  \] Each $\Psi _ i$ lies in $C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. We claim that for $i=1,2,3$, we have 2.76 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1claim} \Psi _ i\textup{ vanishes to second order at almost every point of }\{ \Psi _ i=0\} . \end{equation} To prove this, write $\{ \Psi _ i=0\} $ as the disjoint union $A_ i\sqcup B_ i\sqcup C_ i\sqcup D_ i$ of the following four sets: $A_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i\neq 0\} $; $B_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian of }\Psi _ i\textup{ does not exist}\} $; $C_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian exists and is non-zero}\} $; $D_ i\coloneqq \{ \Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \mathrm{d}\Psi _ i=0\} \cap \{ \textup{the classical real Hessian exists and equals zero}\} $. It suffices to prove $A_ i$, $B_ i$, $C_ i$ are Lebesgue null sets. The set $A_ i$ is a $C^1$ real hypersurface in $X$, hence has Lebesgue measure zero. Since $\Psi _ i\in W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the classical pointwise real Hessian of $\Psi _ i$ exists almost everywhere, so $B_ i$ is Lebesgue null. Finally $C_ i$ is Lebesgue null by Stampacchia's lemma. This proves ( 2.76 ). Specialising ( 2.76 ) to $\Psi _1,\Psi _2$, the functions $\varphi $ and $f_ i$ agree to order two at almost every point of the contact set $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $. Consequently $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i$ have the same matrix of coefficients almost everywhere on $\{ \varphi =f_ i\} $, and therefore so do their $n$-fold wedge powers: 2.77 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1eq} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ i},\qquad i\in \{ 1,2\} . \end{equation} The analogous statement applied to $\Psi _3$ gives 2.78 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1eqf12} \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} = \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2}. \end{equation} Step 2 . The barrier $\min \{ f_1,f_2\} $ is continuous, hence quasi-continuous, so theorem 2.4.14 yields 2.79 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step2conc} \int _{X\setminus \left(\{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\} \right)}\omega ^ n_\varphi = \int _{\left\{ \varphi <\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right\} }\omega ^ n_\varphi =0. \end{equation} Set $V_1\coloneqq \{ f_1<f_2\} $ and $V_2\coloneqq \{ f_1>f_2\} $, both open. We may decompose \[  \{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\}  = \bigl (V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} \bigr ) \sqcup \bigl (V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} \bigr ) \sqcup \{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} .  \] This combined with ( 2.79 ) and ( 2.77 ) yields \[  \begin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_\varphi ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi \\  ={}&  \mathds {1}_{V_1\cap \{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{V_2\cap \{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned}  \] On the other hand, \[  \mathds {1}_{V_ j\cap \{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ j\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j} - \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}.  \] Therefore, \[  \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} + \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_1=f_2\} } \, \bigl (\omega ^ n_{f_ j}-\omega ^ n_{f_1}-\omega ^ n_{f_2}\bigr ).  \] Together with ( 2.78 ) we obtain ( 2.72 ). $\square$

2.72 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_Pomega} \begin{aligned}  \omega ^ n_{P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)} = &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_1\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} + \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2} \\ & - \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega (\min \{ f_1,f_2\} )=f_1=f_2\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}\\  \geq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\omega \left(\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right)=f_ j\right\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ j}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
2.76 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1claim} \Psi _ i\textup{ vanishes to second order at almost every point of }\{ \Psi _ i=0\} . \end{equation}
2.77 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1eq} \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_\varphi = \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f_ i\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_ i},\qquad i\in \{ 1,2\} . \end{equation}
2.78 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step1eqf12} \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_1} = \mathds {1}_{\{ f_1=f_2\} }\, \omega ^ n_{f_2}. \end{equation}

2.79 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTroof_step2conc} \int _{X\setminus \left(\{ \varphi =f_1\} \cup \{ \varphi =f_2\} \right)}\omega ^ n_\varphi = \int _{\left\{ \varphi <\min \{ f_1,f_2\} \right\} }\omega ^ n_\varphi =0. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 2.4.24 (Di Nezza–Trapani)
text: Theorem 2.4.24 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . Let $\theta _1,\dots ,\theta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing pseudo-effective cohomology classes. For each $i=1,\dots ,n$, let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ and $f_ i\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ be functions with $\varphi _ i\leq f_ i$. Then 2.82 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTcontact} \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n} = \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,f_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,f_ n}. \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $\theta _1=\cdots =\theta _ n$, $\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n$ and $f_1=\cdots =f_ n$. Assume for the moment that this special case is known. Let us handle the general case. For $\lambda =(\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n)\in (\mathbb {R}_{>0})^ n$, we set \[  \theta _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j\theta _ j,\quad \varphi _\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j\varphi _ j,\quad f_\lambda \coloneqq \sum _{j=1}^ n\lambda _ j f_ j.  \] Then $\varphi _\lambda \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _\lambda )$, $f_\lambda \in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, $\varphi _\lambda \leq f_\lambda $, and \[  \bigcap _{j=1}^ n\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} \subseteq \{ \varphi _\lambda =f_\lambda \} .  \] So \[  \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(\theta _\lambda )^ n_{\varphi _\lambda } = \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ j\{ \varphi _ j=f_ j\} }(\theta _\lambda )^ n_{f_\lambda }.  \] Both sides are polynomials in $\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _ n$; comparing the coefficient of $\lambda _1\cdots \lambda _ n$ gives ( 2.82 ). From now on, we assume \[  \theta =\theta _1=\dots =\theta _ n,\quad \varphi =\varphi _1=\cdots =\varphi _ n\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),  \] and \[  f=f_1=\cdots =f_ n\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)  \] with \[  \varphi \leq f.  \] We wish to prove that 2.83 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNT_temp1} \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{f}^ n. \end{equation} Step 2 . We first handle the special case where $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Step 2.1 . We assume that $\theta $ is a Kähler form, denoted by $\omega $ for clarity. Pick a decreasing sequence $(\phi _ j)_ j$ in $C^{\infty }(X)$ Note. The functions $\phi _ j$ are not required to be $\omega $-psh. with pointwise limit $\varphi $ and set \[  \psi _ j\coloneqq P_{\omega }\left(\min \{ \phi _ j,f\} \right).  \] Then $\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, and \[  \varphi \leq \psi _ j\leq \min \{ \phi _ j,f\}  \leq f,  \] and hence $\psi _ j\searrow \varphi $. Applying 2.4.23 with $f_1=\phi _ j$ and $f_2=f$ gives 2.84 \begin{equation} \label{eq:omegapsij_temp1} \omega ^ n_{\psi _ j}\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ j=f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f \geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f. \end{equation} Fix $C>0$ with $\min _ X f>-C$ and $\epsilon >0$. Let \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq \frac{(\psi _ j+C)\lor 0}{\left((\psi _ j+C)\lor 0 \right)+\epsilon },\qquad h^{C,\epsilon }\coloneqq \frac{(\varphi +C)\lor 0}{\left((\varphi +C)\lor 0\right)+\epsilon }.  \] These functions are both quasi-continuous with values in $[0,1]$. Observe that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }$ converges in capacity to $h^{C,\epsilon }$ as $j\to \infty $. Now fix $g\in C^0(X)$, $g\geq 0$. Note that $h_ j^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \psi _ j\leq -C\} $ and $h^{C,\epsilon }=0$ on the set $\{ \varphi \leq -C\} $. Using locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we have \[  h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n=h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n,\quad h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n=h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq &  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi }^ n & \\  =&  \int _ X h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\varphi \lor (-C)}^ n & \\  =&  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j\lor (-C)}^ n &  \textup{by theorem \gerbyref{B4CE255F}{2.3.8}}\\  =& \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{\psi _ j}^ n & \\  \geq &  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} } h_ j^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n &  \textup{by }(\gerbyref{4EC9ECC1}{2.84})\\  =&  \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }h^{C,\epsilon }g \, \omega _{f}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the last equality follows from the dominated convergence theorem. By our choice of $C$, we have $h^{C,\epsilon }>0$ on $\{ \varphi =f\} $, and hence when $\epsilon \to 0+$, $h^{C,\epsilon }\to 1$ everywhere on this set. Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, we find \[  \int _ X g\, \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g \, \omega _{f}^ n  \] by the dominated convergence theorem. By the Riesz representation theorem, we conclude that \[  \omega _{\varphi }^ n\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega _{f}^ n.  \] Then by 2.4.10 , the reverse inequality also holds, and ( 2.83 ) follows in this case. Step 2.2 . We no longer assume that $\theta $ is a Kähler form. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\theta +\omega $ is a Kähler form and $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\omega )$. Fix $g\in C^0(X)$ and consider, for $t\geq 0$, \[  Q(t)\coloneqq \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )^ n - \int _{\{ \varphi =f\} }g\, (\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ n.  \] By multilinearity of the non-pluripolar product, $Q$ is a polynomial in $t$. Step 2.1 applied to $\theta +t\omega $ for $t>1$ gives $Q(t)\equiv 0$ for $t>1$, hence $Q\equiv 0$, and in particular $Q(0)=0$. Since $g$ is arbitrary, ( 2.83 ) holds. Step 3 . We handle the general case. We no longer assume that $f\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Choose a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\theta +\omega $ is a Kähler form. Then \[  \varphi \leq P_{\theta +\omega }(f)\leq f.  \] By 2.4.23 applied to $f_1=f_2=f$, we find that $f$ and $P_{\theta +\omega }(f)$ agree to the second order on the contact set $\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \} $, so \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \right\} }\, \theta _{P_{\theta +\omega }(f)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=f \right\} }\, \theta _{f}^ n.\footnotemark  \] Note. This expression looks slightly unusual, as $P_{\theta +\omega }(f)$ is not $\theta $-psh in general, but it does make sense. However, Step 2 implies that \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=\varphi \right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{  P_{\theta +\omega }(f)=\varphi \right\} }\, \theta _{P_{\theta +\omega }(f)}^ n.  \] Combining these results, we conclude ( 2.83 ). $\square$

2.82 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNTcontact} \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n} = \mathds {1}_{\bigcap _ i\{ \varphi _ i=f_ i\} }\,  \theta _{1,f_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,f_ n}. \end{equation}
2.83 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DNT_temp1} \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =f\right\} }\, \theta _{f}^ n. \end{equation}
2.84 \begin{equation} \label{eq:omegapsij_temp1} \omega ^ n_{\psi _ j}\geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \psi _ j=f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f \geq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =f\} }\, \omega ^ n_ f. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 2.4.25
text: Corollary 2.4.25 . Assume that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\neq \varnothing $. For any $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$, we have \[  \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ V_{\theta }=0\} }\, \theta ^ n.  \] Proof. From theorem 2.4.24 , we find \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] By the concentration property theorem 2.4.14 , our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 2.4.26 (Di Nezza–Trapani)
text: Theorem 2.4.26 (Di Nezza–Trapani) . Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$. Then \[  P_\theta (f)\in C^{1,\overline{1}}\bigl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )\bigr ).  \] In particular, $V_{\theta }\in C^{1,\overline{1}}\bigl (X\setminus \operatorname{nK}(\{ \theta \} )\bigr )$.

title: 3 The envelope operators
text: 3 The envelope operators This chapter develops the envelope formalism that will be used throughout the rest of the book. There are two parallel constructions. The first is the $P$-envelope, which records the singularity type relevant to non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère mass. The second is the $\mathcal I$-envelope, which records the singularity type detected by multiplier ideal sheaves. The distinction between these two envelopes is one of the main organizing principles of the book. The starting point is the rooftop operator. Given two singular potentials, the rooftop construction produces the largest potential lying below both, and it provides a flexible way to compare singularities. From this we define the $P$-envelope $P_\theta [\varphi ]$. Its fixed points are the model potentials. Model potentials are the natural representatives of $P$-singularity types: they preserve non-pluripolar mass and satisfy strong contact-set properties. The first part of the chapter establishes the basic algebra of these envelopes, their behavior under monotone limits, and the domination and contact principles needed later. We then introduce the Monge–Ampère energy relative to a model potential. This leads to the finite-energy classes $\mathcal E^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and to stability results for rooftop envelopes. These results will be used in the metric theory of singularities and in the study of geodesic rays. The second part of the chapter develops the $\mathcal I$-envelope $P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$. This envelope is defined by imposing multiplier ideal conditions rather than ordinary singularity-type conditions. It is therefore sensitive to valuative data in a way that the ordinary $P$-envelope is not. We prove its basic functorial properties, its independence of the chosen representative of the cohomology class, its bimeromorphic behavior, and its compatibility with analytic singularities. The comparison between $P_\theta [\varphi ]$ and $P_\theta [\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}$ is delicate. They agree in important cases, for instance for analytic singularities, but they differ in general. Later chapters use this comparison to define $\mathcal I$-good singularities, trace operators, partial Okounkov bodies and non-Archimedean potentials. Thus the technical results of this chapter should be regarded as the basic calculus of singularity types used in the sequel. Several results about $P$-envelopes are developed by Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu in various papers and summarized in their survey [ DDNLsurv ] . The reader is invited to read their survey for more details and further results.

title: 3.1 The -envelope
text: 3.1 The $P$-envelope In this section, $X$ will denote a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$.

title: 3.1.1 Rooftop operator and the definition of the -envelope
search_title: Rooftop operator and the definition of the -envelope
