3.1.1 Rooftop operator and the definition of the $P$-envelope Fix a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$. Definition 3.1.1 . Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we define their rooftop operator as follows: 3.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:rooftopdef1} \varphi \land \psi =\sup \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi ight\} . \end{equation} For simplicity of notation, we extend the definition to the case where $\varphi $ or $\psi $ is constantly $-\infty $, in which case we simply set \[  \varphi \land \psi =-\infty .  \] When we want to be more specific, we may also write $\varphi \land _{	heta }\psi $. Note that it is possible that the set in ( 3.1 ) is empty, in which case $\varphi \land \psi =-\infty $. Proposition 3.1.2 . The operator $\land $ is a well-defined commutative, associative binary operator \[   igl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \}  igr )	imes  igl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \}  igr )ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Proof. We first show that the map is well-defined. For this purpose, take $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. When the set in ( 3.1 ) is empty, there is nothing to prove. So let us assume that the set is not empty. Define \[  \gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi ight\} .  \] Then by proposition 1.2.2 , we find that $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and hence $\gamma $ is a candidate for the supremum in ( 3.1 ). Therefore, $\gamma \leq \varphi \land \psi $. The reverse inequality follows from the definition of $\gamma $, so \[  \varphi \land \psi =\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] The commutativity and the associativity of $\land $ follow directly from the defining maximality property. $\square$ Note that from the proof, we have \[  \varphi \land \psi =P_{	heta }\Bigl ( \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \}  \Bigr ).  \] See definition 2.4.12 for the notation $P_{	heta }( ullet )$. Lemma 3.1.3 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then 3.2  egin{equation} \label{eq:rooftopMAineq1} 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, $	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n$ is carried by the union $\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} \cup \{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} $. Proof. We first observe that as a consequence of 2.4.10 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying theorem 2.4.14 to $\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} $, we conclude that \[  	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n,  \] and ( 3.2 ) is established. $\square$ We recall that the relations $\preceq $ and $\sim $ are introduced in definition 1.5.2 . Definition 3.1.4 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we define its $P$-envelope as follows: 3.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetavarphi} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0,\psi \preceq \varphi ight\} . \end{equation} Note that $\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi $ is always a candidate for the supremum. By proposition 1.2.2 , we have $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\leq 0$. Moreover, the definition can be equivalently described as 3.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:Penvsups} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=\operatorname *{sup}_{C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}(\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }. \end{equation} Recall that $V_{	heta }$ is introduced in ( 2.20 ). For any $C\in \mathbb {R}$, we have $(\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and \[  (\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }\sim \varphi .  \] In other words, in ( 3.3 ), we may replace the condition $\psi \preceq \varphi $ by $\psi \sim \varphi $. Also note that as a consequence, 3.5  egin{equation} \label{eq:varphipreceqP} \varphi \preceq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation} The idea lying behind the definition of $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ is that we choose the least singular element out of all potentials with the same singularity type as $\varphi $. As we shall see in example 3.1.14 below, $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ does not necessarily have the same singularity type as $\varphi $. This forces us to define a rougher equivalence relation in definition 6.1.1 . The envelope depends on the choice of $	heta $, but the dependence is easy to understand: Proposition 3.1.5 . Let $	heta '=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$ for some $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$. Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, we have $\varphi '\coloneqq \varphi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')$ and \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\sim P_{	heta '}[\varphi '].  \] Proof. By symmetry, it suffices to show that \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{	heta '}[\varphi '].  \] We may assume that $g\geq 0$ (after replacing $g$ by $g+C$ with $C\geq -\inf _ X g$, which leaves $	heta '$ unchanged and shifts $\varphi '$ by an additive constant). Then for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\psi \preceq \varphi $ and $\psi \leq 0$, we set $\psi '\coloneqq \psi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')$. Then $\psi '\preceq \varphi '$ and $\psi '\leq 0$, so $\psi '\leq P_{	heta '}[\varphi ']$. Since $\psi $ is arbitrary, it follows that \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]-\sup _ X g\leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]-g\leq P_{	heta '}[\varphi '],  \] which gives $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{	heta '}[\varphi ']$. $\square$ The $P$-envelope preserves the non-pluripolar masses: Proposition 3.1.6 . Suppose that $	heta _1,\ldots ,	heta _ n$ are smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 3.6  egin{equation} \label{eq:Penvpremass} \int _ X 	heta _{1,P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]}=\int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} This proposition together with theorem 2.4.8 will be combined to a common generalization in proposition 6.1.16 after introducing the $P$-preorder. Proof. For each $C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  (\varphi _ i+C)\land V_{	heta _ i}\sim \varphi _ i.  \] It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 that \[  \int _ X 	heta _{1,(\varphi _1+C)\land V_{	heta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,(\varphi _ n+C)\land V_{	heta _ n}}=\int _ X 	heta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] So ( 3.6 ) follows from ( 3.4 ) and corollary 2.4.9 . $\square$ Conversely, proposition 3.1.6 characterizes the $P$-envelope, as we will see in a moment in theorem 3.1.9 . We need some preparation for the proof. We first show that the $P$-envelope can be regarded as a concentration of the non-pluripolar mass: Theorem 3.1.7 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then 3.7  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPthetaphin} 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=0\} }\, 	heta ^ n. \end{equation} In fact, equality holds as we will see in proposition 3.1.21 below. Proof. Thanks to 3.1.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }}^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }=\varphi +C\}  }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }=V_{	heta }\}  }\,  	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{	heta }\}  }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=V_{	heta }\}  } \, 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C	o \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 2.4.9 give, as $C	o \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{	heta }\}  } 	heta _{\varphi }^ nightharpoonup 0,\quad 	heta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }}^ nightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=V_{	heta }\} } \, 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n.  \] Taking corollary 2.4.25 into consideration, we conclude ( 3.7 ). $\square$ Using essentially the same proof, we arrive at the following conclusion: Corollary 3.1.8 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land \psi . ootnotemark  \] Note. Using the terminology to be introduced in definition 3.1.19 , we can also write $\eta =P_{	heta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. Assume that $\eta 
ot\equiv -\infty $ (for example when $\varphi \preceq \psi $). Then \[  	heta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. Thanks to 3.1.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\varphi +C\}  }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\psi \}  }\,  	heta _{\psi }^ n\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  }\,  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \}  } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C	o \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 2.4.9 give, as $C	o \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  } 	heta _{\varphi }^ nightharpoonup 0,\quad 	heta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ nightharpoonup 	heta _{\eta }^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  	heta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} } \, 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Theorem 3.1.9 . Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 3.12  egin{equation} \label{eq:Penvdef} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=\sup \left\{ \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0,\varphi \preceq \psi , \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ night\} . \end{equation} In particular, in this case, Note. Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou [ PSWZ26 ] recently proved that, ( 3.13 ) continues to hold even when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. 3.13  egin{equation} \label{eq:Penvprojop} P_{	heta }\Bigl [P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{	heta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation} Note that in ( 3.12 ) and ( 3.3 ), the auxiliary function $\psi $ lies on different sides of $\varphi $. Proof. Let $\psi $ be a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 3.12 ). It follows from theorem 3.1.7 that \[  \int _{\{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} } 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \int _{\{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} \cap \{ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=0\}  } 	heta ^ n=0.  \] On the other hand, we have \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{	heta }[\psi ],\quad \psi \preceq P_{	heta }[\psi ]  \] and all these potentials have the same mass due to proposition 3.1.6 . So the domination principle theorem 2.4.17 is applicable and gives \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\geq \psi .  \] Hence we get the $\geq $ direction in ( 3.12 ). On the other hand, $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ itself is a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 3.12 ), as a consequence of proposition 3.1.6 . Therefore, ( 3.12 ) follows. As for ( 3.13 ), the $\geq $ direction is trivial. For the other direction, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential satisfying \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Then it follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad \varphi \preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In view of ( 3.12 ), we conclude the $\leq $ direction of ( 3.13 ). $\square$ Definition 3.1.10 . If $\varphi =P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ and $\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0$, we say $\varphi $ is a model potential . Recall that the notion of model potentials depends heavily on the choice of $	heta $. When there is a risk of confusion, we also say $\varphi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Remark 3.1.11 . definition 3.1.10 is different from the common definition in the literature: We impose the extra condition $\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. The author believes that this is the only case where this notion is natural. We sometimes emphasize this point by saying $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is a model potential. There are plenty of model potentials: Corollary 3.1.12 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Moreover, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 3.1.9 and proposition 3.1.6 . $\square$ As we have already seen in the proof of 2.4.15 , we have the following interesting property: Proposition 3.1.13 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Consider a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq \phi $. Then \[  \sup _{\{ \phi 
eq -\infty \} } (\varphi -\phi )=\sup _ X \varphi .  \] In particular, for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, $\varphi \preceq \phi $ and $\varphi \leq 0$ implies $\varphi \leq \phi $. Proof. Observe that $\phi \leq 0$, so on the set $\{ \phi 
eq -\infty \} $, we have \[  \varphi -\phi \geq \varphi .  \] So the $\geq $ direction follows from corollary 1.3.18 . Conversely, by assumption, we can find a constant $C>0$ so that \[  \varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq \min \{ \phi +C,0 \} .  \] It follows that $\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq P_{	heta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Therefore, the reverse inequality follows. $\square$ Example 3.1.14 . We continue our favorite example example 1.8.5 . Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. We define $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ as follows: For $z\in \mathbb {C}$, we let \[  \varphi (z)=  egin{cases}  -\log \left(|z|^2+1ight)+\Bigl (-\log \left(-\log |z|^2ight)\Bigr ) \lor \Bigl (2+\log |z|^2\Bigr ),&  	extup{if }|z|<1/\sqrt{2},\  2+\log  rac{|z|^2}{|z|^2+1},&  	extup{otherwise}, \end{cases}  \] while $\varphi (\infty )=2$. Note that $\varphi $ is $\omega $-psh on $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ by the gluing lemma 1.2.12 . The singularity of $\varphi $ only occurs at $z=0$, close to which, $\varphi $ is approximately $-\log \left(-\log |z|^2ight)$. This type of singularity is therefore called the log-log type singularity . We claim that 3.16  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp1} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0. \end{equation} In particular, we find that $\varphi $ and $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]$ have different singularity types. By theorem 3.1.9 , in order to verify ( 3.16 ), it suffices to verify that 3.17  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp2} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^1=1. \end{equation} Here $\omega _{\varphi }^1$ is taken in the non-pluripolar sense. Since $\{ 0,\infty \} \subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ is pluripolar, this reduces to showing that \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi = rac{1}{4\pi }\int _{\mathbb {C}^*} (\Delta \psi )\, \mathrm{d}\mu =1,  \] where $\psi (z)=\varphi (z)+\log (|z|^2+1)$ and $\mu $ is the standard Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb {C}$. Note that the Laplacian vanishes outside $\overline{B(0,0.7)}$ since $\psi (z)=2+\log |z|^2$ there, which is harmonic. Therefore, \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi = rac{1}{4\pi }\int _{|z|<1/\sqrt{2}} (\Delta \psi )(z)\, \mathrm{d}\mu .  \] It is an elementary exercise to see that the right-hand side is exactly equal to $1$. If you are familiar with toric geometry, this is more or less trivial since \[  
abla _ r \Bigl ( \left(-\log (-r)ight)\lor (2+r) \Bigr ) igl ((-\infty ,-\log 2) igr )= (0,1].  \] Otherwise, just try to evaluate the integral using Green's identities. Therefore, ( 3.17 ) is proved and our assertion ( 3.16 ) follows. Next we give a criterion on when the rooftop operator is not identically $-\infty $. Proposition 3.1.15 . Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and 3.18  egin{equation} \label{eq:varphimassppsimass_greater} \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , we may also replace $\varphi \lor \psi $ on the right-hand side of ( 3.18 ) by any $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq \gamma $. Proof. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$. For simplicity, we write \[  \eta =P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ].  \] Note that due to our assumption ( 3.18 ), $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, and hence so is $\varphi \lor \psi $ thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . By corollary 3.1.12 , $\eta $ is a model potential, and $\int _ X	heta _\eta ^ n=\int _ X	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n>0$. Take $C>0$ large enough, so that 3.19  egin{equation} \label{eq:intsumintbiggerinttemp1} \int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} } 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} } 	heta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n. \end{equation} This is possible thanks to proposition 2.2.2 4 . Fix $C'>C$. Write \[  \gamma _{C'}\coloneqq \Bigl (\varphi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr )\land \Bigl (\psi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr ).  \] Then observe that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $, and \[  \inf _{C'>C}\gamma _{C'}=\varphi \land \psi .  \] Suppose, for contradiction, that $\varphi \land \psi \equiv -\infty $. Then \[  \adjustlimits \lim _{C'	o \infty } \sup _ X\gamma _{C'}=-\infty .  \] Thanks to proposition 3.1.13 , for each $C'>C$, \[  \sup _{X} \gamma _{C'}=\sup _{\{ \eta 
eq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta ),  \] since $\eta $ is a model potential. It follows that 3.20  egin{equation} \label{eq:limsupgammametatemp1} \adjustlimits \lim _{C'	o \infty } \sup _{\{ \eta 
eq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta )=-\infty . \end{equation} In particular, we can take $C'$ large enough so that \[  \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C.  \] For such $C'$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n=& \int _{\{ \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C\} } 	heta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n \  \leq &  \int _{\left\{ \varphi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -Cight\} } 	heta _{\varphi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n +\int _{\left\{ \psi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -C ight\} } 	heta _{\psi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n\  =&  2\int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} }	heta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} }	heta _{\psi }^ n\  <&  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the second line follows from 3.1.3 , the fourth line follows from ( 3.19 ). This contradicts the fact that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $ in view of theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$ Proposition 3.1.16 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that 3.25  egin{equation} \label{eq:varphipsimodel_landpsh} \varphi =P_{	heta }[\varphi ],\quad \psi =P_{	heta }[\psi ],\quad \varphi \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty . \end{equation} Then 3.26  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetaphilandpsi} P_{	heta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\varphi \land \psi . \end{equation} Proof. Observe that by proposition 3.1.24 3 , \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi \land \psi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=\varphi ,\quad P_{	heta }[\varphi \land \psi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]=\psi .  \] So the $\leq $ direction in ( 3.26 ) holds. The reverse direction is trivial. $\square$ Lemma 3.1.17 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that ( 3.25 ) holds and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n>0.  \] Suppose that $\gamma ,\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and satisfy \[  \gamma \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Then $\gamma \land \eta 
ot\equiv -\infty $ and 3.27  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaeta_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \eta }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Later on in chapter 6 , we shall reformulate and generalize this lemma in terms of the $P$-preorder, which is a more natural language to express the result. See proposition 6.1.21 . Proof. Choose constants $A,B>0$ such that \[  \gamma -A\leq \varphi ,\quad \eta -B\leq \psi .  \] Since \[  (\gamma -A)\land (\eta -B)\sim \gamma \land \eta ,  \] the non-pluripolar masses of these two rooftop potentials are equal by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Hence it suffices to prove the lemma after replacing $\gamma ,\eta $ by $\gamma -A,\eta -B$. We can therefore assume that \[  \gamma \leq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq \psi .  \] Step 1 . We first show that $\gamma \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty $ and 3.28  egin{equation} \label{eq:theta_gammalandpsi_mass_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} For any $a>1$, we define \[  \gamma _ a\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a\gamma +(1-a)\varphi \Bigr ).  \] When $a=1$, we simply write $\gamma _1=\gamma $. Thanks to corollary 2.4.16 , for any $a\geq 1$, we have $\gamma _ a\leq \varphi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By our assumption, for any $a\geq 1$, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma _ a}^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n> \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \gamma _ a\preceq \varphi ,\quad \varphi \land \psi \preceq \varphi .  \] So proposition 3.1.15 gives \[  \gamma _ a\land \varphi \land \psi =\gamma _ a\land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] In particular, for $a=1$, we find $\gamma \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty $. It remains to verify ( 3.28 ). For $a>1$, we have \[  \gamma \geq a^{-1}\gamma _ a+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\varphi ,  \] thanks to the definition of $\gamma _ a$ (cf. ( 2.52 )). Hence \[  \gamma \land \psi \geq a^{-1}\left( \gamma _ a\land \psi ight)+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\left(\varphi \land \psi ight).  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n\geq \left(1-a^{-1}ight)^ n \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n.  \] Letting $a	o \infty $ and taking theorem 2.4.8 into account, ( 3.28 ) follows. Step 2 . We complete the proof. For any $a>1$, we let \[  \eta _ a\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a\eta +(1-a)\psi \Bigr ).  \] When $a=1$, we set $\eta _1=\eta $. Thanks to corollary 2.4.16 , for each $a\geq 1$, we have $\eta _ a\leq \psi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] From Step 1, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying proposition 3.1.15 again, we find \[  \gamma \land \psi \land \eta _ a =\gamma \land \eta _ a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] When $a=1$, we find $\gamma \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. It remains to prove ( 3.27 ). By definition of $\eta _ a$, we have \[  \eta \geq a^{-1}\eta _ a+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  \gamma \land \eta \geq a^{-1} (\gamma \land \eta _ a)+\left(1-a^{-1}ight) \left( \gamma \land \psi ight).  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \eta }^ n\geq \left(1-a^{-1}ight)^ n\int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n.  \] Letting $a	o \infty $ and applying theorem 2.4.8 again, we arrive at ( 3.27 ). $\square$ There is an interesting diamond-like inequality regarding the non-pluripolar masses: Theorem 3.1.18 . Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then 3.29  egin{equation} \label{eq:diamond} \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n\leq \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, as otherwise ( 3.29 ) follows immediately from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Step 1 . We claim that it suffices to prove ( 3.29 ) with $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. In fact, as $\varphi \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty $, we also have $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\land P_{	heta }[\psi ]
ot\equiv -\infty $. Moreover, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n  \] by proposition 3.1.6 . On the other hand, as $C	o \infty $, the potentials \[  \Bigl ( (\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta } \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ( (\psi +C)\land V_{	heta } \Bigr )  \] converge to $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ almost everywhere. Therefore, thanks to corollary 2.4.9 and theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n.  \] Finally, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\land P_{	heta }[\psi ]}^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n  \] as well. When the left-hand side vanishes, this follows from theorem 2.4.8 . Otherwise, it follows from 3.1.17 . In particular, ( 3.29 ) is equivalent to the corresponding result with $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. Step 2 . We shall assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are model potentials in the sequel. We write $\gamma =\varphi \lor \psi $ for simplicity. Note that $\gamma \leq 0$. For each $C>0$, we introduce \[  \varphi _ C=\varphi \lor (\gamma -C),\quad \psi _ C=\psi \lor (\gamma -C).  \] Note that $\varphi _ C\sim \psi _ C\sim \gamma $. Observe that \[  \inf _{C>0} \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi \land \psi .  \] The $\geq $ direction is trivial, and the $\leq $ direction follows from the observation that the left-hand side is dominated by both $\varphi _ C$ and $\psi _ C$ for any $C>0$, and therefore by both $\varphi $ and $\psi $. For $C>0$, we compute 3.30  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaminusvarphi_temp2}  egin{aligned}  	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n & \  =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  	extup{by proposition \gerbyref{B86D7001}{2.2.2} \gerbyref{1C036AD6}{1}}\  =&  	heta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  	extup{by theorem \gerbyref{D18E0263}{3.1.7}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} In the last line we use that $\varphi $ is model, so $	heta _\varphi ^ n$ is carried by $\{ \varphi =0\} \subseteq \{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} $. We also get a similar formula for $	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n$. Therefore, taking the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 into consideration, we find 3.34  egin{equation} \label{eq:intthetagammaminusvarphi_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n=\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{equation} On the other hand, using 3.1.3 and ( 3.30 ), we find \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C\} } \, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C\} } \, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C=0\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C=0\} }\, 	heta _{\psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C<0 \} }\,  	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n.  \] Integrating, we find \[   egin{aligned}  \int _{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=0 \} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \geq &  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\varphi _ C}^ n-\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } 	heta _{\psi _ C}^ n\  =&  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where on the first line we used the fact that $\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C\sim \gamma $, while on the second line, we used ( 3.34 ). Letting $C	o \infty $, and using corollary 2.4.11 , we conclude ( 3.29 ). $\square$ For later use, we also introduce a generalized envelope operator: Definition 3.1.19 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and a function $f\colon X	o [-\infty ,\infty ]$, we define \[  P_	heta [\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*} igl \{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \eta \leq f	extup{ quasi-everywhere},\  \eta \preceq \varphi  igr \} .  \] In general, we cannot replace $\eta \leq f$ quasi-everywhere by everywhere. Example 3.1.20 . When $f=0$, we have $P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. When $\varphi =V_{	heta }$, we have $P_	heta [V_{	heta }](f)=P_{	heta }(f)$. So definition 3.1.19 is a common generalization of definition 3.1.4 and definition 2.4.12 . Proposition 3.1.21 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ with $\varphi \leq f$. Then \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ]} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ]=0ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n.  \] This is a vast generalization of theorem 3.1.7 . Proof. By definition, we have \[  P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_	heta [\varphi ]\Bigl (P_	heta (f)\Bigr )  \] and $\varphi \leq P_	heta (f)$. By corollary 3.1.8 and corollary 2.4.25 , \[  	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_ f.  \] The reverse inequality follows immediately from theorem 2.4.24 . $\square$ Proposition 3.1.22 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ with $\varphi \leq f$. Then \[   egin{aligned}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_\varphi , \  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)\} }\, 	heta ^ n_\varphi . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. By corollary 2.4.25 and theorem 2.4.24 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{f}=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)=f\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{\varphi }\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta (f)\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{\varphi }.  \] The reverse inequality follows from 2.4.10 . The first equality follows. As for the second, we compute using proposition 3.1.21 and theorem 2.4.24 that \[   egin{split}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{P_	heta [\varphi ](f)}=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta ^ n_{f}\  =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)=fight\} }\, 	heta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_	heta [\varphi ](f)\} }\, 	heta ^ n_\varphi . \end{split}  \] Since $\varphi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ](f)$, 2.4.10 gives the opposite inequality. The second equality follows. $\square$
3.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:rooftopdef1} \varphi \land \psi =\sup \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi \right\} . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.2
text: Proposition 3.1.2 . The operator $\land $ is a well-defined commutative, associative binary operator \[  \bigl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} \bigr )\times \bigl (\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} \bigr )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Proof. We first show that the map is well-defined. For this purpose, take $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. When the set in ( 3.1 ) is empty, there is nothing to prove. So let us assume that the set is not empty. Define \[  \gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ):\eta \leq \varphi ,\eta \leq \psi \right\} .  \] Then by proposition 1.2.2 , we find that $\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and hence $\gamma $ is a candidate for the supremum in ( 3.1 ). Therefore, $\gamma \leq \varphi \land \psi $. The reverse inequality follows from the definition of $\gamma $, so \[  \varphi \land \psi =\gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] The commutativity and the associativity of $\land $ follow directly from the defining maximality property. $\square$

title: Lemma 3.1.3
text: Lemma 3.1.3 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 3.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:rooftopMAineq1} \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We first observe that as a consequence of 2.4.10 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying theorem 2.4.14 to $\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} $, we conclude that \[  \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n,  \] and ( 3.2 ) is established. $\square$

3.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:rooftopMAineq1} \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\varphi \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \land \psi =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Definition 3.1.4
text: Definition 3.1.4 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define its $P$-envelope as follows: 3.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetavarphi} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0,\psi \preceq \varphi \right\} . \end{equation}

3.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetavarphi} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0,\psi \preceq \varphi \right\} . \end{equation}
3.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvsups} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\operatorname *{sup}_{C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}(\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }. \end{equation}
3.5 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphipreceqP} \varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.5
text: Proposition 3.1.5 . Let $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$ for some $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$. Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have $\varphi '\coloneqq \varphi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$ and \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\sim P_{\theta '}[\varphi '].  \] Proof. By symmetry, it suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta '}[\varphi '].  \] We may assume that $g\geq 0$ (after replacing $g$ by $g+C$ with $C\geq -\inf _ X g$, which leaves $\theta '$ unchanged and shifts $\varphi '$ by an additive constant). Then for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \preceq \varphi $ and $\psi \leq 0$, we set $\psi '\coloneqq \psi -g\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$. Then $\psi '\preceq \varphi '$ and $\psi '\leq 0$, so $\psi '\leq P_{\theta '}[\varphi ']$. Since $\psi $ is arbitrary, it follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-\sup _ X g\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-g\leq P_{\theta '}[\varphi '],  \] which gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta '}[\varphi ']$. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.6
text: Proposition 3.1.6 . Suppose that $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ are smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 3.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvpremass} \int _ X \theta _{1,P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]}=\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation} Proof. For each $C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  (\varphi _ i+C)\land V_{\theta _ i}\sim \varphi _ i.  \] It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,(\varphi _1+C)\land V_{\theta _1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,(\varphi _ n+C)\land V_{\theta _ n}}=\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}.  \] So ( 3.6 ) follows from ( 3.4 ) and corollary 2.4.9 . $\square$

3.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvpremass} \int _ X \theta _{1,P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]}=\int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 3.1.7
text: Theorem 3.1.7 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 3.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPthetaphin} \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=0\} }\, \theta ^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Thanks to 3.1.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }}^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }=\varphi +C\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }=V_{\theta }\}  }\,  \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{\theta }\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=V_{\theta }\}  } \, \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C\to \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 2.4.9 give, as $C\to \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq V_{\theta }\}  } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\rightharpoonup 0,\quad \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta }}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=V_{\theta }\} } \, \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Taking corollary 2.4.25 into consideration, we conclude ( 3.7 ). $\square$
3.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPthetaphin} \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=0\} }\, \theta ^ n. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 3.1.8
text: Corollary 3.1.8 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land \psi .\footnotemark  \] Note. Using the terminology to be introduced in definition 3.1.19 , we can also write $\eta =P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. Assume that $\eta \not\equiv -\infty $ (for example when $\varphi \preceq \psi $). Then \[  \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. Thanks to 3.1.3 , for each $C>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ n\leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\varphi +C\}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\psi \}  }\,  \theta _{\psi }^ n\\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  }\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \}  } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] We wish to let $C\to \infty $. The dominated convergence theorem and the semicontinuity theorem corollary 2.4.9 give, as $C\to \infty $, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi +C\leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\rightharpoonup 0,\quad \theta _{(\varphi +C)\land \psi }^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{\eta }^ n.  \] So we conclude that \[  \theta _{\eta }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} } \, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Theorem 3.1.9
text: Theorem 3.1.9 . Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 3.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvdef} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\sup \left\{ \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0,\varphi \preceq \psi , \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\right\} . \end{equation} In particular, in this case, Note. Pang–Sun–Wang–Zhou [ PSWZ26 ] recently proved that, ( 3.13 ) continues to hold even when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. 3.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvprojop} P_{\theta }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation} Proof. Let $\psi $ be a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 3.12 ). It follows from theorem 3.1.7 that \[  \int _{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} } \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n\leq \int _{\{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]<\psi \} \cap \{ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=0\}  } \theta ^ n=0.  \] On the other hand, we have \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ],\quad \psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ]  \] and all these potentials have the same mass due to proposition 3.1.6 . So the domination principle theorem 2.4.17 is applicable and gives \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\geq \psi .  \] Hence we get the $\geq $ direction in ( 3.12 ). On the other hand, $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ itself is a candidate of the right-hand side of ( 3.12 ), as a consequence of proposition 3.1.6 . Therefore, ( 3.12 ) follows. As for ( 3.13 ), the $\geq $ direction is trivial. For the other direction, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential satisfying \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Then it follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[  \psi \leq 0,\quad \varphi \preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In view of ( 3.12 ), we conclude the $\leq $ direction of ( 3.13 ). $\square$

3.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvdef} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\sup \left\{ \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0,\varphi \preceq \psi , \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\right\} . \end{equation}
3.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvprojop} P_{\theta }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]. \end{equation}

title: Definition 3.1.10
text: Definition 3.1.10 . If $\varphi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$, we say $\varphi $ is a model potential .

title: Remark 3.1.11
text: Remark 3.1.11 . definition 3.1.10 is different from the common definition in the literature: We impose the extra condition $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. The author believes that this is the only case where this notion is natural. We sometimes emphasize this point by saying $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is a model potential.

title: Corollary 3.1.12
text: Corollary 3.1.12 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Moreover, \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 3.1.9 and proposition 3.1.6 . $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.13
text: Proposition 3.1.13 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Consider a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq \phi $. Then \[  \sup _{\{ \phi \neq -\infty \} } (\varphi -\phi )=\sup _ X \varphi .  \] Proof. Observe that $\phi \leq 0$, so on the set $\{ \phi \neq -\infty \} $, we have \[  \varphi -\phi \geq \varphi .  \] So the $\geq $ direction follows from corollary 1.3.18 . Conversely, by assumption, we can find a constant $C>0$ so that \[  \varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq \min \{ \phi +C,0 \} .  \] It follows that $\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\phi ]=\phi $. Therefore, the reverse inequality follows. $\square$

title: Example 3.1.14
text: Example 3.1.14 . We continue our favorite example example 1.8.5 . Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. We define $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ as follows: For $z\in \mathbb {C}$, we let \[  \varphi (z)= \begin{cases}  -\log \left(|z|^2+1\right)+\Bigl (-\log \left(-\log |z|^2\right)\Bigr ) \lor \Bigl (2+\log |z|^2\Bigr ),&  \textup{if }|z|<1/\sqrt{2},\\  2+\log \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^2+1},&  \textup{otherwise}, \end{cases}  \] while $\varphi (\infty )=2$. Note that $\varphi $ is $\omega $-psh on $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ by the gluing lemma 1.2.12 . The singularity of $\varphi $ only occurs at $z=0$, close to which, $\varphi $ is approximately $-\log \left(-\log |z|^2\right)$. This type of singularity is therefore called the log-log type singularity . We claim that 3.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp1} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0. \end{equation} In particular, we find that $\varphi $ and $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]$ have different singularity types. By theorem 3.1.9 , in order to verify ( 3.16 ), it suffices to verify that 3.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp2} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^1=1. \end{equation} Here $\omega _{\varphi }^1$ is taken in the non-pluripolar sense. Since $\{ 0,\infty \} \subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ is pluripolar, this reduces to showing that \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\frac{1}{4\pi }\int _{\mathbb {C}^*} (\Delta \psi )\, \mathrm{d}\mu =1,  \] where $\psi (z)=\varphi (z)+\log (|z|^2+1)$ and $\mu $ is the standard Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb {C}$. Note that the Laplacian vanishes outside $\overline{B(0,0.7)}$ since $\psi (z)=2+\log |z|^2$ there, which is harmonic. Therefore, \[  \int _{\mathbb {C}^*} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\frac{1}{4\pi }\int _{|z|<1/\sqrt{2}} (\Delta \psi )(z)\, \mathrm{d}\mu .  \] It is an elementary exercise to see that the right-hand side is exactly equal to $1$. If you are familiar with toric geometry, this is more or less trivial since \[  \nabla _ r \Bigl ( \left(-\log (-r)\right)\lor (2+r) \Bigr )\bigl ((-\infty ,-\log 2)\bigr )= (0,1].  \] Otherwise, just try to evaluate the integral using Green's identities. Therefore, ( 3.17 ) is proved and our assertion ( 3.16 ) follows.
3.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp1} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0. \end{equation}
3.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pomegavarphi0temp2} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^1=1. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.15
text: Proposition 3.1.15 . Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and 3.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphimassppsimass_greater} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Then $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$. For simplicity, we write \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ].  \] Note that due to our assumption ( 3.18 ), $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, and hence so is $\varphi \lor \psi $ thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . By corollary 3.1.12 , $\eta $ is a model potential, and $\int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n>0$. Take $C>0$ large enough, so that 3.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intsumintbiggerinttemp1} \int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n. \end{equation} This is possible thanks to proposition 2.2.2 4 . Fix $C'>C$. Write \[  \gamma _{C'}\coloneqq \Bigl (\varphi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr )\land \Bigl (\psi \lor (\eta -C')\Bigr ).  \] Then observe that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $, and \[  \inf _{C'>C}\gamma _{C'}=\varphi \land \psi .  \] Suppose, for contradiction, that $\varphi \land \psi \equiv -\infty $. Then \[  \adjustlimits \lim _{C'\to \infty } \sup _ X\gamma _{C'}=-\infty .  \] Thanks to proposition 3.1.13 , for each $C'>C$, \[  \sup _{X} \gamma _{C'}=\sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta ),  \] since $\eta $ is a model potential. It follows that 3.20 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limsupgammametatemp1} \adjustlimits \lim _{C'\to \infty } \sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta )=-\infty . \end{equation} In particular, we can take $C'$ large enough so that \[  \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C.  \] For such $C'$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \theta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n=& \int _{\{ \gamma _{C'}\leq \eta -C\} } \theta _{\gamma _{C'}}^ n \\  \leq &  \int _{\left\{ \varphi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -C\right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n +\int _{\left\{ \psi \lor (\eta -C')\leq \eta -C \right\} } \theta _{\psi \lor (\eta -C')}^ n\\  =&  2\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} }\theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} }\theta _{\psi }^ n\\  <&  \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the second line follows from 3.1.3 , the fourth line follows from ( 3.19 ). This contradicts the fact that $\gamma _{C'}\sim \eta $ in view of theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$
3.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphimassppsimass_greater} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n. \end{equation}

3.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intsumintbiggerinttemp1} \int _{\{ \varphi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _{\{ \psi >\eta -C\} } \theta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n. \end{equation}
3.20 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limsupgammametatemp1} \adjustlimits \lim _{C'\to \infty } \sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } (\gamma _{C'}-\eta )=-\infty . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.16
text: Proposition 3.1.16 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 3.25 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphipsimodel_landpsh} \varphi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad \psi =P_{\theta }[\psi ],\quad \varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty . \end{equation} Then 3.26 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetaphilandpsi} P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\varphi \land \psi . \end{equation} Proof. Observe that by proposition 3.1.24 3 , \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\varphi ,\quad P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]=\psi .  \] So the $\leq $ direction in ( 3.26 ) holds. The reverse direction is trivial. $\square$
3.25 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphipsimodel_landpsh} \varphi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad \psi =P_{\theta }[\psi ],\quad \varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty . \end{equation}
3.26 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetaphilandpsi} P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\varphi \land \psi . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 3.1.17
text:
Lemma 3.1.17 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that ( 3.25 ) holds and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n>0.  \] Suppose that $\gamma ,\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and satisfy \[  \gamma \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \preceq \psi ,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Then $\gamma \land \eta 
ot\equiv -\infty $ and 3.27  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaeta_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \eta }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Choose constants $A,B>0$ such that \[  \gamma -A\leq \varphi ,\quad \eta -B\leq \psi .  \] Since \[  (\gamma -A)\land (\eta -B)\sim \gamma \land \eta ,  \] the non-pluripolar masses of these two rooftop potentials are equal by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Hence it suffices to prove the lemma after replacing $\gamma ,\eta $ by $\gamma -A,\eta -B$. We can therefore assume that \[  \gamma \leq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq \psi .  \] Step 1 . We first show that $\gamma \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty $ and 3.28  egin{equation} \label{eq:theta_gammalandpsi_mass_temp1} \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} For any $a>1$, we define \[  \gamma _ a\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a\gamma +(1-a)\varphi \Bigr ).  \] When $a=1$, we simply write $\gamma _1=\gamma $. Thanks to corollary 2.4.16 , for any $a\geq 1$, we have $\gamma _ a\leq \varphi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By our assumption, for any $a\geq 1$, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma _ a}^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n> \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \gamma _ a\preceq \varphi ,\quad \varphi \land \psi \preceq \varphi .  \] So proposition 3.1.15 gives \[  \gamma _ a\land \varphi \land \psi =\gamma _ a\land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] In particular, for $a=1$, we find $\gamma \land \psi 
ot\equiv -\infty $. It remains to verify ( 3.28 ). For $a>1$, we have \[  \gamma \geq a^{-1}\gamma _ a+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\varphi ,  \] thanks to the definition of $\gamma _ a$ (cf. ( 2.52 )). Hence \[  \gamma \land \psi \geq a^{-1}\left( \gamma _ a\land \psi ight)+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\left(\varphi \land \psi ight).  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n\geq \left(1-a^{-1}ight)^ n \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n.  \] Letting $a	o \infty $ and taking theorem 2.4.8 into account, ( 3.28 ) follows. Step 2 . We complete the proof. For any $a>1$, we let \[  \eta _ a\coloneqq P_{	heta }\Bigl ( a\eta +(1-a)\psi \Bigr ).  \] When $a=1$, we set $\eta _1=\eta $. Thanks to corollary 2.4.16 , for each $a\geq 1$, we have $\eta _ a\leq \psi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] From Step 1, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\eta _ a}^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n+\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n>\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Applying proposition 3.1.15 again, we find \[  \gamma \land \psi \land \eta _ a =\gamma \land \eta _ a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] When $a=1$, we find $\gamma \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. It remains to prove ( 3.27 ). By definition of $\eta _ a$, we have \[  \eta \geq a^{-1}\eta _ a+\left(1-a^{-1}ight)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  \gamma \land \eta \geq a^{-1} (\gamma \land \eta _ a)+\left(1-a^{-1}ight) \left( \gamma \land \psi ight).  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \eta }^ n\geq \left(1-a^{-1}ight)^ n\int _ X 	heta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n.  \] Letting $a	o \infty $ and applying theorem 2.4.8 again, we arrive at ( 3.27 ). $\square$
3.27 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaeta_temp1} \int _ X \theta _{\gamma \land \eta }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation}
3.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:theta_gammalandpsi_mass_temp1} \int _ X \theta _{\gamma \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 3.1.18
text: Theorem 3.1.18 . Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then 3.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:diamond} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, as otherwise ( 3.29 ) follows immediately from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Step 1 . We claim that it suffices to prove ( 3.29 ) with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. In fact, as $\varphi \land \psi \not\equiv -\infty $, we also have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\land P_{\theta }[\psi ]\not\equiv -\infty $. Moreover, \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n,\quad \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n  \] by proposition 3.1.6 . On the other hand, as $C\to \infty $, the potentials \[  \Bigl ( (\varphi +C)\land V_{\theta } \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ( (\psi +C)\land V_{\theta } \Bigr )  \] converge to $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ almost everywhere. Therefore, thanks to corollary 2.4.9 and theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n.  \] Finally, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\land P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n  \] as well. When the left-hand side vanishes, this follows from theorem 2.4.8 . Otherwise, it follows from 3.1.17 . In particular, ( 3.29 ) is equivalent to the corresponding result with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\varphi $ and $\psi $. Step 2 . We shall assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are model potentials in the sequel. We write $\gamma =\varphi \lor \psi $ for simplicity. Note that $\gamma \leq 0$. For each $C>0$, we introduce \[  \varphi _ C=\varphi \lor (\gamma -C),\quad \psi _ C=\psi \lor (\gamma -C).  \] Note that $\varphi _ C\sim \psi _ C\sim \gamma $. Observe that \[  \inf _{C>0} \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi \land \psi .  \] The $\geq $ direction is trivial, and the $\leq $ direction follows from the observation that the left-hand side is dominated by both $\varphi _ C$ and $\psi _ C$ for any $C>0$, and therefore by both $\varphi $ and $\psi $. For $C>0$, we compute 3.30 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaminusvarphi_temp2} \begin{aligned}  \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n & \\  =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by proposition \gerbyref{B86D7001}{2.2.2} \gerbyref{1C036AD6}{1}}\\  =&  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by theorem \gerbyref{D18E0263}{3.1.7}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} In the last line we use that $\varphi $ is model, so $\theta _\varphi ^ n$ is carried by $\{ \varphi =0\} \subseteq \{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} $. We also get a similar formula for $\theta _{\psi _ C}^ n$. Therefore, taking the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 into consideration, we find 3.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intthetagammaminusvarphi_temp1} \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{equation} On the other hand, using 3.1.3 and ( 3.30 ), we find \[  \begin{aligned}  \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C\} } \, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n \\  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\varphi _ C=0\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=\psi _ C=0\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\\ & +\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] In particular, \[  \mathds {1}_{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C<0 \} }\,  \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\mathds {1}_{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n.  \] Integrating, we find \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{\{  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C=0 \} } \theta _{\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C}^ n \geq &  \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n-\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where on the first line we used the fact that $\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C\sim \gamma $, while on the second line, we used ( 3.34 ). Letting $C\to \infty $, and using corollary 2.4.11 , we conclude ( 3.29 ). $\square$

3.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:diamond} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n+\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n. \end{equation}

3.30 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetagammaminusvarphi_temp2} \begin{aligned}  \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n & \\  =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by proposition \gerbyref{B86D7001}{2.2.2} \gerbyref{1C036AD6}{1}}\\  =&  \theta _{\varphi }^ n+ \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n &  \textup{by theorem \gerbyref{D18E0263}{3.1.7}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

3.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intthetagammaminusvarphi_temp1} \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n,\quad \int _ X \theta _{\gamma }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _{\{ \psi \leq \gamma -C\} } \theta _{\psi _ C}^ n. \end{equation}

title: Definition 3.1.19
text: Definition 3.1.19 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and a function $f\colon X\to [-\infty ,\infty ]$, we define \[  P_\theta [\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\bigl \{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\  \eta \preceq \varphi \bigr \} .  \]

title: Example 3.1.20
text: Example 3.1.20 . When $f=0$, we have $P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. When $\varphi =V_{\theta }$, we have $P_\theta [V_{\theta }](f)=P_{\theta }(f)$. So definition 3.1.19 is a common generalization of definition 3.1.4 and definition 2.4.12 .

title: Proposition 3.1.21
text: Proposition 3.1.21 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ with $\varphi \leq f$. Then \[  \theta ^ n_{P_\theta [\varphi ](f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=f\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] In particular, \[  \theta ^ n_{P_\theta [\varphi ]} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\theta [\varphi ]=0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n.  \] Proof. By definition, we have \[  P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=P_\theta [\varphi ]\Bigl (P_\theta (f)\Bigr )  \] and $\varphi \leq P_\theta (f)$. By corollary 3.1.8 and corollary 2.4.25 , \[  \theta ^ n_{P_\theta [\varphi ](f)} \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=P_\theta (f)\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)} = \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=f\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_ f.  \] The reverse inequality follows immediately from theorem 2.4.24 . $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.22
text: Proposition 3.1.22 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $f\in C^{1,\overline{1}}(X)$ with $\varphi \leq f$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_\varphi , \\  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta [\varphi ](f)} =&  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)\} }\, \theta ^ n_\varphi . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. By corollary 2.4.25 and theorem 2.4.24 , we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta (f)}=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_{f}=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)=f\} }\, \theta ^ n_{\varphi }\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta (f)\} }\, \theta ^ n_{\varphi }.  \] The reverse inequality follows from 2.4.10 . The first equality follows. As for the second, we compute using proposition 3.1.21 and theorem 2.4.24 that \[  \begin{split}  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_{P_\theta [\varphi ](f)}=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=f\right\} }\, \theta ^ n_{f}\\  =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)=f\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi =P_\theta [\varphi ](f)\} }\, \theta ^ n_\varphi . \end{split}  \] Since $\varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ](f)$, 2.4.10 gives the opposite inequality. The second equality follows. $\square$

title: 3.1.2 Properties of the -envelope
Proposition 3.1.23
text: Proposition 3.1.23 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ to $X$. Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have \[  P_{\pi ^*\theta }[\pi ^*\varphi ]=\pi ^*P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] In particular, a potential $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is model if and only if $\pi ^*\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\pi ^*\theta )_{>0}$ is model. Proof. By proposition 1.5.8 , every $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\pi ^*\theta )$ is of the form $\chi =\pi ^*\psi $ for a unique $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Since $\pi $ is surjective, $\chi \leq 0$ if and only if $\psi \leq 0$. Moreover, \[  \chi \preceq \pi ^*\varphi \Longleftrightarrow \psi \preceq \varphi .  \] Thus the candidates defining $P_{\pi ^*\theta }[\pi ^*\varphi ]$ are exactly the pull-backs of the candidates defining $P_\theta [\varphi ]$, and hence \[  P_{\pi ^*\theta }[\pi ^*\varphi ]=\pi ^*P_\theta [\varphi ].  \] Finally, the non-pluripolar mass is preserved under bimeromorphic pull-back by proposition 2.4.3 . Therefore $\varphi $ is model of positive mass if and only if $\pi ^*\varphi $ is. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.24
text: Proposition 3.1.24 . Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then \[  P_{\lambda \theta }[\lambda \varphi ]=\lambda P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] Suppose that $\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _1)$ and $\varphi _2\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _2)$. Then \[  P_{\theta _1+\theta _2}[\varphi _1+\varphi _2]\geq P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]+P_{\theta _2}[\varphi _2].  \] Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq \psi $. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ].  \] Proof. 1 This follows by rescaling the candidates in the definition of the $P$-envelope. 2 Suppose that $\psi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _1)$ and $\psi _2\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _2)$ satisfy \[  \psi _ i\leq 0,\quad \psi _ i\preceq \varphi _ i  \] for $i=1,2$. Then \[  \psi _1+\psi _2\leq 0,\quad \psi _1+\psi _2\preceq \varphi _1+\varphi _2.  \] It follows from ( 3.3 ) that \[  \psi _1+\psi _2\leq P_{\theta _1+\theta _2}[\varphi _1+\varphi _2].  \] Since $\psi _1$ and $\psi _2$ are arbitrary, we conclude. 3 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.25
text: Proposition 3.1.25 . Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a decreasing net of potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying $P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]=\varphi _ j$ for each $j\in I$. Set $\varphi \coloneqq \inf _{j\in I} \varphi _ j$. Then $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\varphi $. Proof. Since $P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j]=\varphi _ j$, we have $\sup _ X\varphi _ j=0$. By corollary 1.5.6 , we have $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\varphi \leq 0$. Therefore, for each $j\in I$, \[  \varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi _ j] =\varphi _ j.  \] Therefore, $\varphi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.26

text: 3.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Palmostmodeltemp} P_{\theta +\epsilon _ i\omega }\left[\varphi _ i\right]=\varphi _ i \end{equation}
3.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:massmodeldec} \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \left(\theta + \epsilon _ i \omega \right)^ n_{\varphi _ i}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation}
