title: Corollary 3.1.27
text: Corollary 3.1.27 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then \[  \varphi =\inf _{\epsilon >0} P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ].  \] Proof. Set \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ].  \] Since $\varphi $ is model, $\varphi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]$ for every $\epsilon >0$, hence $\varphi \leq \eta \leq 0$. Next we prove the reverse direction. Applying proposition 3.1.26 to the decreasing net $(P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ])_{\epsilon >0}$ and using proposition 3.1.6 , we get \[  P_\theta [\eta ]=\eta ,\quad \int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\int _ X\theta _\varphi ^ n.  \] Thus $\eta $ is a candidate in the characterization theorem 3.1.9 of $P_\theta [\varphi ]$. Hence $\eta \leq P_\theta [\varphi ]=\varphi $. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.28
text: Proposition 3.1.28 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net of potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ uniformly bounded from above. Let $\varphi \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] In particular, if $\varphi _ i$ is model for all $i\in I$, then so is $\varphi $. Proof. We may assume that $I$ is infinite since otherwise, there is nothing to prove. We write \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i].  \] Then it is clear that $\eta \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. By corollary 2.4.9 , we have \[  \lim _{i\in I} \int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n>0.  \] We may assume that for each $i\in I$, $\int _ X\theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n<\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$, since otherwise $P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ by theorem 3.1.9 , and the same holds for all $j\geq i$; in that case there is nothing to prove. So by 2.4.15 , we can find a decreasing net $\epsilon _ i\searrow 0$ ($i\in I$) with $\epsilon _ i\in (0,1)$ and $\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ ($i\in I$) such that for all $i\in I$, \[  (1-\epsilon _ i) \varphi +\epsilon _ i\psi _ i\leq \varphi _ i.  \] We may, for example, take 3.50 \begin{equation} \label{eq:epsilon_inetchoice} \epsilon _ i^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\left( 1+\left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right). \end{equation} By the concavity property of the envelope proposition 3.1.24 , we have \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\epsilon _ i P_{\theta }[\psi _ i]\leq (1-\epsilon _ i) P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\epsilon _ i P_{\theta }[\psi _ i]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi _ i]\leq \eta .  \] Each $P_{\theta }[\psi _ i]$ has supremum $0$, hence the family is bounded in $L^1$ by proposition 1.5.4 . Thus $\epsilon _ iP_{\theta }[\psi _ i]\to 0$ in $L^1$. The previous inequality then gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq \eta $ almost everywhere, and hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . $\square$

3.50 \begin{equation} \label{eq:epsilon_inetchoice} \epsilon _ i^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\left( 1+\left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right). \end{equation}

title: 3.1.3 Relative full mass classes
text:
3.1.3 Relative full mass classes Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Fix a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Definition 3.1.29 . We define \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \preceq \phi \right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \sim \phi \right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi ): \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n\right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi ): \int _ X |\phi -\eta |\, \theta _{\eta }^ n<\infty \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Potentials in the last three classes are said to have relatively minimal singularities , full mass and finite energy relative to $\phi $ respectively. We have the following inclusions: 3.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:energyclassinc} \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation} The only non-trivial part is the first inclusion, which follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Remark 3.1.30 . Note that this integral \[  \int _ X |\phi -\eta |\, \theta _{\eta }^ n  \] is defined: The locus where $\phi -\eta $ is undefined is a pluripolar set, while the product $\theta _{\eta }^ n$ puts no mass on pluripolar sets (proposition 2.2.2 ). Similar remarks apply when we talk about similar integrals in the sequel. When $\phi =V_{\theta }$, we usually write \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;V_{\theta })=&  \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ),\\  \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;V_{\theta })=&  \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ),\\  \mathcal{E}^{1}(X,\theta ;V_{\theta })=&  \mathcal{E}^{1}(X,\theta ). \end{aligned}  \] Potentials in the three classes are said to have minimal singularities , full mass and finite energy respectively. The relation ( 3.55 ) can be written as \[  \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta )\subseteq \mathcal{E}^{1}(X,\theta ) \subseteq \mathcal{E}(X,\theta )  \] in this case. The $P$-envelope can be used to characterize the full mass classes: Proposition 3.1.31 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$; $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\phi $. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By proposition 3.1.6 , \[  \int _ X\theta _\varphi ^ n=\int _ X\theta _{P_\theta [\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X\theta _\phi ^ n.  \] Moreover, since the mass is positive, theorem 3.1.9 implies that \[  \varphi \preceq P_\theta [\varphi ]=\phi .  \] Thus $\varphi \in \mathcal E(X,\theta ;\phi )$. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Then $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Note that $\phi $ is a candidate of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ as in ( 3.12 ). So $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\geq \phi $. The reverse inequality is trivial. $\square$ We have the following comparison principle. Proposition 3.1.32 (Comparison principle) . Fix $j\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $. Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ j$ be closed smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ and $\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,j$. Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi1} \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation} As a consequence, we also have 3.60 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi12} \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation} Proof. Observe that $\varphi \lor \psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, as a consequence of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Using the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  \geq &  \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}+\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  =&  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & +\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  =& \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & +\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}, \end{aligned}  \] where in the last step, we applied proposition 3.1.6 to $\varphi $ and $\varphi \lor \psi $. Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} }&  \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & \geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{aligned}  \] Applying the preceding inequality to $\varphi +\epsilon $ in place of $\varphi $, and using $\theta _{\varphi +\epsilon }=\theta _\varphi $, we get \[  \int _{\{ \varphi +\epsilon \leq \psi \} }\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j} \geq \int _{\{ \varphi +\epsilon <\psi \} }\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}.  \] As $\epsilon \searrow 0$, by monotone convergence theorem, we obtain \[  \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j} \geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j},  \] which proves ( 3.59 ). Finally, the ( 3.60 ) follows by subtracting ( 3.59 ) (with the role of $\varphi $ and $\psi $ switched) from the total mixed mass equality \[  \int _ X\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}= \int _ X\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j},  \] which itself follows from proposition 3.1.6 and proposition 3.1.31 . $\square$ The full mass potentials are essential in resolving the Monge–Ampère equations. We recall the following two Aubin–Yau type theorems. Recall that a measure $\mu $ on $X$ is non-pluripolar if it is a Radon measure and $\mu (K)=0$ for each pluripolar set $K\subseteq X$. Note. Here we identify as usual a Radon measure with its completion. Theorem 3.1.33 . Let $\mu $ be a non-pluripolar measure on $X$ with $\mu (X)=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n$. Then there is a unique $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ such that \[  \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mu ,\quad \sup _ X \varphi =0.  \] Theorem 3.1.34 . Fix $\lambda >0$. Let $\mu $ be a non-pluripolar measure on $X$ with $\mu (X)>0$. Then there is a unique $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ such that \[  \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda \varphi }\mu .  \] Furthermore, for any $\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ satisfying \[  \theta _{\psi }^ n\geq \mathrm{e}^{\lambda \psi }\mu ,  \] we have $\varphi \geq \psi $. The proofs are beyond the scope of this book; we refer to [ DDNL19log ] . In order to handle the finite energy classes, it is convenient to introduce the following quantity: Definition 3.1.35 . We define the Monge–Ampère energy $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ as follows 3.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Edefbdd} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}. \end{equation} More generally, we extend $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$ to a functional $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ as follows 3.70 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Eextendgeneral} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \inf \left\{ E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi ):\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ),\varphi \leq \psi \right\} . \end{equation} We write $E_{\theta }$ instead of $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$ when $\phi =V_{\theta }$. The set in ( 3.70 ) is non-empty, since $\phi +\sup _ X \varphi $ is a candidate. Therefore, $E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )<\infty $. Note that 3.71 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ephiaddcst} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi +C)=E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )+C\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \end{equation} for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Lemma 3.1.36 . The functional $E_{\theta }^{\phi }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is increasing. In particular, the extended definition ( 3.70 ) agrees with ( 3.69 ) on $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, and is increasing as well. Proof. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & (n+1)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )-(n+1)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \left( \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \right)\\ & +\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j} \right)\\  =&  \sum _{\substack {j+a+b=n-1,\\ \begin{bgroup}  j,a,b\geq 0

\end{bgroup}}} (n-j)\int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\phi }^ a\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b+1}\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^ j- \theta _{\phi }^ a\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b}\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j+1}\right)\\ & +\sum _{\substack {j+a+b=n-1,\\ \begin{bgroup}  j,a,b\geq 0

\end{bgroup}}} (n-j)\int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\phi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{a+1}\wedge \theta _{\psi }^ b- \theta _{\phi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{a}\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b+1}\right)\\  =& 0, \end{aligned}  \] where the third equality follows from the integration by parts formula. See [ Xia19b , Lu21 ] for the proof in the context of non-pluripolar products. In other words, 3.81 \begin{equation} \label{eq:int_by_part_E_temp1} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}. \end{equation} The monotonicity follows. $\square$ Lemma 3.1.37 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.82 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_int_ene} \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n \geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )\geq \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Thanks to ( 3.71 ), we may assume that $\varphi \geq \psi $. As we have seen in ( 3.81 ), the middle term can be written as \[  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}.  \] We claim that for each individual $j$, the inequality ( 3.82 ) holds: \[  \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n \geq \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \geq \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Thanks to proposition 3.1.32 , we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}=& \int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi +t\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\, \mathrm{d}t\\  \geq &  \int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi +t\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t \\  =&  \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] The other inequality is similar. $\square$ Lemma 3.1.38 . The function $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is concave. Proof. Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We write $\varphi _ t=t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0$ for each $t\in [0,1]$. We claim that for each $t\in [0,1]$, we have 3.86 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ddtEphi_temp1} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _ t) =\int _ X \left(\varphi _1-\varphi _0\right)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n. \end{equation} At the boundary $t=0,1$, the derivative is understood as the one-sided derivative. Since $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, the difference $\varphi _1-\varphi _0$ is quasi-everywhere bounded. Hence all mixed integrals below are finite. We compute the right derivative first. Fix $t\in [0,1)$ and take $s>0$ small enough so that $t+s\leq 1$. By the cocycle formula ( 3.81 ), \[  \begin{aligned}  \frac{E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _{t+s})-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _ t)}{s} =& \frac{1}{(n+1)s}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi _{t+s}-\varphi _ t)\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j}\\  =& \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] For each fixed $j$, the last integral is a polynomial in $s$ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 . Letting $s\to 0+$, it converges to \[  \int _ X(\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n.  \] Thus the right derivative is given by the right-hand side of ( 3.86 ). The proof for the left derivative is identical, using $s<0$ with $t+s\in [0,1]$. Hence the left and right derivatives agree for $t\in (0,1)$, and the endpoint derivatives are the corresponding one-sided derivatives. Now it suffices to show that the derivative ( 3.86 ) is decreasing in $t$. Take $0\leq s<t \leq 1$. We wish to show that \[  \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ s}^ n.  \] This can be equivalently written as \[  \int _ X (\varphi _ t-\varphi _ s)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _ t-\varphi _ s)\, \theta _{\varphi _ s}^ n.  \] In particular, replacing $\varphi _0$ by $\varphi _ s$ and $\varphi _1$ by $\varphi _ t$, we are reduced to proving the following \[  \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _1}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _0}^ n.  \] But this is just a consequence of 3.1.37 . $\square$ Proposition 3.1.39 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ with \[  \varphi =\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i\not\equiv -\infty .  \] Then 3.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:E_cont_decnet} \lim _{i\in I} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. We first handle the case where $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a decreasing sequence. Thanks to 3.1.36 , we know that $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)$ is decreasing in $i$. So the limit in ( 3.89 ) exists and the $\geq $ inequality holds. Conversely, let $\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $\varphi \leq \psi $. We need to show that \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )\geq \lim _{i\to \infty } E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\varphi _ i\lor \psi \right).  \] Replacing the sequence $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ by $(\varphi _ i\lor \psi )_ i$, we are reduced to proving the $\leq $ direction of ( 3.89 ) when $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, thanks to 3.1.37 , we have \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )\leq \int _ X (\varphi _ i-\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Our assertion follows from the monotone convergence theorem. We now treat the general net case. By 3.1.36 , the net $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)$ is decreasing and bounded below by $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. Thus \[  L\coloneqq \lim _{i\in I}E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)  \] exists and satisfies $L\geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Since $\varphi \leq \varphi _ i$ for every $i\in I$, the hypotheses of corollary 1.5.6 are satisfied, and hence $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {L^1}\varphi $. For each $k\geq 1$, choose $a_ k\in I$ such that \[  \| \varphi _ i-\varphi \| _{L^1}<k^{-1},\quad i\geq a_ k.  \] We can recursively choose an increasing sequence $(i_ k)_{k\geq 1}$ in $I$ such that $i_ k\geq a_ k$ for all $k$. Then $(\varphi _{i_ k})_ k$ is a decreasing sequence and $\varphi _{i_ k}\to \varphi $ in $L^1$. Its pointwise decreasing limit is therefore equal to $\varphi $ almost everywhere, hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . Applying the sequence case to $(\varphi _{i_ k})_ k$, we get \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{i_ k})=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ).  \] Since $L\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{i_ k})$ for every $k$, we conclude $L\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. $\square$ Proposition 3.1.40 . Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. The following are equivalent: $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$; $E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )>-\infty $. Proof. Fix $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. In particular, $\varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\phi ]=\phi $. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . Using the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we have that $\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n$ converges strongly Note. Namely, the convergence holds after integrating against any $L^{\infty }$ function. to $\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ as $C\to \infty $ by the dominated convergence theorem. Therefore, for a fixed $D>0$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -D)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=& \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\}  } \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -D)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\}  } \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } (n+1)E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C) \Bigr )\\  \geq &  (n+1)E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{aligned}  \] Here the last but one inequality follows from ( 3.69 ) and the fact that $\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \phi $. Letting $D\to \infty $, we conclude 1 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Observe the following inclusions: \[  \{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} \subseteq \left\{  \varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \frac{1}{2}\Bigl ( \psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C \Bigr ) \right\} \subseteq \{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} .  \] By proposition 3.1.32 , we find \[  \begin{aligned} & C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}\\  \leq & _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  = &  2^{n-k}C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Here on the final step, we have We now pass from sequences to nets. By 3.1.36 , the net $(E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i))_{i\in I}$ is increasing and bounded above by $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. For this purpose, we shall need a few preliminary results. We shall approximate the rooftop operator by solutions of certain Monge–Ampère equations. Lemma 3.1.48 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then there is $\gamma \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ such that 3.147 \begin{equation} \label{eq:solution_thetavarphiephiu} \theta _{\gamma }^ n=\mathrm{e}^{\gamma -\varphi }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathrm{e}^{\gamma -\psi }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n. \end{equation} It is not clear if $\int _ X\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\theta _{\varphi }^ n<\infty $, hence we cannot say that $\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\theta _{\varphi }^ n+\mathrm{e}^{-\psi }\theta _{\psi }^ n$ is a Radon measure, so theorem 3.1.34 is not directly applicable. Proof. For each $j\geq 1$, let $\varphi _ j\coloneqq \varphi \lor (-j)$, $\psi _ j\coloneqq \psi \lor (-j)$. These functions are not necessarily $\theta $-psh. By theorem 3.1.34 again, $\gamma _ j$ is decreasing in $j$; let $\gamma =\inf _{j>0}\gamma _ j$. Then $\gamma \geq \eta $, hence $\gamma \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Now observe that \[  \theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{\gamma }^ n  \] as $j\to \infty $, by theorem 2.4.7 . Therefore, for each $j>0$, \[  \gamma _ j\leq \varphi _ j+C',\quad \gamma _ j\leq \psi _ j+C'.  \] Hence, ( 3.147 ) follows from ( 3.148 ) and the dominated convergence theorem by letting $j\to \infty $. $\square$ We also need a few integral estimates. Lemma 3.1.49 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\gamma \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that $\varphi \leq \psi \leq \gamma $. Then \[  \int _ X (\gamma -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq 2^{n+1}\int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Proof. Observe that for any $t\geq 0$, 3.154 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ppgcomp} \begin{split}  \{ \gamma >\psi +2t\} \setminus \{ \psi =-\infty \} \subseteq \left\{ (\gamma +\psi )/2>\psi +t\right\} \\  \subseteq \left\{ (\gamma +\psi )/2>\varphi +t\right\} \subseteq \{ \gamma >\varphi +t\} . \end{split} \end{equation} So \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X (\gamma -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n =&  2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \gamma -\psi >2t\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t & \\  \leq &  2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\left\{ (\gamma +\psi )/2>\psi +t\right\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t &  \textup{by (\gerbyref{E29AC9D9}{3.154})}\\  \leq &  2^{n+1}\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\left\{ (\gamma +\psi )/2>\varphi +t\right\} }\, \theta _{(\gamma +\psi )/2}^ n\, \mathrm{d}t & \\  \leq &  2^{n+1}\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\left\{ (\gamma +\psi )/2>\varphi +t\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t &  \textup{by proposition \gerbyref{EEAA4F47}{3.1.32}}\\  \leq & 2^{n+1}\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\left\{ \gamma >\varphi +t\right\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t & \textup{by (\gerbyref{E29AC9D9}{3.154})}\\  =&  2^{n+1} \int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n & . \end{aligned}  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Lemma 3.1.50 . Let $\varphi _ j\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ ($j\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$) and $\gamma \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\leq \gamma $ for each $j$ and that $\varphi _ j$ converges to $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with respect to the $L^1$-topology. Assume that there is a constant $A>0$ such that for any $j>0$, \[  \int _ X (\varphi _ j-\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq -A.  \] Then $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and 3.163 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphigammageqm2np3A} \int _ X (\varphi -\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq - 2^{n+3}A. \end{equation} Proof. Replacing simultaneously $\gamma ,\varphi _ j,\varphi $ by $\gamma -B,\varphi _ j-B,\varphi -B$ for $B\gg 1$, we may assume that $\gamma \leq 0$. The assumptions and the conclusion are invariant under this translation. Since $\gamma \in \mathcal E(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $P_\theta [\phi ]=\phi $, we then have $\gamma \leq \phi $. Step 1 . Assume that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing. In this case, we prove 3.164 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphigammageqm4A_temp1} \int _ X (\varphi -\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq -4A. \end{equation} By 3.1.43 , for any $j, k>0$, \[  \int _ X (\varphi _ j-\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\geq -4A.  \] For any $C>0$, \[  \int _ X \Bigl (\varphi _ j \lor (\gamma -C)-\gamma \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\geq \int _ X (\varphi _ j-\gamma ) \, \theta _{\varphi _ k}^ n\geq -4A.  \] Letting $k\to \infty $, by theorem 2.4.7 , we find \[  \int _ X \Bigl (\varphi _ j \lor (\gamma -C)-\gamma \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq -4A.  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, by the monotone convergence theorem, we get \[  \int _ X \Bigl (\varphi \lor (\gamma -C)-\gamma \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq -4A.  \] Then we let $C\to \infty $, again by the monotone convergence theorem, we conclude ( 3.164 ). Step 2 . In general, let \[  \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ k.  \] Then $\varphi =\inf _{j>0}\psi _ j$ due to corollary 1.2.8 . For each $C>0$, let \[  \psi _{j,C}=\psi _ j \lor (\gamma -C),\quad \varphi _ C=\varphi \lor (\gamma -C).  \] Then $\psi _{j,C},\varphi _ C\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ since $\gamma -C\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Observe that $\psi _{j,C}$ decreases to $\varphi _ C$ as $j\to \infty $. Moreover, \[  \gamma \geq \psi _{j,C} \geq \psi _ j\geq \varphi _ j.  \] By 3.1.49 , \[  \int _ X (\psi _{j,C}-\gamma )\, \theta _{\psi _{j,C}}^ n\geq -2^{n+1}A.  \] By Step 1, 3.165 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproof1} \int _ X(\varphi _ C-\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\geq -2^{n+3}A. \end{equation} In particular, by the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , \[  \int _{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} }(\varphi -\gamma )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\geq -2^{n+3}A.  \] Letting $C\to \infty $, we conclude ( 3.163 ). As a consequence, \[  \int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n<\infty .  \] We still have to prove that $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In fact, by ( 3.165 ), for any $C>0$, \[  \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\leq \frac{1}{C}\int _ X (\gamma -\varphi _ C)\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n\leq 2^{n+3}C^{-1}A.  \] Using the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 and the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we find \[  \int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n=\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi _ C}^ n+\int _{\{ \varphi >\gamma -C\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Letting $C\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Proposition 3.1.51 . Assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ (resp. $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$), then so is $\varphi \land \psi $. Proof. The case of $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is trivial. We consider the case $\mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. It follows from proposition 3.1.15 that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By theorem 3.1.18 , we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , equality holds. By theorem 3.1.9 , we conclude that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\phi .  \] Finally, assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq \phi $. For each $j\geq 1$, consider the approximations: \[  \varphi _ j\coloneqq \varphi \lor (\phi -j)\, ,\quad \psi _ j\coloneqq \psi \lor (\phi -j).  \] By 3.1.48 , we can take $\gamma _ j\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ solving the following equation: \[  \theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n=\mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n+\mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\psi _ j}\, \theta _{\psi _ j}^ n.  \] In particular, \[  \theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n\geq \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n.  \] We claim that this implies $\gamma _ j\leq \varphi _ j$. Indeed, by proposition 3.1.32 , \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _ j<\gamma _ j\} }\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n \geq \int _{\{ \varphi _ j<\gamma _ j\} }\theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n \geq \int _{\{ \varphi _ j<\gamma _ j\} }\mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n.  \] Hence \[  \int _{\{ \varphi _ j<\gamma _ j\} }\left(\mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}-1\right)\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=0.  \] It follows that $\int _{\{ \varphi _ j<\gamma _ j\} }\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=0$, and the domination principle theorem 2.4.17 gives $\gamma _ j\leq \varphi _ j$. Similarly, $\gamma _ j\leq \psi _ j$. In particular, $\gamma _ j\leq \varphi _ j\land \psi _ j$. We claim that 3.166 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intgammajphi_unif_lower} \int _ X (\gamma _ j-\phi )\, \theta _{\gamma _ j}^ n >-C \end{equation} for some $C$ independent of $j$. Assume the claim is true for now. We get immediately that \[  \sup _{X}\gamma _ j=\sup _{X\setminus \{ \phi =-\infty \} }(\gamma _ j-\phi )\geq -\frac{C}{\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n},  \] where the first equality follows from proposition 3.1.13 . By proposition 1.5.4 , after possibly extracting a subsequence, we may assume that $\gamma _ j\to \gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ in $L^1$-topology. Then $\gamma \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ by 3.1.50 and proposition 3.1.40 . Since $\gamma \leq \varphi \land \psi \leq \phi $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X\theta _\phi ^ n.  \] Moreover, by the monotonicity of $E^\phi _\theta $, \[  E^\phi _\theta (\varphi \land \psi )\geq E^\phi _\theta (\gamma )>-\infty .  \] Thus $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathcal E^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ by proposition 3.1.40 . Now we prove the claim ( 3.166 ). By symmetry, it suffices to prove \[  \int _ X (\phi -\gamma _ j) \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\leq C.  \] But note that \[  \int _ X (\phi -\gamma _ j) \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X (\phi -\varphi _ j) \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n+\int _ X (\varphi _ j-\gamma _ j) \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n.  \] But $x \mathrm{e}^{-x}\leq \mathrm{e}^{-1}$ for $x\geq 0$ (with maximum at $x=1$), so the second term is bounded; it remains to prove \[  \int _ X (\phi -\varphi _ j) \mathrm{e}^{\gamma _ j-\varphi _ j}\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\leq C.  \] As $\gamma _ j\leq \varphi _ j$, it suffices to prove 3.167 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproof2} \int _ X (\phi -\varphi _ j)\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\leq C. \end{equation} We compute, using ( 3.69 ) and the fact that the $k<n$ terms $\int _ X(\varphi _ j-\phi )\theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _\phi ^{n-k}$ are all non-positive (since $\varphi _ j\leq \phi $), \[  \int _ X (\varphi _ j-\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\geq (n+1)E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ j).  \] Since $\varphi _ j\searrow \varphi $ and $E_\theta ^{\phi }$ is continuous along decreasing sequences (proposition 3.1.39 ), $E_\theta ^{\phi }(\varphi _ j)$ is bounded below uniformly in $j$. Thus, ( 3.167 ) follows. $\square$ Proposition 3.1.52 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be potentials such that $\varphi \preceq \psi \preceq \phi $. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ (resp. $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$), then so is $\psi $. Proof. We may assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. The case $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is trivial. The case $\mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ follows from theorem 2.4.8 . The case $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ follows from the characterization of $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ in proposition 3.1.40 and the monotonicity of $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$ proved in 3.1.36 . $\square$ Proposition 3.1.53 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a uniformly bounded from above non-empty family in $\mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ (resp. $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$), then so is $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i$. Proof. Thanks to proposition 3.1.52 , it suffices to show that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i\preceq \phi .  \] Since $\phi $ is model and $\varphi _ i\preceq \phi $, we know that \[  \varphi _ i-\sup _ X \varphi _ i \leq \phi  \] for any $i\in I$. Since $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is uniformly bounded from above by assumption, our assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 3.1.54 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C > 0}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land \psi =\psi .  \] Proof. The first equality follows from the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. We focus on the second equality. Since for each $C\geq 0$, \[  (\varphi \land \psi +C)\land \psi \leq (\varphi +C)\land \psi \leq \psi ,  \] we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi \land \psi $ (cf. proposition 3.1.51 ) and assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. Let \[  \gamma \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C > 0}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land \psi .  \] Observe that $\gamma \leq \psi $, and $\gamma \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ due to proposition 3.1.51 and proposition 3.1.53 . Then corollary 3.1.8 guarantees that \[  \int _{\{ \gamma <\psi \}  } \theta _{\gamma }^ n=0.  \] Therefore, we can apply the domination principle theorem 2.4.17 to conclude that $\gamma =\psi $. $\square$ Lemma 3.1.55 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Define \[  \eta _ t\coloneqq \Bigl ( (1-t)\varphi +t\psi \Bigr )\land \psi ,\quad t\in [0,1].  \] Then $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _ t)$ is differentiable for $t\in [0,1]$ and 3.168 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Iphit_diff} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _ t)=\int _{X} \Bigl ( \psi -\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \}  \Bigr )\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n. \end{equation} The derivatives at $t=0$ or $1$ are understood as one-sided derivatives. Proof. Let us prove ( 3.168 ) with right-derivative instead of derivative, and $t\in [0,1)$. The left-derivative case is completely parallel. For each $t\in [0,1]$, we let \[  f_ t=\min \{  (1-t)\varphi +t\psi , \psi \} .  \] Fix $t\in [0,1)$ and $s>0$ small enough so that $t+s<1$. Thanks to proposition 3.1.46 , we have \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _{t+s})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _{t})\leq &  \int _ X \left(\eta _{t+s}-\eta _ t\right)\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n \\  =&  \int _ X \left(\eta _{t+s}-f_ t\right)\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n & \textup{by \gerbyref{FEE0E763}{3.1.3}}\\  \leq &  \int _ X \left(f_{t+s}-f_ t \right)\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n\\  =&  s\int _ X \Bigl (\psi -\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} \Bigr )\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Similarly, we get \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _{t+s})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\eta _{t})\geq s\int _ X \Bigl (\psi -\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} \Bigr )\, \theta _{\eta _{t+s}}^ n.  \] Observe that $\eta _{t+s}$ converges in capacity (in fact, even uniformly) to $\eta _ t$ as $s\to 0+$. The desired result ( 3.168 ) is then just a consequence of theorem 2.3.8 . $\square$ Lemma 3.1.56 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{1}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, and set \[  \varphi _ t\coloneqq (1-t)\varphi +t\psi ,\qquad t\in [0,1].  \] Then the function \[  t\mapsto E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ t)  \] is differentiable on $[0,1]$, where the derivative at the endpoints is understood as the one-sided derivative. Moreover, 3.173 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Eaffinediff} \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ t) = \int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n. \end{equation} Proof. By corollary 3.1.42 , $\varphi _ t\in \mathcal E^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ for all $t\in [0,1]$. For $a=0,\ldots ,n$, put \[  M_ a=\int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ a\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{n-a}.  \] Note that each $M_ a$ is finite by corollary 3.1.44 . By the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 , the quantity \[  \int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n  \] is therefore a polynomial in $t$ with coefficients given by the $M_ a$'s. In particular, the right-hand side of ( 3.173 ) is finite and continuous in $t$. We prove the formula for the right derivative at a point $t\in [0,1)$. Let $s>0$ be small enough so that $t+s\leq 1$. By the cocycle formula proposition 3.1.45 , we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \frac{E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{t+s})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ t)}{s} =& \frac{1}{(n+1)s}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi _{t+s}-\varphi _ t)\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j} \\  =& \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] Again by proposition 2.2.2 6 , for each fixed $j$ the last integral is a polynomial in $s$, expressed as a linear combination of the $M_ a$'s with coefficients depending on $t$. Letting $s\to 0+$, it converges to \[  \int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \lim _{s\to 0+} \frac{E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{t+s})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ t)}{s} = \int _ X(\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n.  \] The proof for the left derivative is identical, using $s<0$ with $t+s\in [0,1]$. Thus the left and right derivatives agree for $t\in (0,1)$, and the endpoint derivatives are given by the same formula. $\square$ In particular, we have a diamond-like inequality. Corollary 3.1.57 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.176 \begin{equation} \label{eq:diam_E} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi \lor \psi )+E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi \land \psi )\geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )+E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that ( 3.176 ) is known in that case. For each $C>0$, we let \[  \varphi _ C=\varphi \lor (\phi -C),\quad \psi _ C=\psi \lor (\phi -C).  \] Then \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ C\lor \psi _ C)+E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ C\land \psi _ C)\geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi _ C)+E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ C).  \] As $C\to \infty $, we have \[  \varphi _ C\searrow \varphi ,\quad \psi _ C\searrow \psi ,\quad \varphi _ C\lor \psi _ C\searrow \varphi \lor \psi ,  \] and, by the monotonicity and maximality of the rooftop, \[  \varphi _ C\land \psi _ C\searrow \varphi \land \psi .  \] Applying proposition 3.1.39 to these four decreasing sequences gives ( 3.176 ). Step 2 . We assume that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Thanks to 3.1.56 and the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we have \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi \lor \psi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )=& \int _0^1\int _ X (\varphi \lor \psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{(1-t)\varphi +t(\varphi \lor \psi )}^ n\, \mathrm{d}t\\  =&  \int _0^1 \int _{\{ \psi >\varphi \} } (\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{(1-t)\varphi +t\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t. \end{aligned}  \] On the other hand, \[  \begin{aligned} & E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi \land \psi )\\  =&  \int _0^1 \int _ X (\psi -\min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} )\, \theta _{((1-t)\varphi +t\psi )\land \psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t\\  \leq &  \int _0^1 \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } (\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{(1-t)\varphi +t\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t&  \textup{by \gerbyref{FEE0E763}{3.1.3}}. \end{aligned}  \] Adding these equations together, we conclude ( 3.176 ). $\square$

title: Definition 3.1.29
text: Definition 3.1.29 . We define \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \preceq \phi \right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \sim \phi \right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi ): \int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n\right\} ,\\  \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\coloneqq & \left\{ \eta \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi ): \int _ X |\phi -\eta |\, \theta _{\eta }^ n<\infty \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Potentials in the last three classes are said to have relatively minimal singularities , full mass and finite energy relative to $\phi $ respectively.

3.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:energyclassinc} \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )\subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation}

title: Remark 3.1.30
text: Remark 3.1.30 . Note that this integral \[  \int _ X |\phi -\eta |\, \theta _{\eta }^ n  \] is defined: The locus where $\phi -\eta $ is undefined is a pluripolar set, while the product $\theta _{\eta }^ n$ puts no mass on pluripolar sets (proposition 2.2.2 ). Similar remarks apply when we talk about similar integrals in the sequel.

title: Proposition 3.1.31
text: Proposition 3.1.31 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$; $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=\phi $. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By proposition 3.1.6 , \[  \int _ X\theta _\varphi ^ n=\int _ X\theta _{P_\theta [\varphi ]}^ n=\int _ X\theta _\phi ^ n.  \] Moreover, since the mass is positive, theorem 3.1.9 implies that \[  \varphi \preceq P_\theta [\varphi ]=\phi .  \] Thus $\varphi \in \mathcal E(X,\theta ;\phi )$. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Then $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Note that $\phi $ is a candidate of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ as in ( 3.12 ). So $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\geq \phi $. The reverse inequality is trivial. $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.32 (Comparison principle)
text: Proposition 3.1.32 (Comparison principle) . Fix $j\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $. Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ j$ be closed smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ and $\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,j$. Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi1} \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation} As a consequence, we also have 3.60 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi12} \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation} Proof. Observe that $\varphi \lor \psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, as a consequence of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Using the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  \geq &  \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}+\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  =&  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & +\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\  =& \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}-\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \}  } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & +\int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \}  } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}, \end{aligned}  \] where in the last step, we applied proposition 3.1.6 to $\varphi $ and $\varphi \lor \psi $. Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} }&  \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\\ & \geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{aligned}  \] Applying the preceding inequality to $\varphi +\epsilon $ in place of $\varphi $, and using $\theta _{\varphi +\epsilon }=\theta _\varphi $, we get \[  \int _{\{ \varphi +\epsilon \leq \psi \} }\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j} \geq \int _{\{ \varphi +\epsilon <\psi \} }\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}.  \] As $\epsilon \searrow 0$, by monotone convergence theorem, we obtain \[  \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j} \geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} }\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j},  \] which proves ( 3.59 ). Finally, the ( 3.60 ) follows by subtracting ( 3.59 ) (with the role of $\varphi $ and $\psi $ switched) from the total mixed mass equality \[  \int _ X\theta _\varphi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}= \int _ X\theta _\psi ^{n-j}\wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j},  \] which itself follows from proposition 3.1.6 and proposition 3.1.31 . $\square$

3.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi1} \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi <\psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation}

3.60 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_princi12} \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}\geq \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \psi \} } \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \wedge \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{j,\psi _ j}. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 3.1.33
text: Theorem 3.1.33 . Let $\mu $ be a non-pluripolar measure on $X$ with $\mu (X)=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n$. Then there is a unique $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ such that \[  \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mu ,\quad \sup _ X \varphi =0.  \]

title: Theorem 3.1.34
text: Theorem 3.1.34 . Fix $\lambda >0$. Let $\mu $ be a non-pluripolar measure on $X$ with $\mu (X)>0$. Then there is a unique $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ such that \[  \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda \varphi }\mu .  \] Furthermore, for any $\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ satisfying \[  \theta _{\psi }^ n\geq \mathrm{e}^{\lambda \psi }\mu ,  \] we have $\varphi \geq \psi $.

title: Definition 3.1.35
text: Definition 3.1.35 . We define the Monge–Ampère energy $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ as follows 3.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Edefbdd} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}. \end{equation} More generally, we extend $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$ to a functional $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ as follows 3.70 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Eextendgeneral} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \inf \left\{ E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi ):\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ),\varphi \leq \psi \right\} . \end{equation} We write $E_{\theta }$ instead of $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$ when $\phi =V_{\theta }$.

3.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Edefbdd} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}. \end{equation}

3.70 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Eextendgeneral} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )\coloneqq \inf \left\{ E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi ):\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ),\varphi \leq \psi \right\} . \end{equation}
3.71 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ephiaddcst} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi +C)=E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )+C\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \end{equation}

title: Lemma 3.1.36
text:
Lemma 3.1.36 . The functional $E_{\theta }^{\phi }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is increasing. In particular, the extended definition ( 3.70 ) agrees with ( 3.69 ) on $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, and is increasing as well. Proof. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & (n+1)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )-(n+1)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\phi )\,  \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \left( \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \right)\\ & +\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j}-\theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\phi }^{n-j} \right)\\  =&  \sum _{\substack {j+a+b=n-1,\\ \begin{bgroup}  j,a,b\geq 0

\end{bgroup}}} (n-j)\int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\phi }^ a\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b+1}\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^ j- \theta _{\phi }^ a\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b}\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{j+1}\right)\\ & +\sum _{\substack {j+a+b=n-1,\\ \begin{bgroup}  j,a,b\geq 0

\end{bgroup}}} (n-j)\int _ X (\psi -\phi )\, \left( \theta _{\phi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{a+1}\wedge \theta _{\psi }^ b- \theta _{\phi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{a}\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{b+1}\right)\\  =& 0, \end{aligned}  \] where the third equality follows from the integration by parts formula. See [ Xia19b , Lu21 ] for the proof in the context of non-pluripolar products. In other words, 3.81 \begin{equation} \label{eq:int_by_part_E_temp1} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}. \end{equation} The monotonicity follows. $\square$

3.81 \begin{equation} \label{eq:int_by_part_E_temp1} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 3.1.37
text: Lemma 3.1.37 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.82 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_int_ene} \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n \geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )\geq \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Thanks to ( 3.71 ), we may assume that $\varphi \geq \psi $. As we have seen in ( 3.81 ), the middle term can be written as \[  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}.  \] We claim that for each individual $j$, the inequality ( 3.82 ) holds: \[  \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n \geq \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j} \geq \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Thanks to proposition 3.1.32 , we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X(\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}=& \int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi +t\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\, \mathrm{d}t\\  \geq &  \int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\psi +t\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t \\  =&  \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] The other inequality is similar. $\square$

3.82 \begin{equation} \label{eq:comp_int_ene} \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n \geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )\geq \int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 3.1.38
text: Lemma 3.1.38 . The function $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is concave. Proof. Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We write $\varphi _ t=t\varphi _1+(1-t)\varphi _0$ for each $t\in [0,1]$. We claim that for each $t\in [0,1]$, we have 3.86 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ddtEphi_temp1} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _ t) =\int _ X \left(\varphi _1-\varphi _0\right)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n. \end{equation} At the boundary $t=0,1$, the derivative is understood as the one-sided derivative. Since $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, the difference $\varphi _1-\varphi _0$ is quasi-everywhere bounded. Hence all mixed integrals below are finite. We compute the right derivative first. Fix $t\in [0,1)$ and take $s>0$ small enough so that $t+s\leq 1$. By the cocycle formula ( 3.81 ), \[  \begin{aligned}  \frac{E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _{t+s})-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _ t)}{s} =& \frac{1}{(n+1)s}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi _{t+s}-\varphi _ t)\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j}\\  =& \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\,  \theta _{\varphi _{t+s}}^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ t}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] For each fixed $j$, the last integral is a polynomial in $s$ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 . Letting $s\to 0+$, it converges to \[  \int _ X(\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n.  \] Thus the right derivative is given by the right-hand side of ( 3.86 ). The proof for the left derivative is identical, using $s<0$ with $t+s\in [0,1]$. Hence the left and right derivatives agree for $t\in (0,1)$, and the endpoint derivatives are the corresponding one-sided derivatives. Now it suffices to show that the derivative ( 3.86 ) is decreasing in $t$. Take $0\leq s<t \leq 1$. We wish to show that \[  \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _ s}^ n.  \] This can be equivalently written as \[  \int _ X (\varphi _ t-\varphi _ s)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _ t-\varphi _ s)\, \theta _{\varphi _ s}^ n.  \] In particular, replacing $\varphi _0$ by $\varphi _ s$ and $\varphi _1$ by $\varphi _ t$, we are reduced to proving the following \[  \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _1}^ n\leq \int _ X (\varphi _1-\varphi _0)\, \theta _{\varphi _0}^ n.  \] But this is just a consequence of 3.1.37 . $\square$
3.86 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ddtEphi_temp1} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi _ t) =\int _ X \left(\varphi _1-\varphi _0\right)\, \theta _{\varphi _ t}^ n. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.39
text: Proposition 3.1.39 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ with \[  \varphi =\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i\not\equiv -\infty .  \] Then 3.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:E_cont_decnet} \lim _{i\in I} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. We first handle the case where $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a decreasing sequence. Thanks to 3.1.36 , we know that $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)$ is decreasing in $i$. So the limit in ( 3.89 ) exists and the $\geq $ inequality holds. Conversely, let $\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $\varphi \leq \psi $. We need to show that \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )\geq \lim _{i\to \infty } E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\varphi _ i\lor \psi \right).  \] Replacing the sequence $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ by $(\varphi _ i\lor \psi )_ i$, we are reduced to proving the $\leq $ direction of ( 3.89 ) when $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, thanks to 3.1.37 , we have \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )\leq \int _ X (\varphi _ i-\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Our assertion follows from the monotone convergence theorem. We now treat the general net case. By 3.1.36 , the net $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)$ is decreasing and bounded below by $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. Thus \[  L\coloneqq \lim _{i\in I}E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)  \] exists and satisfies $L\geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Since $\varphi \leq \varphi _ i$ for every $i\in I$, the hypotheses of corollary 1.5.6 are satisfied, and hence $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {L^1}\varphi $. For each $k\geq 1$, choose $a_ k\in I$ such that \[  \| \varphi _ i-\varphi \| _{L^1}<k^{-1},\quad i\geq a_ k.  \] We can recursively choose an increasing sequence $(i_ k)_{k\geq 1}$ in $I$ such that $i_ k\geq a_ k$ for all $k$. Then $(\varphi _{i_ k})_ k$ is a decreasing sequence and $\varphi _{i_ k}\to \varphi $ in $L^1$. Its pointwise decreasing limit is therefore equal to $\varphi $ almost everywhere, hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . Applying the sequence case to $(\varphi _{i_ k})_ k$, we get \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{i_ k})=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ).  \] Since $L\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _{i_ k})$ for every $k$, we conclude $L\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )$. $\square$
3.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:E_cont_decnet} \lim _{i\in I} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.40
text: Proposition 3.1.40 . Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. The following are equivalent: $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$; $E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )>-\infty $. Proof. Fix $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. In particular, $\varphi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\phi ]=\phi $. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . Using the plurifine locality of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 1 , we have that $\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n$ converges strongly Note. Namely, the convergence holds after integrating against any $L^{\infty }$ function. to $\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ as $C\to \infty $ by the dominated convergence theorem. Therefore, for a fixed $D>0$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -D)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n=& \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\}  } \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -D)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi >\phi -C\}  } \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \geq &  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } (n+1)E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C) \Bigr )\\  \geq &  (n+1)E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{aligned}  \] Here the last but one inequality follows from ( 3.69 ) and the fact that $\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \phi $. Letting $D\to \infty $, we conclude 1 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Thanks to 3.1.37 , we know that for each $C>0$, \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )\geq &  \int _ X \Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  =&  \int _{\left\{  \varphi >\phi -C \right\} } \Bigl (\varphi -\phi \Bigr )\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n+ \int _{\left\{  \varphi \leq \phi -C \right\} } (-C)\, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n \\  =&  \int _{\{ \varphi +C>\phi \} } \left(\varphi +C-\phi \right)\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n-C\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(\varphi +C-\phi \right)\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n-C\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n\\  =&  \int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Due to proposition 3.1.39 , we have \[  \lim _{C\to \infty }E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ),  \] so 2 holds. $\square$

title: Corollary 3.1.41
text: Corollary 3.1.41 . The function $E^{\phi }_{\theta }\colon \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ is concave. Proof. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $t\in (0,1)$. We need to show that 3.100 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Econcave_temp1} E^{\phi }_{\theta }\Bigl ( t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \Bigr )\geq tE^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )+(1-t)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi ). \end{equation} For this purpose, observe that when $C\to \infty $, we have \[  t\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )+(1-t)\Bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )\searrow t\varphi +(1-t)\psi .  \] Observe that \[  \varphi \lor (\phi -C),\psi \lor (\phi -C)\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ).  \] By 3.1.38 , for each $C>0$, we have \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Biggl ( t\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )+(1-t)\Bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr ) \Biggr )\geq tE_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\varphi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr )+(1-t)E_{\theta }^{\phi }\Bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)\Bigr ).  \] Letting $C\to \infty $, we conclude ( 3.100 ) using proposition 3.1.39 . $\square$
3.100 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Econcave_temp1} E^{\phi }_{\theta }\Bigl ( t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \Bigr )\geq tE^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )+(1-t)E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi ). \end{equation}

title: Corollary 3.1.42
text: Corollary 3.1.42 . The sets $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ are all convex. Proof. The sets $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $\mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ are trivially convex. We next handle $\mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $t\in (0,1)$. Then we compute \[  \begin{split}  \int _ X \theta _{t\varphi +(1-t)\psi }^ n=\sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j}t^ j (1-t)^{n-j} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-j}\\  =\sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j}t^ j (1-t)^{n-j} \int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n, \end{split}  \] where we applied proposition 3.1.6 in the second equality. Therefore, $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Finally, let us consider $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $t\in (0,1)$. We have already shown that $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Furthermore, the energy of this potential is finite due to corollary 3.1.41 . Therefore, $t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ in view of proposition 3.1.40 . $\square$

title: Lemma 3.1.43
text: Lemma 3.1.43 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\gamma \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that $\gamma \geq \varphi \lor \psi $. Then \[  \int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\leq 2\int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n+2\int _ X (\gamma -\psi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. Observe that 3.103 \begin{equation} \label{eq:gvp2} \{ \gamma >\varphi +2t\} \subseteq \{ \gamma >\psi +t \} \cup \{ \psi >\varphi +t\} \, . \end{equation} So \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X (\gamma -\varphi )\, \theta _{\psi }^ n =&  2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \gamma >\varphi +2t\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t \\  \leq &  2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \gamma >\psi +t\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t+ 2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \psi >\varphi +t\} }\, \theta _{\psi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t\\  \leq &  2\int _ X (\gamma -\psi ) \, \theta _{\psi }^ n+2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \psi >\varphi +t\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t\\  \leq &  2\int _ X (\gamma -\psi ) \, \theta _{\psi }^ n+2\int _0^{\infty } \int _{\{ \gamma >\varphi +t\} }\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}t\\  =& 2\int _ X (\gamma -\psi ) \, \theta _{\psi }^ n+2\int _ X (\gamma -\varphi ) \, \theta _{\varphi }^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the second line follows from ( 3.103 ), while the third line follows from proposition 3.1.32 . $\square$
3.103 \begin{equation} \label{eq:gvp2} \{ \gamma >\varphi +2t\} \subseteq \{ \gamma >\psi +t \} \cup \{ \psi >\varphi +t\} \, . \end{equation}

title: Corollary 3.1.44
text: Corollary 3.1.44 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\gamma _1,\ldots ,\gamma _ n\in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.109 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mix_MA_energy} \int _ X (\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\gamma _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{\gamma _ n} \end{equation} is well-defined and is in $\mathbb {R}$. Proof. Step 1 . We first consider the case $\psi =\phi $. We can find $C>0$ so that $\varphi \leq \phi +C$. Therefore, $\phi -\varphi \geq -C$ almost everywhere with respect to $\theta _{\gamma _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{\gamma _ n}$. So the integral ( 3.109 ) is well-defined and takes value in $\mathbb {R}\cup \{ \infty \} $. We show that the integral is finite. For this purpose, we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi -C$ and assume that $\varphi \leq \phi $. Put \[  \eta =n^{-1}(\gamma _1+\cdots +\gamma _ n).  \] Then by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 and positivity, we have \[  \int _ X (\phi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\gamma _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{\gamma _ n}\leq n^ n\int _ X (\phi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\eta }^ n.  \] Thanks to corollary 3.1.42 , $\eta \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Choose $A>0$ so that $\eta \leq \phi +A$. Applying 3.1.43 to $\varphi ,\eta $ and $\phi +A$, we get \[  \int _ X(\phi +A-\varphi )\, \theta _{\eta }^ n \leq 2\int _ X(\phi +A-\varphi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ n +2\int _ X(\phi +A-\eta )\, \theta _{\eta }^ n<\infty .  \] Hence $\int _ X(\phi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\eta }^ n<\infty $, and Step 1 follows. Step 2 . We handle the general case. Take $C>0$ so that \[  \psi \leq \phi +C,\quad \varphi \leq \phi +C.  \] Then \[  (\psi -C)-\phi \leq \psi -\varphi \leq \phi -(\varphi -C).  \] Step 1 applied to $\varphi -C$ and to $\psi -C$ shows that $\phi -(\varphi -C)$ and $\phi -(\psi -C)$ are integrable with respect to $\theta _{\gamma _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{\gamma _ n}$. Hence the positive and negative parts of $\psi -\varphi $ are both integrable, so ( 3.109 ) is well-defined and finite. $\square$
3.109 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mix_MA_energy} \int _ X (\psi -\varphi )\, \theta _{\gamma _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{\gamma _ n} \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.45
text: Proposition 3.1.45 . Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have the following cocycle equality 3.110 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ecocyc} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\varphi )\,  \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}. \end{equation} Proof. Since the conclusion is known when $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ (see ( 3.81 )), it suffices to prove that for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have 3.111 \begin{equation} \label{eq:canonic_app_energy_conv} \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\psi \lor (\phi -C) \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=\int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}. \end{equation} For this purpose, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq \phi $ and it suffices to establish the following: 3.112 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphilorphimCmphi_temp1} \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=\int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}. \end{equation} Fix $C>0$. We compute the difference as follows: \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}-\int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}\\  =&  \int _{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} >\phi -C\} }\left( \varphi -\phi \right) \, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}-\int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}\\ & +\int _{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} \leq \phi -C\} }\Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}\\  =&  -\int _{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} \leq \phi -C\} }\left( \varphi -\phi \right) \, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}+\\ & +\int _{\{ \min \{ \varphi ,\psi \} \leq \phi -C\} }\Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k} \end{aligned}  \] We first handle the first term. In order to show that it converges to $0$ when $C\to \infty $, it suffices to show that \[  \int _ X\left( \phi -\varphi \right) \, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}<\infty .  \] For this purpose, it suffices to prove a stronger inequality: 3.118 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intXphimvarphifinite_temp1} \int _ X\left( \phi -\varphi \right) \, \theta _{(\varphi +\psi )/2}^ n<\infty . \end{equation} From corollary 3.1.42 , we know that $(\varphi +\psi )/2\in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Therefore, ( 3.118 ) follows from 3.1.43 . It remains to handle the second term. It then suffices to prove the following: 3.119 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limCCintvarphiphiC_temp1} \begin{split}  \lim _{C\to \infty } C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=& 0,\\  \lim _{C\to \infty } C\int _{\{ \psi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=& 0. \end{split} \end{equation} By symmetry, it suffices to handle the first. Observe the following inclusions: \[  \{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} \subseteq \left\{  \varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \frac{1}{2}\Bigl ( \psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C \Bigr ) \right\} \subseteq \{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} .  \] By proposition 3.1.32 , we find \[  \begin{aligned} & C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}\\  \leq &  C\int _{\left\{ \varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \frac{1}{2}\bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C\bigr )\right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}\\  \leq &  2^{n-k}C\int _{\left\{ \varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \frac{1}{2}\bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C\bigr )\right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\frac{1}{2}\bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C\bigr )}^{n-k}\\  \leq &  2^{n-k}C\int _{\{ \varphi \lor (\phi -C)\leq \frac{1}{2}\bigl (\psi \lor (\phi -C)+\phi -C\bigr )\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  \leq &  2^{n-k}C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n\\  = &  2^{n-k}C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Here on the final step, we have applied the following argument: \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _{\left\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2 \right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n & \\  = & \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n-\int _{\left\{ \varphi > \phi -C/2 \right\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ n & \\  = &  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _{\left\{ \varphi > \phi -C/2 \right\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n &  \textup{by proposition \gerbyref{B86D7001}{2.2.2} \gerbyref{1C036AD6}{1}}\\  =&  \int _{\left\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2 \right\} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n. & \end{aligned}  \] On the other hand, \[  \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C/2 \} } \theta _{\varphi }^ n\leq 2 \varlimsup _{C\to \infty } \int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C \} }(\phi -\varphi )\,  \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0,  \] since $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We conclude ( 3.119 ). $\square$

3.110 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ecocyc} E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\psi )-E^{\phi }_{\theta }(\varphi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X (\psi -\varphi )\,  \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{\varphi }^{n-j}. \end{equation}

3.111 \begin{equation} \label{eq:canonic_app_energy_conv} \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\psi \lor (\phi -C) \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=\int _ X (\varphi -\psi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}. \end{equation}

3.112 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intvarphilorphimCmphi_temp1} \lim _{C\to \infty } \int _ X \Bigl ( \varphi \lor (\phi -C)-\phi \Bigr ) \, \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=\int _ X (\varphi -\phi )\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi }^{n-k}. \end{equation}
3.118 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intXphimvarphifinite_temp1} \int _ X\left( \phi -\varphi \right) \, \theta _{(\varphi +\psi )/2}^ n<\infty . \end{equation}

3.119 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limCCintvarphiphiC_temp1} \begin{split}  \lim _{C\to \infty } C\int _{\{ \varphi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=& 0,\\  \lim _{C\to \infty } C\int _{\{ \psi \leq \phi -C\} } \theta _{\varphi \lor (\phi -C)}^ k\wedge \theta _{\psi \lor (\phi -C)}^{n-k}=& 0. \end{split} \end{equation}

title: Proposition 3.1.46
text: Proposition 3.1.46 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 3.132 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \left(\psi -\varphi \right)\theta ^ n_{\psi }\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\psi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )\leq \int _ X \left(\psi -\varphi \right)\theta ^ n_{\varphi }. \end{equation} Proof. Thanks to ( 3.111 ), this can be reduced to the case where $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$, which is established in 3.1.37 . $\square$

title: Proposition 3.1.47
text: Proposition 3.1.47 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and either one of the following conditions holds: $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a decreasing net with $\varphi =\inf _{i\in I}\varphi _ i$; $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is an increasing net with almost everywhere limit $\varphi $. Then 3.133 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Iconv_mono} \lim _{i\in I} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ i)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. The decreasing case is already proved in proposition 3.1.39 , so let us focus on the case where $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is increasing. We first handle the case where $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Namely, $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is an increasing sequence. Step 1 . We first prove the result when $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ for each $j\geq 1$. Due to corollary 2.4.9 , we have \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ j}^{n-k}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n  \] for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$. By ( 3.81 ), we have \[  \begin{aligned}  0\leq &  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi )-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\varphi _ j)\\  =&  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{k=0}^ n \int _ X(\varphi -\varphi _ j)\, \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{\varphi _ j}^{n-k}. \end{aligned}  \] We then apply theorem 2.4.7 to conclude that the right-hand side converges to $0$. Step 2 . We prove the general case. The $\leq $ direction in ( 3.133 ) follows from the monotonicity of $E_{\theta }^{\phi }$, as proved in 3.1.36 . It remains to prove the $\geq $ direction. After subtracting a constant from all $\varphi _ j$ and from $\varphi $, which shifts all the energies by the same constant in view of ( 3.71 ), we may assume that $\varphi \leq \phi $.
