title: 2 The theory of -good singularities
text:
2 The theory of $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities This part develops the comparison theory of singularities that forms the technical core of the book. The basic objects are positive-mass $\theta $-psh potentials, their $P$- and $\mathcal I$-singularity types, and the envelopes introduced in chapter 3 . The central theme is that the ordinary pluripotential-theoretic equivalence relation and the equivalence relation detected by multiplier ideals are different in general, but coincide on a large and geometrically meaningful class of singularities: the $\mathcal I$-good ones. The first chapter of the part, chapter 6 , introduces the general language for comparing singularities. It studies the $P$- and $\mathcal I$-preorders and defines the pseudometric $d_ S$ on positive-mass potentials. This pseudometric is not restricted to $\mathcal I$-good potentials; rather, it is the ambient convergence tool used to compare singularity types. The chapter proves the main continuity and convergence properties of $d_ S$, including its compatibility with envelopes and with changes of the background form. In chapter 7 we introduce $\mathcal I$-good singularities. The main structural result is the characterization theorem theorem 7.1.1 , which relates $\mathcal I$-goodness to approximation by analytic singularities, equality between non-pluripolar mass and volume, and the coincidence of the $P$- and $\mathcal I$-envelopes. The chapter also develops the mixed volume formalism needed later and proves the asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula theorem 7.4.2 , which identifies the non-pluripolar volume of an $\mathcal I$-good current with the asymptotic growth of multiplier-ideal sections. chapter 8 develops the trace operator. Its purpose is to give a meaningful restriction of a quasi-psh singularity to a possibly singular subvariety, in a way compatible with multiplier ideals and birational modifications. The trace operator is accompanied by analytic Bertini-type results and by restricted-volume formulae. These results allow the singularity theory developed in the previous chapters to be used inductively on subvarieties. chapter 9 studies test curves, namely concave decreasing families of model potentials. It proves the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence between test curves and geodesic rays and develops the operations on test curves needed later. The chapter also introduces the $\mathcal I$-model version of the theory, which will be used in the non-Archimedean applications. chapter 10 develops partial Okounkov bodies for singular metrics. These convex bodies extend the classical Newton–Okounkov construction to the setting of psh metrics and record the valuative data of multiplier ideals. The chapter treats both algebraic and transcendental versions and proves the continuity and volume formulae needed in the big toric and non-Archimedean chapters. Finally, chapter 11 translates the preceding singularity theory into the language of b-divisors. It associates with a positive current a nef b-divisor recording the regular parts of its pullbacks on all modifications, and it compares $\mathcal I$-equivalence with b-divisorial data. The mixed intersection theory of nef b-divisors developed there provides a geometric counterpart to the mixed volume theory of $\mathcal I$-good currents. The chapters are arranged linearly. The comparison theory of chapter 6 is used throughout the part; chapter 7 , chapter 8 provide the main analytic tools; chapter 9 , chapter 10 , chapter 11 develop three complementary languages for the same singularity theory: geodesic/test-curve language, Okounkov-body language and b-divisorial language. These languages are then used separately in the application chapters chapter 12 , chapter 13 , chapter 14 . Algebra is the offer made by the devil to the mathematician. The devil says: “I will give you this powerful machine, it will answer any question you like. All you need to do is give me your soul: give up geometry and you will have this marvelous machine.” 
— Michael Atiyah Note. Sir Michael Francis Atiyah (1929–2019) wrote the influential Introduction to commutative algebra together with I. G. MacDonald, whose name is often omitted or misspelled.

title: 6 Comparison of singularities
text: 6 Comparison of singularities A central theme of this book is that singularities of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be compared at several levels of precision. The preorder $\preceq $ of definition 1.5.2 compares potentials up to additive constants. It is the most concrete notion, but it is often too fine for global pluripotential theory: the $P$-envelope identifies potentials with the same model representative, while multiplier ideals identify singularities that have the same integrability behavior. This chapter makes these two coarser comparisons systematic. We first introduce the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal I$-preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. The $P$-preorder is defined by comparing $P$-envelopes, and its equivalence classes are the $P$-singularity types. The $\mathcal I$-preorder is defined by comparing multiplier ideals $\mathcal I(k\varphi )$ for all $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. These two preorders are compatible with ordinary singularity comparison, but they capture different information: the former is governed by non-pluripolar mass, while the latter is governed by valuative and multiplier-ideal data. The second main object of the chapter is the pseudometric $d_ S$. For positive-mass potentials in a fixed class, $d_ S$ is defined through the Darvas $d_1$-distance between the associated geodesic rays. Its zero locus is precisely $P$-equivalence. Thus $d_ S$ should be viewed as a convergence structure on $P$-singularity types. The chapter proves the basic properties of $d_ S$, including monotone convergence, sandwich criteria and compatibility with changing the background form. The final results establish the continuity properties that will be used throughout the rest of the book. We prove continuity of the $\mathcal I$-envelope, continuity of non-pluripolar mass and volume, and a general equisingularity criterion. These results allow one to pass from analytic approximations to limiting singularities while controlling both $P$-types and multiplier ideals. They are used repeatedly in the theory of $\mathcal I$-good singularities, trace operators, test curves, partial Okounkov bodies and non-Archimedean potentials.

title: 6.1 The  and -preorders
text: 6.1 The $P$ and $\mathcal{I}$-preorders Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Recall that we defined a preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ in definition 1.5.2 to compare the singularity types of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions. The problem with this preorder is that it is too fine. For our purposes, it is useful to consider rougher relations.

title: 6.1.1 The definitions of the preorders
text:
6.1.1 The definitions of the preorders Recall that the $P$-envelope is defined in definition 3.1.4 . Definition 6.1.1 . For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we say $\varphi $ is $P$-more singular than $\psi $ and write $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ if for some (equivalently, every, due to 6.1.2 below) closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, we have 6.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:Penvleq} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]. \end{equation} If $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we write $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ and say that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ have the same $P$-singularity type . Recall that $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ was introduced in ( 2.19 ). Note that if $\varphi \preceq \psi $, then $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. So the $P$-preorder is coarser than $\preceq $. The $P$-equivalence relation can also be formulated using the language of relative full mass classes developed in 3.1.3 . In fact, $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ satisfies $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ if and only if $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathcal{E}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ for a common model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. The condition ( 6.1 ) is independent of the choice of $	heta $: Lemma 6.1.2 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, the following are equivalent: $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]$; $P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ]\leq P_{	heta +\omega }[\psi ]$. In particular, $\preceq _ P$ defines a preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Observe that \[  \varphi \preceq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ].  \] Taking the $P_{	heta +\omega }$-envelope, we find \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ] \leq P_{	heta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ] \leq P_{	heta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ],  \] where the equality follows from theorem 3.1.9 . In particular, 6.2  egin{equation} \label{eq:doubleP} P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi ]=P_{	heta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]. \end{equation} A similar formula holds for $\psi $. So we see that 2 holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By ( 6.2 ), we may assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are both model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Observe that $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq P_{	heta +\omega }[\psi ]$. It follows that $P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]\leq P_{	heta +\omega }[\psi ]$. The reverse inequality is trivial, so \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{	heta +\omega }[\psi ].  \] From the direction we have proved, for any $C\geq 1$, \[  P_{	heta +C\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{	heta +C\omega }[\psi ].  \] So by proposition 3.1.6 , \[  \int _ X \Bigl (	heta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi \lor \psi )\Bigr )^ n=\int _ X\left(	heta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi ight)^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $C$, the equality extends to $C=0$, namely, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In particular, $\varphi \lor \psi \leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]=\psi $ by ( 3.12 ). So 1 follows. $\square$ As a consequence of 6.1.2 , we can define the $P$-preorder at the level of currents. Given closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T=	heta _{\varphi }$, $S=	heta '_{\psi }$, we write $T\preceq _ P S$ (resp. $T\sim _ P S$) if $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ (resp. $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $). This definition is independent of the decompositions of $T$ and $S$. As a first example of $P$-equivalence, we have: Example 6.1.3 . Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \varphi \sim _ P P_{	heta }[\varphi ] ootnotemark .  \] Note. It is not known to us whether the same holds when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. This follows immediately from theorem 3.1.9 . We give a very useful criterion of the $P$-equivalence in terms of the non-pluripolar masses. Proposition 6.1.4 . Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, we have 6.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:mixedmassequal} \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation} Assume furthermore that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, then these conditions are equivalent to the following: We have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Recall that $V_{	heta }$ is introduced in ( 2.20 ). Proof. We first prove the equivalence between 1 and 1 when $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. 1 $\implies $ 1 . Assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. By 6.1.2 , we have \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=P_{	heta }[\psi ].  \] So 1 follows from proposition 3.1.6 . 1 $\implies $ 1 . Since $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we have $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]$. Moreover, proposition 3.1.6 shows that $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ have the same positive mass. By theorem 3.1.9 , $P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ is a candidate in the characterization of $P_{	heta } igl [P_{	heta }[\varphi ] igr ]=P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. Hence $P_{	heta }[\psi ]\leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$, and therefore $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=P_{	heta }[\psi ]$. So 1 follows. Let us come back to the general case with $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Fix $j\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $. We argue ( 6.3 ). Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By 6.1.2 , for each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]= P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ].  \] It follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ X \left(	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi ight)^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}=& \int _ X \Bigl (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}\  =& \int _ X \Bigl (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j} \  =&  \int _ X \left(	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi ight)^ j\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] Since the two extremes are both polynomials in $\epsilon $ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , we conclude that the same holds when $\epsilon =0$, that is, ( 6.3 ) holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume ( 6.3 ) holds for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. Then the same holds with $P_{	heta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\psi $, thanks to proposition 3.1.6 . Therefore, for each $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{	heta }}^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{tP_{	heta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{	heta }}^ n  \] by the binomial expansion. Furthermore, $t\varphi +(1-t)V_{	heta }\preceq tP_{	heta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{	heta }$. By the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  t\varphi +(1-t)V_{	heta }\sim _ P t P_{	heta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{	heta }  \] for each $t\in (0,1)$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  \int _ X (	heta +\omega )_{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{	heta }}^ n= \int _ X (	heta +\omega )_{tP_{	heta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{	heta }}^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $t$ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , the same holds when $t=1$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 again, we have $\varphi \sim _ P P_{	heta }[\psi ]\sim _ P \psi $. $\square$ Next we introduce a different preorder. Proposition 6.1.5 . Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, the following are equivalent: For any $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\psi );  \] for any $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$, we have \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi );  \] for any modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ and any $y\in Y$, we have \[  
u (\pi ^*\varphi ,y)\geq 
u (\pi ^*\psi ,y);  \] for any proper bimeromorphic morphism $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ from a Kähler manifold and any $y\in Y$, we have \[  
u (\pi ^*\varphi ,y)\geq 
u (\pi ^*\psi ,y);  \] for any prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  
u (\varphi ,E)\geq 
u (\psi ,E).  \] Proof. The proof is almost identical to that of proposition 3.2.1 . $\square$ Definition 6.1.6 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we say $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-more singular than $\psi $ and write $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $ if the equivalent conditions in proposition 6.1.5 are satisfied. It is clear that $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a preorder on $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Note that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $ and $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ both hold if and only if $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $ in the sense of definition 3.2.2 . Given closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T=	heta _{\varphi }$, $S=	heta '_{\psi }$, we write $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$ (resp. $T\sim _{\mathcal{I}} S$) if $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $ (resp. $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $). This definition is independent of the decompositions of $T$ and $S$. Lemma 6.1.7 . Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 6.7  egin{equation} \label{eq:Plor1} P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]=P_{	heta }\Bigl [ P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ] \Bigr ]. \end{equation} Proof. Since $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]$, the $\leq $ direction of ( 6.7 ) follows. Conversely, it suffices to show that \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]\geq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ],  \] which follows from $\varphi \preceq \varphi \lor \psi $, $\psi \preceq \varphi \lor \psi $, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope with respect to $\preceq $. $\square$ Lemma 6.1.8 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ (resp. $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $); $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P\psi $ (resp. $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $). Proof. Take a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. We only prove the $P$ case, the $\mathcal{I}$ case is similar. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By 2 and example 6.1.3 , $P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]=P_{	heta }[\psi ]\sim _ P \psi $. But $\varphi \preceq P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]$, so 1 follows. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi $ are both model by 6.1.7 . Then $\varphi \leq \psi $ and 2 follows. $\square$ Corollary 6.1.9 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $. Therefore, the preorder $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is coarser than $\preceq _ P$. Given $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we therefore have the implications: \[  \varphi \preceq \psi \implies \varphi \preceq _ P \psi \implies \varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi .  \] Proof. Thanks to 6.1.8 , we have $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P \psi $. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then by proposition 3.2.13 , we have \[  \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} P_{	heta }[\psi ]= P_{	heta }\left[\varphi \lor \psi ight]\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \lor \psi .  \] Our assertion follows from the $\mathcal{I}$-version of 6.1.8 . $\square$ Next we give a few extra characterizations of the $P$-envelope. Corollary 6.1.10 . Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then \[   egin{aligned}  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi ight\} \  =&  \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _ P \varphi ight\} . \end{aligned}  \] Just for comparison, let us recall a few other characterizations of the $P$-envelope for $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$: \[   egin{aligned}  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\psi \leq 0,\psi \preceq \varphi ight\} \  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ):\psi \leq 0,\psi \sim \varphi ight\} \  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{C\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*} (\varphi +C)\land V_{	heta }\  =&  \sup \left\{ \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0,\varphi \preceq \psi , \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^ night\} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. Note that $\psi \sim _ P \varphi $ implies that $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ by proposition 3.1.6 . We observe that \[   egin{split} & \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi ight\} \ =& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \varphi \preceq \psi , \psi \sim _ P \varphi ight\}  \end{split}  \] since for any candidate $\psi $ for the first supremum, $\psi \lor (\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi )$ is larger than $\psi $, and is a candidate for the second supremum thanks to 6.1.8 . So the first equality is a direct consequence of proposition 6.1.4 and theorem 3.1.9 . Next we prove the second equality. We only need to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. By 6.1.8 and example 6.1.3 , we know that $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \sim _ P \varphi $ and $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \leq 0$. It follows from the first equality that $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$ Similarly, we have a new characterization of the $\mathcal{I}$-envelope. Corollary 6.1.11 . Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi ight\} .  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. By 6.1.8 and proposition 3.2.8 , we know that $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Therefore, $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi $ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ (cf. ( 3.182 )), so \[  \psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \leq P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$ Proposition 6.1.12 . Let $	heta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $; $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . This follows immediately from corollary 6.1.11 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . It follows from proposition 3.2.8 that \[  \varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}} \sim _{\mathcal{I}} \psi .  \] We conclude 1 . $\square$ Example 6.1.13 . Let us continue our example example 3.1.14 , where $X=\mathbb {P}^1$, $\omega $ is the Fubini–Study metric and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ has log-log singularity at $0$. We have shown that $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0$ in ( 3.16 ), so $\varphi \sim _{P} 0$ and hence $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$. In particular, $P$-equivalence is not equivalent to the equivalence of singularity types. On the other hand, consider a potential $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with log singularity at $0$, as in example 1.8.9 . We know that $
u (\psi ,0)=1$ from the explicit expression ( 1.50 ). So $\psi 
ot\sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ and hence $\psi 
ot\sim _{P} 0$. Moreover, $\psi \preceq _{P} \varphi $ and hence $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. We give an example showing that $P$-equivalence is not equivalent to $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence. Example 6.1.14 . Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. Let $K\subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ be a polar Cantor set carrying an atom free probability measure $\mu $ supported on $K$ (see [ Page 31 , Car83 ] ). Write $\mu =\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\omega $-subharmonic function $\varphi $. Since $\mu $ is atom free, we know that all Lelong numbers of $\varphi $ are $0$. On the other hand, $\varphi $ has $0$ non-pluripolar mass since $K$ is pluripolar. Then observe that $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ while $\varphi 
ot\sim _ P 0$. For later use, we give the following definition. Definition 6.1.15 . Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. An elementary metric on $L$ is a psh metric $h$ on $L$ such that there is a generalized Fubini–Study metric $h'$ on $L$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\sim _{P} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h'.  \] The set of elementary metrics on $L$ is denoted by $\mathrm{Ele}(L)$. We also say $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is elementary. If we have fixed a Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$, and if we represent $h$ as $h_0\exp (-\varphi )$, we also say the quasi-psh function $\varphi $ is elementary. Recall that the generalized Fubini–Study metrics are defined in definition 1.8.11 .

title: Definition 6.1.1
text: Definition 6.1.1 . For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we say $\varphi $ is $P$-more singular than $\psi $ and write $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ if for some (equivalently, every, due to 6.1.2 below) closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we have 6.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvleq} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]. \end{equation} If $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we write $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ and say that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ have the same $P$-singularity type .
6.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Penvleq} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 6.1.2
text: Lemma 6.1.2 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, the following are equivalent: $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$; $P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . Observe that \[  \varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ].  \] Taking the $P_{\theta +\omega }$-envelope, we find \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ] \leq P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ],  \] where the equality follows from theorem 3.1.9 . In particular, 6.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:doubleP} P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]. \end{equation} A similar formula holds for $\psi $. So we see that 2 holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By ( 6.2 ), we may assume that $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are both model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Observe that $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. It follows that $P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ]$. The reverse inequality is trivial, so \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{\theta +\omega }[\psi ].  \] From the direction we have proved, for any $C\geq 1$, \[  P_{\theta +C\omega }[\varphi \lor \psi ]= P_{\theta +C\omega }[\psi ].  \] So by proposition 3.1.6 , \[  \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi \lor \psi )\Bigr )^ n=\int _ X\left(\theta +C\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \right)^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $C$, the equality extends to $C=0$, namely, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] In particular, $\varphi \lor \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]=\psi $ by ( 3.12 ). So 1 follows. $\square$
6.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:doubleP} P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta +\omega }\Bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\Bigr ]. \end{equation}

title: Example 6.1.3
text: Example 6.1.3 . Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \varphi \sim _ P P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\footnotemark .  \] Note. It is not known to us whether the same holds when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. This follows immediately from theorem 3.1.9 .

title: Proposition 6.1.4
text: Proposition 6.1.4 . Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, we have 6.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mixedmassequal} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation} Assume furthermore that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then these conditions are equivalent to the following: We have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n.  \] Proof. We first prove the equivalence between 1 and 1 when $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. 1 $\implies $ 1 . Assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. By 6.1.2 , we have \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi ].  \] So 1 follows from proposition 3.1.6 . 1 $\implies $ 1 . Since $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Moreover, proposition 3.1.6 shows that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$ and $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ have the same positive mass. By theorem 3.1.9 , $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ is a candidate in the characterization of $P_{\theta }\bigl [P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\bigr ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. Hence $P_{\theta }[\psi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and therefore $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. So 1 follows. Let us come back to the general case with $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Fix $j\in \{ 0,\ldots ,n\} $. We argue ( 6.3 ). Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By 6.1.2 , for each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]= P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ].  \] It follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \right)^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=& \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\psi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\\  =& \int _ X \Bigl (\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ] \Bigr )^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \\  =&  \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{aligned}  \] Since the two extremes are both polynomials in $\epsilon $ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , we conclude that the same holds when $\epsilon =0$, that is, ( 6.3 ) holds. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume ( 6.3 ) holds for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. Then the same holds with $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$ in place of $\psi $, thanks to proposition 3.1.6 . Therefore, for each $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n  \] by the binomial expansion. Furthermore, $t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }\preceq tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }$. By the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }\sim _ P t P_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }  \] for each $t\in (0,1)$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 , we have \[  \int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{t\varphi +(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n= \int _ X (\theta +\omega )_{tP_{\theta }[\psi ]+(1-t)V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Since both sides are polynomials in $t$ by the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , the same holds when $t=1$. From the implication 1 $\implies $ 1 again, we have $\varphi \sim _ P P_{\theta }[\psi ]\sim _ P \psi $. $\square$
6.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mixedmassequal} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}. \end{equation}

text: Definition 6.1.6 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, we say $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-more singular than $\psi $ and write $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $ if the equivalent conditions in proposition 6.1.5 are satisfied.

title: Lemma 6.1.7
text: Lemma 6.1.7 . Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 6.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Plor1} P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]=P_{\theta }\Bigl [ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ] \Bigr ]. \end{equation} Proof. Since $\varphi \lor \psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ]$, the $\leq $ direction of ( 6.7 ) follows. Conversely, it suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]\geq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ],  \] which follows from $\varphi \preceq \varphi \lor \psi $, $\psi \preceq \varphi \lor \psi $, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope with respect to $\preceq $. $\square$
6.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Plor1} P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]=P_{\theta }\Bigl [ P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor P_{\theta }[\psi ] \Bigr ]. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 6.1.8
text: Lemma 6.1.8 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $ (resp. $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $); $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P\psi $ (resp. $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $). Proof. Take a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We only prove the $P$ case, the $\mathcal{I}$ case is similar. 2 $\implies $ 1 . Assume 2 . By 2 and example 6.1.3 , $P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi ]\sim _ P \psi $. But $\varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]$, so 1 follows. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Assume 1 . We may assume that $\varphi ,\psi $ are both model by 6.1.7 . Then $\varphi \leq \psi $ and 2 follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 6.1.9
text: Corollary 6.1.9 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $. Proof. Thanks to 6.1.8 , we have $\varphi \lor \psi \sim _ P \psi $. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then by proposition 3.2.13 , we have \[  \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} P_{\theta }[\psi ]= P_{\theta }\left[\varphi \lor \psi \right]\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \lor \psi .  \] Our assertion follows from the $\mathcal{I}$-version of 6.1.8 . $\square$

title: Corollary 6.1.10
text: Corollary 6.1.10 . Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\} \\  =&  \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _ P \varphi \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. Note that $\psi \sim _ P \varphi $ implies that $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by proposition 3.1.6 . We observe that \[  \begin{split} & \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\} \\ =& \sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \varphi \preceq \psi , \psi \sim _ P \varphi \right\}  \end{split}  \] since for any candidate $\psi $ for the first supremum, $\psi \lor (\varphi -\sup _ X \varphi )$ is larger than $\psi $, and is a candidate for the second supremum thanks to 6.1.8 . So the first equality is a direct consequence of proposition 6.1.4 and theorem 3.1.9 . Next we prove the second equality. We only need to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. By 6.1.8 and example 6.1.3 , we know that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \sim _ P \varphi $ and $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\lor \psi \leq 0$. It follows from the first equality that $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$. $\square$

title: Corollary 6.1.11
text: Corollary 6.1.11 . Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\sup \left\{  \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \psi \leq 0, \psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \right\} .  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\psi \leq 0$ and $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, we have $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. By 6.1.8 and proposition 3.2.8 , we know that $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Therefore, $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi $ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ (cf. ( 3.182 )), so \[  \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor \psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$

title: Proposition 6.1.12
text: Proposition 6.1.12 . Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $; $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . This follows immediately from corollary 6.1.11 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . It follows from proposition 3.2.8 that \[  \varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}} \sim _{\mathcal{I}} \psi .  \] We conclude 1 . $\square$

title: Example 6.1.13
text:
Example 6.1.13 . Let us continue our example example 3.1.14 , where $X=\mathbb {P}^1$, $\omega $ is the Fubini–Study metric and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ has log-log singularity at $0$. We have shown that $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=0$ in ( 3.16 ), so $\varphi \sim _{P} 0$ and hence $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$. In particular, $P$-equivalence is not equivalent to the equivalence of singularity types. On the other hand, consider a potential $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with log singularity at $0$, as in example 1.8.9 . We know that $
u (\psi ,0)=1$ from the explicit expression ( 1.50 ). So $\psi 
ot\sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ and hence $\psi 
ot\sim _{P} 0$. Moreover, $\psi \preceq _{P} \varphi $ and hence $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $.

title: Example 6.1.14
text: Example 6.1.14 . Let $X=\mathbb {P}^1$ and $\omega $ be the Fubini–Study metric. Let $K\subseteq \mathbb {P}^1$ be a polar Cantor set carrying an atom free probability measure $\mu $ supported on $K$ (see [ Page 31 , Car83 ] ). Write $\mu =\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\omega $-subharmonic function $\varphi $. Since $\mu $ is atom free, we know that all Lelong numbers of $\varphi $ are $0$. On the other hand, $\varphi $ has $0$ non-pluripolar mass since $K$ is pluripolar. Then observe that $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}} 0$ while $\varphi \not\sim _ P 0$.

title: Definition 6.1.15
text: Definition 6.1.15 . Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. An elementary metric on $L$ is a psh metric $h$ on $L$ such that there is a generalized Fubini–Study metric $h'$ on $L$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\sim _{P} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h'.  \] The set of elementary metrics on $L$ is denoted by $\mathrm{Ele}(L)$. We also say $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is elementary. If we have fixed a Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$, and if we represent $h$ as $h_0\exp (-\varphi )$, we also say the quasi-psh function $\varphi $ is elementary.

title: 6.1.2 Properties of the preorders
text: 6.1.2 Properties of the preorders Now we state a more natural version of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Proposition 6.1.16 (Monotonicity theorem) . Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for each $i$. Then \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass is a decreasing quantity with respect to the $P$-singularity types of the potentials. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, since $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P\psi _ i$, we have \[  P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]\leq P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\psi _ i]  \] for all $\epsilon >0$. Therefore, by proposition 3.1.6 and our previous monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , we have \[  \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _ n}.  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ and applying the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , we find the desired inequality. $\square$ The $P$-preorder allows us to derive a natural generalization of 2.4.15 . Theorem 6.1.17 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then for any 6.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:arangetemp_reproduce} a\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right), \end{equation} the function \[  \eta \coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )  \] lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ and 6.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:path_env_reproduce} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} If in addition, $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $, then $\eta \sim _ P \varphi $ as well. In ( 6.16 ), the fraction is understood as $\infty $ if either $\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$ or $n=0$, exactly as in 2.4.15 . Proof. By our assumption and ( 3.5 ), we have $\varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Due to proposition 3.1.6 , the interval ( 6.16 ) remains unchanged after replacing $\psi $ by $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Fix $a$ in this interval. So by 2.4.15 and the discussions afterwards, \[  \eta '\coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\Bigr )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] We first check that $\eta $ is a genuine $\theta $-psh function. Choose a closed non-pluripolar set $K\subseteq X$ on which $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are bounded. Then the obstacle $a\varphi +(1-a)\psi $ is bounded above on $K$. Every candidate in the definition of $\eta $ is therefore uniformly bounded above on $X$ by 1.5.5 , so $\eta \not\equiv \infty $ and hence $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. On the other hand, since $\psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$, we can find $C>0$ such that $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]+C$. Then \[  \eta '-(a-1)C\leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere, hence $\eta \geq \eta '-(a-1)C$. Thus $\eta '\preceq \eta $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. By ( 2.32 ), \[  \eta \leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere. Equivalently, ( 6.17 ) holds quasi-everywhere. Since both sides of ( 6.17 ) are $\theta $-psh, proposition 1.2.6 upgrades the inequality to an everywhere inequality. It remains to prove the assertion about the $P$-order. Using proposition 3.1.24 , we get \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]+\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ] \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By the assumption $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we also have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Therefore, \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\leq a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]  \] quasi-everywhere and hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . It follows that $P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, namely $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $. Finally assume that $\varphi \sim _ P\psi $. Then $\int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ by proposition 3.1.6 . Applying corollary 2.4.16 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta '}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Since $\eta '\preceq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] The reverse inequality follows from $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $ and proposition 6.1.16 . Hence $\eta \sim _ P\varphi $ by proposition 6.1.4 . $\square$ Next we show that the $P$ and $\mathcal{I}$-preorders are preserved by some natural operations. Lemma 6.1.18 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Given two quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi ,\psi $ on $X$, then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $; $\pi ^*\varphi \preceq _{P} \pi ^*\psi $. The same holds with $\mathcal{I}$ in place of $P$. Proof. In the $P$-case, this follows from proposition 3.1.23 , while in the $\mathcal{I}$-case, this follows from proposition 3.2.7 . $\square$ Proposition 6.1.19 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that \[  \varphi \preceq _ P \psi ,\quad \varphi '\preceq _ P \psi '.  \] Then \[  \varphi +\varphi '\preceq _ P \psi +\psi '.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of proposition 1.4.5 . We only need to handle the case of $\preceq _{P}$. Step 1 . We first show that \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\sim _ P \varphi +\varphi '.  \] In fact, we clearly have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\succeq \varphi +\varphi '.  \] So by proposition 6.1.4 , it suffices to show that they have the same mass. We compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \Bigl (2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^ n\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr )^ j\wedge \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^{n-j}\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \omega _{\varphi '}^{n-j}\\  =&  \int _ X \left(2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi '\right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where we applied proposition 3.1.6 to the mixed products on the third line. Step 2 . By Step 1, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '$ are all model potentials, after replacing them by their $P_{\omega }$-envelopes. So $\varphi \leq \psi $ and $\varphi '\leq \psi '$. Our assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 6.1.20 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$, $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be uniformly bounded from above non-empty families in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i\preceq _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\psi _ i.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. By adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of corollary 1.4.6 , we only have to consider the statement for $\preceq _ P$. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $I$ is a directed set and $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ and $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ are increasing nets. In this case, our assertion follows simply from proposition 3.1.28 . Step 2 . We handle the case where $I$ is finite. We may assume that $I=\{ 0,1\} $. It suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi _0]\lor P_{\theta }[\varphi _1]\sim _ P \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1,  \] which follows from 6.1.7 . Step 3 . The general case can be reduced to the two cases handled in Step 1 and Step 2. More precisely, by applying proposition 1.2.3 to the two families and taking the union of the resulting countable subsets, we can find a countable subset $J\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i,\quad \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ i.  \] We may replace $I$ by $J$ and assume that $I$ is countable. If $I$ is finite, Step 2 applies directly. Otherwise, write $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and set \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ m=\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ m,\quad \tilde{\psi }_ m=\psi _1\lor \cdots \lor \psi _ m.  \] By Step 2, $\tilde{\varphi }_ m\preceq _ P\tilde{\psi }_ m$ for every $m$. The two new sequences are increasing and have the same upper envelopes as the original families, so Step 1 applies. $\square$ We now refine 3.1.17 using the $P$-equivalence relation. Proposition 6.1.21 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that \[  \varphi \sim _ P \varphi ',\quad \psi \sim _ P\psi ',\quad \varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Then \[  \varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \varphi \land \psi \sim _ P \varphi '\land \psi '.  \] Proof. We first observe that $\varphi ,\varphi ',\psi ,\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by assumption. Let \[  \phi \coloneqq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi '],\quad \gamma =P_{\theta }[\psi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi '].  \] Since $\varphi '\preceq \phi $ and $\psi '\preceq \gamma $, after adding a common constant to $\varphi '$ and $\psi '$, we may assume that $\varphi '\leq \phi $ and $\psi '\leq \gamma $. Then $\varphi '\land \psi '\leq \phi \land \gamma $, so the assumption $\varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ implies $\phi \land \gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by monotonicity. It follows from 3.1.17 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n.  \] Next, we apply 3.1.17 again to conclude that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n>0.  \] Since $\varphi \land \psi \preceq \phi \land \gamma $ and the two potentials have the same positive mass, theorem 3.1.9 gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\phi \land \gamma $. The same argument gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi '\land \psi ']=\phi \land \gamma $, hence $\varphi \land \psi \sim _ P\varphi '\land \psi '$. $\square$ We can formulate a generalization of proposition 3.1.54 using the $P$-partial order. Corollary 6.1.22 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $. Then for any $C>0$, $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 6.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supvarphipsipC} P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation} We refer to definition 3.1.19 for the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )$. Proof. Since $\psi \preceq _ P\varphi $, by proposition 6.1.21 , we get \[  \psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}  \] and $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\sim _ P\psi $ for every $C>0$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*}\psi \land (\varphi +C).  \] Then $\eta \sim _ P \psi $. By corollary 3.1.8 , we have \[  \theta _\eta ^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _\psi ^ n.  \] The domination principle theorem 2.4.17 gives $\eta \geq \psi $. The reverse inequality is trivial, so $\eta =\psi $. $\square$ The $P$-equivalence relation characterizes when a subgeodesic exists. See definition 4.1.1 for the notion of subgeodesics. Theorem 6.1.23 . Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: There is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$; $\varphi _0\sim _ P\varphi _1$. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This follows from proposition 4.2.4 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Step 1 . We assume that $\varphi _0\geq \varphi _1$. We first replace the given subgeodesic by the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Note that the geodesic is necessarily a subgeodesic as well by 4.2.2 . Observe that $t\mapsto \varphi _ t$ is decreasing due to 4.2.5 . Let $\varphi _ t=\varphi _1$ for all $t>1$. Then by the gluing lemma 4.1.11 , we find that $(\varphi _ t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a subgeodesic ray. Next, we consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{t\geq 0}(\varphi _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] It follows from Kiselman's principle proposition 1.2.11 that $\Gamma _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. Note that for $\tau >0$, we clearly have $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $. On the other hand, for $\tau \leq 0$, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t\in [0,1]}(\varphi _ t-t\tau )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] By Legendre inversion (cf. corollary A.2.4 ), for $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left(\Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau \right).  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It follows from proposition 6.1.20 that for each $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }].  \] The right-hand side is independent of $t$. Here by adding $\omega $, we no longer have to worry about the possibility where $\Gamma _{\tau }$ has vanishing mass. Write \[  \varphi _0=\operatorname *{sup}_{t\in (0,1)}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ t.  \] By proposition 6.1.20 again, we find that \[  \varphi _0\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }]  \] as well. So $\varphi _0\sim _ P \varphi _1$. Step 2 . We prove the general case. Observe that $(\varphi _ t\lor \varphi _1)_{t\in (0,1)}$ is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0\lor \varphi _1$ to $\varphi _1$. By Step 1, \[  \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1\sim _ P \varphi _1.  \] Hence $\varphi _0\preceq _ P \varphi _1$ by 6.1.8 . The converse is proved similarly. Hence 2 follows. $\square$ Restating the 1 $\implies $ 2 direction in the theorem in terms of the complexification, we find the following interesting result. Let $S=\{ z\in \mathbb {C}:0< \operatorname{Re}z <1\} $. We write $p_1\colon X\times S\rightarrow X$ for the natural projection. Corollary 6.1.24 . Let $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*\theta )$. Assume that for any $c\in \mathbb {R}$, $x\in X$ and $z\in S$, we have \[  \Phi (x,z)=\Phi (x,z+\mathrm{i}c).  \] Then $\int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ z)^ n$ is independent of $z\in S$, where $\Phi _ z \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is given by $\Phi _ z(x)=\Phi (x,z)$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We may regard $\Phi $ as an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*(\theta +\omega ))$. For any $0<a<b<1$, the restriction $(\Phi _ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is then a subgeodesic from $\Phi _ a$ to $\Phi _ b$ in the class $\theta +\omega $. The slices have positive mass in this class, so theorem 6.1.23 gives $\Phi _ a\sim _ P\Phi _ b$. By proposition 6.1.16 , this directly implies \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ b}^ n.  \] Since $\Phi $ is invariant under imaginary translations, $\Phi _ z$ depends only on $\operatorname{Re}z$, so the mass is independent of $z\in S$. $\square$

title: Proposition 6.1.16 (Monotonicity theorem)
text: Proposition 6.1.16 (Monotonicity theorem) . Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Let $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for each $i$. Then \[  \int _ X \theta _{1,\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X \theta _{1,\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \theta _{n,\psi _ n}.  \] In other words, the non-pluripolar mass is a decreasing quantity with respect to the $P$-singularity types of the potentials. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, since $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P\psi _ i$, we have \[  P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]\leq P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\psi _ i]  \] for all $\epsilon >0$. Therefore, by proposition 3.1.6 and our previous monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , we have \[  \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\leq \int _ X (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _1}\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\psi _ n}.  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ and applying the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , we find the desired inequality. $\square$

title: Theorem 6.1.17
text: Theorem 6.1.17 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then for any 6.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:arangetemp_reproduce} a\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right), \end{equation} the function \[  \eta \coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)\psi \Bigr )  \] lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ and 6.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:path_env_reproduce} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation} If in addition, $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $, then $\eta \sim _ P \varphi $ as well. Proof. By our assumption and ( 3.5 ), we have $\varphi \preceq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Due to proposition 3.1.6 , the interval ( 6.16 ) remains unchanged after replacing $\psi $ by $P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Fix $a$ in this interval. So by 2.4.15 and the discussions afterwards, \[  \eta '\coloneqq P_{\theta }\Bigl (a\varphi +(1-a)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\Bigr )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] We first check that $\eta $ is a genuine $\theta $-psh function. Choose a closed non-pluripolar set $K\subseteq X$ on which $\varphi $ and $\psi $ are bounded. Then the obstacle $a\varphi +(1-a)\psi $ is bounded above on $K$. Every candidate in the definition of $\eta $ is therefore uniformly bounded above on $X$ by 1.5.5 , so $\eta \not\equiv \infty $ and hence $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. On the other hand, since $\psi \preceq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$, we can find $C>0$ such that $\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]+C$. Then \[  \eta '-(a-1)C\leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere, hence $\eta \geq \eta '-(a-1)C$. Thus $\eta '\preceq \eta $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. By ( 2.32 ), \[  \eta \leq a\varphi +(1-a)\psi  \] quasi-everywhere. Equivalently, ( 6.17 ) holds quasi-everywhere. Since both sides of ( 6.17 ) are $\theta $-psh, proposition 1.2.6 upgrades the inequality to an everywhere inequality. It remains to prove the assertion about the $P$-order. Using proposition 3.1.24 , we get \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]+\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ] \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By the assumption $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi $, we also have $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\leq P_{\theta }[\psi ]$. Therefore, \[  a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]-\left(1-a^{-1}\right)P_{\theta }[\psi ]\leq a^{-1} P_{\theta }[\varphi ]  \] quasi-everywhere and hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . It follows that $P_{\theta }[\eta ]\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, namely $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $. Finally assume that $\varphi \sim _ P\psi $. Then $\int _ X\theta _{P_{\theta }[\psi ]}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$ by proposition 3.1.6 . Applying corollary 2.4.16 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta '}^ n=\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] Since $\eta '\preceq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ X\theta _{\eta }^ n\geq \int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] The reverse inequality follows from $\eta \preceq _ P\varphi $ and proposition 6.1.16 . Hence $\eta \sim _ P\varphi $ by proposition 6.1.4 . $\square$

6.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:arangetemp_reproduce} a\in \left( 1, \left(\frac{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n}{\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n}\right)^{1/n} \right), \end{equation}
6.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:path_env_reproduce} a^{-1}\eta +\left(1-a^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 6.1.18
text: Lemma 6.1.18 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Given two quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi ,\psi $ on $X$, then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $; $\pi ^*\varphi \preceq _{P} \pi ^*\psi $. The same holds with $\mathcal{I}$ in place of $P$. Proof. In the $P$-case, this follows from proposition 3.1.23 , while in the $\mathcal{I}$-case, this follows from proposition 3.2.7 . $\square$

title: Proposition 6.1.19
text: Proposition 6.1.19 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that \[  \varphi \preceq _ P \psi ,\quad \varphi '\preceq _ P \psi '.  \] Then \[  \varphi +\varphi '\preceq _ P \psi +\psi '.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of proposition 1.4.5 . We only need to handle the case of $\preceq _{P}$. Step 1 . We first show that \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\sim _ P \varphi +\varphi '.  \] In fact, we clearly have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\succeq \varphi +\varphi '.  \] So by proposition 6.1.4 , it suffices to show that they have the same mass. We compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \Bigl (2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^ n\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]\Bigr )^ j\wedge \Bigl (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\omega }[\varphi ']\Bigr )^{n-j}\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^ n \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \omega _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \omega _{\varphi '}^{n-j}\\  =&  \int _ X \left(2\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi '\right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where we applied proposition 3.1.6 to the mixed products on the third line. Step 2 . By Step 1, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '$ are all model potentials, after replacing them by their $P_{\omega }$-envelopes. So $\varphi \leq \psi $ and $\varphi '\leq \psi '$. Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 6.1.20
text: Proposition 6.1.20 . Let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$, $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be uniformly bounded from above non-empty families in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ i\preceq _ P \psi _ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i\preceq _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\psi _ i.  \] The same holds with $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ in place of $\preceq _ P$. Proof. By adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may assume that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$. The statement for $\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}$ is a simple consequence of corollary 1.4.6 , we only have to consider the statement for $\preceq _ P$. Step 1 . We first handle the case where $I$ is a directed set and $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ and $(\psi _ i)_{i\in I}$ are increasing nets. In this case, our assertion follows simply from proposition 3.1.28 . Step 2 . We handle the case where $I$ is finite. We may assume that $I=\{ 0,1\} $. It suffices to show that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi _0]\lor P_{\theta }[\varphi _1]\sim _ P \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1,  \] which follows from 6.1.7 . Step 3 . The general case can be reduced to the two cases handled in Step 1 and Step 2. More precisely, by applying proposition 1.2.3 to the two families and taking the union of the resulting countable subsets, we can find a countable subset $J\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i,\quad \operatorname *{sup}_{j\in J}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ j=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \psi _ i.  \] We may replace $I$ by $J$ and assume that $I$ is countable. If $I$ is finite, Step 2 applies directly. Otherwise, write $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and set \[  \tilde{\varphi }_ m=\varphi _1\lor \cdots \lor \varphi _ m,\quad \tilde{\psi }_ m=\psi _1\lor \cdots \lor \psi _ m.  \] By Step 2, $\tilde{\varphi }_ m\preceq _ P\tilde{\psi }_ m$ for every $m$. The two new sequences are increasing and have the same upper envelopes as the original families, so Step 1 applies. $\square$

title: Proposition 6.1.21
text: Proposition 6.1.21 . Let $\varphi ,\psi ,\varphi ',\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$. Assume that \[  \varphi \sim _ P \varphi ',\quad \psi \sim _ P\psi ',\quad \varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Then \[  \varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \varphi \land \psi \sim _ P \varphi '\land \psi '.  \] Proof. We first observe that $\varphi ,\varphi ',\psi ,\psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by assumption. Let \[  \phi \coloneqq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]=P_{\theta }[\varphi '],\quad \gamma =P_{\theta }[\psi ]=P_{\theta }[\psi '].  \] Since $\varphi '\preceq \phi $ and $\psi '\preceq \gamma $, after adding a common constant to $\varphi '$ and $\psi '$, we may assume that $\varphi '\leq \phi $ and $\psi '\leq \gamma $. Then $\varphi '\land \psi '\leq \phi \land \gamma $, so the assumption $\varphi '\land \psi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ implies $\phi \land \gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ by monotonicity. It follows from 3.1.17 that \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n.  \] Next, we apply 3.1.17 again to conclude that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi \land \psi }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\phi \land \gamma }^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi '\land \psi '}^ n>0.  \] Since $\varphi \land \psi \preceq \phi \land \gamma $ and the two potentials have the same positive mass, theorem 3.1.9 gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi \land \psi ]=\phi \land \gamma $. The same argument gives $P_{\theta }[\varphi '\land \psi ']=\phi \land \gamma $, hence $\varphi \land \psi \sim _ P\varphi '\land \psi '$. $\square$

title: Corollary 6.1.22
text: Corollary 6.1.22 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that $\psi \preceq _ P \varphi $. Then for any $C>0$, $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 6.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supvarphipsipC} P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation} Proof. Since $\psi \preceq _ P\varphi $, by proposition 6.1.21 , we get \[  \psi \land (\varphi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}  \] and $\psi \land (\varphi +C)\sim _ P\psi $ for every $C>0$. Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*}\psi \land (\varphi +C).  \] Then $\eta \sim _ P \psi $. By corollary 3.1.8 , we have \[  \theta _\eta ^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\{ \eta =\psi \} }\, \theta _\psi ^ n.  \] The domination principle theorem 2.4.17 gives $\eta \geq \psi $. The reverse inequality is trivial, so $\eta =\psi $. $\square$
6.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supvarphipsipC} P_{\theta }[\varphi ](\psi )=\operatorname *{sup}_{C>0}{}\! {}^{*} \psi \land (\varphi +C)=\psi . \end{equation}

title: Theorem 6.1.23
text: Theorem 6.1.23 . Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: There is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$; $\varphi _0\sim _ P\varphi _1$. Proof. 2 $\implies $ 1 . This follows from proposition 4.2.4 . 1 $\implies $ 2 . Let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Step 1 . We assume that $\varphi _0\geq \varphi _1$. We first replace the given subgeodesic by the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Note that the geodesic is necessarily a subgeodesic as well by 4.2.2 . Observe that $t\mapsto \varphi _ t$ is decreasing due to 4.2.5 . Let $\varphi _ t=\varphi _1$ for all $t>1$. Then by the gluing lemma 4.1.11 , we find that $(\varphi _ t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a subgeodesic ray. Next, we consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{t\geq 0}(\varphi _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] It follows from Kiselman's principle proposition 1.2.11 that $\Gamma _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $. Note that for $\tau >0$, we clearly have $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $. On the other hand, for $\tau \leq 0$, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t\in [0,1]}(\varphi _ t-t\tau )\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] By Legendre inversion (cf. corollary A.2.4 ), for $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left(\Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau \right).  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It follows from proposition 6.1.20 that for each $t>0$, \[  \varphi _ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }].  \] The right-hand side is independent of $t$. Here by adding $\omega $, we no longer have to worry about the possibility where $\Gamma _{\tau }$ has vanishing mass. Write \[  \varphi _0=\operatorname *{sup}_{t\in (0,1)}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ t.  \] By proposition 6.1.20 again, we find that \[  \varphi _0\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <0}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\tau }]  \] as well. So $\varphi _0\sim _ P \varphi _1$. Step 2 . We prove the general case. Observe that $(\varphi _ t\lor \varphi _1)_{t\in (0,1)}$ is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0\lor \varphi _1$ to $\varphi _1$. By Step 1, \[  \varphi _0\lor \varphi _1\sim _ P \varphi _1.  \] Hence $\varphi _0\preceq _ P \varphi _1$ by 6.1.8 . The converse is proved similarly. Hence 2 follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 6.1.24
text: Corollary 6.1.24 . Let $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*\theta )$. Assume that for any $c\in \mathbb {R}$, $x\in X$ and $z\in S$, we have \[  \Phi (x,z)=\Phi (x,z+\mathrm{i}c).  \] Then $\int _ X (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ z)^ n$ is independent of $z\in S$, where $\Phi _ z \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is given by $\Phi _ z(x)=\Phi (x,z)$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We may regard $\Phi $ as an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(X\times S,p_1^*(\theta +\omega ))$. For any $0<a<b<1$, the restriction $(\Phi _ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is then a subgeodesic from $\Phi _ a$ to $\Phi _ b$ in the class $\theta +\omega $. The slices have positive mass in this class, so theorem 6.1.23 gives $\Phi _ a\sim _ P\Phi _ b$. By proposition 6.1.16 , this directly implies \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ a}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\Phi _ b}^ n.  \] Since $\Phi $ is invariant under imaginary translations, $\Phi _ z$ depends only on $\operatorname{Re}z$, so the mass is independent of $z\in S$. $\square$

title: 6.2 The -pseudometric
text: 6.2 The $d_ S$-pseudometric Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. The goal of this section is to study a pseudometric on the space $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$.

title: 6.2.1 The definition of the -pseudometric
text: 6.2.1 The definition of the $d_ S$-pseudometric Recall that for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, the geodesic ray $\ell ^{\varphi }\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta )$ is defined in example 4.3.26 . Definition 6.2.1 . For $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\coloneqq d_1(\ell ^{\varphi },\ell ^{\psi }).  \] When we want to be more specific, we write $d_{S,\theta }$ instead of $d_ S$. The $d_1$ distance of geodesic rays is defined in definition 4.3.19 . Proposition 6.2.2 . The function $d_ S$ defined in definition 6.2.1 is a pseudometric on $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Proof. This follows immediately from theorem 4.3.20 . $\square$ When studying a pseudometric, the first thing is to understand when the distance between two elements vanishes. We first prove a preparation: Lemma 6.2.3 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )+d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi ) \leq C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. We shall use the notations introduced in example 4.3.26 . Proof. We claim that 6.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:elllorsingtype} \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }. \end{equation} Recall that $\lor $ is defined in definition 4.3.23 . Note that this assertion implies our desired inequality by 4.3.25 . In proving this assertion, we may assume that $\varphi ,\psi \leq 0$ since \[  \ell ^{\varphi +C}=\ell ^{\varphi },\quad \ell ^{\psi +C}=\ell ^{\psi },\quad \ell ^{(\varphi +C)\lor (\psi +C)}=\ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }  \] for any $C\in \mathbb {R}$. In fact, it is clear that \[  \ell ^{\varphi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },\quad \ell ^{\psi }\leq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi },  \] so the $\leq $ direction in ( 6.23 ) holds. Conversely, if $\ell '\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta )$ and $\ell '\geq \ell ^{\varphi }\lor \ell ^{\psi }$, then for each $t\geq 0$, \[  \ell '_ t\geq \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \varphi \Bigr ) \lor \Bigl ((V_{\theta }-t)\lor \psi \Bigr )=(V_{\theta }-t)\lor (\varphi \lor \psi ).  \] See ( 4.105 ) for the first inequality. Therefore, thanks to the definition of the Perron envelopes (cf. ( 4.7 )), we have \[  \ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi ,t}_ s  \] for any $0\leq s\leq t$. It follows from ( 4.105 ) that $\ell '_ s\geq \ell ^{\varphi \lor \psi }_ s$ for any $s\geq 0$. $\square$ Proposition 6.2.4 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $; $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$. In particular, $d_ S(\varphi ,P_{\theta }[\varphi ])=0$ for all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proof. By 6.1.8 , we have $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $ if and only if $\varphi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $ and $\psi \sim _ P \varphi \lor \psi $. By 6.2.3 , $d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=0$ if and only if $d_ S(\varphi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$ and $d_ S(\psi ,\varphi \lor \psi )=0$. So it suffices to prove the assertion when $\varphi \leq \psi $. Assuming this, by proposition 4.3.22 , 2 holds if and only if \[  \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\varphi }\right)= \mathbf{E}\left(\ell ^{\psi }\right),  \] where $\mathbf{E}$ is introduced in definition 4.3.21 . But by ( 4.103 ), this holds if and only if \[  \sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\sum _{j=0}^ n \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Thanks to the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , this holds if and only if for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j},  \] which is equivalent to 1 by proposition 6.1.4 . $\square$ Lemma 6.2.5 . Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Proof. Set $\chi \coloneqq \varphi \lor \psi $. By 6.1.8 , we have $\chi \sim _ P\psi $. Hence proposition 6.2.4 gives $d_ S(\chi ,\psi )=0$, and the pseudometric property gives \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )=d_ S(\varphi ,\chi ).  \] Since $\varphi \leq \chi $, ( 4.103 ) and proposition 4.3.22 give \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\chi )=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left(\int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}\right).  \] Finally, proposition 6.1.4 applied to $\psi \leq \chi $ gives \[  \int _ X \theta _{\chi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for all $j=0,\ldots ,n$. $\square$ Corollary 6.2.6 . Suppose that $\varphi ,\psi ,\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _ P\psi \preceq _ P \eta $. Then \[  d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),\quad d_ S(\varphi ,\eta )\geq d_ S(\psi ,\eta ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of 6.2.5 and the monotonicity theorem proposition 6.1.16 . $\square$ Corollary 6.2.7 . For any $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have 6.24 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ds_biineq} \begin{split}  d_ S(\varphi ,\psi )\leq &  \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{j=0}^ n \left( 2\int _ X \theta _{\varphi \lor \psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \right) \\  \leq &  C_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ), \end{split} \end{equation} where $C_ n=3(n+1)2^{n+2}$. In particular, if $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $d_ S$-limit $\varphi $, then for each $j=0,\ldots ,n$, \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i}^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}=\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}.  \] Proof. The estimates ( 6.24 ) follow from the combination of 6.2.5 and 6.2.3 . Suppose that $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then $\varphi _ i\lor \varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 6.2.3 . Therefore, theorem 2.4.8 and 6.2.5 imply that \[  \lim _{i\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ i\lor \varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}= \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ j\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}  \] for any $j=0,\ldots ,n$. The last assertion now follows from ( 6.24 ) and theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$ Corollary 6.2.8 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold. Given a net $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, the following are equivalent: $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $; $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Proof. It suffices to observe that the middle term in ( 6.24 ) is invariant under $\pi ^*$. $\square$ Corollary 6.2.9 . Suppose that $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ is an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, uniformly bounded from above. Then \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i.  \] If the $\varphi _ i$'s are all model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then so is $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ i$, as we have seen in proposition 3.1.28 . Proof. Write $\varphi =\operatorname *{sup}_{j\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\varphi _ j$. Recall that by proposition 1.2.2 , $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By 6.2.5 , it suffices to show that for each $k=0,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in I}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k} = \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ k\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-k}.  \] The latter follows from corollary 2.4.9 . $\square$ Corollary 6.2.10 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then \[  \left| \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\psi }^ n \right|\leq D_ n d_ S(\varphi ,\psi ),  \] where $D_ n=3(n+1)C_ n$ with $C_ n$ being the same constant as in 6.2.3 . In other words, the non-pluripolar mass is uniformly continuous with respect to the $d_ S$-pseudometric. Proof.
