Write $T_ i=	heta _{i}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$ as before. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta _ i+\omega $ is a Kähler form for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find $N_0>0$ so that for any $N\geq N_0$, the class of \[  \epsilon \omega + \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }c_ i[E_ i]  \] is Kähler. Take a Kähler form $\omega _ N$ in this class. Then the currents \[  \sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega  \] all lie in the same cohomology class. Moreover, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N.  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity in 5 , followed by the finite divisorial case of Step 1, \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(T+\epsilon \omega ,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \int _ X \omega _ N\wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ). \end{aligned}  \] Letting $N	o \infty $, and using $\{ \omega _ N\} 	o \{ \epsilon \omega \} $, we get \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ).  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 7.27 ). 6 Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$. In more concrete terms, we need to show that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ X (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n=\int _ X (	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n.  \] We may replace $\varphi $ by $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then we claim that \[  \varphi =\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] From this, our assertion follows from proposition 3.1.26 . The $\leq $ direction is clear. For the converse, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it suffices to show that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  
u (\varphi ,E)\leq 
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight).  \] We simply compute \[  
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)\geq \sup _{\epsilon >0}
u \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)=
u (\varphi ,E).  \] $\square$ Lemma 7.3.5 . Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X,\omega ,\{ T_1\} ,\ldots ,\{ T_ n\} $ such that \[  0\leq \operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega )-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq C\epsilon  \] for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$. Proof. By the multi-linearity established in proposition 7.3.4 , we can write \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega ight)-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)  \] as a linear combination of the $2^ n-1$-terms: \[  \epsilon ^ m\operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} ight)  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. It suffices to show that the coefficients are bounded by a constant as above. Take $D\geq 0$ as the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} +\{ T_ i\} $ is nef for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} ight)\leq \{ \omega \} ^ m\cap \left( \{ T_{i_1}\} +D\{ \omega \}  ight) \cap \cdots \cap \left( \{ T_{i_{n-m}}\} +D\{ \omega \}  ight).  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$ Next we show that theorem 6.2.30 continues to hold even when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. We prove a slightly more general result: Theorem 7.3.6 . Let $	heta _1,\ldots ,	heta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.39  egin{equation} \label{eq:convmixedvolds} \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}ight). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $. Then for any $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}ight)  \] as a consequence of corollary 6.2.19 , theorem 6.2.17 and theorem 6.2.27 . Now thanks to 7.3.5 , there is $C>0$ so that for each $k\in I$, \[   egin{aligned}  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}ight)-\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}ight)\leq C\epsilon ,\  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}ight)-\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}ight)\leq C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, ( 7.39 ) follows. $\square$ Corollary 7.3.7 . Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form representing a big cohomology class. Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then 7.42  egin{equation} \label{eq:Ivolcont2} \operatorname{vol}	heta _{\varphi _ j}	o \operatorname{vol}	heta _{\varphi },\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n	o \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. The first part of ( 7.42 ) is a special case of theorem 7.3.6 , while the second part of ( 7.42 ) is a special case of theorem 6.2.17 . $\square$ The mixed volume has a log-concavity property: Proposition 7.3.8 . Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n(\operatorname{vol}T_ i)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, we need to show that \[   egin{split} & \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  \geq &  \prod _{i=1}^ n\left(\int _ X \left(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^ n ight)^{1/n}. \end{split}  \] This is a special case of theorem 2.4.4 . $\square$ Next, we also study how the mixed volume behaves under bimeromorphic transforms. Proposition 7.3.9 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ to $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\pi ^*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*T_ night)=\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ night).  \] Proof. Using the definition of the mixed volume, we may easily reduce to the case where $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. By proposition 3.2.7 , we know that if we write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$, then \[  \pi ^*P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\pi ^*	heta _ i}[\pi ^*\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In particular, \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi ^*T_ i=\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0.  \] Our assertion follows from the bimeromorphic invariance of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.4.3 . $\square$ As for pushforward, we also have a similar result. We need a preliminary result: Lemma 7.3.10 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then for any non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $Y$, we have \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T=T+\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]  \] for finitely many $\pi $-exceptional divisors $E_ i$ and $c_ i>0$. Proof. Let $E$ be the exceptional locus of $\pi $. Then \[  T=\mathds {1}_{Y\setminus E}\pi ^* \pi _* T.  \] Therefore, \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T-T=\mathds {1}_ E\pi ^* \pi _* T,  \] which has the stated form, due to the support theorems, see [ Section 8 , DemBook ] . $\square$ Corollary 7.3.11 . Let $\pi \colon Xightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Then 7.45  egin{equation} \label{eq:volpushinc} \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation} Proof. Observe that we may assume that $T_ i=\operatorname{Reg}T_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In fact, since the pushforward of the divisorial part of $T_ i$ is divisorial as well, hence by proposition 7.3.4 5 , they do not contribute to the volumes. Now by proposition 7.3.9 , it remains to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi ^*\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*\pi _*T_ n).  \] By 7.3.10 , the difference $\pi ^*\pi _*T_ i-T_ i$ is divisorial, hence our desired equality follows from proposition 7.3.4 5 . $\square$ A particular corollary of corollary 7.3.11 will be useful later. Corollary 7.3.12 . Let $\pi \colon Xightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Assume that $T$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then so is $\pi _*T$. Proof. We may assume that $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then by corollary 7.3.11 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\operatorname{vol}T>0  \] as well. Since $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}T=\int _ X T^ n.  \] But $\int _ X T^ n=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n$, so \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n>0.  \] It follows that $\pi _*T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. $\square$ Finally we establish a semicontinuity property of the mixed volumes. Theorem 7.3.13 . Let $(\varphi _ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) be nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$, and $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$). Assume that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in J} 
u \left(\varphi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night).  \] Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i^ j)>0$ and $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $\varphi _ i^ j$'s and the $\varphi _ i$'s are $\mathcal{I}$-model for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Our assertion becomes 7.46  egin{equation} \label{eq:volineq_1} \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1ight) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{equation} For each $j\in J$, define \[  \psi _ i^ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i^ k,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Observe that $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good thanks to proposition 7.2.3 , since after the preceding reduction the tail family is bounded above by $0$. It follows from corollary 1.4.6 and our assumption that \[  \lim _{j\in J}
u \left(\psi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Moreover, for each $j\in J$, the same formula gives $\varphi _ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi _ i^ j$. Since $\varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model and $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, proposition 6.1.12 gives \[  \varphi _ i\leq P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we define \[  \psi _ i=\inf _{j\in J}P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] In particular, $\psi _ i\geq \varphi _ i$, so $\int _ X	heta _{i,\psi _ i}^ n>0$. Since $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, $P_{	heta _ i}[\psi _ i^ j]$ is both model and $\mathcal{I}$-model. Due to proposition 3.2.18 , $\psi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Thanks to proposition 3.1.26 , we know \[  
u (\psi _ i,E)=
u (\varphi _ i,E)  \] for any $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and any prime divisor $E$ over $X$. In other words, $\psi _ i\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi _ i$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. But both $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, therefore, \[  \psi _ i\sim _{P} \varphi _ i,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] By proposition 6.1.16 , we have \[  \int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n).  \] Next by proposition 6.1.16 again, \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight). \end{split}  \] On the other hand, due to proposition 3.1.26 and corollary 6.2.11 , for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \psi _ i^ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ i.  \] We conclude from theorem 6.2.17 that \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n).  \] Putting these equations together, ( 7.46 ) follows. Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, from Step 1, we know that \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{split}  \] Using 7.3.5 , we have \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] But since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Definition 7.3.1
text: Definition 7.3.1 . Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. We define the mixed volume $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ as follows: 7.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volmixed} \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right). \end{equation}

7.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volmixed} \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right). \end{equation}

title: Lemma 7.3.2
text: Lemma 7.3.2 . The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have 7.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mix_vol_comp1} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right). \end{equation} Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$ with positive volumes, then 7.10 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ with positive volumes and $\lambda > 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.11 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} Proof. 1 This follows from the symmetry of the mixed non-pluripolar product in ( 7.8 ), cf. proposition 2.2.2 2 . 2 For each $i$ and each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }\left[P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] as a consequence of example 7.1.7 . Hence using proposition 6.1.16 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 , \[  \begin{aligned} & \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega )\\  =& \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\int _ X \left(\theta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 3 We write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ as before for each $i$ and $T_1'=\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1'$. The potentials $P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal I}$ and $P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal I}$ are $\mathcal I$-model with positive masses, hence $\mathcal I$-good. By proposition 7.2.1 , their sum is $\mathcal I$-good. Moreover, it is $\mathcal I$-equivalent to $\varphi _1+\varphi _1'$. Then thanks to proposition 7.2.1 , \[  P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}\left[P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right]_{\mathcal{I}} = P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}\left[\varphi _1+\varphi _1'\right]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] Thus by proposition 6.1.16 , we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\\  =& \int _ X \left( \theta _1+\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}[\varphi _1+\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right)\wedge \left( \theta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \\ & \wedge \left( \theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =& \int _ X \left( \theta _1+\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right)\wedge \left( \theta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \\ & \wedge \left( \theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 4 This follows from ( 7.8 ), proposition 3.2.16 1 and proposition 2.2.2 6 . 5 Our assertion follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$

7.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mix_vol_comp1} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right). \end{equation}

title: Definition 7.3.3
text: Definition 7.3.3 . Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We define the mixed volume $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ as 7.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volmixedgeneral} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right). \end{equation} Note that $\operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega )$ is decreasing as $\epsilon \to 0+$ due to 7.3.2 3 , so the limit exists. Furthermore, $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ does not depend on the choice of $\omega $, as a consequence of 7.3.2 3 .

7.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volmixedgeneral} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 7.3.4
text:
Proposition 7.3.4 . The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$, then 7.22  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.23  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then 7.24  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\operatorname{Reg}T_1,\ldots ,\operatorname{Reg}T_ n ight). \end{equation} For any closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$, we have 7.25  egin{equation} \label{eq:mix_vol_ext_pure} \operatorname{vol}(T,\ldots ,T)=\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} Proof. 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 are immediate consequences of the corresponding properties proved in 7.3.2 . 5 Using 3 and 4 , it suffices to establish the following: Suppose that 7.26  egin{equation} \label{eq:T_count_sum_temp1} T=\sum _ i c_ i[E_ i] \end{equation} is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$, where $\{ E_ i\} $ is a countable collection of prime divisors on $X$ and $c_ i>0$. Then 7.27  egin{equation} \label{eq:volTT2Tn_temp1} \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=0 \end{equation} for any closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that ( 7.26 ) is a finite sum. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. In this case, thanks to 3 and 4 again, we may assume that $T=[E]$ for some prime divisor $E$ on $X$. Write $[E]=	heta _{\varphi }$. Then $\varphi $ has analytic singularities thanks to proposition 1.8.4 . Therefore, $P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim \varphi $ for any $\epsilon >0$ due to proposition 3.2.15 . Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$, and choose $C>0$ so that $C\omega +	heta _ i$ are Kähler forms for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Then \[   egin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\  =&  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ X \left([E]+\epsilon \omega ight)\wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =& \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  \leq & \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+C\omega ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+C\omega ight)\  =& 0, \end{aligned}  \] where the inequality step follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 and the fact that $P_{	heta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq 0$ for all $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Step 2 . We prove the case where $\{ E_ i\} $ is infinite. We may assume that $i$ runs over $\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Write $T_ i=	heta _{i}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$ as before. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta _ i+\omega $ is a Kähler form for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find $N_0>0$ so that for any $N\geq N_0$, the class of \[  \epsilon \omega + \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }c_ i[E_ i]  \] is Kähler. Take a Kähler form $\omega _ N$ in this class. Then the currents \[  \sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega  \] all lie in the same cohomology class. Moreover, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N.  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity in 5 , followed by the finite divisorial case of Step 1, \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(T+\epsilon \omega ,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \int _ X \omega _ N\wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ). \end{aligned}  \] Letting $N	o \infty $, and using $\{ \omega _ N\} 	o \{ \epsilon \omega \} $, we get \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ).  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 7.27 ). 6 Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$. In more concrete terms, we need to show that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ X (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n=\int _ X (	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n.  \] We may replace $\varphi $ by $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then we claim that \[  \varphi =\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] From this, our assertion follows from proposition 3.1.26 . The $\leq $ direction is clear. For the converse, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it suffices to show that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  
u (\varphi ,E)\leq 
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight).  \] We simply compute \[  
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)\geq \sup _{\epsilon >0}
u \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)=
u (\varphi ,E).  \] $\square$
7.25 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mix_vol_ext_pure} \operatorname{vol}(T,\ldots ,T)=\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation}
7.26 \begin{equation} \label{eq:T_count_sum_temp1} T=\sum _ i c_ i[E_ i] \end{equation}
7.27 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volTT2Tn_temp1} \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n \right)=0 \end{equation}

title: Lemma 7.3.5
text: Lemma 7.3.5 . Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X,\omega ,\{ T_1\} ,\ldots ,\{ T_ n\} $ such that \[  0\leq \operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega )-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq C\epsilon  \] for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$. Proof. By the multi-linearity established in proposition 7.3.4 , we can write \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right)-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)  \] as a linear combination of the $2^ n-1$-terms: \[  \epsilon ^ m\operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} \right)  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. It suffices to show that the coefficients are bounded by a constant as above. Take $D\geq 0$ as the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} +\{ T_ i\} $ is nef for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} \right)\leq \{ \omega \} ^ m\cap \left( \{ T_{i_1}\} +D\{ \omega \}  \right) \cap \cdots \cap \left( \{ T_{i_{n-m}}\} +D\{ \omega \}  \right).  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 7.3.6
text: Theorem 7.3.6 . Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.39 \begin{equation} \label{eq:convmixedvolds} \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\right). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $. Then for any $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\right)  \] as a consequence of corollary 6.2.19 , theorem 6.2.17 and theorem 6.2.27 . Now thanks to 7.3.5 , there is $C>0$ so that for each $k\in I$, \[  \begin{aligned}  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}\right)-\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\right)\leq C\epsilon ,\\  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\right)-\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\right)\leq C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, ( 7.39 ) follows. $\square$

7.39 \begin{equation} \label{eq:convmixedvolds} \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\right). \end{equation}

title: Corollary 7.3.7
text: Corollary 7.3.7 . Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form representing a big cohomology class. Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then 7.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ivolcont2} \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}\to \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi },\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\to \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. The first part of ( 7.42 ) is a special case of theorem 7.3.6 , while the second part of ( 7.42 ) is a special case of theorem 6.2.17 . $\square$

7.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ivolcont2} \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}\to \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi },\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\to \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 7.3.8
text: Proposition 7.3.8 . Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n(\operatorname{vol}T_ i)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, we need to show that \[  \begin{split} & \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  \geq &  \prod _{i=1}^ n\left(\int _ X \left(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} \right)^ n \right)^{1/n}. \end{split}  \] This is a special case of theorem 2.4.4 . $\square$

title: Proposition 7.3.9
text: Proposition 7.3.9 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ to $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\pi ^*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*T_ n\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right).  \] Proof. Using the definition of the mixed volume, we may easily reduce to the case where $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. By proposition 3.2.7 , we know that if we write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$, then \[  \pi ^*P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\pi ^*\theta _ i}[\pi ^*\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In particular, \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi ^*T_ i=\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0.  \] Our assertion follows from the bimeromorphic invariance of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.4.3 . $\square$

title: Lemma 7.3.10
text: Lemma 7.3.10 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then for any non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $Y$, we have \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T=T+\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]  \] for finitely many $\pi $-exceptional divisors $E_ i$ and $c_ i>0$. Proof. Let $E$ be the exceptional locus of $\pi $. Then \[  T=\mathds {1}_{Y\setminus E}\pi ^* \pi _* T.  \] Therefore, \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T-T=\mathds {1}_ E\pi ^* \pi _* T,  \] which has the stated form, due to the support theorems, see [ Section 8 , DemBook ] . $\square$

title: Corollary 7.3.11
text: Corollary 7.3.11 . Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Then 7.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volpushinc} \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation} Proof. Observe that we may assume that $T_ i=\operatorname{Reg}T_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In fact, since the pushforward of the divisorial part of $T_ i$ is divisorial as well, hence by proposition 7.3.4 5 , they do not contribute to the volumes. Now by proposition 7.3.9 , it remains to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi ^*\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*\pi _*T_ n).  \] By 7.3.10 , the difference $\pi ^*\pi _*T_ i-T_ i$ is divisorial, hence our desired equality follows from proposition 7.3.4 5 . $\square$
7.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volpushinc} \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation}

title: Corollary 7.3.12
text: Corollary 7.3.12 . Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Assume that $T$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then so is $\pi _*T$. Proof. We may assume that $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then by corollary 7.3.11 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\operatorname{vol}T>0  \] as well. Since $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}T=\int _ X T^ n.  \] But $\int _ X T^ n=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n$, so \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n>0.  \] It follows that $\pi _*T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. $\square$

title: Theorem 7.3.13
text:
Theorem 7.3.13 . Let $(\varphi _ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) be nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$, and $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$). Assume that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in J} 
u \left(\varphi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night).  \] Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i^ j)>0$ and $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $\varphi _ i^ j$'s and the $\varphi _ i$'s are $\mathcal{I}$-model for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Our assertion becomes 7.46  egin{equation} \label{eq:volineq_1} \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1ight) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{equation} For each $j\in J$, define \[  \psi _ i^ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i^ k,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Observe that $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good thanks to proposition 7.2.3 , since after the preceding reduction the tail family is bounded above by $0$. It follows from corollary 1.4.6 and our assumption that \[  \lim _{j\in J}
u \left(\psi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Moreover, for each $j\in J$, the same formula gives $\varphi _ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi _ i^ j$. Since $\varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model and $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, proposition 6.1.12 gives \[  \varphi _ i\leq P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we define \[  \psi _ i=\inf _{j\in J}P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] In particular, $\psi _ i\geq \varphi _ i$, so $\int _ X	heta _{i,\psi _ i}^ n>0$. Since $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, $P_{	heta _ i}[\psi _ i^ j]$ is both model and $\mathcal{I}$-model. Due to proposition 3.2.18 , $\psi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Thanks to proposition 3.1.26 , we know \[  
u (\psi _ i,E)=
u (\varphi _ i,E)  \] for any $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and any prime divisor $E$ over $X$. In other words, $\psi _ i\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi _ i$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. But both $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, therefore, \[  \psi _ i\sim _{P} \varphi _ i,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] By proposition 6.1.16 , we have \[  \int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n).  \] Next by proposition 6.1.16 again, \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight). \end{split}  \] On the other hand, due to proposition 3.1.26 and corollary 6.2.11 , for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \psi _ i^ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ i.  \] We conclude from theorem 6.2.17 that \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n).  \] Putting these equations together, ( 7.46 ) follows. Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, from Step 1, we know that \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{split}  \] Using 7.3.5 , we have \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] But since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$

7.46 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volineq_1} \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j\right)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j \right) \leq \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\right) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n\right). \end{equation}

title: 7.4 The volumes of Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles
search_title: The volumes of Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles
text:
7.4 The volumes of Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Definition 7.4.1 . A Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L,h)$ on a complex manifold $Y$ consists of a holomorphic line bundle $L$ on $Y$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $h$ on $L$. Theorem 7.4.2 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula) . Let $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$ and $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. We have 7.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DXmain1} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation} In particular, the limit exists. For the proof, let us fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h_0)$. We identify $h$ with $h_0\exp (-\varphi )$ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. See section 1.8 for the relevant notations. Recall that when $X$ admits a big line bundle, it is necessarily projective. See [ Theorem 2.2.26 , MM07 ] . We first handle the case where $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. Proposition 7.4.3 . Under the assumptions of theorem 7.4.2 , assume furthermore that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then ( 7.55 ) holds. Proof. Step 1 . Reduce to the case of log singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a log resolution of $\varphi $. In this case, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  h^0\Bigl (X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\Bigr )=h^0\Bigl (Y,K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T\otimes \pi ^*L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\pi ^*\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] By proposition 3.2.7 , we have \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)=\operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*h).  \] Therefore, it suffices to argue ( 7.55 ) with $K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T$, $\pi ^*L$ and $\pi ^*h$ in place of $T$, $L$ and $h$. Note that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is no longer a Kähler current, but it still has positive mass. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $D$. We may assume that $D$ is simple normal crossing by replacing $X$ by a modification and $D$ by the pull-back. We decompose $D$ into irreducible components, say \[  D=\sum _{i=1}^ N a_ iD_ i.  \] In this case, we can easily compute \[  \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Observe that $L-D$ is nef (see 1.6.4 ). Choose an integer $q>0$ so that $qD$ is integral. For each residue class $s=0,\ldots ,q-1$, we have \[  \left\lfloor (mq+s)D\right\rfloor =mqD+\lfloor sD\rfloor .  \] Hence, on the residue class $k=mq+s$, the line bundle \[  T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] is a fixed twist of $\left(q(L-D)\right)^ m$. Applying the asymptotic Riemann–Roch theorem [ Corollary 1.4.41 , PAG1 ] to the nef line bundle $q(L-D)$ and then letting $m\to \infty $ in each residue class, we conclude that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)\right)= (L-D)^ n.  \] Observe that by proposition 1.8.4 , \[  \theta _{\varphi }=[D]+S,  \] where $S$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential. Therefore, \[  (L-D)^ n=\int _ X S^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By example 7.1.6 , we know that the right-hand side is exactly $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$. $\square$ Proof of theorem 7.4.2 . Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Fix a Kähler form $\omega \geq \theta $ on $X$ such that $\theta _{\varphi }\geq 2\delta \omega $ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}\geq \delta \omega $ for all $j$. From proposition 7.4.3 , we know that for each $j\geq 1$, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}.  \] It follows from theorem 7.1.1 and theorem 6.2.30 that the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$ as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] Conversely, fix an integer $N>\delta ^{-1}$. From theorem 7.1.1 and theorem 6.2.17 , we know that 7.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:quasiequmassconvtemp1} \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n>0. \end{equation} Therefore, by 2.4.15 , we can find $j_0>0$ such that for $j\geq j_0$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ (depending on $j$) with 7.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:linearlowerbdPItemp1} (1-N^{-1})\varphi _ j+N^{-1}\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} For each $k>0$, we write $k=k'N-r$, where $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then we compute for $j\geq j_0$ and large enough $k$ (to be specified shortly) that \[  \begin{aligned} &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'(\psi +(N-1)\varphi _ j)\right)\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right), \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows from ( 7.57 ), the fourth line can be argued as follows: For large enough $k$, there is a non-zero section $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'\psi ))$ by 2.4.20 . It follows from 1.6.14 that for large enough $k$, \[  \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right).  \] It follows that multiplication by $s$ gives an injective map \[  \begin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right)\hookrightarrow \\  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'\psi +k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right)\right). \end{split}  \] Next observe that \[  (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j= N\theta _{\varphi _ j}-\theta \geq N\delta \omega -\theta \geq (N\delta -1)\omega .  \] Since $N>\delta ^{-1}$, this is a Kähler current. Hence proposition 7.4.3 is applicable. We let $k\to \infty $ to conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) \geq &  N^{-n}\int _{X} \left( (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \left((1-N^{-1})\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n -C N^{-1}, \end{aligned}  \] where $C$ is a constant independent of $N$ and $j$. Letting $j\to \infty $ and then $N\to \infty $ and using ( 7.56 ), we find that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n.  \] Therefore, ( 7.55 ) follows. Step 2 . We handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. First observe that $L$ is big by proposition 2.4.2 . Hence $X$ is projective. Take a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(A)$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A=\omega $. Fix $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We decompose any $k>0$ as $k=k'N+r$ with $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then \[  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes A^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  =&  \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)^{n}, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line uses multiplication by a non-zero section of $A^{k'}$, and we have applied Step 1 to the Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L^ N\otimes A,h^{\otimes N}\otimes h_ A)$ on the fourth line. On the other hand, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 7.1.7 , 7.1.4 gives \[  P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ].  \] It follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ n.  \] Letting $N\to \infty $, we conclude \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] It remains to argue the reverse inequality. Choose $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. The existence of $\psi $ is guaranteed by 2.4.19 . Then for any $t\in (0,1)$, we set \[  \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t\psi .  \] It follows again from Step 1 that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ t)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}.  \] On the other hand, by theorem 7.3.6 and corollary 6.2.20 , \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] So we find \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] We conclude ( 7.55 ) in this case. Step 3 . We finally handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }=0$. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Assume that ( 7.55 ) fails. That is, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\right)\geq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)>0,  \] then $L$ is a big line bundle and hence $X$ is projective. Fix a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(A)$. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ of rational numbers with limit $0$ and a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )_{>0}$. We claim that as $j\to \infty $, the sequence $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $. It is clear that this sequence is decreasing. Let $\psi $ denote its limit for the moment. It is also clear that $\psi \geq \varphi $. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it remains to show that $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Fix $\lambda >0$. By strong openness, choose $\lambda '>\lambda $ such that $\mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )=\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )$. For $j$ large enough, the quasi-equisingularity of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ gives \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ),  \] where the first inclusion uses $\psi \leq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ and $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi _ j$. Thus $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, and the claim follows. By our claim, proposition 3.1.6 and proposition 3.1.26 , we find that 7.71 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volumeconv0temp1} \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Fix $j>0$, take an integer $N>0$ so that $N\epsilon _ j$ is an integer. Then we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes A^{k'N\epsilon _ j}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  =&  \frac{1}{N^ n}\int _ X \left( N\theta +\epsilon _ jN\omega +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows by writing $k=Nk'+a$ as before, we applied Step 2 on the last line. Dividing by $N^ n$, we find that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n.  \] Since we know ( 7.71 ), letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=0,  \] which is a contradiction. Hence ( 7.55 ) is established in full generality. $\square$ Corollary 7.4.4 . Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$, and let $h$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Then we have 7.77 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volbig} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\right)=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to observe that 7.78 \begin{equation} \label{eq:H0eqH0IVtheta} \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\right) \end{equation} for all $k>0$, since for any holomorphic section $s$ of $L^ k$, the function $\log |s|_{h^ k}^2$ is $\theta $-psh thanks to proposition 1.8.4 and therefore, we have \[  \frac{1}{k}\log |s|_{h^ k}^2\preceq V_{\theta }.  \] In particular, $s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)$. $\square$ This common quantity is the volume of $L$, usually denoted by $\operatorname{vol}L$. In view of definition 3.2.11 , we have 7.79 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volL_volc1L} \operatorname{vol}L=\operatorname{vol}c_1(L). \end{equation} Example 7.4.5 . If $X$ is a smooth projective toric variety and $\theta $ is invariant under the action of the compact torus, then any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. Thanks to 7.1.4 , we may assume that $\theta \in c_1(L)$ for some toric invariant ample line bundle $L$. In this case, the result follows from theorem 7.1.1 , theorem 7.4.2 and theorem 5.2.14 . $\square$ Some of our philosophers made a serious mistake: without having grasped the substance of the matter, they began to deny the significance of a new direction in science. 
— S. L. Sobolev Note. Sergei Lvovich Sobolev (1908–1989) was a Soviet mathematician whose work on weak derivatives, generalized functions, and embedding theorems became foundational for modern analysis and partial differential equations. He also contributed to mathematical physics, numerical analysis, cubature formulas, and cybernetics, and was later central to the mathematical life of Akademgorodok in Novosibirsk. , A. I. Kitov and A. A. Lyapunov in Вопросы философии

title: Definition 7.4.1
text: Definition 7.4.1 . A Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L,h)$ on a complex manifold $Y$ consists of a holomorphic line bundle $L$ on $Y$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $h$ on $L$.

title: Theorem 7.4.2 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula)
text: Theorem 7.4.2 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula) . Let $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$ and $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. We have 7.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DXmain1} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation} In particular, the limit exists. Proof of theorem 7.4.2 . Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Fix a Kähler form $\omega \geq \theta $ on $X$ such that $\theta _{\varphi }\geq 2\delta \omega $ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}\geq \delta \omega $ for all $j$. From proposition 7.4.3 , we know that for each $j\geq 1$, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}.  \] It follows from theorem 7.1.1 and theorem 6.2.30 that the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$ as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] Conversely, fix an integer $N>\delta ^{-1}$. From theorem 7.1.1 and theorem 6.2.17 , we know that 7.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:quasiequmassconvtemp1} \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n>0. \end{equation} Therefore, by 2.4.15 , we can find $j_0>0$ such that for $j\geq j_0$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ (depending on $j$) with 7.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:linearlowerbdPItemp1} (1-N^{-1})\varphi _ j+N^{-1}\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} For each $k>0$, we write $k=k'N-r$, where $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then we compute for $j\geq j_0$ and large enough $k$ (to be specified shortly) that \[  \begin{aligned} &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'(\psi +(N-1)\varphi _ j)\right)\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right), \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows from ( 7.57 ), the fourth line can be argued as follows: For large enough $k$, there is a non-zero section $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'\psi ))$ by 2.4.20 . It follows from 1.6.14 that for large enough $k$, \[  \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right).  \] It follows that multiplication by $s$ gives an injective map \[  \begin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right)\hookrightarrow \\  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'\psi +k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right)\right). \end{split}  \] Next observe that \[  (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j= N\theta _{\varphi _ j}-\theta \geq N\delta \omega -\theta \geq (N\delta -1)\omega .  \] Since $N>\delta ^{-1}$, this is a Kähler current. Hence proposition 7.4.3 is applicable. We let $k\to \infty $ to conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) \geq &  N^{-n}\int _{X} \left( (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \left((1-N^{-1})\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n -C N^{-1}, \end{aligned}  \] where $C$ is a constant independent of $N$ and $j$. Letting $j\to \infty $ and then $N\to \infty $ and using ( 7.56 ), we find that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n.  \] Therefore, ( 7.55 ) follows. Step 2 . We handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. First observe that $L$ is big by proposition 2.4.2 . Hence $X$ is projective. Take a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(A)$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A=\omega $. Fix $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We decompose any $k>0$ as $k=k'N+r$ with $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then \[  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes A^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  =&  \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)^{n}, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line uses multiplication by a non-zero section of $A^{k'}$, and we have applied Step 1 to the Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L^ N\otimes A,h^{\otimes N}\otimes h_ A)$ on the fourth line. On the other hand, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 7.1.7 , 7.1.4 gives \[  P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ].  \] It follows from proposition 3.1.6 that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ n.  \] Letting $N\to \infty $, we conclude \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] It remains to argue the reverse inequality. Choose $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. The existence of $\psi $ is guaranteed by 2.4.19 . Then for any $t\in (0,1)$, we set \[  \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t\psi .  \] It follows again from Step 1 that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ t)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}.  \] On the other hand, by theorem 7.3.6 and corollary 6.2.20 , \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] So we find \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] We conclude ( 7.55 ) in this case. Step 3 . We finally handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }=0$. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Assume that ( 7.55 ) fails. That is, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\right)\geq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)>0,  \] then $L$ is a big line bundle and hence $X$ is projective. Fix a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(A)$. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ of rational numbers with limit $0$ and a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )_{>0}$. We claim that as $j\to \infty $, the sequence $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $. It is clear that this sequence is decreasing. Let $\psi $ denote its limit for the moment. It is also clear that $\psi \geq \varphi $. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it remains to show that $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Fix $\lambda >0$. By strong openness, choose $\lambda '>\lambda $ such that $\mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )=\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )$. For $j$ large enough, the quasi-equisingularity of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ gives \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ),  \] where the first inclusion uses $\psi \leq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ and $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi _ j$. Thus $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, and the claim follows. By our claim, proposition 3.1.6 and proposition 3.1.26 , we find that 7.71 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volumeconv0temp1} \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Fix $j>0$, take an integer $N>0$ so that $N\epsilon _ j$ is an integer. Then we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes A^{k'N\epsilon _ j}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  =&  \frac{1}{N^ n}\int _ X \left( N\theta +\epsilon _ jN\omega +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows by writing $k=Nk'+a$ as before, we applied Step 2 on the last line. Dividing by $N^ n$, we find that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n.  \] Since we know ( 7.71 ), letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=0,  \] which is a contradiction. Hence ( 7.55 ) is established in full generality. $\square$

7.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DXmain1} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 7.4.3
text: Proposition 7.4.3 . Under the assumptions of theorem 7.4.2 , assume furthermore that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then ( 7.55 ) holds. Proof. Step 1 . Reduce to the case of log singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a log resolution of $\varphi $. In this case, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  h^0\Bigl (X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\Bigr )=h^0\Bigl (Y,K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T\otimes \pi ^*L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\pi ^*\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] By proposition 3.2.7 , we have \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)=\operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*h).  \] Therefore, it suffices to argue ( 7.55 ) with $K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T$, $\pi ^*L$ and $\pi ^*h$ in place of $T$, $L$ and $h$. Note that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is no longer a Kähler current, but it still has positive mass. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $D$. We may assume that $D$ is simple normal crossing by replacing $X$ by a modification and $D$ by the pull-back. We decompose $D$ into irreducible components, say \[  D=\sum _{i=1}^ N a_ iD_ i.  \] In this case, we can easily compute \[  \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Observe that $L-D$ is nef (see 1.6.4 ). Choose an integer $q>0$ so that $qD$ is integral. For each residue class $s=0,\ldots ,q-1$, we have \[  \left\lfloor (mq+s)D\right\rfloor =mqD+\lfloor sD\rfloor .  \] Hence, on the residue class $k=mq+s$, the line bundle \[  T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] is a fixed twist of $\left(q(L-D)\right)^ m$. Applying the asymptotic Riemann–Roch theorem [ Corollary 1.4.41 , PAG1 ] to the nef line bundle $q(L-D)$ and then letting $m\to \infty $ in each residue class, we conclude that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)\right)= (L-D)^ n.  \] Observe that by proposition 1.8.4 , \[  \theta _{\varphi }=[D]+S,  \] where $S$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential. Therefore, \[  (L-D)^ n=\int _ X S^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By example 7.1.6 , we know that the right-hand side is exactly $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$. $\square$
7.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:quasiequmassconvtemp1} \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n>0. \end{equation}
7.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:linearlowerbdPItemp1} (1-N^{-1})\varphi _ j+N^{-1}\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation}

7.71 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volumeconv0temp1} \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 7.4.4
text: Corollary 7.4.4 . Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$, and let $h$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Then we have 7.77 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volbig} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\right)=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to observe that 7.78 \begin{equation} \label{eq:H0eqH0IVtheta} \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\right) \end{equation} for all $k>0$, since for any holomorphic section $s$ of $L^ k$, the function $\log |s|_{h^ k}^2$ is $\theta $-psh thanks to proposition 1.8.4 and therefore, we have \[  \frac{1}{k}\log |s|_{h^ k}^2\preceq V_{\theta }.  \] In particular, $s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)$. $\square$
7.77 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volbig} \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\right)=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{equation}
7.78 \begin{equation} \label{eq:H0eqH0IVtheta} \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\right) \end{equation}
7.79 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volL_volc1L} \operatorname{vol}L=\operatorname{vol}c_1(L). \end{equation}

title: Example 7.4.5
text: Example 7.4.5 . If $X$ is a smooth projective toric variety and $\theta $ is invariant under the action of the compact torus, then any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. Thanks to 7.1.4 , we may assume that $\theta \in c_1(L)$ for some toric invariant ample line bundle $L$. In this case, the result follows from theorem 7.1.1 , theorem 7.4.2 and theorem 5.2.14 . $\square$

title: 8 The trace operator
text: 8 The trace operator The goal of this chapter is to give a meaning to the restriction of a quasi-psh singularity to a subvariety. If $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ and $Y\subseteq X$ is a subvariety, the naive restriction $\varphi |_ Y$ is often unsatisfactory: it may be identically $-\infty $, or it may fail to preserve quasi-equisingular approximations. There is a useful analogy with the trace operator in real analysis. A Sobolev function on a domain cannot, in general, be restricted pointwise to the boundary; instead, it admits a trace obtained by approximation using smooth functions, and the trace is well-defined modulo almost everywhere equality. 8 summarizes the corresponding dictionary. Real analysis Pluripotential theory smooth functions potentials with analytic singularities Sobolev functions potentials with $\mathcal I$-good singularities Sobolev convergence $d_ S$-convergence equality almost everywhere $P$-equivalence Table 8.1 A dictionary for the trace operator. The situation here is similar. A singular quasi-psh function need not have a meaningful pointwise restriction to $Y$, but after replacing it by quasi-equisingular approximants and passing to the appropriate $d_ S$-limit of the pointwise restriction of these approximants to $Y$, one obtains a well-defined $P$-singularity type. This is the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$. The trace operator is designed to be compatible with the two comparison theories developed earlier. It depends only on the $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type of $\varphi $, and itself is well-defined modulo $P$-equivalence. The first part of the chapter defines the trace and proves its basic properties: independence of the quasi-equisingular approximation, monotonicity, linearity, compatibility with bimeromorphic pullback, and continuity under decreasing $d_ S$-limits. These results provide the analytic foundation for later applications. The second part relates the trace operator to restricted volumes. For a big class $\alpha $ and a subvariety $Y$ not contained in the non-Kähler locus, the classical restricted volume $\operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )$ can be expressed as the non-pluripolar volume of the trace of a potential with minimal singularities. We also prove an asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula for the restricted multiplier ideal sheaves. The final part develops analytic Bertini-type statements. These results describe when multiplier ideals restrict correctly to a general hypersurface and when $\mathcal I$-goodness is preserved under restriction.

title: 8.1 The definition of the trace operator
