text:
8.1 The definition of the trace operator Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. The trace operator gives a way to restrict a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on $X$ to $\widetilde{Y}$, the normalization of $Y$. It follows from [ Proposition 3.6 , GK20 ] that $\widetilde{Y}$ is a normal Kähler space. We refer to chapter B for the pluripotential theory on unibranch Kähler spaces. For later applications, we need this generality even if initially we are only interested in the smooth case. Before diving into the trace operator, let us try to understand what goes wrong with the naive restriction procedure: simply take $\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}$. Both examples below are local, but can easily be globalized since the singularities are isolated. Example 8.1.1 . Consider the case where $\varphi $ has log-log singularities as in example 3.1.14 . Locally we can take $\varphi (z)=-\log (-\log |z|^2)$. We have $
u (\varphi ,0)=0$ but $\varphi |_0=-\infty $. So the naive restriction is not defined in this case. Even if the naive restriction is defined, it does not behave well. Example 8.1.2 . Consider a psh function $\varphi $ in two variables, say \[  \varphi (z,w)=\left( -\log (-\log |z|^2)ight) \lor \left(\log |w|^2ight).  \] Take an arbitrary quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$. Then each $\varphi _ j$ is locally bounded since $
u (\varphi ,(0,0))=0$. Let us consider the restrictions to $H=\{ z=0\} $. Then $\varphi _ j|_ H$ is still bounded, while \[  \varphi |_ H(w)=\log |w|^2.  \] In other words, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ fail to be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi |_ H$. Our trace operator gives an elegant way to solve both problems. We first observe that if $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ has analytic singularities and $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$, then $\varphi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $. Indeed, if $\varphi |_ Y\equiv -\infty $, then in a local presentation \[  \varphi =c\log (|f_1|^2+\cdots +|f_ N|^2)+\mathcal{O}(1)  \] all generators $f_1,\ldots ,f_ N$ vanish along $Y$, which gives $
u (\varphi ,Y)>0$, a contradiction. This observation will be crucial in the sequel. Proposition 8.1.3 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be a function such that $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Let $(\varphi _ i)_ i$, $(\psi _ i)_ i$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $. Then 8.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:dsequivtemp1} \lim _{i	o \infty } d_ S\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)=0. \end{equation} Here in ( 8.1 ), $d_ S$ refers to any $d_{S,	heta }$, where $	heta $ is any closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $\widetilde{Y}$ representing a big cohomology class and satisfying $\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(\widetilde{Y},	heta )$. For different choices of $	heta $, ( 8.1 ) remains equivalent, as explained in corollary 6.2.19 . Proof. After subtracting a common constant from $\varphi $, $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$, we may assume that $\varphi _ i\leq 0$ for all $i\geq 1$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega /2)$ for all $i\geq 1$. By corollary 6.2.19 , we need to show that \[  \lim _{i	o \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)=0.  \] Assume that this fails. Then, up to replacing the sequences by subsequences, we may assume that the following limit exists and \[  \lim _{i	o \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)>0.  \] Take a Kähler form $	ilde{\omega }$ on $\widetilde{Y}$. Then \[  \lim _{i	o \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+	ilde{\omega }}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)>0  \] by corollary 6.2.19 . By corollary 7.1.10 , after changing the background class from $\omega /2$ to $\omega $ if necessary, we have \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I},\quad \psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Let \[  \chi _ i\coloneqq \varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i.  \] By proposition 6.2.23 , we have $\chi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Moreover, $(\chi _ i)_ i$ is again a quasi-equisingular approximation of the original potential $\varphi $ as follows from corollary 7.1.10 . The triangle inequality gives \[  d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}) \leq d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}})+ d_ S(\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}).  \] Thus, after passing to a subsequence and interchanging the two quasi-equisingular approximations if necessary, we may assume that \[  \varliminf _{i	o \infty }d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}})>0.  \] Replacing $(\psi _ i)_ i$ by $(\chi _ i)_ i$, we may therefore assume that \[  \varphi _ i\leq \psi _ i  \] for all $i$, while preserving the contradiction assumption. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $\mathbb {R}_{>0}$ with limit $0$ such that $(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. We first observe that \[  \lim _{i	o \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)=0.  \] This is a consequence of 6.2.14 . title: Example 8.1.1
text: Example 8.1.1 . Consider the case where $\varphi $ has log-log singularities as in example 3.1.14 . Locally we can take $\varphi (z)=-\log (-\log |z|^2)$. We have $\nu (\varphi ,0)=0$ but $\varphi |_0=-\infty $. So the naive restriction is not defined in this case.

title: Example 8.1.2
text: Example 8.1.2 . Consider a psh function $\varphi $ in two variables, say \[  \varphi (z,w)=\left( -\log (-\log |z|^2)\right) \lor \left(\log |w|^2\right).  \] Take an arbitrary quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$. Then each $\varphi _ j$ is locally bounded since $\nu (\varphi ,(0,0))=0$. Let us consider the restrictions to $H=\{ z=0\} $. Then $\varphi _ j|_ H$ is still bounded, while \[  \varphi |_ H(w)=\log |w|^2.  \] In other words, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ fail to be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi |_ H$.

title: Proposition 8.1.3
text: Proposition 8.1.3 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be a function such that $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Let $(\varphi _ i)_ i$, $(\psi _ i)_ i$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $. Then 8.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:dsequivtemp1} \lim _{i\to \infty } d_ S\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)=0. \end{equation} Proof. After subtracting a common constant from $\varphi $, $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$, we may assume that $\varphi _ i\leq 0$ for all $i\geq 1$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi _ i,\psi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega /2)$ for all $i\geq 1$. By corollary 6.2.19 , we need to show that \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)=0.  \] Assume that this fails. Then, up to replacing the sequences by subsequences, we may assume that the following limit exists and \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)>0.  \] Take a Kähler form $\tilde{\omega }$ on $\widetilde{Y}$. Then \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)>0  \] by corollary 6.2.19 . By corollary 7.1.10 , after changing the background class from $\omega /2$ to $\omega $ if necessary, we have \[  \varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I},\quad \psi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] Let \[  \chi _ i\coloneqq \varphi _ i\lor \psi _ i.  \] By proposition 6.2.23 , we have $\chi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Moreover, $(\chi _ i)_ i$ is again a quasi-equisingular approximation of the original potential $\varphi $ as follows from corollary 7.1.10 . The triangle inequality gives \[  d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}) \leq d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}})+ d_ S(\psi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}).  \] Thus, after passing to a subsequence and interchanging the two quasi-equisingular approximations if necessary, we may assume that \[  \varliminf _{i\to \infty }d_ S(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},\chi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}})>0.  \] Replacing $(\psi _ i)_ i$ by $(\chi _ i)_ i$, we may therefore assume that \[  \varphi _ i\leq \psi _ i  \] for all $i$, while preserving the contradiction assumption. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $\mathbb {R}_{>0}$ with limit $0$ such that $(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. We first observe that \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)=0.  \] This is a consequence of 6.2.14 . Hence, by corollary 6.2.19 , we find \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}},(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)=0.  \] Since $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ and $(\epsilon _ i)_ i$ are decreasing and $\varphi _ i\leq 0$, the sequence $\bigl ((1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\bigr )_ i$ is decreasing. It has uniformly positive mass in the class $\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }$. Hence corollary 6.2.13 , together with the preceding estimate, gives a potential $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(\widetilde{Y},\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega })$ such that \[  \varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi .  \] Hence, \[  \lim _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\psi ,(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)=0.  \] By proposition 1.6.11 , after choosing $j_ i$ inductively with $j_ i\geq i$ and $j_ i>j_{i-1}$, we may assume that \[  \psi _{j_ i}\preceq (1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i.  \] Since we have arranged $\varphi _ j\leq \psi _ j$ for all $j$, it follows that \[  \varphi _{j_ i}\leq \psi _{j_ i}\preceq (1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i.  \] Hence, \[  \varphi _{j_ i}|_{\widetilde{Y}}\leq \psi _{j_ i}|_{\widetilde{Y}}\preceq (1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}.  \] Therefore, by corollary 6.2.6 , \[  \begin{aligned}  \varlimsup _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\varphi _{j_ i}|_{\widetilde{Y}},\psi _{j_ i}|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right) \leq &  \varlimsup _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\varphi _{j_ i}|_{\widetilde{Y}},(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)\\  =&  \varlimsup _{i\to \infty } d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\tilde{\omega }}\left(\psi ,(1-\epsilon _ i)\varphi _ i|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)\\  = &  0, \end{aligned}  \] which is a contradiction. $\square$

title: 8.2 Properties of the trace operator
text:
8.2 Properties of the trace operator Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We prove a few elementary properties of the trace operator. Proposition 8.2.1 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, $\lambda >0$. Assume that $
u (\varphi ,Y)=
u (\psi ,Y)=0$. Then we have the following: Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $. Then $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi )$. We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi +\psi )\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )+\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi ).  \] We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\lambda \varphi )\sim _ P \lambda \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi \lor \psi )\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\lor \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi ).  \] As a consequence of 1 , the $P$-equivalence class of $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$ depends only on the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\varphi $. Proof. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ such that $	heta _{\varphi }$, $	heta _{\psi }$ are both Kähler currents. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ and $(\psi _ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $ and $\psi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ respectively. We may assume that $\varphi _ j\leq 0$ and $\psi _ j\leq 0$ for all $j\geq 1$. 1 We choose the quasi-equisingular approximations compatibly. By theorem 1.6.10 , we may take $\varphi _ j$ and $\psi _ j$ with analytic singularities of types \[  \left(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi )ight), \quad \left(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\psi )ight),  \] respectively. Since $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal I}\psi $, we have \[  \mathcal I(2^ j\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal I(2^ j\psi )  \] for every $j$. Hence $\varphi _ j\preceq \psi _ j$ for every $j$. Restricting to $\widetilde{Y}$, we get $\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\preceq \psi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$. Then $(\lambda _ j\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\lambda \varphi $. Since $\lambda _ j/\lambda 	o 1$, 6.2.14 gives \[  d_ S\left((\lambda _ j/\lambda )\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}},\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)	o 0.  \] After scaling the background class, 6.2.22 shows that $\lambda _ j\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ and $\lambda \varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ have the same $d_ S$-limit. The assertion follows. 4 By proposition 6.2.23 , we have \[  \varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] By proposition 3.2.16 and proposition 7.2.1 , we have \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Therefore, our assertion follows exactly as in the proof of 2 . $\square$ The trace operator is continuous along $d_ S$-convergent decreasing sequences. Proposition 8.2.2 . Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ such that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ for each $j\in I$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ and $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Then \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ j)\xrightarrow {d_ S}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] In view of corollary 7.1.10 , the trace operator preserves the property of being a quasi-equisingular approximation, thereby solving the problem in example 8.1.1 . Proof. It is enough to prove the sequential assertion. Indeed, suppose that the net statement fails. Then there is $\delta >0$ such that for every $i_0\in I$ one can find $i\geq i_0$ with \[  d_ S(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ i),\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\geq \delta .  \] Using also $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, we may choose an increasing sequence $i_ j\in I$ such that \[  d_ S(\varphi _{i_ j},\varphi )<j^{-1},\quad d_ S(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _{i_ j}),\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\geq \delta .  \] The sequence $(\varphi _{i_ j})_ j$ is decreasing and converges to $\varphi $ in $d_ S$, contradicting the sequential assertion. Thus we assume that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\geq 1}$ is a decreasing sequence and that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]$, we may then assume that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials. By proposition 6.2.26 , we have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=\inf _{j\geq 1}\varphi _ j.  \] By proposition 6.2.4 , we may assume from now on that \[  \varphi =\inf _{j\geq 1}\varphi _ j.  \] After adding a Kähler form to $\omega $, we may assume that $\omega _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. For each $j\geq 1$, choose a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\geq 1}$ of $\varphi _ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. Using the standard construction in theorem 1.6.10 , we may choose these approximations compatibly in $j$, so that for each fixed $k$, \[  \varphi _{j+1}^ k\preceq \varphi _ j^ k  \] We shall choose an increasing sequence of integers $k_ j$ and put \[  \eta _ j\coloneqq \varphi _ j^{k_ j}.  \] The sequence $(k_ j)_ j$ is chosen inductively: Choose $k_1>1$, for $j>1$, we choose $k_ j$ large enough so that $k_{j}\geq k_{j-1}$; $d_{S,\omega }(\eta _ j,P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}})\leq 1/(j-1)$; $d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}(\eta _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}},\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\omega }(\varphi _ j))<1/(j-1)$. Indeed, \[  \eta _{j+1}=\varphi _{j+1}^{k_{j+1}}\preceq \varphi _{j+1}^{k_ j}\preceq \varphi _ j^{k_ j}=\eta _ j.  \] By theorem 6.2.27 , we have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xlongrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] By 2 and corollary 7.1.10 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Observe that by proposition 6.2.26 , \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\inf _{j>0} P_{\omega }\left[\eta _ jight].  \] By proposition 3.2.15 , for each $j>0$, $P_{\omega }[\eta _ j]$ has analytic singularities. The trace operator is not continuous along increasing sequences. Let us consider the case $X=\mathbb {P}^2$ with coordinates $(z_1,z_2)$ on $\mathbb {C}^2\subseteq X$. Consider an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}})$, whose potentials near $(0,0)$ are given by \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2ight)+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] The pointwise restriction of these potentials to $Y$ are given locally by \[  \log |z_1|^2+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] On the other hand, locally \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2ight)	o 0  \] almost everywhere as $j	o \infty $. Let $\pi \colon Zightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism, where $Z$ is a connected Kähler manifold. Assume that $W$ (resp. $Y$) is an irreducible analytic subset of $Z$ (resp. $X$) such that the restriction $\Pi \colon Wightarrow Y$ of $\pi $ is defined and is bimeromorphic, so that we have the following commutative diagram \[  \gerbyimage{sgpt/4a441c4a133434105b61.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source}  \] Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $

Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Assume that $Y$ is smooth. We may assume that $Y
eq X$ and that $	heta _{\varphi } \geq 3\delta \omega $ for some $\delta >0$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be the decreasing quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Restricting to $\widetilde{Y}$, we get $\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\preceq \psi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$. Since $\lambda _ j/\lambda \to 1$, 6.2.14 gives \[  d_ S\left((\lambda _ j/\lambda )\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}},\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)\to 0.  \] After scaling the background class, 6.2.22 shows that $\lambda _ j\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ and $\lambda \varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ have the same $d_ S$-limit. title: Theorem 8.2.6
text: Theorem 8.2.6 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing $c_1(L)$. Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Assume that $Y$ is smooth and $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Let $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k_0$ such that for all $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$, there exists an extension $\tilde s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a Hermitian metric $h_ T$ on $T$. We may assume that $Y\neq X$ and that $\theta _{\varphi } \geq 3\delta \omega $ for some $\delta >0$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be the decreasing quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We can assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j} \geq 2\delta \omega $ for all $j\geq 1$. Also, there exists $\epsilon _0 >0$ such that $\theta _{(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j} \geq \delta \omega $ for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. Take $k_0=k_0(\delta ,h_ T)$ as in theorem 1.8.12 . We fix $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$. By theorem 1.4.16 , there exists $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$ such that $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$. As a result, $\tilde s_ j \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for high enough $j$, finishing the argument. $\square$

8.3 Relation to the classical restricted volumes Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $Y$ be a connected submanifold of dimension $m$. Fix a big class $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta \in \alpha $. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Recall that the notions of non-Kähler locus and non-nef locus were defined in definition 1.7.8 and definition 1.7.10 . When $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nK}(\alpha )$, Matsumura ( [ Definition 1.4 , Mat13 ] ) defines the restricted volume of $\{ 	heta \} $ to $Y$ in the following manner: 8.12  egin{equation} \label{eq:rest_vol_Mat_def} \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )\coloneqq \sup _{\varphi } \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ Yight)^{m}, \end{equation} where $\varphi $ runs over elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $. This definition is independent of the choice of $	heta $. In case $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nn}(\alpha )$, Collins–Tosatti [ CT22 ] extend the above definition of restricted volume: 8.13  egin{equation} \label{eq:rest_vol_CT_def} \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )\coloneqq \lim _{\epsilon \searrow 0}\sup _{\varphi } \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ Yight)^ m. \end{equation} where $\varphi $ runs over elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\epsilon \omega )$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $. This definition is independent of the choice of $	heta $. These definitions extend the more classical definition in the algebraic setting due to [ ELMNP09 ] . Proposition 8.3.1 . Assume that $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nK}(\alpha )$. Then 8.14  egin{equation} \label{eq:volrest} \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )= \int _ Y \left( 	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta }) ight)^ m =\int _ Y (	heta |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_	heta |_ Y)^ m. \end{equation} Proof. We start with the first equality of ( 8.14 ). Since $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nK}(\alpha )$, $V_{	heta }|_ Y 
ot\equiv -\infty $ as a consequence of 2.4.6 , hence also $
u (V_{	heta },Y)=0$. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$ of $V_{	heta }$ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$ for a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_{j>0}$ converging to $0$. By the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , we have for each $j>0$, \[  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _ j\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\geq \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi |_ Yight)^ m  \] for every $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ with $\chi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $. Since $\chi $ is arbitrary, we conclude that \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _ j\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\geq \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha ).  \] For any fixed $\epsilon >0$, we have \[   egin{split}  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _ j\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\leq &  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon \omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\  =&  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon \omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta +\epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta })ight)^ m. \end{split}  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$ and applying example 8.1.12 , we conclude that the $\leq $ direction in the first equality of ( 8.14 ) holds. Moreover, $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nK}(\alpha )$ implies $\operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )>0$ by ( 8.12 ). Hence the limiting mass in example 8.1.12 is positive, and $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^	heta (V_	heta )$ is indeed defined in the present situation. For the reverse direction, by definition, for any fixed $\epsilon >0$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _ j\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m & \leq \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon \omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\ & \leq \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\{ 	heta \} +\epsilon \{ \omega \} ) \end{aligned}  \] for all large enough $j$. Therefore, for large $j$, by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 , we have \[  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _ j\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta })ight)^ m\leq \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\{ 	heta \} +\epsilon \{ \omega \} ).  \] Letting $j	o \infty $ and $\epsilon \searrow 0$, using the continuity of $\operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}$ ( [ Corollary 4.11 , Mat13 ] ) together with example 8.1.12 , we conclude the first equality of ( 8.14 ). ot\subseteq \operatorname{nn}(\alpha )$, then 8.19  egin{equation} \label{eq:non-nef_rest_vol}  egin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha ) & = \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \Bigl (	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }|_ Y\Bigr )^ m\  =& \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }) ight)^ m \ & =\int _ Y \left( 	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta }) ight)^ m, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the last term is understood as $0$ if $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta })$ is not defined. Proof. Since $
u (V_	heta , Y)=0$, we have $Y
ot\subseteq \operatorname{nK}(\alpha +\epsilon \{ \omega \} )$ for all $\epsilon >0$. Therefore, by ( 8.13 ) and ( 8.14 ), only the last equality of ( 8.19 ) needs to be argued. Thus $M$ is the last term of ( 8.19 ), with the convention made in the statement. Thanks to theorem 6.2.17 , for any $\epsilon _0>0$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _0 \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _0 \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega })} & = \int _ Y (	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _0 \omega |_ Y)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _0 \omega }(V_{	heta })}. \end{aligned}  \] By the definition of $M$, this implies the existence of $(\epsilon _ j)_{j>0}$ such that $0<\epsilon _ j<1/j$ and 8.24  egin{equation} \label{eq:limit_1} \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + j^{-1}\omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + j^{-1} \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } = M. \end{equation} Moreover, for each $j>0$, 8.25  egin{equation} \label{eq:limit_2}  egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + j^{-1} \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + j^{-1} \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } \geq &  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _ j \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _ j\omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } \  \geq &  M. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Indeed, the first inequality follows from the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 . For the second one, if $M=0$ there is nothing to prove; if $M>0$, then example 8.1.12 shows that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^	heta (V_	heta )$ is defined, and the inequality follows from the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 and the monotonicity theorem proposition 6.1.16 . Putting ( 8.24 ) and ( 8.25 ) together, it follows that \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _ j \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } = M.  \] Finally, since $\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }) ight)^ m$ depends monotonically on $\epsilon >0$, we conclude that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }) ight)^ m=M.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: 8.4 Restricted volumes of line bundles
text:
8.4 Restricted volumes of line bundles Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n$ and $Y\subseteq X$ be a connected submanifold of dimension $m$. Consider a big line bundle $L$ on $X$, a Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$ with $	heta =c_1(L,h_0)$. Let $A$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ such that $\omega =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A$ is a Kähler form. Using the trace operator, one could prove the following generalization of theorem 7.4.2 : Theorem 8.4.1 . Let $h$ be a (singular) plurisubharmonic metric on $L$ with $
u (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h,Y)=0$. Assume that 8.28  egin{equation} \label{eq:traceposmasscond2} \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ Y\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)+\epsilon \omega |_ Y} igl (c_1(L,h) igr ) ight)^ m>0. \end{equation} Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have 8.29  egin{equation} \label{eq:DXmainrelative} \int _ Y \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)} igl (c_1(L,h) igr )ight)^ m = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(h^{k})ight) ight). \end{equation} Recall that $\operatorname{Res}_ Y$ is defined in definition 1.4.18 . Observe that by example 8.1.12 , ( 8.28 ) implies that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)}(c_1(L,h))$ is defined. So ( 8.29 ) is defined. We will identify $h$ with $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ as in ( 1.47 ). For the proof, recall that the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_{\infty }$ is introduced in definition 1.6.12 . Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. After possibly replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there exists $\epsilon _0 \in (0,1)\cap \mathbb {Q}$ such that the $	heta _{(1-\epsilon ) \varphi _ j}$'s are also Kähler currents for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. For any rational $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$, and sufficiently large $k$, we have \[   egin{aligned} &  rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m \  =&  \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight) \quad 	extup{by theorem \gerbyref{60272F70}{7.4.2}}\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight) \quad 	extup{ by proposition \gerbyref{B56231C4}{8.2.5}}\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi _ jight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ jight)ight) \quad 	extup{by \gerbyref{D0481B70}{1.6.14}}\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j|_ Yight)ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left((1-\epsilon ) k\varphi _ j|_ Yight) ight)\  = &   rac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+(1-\epsilon )\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\quad 	extup{by theorem \gerbyref{60272F70}{7.4.2}}. \end{aligned}  \] Here we used the observation that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with analytic singularities with $\psi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_ Y \mathcal{I}_{\infty }(\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(\psi |_ Yight).  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, 6.2.14 gives \[  (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Hence, by theorem 6.2.17 , the last term converges to \[   rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m.  \] We conclude that \[   egin{aligned}   rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m\leq &  \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight)\  \leq &   rac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $j	o \infty $, we conclude ( 8.29 ). Step 2 . We handle the general case. After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Using proposition 8.2.5 and theorem 7.4.2 we obtain that \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m & = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight)\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight). \end{aligned}  \] Now we address the other direction in ( 8.29 ). Let $\phi \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$ be a section that does not vanish identically on $Y$. Such $\phi $ exists since $A$ is very ample. We fix $k_0 \in \mathbb {N}$. For any $k \geq 0$, we have $k = q k_0 + r$ with $q,r \in \mathbb {N}$ and $r \in \{ 0,\ldots , k_0-1\} $. Also, we have an injective linear map \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight)\xrightarrow {\cdot \phi ^{\otimes q}} \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight).  \] Therefore, \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi ight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi ight)ight) \  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1} rac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q	o \infty }  rac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left((qk_0+r)\varphi ight)ight)\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1} rac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q	o \infty }  rac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k_0q \varphi ight)ight)\  = &  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta +k_0^{-1}\omega }(\varphi )ight)^ m\  =&  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where the maximum is taken over the finitely many residue classes $k=qk_0+r$, the following inequality uses $k_0q\leq k$, the first equality follows by applying Step 1 for each $r$ to the big line bundle $L^{k_0} \otimes A$, the Kähler current $k_0 	heta _{\varphi } + \omega $, and twisting bundle $T \otimes L^ r$, and the second equality follows from proposition 3.1.6 . Letting $k_0	o \infty $ and using the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight)\leq \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Theorem 8.4.2 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $
u (\varphi ,Y) =0$. Assume that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have \[  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} .  \] Proof. This is a consequence of theorem 7.4.2 , theorem 8.2.6 and theorem 8.4.1 : \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m &  = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight)\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} \ &  \leq \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} \ &  \leq \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y ,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)\ &  = \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Remark 8.4.3 . One could also show that when ( 8.28 ) fails, the right-hand side of ( 8.29 ) is $0$. See [ DX24 ] .

title: Theorem 8.4.1
text: Theorem 8.4.1 . Let $h$ be a (singular) plurisubharmonic metric on $L$ with $\nu (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h,Y)=0$. Assume that 8.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:traceposmasscond2} \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ Y\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)+\epsilon \omega |_ Y}\bigl (c_1(L,h)\bigr ) \right)^ m>0. \end{equation} Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have 8.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DXmainrelative} \int _ Y \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)}\bigl (c_1(L,h)\bigr )\right)^ m = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(h^{k})\right) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. After possibly replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there exists $\epsilon _0 \in (0,1)\cap \mathbb {Q}$ such that the $\theta _{(1-\epsilon ) \varphi _ j}$'s are also Kähler currents for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. For any rational $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$, and sufficiently large $k$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m \\  =&  \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right) \quad \textup{by theorem \gerbyref{60272F70}{7.4.2}}\\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right) \quad \textup{ by proposition \gerbyref{B56231C4}{8.2.5}}\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi _ j\right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j\right)\right) \quad \textup{by \gerbyref{D0481B70}{1.6.14}}\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left((1-\epsilon ) k\varphi _ j|_ Y\right) \right)\\  = &  \frac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+(1-\epsilon )\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m\quad \textup{by theorem \gerbyref{60272F70}{7.4.2}}. \end{aligned}  \] Here we used the observation that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with analytic singularities with $\psi |_ Y\not\equiv -\infty $, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_ Y \mathcal{I}_{\infty }(\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(\psi |_ Y\right).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, 6.2.14 gives \[  (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Hence, by theorem 6.2.17 , the last term converges to \[  \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m.  \] We conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m\leq &  \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude ( 8.29 ). Step 2 . We handle the general case. After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Using proposition 8.2.5 and theorem 7.4.2 we obtain that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m & = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right)\\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right). \end{aligned}  \] Now we address the other direction in ( 8.29 ). Let $\phi \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$ be a section that does not vanish identically on $Y$. Such $\phi $ exists since $A$ is very ample. We fix $k_0 \in \mathbb {N}$. For any $k \geq 0$, we have $k = q k_0 + r$ with $q,r \in \mathbb {N}$ and $r \in \{ 0,\ldots , k_0-1\} $. Also, we have an injective linear map \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right)\xrightarrow {\cdot \phi ^{\otimes q}} \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi \right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi \right)\right) \\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1}\frac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q\to \infty } \frac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left((qk_0+r)\varphi \right)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1}\frac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q\to \infty } \frac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k_0q \varphi \right)\right)\\  = &  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +k_0^{-1}\omega }(\varphi )\right)^ m\\  =&  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where the maximum is taken over the finitely many residue classes $k=qk_0+r$, the following inequality uses $k_0q\leq k$, the first equality follows by applying Step 1 for each $r$ to the big line bundle $L^{k_0} \otimes A$, the Kähler current $k_0 \theta _{\varphi } + \omega $, and twisting bundle $T \otimes L^ r$, and the second equality follows from proposition 3.1.6 . Letting $k_0\to \infty $ and using the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 2.2.2 6 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right)\leq \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$
8.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:traceposmasscond2} \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ Y\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)+\epsilon \omega |_ Y}\bigl (c_1(L,h)\bigr ) \right)^ m>0. \end{equation}

title: Theorem 8.4.2
text: Theorem 8.4.2 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\nu (\varphi ,Y) =0$. Assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have \[  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} .  \] Proof. This is a consequence of theorem 7.4.2 , theorem 8.2.6 and theorem 8.4.1 : \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m &  = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right)\\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} \\ &  \leq \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} \\ &  \leq \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y ,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\ &  = \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] This completes the proof. $\square$
