title: 8.5 Analytic Bertini theorems
text:
8.5 Analytic Bertini theorems Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$. The analytic Bertini theorem handles the restriction along a generic subvariety. Theorem 8.5.1 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Let $p\colon Xightarrow \mathbb {P}^ N$ be a morphism ($N\geq 1$). Define \[  \mathcal{G}\coloneqq \Bigl \{ H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|: H'\coloneqq H\cap X 	extup{ is smooth and } \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H'})=\operatorname{Res}_{H'} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr \} .  \] Then $\mathcal{G}\subseteq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ is co-pluripolar. Recall that co-pluripolar sets are defined in definition 1.1.15 . We adopt the convention that $\mathcal{I}(-\infty )=0$. Remark 8.5.2 . Here and in the sequel, we slightly abuse the notation by writing $H\cap X$ for $p^{-1}H$, the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $H$. In other words, $H\cap X\coloneqq H	imes _{\mathbb {P}^ N} X$. By definition, any $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ such that $p^{-1}H=\emptyset $ lies in $\mathcal{G}$. Proof. Take an ample line bundle $L$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ such that $c_1(L,h)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq 0$, where $c_1(L,h)$ is the first Chern form of $(L,h)$, namely the curvature form of $h$. We introduce $\Lambda \coloneqq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ to simplify our notations. Step 1 . We prove that the following set is co-pluripolar: \[   egin{split}  \mathcal{G}_{L}\coloneqq \left\{ H\in \Lambda : H\cap X 	ext{ is smooth and } \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )= ight.\  \left. \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr )ight\} . \end{split}  \] Here $\omega _{H\cap X}$ denotes the dualizing sheaf of $H\cap X$. Let $U\subseteq \Lambda 	imes X$ be the closed subvariety whose $\mathbb {C}$-points correspond to pairs $(H,x)\in \Lambda 	imes X$ with $p(x)\in H$. Let $\pi _1\colon Uightarrow \Lambda $ be the natural projection. We may assume that $\pi _1$ is surjective, as otherwise there is nothing to prove. Observe that $U$ is a local complete intersection scheme by Krull's Hauptidealsatz and a fortiori a Cohen–Macaulay scheme. It follows from miracle flatness [ Theorem 23.1 , Mat89 ] that the natural projection $\pi _2\colon Uightarrow X$ is flat. As the fibers of $\pi _2$ over closed points of $X$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb {P}^{N-1}$, it follows that $\pi _2$ is smooth. Thus, $U$ is smooth as well. Moreover, observe that 8.57  egin{equation} \label{eq:pi2pullvarphiItemp1} \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )=\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) \end{equation} by proposition 1.4.17 . In the following, we will construct pluripolar sets $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Sigma _2 \subseteq \Sigma _3\subseteq \Sigma _4\subseteq \Lambda $ such that the behavior of $\pi _1$ is improved successively on the complement of $\Sigma _ i$. Step 1.1 . The usual Bertini theorem shows that there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\pi _1$ has smooth fibers outside $\Sigma _1$. Enlarging $\Sigma _1$, we may guarantee that $\pi _1$ and $\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ are both flat outside $\Sigma _1$. See [ Théorème 6.9.1 , EGAIV2 ] . Then after further enlarging $\Sigma _1$ we may assume that $p^{-1}(H)$ avoids all associated points of $\mathcal{O}_ X/\mathcal{I}(\varphi )$, for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Let $\pi _{1,H}$ denote the fiber of $\pi _1$ at $H$ and write $i_ H\colon \pi _{1,H}ightarrow U$ for the inclusion morphism. We arrive at \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ))=i_ H^*\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )  \] for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Note. This subtle point was overlooked in the proof of [ XiaBer ] . Step 1.2 . By Grauert's coherence theorem, \[  \mathcal{F}^ i\coloneqq R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L\otimes \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ) ight)  \] is coherent for all $i$. Here $\omega _{U/\Lambda }$ denotes the relative dualizing sheaf of the morphism $Uightarrow \Lambda $. Thus, there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _2\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\Sigma _2\supseteq \Sigma _1$. The $\mathcal{F}^ i$'s are locally free outside $\Sigma _2$. We write $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}^0$. By cohomology and base change [ Theorem III.12.11 , Har ] , for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _2$, the fiber $\mathcal{F}|_ H$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is given by \[  \mathcal{F}|_ H= \mathrm{H}^0\left(\pi _{1,H},\omega _{U/\Lambda }|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \pi _2^*L|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )) ight).  \] Step 1.3 . In order to proceed, we need to make use of the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ on $\mathcal{F}$ defined in [ HPS18 ] . We briefly recall its definition in our setting. By [ Section 22 , HPS18 ] , we can find a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _3\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\Sigma _3\supseteq \Sigma _2$, $\pi _1$ is smooth outside $\Sigma _3$, both $\mathcal{F}$ and $\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)/\mathcal{F}$ are locally free outside $\Sigma _3$, and for each $i$, \[  R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)  \] is locally free outside $\Sigma _3$. Then for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, \[   egin{gathered} \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})ight)\ \subseteq \mathcal{F}|_ H\subseteq \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}ight). \end{gathered}  \] See [ Lemma 22.1 , HPS18 ] . Now we can give the definition of the Hodge metric on $\Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$. Given any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, any $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}|_ H$, the Hodge metric is defined as \[  h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha ):=\int _{X\cap H} |\alpha |^2_{h}\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\in [0,\infty ].  \] Observe that $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )<\infty $ if and only if $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^0(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X}))$. Moreover, $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )>0$ if $\alpha 
eq 0$. It is shown in [ HPS18 ] (cf. [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] ) that $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is indeed a singular Hermitian metric, and it extends to a positive metric on $\mathcal{F}$. Step 1.4 . The determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )
eq \mathcal{F}|_ H.  \] As the map $\pi _2$ is smooth, we have $\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )= \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ by proposition 1.4.17 . Under the identification $\pi _{1,H}\cong H\cap X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}\Bigl (\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr )\cong \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\Bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] Thus, we have the following inclusions: \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  \subseteq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ), \end{split}  \] the right-hand side being $\mathcal{F}|_ H$. Recall that the first inclusion follows from theorem 1.4.19 . Hence, $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|\setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  
eq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Let $\Sigma _4$ be the union of $\Sigma _3$ and the set of all such $H$. Since the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is positive ( [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] and [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS18 ] ), its determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is also positive ( [ Proposition 1.3 , Rau15 ] and [ Proposition 25.1 , HPS18 ] ), it follows that $\Sigma _4$ is pluripolar. As a consequence, $\mathcal{G}_{L}$ is co-pluripolar. Step 2 . Fix an ample invertible sheaf $S$ on $X$. The same result holds with $L\otimes S^{\otimes a}$ in place of $L$. Thus, the set \[  A\coloneqq  igcap _{a=0}^{\infty }\mathcal{G}_{L\otimes S^{\otimes a}}  \] is co-pluripolar. For each $H\in \Lambda $ such that $X\cap H$ is smooth and $\mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})
eq \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}(\mathcal{I}(\varphi ))$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be the following cokernel: \[  0ightarrow \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)ightarrow \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )ightarrow \mathcal{K}ightarrow 0.  \] By Serre vanishing theorem, taking $a$ large enough, we may guarantee that \[  \mathrm{H}^1\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})\Bigr )=0  \] and \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{K}\Bigr )
eq 0.  \] Then \[   egin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)\Bigr )
eq \  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Thus, $H
ot\in A$. We conclude that $\mathcal{G}$ is co-pluripolar. $\square$ Remark 8.5.3 . More generally, the same technique implies the following general result: Let $f\colon Xightarrow Y$ be a projective morphism between complex manifolds and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Then for quasi-every Note. That is, for all $y$ outside a pluripolar subset of $Y$. $y\in Y$, the fiber $X_ y$ is smooth and \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda h|_{X_ y})=\operatorname{Res}_{X_ y}\left( \mathcal{I}(\lambda h) ight).  \] In the sequel of this section, we fix a base-point free linear system $\Lambda $ on $X$. For the results below that assert connectedness, we assume in addition that the set of connected smooth members of $\Lambda $ is co-pluripolar in $\Lambda $. Corollary 8.5.4 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, we have $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $. Proof. For quasi-every $H$, theorem 8.5.1 gives \[  \mathcal I(\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_ H\mathcal I(\varphi ).  \] After removing the hyperplanes meeting the associated points of $\mathcal O_ X/\mathcal I(\varphi )$ improperly, the right-hand side is non-zero. Since $\mathcal I(-\infty )=0$, this implies $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $. $\square$ Corollary 8.5.5 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, satisfies $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi |_ H.  \] The connectedness assumption on $H$ is used here because we developed most of the trace theory above for connected submanifolds. Proof. First observe that the set $\{ x\in X:
u (\varphi ,x)>0\} $ is a countable union of proper analytic subsets by Siu's semicontinuity theorem theorem 1.4.4 . It follows that a very general element in $\Lambda $ is not contained in this set. Fix an ample line bundle $L$ so that there is a smooth Hermitian metric $h_ L$ such that $c_1(L,h_ L)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Thanks to theorem 8.5.1 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies the following: $H$ is smooth and connected; $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; $\mathcal{I}(k\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_{H}(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for all $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Put $\alpha _ H\coloneqq c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H$. It follows from theorem 8.4.1 and theorem 7.4.2 that \[  \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{c_1(L,h_ L)}(\varphi )ight)^{n-1} = \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}\left[\varphi |_ Hight]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^{n-1}.  \] Since $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ by proposition 8.1.9 , we also have $\varphi |_ H\preceq _{\mathcal I}\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$. Hence \[  P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\varphi |_ H]_{\mathcal I}\leq P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The trace is $\mathcal I$-good, so the right-hand side agrees with its $P$-envelope. The equality of the masses above and theorem 3.1.9 then imply that the two sides have the same $P$-singularity type, hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] $\square$ Lemma 8.5.6 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $T|_ H$ is well-defined and satisfies \[  \int _ H T|_ H^{n-1}>0.  \] Proof. Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$ for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Thanks to 2.4.19 , we can find $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $	heta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. By corollary 8.5.4 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; the restriction $\psi |_ H$ is not identically $-\infty $. Since $	heta _\psi $ is a Kähler current, its restriction to such an $H$ has positive non-pluripolar mass. As $\psi |_ H\leq \varphi |_ H$, theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ H(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H)^{n-1} \geq \int _ H(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H)^{n-1}>0.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$ Corollary 8.5.7 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{\{ T\} |_ H}(T)$ is well-defined and has positive volume. Proof. Write $T=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and set $\psi =P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Then $\psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^{n}=\operatorname{vol}T>0.  \] By 8.5.6 , for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, the hypersurface $H$ is connected and smooth, $\psi |_ H$ is well-defined, and \[  \int _ H \left(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ Hight)^{n-1}>0.  \] For such $H$, corollary 8.5.5 gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi |_ H$. Since $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, proposition 8.2.1 also gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )$. The assertion now follows from example 8.1.12 . $\square$ Proposition 8.5.8 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \psi |_ H$. Proof. Thanks to 6.1.8 , we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. It suffices to show that $\varphi |_ H\sim _ P \psi |_ H$ for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $. Take a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ so that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. It suffices to compare $\varphi $ and $\psi $ with $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$, so without loss of generality, we may assume that $\psi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Up to adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may then assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. It follows from 2.4.15 that we can find a sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ such that \[  j^{-1}\eta _ j+\left(1-j^{-1}ight)\psi \leq \varphi  \] for all $j\geq 2$. By corollary 8.5.4 , 8.5.6 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 2$ and $\psi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 3.1.24 into account, we arrive at \[  j^{-1} P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\eta _ j|_ H igr ]+\left(1-j^{-1}ight)P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\psi |_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ]  \] for all $j\geq 2$. The normalized envelopes $P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are uniformly bounded in $L^1$, hence \[  j^{-1}P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\xrightarrow {L^1} 0.  \] We conclude that \[  P_{	heta |_ H}[\psi |_ H]\leq P_{	heta |_ H}[\varphi |_ H]  \] and hence $\psi |_ H\preceq _ P \varphi |_ H$. $\square$ Lemma 8.5.9 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class and $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Furthermore, assume that $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j$ for each $j>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $\varphi _ j|_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $ for all $j\geq 1$, $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. By corollary 6.2.19 , we may assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Using 2.4.15 , we can find a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $(0,1)$ with limit $0$ and $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ such that $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j$ and \[  \epsilon _ j\eta _ j+(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] By corollary 8.5.4 , 8.5.6 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 1$ and $\varphi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 3.1.24 into account, we arrive at \[  \epsilon _ j P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\eta _ j|_ H igr ]+\left(1-\epsilon _ jight)P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi _ j|_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ].  \] Since the normalized envelopes $P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are relatively compact in $L^1$, we have $\epsilon _ jP_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]	o 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $j	o \infty $, we get \[  \lim _{j	o \infty } P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi _ j|_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ].  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, so we get an equality here. By theorem 2.4.8 and proposition 3.1.26 , we conclude that \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ H \Bigl (	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}=\int _ H \Bigl (	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}.  \] Therefore, using corollary 6.2.11 , we conclude that $\varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H$. $\square$ Corollary 8.5.10 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be an $\mathcal{I}$-good potential. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ satisfies: $H$ is connected and smooth; $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good; $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; $\operatorname{Tr}_ H \varphi \sim _ P \varphi |_ H$. Furthermore, if $	heta $ is a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, then we can further guarantee, on the same co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Proof. Choose a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta _0$ representing a big class such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _0)$ and $	heta _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _0)_{>0}$. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal I$-good, corollary 7.1.10 , theorem 7.1.1 , proposition 6.2.4 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi .  \] Applying 8.5.9 , we find a co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $ such that $H$ is connected and smooth, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are not identically $-\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] For such an $H$, the potentials $\varphi _ j|_ H$ have analytic singularities, hence are $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.6 . It follows from corollary 7.1.5 that $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal I$-good. On the other hand, corollary 8.5.5 gives, after intersecting with another co-pluripolar set of parameters $H$, that $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] The trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 8.1.5 . Since both $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are $\mathcal I$-good, their $\mathcal I$-equivalence identifies their $\mathcal I$-envelopes, which agree with their $P$-envelopes. Hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\varphi |_ H.  \] Finally corollary 8.5.7 shows, after intersecting with one more co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative in $\mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. $\square$ For later use, let us also prove a reverse Bertini theorem here. Lemma 8.5.11 (Reverse Bertini theorem) . Let $X$ be a complex manifold, $f\colon Xightarrow \Delta ^*$ be a projective surjective morphism to the punctured unit disk $\Delta ^*$. Let $(L,h)$, $(L,h')$ be Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles on $X$ with the same underlying line bundle. Assume that there is a biholomorphic $S^1$-action on $(X,L)$ making $f$ equivariant and such that $h$ and $h'$ are invariant under this action. Assume that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, $X_ z$ is smooth and $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$. Then $h\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'$. Proof. We need to show that $\mathcal{I}(kh)=\mathcal{I}(kh')$ for every positive integer $k$. It suffices to prove the case $k=1$, since our assumptions are invariant after replacing $h$ and $h'$ by $h^ k$ and $h'^ k$. We will therefore prove $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. First observe that it suffices to prove that 8.64  egin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr )=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \end{equation} as subsheaves of $f_*(K_{X}\otimes L)$. In fact, suppose that ( 8.64 ) holds. Let $H$ be a $f$-ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Then ( 8.64 ) also holds with $L\otimes H^ m$ in place of $L$. It follows from Grauert–Remmert's version of Serre vanishing theorem [ Theorem 2.1(A) , BS76 ] that $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. It remains to prove ( 8.64 ). Observe that both sides of ( 8.64 ) are locally free by [ Corollary 1.5 , Mat16 ] . We claim that it suffices to show that 8.65  egin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin2} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z) \end{equation} for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$. In fact, this implies that the same holds outside a countable subset of $\Delta ^*$. But the set where ( 8.65 ) fails has to be $S^1$-invariant, it has to be empty. By cohomology and base change together with the analytic Bertini theorem 8.5.3 , for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, we have \[   egin{split}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h|_{X_ z})\Bigr ),\  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h'|_{X_ z})\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] But we assumed that for quasi-every $z$, $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$, it follows that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, ( 8.65 ) holds. The proof is complete. $\square$ Comment se fait-il que M. Gauss ait osé vous faire dire que la plupart de vos théorèmes lui étaient connus et qu'il en avait fait la découverte dès 1808. Cet excès d'impudence n'est pas croyable de la part d'un homme qui a assez de mérite personnel pour n'avoir pas besoin de s'approprier les découvertes des autres. 
— Adrien-Marie Legendre Note. Adrien-Marie Legendre (1752–1833) was a French mathematician known for his foundational contributions to number theory, statistics, and mathematical analysis. Apart from his mathematical contributions, he also helped formalize the metric system during the French Revolution. , in a letter to Jacobi in 1827

title: Theorem 8.5.1
text: Theorem 8.5.1 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Let $p\colon X\rightarrow \mathbb {P}^ N$ be a morphism ($N\geq 1$). Define \[  \mathcal{G}\coloneqq \Bigl \{ H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|: H'\coloneqq H\cap X \textup{ is smooth and } \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H'})=\operatorname{Res}_{H'}\bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\bigr )\Bigr \} .  \] Then $\mathcal{G}\subseteq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ is co-pluripolar.

title: Remark 8.5.2
text:
Remark 8.5.2 . Here and in the sequel, we slightly abuse the notation by writing $H\cap X$ for $p^{-1}H$, the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $H$. In other words, $H\cap X\coloneqq H	imes _{\mathbb {P}^ N} X$. By definition, any $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ such that $p^{-1}H=\emptyset $ lies in $\mathcal{G}$. Proof. Take an ample line bundle $L$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ such that $c_1(L,h)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq 0$, where $c_1(L,h)$ is the first Chern form of $(L,h)$, namely the curvature form of $h$. We introduce $\Lambda \coloneqq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ to simplify our notations. Step 1 . We prove that the following set is co-pluripolar: \[   egin{split}  \mathcal{G}_{L}\coloneqq \left\{ H\in \Lambda : H\cap X 	ext{ is smooth and } \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )= ight.\  \left. \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr )ight\} . \end{split}  \] Here $\omega _{H\cap X}$ denotes the dualizing sheaf of $H\cap X$. Let $U\subseteq \Lambda 	imes X$ be the closed subvariety whose $\mathbb {C}$-points correspond to pairs $(H,x)\in \Lambda 	imes X$ with $p(x)\in H$. Let $\pi _1\colon Uightarrow \Lambda $ be the natural projection. We may assume that $\pi _1$ is surjective, as otherwise there is nothing to prove. Observe that $U$ is a local complete intersection scheme by Krull's Hauptidealsatz and a fortiori a Cohen–Macaulay scheme. It follows from miracle flatness [ Theorem 23.1 , Mat89 ] that the natural projection $\pi _2\colon Uightarrow X$ is flat. As the fibers of $\pi _2$ over closed points of $X$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb {P}^{N-1}$, it follows that $\pi _2$ is smooth. Thus, $U$ is smooth as well. Moreover, observe that 8.57  egin{equation} \label{eq:pi2pullvarphiItemp1} \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )=\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) \end{equation} by proposition 1.4.17 . In the following, we will construct pluripolar sets $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Sigma _2 \subseteq \Sigma _3\subseteq \Sigma _4\subseteq \Lambda $ such that the behavior of $\pi _1$ is improved successively on the complement of $\Sigma _ i$. Step 1.1 . The usual Bertini theorem shows that there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\pi _1$ has smooth fibers outside $\Sigma _1$. Enlarging $\Sigma _1$, we may guarantee that $\pi _1$ and $\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ are both flat outside $\Sigma _1$. See [ Théorème 6.9.1 , EGAIV2 ] . Then after further enlarging $\Sigma _1$ we may assume that $p^{-1}(H)$ avoids all associated points of $\mathcal{O}_ X/\mathcal{I}(\varphi )$, for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Let $\pi _{1,H}$ denote the fiber of $\pi _1$ at $H$ and write $i_ H\colon \pi _{1,H}ightarrow U$ for the inclusion morphism. We arrive at \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ))=i_ H^*\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )  \] for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Note. This subtle point was overlooked in the proof of [ XiaBer ] . Step 1.2 . By Grauert's coherence theorem, \[  \mathcal{F}^ i\coloneqq R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L\otimes \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ) ight)  \] is coherent for all $i$. Here $\omega _{U/\Lambda }$ denotes the relative dualizing sheaf of the morphism $Uightarrow \Lambda $. Thus, there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _2\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\Sigma _2\supseteq \Sigma _1$. The $\mathcal{F}^ i$'s are locally free outside $\Sigma _2$. We write $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}^0$. By cohomology and base change [ Theorem III.12.11 , Har ] , for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _2$, the fiber $\mathcal{F}|_ H$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is given by \[  \mathcal{F}|_ H= \mathrm{H}^0\left(\pi _{1,H},\omega _{U/\Lambda }|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \pi _2^*L|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )) ight).  \] Step 1.3 . In order to proceed, we need to make use of the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ on $\mathcal{F}$ defined in [ HPS18 ] . We briefly recall its definition in our setting. By [ Section 22 , HPS18 ] , we can find a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _3\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\Sigma _3\supseteq \Sigma _2$, $\pi _1$ is smooth outside $\Sigma _3$, both $\mathcal{F}$ and $\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)/\mathcal{F}$ are locally free outside $\Sigma _3$, and for each $i$, \[  R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)  \] is locally free outside $\Sigma _3$. Then for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, \[   egin{gathered} \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})ight)\ \subseteq \mathcal{F}|_ H\subseteq \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}ight). \end{gathered}  \] See [ Lemma 22.1 , HPS18 ] . Now we can give the definition of the Hodge metric on $\Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$. Given any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, any $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}|_ H$, the Hodge metric is defined as \[  h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha ):=\int _{X\cap H} |\alpha |^2_{h}\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\in [0,\infty ].  \] Observe that $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )<\infty $ if and only if $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^0(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X}))$. Moreover, $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )>0$ if $\alpha 
eq 0$. It is shown in [ HPS18 ] (cf. [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] ) that $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is indeed a singular Hermitian metric, and it extends to a positive metric on $\mathcal{F}$. Step 1.4 . The determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )
eq \mathcal{F}|_ H.  \] As the map $\pi _2$ is smooth, we have $\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )= \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ by proposition 1.4.17 . Under the identification $\pi _{1,H}\cong H\cap X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}\Bigl (\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr )\cong \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\Bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] Thus, we have the following inclusions: \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  \subseteq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ), \end{split}  \] the right-hand side being $\mathcal{F}|_ H$. Recall that the first inclusion follows from theorem 1.4.19 . Hence, $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|\setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  
eq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Let $\Sigma _4$ be the union of $\Sigma _3$ and the set of all such $H$. Since the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is positive ( [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] and [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS18 ] ), its determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is also positive ( [ Proposition 1.3 , Rau15 ] and [ Proposition 25.1 , HPS18 ] ), it follows that $\Sigma _4$ is pluripolar. As a consequence, $\mathcal{G}_{L}$ is co-pluripolar. Step 2 . Fix an ample invertible sheaf $S$ on $X$. The same result holds with $L\otimes S^{\otimes a}$ in place of $L$. Thus, the set \[  A\coloneqq  igcap _{a=0}^{\infty }\mathcal{G}_{L\otimes S^{\otimes a}}  \] is co-pluripolar. For each $H\in \Lambda $ such that $X\cap H$ is smooth and $\mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})
eq \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}(\mathcal{I}(\varphi ))$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be the following cokernel: \[  0ightarrow \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)ightarrow \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )ightarrow \mathcal{K}ightarrow 0.  \] By Serre vanishing theorem, taking $a$ large enough, we may guarantee that \[  \mathrm{H}^1\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})\Bigr )=0  \] and \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{K}\Bigr )
eq 0.  \] Then \[   egin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)\Bigr )
eq \  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Thus, $H
ot\in A$. We conclude that $\mathcal{G}$ is co-pluripolar. $\square$
8.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pi2pullvarphiItemp1} \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )=\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) \end{equation}

title: Remark 8.5.3
text: Remark 8.5.3 . More generally, the same technique implies the following general result: Let $f\colon X\rightarrow Y$ be a projective morphism between complex manifolds and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Then for quasi-every Note. That is, for all $y$ outside a pluripolar subset of $Y$. $y\in Y$, the fiber $X_ y$ is smooth and \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda h|_{X_ y})=\operatorname{Res}_{X_ y}\left( \mathcal{I}(\lambda h) \right).  \]

title: Corollary 8.5.4
text: Corollary 8.5.4 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, we have $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $. Proof. For quasi-every $H$, theorem 8.5.1 gives \[  \mathcal I(\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_ H\mathcal I(\varphi ).  \] After removing the hyperplanes meeting the associated points of $\mathcal O_ X/\mathcal I(\varphi )$ improperly, the right-hand side is non-zero. Since $\mathcal I(-\infty )=0$, this implies $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $. $\square$

title: Corollary 8.5.5
text:
Corollary 8.5.5 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, satisfies $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. First observe that the set $\{ x\in X:
u (\varphi ,x)>0\} $ is a countable union of proper analytic subsets by Siu's semicontinuity theorem theorem 1.4.4 . It follows that a very general element in $\Lambda $ is not contained in this set. Fix an ample line bundle $L$ so that there is a smooth Hermitian metric $h_ L$ such that $c_1(L,h_ L)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Thanks to theorem 8.5.1 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies the following: $H$ is smooth and connected; $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; $\mathcal{I}(k\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_{H}(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for all $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Put $\alpha _ H\coloneqq c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H$. It follows from theorem 8.4.1 and theorem 7.4.2 that \[  \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{c_1(L,h_ L)}(\varphi )ight)^{n-1} = \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}\left[\varphi |_ Hight]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^{n-1}.  \] Since $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ by proposition 8.1.9 , we also have $\varphi |_ H\preceq _{\mathcal I}\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$. Hence \[  P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\varphi |_ H]_{\mathcal I}\leq P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The trace is $\mathcal I$-good, so the right-hand side agrees with its $P$-envelope. The equality of the masses above and theorem 3.1.9 then imply that the two sides have the same $P$-singularity type, hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] $\square$

title: Lemma 8.5.6
text: Lemma 8.5.6 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $T|_ H$ is well-defined and satisfies \[  \int _ H T|_ H^{n-1}>0.  \] Proof. Write $T=\theta _{\varphi }$ for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Thanks to 2.4.19 , we can find $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. By corollary 8.5.4 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; the restriction $\psi |_ H$ is not identically $-\infty $. Since $\theta _\psi $ is a Kähler current, its restriction to such an $H$ has positive non-pluripolar mass. As $\psi |_ H\leq \varphi |_ H$, theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ H(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H)^{n-1} \geq \int _ H(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H)^{n-1}>0.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$

title: Corollary 8.5.7
text: Corollary 8.5.7 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{\{ T\} |_ H}(T)$ is well-defined and has positive volume. Proof. Write $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and set $\psi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Then $\psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^{n}=\operatorname{vol}T>0.  \] By 8.5.6 , for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, the hypersurface $H$ is connected and smooth, $\psi |_ H$ is well-defined, and \[  \int _ H \left(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H\right)^{n-1}>0.  \] For such $H$, corollary 8.5.5 gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi |_ H$. Since $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, proposition 8.2.1 also gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )$. The assertion now follows from example 8.1.12 . $\square$

title: Proposition 8.5.8
text: Proposition 8.5.8 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \psi |_ H$. Proof. Thanks to 6.1.8 , we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. It suffices to show that $\varphi |_ H\sim _ P \psi |_ H$ for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $. Take a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ so that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. It suffices to compare $\varphi $ and $\psi $ with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, so without loss of generality, we may assume that $\psi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Up to adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may then assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. It follows from 2.4.15 that we can find a sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  j^{-1}\eta _ j+\left(1-j^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi  \] for all $j\geq 2$. By corollary 8.5.4 , 8.5.6 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 2$ and $\psi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 3.1.24 into account, we arrive at \[  j^{-1} P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\eta _ j|_ H\bigr ]+\left(1-j^{-1}\right)P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\psi |_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ]  \] for all $j\geq 2$. The normalized envelopes $P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are uniformly bounded in $L^1$, hence \[  j^{-1}P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\xrightarrow {L^1} 0.  \] We conclude that \[  P_{\theta |_ H}[\psi |_ H]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}[\varphi |_ H]  \] and hence $\psi |_ H\preceq _ P \varphi |_ H$. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.5.9
text: Lemma 8.5.9 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class and $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Furthermore, assume that $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j$ for each $j>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $\varphi _ j|_ H\not\equiv -\infty $ for all $j\geq 1$, $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. By corollary 6.2.19 , we may assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Using 2.4.15 , we can find a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $(0,1)$ with limit $0$ and $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j$ and \[  \epsilon _ j\eta _ j+(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] By corollary 8.5.4 , 8.5.6 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: $H$ is smooth and connected; $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 1$ and $\varphi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 3.1.24 into account, we arrive at \[  \epsilon _ j P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\eta _ j|_ H\bigr ]+\left(1-\epsilon _ j\right)P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi _ j|_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ].  \] Since the normalized envelopes $P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are relatively compact in $L^1$, we have $\epsilon _ jP_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\to 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $j\to \infty $, we get \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi _ j|_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ].  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, so we get an equality here. By theorem 2.4.8 and proposition 3.1.26 , we conclude that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ H \Bigl (\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}=\int _ H \Bigl (\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}.  \] Therefore, using corollary 6.2.11 , we conclude that $\varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H$. $\square$

title: Corollary 8.5.10
text: Corollary 8.5.10 . Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be an $\mathcal{I}$-good potential. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ satisfies: $H$ is connected and smooth; $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good; $\nu (\varphi ,H)=0$; $\operatorname{Tr}_ H \varphi \sim _ P \varphi |_ H$. Furthermore, if $\theta $ is a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then we can further guarantee, on the same co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Proof. Choose a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta _0$ representing a big class such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _0)$ and $\theta _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _0)_{>0}$. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal I$-good, corollary 7.1.10 , theorem 7.1.1 , proposition 6.2.4 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi .  \] Applying 8.5.9 , we find a co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $ such that $H$ is connected and smooth, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are not identically $-\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] For such an $H$, the potentials $\varphi _ j|_ H$ have analytic singularities, hence are $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.6 . It follows from corollary 7.1.5 that $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal I$-good. On the other hand, corollary 8.5.5 gives, after intersecting with another co-pluripolar set of parameters $H$, that $\nu (\varphi ,H)=0$ and \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] The trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 8.1.5 . Since both $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are $\mathcal I$-good, their $\mathcal I$-equivalence identifies their $\mathcal I$-envelopes, which agree with their $P$-envelopes. Hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\varphi |_ H.  \] Finally corollary 8.5.7 shows, after intersecting with one more co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative in $\mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.5.11 (Reverse Bertini theorem)
text: Lemma 8.5.11 (Reverse Bertini theorem) . Let $X$ be a complex manifold, $f\colon X\rightarrow \Delta ^*$ be a projective surjective morphism to the punctured unit disk $\Delta ^*$. Let $(L,h)$, $(L,h')$ be Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles on $X$ with the same underlying line bundle. Assume that there is a biholomorphic $S^1$-action on $(X,L)$ making $f$ equivariant and such that $h$ and $h'$ are invariant under this action. Assume that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, $X_ z$ is smooth and $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$. Then $h\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'$. Proof. We need to show that $\mathcal{I}(kh)=\mathcal{I}(kh')$ for every positive integer $k$. It suffices to prove the case $k=1$, since our assumptions are invariant after replacing $h$ and $h'$ by $h^ k$ and $h'^ k$. We will therefore prove $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. First observe that it suffices to prove that 8.64 \begin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr )=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \end{equation} as subsheaves of $f_*(K_{X}\otimes L)$. In fact, suppose that ( 8.64 ) holds. Let $H$ be a $f$-ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Then ( 8.64 ) also holds with $L\otimes H^ m$ in place of $L$. It follows from Grauert–Remmert's version of Serre vanishing theorem [ Theorem 2.1(A) , BS76 ] that $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. It remains to prove ( 8.64 ). Observe that both sides of ( 8.64 ) are locally free by [ Corollary 1.5 , Mat16 ] . We claim that it suffices to show that 8.65 \begin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin2} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z) \end{equation} for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$. In fact, this implies that the same holds outside a countable subset of $\Delta ^*$. But the set where ( 8.65 ) fails has to be $S^1$-invariant, it has to be empty. By cohomology and base change together with the analytic Bertini theorem 8.5.3 , for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, we have \[  \begin{split}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h|_{X_ z})\Bigr ),\\  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h'|_{X_ z})\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] But we assumed that for quasi-every $z$, $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$, it follows that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, ( 8.65 ) holds. The proof is complete. $\square$
8.64 \begin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr )=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \end{equation}

8.65 \begin{equation} \label{eq:fstarcoin2} f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z) \end{equation}

title: 9 Test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: 9 Test curves A geodesic ray $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in [0,\infty )}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ records the asymptotic behavior of singularities along a path of potentials. In this chapter we encode the same information in the dual variable $\tau $. Instead of recording the potential at time $t$, the Legendre transform records, for each slope $\tau $, the model potential determined by the part of the ray growing at least linearly with slope $\tau $. This produces a concave decreasing family $\tau \mapsto \Gamma _\tau $ of model potentials; more precisely, a test curve $\Gamma $ is a concave decreasing family $(\Gamma _\tau )_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}$ of model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. The central result is a correspondence initiated by Ross and Witt Nyström Note. Witt and Nyström are both family names of a single person. Some Swedes have double family names. It should not be spelled as Witt-Nyström as some people do in the literature. . It is the pluripotential-theoretic analogue of Legendre duality: a test curve gives a geodesic ray by taking a Legendre transform, and a suitable geodesic ray gives back a test curve by the inverse transform. Thus test curves provide an intrinsic language for the singularity data carried by geodesic rays. We first develop test curves as self-contained objects. In section 9.1 we introduce their basic properties, including independence of the auxiliary form, behavior under bimeromorphic morphisms, closedness in the parameter $\tau $, log-concavity of the mass function and the $P$-equivalence relation on test curves. The Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence is proved in section 9.2 , where the Legendre transform is shown to give a bijection between test curves and geodesic rays. The later sections adapt this picture to the singularity types needed elsewhere in the book. In section 9.3 we develop the $\mathcal I$-model version of the theory, including the $\mathcal I$-envelope of a test curve, the transition from $P$-model to $\mathcal I$-model test curves, and the corresponding notion of maximal geodesic ray. Finally, section 9.4 studies sums, translations, maxima, suprema, infima and rescalings of test curves. These operations are needed in the non-Archimedean theory of chapter 13 , where test curves provide the analytic input for the construction of non-Archimedean potentials. Throughout the chapter we freely use the convex-analytic results of chapter A . Those results are stated for convex functions; when they are applied to concave functions here, they are applied to the negatives.

title: 9.1 The notion of test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
9.1 The notion of test curves Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Recall that the notion of model potentials is defined in definition 3.1.10 . Definition 9.1.1 . A test curve $\Gamma $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ consists of a real number $\Gamma _{\max }$ together with a map $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ denoted by $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }$ satisfying the following conditions: The map $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }$ is concave and decreasing; $P_{	heta }[\Gamma _{	au }]=\Gamma _{	au }$; the potential 9.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:Gammaminf} \Gamma _{-\infty }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma _{	au } \end{equation} satisfies \[  \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }ight)^ n>0.  \] Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. The set of test curves $\Gamma $ with $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\phi $ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. The union of all $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$'s for various model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. By 2 , $\sup _{X}\Gamma _{	au }=0$ for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. So $\Gamma _{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ by proposition 1.2.2 . Thanks to corollary 2.4.9 and 3 , there is $C<\Gamma _{\max }$ so that whenever $	au <C$, we have $\Gamma _{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then it follows that $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is a model potential by proposition 3.1.28 . Remark 9.1.2 . Sometimes it is convenient to extend $\Gamma _{	au }$ to $	au \geq \Gamma _{\max }$ as well. This can be done as follows: for $	au >\Gamma _{\max }$, we set $\Gamma _{	au }\equiv -\infty $. For $	au =\Gamma _{\max }$, we set \[  \Gamma _{	au }\coloneqq \inf _{	au '<\Gamma _{\max }}\Gamma _{	au '}\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] Note that $\Gamma _{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ by corollary 1.5.6 . In general, for any $x\in X$, the map $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ falls into one of the following three categories: $\Gamma _{	au }(x)\equiv -\infty $; $\Gamma _{	au }(x)>-\infty $ for all $	au \leq \Gamma _{\max }$; there is $	au (x)\in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max }]$ so that $\Gamma _{	au }(x)>-\infty $ for all $	au \in (-\infty ,	au (x))$, and $\Gamma _{	au }(x)=-\infty $ for all $	au \geq 	au (x)$. The last two possibilities are illustrated in 9.1 . 9.1 The last two pointwise possibilities for $	au \mapsto \Gamma _	au (x)$. Note that 2 is the generic situation. It occurs whenever $x
otin \{ \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}=-\infty \} $. In particular, when this situation occurs, $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ is finite concave, and hence continuous. As a consequence, for any $	au \in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$, we have 9.2  egin{equation} \label{eq:Gammataucont} \Gamma _{	au }=\inf _{	au '<	au }\Gamma _{	au '},\quad \Gamma _{	au }=\operatorname *{sup}_{	au '\in (	au ,\Gamma _{\max })}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma _{	au '} \end{equation} almost everywhere and hence everywhere due to proposition 1.2.6 . Recall that according to our general principle, we speak of model potentials only when a potential has positive mass. Lemma 9.1.3 . Assume that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have 9.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:dalethtauposmass} \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{	au }ight)^ n>0. \end{equation} In particular, $\Gamma _{	au }$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. The notations in the proof below are summarized in 9.2 . 9.2 The test curve $\Gamma $. Proof. Fix $	au \in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. By assumption, $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ has positive mass. By corollary 2.4.9 , we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{	au 	o -\infty }\int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n.  \] In particular, for a sufficiently small $	au _0<	au $, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n>0.  \] Now take $	au '\in (	au , \Gamma _{\max })$ and $t\in (0,1)$ so that \[  	au =(1-t)	au '+t	au _0.  \] From the concavity of $\Gamma $, we find that \[  \Gamma _{	au }\geq (1-t)\Gamma _{	au '}+t\Gamma _{	au _0}.  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n\geq \int _ X 	heta _{(1-t)\Gamma _{	au '}+t\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n\geq t^ n \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n>0  \] and ( 9.3 ) follows. $\square$ Proposition 9.1.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then the map \[  [-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathbb {R},\quad 	au \mapsto \log \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n  \] is continuous and concave on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. Proof. The concavity of this function follows from theorem 2.4.4 and theorem 2.4.8 . The continuity at $-\infty $ is a consequence of corollary 2.4.9 . The continuity on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$ follows from the fact that finite concave functions on open intervals are continuous. $\square$ Definition 9.1.5 . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is said to be bounded if for $	au $ small enough, $\Gamma _{	au }=\phi $. The subset of bounded test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;\phi )$. In this case, we write 9.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:Gammamin} \Gamma _{\min }\coloneqq \sup \{ 	au \in \mathbb {R}:\Gamma _{	au }=\phi \} . \end{equation} A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is said to have finite energy if 9.5  egin{equation} \label{eq:tcfiniteenergy} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max } \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n+\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\int _ X	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ night)\, \mathrm{d}	au >-\infty . \end{equation} When $\phi =V_{	heta }$, we write $\mathbf{E}$ instead of $\mathbf{E}^{\phi }$. The subset of test curves with finite energy in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Example 9.1.6 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, there is a canonically associated test curve $\Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;V_{	heta })$: Set $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$ and \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }_{	au }=  egin{cases}  V_{	heta },& 	extup{if }	au \leq -1;\  P_{	heta }\left[ (1+	au )\varphi -	au V_{	heta } ight],&  	extup{if }-1<	au <0. \end{cases}  \] Note that $\Gamma ^{\varphi }$ is indeed a test curve, as follows from proposition 3.1.24 . Indeed, the concavity and monotonicity in $	au $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 , and $\Gamma ^\varphi _{-\infty }=V_	heta $ has positive mass. We first observe that the notion of test curves does not really depend on the choice of $	heta $ within its cohomology class. Proposition 9.1.7 . Let $	heta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $	heta $. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. Let $\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')_{>0}$ be the unique model potential satisfying $\phi \sim \phi '$. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ').  \] This bijection induces the following bijections: \[  \mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ';\phi '),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ';\phi ').  \] These bijections satisfy the obvious cocycle conditions. Proof. Choose $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$ such that $	heta '=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. Given any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$, we observe that $\Gamma '\colon (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')$ defined as \[  	au \mapsto P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _{	au }-g]  \] lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ')$. In fact, the concavity and monotonicity of $\Gamma '$ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . Moreover, applying proposition 3.1.28 to the increasing net obtained as $	au 	o -\infty $ gives \[  \Gamma '_{-\infty }=P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _{-\infty }-g]=P_{	heta '}[\phi -g]=\phi '.  \] Thus $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ')$. Moreover, the choice of $g$ is irrelevant since for any other choice of $g$, say $g'$, we have \[  \Gamma _{	au }-g\sim \Gamma _{	au }-g'  \] for all $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. The inverse construction is obtained by replacing $g$ with $-g$. The boundedness condition is clearly preserved. Finally, by proposition 3.1.6 , for every $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \int _ X(	heta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_	au )^ n=\int _ X(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n,  \] and the same holds for $\phi $ and $\phi '$. Hence the finite energy condition is preserved. The cocycle condition is immediate from the uniqueness of the model representative in a fixed singularity type. $\square$ Proposition 9.1.8 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xlongrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(Y,\pi ^*	heta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. The bijectivity on the underlying potentials follows from proposition 1.5.8 . The compatibility with model potentials follows from proposition 3.1.23 . These two facts also preserve concavity, monotonicity and the value of $\Gamma _{-\infty }$, hence give the asserted bijection of test curves. $\square$ Next we verify the closedness of a test curve as a family of concave functions, so that no pathology arises in the Legendre transforms considered below. The notion of closedness is recalled in definition A.1.13 . Proposition 9.1.9 . Let $\Gamma $ be a test curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. For each $x\in X$, the map $\mathbb {R} 
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ is a closed concave function. Moreover, the map is proper as long as $\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}(x)
eq -\infty $. Proof. We prove closedness. Fix $x\in X$. Assume that $\Gamma _{	au }(x)
eq -\infty $ for some $	au \in \mathbb {R}$. We only need to argue the upper semicontinuity of $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$. The upper semicontinuity is clear at $	au \geq \Gamma _{\max }$, so we are reduced to prove the following: 9.8  egin{equation} \label{eq:Gammatautemp1} \Gamma _{	au }=\inf _{	au '<	au }\Gamma _{	au '} \end{equation} for any $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. Take $	au ''\in (	au ,\Gamma _{\max })$. Outside the polar locus of $\Gamma _{	au ''}$, we know that ( 9.8 ) holds by continuity of real-valued concave functions. So ( 9.8 ) holds everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . The final assertion follows from properness of a finite closed concave function on its effective domain. $\square$ Definition 9.1.10 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a smooth closed real positive $(1,1)$-form. Then we define $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta +\omega )_{>0}$ as follows: Define \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max };  \] for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, define \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{	au }=P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma _{	au }].  \] It follows from proposition 3.1.24 that the family $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]$ is concave and decreasing. Moreover, since $\omega $ is positive, \[  \int _ X(	heta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n \geq \int _ X(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n>0  \] for every $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, and hence $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_	au $ is a model potential by corollary 3.1.12 . Thus $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta +\omega )_{>0}$. Proposition 9.1.11 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{-\infty }=P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma _{-\infty }].  \] Proof. This follows from proposition 3.1.28 . $\square$

title: Example 9.1.6

text: Example 9.1.6 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, there is a canonically associated test curve $\Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;V_{\theta })$: Set $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$ and \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  V_{\theta },& \textup{if }\tau \leq -1;\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta } \right],&  \textup{if }-1<\tau <0. \end{cases}  \] Note that $\Gamma ^{\varphi }$ is indeed a test curve, as follows from proposition 3.1.24 . Indeed, the concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 , and $\Gamma ^\varphi _{-\infty }=V_\theta $ has positive mass.

title: Proposition 9.1.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.1.7 . Let $\theta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $\theta $. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. Let $\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ be the unique model potential satisfying $\phi \sim \phi '$. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ').  \] This bijection induces the following bijections: \[  \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ';\phi '),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ';\phi ').  \] These bijections satisfy the obvious cocycle conditions. Proof. Choose $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$ such that $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. Given any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we observe that $\Gamma '\colon (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$ defined as \[  \tau \mapsto P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _{\tau }-g]  \] lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ')$. In fact, the concavity and monotonicity of $\Gamma '$ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . Moreover, applying proposition 3.1.28 to the increasing net obtained as $\tau \to -\infty $ gives \[  \Gamma '_{-\infty }=P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _{-\infty }-g]=P_{\theta '}[\phi -g]=\phi '.  \] Thus $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ')$. Moreover, the choice of $g$ is irrelevant since for any other choice of $g$, say $g'$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }-g\sim \Gamma _{\tau }-g'  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. The inverse construction is obtained by replacing $g$ with $-g$. The boundedness condition is clearly preserved. Finally, by proposition 3.1.6 , for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \int _ X(\theta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_\tau )^ n=\int _ X(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _\tau )^ n,  \] and the same holds for $\phi $ and $\phi '$. Hence the finite energy condition is preserved. The cocycle condition is immediate from the uniqueness of the model representative in a fixed singularity type. $\square$

title: 9.2 Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
9.2 Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class.
