So from the lower bound in ( 9.29 ), we have \[   egin{aligned}  E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}ight)-E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}ight)\geq &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}ight)\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}}\  = &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}ight)\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}\  \geq &  \int _{\left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0ight\} }t2^{-N}\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}, \end{aligned}  \] where on the second line, we applied ( 9.32 ) and proposition 2.2.2 , on the third line, we applied the fact that $	heta _{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}^ n$ is supported on the set (cf. theorem 3.1.7 ) \[  \left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0ight\} \subseteq U_ t\cap \left\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0ight\} .  \] When $(M+1)/2^ N=0$, we use proposition 3.1.25 to see that $P_	heta [\Gamma _0]=\Gamma _0$, since $\Gamma _0$ is the decreasing limit of the model potentials $\Gamma _	au $ as $	au 
earrow 0$. Thus theorem 3.1.7 applies to this endpoint as well. We have deduced the first inequality in ( 9.27 ). Next, we apply the upper bound part in ( 9.29 ) and compute similarly \[   egin{aligned}  E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1})-E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M})\leq &  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}ight)\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}}\  =&  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}ight)\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}\  \leq &  \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t}\left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}+t2^{-N}ight)\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}} \  \leq & \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t} t2^{-N}\, 	heta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}. \end{aligned}  \] We conclude the latter half of ( 9.27 ). Step 3.3 . We assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Now $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ only. For each $\epsilon >0$, we introduce $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;\phi )$ as follows: Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{	au }=  egin{cases}  \phi ,& 	extup{if }	au \leq -\epsilon ^{-1};\  P_{	heta }\left[ (1+\epsilon 	au )\Gamma _{	au }-\epsilon 	au \phi ight],& 	extup{if }	au \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0ight). \end{cases}  \] The concavity and monotonicity in $	au $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . The value at $-\infty $ is $\phi $. Moreover, $\Gamma ^\epsilon _	au =\phi $ for $	au \leq -\epsilon ^{-1}$, so $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{TC}^\infty (X,	heta ;\phi )$. It follows from corollary 6.2.20 and corollary 6.2.11 that for each $	au <0$, the potentials $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{	au }$ decrease to $\Gamma _{	au }$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Applying proposition 3.1.26 , we have \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{	au }ight)^ n=\int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{	au }ight)^ n  \] for all $	au <0$. Hence, by the monotone convergence theorem and Step 3.2, we find 9.42  egin{equation} \label{eq:EphiGammatemp1} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon })=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *})=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1), \end{equation} where the last equality follows from ( 9.28 ). Furthermore, according to proposition A.2.10 , we have \[  \Gamma ^*_ t=\inf _{\epsilon >0} \Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_ t  \] for all $t>0$. Note that we do not have to take the closure of the right-hand side since it is automatically upper semicontinuous in $t$. Now suppose that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then by ( 9.42 ), as $\epsilon 	o 0+$, $(\Gamma _ t^{\epsilon *})_{\epsilon }$ is a decreasing Cauchy net in $\mathcal{E}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$ and hence by theorem 4.3.15 for each $t>0$, \[  E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_ tight)=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon ,*}_ tight)=t\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )>-\infty ,  \] where we have applied ( 9.28 ) and ( 9.42 ). Hence, $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Moreover, ( 9.23 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then ( 9.42 ) implies that \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1ight) \geq E_{	heta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_1ight)>-\infty .  \] Hence, $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. $\square$ Remark 9.2.10 . One could also consider geodesic rays emanating from another potential $\Phi \in \mathcal{E}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. In this case, one can show that these geodesic rays are in bijection with $\Phi $-twisted test curves: In definition 9.1.1 , we replace 2 by the following condition: \[  P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight](\Phi )=\Gamma _{	au }.  \] Furthermore, we require that $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\Phi $. The above results equally work in the twisted setting. The proofs are almost identical to the untwisted case. Corollary 9.2.11 . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then $\sup _ X \ell _ t=\ell ^*_{\max }t$ for any $t\geq 0$. In particular, $\ell _ t-\ell ^*_{\max }t$ is a decreasing function of $t\geq 0$. Proof. This follows from 9.2.6 and theorem 9.2.9 . $\square$ Example 9.2.12 . Let us see what the test curve in example 9.1.6 corresponds to under the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. We claim that 9.43  egin{equation} \label{eq:RWNsingtype} \ell ^{\varphi }=\Gamma ^{\varphi *}, \end{equation} where $\ell ^{\varphi }$ is as in example 4.3.26 . We may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ since both sides are invariant after adding a constant to $\varphi $. We first prove the easy direction $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$, which is equivalent to $\ell ^{\varphi *}\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi }$. Since $\ell ^{\varphi *}$ is a test curve, the latter is equivalent to \[  \ell ^{\varphi *}_{	au }\geq (1+	au )\varphi -	au V_{	heta }  \] for all $	au \in (-1,0)$. By Legendre duality, this is equivalent to 9.44  egin{equation} \label{eq:lvarphigeq_temp1} \ell ^{\varphi }_ t\geq \sup _{	au \in (-1,0)} \Bigl ((1+	au )\varphi -	au V_{	heta }+t	au \Bigr )=\varphi \lor (V_{	heta }-t) \end{equation} for all $t>0$. Using the notations of example 4.3.26 , we find easily that \[  \ell ^{\varphi ,C}_ t\geq \varphi \lor (V_{	heta }-t)  \] for any $C>0$ and $t\in [0,C]$, since it holds at $t=0$ and $t=C$. Letting $C	o \infty $, we find ( 9.44 ). Therefore, $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$ follows. In order to prove the equality in ( 9.43 ), it suffices to show that the two sides have the same energy, as a consequence of ( 4.94 ). So we compute \[   egin{aligned}  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi *}ight)=&  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi }ight)\  =&  \int _{-1}^0 \left(\int _ X 	heta _{(1+	au )\varphi -	au V_{	heta }}^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ night)\, \mathrm{d}	au \  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n}  inom {n}{j} \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j} \int _0^1 	au ^ j (1-	au )^{n-j}\, \mathrm{d}	au -\int _ X 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n}  inom {n}{j} rac{j!(n-j)!}{(n+1)!} \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X 	heta _{V_{	heta }}^ n\  =&  \mathbf{E}(\ell ^{\varphi }), \end{aligned}  \] where in the second line we used proposition 3.1.6 , in the fourth line we used the value of the $ eta $-function Note. Also known as Euler integral of the first kind. , and the last line is just ( 4.103 ). The multiplier ideal sheaves of a test curve can be characterized using the corresponding geodesic ray in a very simple manner. Proposition 9.2.13 (He–Testorf–Wang) . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Given any $	au <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $x\in X$, we have 9.50  egin{equation} \label{eq:mis_RWN} \mathcal{I}\left(\ell ^*_{	au }ight)_{x}=\left\{  f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}: |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t	au )\, \mathrm{d}t 	extup{ is integrable near }x ight\} . \end{equation} Proof. Fix $x\in X$, $	au <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 9.50 ). Given any $y\in X$, it follows from ( 9.15 ) that there is $t_0>0$ with \[  \ell ^*_{	au }(y)+1\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0	au .  \] Observe that $t\mapsto \ell _ t-t\ell ^*_{\max }$ is decreasing in $t$ by corollary 9.2.11 , it follows that for $t\in [t_0,t_0+1]$, we have \[  \ell ^*_{	au }(y)+1-t_0(\ell ^*_{\max }-	au )\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0\ell ^*_{\max }\geq \ell _{t}(y)-t\ell ^*_{\max }.  \] Since $	au < \ell ^*_{\max }$ and $t_0\geq t-1$, we deduce that 9.51  egin{equation} \label{eq:mis_RWN_temp1} \ell ^*_{	au }(y)+1+\ell ^*_{\max }-	au \geq \ell _{t}(y)-t	au ,\quad t\in [t_0,t_0+1]. \end{equation} Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t	au )\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Applying ( 9.51 ), we deduce that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{	au }ight)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Therefore, $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{	au })_ x$. Step 2 . Assume that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{	au })_ x$. It follows from the strong openness theorem theorem 1.4.16 (cf. ( 9.2 )) that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{	au +\epsilon })_ x$ for some small enough $\epsilon >0$ with $	au +\epsilon <\ell ^*_{\max }$. Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2 \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{	au +\epsilon }ight)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] We compute \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell _ t+t	au ight)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\leq &  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{	au +\epsilon }-t\epsilon ight)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\  =&  rac{1}{\epsilon }\int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{	au +\epsilon }ight)\, \omega ^ n\  <& \infty . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 9.50 ). $\square$ The masses of potentials on a test curve can also be expressed in terms of the corresponding geodesic ray. Proposition 9.2.14 (Hisamoto) . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Given any $	au <\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have 9.55  egin{equation} \label{eq:mass_tc} \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\ell ^*_{	au }ight)^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au \} } 	heta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Here $\dot{\ell }_0$ denotes the right-derivative of $\ell _ t$ with respect to $t$ at $t=0$. It is well-defined quasi-everywhere by corollary 4.1.7 , and hence the right-hand side of ( 9.55 ) makes sense, even though $\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au \} $ is not well-defined. Proof. Fix $	au <\ell ^*_{\max }$. We first observe that it suffices to show that 9.56  egin{equation} \label{eq:mass_tc_temp1} \int _{\left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au ight\} } 	heta _{\phi }^ n=\int _{\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=\phi ight\} } 	heta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Assuming ( 9.56 ) for the moment. By theorem 9.2.9 , $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. In particular, $\ell ^*_	au $ is a model potential and \[  \ell ^*_	au \leq \ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi .  \] Since $\phi $ is model as well, proposition 3.1.21 gives \[  	heta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{	au }}=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=0ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n,\quad 	heta ^ n_{\phi }=\mathds {1}_{\{ \phi =0\} }\, 	heta ^ n.  \] Since $\ell ^*_{	au }\leq \phi \leq 0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=\phi ight\} }\, 	heta _{\phi }^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=\phi =0ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=0ight\} }\, 	heta ^ n =	heta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{	au }}.  \] Therefore, ( 9.55 ) follows from ( 9.56 ). In order to prove ( 9.56 ), it suffices to show that 9.57  egin{equation} \label{eq:dotell_temp1} \left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au ight\} =\left\{ \ell ^*_{	au }=\phi ight\} \quad 	extup{outside a pluripolar set}. \end{equation} Take $x\in X$ so that $(\ell _ t(x))_{t\geq 0}$ is finite and right-differentiable at $t=0$. Note that this condition holds quasi-everywhere. Suppose that $\ell ^*_{	au }(x)=\phi (x)$. Then \[  \dot{\ell }_0(x)=\inf _{t>0}  rac{\ell _ t(x)-\phi (x)}{t}\geq \inf _{t>0}  rac{\ell ^*_{	au }(x)+t	au -\phi (x)}{t}=	au .  \] Therefore, the $\supseteq $ direction in ( 9.57 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\dot{\ell }_0(x)\geq 	au $, then \[  \ell ^*_{	au }(x)=\inf _{t>0} \left(\ell _ t(x)-t	au ight)\geq \inf _{t>0} \left(\phi (x)+t\dot{\ell }_0(x)-t	au ight)\geq \phi (x).  \] Together with $\ell ^*_	au \leq \phi $, this gives $\ell ^*_	au (x)=\phi (x)$. Therefore, the $\subseteq $ direction in ( 9.57 ) follows as well. $\square$ Corollary 9.2.15 . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then $\dot{\ell }_0\in L^1(X,	heta _{\phi }^ n)$ and 9.58  egin{equation} \label{eq:ray_energy_slope} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, 	heta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, for every $t\geq 0$, \[  E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\ell _ t)=t\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, 	heta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Proof. Set $\Gamma =\ell ^*$. By theorem 9.2.9 , we have $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$ and \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ).  \] By proposition 9.2.14 , for every $	au <\ell ^*_{\max }$, \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au \} } 	heta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Hence ( 9.5 ) gives \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell ) =\ell ^*_{\max }\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{-\infty }^{\ell ^*_{\max }} \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0<	au \} }	heta _{\phi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}	au .  \] For $	au >\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have $\ell ^*_{	au }\equiv -\infty $ by 9.2.8 . Then ( 9.56 ) shows that \[  \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq 	au \} }	heta _{\phi }^ n=0.  \] The layer-cake formula therefore gives ( 9.58 ). The final assertion follows from proposition 4.3.16 , since $E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\ell _0)=E_{	heta }^{\phi }(\phi )=0$. $\square$

We define its Legendre transform as the map $\Gamma ^*\colon (0,\infty )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ given by 9.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:testcurveLegtran} \Gamma ^*_ t=\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left(t\tau + \Gamma _{\tau }\right)\footnotemark . \end{equation} Note. There is no usc regularization in the preceding formula. This is not a typo.

title: Remark 9.2.2

text: Remark 9.2.2 . Here we do not discuss the case $t<0$ because its behavior is straightforward: take $x\in X$; if $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, then $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=-\infty $; otherwise, $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=\infty $.

title: Proposition 9.2.3
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.2.3 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 9.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Leginvtc} \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t>0} \left(\Gamma ^*_ t-t\tau \right) \end{equation} for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Proof. Fix $x\in X$. We want to establish ( 9.11 ) at $x$. We distinguish two cases. First suppose that $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ and hence all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. In this case, we have $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=-\infty $ for all $t>0$. Therefore, ( 9.11 ) follows trivially. Otherwise, by 9.2.2 , we know that $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)=\infty $ for all $t<0$. The relative interior of the domain of $t\mapsto \Gamma ^*_ t(x)$ is contained in $(0,\infty )$. Therefore, ( 9.11 ) follows from theorem A.2.2 , proposition 9.1.9 . $\square$

title: Lemma 9.2.4
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.2.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all $t>0$. In fact, $\Gamma ^*$ is upper semicontinuous as a function of $X\times (0,\infty )$. Proof. We first observe that for each $x\in X$, we have \[  \Gamma _ t^*(x)\leq t\Gamma _{\max }<\infty .  \] Let $R=\{ a+\mathrm{i}b\in \mathbb {C}:a>0,b\in \mathbb {R}\} $. We consider \[  F\colon X\times R\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ),\quad (x,a+\mathrm{i}b)\mapsto \Gamma _ a^*(x).  \] Let $\pi \colon X\times R\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Observe that the upper semicontinuous regularization $G$ of $F$ is $\pi ^*\theta $-psh by proposition 1.2.2 . It suffices to show that $F=G$. We let \[  E\coloneqq \left\{  (x,z)\in X\times R: F(x,z)<G(x,z) \right\} .  \] We want to argue that $E=\varnothing $. Since $F$ is invariant under translations in the imaginary direction of $R$, the same is true for its upper semicontinuous regularization $G$. So $E$ can be written as $B\times \mathrm{i}\mathbb {R}$ for some set $B\subseteq X\times (0,\infty )$. Since $E$ is a pluripolar set by proposition 1.2.5 , it has zero Lebesgue measure. Hence, $B$ has zero Lebesgue measure. For each $x\in X$, write \[  B_ x=\left\{ t\in (0,\infty ): (x,t)\in B \right\} .  \] By Fubini's theorem, $B_ x$ has vanishing $1$-dimensional Lebesgue measure for all $x\in X\setminus Z$, where $Z\subseteq X$ is a subset of measure $0$. We may assume that $Z\supseteq \{ \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}=-\infty \} $ so that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)\neq -\infty $ for all $t>0$. For any $x\in X\setminus Z$, both $t\mapsto F(x,t)$ and $G(x,t)$ are convex functions with values in $\mathbb {R}$ on $(0,\infty )$. They agree almost everywhere, hence everywhere by their continuity. It follows that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have $B_ x=\varnothing $. By proposition 9.2.3 , for any $x\in X$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} (F(x,t)-t\tau ),\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] On the other hand, let 9.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:chiGlegtemp1} \chi _{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} (G(x,t)-t\tau ),\quad \tau < \Gamma _{\max },\quad x\in X. \end{equation} By Kiselman's principle proposition 1.2.11 , $\chi _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. But on $X\setminus Z$, we already know that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\chi _{\tau }$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. By proposition 1.2.6 , \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\chi _{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] Now we conclude that $F(x,t)=G(x,t)$ by corollary A.2.4 . $\square$

title: Corollary 9.2.5
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 9.2.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ for all $t>0$. Proof. Fix $t>0$. We already know that $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by 9.2.4 . It suffices to show that \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\sim _ P \phi .  \] From ( 9.9 ) and proposition 6.1.20 , we know that \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma _{\tau }=\phi .  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.2.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.2.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then \[  \sup _ X \Gamma _ t^*=t\Gamma _{\max }  \] for all $t>0$. In particular, $t\mapsto \Gamma ^*_ t-t\Gamma _{\max }$ is a decreasing function in $t>0$. Proof. Since $\Gamma _{\tau }\leq 0$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \sup _ X \Gamma _ t^*\leq t\Gamma _{\max }  \] for all $t>0$. Conversely, for each $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \sup _ X\Gamma _ t^*\geq \sup _ X(t\tau +\Gamma _{\tau })=t\tau .  \] Letting $\tau \to \Gamma _{\max }$ gives the reverse inequality. The final assertion follows directly from the formula \[  \Gamma _ t^*-t\Gamma _{\max }=\sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}\Bigl (\Gamma _\tau -t(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau )\Bigr ).  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.2.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.2.7 . Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Proof. It follows from 9.2.4 , ( 9.9 ) and proposition 1.2.2 that the restriction of $\Gamma ^*$ to each compact subinterval of $(0,\infty )$ is a subgeodesic. By corollary 9.2.5 , for any $t>0$, $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. First observe that as $t\to 0+$, we have 9.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammatophiL1temp} \Gamma _ t^*\xrightarrow {L^1}\phi . \end{equation} By 9.2.6 and proposition 1.5.4 , it suffices to show each $L^1$-cluster point $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ of $\Gamma _ t^*$ as $t\to 0$ is equal to $\phi $. To see this, first observe that by ( 9.9 ), for any fixed $t>0$, \[  \Gamma _ t^*\leq t\Gamma _{\max }+\phi .  \] Therefore, $\psi \leq \phi $. On the other hand, for any fixed $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, by ( 9.9 ), we have \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\geq \Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau  \] for any $t>0$. So $\psi \geq \Gamma _{\tau }$ almost everywhere and hence everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . It follows that $\psi \geq \phi $. Therefore, $\psi =\phi $. Assume that $\Gamma ^*$ is not a geodesic ray. Then we can find $0\leq a<b$ such that $(\Gamma ^*_ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$ differs from the geodesic $(\eta _ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$ from $\Gamma ^*_ a$ to $\Gamma ^*_ b$. The existence of $(\eta _ t)_ t$ is guaranteed by proposition 4.2.4 . We consider the subgeodesic $(\ell _ t)_{t>0}$ given by $\ell _ t=\eta _ t$ for $t\in (a,b)$ and $\ell _ t=\Gamma ^*_ t$ otherwise. Note that $\ell $ is a subgeodesic due to the gluing lemma 4.1.11 . Consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }=\inf _{t>0} (\ell _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] Then $\Gamma '_{\tau }\geq \Gamma _{\tau }$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ by proposition 1.2.11 for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. We claim that 9.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammapGammcomptemp1} \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _{\tau }+(b-a)(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}. \end{equation} Observe that $\Gamma '_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ when $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$ by 9.2.6 . Thus it suffices to consider $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$. Put \[  C_{\tau }\coloneqq (b-a)(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau )\geq 0.  \] For any $s\in [a,b]$, the monotonicity of $t\mapsto \Gamma _ t^*-t\Gamma _{\max }$ from 9.2.6 gives \[  \Gamma _ b^*-b\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau }.  \] Since $\ell _ b=\Gamma _ b^*$, we get \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _ b^*-b\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau },\quad s\in [a,b].  \] For $s\notin [a,b]$, we have $\ell _ s=\Gamma _ s^*$, hence \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau }.  \] Taking the infimum over all $s>0$ gives \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _{\tau }+C_{\tau }.  \] Therefore, ( 9.14 ) follows. In particular, for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have $\Gamma '_{\tau }\sim \Gamma _{\tau }$. Moreover, $\sup _ X\ell _ t\leq t\Gamma _{\max }$ for all $t>0$: this is clear outside $(a,b)$ from 9.2.6 , and on $(a,b)$ it follows from the convexity of subgeodesics applied to the geodesic $(\eta _ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$. Hence, for $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \sup _ X(\ell _ t-t\tau )\leq t(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau ).  \] Letting $t\to 0+$ gives $\Gamma '_{\tau }\leq 0$. It follows from the fact that $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is a model potential that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\Gamma '_{\tau }$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Therefore, by theorem A.2.2 , we have $\Gamma ^*_ t=\ell _ t$ for all $t>0$, which is a contradiction. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.2.8
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.2.8 . Given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, then $\ell ^*=(\ell ^*_\tau )_{\tau <\sup _ X \ell _1}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Proof. Note that it follows from proposition 1.2.11 that $\ell ^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. It is clear that $\mathbb {R}\ni \tau \mapsto \ell ^*_{\tau }$ is a decreasing and concave function. By proposition 4.2.9 , \[  \sup _ X\ell _ t= t\sup _ X \ell _1 \quad \forall t\geq 0.  \] Set $C=\sup _ X\ell _1$. By proposition 4.2.9 , $\sup _ X(\ell _ t-Ct)=0$ for all $t>0$. For each $x$ outside a pluripolar set, the function $t\mapsto \ell _ t(x)-Ct$ is convex on $(0,\infty )$ and bounded above by $0$, hence it is decreasing. By proposition 1.2.6 , the same monotonicity holds as an inequality of $\theta $-psh functions. Thus $(\ell _ t-Ct)_{t>0}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Its infimum is not identically $-\infty $, since the family is normalized by $\sup _ X(\ell _ t-Ct)=0$ and is compact in $L^1$ by proposition 1.5.4 . Therefore \[  \ell ^*_{C}=\inf _{t>0}(\ell _ t-Ct)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )  \] by proposition 1.2.2 . On the other hand, for $\tau >\sup _ X \ell _1$, the same argument shows that \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\equiv -\infty .  \] Therefore, $\ell ^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ if and only if $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }\coloneqq \sup _ X \ell _1$. We claim that $(\ell ^*_{\tau })_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}$ is a test curve. We first observe that for $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \ell _1-\tau \sim _ P \phi .  \] Therefore, 9.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:elltaupreceqpphi} \ell ^*_{\tau }\preceq _ P \phi ,\quad \forall \tau <\ell ^*_{\max }. \end{equation} Also observe that for any $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }$ and any $t>0$, we have \[  \sup _ X \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \sup _ X \ell _ t-t\tau =\ell ^*_{\max }t-t\tau .  \] Letting $t\to 0+$, we find that for any $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }$, we have 9.17 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supXelltaustarnegtemp1} \sup _ X \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq 0. \end{equation} Fix $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$. We want to argue that 9.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pellstartemp1} P_{\theta }\left[\ell ^*_{\tau }\right]=\ell ^*_{\tau }. \end{equation} First we claim that for any $C>0$, we have 9.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ellstartaupCtemp1} (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi =(\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }. \end{equation} The $\leq $ direction is trivial. We argue the reverse inequality, which reduces to \[  \phi \geq (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }.  \] Since $\phi $ is model and $(\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }\leq 0$, it suffices to show that \[  \phi \succeq _ P (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta },  \] which follows from ( 9.16 ). Therefore, ( 9.19 ) is established. Thanks to ( 9.17 ), we have the obvious inequality \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }\geq \ell ^*_{\tau }  \] for any $C>0$. Therefore, in order to prove ( 9.18 ), it remains to argue that for any $C>0$, 9.20 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ellstarleqetemp1} (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi \leq \ell ^*_{\tau }. \end{equation} For this purpose, let us consider the following geodesics: For any $M>0$ and $t\in [0,1]$, let \[  \ell ^{1,M}_ t= \ell _{tM}-tM\tau ,\quad \ell ^{2,M}_ t= (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Ct.  \] It is clear that at $t=0,1$, we have $\ell ^{2,M}_ t\leq \ell ^{1,M}_ t$. Hence, the same holds for all $t\in [0,1]$. In particular, for any fixed $s\in (0,1]$, we have \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Cs\leq \ell _{sM}-sM\tau  \] for all $M>0$. Taking infimum with respect to $M>0$, we find \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Cs\leq \ell ^*_{\tau }.  \] Since $s\in (0,1]$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 9.20 ). Finally, we check the condition at $-\infty $. Set \[  \psi \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\ell ^*_{\tau }.  \] The family $(\ell ^*_{\tau })_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}$ is locally uniformly bounded from above, so $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Thanks to corollary 4.1.7 , outside a pluripolar set, the function $t\mapsto \ell _ t(x)$ is a finite closed convex function on $[0,\infty )$ with value $\phi (x)$ at $t=0$. Applying the one-variable Legendre duality gives \[  \psi (x)=\adjustlimits \sup _{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}\inf _{t>0}\bigl (\ell _ t(x)-t\tau \bigr )=\ell _0(x)=\phi (x)\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Hence $\psi =\phi $ by proposition 1.2.6 . In particular, $\ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi $ has positive mass. $\square$

title: Theorem 9.2.9
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Theorem 9.2.9 . The Legendre transform in definition 9.2.1 is a bijection 9.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:RWNco} \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation} Moreover, this bijection restricts to the following bijections: 9.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:RWNcotwocases} \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi ),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation} For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have 9.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:RWNenergy} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^*). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first establish ( 9.21 ). It follows from 9.2.7 that the forward map is well-defined. The inverse map is given by ( 9.15 ). We show that the inverse map is also well-defined. Given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we know from 9.2.8 that $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We need to show that $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. The equality $\ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi $ was proved in 9.2.8 . Therefore, $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as expected. The two operations are inverse to each other thanks to corollary A.2.4 . Hence, ( 9.21 ) is established. Step 2 . Next we consider the bounded situation. Namely, we want to establish the second half of ( 9.22 ). Suppose that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Take $\tau _0\in \mathbb {R}$ so that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\phi $ for all $\tau \leq \tau _0$. It follows from ( 9.9 ) that \[  \Gamma _ t^*\geq \phi +t\tau _0  \] for all $t>0$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^*_ t\sim \phi $ for all $t>0$ and hence $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Conversely, suppose that $\ell \in \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Thanks to proposition 4.2.7 , there is a constant $C>0$ such that \[  \ell _ t\geq \phi -Ct.  \] Therefore, according to ( 9.15 ), we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\geq \inf _{t>0} \Bigl ( \phi -(C+\tau )t \Bigr )=\phi  \] if $\tau \leq -C$. Therefore, $\ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi $ for all $\tau \leq -C$. Step 3 . We establish ( 9.23 ) and the first half of ( 9.22 ). Step 3.1 . We reduce to the case where $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Suppose that we define \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }=\Gamma _{\tau +\Gamma _{\max }},\quad \forall \tau <0.  \] Then $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as well and for all $t>0$, \[  \Gamma '^*_ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left( t\tau +\Gamma '_{\tau } \right)=\sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left( t\tau +\Gamma _{\tau } \right)-t\Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma ^*_ t-t\Gamma _{\max }.  \] Therefore, \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }\left(\Gamma '^*\right)=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*\right)-\Gamma _{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] by ( 3.71 ). Using ( 9.5 ), we also have \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ')=& \int _{-\infty }^0 \left( \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma '_{\tau }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\left( \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )-\Gamma _{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, it suffices to establish ( 9.23 ) for $\Gamma '$ in place of $\Gamma $. Step 3.2 . We assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$ and $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We prove ( 9.23 ). For $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $M \in \mathbb {Z}$, we introduce the following: \[  \Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t \coloneqq \max _{\substack {k \in \mathbb {Z} \\ k \leq M}} \left(\Gamma _{k/2^ N} + tk/2^ N\right)\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ),\quad t>0.  \] We first claim that for all $t>0$, $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and $M\in \mathbb {Z}_{<0}$, 9.27 \begin{equation} \label{eq:diff_eq_I} \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\leq \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}. \end{equation} Assuming this, let us prove ( 9.23 ). Fixing $N$, let $M=\lfloor 2^{N}\Gamma _{\min }\rfloor $. Recall that $\Gamma _{\min }$ is defined in ( 9.4 ). Then repeated applications of ( 9.27 ) yield \[  \sum _{j=M+1}^0 \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}}\leq E^{\phi }_{\theta }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}\right)-E^{\phi }_{\theta }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\leq \sum _{j=M}^{-1} \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}}.  \] Since $M \leq 2^{N}\Gamma _{\min }$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t =\phi +t M/2^ N.  \] Using ( 3.71 ), we can continue to write \[  \sum _{j=M+1}^0 \frac{t}{2^ N} \left(\int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}} - \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\phi }\right)\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}\right)\leq \sum _{j=M}^{-1} \frac{t}{2^ N} \left(\int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}} - \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\phi }\right).  \] We now notice that we have Riemann sums on both the left and right of the above inequality. Moreover, as $N\to \infty $, the potentials $\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}$ increase to $\Gamma _ t^*$, hence their energies converge to $E^\phi _\theta (\Gamma _ t^*)$ by proposition 3.1.47 . Using proposition 9.1.4 , it is possible to let $N \to \infty $ and obtain 9.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:EGammastartt} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*})=t\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ) \end{equation} So ( 9.23 ) follows as desired. It remains to argue ( 9.27 ). Fix $t>0$, $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and $M\in \mathbb {Z}$. By proposition 3.1.46 , 9.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:first_I_ineq} \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}}\leq &  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\\  \leq &  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Clearly $\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1} \geq \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}$. Moreover, since $\mathbb {R}\ni \tau \mapsto \Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau $ is concave, we notice that \[  U_ t \coloneqq \left\{ \Gamma ^{*,N,M+1}_ t>\Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t\right\}  = \left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N} + 2^{-N}t >\Gamma _{M/2^ N}\right\} ,  \] and on $U_ t$ we have 9.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammstaronUntemp1} \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1} = \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N} + t (M+1)/2^{N},\quad \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M} = \Gamma _{M/2^ N} + t M /2^{N}. \end{equation} We also note that $U_ t$ is $\mathcal{F}$-open by corollary 1.3.16 . So from the lower bound in ( 9.29 ), we have \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\geq &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}}\\  = &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}\\  \geq &  \int _{\left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0\right\} }t2^{-N}\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}, \end{aligned}  \] where on the second line, we applied ( 9.32 ) and proposition 2.2.2 , on the third line, we applied the fact that $\theta _{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}^ n$ is supported on the set (cf. theorem 3.1.7 ) \[  \left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0\right\} \subseteq U_ t\cap \left\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\right\} .  \] When $(M+1)/2^ N=0$, we use proposition 3.1.25 to see that $P_\theta [\Gamma _0]=\Gamma _0$, since $\Gamma _0$ is the decreasing limit of the model potentials $\Gamma _\tau $ as $\tau \nearrow 0$. Thus theorem 3.1.7 applies to this endpoint as well. We have deduced the first inequality in ( 9.27 ). Next, we apply the upper bound part in ( 9.29 ) and compute similarly \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M})\leq &  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}}\\  =&  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}\\  \leq &  \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t}\left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}} \\  \leq & \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t} t2^{-N}\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}. \end{aligned}  \] We conclude the latter half of ( 9.27 ). Step 3.3 . We assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Now $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ only. For each $\epsilon >0$, we introduce $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as follows: Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  \phi ,& \textup{if }\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1};\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _{\tau }-\epsilon \tau \phi \right],& \textup{if }\tau \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0\right). \end{cases}  \] The concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . The value at $-\infty $ is $\phi $. Moreover, $\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau =\phi $ for $\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1}$, so $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{TC}^\infty (X,\theta ;\phi )$. It follows from corollary 6.2.20 and corollary 6.2.11 that for each $\tau <0$, the potentials $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }$ decrease to $\Gamma _{\tau }$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Applying proposition 3.1.26 , we have \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n  \] for all $\tau <0$. Hence, by the monotone convergence theorem and Step 3.2, we find 9.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:EphiGammatemp1} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon })=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *})=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1), \end{equation} where the last equality follows from ( 9.28 ). Furthermore, according to proposition A.2.10 , we have \[  \Gamma ^*_ t=\inf _{\epsilon >0} \Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_ t  \] for all $t>0$. Note that we do not have to take the closure of the right-hand side since it is automatically upper semicontinuous in $t$. Now suppose that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then by ( 9.42 ), as $\epsilon \to 0+$, $(\Gamma _ t^{\epsilon *})_{\epsilon }$ is a decreasing Cauchy net in $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and hence by theorem 4.3.15 for each $t>0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_ t\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon ,*}_ t\right)=t\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )>-\infty ,  \] where we have applied ( 9.28 ) and ( 9.42 ). Hence, $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Moreover, ( 9.23 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then ( 9.42 ) implies that \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1\right) \geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_1\right)>-\infty .  \] Hence, $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. $\square$

title: Remark 9.2.10
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Remark 9.2.10 . One could also consider geodesic rays emanating from another potential $\Phi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, one can show that these geodesic rays are in bijection with $\Phi $-twisted test curves: In definition 9.1.1 , we replace 2 by the following condition: \[  P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right](\Phi )=\Gamma _{\tau }.  \] Furthermore, we require that $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\Phi $. The above results equally work in the twisted setting. The proofs are almost identical to the untwisted case.

title: Corollary 9.2.11
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 9.2.11 . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\sup _ X \ell _ t=\ell ^*_{\max }t$ for any $t\geq 0$. In particular, $\ell _ t-\ell ^*_{\max }t$ is a decreasing function of $t\geq 0$. Proof. This follows from 9.2.6 and theorem 9.2.9 . $\square$

title: Example 9.2.12
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Example 9.2.12 . Let us see what the test curve in example 9.1.6 corresponds to under the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We claim that 9.43 \begin{equation} \label{eq:RWNsingtype} \ell ^{\varphi }=\Gamma ^{\varphi *}, \end{equation} where $\ell ^{\varphi }$ is as in example 4.3.26 . We may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ since both sides are invariant after adding a constant to $\varphi $. We first prove the easy direction $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$, which is equivalent to $\ell ^{\varphi *}\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi }$. Since $\ell ^{\varphi *}$ is a test curve, the latter is equivalent to \[  \ell ^{\varphi *}_{\tau }\geq (1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }  \] for all $\tau \in (-1,0)$. By Legendre duality, this is equivalent to 9.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:lvarphigeq_temp1} \ell ^{\varphi }_ t\geq \sup _{\tau \in (-1,0)} \Bigl ((1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }+t\tau \Bigr )=\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-t) \end{equation} for all $t>0$. Using the notations of example 4.3.26 , we find easily that \[  \ell ^{\varphi ,C}_ t\geq \varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-t)  \] for any $C>0$ and $t\in [0,C]$, since it holds at $t=0$ and $t=C$. Letting $C\to \infty $, we find ( 9.44 ). Therefore, $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$ follows. In order to prove the equality in ( 9.43 ), it suffices to show that the two sides have the same energy, as a consequence of ( 4.94 ). So we compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi *}\right)=&  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi }\right)\\  =&  \int _{-1}^0 \left(\int _ X \theta _{(1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n} \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \int _0^1 \tau ^ j (1-\tau )^{n-j}\, \mathrm{d}\tau -\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n} \binom {n}{j}\frac{j!(n-j)!}{(n+1)!} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  =&  \mathbf{E}(\ell ^{\varphi }), \end{aligned}  \] where in the second line we used proposition 3.1.6 , in the fourth line we used the value of the $\beta $-function Note. Also known as Euler integral of the first kind. , and the last line is just ( 4.103 ).

title: Proposition 9.2.13 (He–Testorf–Wang)
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.2.13 (He–Testorf–Wang) . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Given any $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $x\in X$, we have 9.50 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mis_RWN} \mathcal{I}\left(\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)_{x}=\left\{  f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}: |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t\tau )\, \mathrm{d}t \textup{ is integrable near }x \right\} . \end{equation} Proof. Fix $x\in X$, $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 9.50 ). Given any $y\in X$, it follows from ( 9.15 ) that there is $t_0>0$ with \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0\tau .  \] Observe that $t\mapsto \ell _ t-t\ell ^*_{\max }$ is decreasing in $t$ by corollary 9.2.11 , it follows that for $t\in [t_0,t_0+1]$, we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1-t_0(\ell ^*_{\max }-\tau )\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0\ell ^*_{\max }\geq \ell _{t}(y)-t\ell ^*_{\max }.  \] Since $\tau < \ell ^*_{\max }$ and $t_0\geq t-1$, we deduce that 9.51 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mis_RWN_temp1} \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1+\ell ^*_{\max }-\tau \geq \ell _{t}(y)-t\tau ,\quad t\in [t_0,t_0+1]. \end{equation} Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t\tau )\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Applying ( 9.51 ), we deduce that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Therefore, $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau })_ x$. Step 2 . Assume that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau })_ x$. It follows from the strong openness theorem theorem 1.4.16 (cf. ( 9.2 )) that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon })_ x$ for some small enough $\epsilon >0$ with $\tau +\epsilon <\ell ^*_{\max }$. Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2 \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }\right)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell _ t+t\tau \right)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\leq &  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }-t\epsilon \right)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\\  =& \frac{1}{\epsilon }\int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }\right)\, \omega ^ n\\  <& \infty . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 9.50 ). $\square$

title: Proposition 9.2.14 (Hisamoto)
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.2.14 (Hisamoto) . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Given any $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have 9.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mass_tc} \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} } \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$. We first observe that it suffices to show that 9.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mass_tc_temp1} \int _{\left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \right\} } \theta _{\phi }^ n=\int _{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} } \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Assuming ( 9.56 ) for the moment. By theorem 9.2.9 , $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In particular, $\ell ^*_\tau $ is a model potential and \[  \ell ^*_\tau \leq \ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi .  \] Since $\phi $ is model as well, proposition 3.1.21 gives \[  \theta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n,\quad \theta ^ n_{\phi }=\mathds {1}_{\{ \phi =0\} }\, \theta ^ n.  \] Since $\ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \phi \leq 0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} }\, \theta _{\phi }^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi =0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n =\theta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}.  \] Therefore, ( 9.55 ) follows from ( 9.56 ). In order to prove ( 9.56 ), it suffices to show that 9.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:dotell_temp1} \left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \right\} =\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} \quad \textup{outside a pluripolar set}. \end{equation} Take $x\in X$ so that $(\ell _ t(x))_{t\geq 0}$ is finite and right-differentiable at $t=0$. Note that this condition holds quasi-everywhere. Suppose that $\ell ^*_{\tau }(x)=\phi (x)$. Then \[  \dot{\ell }_0(x)=\inf _{t>0} \frac{\ell _ t(x)-\phi (x)}{t}\geq \inf _{t>0} \frac{\ell ^*_{\tau }(x)+t\tau -\phi (x)}{t}=\tau .  \] Therefore, the $\supseteq $ direction in ( 9.57 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\dot{\ell }_0(x)\geq \tau $, then \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} \left(\ell _ t(x)-t\tau \right)\geq \inf _{t>0} \left(\phi (x)+t\dot{\ell }_0(x)-t\tau \right)\geq \phi (x).  \] Together with $\ell ^*_\tau \leq \phi $, this gives $\ell ^*_\tau (x)=\phi (x)$. Therefore, the $\subseteq $ direction in ( 9.57 ) follows as well. $\square$

title: Corollary 9.2.15
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 9.2.15 . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\dot{\ell }_0\in L^1(X,\theta _{\phi }^ n)$ and 9.58 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ray_energy_slope} \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, for every $t\geq 0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\ell _ t)=t\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Proof. Set $\Gamma =\ell ^*$. By theorem 9.2.9 , we have $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ).  \] By proposition 9.2.14 , for every $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} } \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Hence ( 9.5 ) gives \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell ) =\ell ^*_{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{-\infty }^{\ell ^*_{\max }} \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0<\tau \} }\theta _{\phi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}\tau .  \] For $\tau >\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have $\ell ^*_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ by 9.2.8 . Then ( 9.56 ) shows that \[  \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} }\theta _{\phi }^ n=0.  \] The layer-cake formula therefore gives ( 9.58 ). The final assertion follows from proposition 4.3.16 , since $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\ell _0)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\phi )=0$. $\square$

title: 9.3 -model test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
9.3 $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Fix a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Definition 9.3.1 . A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model if for any $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma _{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. The subset of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. When $\phi =V_{	heta }$, we omit $\phi $ and write $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$ instead. The union of the sets of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ for all model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Note that $\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}$ is automatically $\mathcal{I}$-model, since \[  \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}\leq P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}ight]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq \inf _{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}=\inf _{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}\Gamma _{	au }=\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}.  \] Here we write $\mathrm{NA}$ with non-Archimedean in mind. The precise relation with non-Archimedean pluripotential theory will be clear in chapter 13 . This section and the next can be skipped on a first reading; the necessary results can be consulted when reading chapter 13 . Proposition 9.3.2 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Proof. This follows from proposition 3.2.19 . $\square$ Proposition 9.3.3 . Let $	heta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $	heta $. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ')_{>0}.  \] This bijection satisfies the obvious cocycle condition. Proof. Let $	heta '=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. By proposition 9.1.7 , the canonical map sends $\Gamma $ to the test curve with levels \[  \Gamma '_	au =P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g].  \] If $\Gamma _	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model, then it is $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.7 . Note that $\Gamma _	au -g$ is $\mathcal I$-good since $\Gamma _{	au }$ is. Hence \[  P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g]=P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g]_{\mathcal I},  \] so $\Gamma '_	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model. The same argument applied to $-g$ gives the inverse map, and the cocycle condition follows from the one in proposition 9.1.7 . $\square$ Proposition 9.3.4 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*	heta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 9.1.8 and proposition 3.2.7 . $\square$ Definition 9.3.5 . Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$, we define its $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{	heta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ),\quad 	au \mapsto P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we define $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega ),\quad 	au \mapsto P_{	heta +\omega }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proposition 9.3.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then \[  P_{	heta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;P_{	heta }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta +\omega ;P_{	heta +\omega }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] Proof. We prove the first assertion; the second is identical, replacing $	heta $ by $	heta +\omega $. Set \[  \widetilde\Gamma _	au \coloneqq P_	heta [\Gamma _	au ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The family is decreasing by 3.2.17 . If $	au =(1-s)	au _0+s	au _1$, then the concavity of $\Gamma $ gives \[  \Gamma _	au \geq (1-s)\Gamma _{	au _0}+s\Gamma _{	au _1}.  \] Hence, by 3.2.17 and proposition 3.2.16 , \[  \widetilde\Gamma _	au \geq (1-s)\widetilde\Gamma _{	au _0}+s\widetilde\Gamma _{	au _1}.  \] Thus the family is concave. Finally, \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\widetilde\Gamma _	au = P_	heta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}  \] follows from proposition 3.2.19 . Since $P_	heta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}\geq \phi $, its mass is positive by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . This proves the assertion. $\square$ Definition 9.3.7 . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A geodesic ray $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is maximal if $\ell ^*$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, namely, if $\ell ^*\in \mathcal E^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. An important class of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves is given by filtrations. We briefly recall the corresponding terminology. Definition 9.3.8 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle. We write \[  R(X,L)= igoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)  \] for the section ring Note. It is more natural to replace the direct sum by a disjoint union, leading to the notion of ringoids ( annénoïdes in French), introduced by Ducros in [ Duc21 ] in the context of Temkin's graded reduction of Berkovich germs. of $L$. A filtration on $R(X,L)$ is a decreasing family of graded linear subspaces $(\mathcal{F}^{\lambda })_{\lambda \in \mathbb {R}}$ of $R(X,L)$ with graded pieces \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }= igoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k,  \] such that the following conditions are satisfied: The filtration is left-continuous: For any $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }= igcap _{\lambda '<\lambda }\mathcal{F}^{\lambda '};  \] the filtration is multiplicative: For any $\lambda ,\lambda '\in \mathbb {R}$ and any $k,k'\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\cdot \mathcal{F}^{\lambda '}_{k'}\subseteq \mathcal{F}^{\lambda +\lambda '}_{k+k'};  \] there is an integer $C>0$ such that 9.59  egin{equation} \label{eq:Flinearlybdd} \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation} for all $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Given a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ on $R(X,L)$, we define \[  	au _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup \left\{ \lambda \in \mathbb {R}: \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k
eq 0ight\} .  \] By Fekete's lemma, we can introduce \[  	au (\mathcal{F})=\lim _{k	o \infty } rac{1}{k}	au _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}	au _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] Note that $	au (\mathcal{F})$ is bounded from above by the constant $C$ in ( 9.59 ), hence finite. Example 9.3.9 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be a filtration on $R(X,L)$. Fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ and write $	heta =c_1(L,h)$. We introduce a few auxiliary functions. For each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we introduce \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \log |s|_{h^ k}^2: s\in \mathcal{F}^{k	au }_ k, |s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1 ight\} .  \] When $k	au \leq 	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $\mathcal{F}_ k^{k	au }
eq 0$. Moreover, proposition 1.8.4 and proposition 1.2.2 imply that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,k	heta ),\quad 	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] Observe that for $k,k'\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k+k'}_{	au }\geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }+\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k'}_{	au }.  \] In particular, by Fekete's lemma, 9.60  egin{equation} \label{eq:limkGammaFk} \lim _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au } \end{equation} exists for any $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. We define $(\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au })_{	au <	au (\mathcal{F})}$ as follows: \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }\coloneqq P_{	heta }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }ight] ootnotemark .  \] Note. It is not clear if $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ is necessary here. When $L$ is ample, it is shown in [ Proposition 7.11 , RWN14 ] that it is not necessary. The proof in the reference relies on a Skoda division theorem [ Theorem 7.10 , RWN14 ] , which is not known in the case of big line bundles. We claim that $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$ and is bounded. It is clear that $(-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F}))
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is decreasing. We prove its concavity. By proposition 3.1.24 , it suffices to show that \[  \Bigl (-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F})\Bigr )
i 	au \mapsto \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }  \] is concave. In other words, we need to prove the following: Given $	au _0<	au _1<	au (\mathcal{F})$ and $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}.  \] But thanks to proposition 1.2.6 and proposition 1.2.5 , it suffices to show that \[  \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}  \] for all $t\in (0,1)$. Take $s_ i\in \mathcal{F}^{k_ i	au _ i}_{k_ i}$ for $i=0,1$ with $|s_ i|_{h^{k_ i}}^2\leq 1$, where $k_0,k_1\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We need to prove that 9.61  egin{equation} \label{eq:GammaFconctemp1} \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{equation} Approximating $t$ by rational numbers $t_ m\searrow t$, and using the decreasingness of the filtration in the parameter $\lambda $, we reduce to the case $t\in \mathbb Q$. Write $t=p/q$ with $p,q\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Then \[  s\coloneqq s_0^{k_1(q-p)}\otimes s_1^{k_0p}\in \mathcal{F}_{k_0k_1 q}^{k_0k_1	au _0(q-p)+k_0k_1	au _1 p},  \] and \[   egin{aligned} &  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q} \log |s|_{h^{k_0k_1 q}}^2\  =&  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q}\left(k_1(q-p)\log |s_0|^2+ k_0p\log |s_1|^2ight)\  = &  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{aligned}  \] So ( 9.61 ) follows. Note that for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $k^{-1}\Gamma _{	au }^{\mathcal{F},k}$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 7.2.3 . The family is bounded above by $0$, so it follows from the same proposition that the obstacle in the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Hence the $P$- and $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes of this obstacle agree, so $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model for each $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. It remains to show that the test curve $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}$ is bounded and lies in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$. Fix $	au \leq -C$, where $C$ is as in ( 9.59 ). We will show that 9.65  egin{equation} \label{eq:Gammatautheta} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }=V_{	heta }. \end{equation} This follows from the Bergman kernel technique. Based on the theory developed so far, we can also give an elementary argument. Fix $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. Since $	au \leq -C$, we have $\mathcal F^{k	au }_ k=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. Let $s\in \mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. After multiplying $s$ by a constant, we may assume that $|s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1$. By the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au $, \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au \geq \log |s|_{h^ k}^2.  \] Hence \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au )ight).  \] Since \[  k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au \geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au ,  \] we get \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight).  \] Thus \[  \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight)=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)  \] for every $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. By theorem 7.4.2 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)=\operatorname{vol}L.  \] As $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model, this volume is equal to $\int _ X\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)^ n$. Hence $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ has full Monge–Ampère mass. Since it is also model, it must be equal to $V_	heta $. This proves ( 9.65 ). Remark 9.3.10 . There is an important special case of example 9.3.9 : Suppose that $L$ is ample and $\mathcal{F}$ is the filtration induced by a smooth test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ of $(X,L)$. Then the geodesic ray $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}*}$ is exactly the Phong–Sturm geodesic ray associated with $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$. See [ Section 9 , RWN14 ] . Remark 9.3.11 . We deduce from example 9.3.9 that the ray $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}*}$ induced by a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ is maximal.

title: Definition 9.3.1
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.3.1 . A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model if for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. The subset of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. When $\phi =V_{\theta }$, we omit $\phi $ and write $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ instead. The union of the sets of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$.

title: Proposition 9.3.2
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.3.2 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Proof. This follows from proposition 3.2.19 . $\square$

title: Proposition 9.3.3
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.3.3 . Let $\theta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $\theta $. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}.  \] This bijection satisfies the obvious cocycle condition. Proof. Let $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. By proposition 9.1.7 , the canonical map sends $\Gamma $ to the test curve with levels \[  \Gamma '_\tau =P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g].  \] If $\Gamma _\tau $ is $\mathcal I$-model, then it is $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.7 . Note that $\Gamma _\tau -g$ is $\mathcal I$-good since $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is. Hence \[  P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g]=P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g]_{\mathcal I},  \] so $\Gamma '_\tau $ is $\mathcal I$-model. The same argument applied to $-g$ gives the inverse map, and the cocycle condition follows from the one in proposition 9.1.7 . $\square$

title: Proposition 9.3.4
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.3.4 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 9.1.8 and proposition 3.2.7 . $\square$

title: Definition 9.3.5
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.3.5 . Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we define its $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{\theta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),\quad \tau \mapsto P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we define $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\omega ),\quad \tau \mapsto P_{\theta +\omega }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \]

title: Proposition 9.3.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.3.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;P_{\theta }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ;P_{\theta +\omega }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] Proof. We prove the first assertion; the second is identical, replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega $. Set \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \coloneqq P_\theta [\Gamma _\tau ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The family is decreasing by 3.2.17 . If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then the concavity of $\Gamma $ gives \[  \Gamma _\tau \geq (1-s)\Gamma _{\tau _0}+s\Gamma _{\tau _1}.  \] Hence, by 3.2.17 and proposition 3.2.16 , \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \geq (1-s)\widetilde\Gamma _{\tau _0}+s\widetilde\Gamma _{\tau _1}.  \] Thus the family is concave. Finally, \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\widetilde\Gamma _\tau = P_\theta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}  \] follows from proposition 3.2.19 . Since $P_\theta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}\geq \phi $, its mass is positive by the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . This proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Definition 9.3.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.3.7 . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A geodesic ray $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is maximal if $\ell ^*$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, namely, if $\ell ^*\in \mathcal E^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$.

title: Definition 9.3.8
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.3.8 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle. We write \[  R(X,L)=\bigoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)  \] for the section ring Note. It is more natural to replace the direct sum by a disjoint union, leading to the notion of ringoids ( annénoïdes in French), introduced by Ducros in [ Duc21 ] in the context of Temkin's graded reduction of Berkovich germs. of $L$. A filtration on $R(X,L)$ is a decreasing family of graded linear subspaces $(\mathcal{F}^{\lambda })_{\lambda \in \mathbb {R}}$ of $R(X,L)$ with graded pieces \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }=\bigoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k,  \] such that the following conditions are satisfied: The filtration is left-continuous: For any $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }=\bigcap _{\lambda '<\lambda }\mathcal{F}^{\lambda '};  \] the filtration is multiplicative: For any $\lambda ,\lambda '\in \mathbb {R}$ and any $k,k'\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\cdot \mathcal{F}^{\lambda '}_{k'}\subseteq \mathcal{F}^{\lambda +\lambda '}_{k+k'};  \] there is an integer $C>0$ such that 9.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Flinearlybdd} \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation} for all $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Given a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ on $R(X,L)$, we define \[  \tau _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup \left\{ \lambda \in \mathbb {R}: \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\neq 0\right\} .  \] By Fekete's lemma, we can introduce \[  \tau (\mathcal{F})=\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}\tau _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}\frac{1}{k}\tau _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \]

text: 9.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Flinearlybdd} \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation}

title: Remark 9.3.10

text: Remark 9.3.10 . There is an important special case of example 9.3.9 : Suppose that $L$ is ample and $\mathcal{F}$ is the filtration induced by a smooth test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ of $(X,L)$. Then the geodesic ray $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}*}$ is exactly the Phong–Sturm geodesic ray associated with $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$. See [ Section 9 , RWN14 ] .

title: 9.4 Operations on test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
9.4 Operations on test curves Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta ,\theta ',\theta ''$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. In this section, we develop several general operations on test curves, anticipating the applications in non-Archimedean geometry in chapter 13 . One may read chapter 13 first and consult this section when necessary. Definition 9.4.1 . Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, we say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if $\Gamma _{\max }\leq \Gamma '_{\max }$ and, for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have 9.66 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammatauGammap} \Gamma _{\tau }\preceq _ P \Gamma '_{\tau }. \end{equation} Observe that ( 9.66 ) actually holds for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ if $\theta =\theta '$. Here we use the convention that $-\infty \preceq _ P \varphi $ for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)\cup \{ -\infty \} $. The relation $\leq $ defines a partial order on $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Lemma 9.4.2 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']$. Proof. This follows from example 6.1.3 . $\square$ Definition 9.4.3 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max };  \] for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define Note. There is no usc regularization in the formula. It is not a typo. 9.67 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammaGammapsum} (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\right]. \end{equation} Lemma 9.4.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, \[  \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ').  \] This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, ( 9.67 ) in definition 9.4.3 makes sense. Proof. Let \[  \eta _{\tau }=\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)=\sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Set \[  Z=\left\{ x\in X: \Gamma _{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} \cup \left\{ x\in X: \Gamma '_{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} .  \] It follows from proposition A.2.11 that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \eta ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)+\Gamma '^*_ t(x)  \] for all $t>0$. The same trivially holds when $x\in Z$, so the equation holds everywhere. In particular, by corollary A.2.4 and proposition 1.2.11 , we have \[  \eta _{\tau }=\left(\Gamma ^*+\Gamma '^*\right)^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')  \] when $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is a test curve. The family $\tau \mapsto \eta _\tau $ is decreasing, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 3.1.24 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then for arbitrary $\delta _0,\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\delta =(1-s)\delta _0+s\delta _1$, \[  \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\geq (1-s)(\Gamma _{\delta _0}+\Gamma '_{\tau _0-\delta _0})+s(\Gamma _{\delta _1}+\Gamma '_{\tau _1-\delta _1}).  \] Taking suprema and using proposition 3.1.24 gives the concavity of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Choose $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ with $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then \[  \eta _\tau \geq \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }.  \] By 9.1.3 , $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Hence $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ has positive $(\theta +\theta ')$-mass by the multi-linearity of non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 . It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 that $\eta _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. By corollary 3.1.12 , \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by proposition 1.2.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Thus $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Next, assume that $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$ are $\mathcal{I}$-model. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then for each $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ such that $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$, we know that $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ by 9.1.3 .
