Then there is a countable subset $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. We may assume that $I$ is infinite. Set \[  M\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }.  \] For each rational number $q<M$, apply Choquet's lemma proposition 1.2.3 to the locally uniformly bounded above family \[  \left\{ \left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q:J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)\right\} \subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] We obtain a countable subfamily $\mathcal J_ q\subseteq \operatorname{Fin}(I)$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q = \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \mathcal J_ q}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q.  \] Let \[  I'\coloneqq \bigcup _{q\in \mathbb Q, q<M} \bigcup _{J\in \mathcal J_ q}J.  \] Then $I'$ is countable and, for every rational $q<M$, \[  \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q= \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q.  \] Moreover, $\sup _{i\in I'}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }=M$, since the last equality is non-trivial for every rational $q<M$. Let $\Gamma '=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then clearly, $\Gamma '\leq \Gamma $. We claim that they are actually equal. Thanks to proposition 6.1.4 and 9.1.3 , it suffices to show that for any $\tau <\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$, we have \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n.  \] The equality is already known for all rational $\tau <M$. Since both \[  \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma '_\tau }^ n,\quad \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _\tau }^ n  \] are continuous on $(-\infty ,M)$ by proposition 9.1.4 , the equality of masses holds for every $\tau <M$. $\square$ Proposition 9.4.20 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Definition 9.4.21 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$, we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$  as follows: We set \[  \left(\lambda \Gamma \right)_{\max }=\lambda \Gamma _{\max };  \] for any $\tau < \left(\lambda \Gamma \right)_{\max }$, we set \[  (\lambda \Gamma )_{\tau }=\lambda \Gamma _{\lambda ^{-1}\tau }.  \] Proposition 9.4.22 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$. Then $\lambda \Gamma $ as defined in definition 9.4.21 lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$. We have 9.92 \begin{equation}  (\lambda \Gamma )_{-\infty }=\lambda \Gamma _{-\infty }. \end{equation} Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Proposition 9.4.23 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Lemma 9.4.24 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\lambda \omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]=\lambda P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ].  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 9.4.25 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that 9.96 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gammaiinffinite1} \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation} and 9.97 \begin{equation} \label{eq:massnondeg} \inf _{i\in I} \int _ X \left( \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right)^ n>0,\quad \textup{for some }\tau < \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }. \end{equation} Then we define $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\max }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max };  \] for any $\tau < \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\max }$, we let \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}_{\tau }.  \] Proposition 9.4.26 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.96 ) and ( 9.97 ). Then $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then so is $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}$. Proof. The first assertion is an immediate consequence of proposition 3.1.25 , except for the positivity of the mass at $-\infty $. Choose $\tau _0$ as in ( 9.97 ). Applying proposition 3.1.26 gives \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau _0}\right)^ n =\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i}_{\tau _0}\right)^ n>0.  \] Hence the value at $-\infty $ has positive mass by monotonicity. The last assertion follows from proposition 3.2.18 . $\square$ In general, it is not true that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{-\infty }.  \] Lemma 9.4.27 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.96 ) and ( 9.97 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. First observe that \[  \left( P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right] \right)_{\max }= \left(\inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]\right)_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Then we need to show the following: 9.98 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetaomega_inf} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\sim _ P \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation} Applying proposition 3.1.26 gives the mass convergence required in corollary 6.2.11 . Hence $\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S}\inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } $. Thanks to corollary 6.2.19 and corollary 6.2.11 , we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right],\quad P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} \inf _{j\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right].  \] Hence, ( 9.98 ) follows from proposition 6.2.4 . $\square$ It is very fortunate that, unlike people who dig for gold, mathematicians can freely share their precious treasures with everybody. Once you understand something really well, it feels great to explain it to all. 
— Andrei Okounkov Note. Andrei Yuryevich Okounkov (1969–) is a Russian-American mathematician renowned for his contributions to representation theory. He was one of the key organizers of the ICM 2022 in St. Petersburg, which was unfortunately canceled under the indiscriminate discrimination against Russian citizens by the virtue signalers all over the western world after the war waged by the ruling class.

Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, we say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if $\Gamma _{\max }\leq \Gamma '_{\max }$ and, for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have 9.66 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammatauGammap} \Gamma _{\tau }\preceq _ P \Gamma '_{\tau }. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 9.4.2
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.2 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']$. Proof. This follows from example 6.1.3 . $\square$

title: Definition 9.4.3
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.4.3 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max };  \] for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define Note. There is no usc regularization in the formula. It is not a typo. 9.67 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammaGammapsum} (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\right]. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 9.4.4
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, \[  \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ').  \] This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, ( 9.67 ) in definition 9.4.3 makes sense. Proof. Let \[  \eta _{\tau }=\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)=\sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Set \[  Z=\left\{ x\in X: \Gamma _{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} \cup \left\{ x\in X: \Gamma '_{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} .  \] It follows from proposition A.2.11 that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \eta ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)+\Gamma '^*_ t(x)  \] for all $t>0$. The same trivially holds when $x\in Z$, so the equation holds everywhere. In particular, by corollary A.2.4 and proposition 1.2.11 , we have \[  \eta _{\tau }=\left(\Gamma ^*+\Gamma '^*\right)^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')  \] when $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is a test curve. The family $\tau \mapsto \eta _\tau $ is decreasing, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 3.1.24 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then for arbitrary $\delta _0,\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\delta =(1-s)\delta _0+s\delta _1$, \[  \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\geq (1-s)(\Gamma _{\delta _0}+\Gamma '_{\tau _0-\delta _0})+s(\Gamma _{\delta _1}+\Gamma '_{\tau _1-\delta _1}).  \] Taking suprema and using proposition 3.1.24 gives the concavity of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Choose $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ with $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then \[  \eta _\tau \geq \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }.  \] By 9.1.3 , $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Hence $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ has positive $(\theta +\theta ')$-mass by the multi-linearity of non-pluripolar products proposition 2.2.2 6 . It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 that $\eta _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. By corollary 3.1.12 , \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by proposition 1.2.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Thus $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Next, assume that $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$ are $\mathcal{I}$-model. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then for each $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ such that $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$, we know that $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ by 9.1.3 . It follows from example 7.1.7 that $\Gamma _\delta $ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ are both $\mathcal{I}$-good, hence so is $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ by proposition 7.2.1 . These sums are bounded above by $0$, so $\eta _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 7.2.3 . Since $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]$, we conclude that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. $\square$

title: Proposition 9.4.5
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.4.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Moreover, 9.68 \begin{equation} \label{eq:sumGammaGammap} (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }=P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }\right]. \end{equation} When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. The operation $+$ is commutative and associative. Proof. It follows immediately from 9.4.4 that $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. It lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. We argue ( 9.68 ). By definition, for any small enough $\tau $, we have \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{2\tau }\succeq _ P \Gamma _{\tau }+\Gamma '_{\tau }.  \] Letting $\tau \to -\infty $ and applying proposition 6.2.24 and theorem 6.2.25 , we find that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\succeq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] On the other hand, for each small enough $\tau $, we have \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right) \preceq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }  \] by proposition 6.1.19 and proposition 6.2.24 . We apply proposition 6.2.24 again, we conclude that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty } \preceq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] So ( 9.68 ) follows. Finally, let us show that $+$ is commutative and associative. Commutativity follows from the symmetry of the defining supremum. Let $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta '')_{>0}$. Then we want to show that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] First observe that \[  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma '' \right)_{\max }=\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '')\right)_{\max }.  \] Fix $\tau $ less than this common value. We compute that \[  \begin{aligned} & \left( (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''\right)_{\tau }\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '+\theta ''}\left[\sup _{\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}} \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\delta _1}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right)\right]\\  \sim _ P &  \sup _{\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}} \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\delta _1}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right)\\  \sim _ P &  \sup _{\delta _1,\delta _2\in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _{\delta _2}+\Gamma '_{\delta _1-\delta _2}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line, we applied proposition 6.2.24 and proposition 6.1.19 . Similarly, for $\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '')\right)_{\tau }$, we get the same expression. The associativity follows. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.4.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-forms $\omega $ and $\omega '$ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\theta '+\omega +\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '].  \] Proof. Observe that \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta +\theta '+\omega +\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']_{\max }=& \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '] \right)_{\max }\\  =& \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }. \end{aligned}  \] Take $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this common value. We need to verify that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \Bigl ( P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma ']\Bigr )_{\tau }.  \] By definition, this means that \[  \sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\delta }+\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\sim _ P \sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\delta }]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }]\right).  \] This is a consequence of proposition 6.1.19 and proposition 6.1.20 . $\square$

title: Definition 9.4.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.4.7 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$, we define $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  (\Gamma +C)_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }+C;  \] for any $\tau <(\Gamma +C)_{\max }$, we set \[  (\Gamma +C)_{\tau }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\tau -C}.  \]

title: Proposition 9.4.8
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.4.8 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ and $C,C'\in \mathbb {R}$. Then $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+C)=(\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '$; $\Gamma +(C+C')=(\Gamma +C)+C'$. Proof. 1 We first observe that \[  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C\right)_{\max }=\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+C) \right)_{\max }=\left( (\Gamma +C)+\Gamma ' \right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }+C.  \] Take any $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this common value. We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C\right)_{\tau }=& (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau -C} = P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right],\\  \left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+C) \right)_{\tau }=&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +(\Gamma '+C)_{\tau -\delta } \right) \right]\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right],\\  \left((\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '\right)_{\tau }=&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( (\Gamma +C)_{C+\delta }+\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right]\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right]. \end{aligned}  \] 2 Observe that \[  \left( \Gamma +(C+C') \right)_{\max }=\left( (\Gamma +C)+C' \right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }+C+C'.  \] For any $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this value, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +(C+C') \right)_{\tau }=\Gamma _{\tau -C-C'}=\left( (\Gamma +C)+C' \right)_{\tau }.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Definition 9.4.9
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 9.4.9 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We define $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max };  \] for any $\tau <(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define 9.80 \begin{equation} \label{eq:testcurlordef} (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta }\left[ \operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation}

text: 9.80 \begin{equation} \label{eq:testcurlordef} (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta }\left[ \operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 9.4.10
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.10 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$, we have \[  \operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),  \] and $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. In particular, ( 9.80 ) in definition 9.4.9 makes sense. Proof. To simplify the notation, we write \[  \psi _{\tau }=\operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau }  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Thanks to proposition A.2.10 , for any fixed $x\in X$, we have 9.81 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psistartemp1} \psi ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)\lor \Gamma '^*_ t(x) \end{equation} for all $t>0$ as long as $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)\neq -\infty $ and $\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)\neq -\infty $ for some $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Otherwise, assume for instance that $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$; then by definition, $\psi _{\tau }(x)=\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)$ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)=-\infty $ for all $t>0$ and ( 9.81 ) continues to hold. The case where $\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau $ is symmetric. Therefore, we have shown that \[  \psi ^*_ t=\Gamma ^*_ t\lor \Gamma '^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] It follows from proposition 4.1.9 that $(\psi ^*_ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is a subgeodesic for any $0< a<b$. Next we observe that $\psi _{\bullet }$ is closed by definition. So it follows from proposition A.2.10 and proposition 1.2.11 that \[  \psi _{\tau }=(\psi ^*_{\bullet })^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Due to proposition 9.1.9 and proposition A.1.11 , there is a pluripolar set $Z\subseteq X$ such that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \psi _{\tau }(x)=\sup \left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }(x)+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}(x): \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\}  \end{split}  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. It follows from proposition 1.2.6 that 9.83 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psitausupslineartemp} \begin{split}  \psi _{\tau }=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}: \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\}  \end{split} \end{equation} for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$ is a test curve. The function $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $ is decreasing, hence its upper concave envelope $\psi _\bullet $ is decreasing. The monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 3.1.24 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Since $\psi _\bullet $ is concave by construction, proposition 3.1.24 gives the concavity of $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. Then either $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ or $\tau <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Since $\psi _\bullet $ is a concave majorant of $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $, we have \[  \psi _\tau \geq \Gamma _\tau \quad \text{if } \tau <\Gamma _{\max }, \qquad \psi _\tau \geq \Gamma '_\tau \quad \text{if } \tau <\Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Together with the fact that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $, these inequalities show that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. It follows from 9.1.3 and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. By corollary 3.1.12 , \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau =P_\theta [\psi _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by proposition 1.2.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Thus $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. It follows from ( 9.83 ) that $\psi _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, thanks to proposition 7.2.1 and proposition 7.2.3 ; the family in the upper envelope is bounded above by $0$. Since $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau =P_\theta [\psi _\tau ]$, we conclude that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in this case. $\square$

title: Corollary 9.4.11
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 9.4.11 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 9.85 \begin{equation} \label{eq:GammalorGammapminfty} (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }=P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{-\infty }\lor \Gamma '_{-\infty }\right]. \end{equation} If $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and each $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma $ and $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma '$, we have $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Moreover, the operation $\lor $ is associative and commutative. Proof. It follows immediately from 9.4.10 that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, and it lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We argue ( 9.85 ). Set \[  \eta \coloneqq \Gamma _{-\infty }\lor \Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] Since $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\geq \Gamma $ and $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\geq \Gamma '$, we have $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq \eta $. As $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }$ is a model potential, it follows that \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq P_\theta [\eta ].  \] Conversely, for each $\rho \in \mathbb {R}$ we have $\Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho \leq \eta $. Hence the constant curve with value $\eta $ is a concave majorant of $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $, and therefore \[  \operatorname{CE}\left(\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho \right)_\tau \leq \eta ,\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Applying the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope and then letting $\tau \to -\infty $ gives \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\leq P_\theta [\eta ].  \] This proves ( 9.85 ). Take $\Gamma ''$ as in the statement of the corollary. First observe that \[  \Gamma ''_{\max }\geq \Gamma _{\max } \lor \Gamma '_{\max }=(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }.  \] Take $\tau <(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }$. We argue that \[  \Gamma ''_{\tau }\geq (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }.  \] By the concavity of $\Gamma ''$, the potential $\Gamma ''_\tau $ dominates the concave envelope \[  \operatorname{CE}\left(\rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho }\right)_\tau .  \] Since $\Gamma ''_\tau $ is model, the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope gives \[  \Gamma ''_{\tau }\geq (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }.  \] Therefore, \[  \Gamma ''\geq \Gamma \lor \Gamma '.  \] Commutativity is immediate from the definition. Associativity follows from the least-upper-bound property just proved: both $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')\lor \Gamma ''$ and $\Gamma \lor (\Gamma '\lor \Gamma '')$ are the least upper bound of $\Gamma ,\Gamma ',\Gamma ''$. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.4.12
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.12 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma '].  \] Proof. We first observe that \[  \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']\right)_{\max }=\left( P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']\right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. We need to show that \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma '] \right)_{\tau }.  \] We need the formula ( 9.83 ) proved in the proof of 9.4.10 : \[  \begin{split}  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}: \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\} . \end{split}  \] A similar result holds with $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]$ and $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']$ in place of $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$. So our assertion is a direct consequence of proposition 6.1.19 and proposition 6.1.20 . $\square$

title: Definition 9.4.13

text: Definition 9.4.13 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that 9.87 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gammaisupfinite1} \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }<\infty . \end{equation} Then we define $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: We set \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\max }=\sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max };  \] for any $\tau < \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }$, we let \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\tau }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}_{\tau }.  \]

title: Proposition 9.4.14
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.4.14 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}$ as defined in definition 9.4.13 lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}$ lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as well. Moreover, we have 9.88 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gammiminf} \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $\tau <\sup _ i\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$. Choose $i_0$ such that $\tau <\Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }$. On the tail $i\geq i_0$, the potentials $\Gamma ^ i_\tau $ form an increasing net of model potentials of positive mass, uniformly bounded above by $0$. Hence proposition 3.1.28 shows that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_\tau = \operatorname *{sup}_{i\geq i_0}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_\tau  \] is model. Its mass is positive by monotonicity, since it dominates $\Gamma ^{i_0}_\tau $. The decreasingness and concavity in $\tau $ follow from the directedness of the net and the corresponding properties of the curves $\Gamma ^ i$. Thus $\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}_ i\Gamma ^ i$ is a test curve. If all $\Gamma ^ i$ are $\mathcal I$-model, the same tail argument and proposition 3.2.19 show that the supremum is $\mathcal I$-model. It remains to argue ( 9.88 ). Fix any $i_0\in I$. Since the curves are decreasing and are extended as in 9.1.2 , the value at $-\infty $ can be computed by taking the supremum over rational $\tau <\Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }$. By proposition 1.2.5 , there is a pluripolar set $Z\subseteq X$ such that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }(x)=\sup _{\mathbb {Q}\ni \tau < \Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }}\left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }\right)(x)=\sup _{\mathbb {Q}\ni \tau < \Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max },i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }(x)=\sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }(x).  \] So they are equal everywhere by proposition 1.2.6 . $\square$

text: Lemma 9.4.15 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. Observe that \[  \left( P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right] \right)_{\max }= \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]\right)_{\max }=\sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }.  \] Fix $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this common value. It suffices to show that \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\tau }\sim _ P \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[\Gamma ^{i}\right] \right)_{\tau }.  \] This is an immediate consequence of proposition 6.1.20 . $\square$

title: Proposition 9.4.17

text: Proposition 9.4.17 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then so is $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Finally, we have 9.91 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supsminfty} \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)_{-\infty }=P_{\theta }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty } \right]. \end{equation} Proof. The first assertion and the second follow from proposition 9.4.14 and corollary 9.4.11 . It remains to argue ( 9.91 ). For this purpose, it suffices to show that \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)_{-\infty }\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] For any $J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)$, it follows from corollary 9.4.11 and proposition 6.1.20 that \[  \left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_{-\infty }\sim _ P \bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j_{-\infty }.  \] From this, applying proposition 3.1.28 , proposition 6.1.20 and proposition 9.4.14 , we conclude our assertion. $\square$

title: Proposition 9.4.19
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 9.4.19 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Then there is a countable subset $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. We may assume that $I$ is infinite. Set \[  M\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }.  \] For each rational number $q<M$, apply Choquet's lemma proposition 1.2.3 to the locally uniformly bounded above family \[  \left\{ \left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q:J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)\right\} \subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] We obtain a countable subfamily $\mathcal J_ q\subseteq \operatorname{Fin}(I)$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q = \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \mathcal J_ q}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q.  \] Let \[  I'\coloneqq \bigcup _{q\in \mathbb Q, q<M} \bigcup _{J\in \mathcal J_ q}J.  \] Then $I'$ is countable and, for every rational $q<M$, \[  \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q= \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q.  \] Moreover, $\sup _{i\in I'}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }=M$, since the last equality is non-trivial for every rational $q<M$. Let $\Gamma '=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then clearly, $\Gamma '\leq \Gamma $. We claim that they are actually equal. Thanks to proposition 6.1.4 and 9.1.3 , it suffices to show that for any $\tau <\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$, we have \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n.  \] The equality is already known for all rational $\tau <M$. Since both \[  \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma '_\tau }^ n,\quad \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _\tau }^ n  \] are continuous on $(-\infty ,M)$ by proposition 9.1.4 , the equality of masses holds for every $\tau <M$. $\square$

title: Proposition 9.4.20

text: Proposition 9.4.20 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$

text: Proposition 9.4.23 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.87 ). title: Proposition 9.4.26

text: Proposition 9.4.26 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.96 ) and ( 9.97 ). Then $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then so is $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}$. Proof. The first assertion is an immediate consequence of proposition 3.1.25 , except for the positivity of the mass at $-\infty $. Choose $\tau _0$ as in ( 9.97 ). Applying proposition 3.1.26 gives \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau _0}\right)^ n =\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i}_{\tau _0}\right)^ n>0.  \] Hence the value at $-\infty $ has positive mass by monotonicity. The last assertion follows from proposition 3.2.18 . $\square$

title: Lemma 9.4.27
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 9.4.27 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 9.96 ) and ( 9.97 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. First observe that \[  \left( P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right] \right)_{\max }= \left(\inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]\right)_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Then we need to show the following: 9.98 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetaomega_inf} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\sim _ P \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation} Applying proposition 3.1.26 gives the mass convergence required in corollary 6.2.11 . Hence $\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S}\inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } $. Thanks to corollary 6.2.19 and corollary 6.2.11 , we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right],\quad P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} \inf _{j\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right].  \] Hence, ( 9.98 ) follows from proposition 6.2.4 . $\square$

title: 10 The theory of Okounkov bodies
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
10 The theory of Okounkov bodies In this chapter, we apply our theory of singularities to the study of Okounkov bodies. We construct convex bodies $\Delta (L,\phi )$, the partial Okounkov bodies , attached to a big line bundle $L$ on a smooth projective variety $X$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $\phi $ on $L$. These convex bodies provide a universal numerical invariant of the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\phi $, and reduce many problems in pluripotential theory to problems in convex geometry, which are often more tractable. We develop two parallel constructions: an algebraic one in section 10.3 , where $\phi $ is encoded by the multiplier ideals $\mathcal{I}(k\phi )$, and a transcendental one in section 10.4 , where $\phi $ is treated directly as an analytic object via valuations on closed positive currents. The two constructions agree when both apply, but each has its own natural domain of definition and its own range of applications. We assume some familiarity with the classical Okounkov bodies. Excellent references are the original papers of Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă [ LM09 ] and Kaveh–Khovanskii [ KK12 ] ; we give a rapid review here. Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ and $L$ a big holomorphic line bundle on $X$. Given an admissible flag $X=Y_0\supseteq Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n$ on $X$ (definition 10.2.1 ), one attaches to $L$ a natural $n$-dimensional convex body $\Delta (L)\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$, generalizing the Newton polytope construction in toric geometry (definition 5.2.11 ). This construction was first considered by Okounkov [ Oko96 , Oko03 ] and extended by Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă [ LM09 ] and Kaveh–Khovanskii [ KK12 ] . The convex body $\Delta (L)$ is the Okounkov body of $L$ with respect to the chosen flag. Concretely, the successive vanishing order along the flag defines a valuation $
u \colon \mathbb {C}(X)^{	imes }	o \mathbb {Z}^ n$, and \[  \Gamma (L)\coloneqq \left\{ (
u (s),k)\in \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}:k\in \mathbb {N},\,  s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)^{	imes } ight\}   \] is a semigroup whose closed convex cone, intersected with the slice $\{ (x,1)\} $, is $\Delta (L)$. Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă [ LM09 ] showed that $\Delta (L)$ depends only on the numerical class of $L$, and Jow [ Jow10 ] showed that the Okounkov bodies for all flags determine this class, so $\Delta (L)$ may be regarded as a universal numerical invariant of $L$. The aim of this chapter is to perform the analogous construction at the level of singularity types of psh metrics. Setting \[  \Gamma (L,\phi )\coloneqq \left\{ (
u (s),k)\in \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}:k\in \mathbb {N},\,  s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\phi ))^{	imes } ight\} ,  \] one immediately encounters the obstruction that $\Gamma (L,\phi )$ is in general not a semigroup, so the Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă and Kaveh–Khovanskii constructions break down. The remedy is the notion of an almost semigroup : $\Gamma (L,\phi )$ does satisfy a near-semigroup property (theorem 10.3.12 ), and the convex-body construction $\Gamma \mapsto \Delta (\Gamma )$ extends continuously from semigroups to almost semigroups (theorem 10.1.6 ). The partial Okounkov body of $(L,\phi )$ is then \[  \Delta (L,\phi )\coloneqq \Delta  igl (\Gamma (L,\phi ) igr ),  \] and is a convex sub-body of $\Delta (L)$ — explaining the name partial . The universality of partial Okounkov bodies is captured by corollary 10.3.28 : the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\phi $ is determined by the Okounkov bodies of $(L,\phi )$ for sufficiently many flags. The results in this chapter will be applied in chapter 12 to develop toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles.

title: 10.1 Almost semigroups

text: 10.1 Almost semigroups We give a brief presentation of the theory of almost semigroups. The arguments are provided in chapter C . Fix an integer $n\geq 0$. Fix a closed convex cone $C\subseteq \mathbb {R}^{n}\times \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0}$ such that $C\cap \{ x_{n+1}=0\} =\{ 0\} $. Here $x_{n+1}$ is the last coordinate of $\mathbb {R}^{n+1}$. Write $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ for the set of subsets of $C\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ and $\mathcal{S}(C)$ for the set of subsemigroups $S\subseteq C\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$. For $S\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ and each $k\in \mathbb {N}$ such that $S_ k\neq \varnothing $, we write \[  S_ k\coloneqq \left\{ x\in \mathbb {Z}^ n: (x,k)\in S \right\} .  \] Note that $S_ k$ is a finite set by our assumption on $C$. We introduce a pseudometric on $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ as follows: 10.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:dsgdef} d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')\coloneqq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } k^{-n} \left(|S_ k|+|S'_ k|-2|(S\cap S')_ k|\right). \end{equation} Here $|\bullet |$ denotes the cardinality of a finite set. The quantity $d_{\mathrm{sg}}$ defined above is a pseudometric on $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$. Given $S,S'\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$, we say $S$ is equivalent to $S'$ and write $S\sim S'$ if $d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')=0$. This is an equivalence relation. The volume of $S\in \mathcal{S}(C)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}S\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty } (ka)^{-n}|S_{ka}|=\varlimsup _{k\to \infty } k^{-n}|S_ k|,  \] where $a$ is a sufficiently divisible positive integer. The existence of the limit and its independence from $a$ both follow from theorem C.2.3 . We define $\overline{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ as the closure of $\mathcal{S}(C)$ in $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ with respect to the topology defined by the pseudometric $d_{\mathrm{sg}}$. The function $\operatorname{vol}\colon \mathcal{S}(C)\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ admits a unique $1$-Lipschitz extension to 10.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volex} \operatorname{vol}\colon \overline{\mathcal{S}}(C)\rightarrow \mathbb {R}. \end{equation} Given $S\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$, we will write $C(S)\subseteq C$ for the closed convex cone generated by $S\cup \{ 0\} $. Moreover, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ such that $S_ k\neq \varnothing $, we define \[  \Delta _ k(S)\coloneqq \mathrm{Conv}\left\{ k^{-1}x\in \mathbb {R}^ n:x\in S_ k \right\} \subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n.  \] Here $\mathrm{Conv}$ denotes the convex hull. Definition 10.1.1 . Let $\mathcal{S}'(C)$ be the subset of $\mathcal{S}(C)$ consisting of semigroups $S$ such that $S$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ (as an Abelian group). Note that for any $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, the cone $C(S)$ has full dimension (i.e., the topological interior is non-empty). Given a full-dimensional subcone $C'\subseteq C$, we have $C'\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$. We recall the following definition from [ KK12 ] . Definition 10.1.2 . Given $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, its Okounkov body is defined by \[  \Delta (S)\coloneqq \left\{ x\in \mathbb {R}^ n:(x,1)\in C(S) \right\} .  \] Theorem 10.1.3 . For each $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, we have 10.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volWvolDelta} \operatorname{vol}S=\lim _{k\to \infty } k^{-n}|S_ k|=\operatorname{vol}\Delta (S)>0. \end{equation} Moreover, as $k\to \infty $, 10.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:HausconvDeltaGLS} \Delta _{k}(S)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta (S). \end{equation} Corollary 10.1.4 . Let $S,S'\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$. Assume that $\operatorname{vol}(S\cap S')>0$. Then we have \[  d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')=\operatorname{vol}(S)+\operatorname{vol}(S')-2\operatorname{vol}(S\cap S').  \] Definition 10.1.5 . We define $\overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ as the set of elements in the closure of $\mathcal{S}'(C)$ in $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ with positive volume. An element in $\overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ is called an almost semigroup in $C$. Recall that the volume here is defined in ( 10.2 ). Theorem 10.1.6 . The Okounkov body map $\Delta \colon \mathcal{S}'(C) \rightarrow \mathcal{K}_ n$ as defined in definition 10.1.2 admits a unique continuous extension 10.5 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Deltagensg} \Delta \colon \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}\rightarrow \mathcal{K}_ n. \end{equation} Moreover, for any $S\in \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$, we have 10.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volWfinal} \operatorname{vol}S=\operatorname{vol}\Delta (S). \end{equation} Corollary 10.1.7 . Suppose that $S,S'\in \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ with $S\subseteq S'$. Then 10.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Deltacontain} \Delta (S)\subseteq \Delta (S'). \end{equation}

For each $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, we have C.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volWvolDeltaapp} \operatorname{vol}S=\lim _{k\to \infty } k^{-n}|S_ k|=\operatorname{vol}\Delta (S)>0. \end{equation} Moreover, as $k\to \infty $, C.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:HausconvDeltaGLSapp} \Delta _{k}(S)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta (S). \end{equation} Proof. The equalities ( C.6 ) follow from theorem C.2.3 . It remains to prove ( C.7 ). By the argument of [ Lemma 4.8 , WN14 ] , for any compact set $K\subseteq \operatorname{Int}\Delta (S)$, there is $k_0>0$ such that for any $k\geq k_0$, $\alpha \in K\cap (k^{-1}\mathbb {Z})^ n$ implies that $\alpha \in \Delta _ k(S)$. To conclude, fix $\epsilon >0$. Choose $\delta >0$ such that $K\coloneqq \Delta (S)_{\delta }$ has positive volume and $d_{\mathrm{Haus}}(K,\Delta (S))<\epsilon /2$. Then there is a modification $Wightarrow X$ dominating $Zightarrow X$ such that $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting to $W$. Recall that in this book, a modification means a finite composition of blowing-ups with smooth centers. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem B.1.6 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. We begin by setting $W_0=Z$. We will construct $W_ i$ inductively for each $i$. Assume that for $0\leq i<n$ a smooth partial flag $W_0\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ i$ has been constructed on a modification $\pi _ i:Z_ iightarrow Z$ so that $\pi \circ \pi _ i$ restricts to bimeromorphic morphisms $W_ jightarrow Y_ j$ for each $j=0,\ldots ,i$. The problem is that $W_{i+1}$ is not necessarily smooth. We will further modify $Z_ i$ and lift $W_1,\ldots , W_{i+1}$ in order to make the flag smooth. Definition 10.2.12 . Let $\pi \colon Zightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a normal compact Kähler space, and let $S$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $Z$. u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)\coloneqq 
u _{W_{ ullet }}(h^*S)g^{-1}\in \mathbb {R}^ n. \end{equation} Note that it could happen that $
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)

Then $W_{ ullet }$ is also the lifting of $W^ i_{ ullet }$ with respect to $q_ i$. u _{W_{ ullet }} igl (q_ i^*h_ i^*S igr ) \operatorname{cor}(Y_{ ullet },\pi \circ h_ i\circ q_ i)^{-1} & =

title: Proposition 10.2.10
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Proposition 10.2.10 . Let $\pi \colon Z\rightarrow X$, $p\colon Z'\rightarrow Z$ be proper bimeromorphic morphisms with $Z$ and $Z'$ being Kähler manifolds. Assume that $Y_{\bullet }$ admits a lifting $W_{\bullet }$ (resp. $W_{\bullet }'$) to $Z$ (resp. $Z'$). Then 10.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:cormul} \operatorname{cor}(Y_{\bullet },\pi \circ p)=\operatorname{cor}(Y_{\bullet },\pi )\operatorname{cor}(W_{\bullet },p). \end{equation} Proof. We let $\pi '=\pi \circ p$. Then $W'_{\bullet }$ is also the lifting of $W_{\bullet }$ with respect to $p$. \[  \gerbyimage{sgpt/b8283f944aed9f824ecf.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source}  \] We argue by induction on $n\geq 1$. The case $n=1$ is trivial. Assume that $n\geq 2$ and the case $n-1$ has been solved. Then by ( 10.13 ), the desired formula ( 10.22 ) can be reformulated as \[  \begin{aligned} & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n,\pi '|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow Y_1) 

\end{bmatrix}=\\ & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n}((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n,\pi |_{W_1}:W_1\rightarrow Y_1) 

\end{bmatrix}\cdot \\ & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n,p|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow W_1) 

\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}.  \] By the inductive hypothesis, this is equivalent to \[  \begin{split}  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)= \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)+\\  \nu _{W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n}\left((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1}\right)\operatorname{cor}\left(W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n,p|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow W_1\right), \end{split}  \] which, thanks to proposition 10.2.9 , can be further rewritten as \[  \begin{split}  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)= \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)+\\  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left(p|_{W_1'}^*\left((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1} \right)\right). \end{split}  \] Indeed, as divisors on $W_1'$, \[  (\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}=(p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}+p|_{W_1'}^*((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1}).  \] The desired equality is therefore exactly the additivity of the valuation, proposition 10.2.7 . $\square$

title: Theorem 10.2.11
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 10.2.11 . Let $\pi \colon Z\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a reduced complex space $Z$. Then there is a modification $W\rightarrow X$ dominating $Z\rightarrow X$ such that $Y_{\bullet }$ admits a lifting to $W$. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem B.1.6 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. We begin by setting $W_0=Z$. We will construct $W_ i$ inductively for each $i$. Assume that for $0\leq i<n$ a smooth partial flag $W_0\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ i$ has been constructed on a modification $\pi _ i:Z_ i\rightarrow Z$ so that $\pi \circ \pi _ i$ restricts to bimeromorphic morphisms $W_ j\rightarrow Y_ j$ for each $j=0,\ldots ,i$. By Zariski's main theorem, $W_ i\rightarrow Y_ i$ is an isomorphism outside a codimension $2$ subset of $Y_ i$. We let $W_{i+1}$ be the strict transform of $Y_{i+1}$ in $W_ i$. The problem is that $W_{i+1}$ is not necessarily smooth. We will further modify $Z_ i$ and lift $W_1,\ldots , W_{i+1}$ in order to make the flag smooth. Take the embedded resolution of $(W_{j},W_{i+1})$, say $W_ j'\rightarrow W_ j$ for each $j=0,\ldots ,i$. We have canonical embeddings $W_{i}'\hookrightarrow W_{i-1}'\hookrightarrow \cdots \hookrightarrow W_0'$ making the following diagram commutative: \[  \gerbyimage{sgpt/dd023174a6a92604fb13.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source}  \] Let $W_{i+1}'$ be the strict transform of $W_{i+1}$ in $W_ i'$. It suffices to define $\pi _{i+1}$ as the morphism $W_0'\rightarrow Z_ i\rightarrow Z$ and replace $W_0\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_{i+1}$ by $W_0'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_{i+1}'$. $\square$

text:
Lemma 10.2.13 . The definition in definition 10.2.12 is independent of the choice of $h$. Moreover, if $p\colon Z'ightarrow Z$ is a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a normal compact Kähler space, then, with respect to the model $\pi \circ p\colon Z'ightarrow X$, \[  
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(p^*S)=
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S).  \] Proof. We first prove independence of the choice of $h$. Let $h_ i\colon \widehat Z_ iightarrow Z$, $i=1,2$, be two choices, and let $(W^ i_{ ullet },g_ i)$ be the corresponding liftings, with $g_ i=\operatorname{cor}(Y_{ ullet },\pi \circ h_ i)$. Choose a common modification over $Z$, $q_ i\colon Uightarrow \widehat Z_ i$ such that $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting $W_{ ullet }$ to $U$. Then $W_{ ullet }$ is also the lifting of $W^ i_{ ullet }$ with respect to $q_ i$. Put \[  G_ i=\operatorname{cor}(W^ i_{ ullet },q_ i).  \] By proposition 10.2.9 , proposition 10.2.10 , \[   egin{aligned}  
u _{W_{ ullet }} igl (q_ i^*h_ i^*S igr ) \operatorname{cor}(Y_{ ullet },\pi \circ h_ i\circ q_ i)^{-1} & = 
u _{W^ i_{ ullet }}(h_ i^*S)G_ i(g_ iG_ i)^{-1} \ & = 
u _{W^ i_{ ullet }}(h_ i^*S)g_ i^{-1}. \end{aligned}  \] Since $h_1\circ q_1=h_2\circ q_2$, the left-hand side is independent of $i$. This proves that ( 10.30 ) is well-defined. For the birational invariance, choose a proper bimeromorphic morphism $q\colon \widehat Zightarrow Z'$ from a compact Kähler manifold such that $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting to $\widehat Z$ with respect to $\pi \circ p\circ q$. Computing $
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(p^*S)$ using $q$, and computing $
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)$ using $p\circ q$, gives the same expression. $\square$

title: 10.3 Algebraic partial Okounkov bodies
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: 10.3 Algebraic partial Okounkov bodies Let $X$ be a connected smooth complex projective variety of dimension $n$ and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian big line bundle on $X$. Let $h_0$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$. Let $\theta =c_1(L,h_0)$. Then we can identify $h$ with a function $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We will use interchangeably the notations $(\theta ,\varphi )$ and $(L,h)$. We assume that $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$ in this section. Fix a rank $n$ valuation $\nu \colon \mathbb {C}(X)^{\times }\rightarrow \mathbb {Z}^ n$, which without loss of generality can be assumed to be surjective. We shall frequently use the standard fact that such a full-rank valuation has one-dimensional leaves: for every finite-dimensional subspace $V\subset \mathbb C(X)$, \[  \# \nu (V^\times )=\dim V.  \] See [ Lemma 1.3 , LM09 ] for instance. We will adopt the notations of section 10.1 .

title: Proposition 10.3.4
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Proposition 10.3.4 . There is a convex body $\Delta \in \mathcal{K}_ n$ such that $\Gamma (L)\in \mathcal{S}'(\Delta )$. Proof. Step 1 . We first show that there is $\Delta \in \mathcal{K}_ n$ such that $\Delta _ k(L)\subseteq \Delta $. For this purpose, using 10.2.2 , we may assume that $
u $ is induced by an admissible flag $Y_{ ullet }$ on $X$. We may further assume that each $Y_ i$ is smooth. Fix $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)^{	imes }$ for some $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Assume that $s
eq 0$. We need to show that for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, $
u (s)_ i\leq Ck$ for some constant $C>0$, independent of the choices of $k$ and $s$. Fix an ample divisor $H$ on $X$. Take a large enough integer $b_1>0$ such that \[  (L-b_1 Y_1)\cdot H^{n-1}<0.  \] Then $
u (s)_1\leq b_1 k$. Next take a large enough integer $b_2$ such that, for every $a\in [0,b_1]$, \[  \left((L-aY_1)|_{Y_1}-b_2Y_2ight) \cdot H^{n-2}<0.  \] After removing the first vanishing order of $s$ along $Y_1$, the resulting section on $Y_1$ is a section of $k((L-aY_1)|_{Y_1})$ for some $a\in [0,b_1]$. Hence $
u (s)_2\leq b_2k$. Continuing in this manner and choosing the constants uniformly over the compact ranges of the preceding normalized vanishing orders, we conclude that $
u (s)_ i/k$ is bounded for each $i$. Here the expressions involving $L-aY_1$ are understood numerically. At the $i$-th step the previous normalized vanishing orders lie in a compact polytope, and the intersection number is continuous in these parameters; hence the constants $b_ i$ can be chosen uniformly. Step 2 . Observe that $\Gamma (L)$ is clearly a semigroup. It remains to show that $\Gamma (L)$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ as an Abelian group. For this purpose, take two very ample divisors $A$ and $B$ so that $L=\mathcal{O}_ X(A-B)$. After choosing $A$ and $B$ ample enough, we may guarantee that there exist sections $s_0\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$, $t_ i\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,B)$ for $i=0,\dots ,n$ such that \[  
u (s_0)=
u (t_0)=0  \] and $
u (t_ i)$ is the $i$-th unit vector $e_ i\in \mathbb {R}^ n$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Since $L$ is big, we can find $m_0>0$ such that for any $m\geq m_0$, we can find an effective divisor $F_ m$ on $X$ linearly equivalent to $mL-B$. Let $f_ m=
u ([F_ m])$. Then \[  (f_ m,m),(f_ m+e_1,m),\dots ,(f_ m+e_ n,m)\in \Gamma (L).  \] Since $(m+1)L$ is linearly equivalent to $A+F_ m$, we have \[  (f_ m,m+1)\in \Gamma (L).  \] It follows that $\Gamma (L)$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$. $\square$

title: Theorem 10.3.27
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 10.3.27 . Let $E$ be a prime divisor on $X$. Let $Y_{\bullet }$ be an admissible flag with $E=Y_1$. Then 10.80 \begin{equation} \label{eq:numinOk} \nu (\varphi ,E)=\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1. \end{equation} Proof. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. By theorem 7.1.1 , we can find a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. It follows from theorem 10.3.18 that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi ).  \] Therefore, by C.1.8 , \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j)}x_1=\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1.  \] In view of theorem 6.2.29 , it suffices to prove ( 10.80 ) with $\varphi _ j$ in place of $\varphi $. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. In view of proposition 10.3.19 and theorem 1.6.7 , after replacing $X$ by a modification, we may assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $F$. Perturbing $L$ by an ample $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle by proposition 10.3.23 , we may assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Therefore, $L-F$ is ample by 1.6.4 . Finally, by rescaling, we may assume that $F$ is a divisor and $L$ is a line bundle. By theorem 10.3.24 , we know that \[  \min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1=\adjustlimits \lim _{k\to \infty }\min _{x\in \Delta _ k(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1.  \] By definition, \[  \min _{x\in \Delta _ k(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1=k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right).  \] In view of proposition 1.4.13 , it remains to show that 10.81 \begin{equation} \label{eq:temp1} \lim _{k\to \infty }k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=\lim _{k\to \infty }k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ). \end{equation} The $\geq $ direction is trivial, we prove the converse. Observe that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X(-kF)\right),\quad \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}(-kF).  \] As $L-F$ is ample, for large enough $k$, the line bundle $k(L-F)$ is globally generated. Hence we can choose a section of $k(L-F)$ which does not vanish at the generic point of $E$. Viewed as a section of $L^ k\otimes \mathcal O_ X(-kF)$, it has vanishing order exactly $\operatorname{ord}_ E(kF)$ along $E$. Therefore, \[  \operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X(-kF)\right)=\operatorname{ord}_ E(kF).  \] Thus, ( 10.81 ) follows. $\square$

text: Corollary 10.3.28 . Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. If \[  \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\theta ,\pi ^*\varphi )\subseteq \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\theta ,\pi ^*\psi )  \] for all modifications $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ and all admissible flags $W_{\bullet }$ on $Y$, then $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $. Proof. By theorem 10.3.27 , the assumed inclusions imply that for every prime divisor $E$ on every modification $\pi $, \[  \nu (\pi ^*\varphi ,E)\geq \nu (\pi ^*\psi ,E).  \] Hence $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $ by proposition 6.1.5 . $\square$

text: Corollary 10.3.29 . Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$. After replacing $X$ by a modification, we may assume that $E$ is a prime divisor on $X$. Note that since $X$ is projective, we can always find an admissible flag with $E$ being the first component. title: 10.4 Transcendental partial Okounkov bodies

text: 10.4 Transcendental partial Okounkov bodies Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n>0$. Fix a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$ on $X$. We will extend the theory of partial Okounkov bodies in the previous section to the transcendental setting.

title: 10.4.1 The traditional approach to the Okounkov body problem

topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: 10.4.1 The traditional approach to the Okounkov body problem Definition 10.4.1 . Let $\alpha $ be a big cohomology class on $X$. We define the Okounkov body of $\alpha $ with respect to the flag $Y_{\bullet }$ as 10.83 \begin{equation} \label{eq:twodefspob} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )\coloneqq \overline{\left\{ \nu _{Y_{\bullet }}(S): S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha ),S\textup{ has gentle analytic singularities} \right\} }. \end{equation} See definition 1.6.9 for the definition of gentle analytic singularities. The results of [ DRWNXZ ] can be summarized as follows: Theorem 10.4.2 . For any big cohomology class $\alpha $ on $X$, the set $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$ is a convex body satisfying the following properties: We have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}\alpha ;  \] given another big cohomology class $\alpha '$ on $X$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )+\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ')\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha +\alpha ');  \] let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism where $Y$ is a Kähler manifold. Assume that $(W_{\bullet },g)$ is the lifting of $Y_{\bullet }$ to $Y$. Then \[  \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\alpha )=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )g;  \] the map $\alpha \mapsto \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )$ is continuous in the big cone with respect to the Hausdorff metric; for any small enough $t>0$, we have \[  \left\{  y\in \mathbb {R}^{n-1}: (t,y)\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ) \right\} =\Delta _{Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n}\Bigl ((\alpha -t\{ Y_1\} )|_{Y_1}\Bigr ).  \] See definition 10.2.8 for the notion of lifting. The proof requires some techniques not covered in the current book; this theorem may be used as a black box.

text: 10.4.2 Definitions of partial Okounkov bodies Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class $\alpha $. Let $T=\theta _{\varphi }\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. We shall define a convex body $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$, which is also written as $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )$. This convex body is called the partial Okounkov body of $T$ with respect to the flag $Y_{\bullet }$.

The convex body $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$ defined in definition 10.4.3 is independent of the choice of $\pi $. Proof. Take another map $\pi '\colon Y'ightarrow X$ with the same properties. We want to show that $\pi $ and $\pi '$ define the same $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$. Then \[  \pi '^*T=[p^*D]+p^*R.  \] Write $(Z_{ ullet },g)$ and $(Z_{ ullet }',g')$ for the liftings of $Y_{ ullet }$ to $Y$ and $Y'$ respectively. u _{Z_{ ullet }'}([p^*D])g'^{-1}.  \] By theorem 10.4.2 , applied to the class $\{ R\} $, we have \[  \Delta _{Z'_ ullet }(\{ p^*R\} )=\Delta _{Z_ ullet }(\{ R\} )\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] By proposition 10.2.9 , applied to the divisor current $[D]$, we also have \[  
u _{Z'_ ullet }([p^*D])=
u _{Z_ ullet }([D])\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] Finally, proposition 10.2.10 gives \[  g'=g\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] Multiplying by $(g')^{-1}$ gives the desired equality. $\square$ The above proof also describes the bimeromorphic behavior of $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$: Lemma 10.4.5 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism and $(W_{ ullet },g)$ be the lifting of $Y_{ ullet }$ to $Y$. Then \[  \Delta _{W_{ ullet }}(\pi ^*T)=\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)g.  \] Lemma 10.4.6 . Assume that $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ are two Kähler currents with analytic singularities and $T\preceq S$. Then \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ).  \] Moreover, 10.86  egin{equation} \label{eq:volpobanaly} \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)= rac{1}{n!} \int _ X T^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We first show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(S).  \] Using 10.4.5 , we may assume that $T$ and $S$ have log singularities along effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors $E$ and $F$ respectively. u _{Y_{ ullet }}([E]),  \] which is obvious. Next we prove that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ).  \] By 10.4.5 and theorem 10.4.2 again, we may assume that $T$ has log singularities. u _{Y_{ ullet }}([D])\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ),  \] which is again obvious. Finally, ( 10.86 ) follows immediately from theorem 10.4.2 . $\square$

text: Lemma 10.4.6 . Assume that $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ are two Kähler currents with analytic singularities and $T\preceq S$. Then \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ).  \] Moreover, 10.86 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volpobanaly} \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\frac{1}{n!} \int _ X T^ n. \end{equation} Proof. title: The case of Kähler currents
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: None The case of Kähler currents Definition 10.4.7 . Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(T_ j)_ j$ of $T$ in $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. Then we define \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\coloneqq \bigcap _{j=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T_ j).  \] Lemma 10.4.8 . The convex body $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$ in definition 10.4.7 is independent of the choices of the $T_ j$'s. In particular, if $T$ also has analytic singularities, then the $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$'s defined in definition 10.4.7 and in definition 10.4.3 coincide. Proof. It is more convenient to use the language of $\theta $-psh functions at this point. Let $\psi _ k$ (resp. $\varphi _ k$) denote the potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ corresponding to $S_ k$ (resp. $T_ k$) for each $k\geq 1$. Note that $\psi _ k$ and $\varphi _ k$ are unique up to additive constants. By proposition 1.6.11 , for any small rational $\epsilon >0$, $j>0$, we can find $k>0$ so that \[  \psi _ k\preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j.  \] By 10.4.6 , \[  \bigcap _{k=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\psi _ k)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,(1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j).  \] On the other hand, observe that \[  \bigcap _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}\text{ small enough}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,(1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j)=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j).  \] In fact, the $\supseteq $ direction follows from 10.4.6 , so it suffices to show that the two sides have the same volume, which follows from ( 10.86 ). It follows that \[  \bigcap _{k=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\psi _ k)\subseteq \bigcap _{j=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j).  \] The other inclusion follows by symmetry. $\square$ The same argument shows that Corollary 10.4.9 . Suppose that $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ are two Kähler currents satisfying $T \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$. Then \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ).  \] Proposition 10.4.10 . Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current. Then 10.87 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volOkocur} \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} Proof. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(T_ j)_ j$ of $T$ in $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. Note that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T_ j)$ is decreasing in $j$, as follows from 10.4.6 . Our assertion follows from ( 10.86 ) and theorem 6.2.30 . $\square$ Lemma 10.4.11 . Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current and $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then 10.88 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DeltaTincreaseomegatemp1} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+\omega ). \end{equation} Moreover, 10.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DeltaTincreaseomegatemp2} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\bigcap _{\epsilon >0}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+\epsilon \omega ). \end{equation} Proof. We first prove ( 10.88 ). Taking quasi-equisingular approximations, we reduce immediately to the case where $T$ has analytic singularities. By 10.4.5 , we may assume that $T$ has log singularities. Take $D$ and $R$ as in ( 10.84 ). By definition again, it suffices to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} )\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} +\{ \omega \} ),  \] which is clear by definition. Next we prove ( 10.89 ). Thanks to ( 10.88 ), it remains to prove that both sides have the same volume: \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}(T+\epsilon \omega )=\operatorname{vol}T.  \] This is proved in proposition 7.3.4 . $\square$

text: Corollary 10.4.9 . Suppose that $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ are two Kähler currents satisfying $T \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$. Then \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ).  \]

title: Proposition 10.4.10
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Proposition 10.4.10 . Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current. Then 10.87 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volOkocur} \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} Proof. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(T_ j)_ j$ of $T$ in $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. Note that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T_ j)$ is decreasing in $j$, as follows from 10.4.6 . Our assertion follows from ( 10.86 ) and theorem 6.2.30 . $\square$

title: Lemma 10.4.11
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Lemma 10.4.11 . Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current and $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then 10.88 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DeltaTincreaseomegatemp1} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+\omega ). \end{equation} Moreover, 10.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DeltaTincreaseomegatemp2} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\bigcap _{\epsilon >0}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+\epsilon \omega ). \end{equation} Proof. We first prove ( 10.88 ). Taking quasi-equisingular approximations, we reduce immediately to the case where $T$ has analytic singularities. By 10.4.5 , we may assume that $T$ has log singularities. Take $D$ and $R$ as in ( 10.84 ). By definition again, it suffices to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} )\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} +\{ \omega \} ),  \] which is clear by definition. Next we prove ( 10.89 ). Thanks to ( 10.88 ), it remains to prove that both sides have the same volume: \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}(T+\epsilon \omega )=\operatorname{vol}T.  \] This is proved in proposition 7.3.4 . $\square$
