We will show in corollary 11.1.20 that they are actually equivalent. Before that, by a nef Cartier b-divisor, we always mean nefness in the sense of definition 11.1.7 . Our definition definition 11.1.8 amounts to defining the set of Weil b-divisors as the closure of the set of Cartier b-divisors in $\varprojlim _{\pi }\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$ with respect to the projective limit topology. In particular, the limit of a converging net of nef b-divisors is still nef.

title: Definition 11.1.2
text: Definition 11.1.2 . A (Weil) b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is an assignment $(\mathbb {D}_{\pi })_{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X}$, where $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ runs over all modifications of $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_{\pi }\in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$; The classes are compatible under push-forwards: If $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ and $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ are both modifications of $X$ and $\pi '$ dominates $\pi $ through $g\colon Z\rightarrow Y$, then $g_*\mathbb {D}_{\pi '}=\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$. We also write $\mathbb {D}_ Y=\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$ if there is no risk of confusion. Given two Weil b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ over $X$, we say $\mathbb {D}\leq \mathbb {D}'$ if for each modification $\pi $ of $X$, we have $\mathbb {D}_{\pi }\leq \mathbb {D}'_{\pi }$. Recall that by definition, this means the class $\mathbb {D}'_{\pi }-\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$ is pseudo-effective. A Weil b-divisor with $\mathbb {D}\geq 0$ is called pseudo-effective .

title: Definition 11.1.3
text: Definition 11.1.3 . The volume of a pseudo-effective Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}\coloneqq \lim _{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y.  \] The right-hand side is a decreasing net due to proposition 3.2.12 , hence the limit always exists. The volume of a non-pseudo-effective Weil b-divisor is defined to be $0$. We say $\mathbb {D}$ is big if $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0$.

title: Lemma 11.1.4
text: Lemma 11.1.4 . Let $(\mathbb {D}_ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net of pseudo-effective b-divisors converging to a Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$. Then 11.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:vollimsup} \varlimsup _{i\in I}\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\leq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}. \end{equation} If the net is decreasing, then \[  \lim _{i\in I}\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Proof. First observe that $\mathbb {D}$ is pseudo-effective, since $\mathbb {D}_ i\geq 0$ for all $i$. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a modification. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}\geq \varlimsup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i.  \] The inequality ( 11.2 ) follows. As for the decreasing case, it suffices to observe that both sides of ( 11.2 ) can be written as \[  \inf _ i \inf _{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$
11.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:vollimsup} \varlimsup _{i\in I}\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\leq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}. \end{equation}

title: Example 11.1.5
text: Example 11.1.5 . In general, equality need not hold in ( 11.2 ). Let $X=\mathbb {P}^2$, and let $H=c_1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^2}(1))$. Choose a sequence of points $p_ i\in X$ converging to the generic point in the following sense: for every algebraic curve $C\subseteq X$, the set of indices $i$ with $p_ i\in C$ is finite. Let \[  \pi _ i\colon X_ i\rightarrow X  \] be the blow-up of $X$ at $p_ i$, with exceptional divisor $E_ i$. Let $\mathbb {D}_ i$ be the Cartier b-divisor realized on $X_ i$ by the nef class \[  \pi _ i^*H-\{ E_ i\} ,  \] and let $\mathbb {D}$ be the Cartier b-divisor realized on $X$ by $H$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ i\to \mathbb {D}$. Indeed, for any fixed modification $\rho \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the morphism $\rho $ is an isomorphism over $p_ i$ for all large enough $i$, hence the trace of $\mathbb {D}_ i$ on $Y$ is $\rho ^*H$ for all large enough $i$. On the other hand, \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i=\left(\pi _ i^*H-\{ E_ i\} \right)^2=0  \] for all $i$, whereas \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}=H^2=1.  \] Thus the inequality in ( 11.2 ) is strict for this sequence.

title: Definition 11.1.6
text: Definition 11.1.6 . A Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is a Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ such that there exists a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ and a class $\alpha _ Y\in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$ so that for each $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Z$ is the pull-back of $\alpha _ Y$. Any such $(\pi ,\alpha _ Y)$ is called a realization of $\mathbb {D}$.

title: Definition 11.1.7
text: Definition 11.1.7 . A Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is nef if there exists a realization $(\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X, \alpha _ Y)$ of $\mathbb {D}$ such that $\alpha _ Y$ is nef.

title: Definition 11.1.8
text: Definition 11.1.8 . A Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is nef if it is the limit of a net of nef Cartier b-divisors $(\mathbb {D}_ i)_ i$ over $X$.

title: 11.1.2 The b-divisors of currents
text:
11.1.2 The b-divisors of currents Definition 11.1.9 . Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Given any modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, we define 11.3  egin{equation}  \mathbb {D}(T)_ Y\coloneqq \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T ight\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R}). \end{equation} We call $\mathbb {D}(T)$ the b-divisor of $T$ . This assignment is compatible with push-forwards. Indeed, if $g\colon Z	o Y$ is a modification and $\pi \colon Y	o X$, then \[  g_*\operatorname{Reg} igl (g^*\pi ^*T igr )=\operatorname{Reg}(\pi ^*T)  \] by Siu's decomposition and 7.3.10 . Hence \[  g_*\mathbb D(T)_ Z=\mathbb D(T)_ Y.  \] Thus $\mathbb D(T)$ is a Weil b-divisor. We observe that if $T'$ is another closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$, then \[  \mathbb {D}(T+T')=\mathbb {D}(T)+\mathbb {D}(T'),\quad \mathbb {D}(\lambda T)=\lambda \mathbb {D}(T).  \] We shall use these identities implicitly in the sequel. Note that when $T$ has analytic singularities, $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is Cartier. Theorem 11.1.10 . Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef. Moreover, 11.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:volDT} \operatorname{vol}T=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T). \end{equation} Proof. Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Step 1 . Reduce to the case where $T$ is a Kähler current. Note that $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is the Cartier b-divisor realized by $(X,\{ \omega \} )$. The b-divisors $\mathbb {D}(T+\epsilon \omega )=\mathbb {D}(T)+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ decrease to $\mathbb {D}(T)$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Hence, by 11.1.4 and proposition 7.3.4 , it suffices to prove our assertion with $T+\epsilon \omega $ in place of $T$. Step 2 . We prove the assertion under the additional assumption that $T$ has analytic singularities. Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a modification so that \[  \pi ^*T=[D]+R,  \] where $D$ is an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor on $Y$ and $R$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with locally bounded potentials. See theorem 1.6.7 for the existence of $\pi $. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is the nef Cartier b-divisor realized by $(\pi ,\{ R\} )$. Note that ( 11.4 ) is immediate in this case. Step 3 . We prove the assertion for a general Kähler current $T$. Next, take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ in the cohomology class of $T$ and write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Since $T$ is a Kähler current, we choose the quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ so that, after discarding finitely many terms, each $	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ is a Kähler current. This is possible by Demailly regularization, in the form used in the proof of theorem 7.1.1 . We claim that 11.5  egin{equation} \label{eq:conv_bdiv_temp1} \mathbb {D}(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)	o \mathbb {D}(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi ). \end{equation} By definition of this convergence, we need to establish the following: for every modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, we have \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)ight)ight\} 	o \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )ight)ight\} .  \] This follows immediately from theorem 6.2.29 if $\operatorname{Sing}(\pi ^*T)$ has only finitely many components. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$. We want to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $j_0>0$ so that when $j\geq j_0$, 11.6  egin{equation} \label{eq:Regpivarphij_conv_temp1} \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)ight)ight\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )ight)ight\} +\epsilon \{ \omega _ Y\} . \end{equation} Write the divisorial part of $\pi ^*	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi _ j$ and $\pi ^*	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi $ as \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i^ j [E_ i],\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i [E_ i].  \] Then $a_ i^ j\leq a_ i$. We can find an integer $N>0$ large enough so that, in the pseudo-effective order of cohomology classes, \[  \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }a_ i \{ E_ i\} \leq  rac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] By theorem 6.2.29 , we can take $j_0$ large enough so that for $j>j_0$, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{N}(a_ i-a_ i^ j)\{ E_ i\} \leq  rac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] Then ( 11.6 ) follows, and ( 11.5 ) is established. As a consequence, $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef and the volume can be computed using 11.1.4 : \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T)=\lim _{j	o \infty }\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}\left( 	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j ight)=\lim _{j	o \infty }\operatorname{vol}\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ jight)=\operatorname{vol}T.  \] Hence, ( 11.4 ) follows. $\square$ Conversely, we want to realize nef b-divisors as $\mathbb {D}(T)$. We first prove a continuity result. Proposition 11.1.11 . Let $	heta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. If $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 11.7  egin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont1} \mathbb {D}\left(	heta _{\varphi _ i}ight)	o \mathbb {D}\left(	heta _{\varphi }ight). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to establish the following: 11.8  egin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont2} \mathbb {D}\left(	heta _{\varphi _ i}ight)_ Y	o \mathbb {D}\left(	heta _{\varphi }ight)_ Y. \end{equation} As a map from the pseudometric space $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ to the finite-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$, the continuity of $\mathbb {D}( ullet )_ Y$ can be tested on sequences. Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume that $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a sequence and $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. It is enough to prove that every subsequence has a further subsequence for which ( 11.9 ) holds. By corollary 6.2.8 , $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Hence it suffices to prove the claim on $Y$, so we may assume that $\pi $ is the identity. Therefore, we are reduced to the following assertion: 11.9  egin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont3} \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi _ i} ight\} 	o \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi } ight\} . \end{equation} After adding a Kähler form to $	heta $, we may also assume that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. By theorem 6.2.27 , replacing all potentials by their $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes does not change the divisorial parts and preserves $d_ S$-convergence. The masses are then bounded from below along a tail, so after passing to a subsequence proposition 6.2.12 supplies increasing and decreasing envelopes $\eta _ i\leq \varphi _ i\leq \psi _ i$ which both converge to $\varphi $ in $d_ S$. Since \[  \mathbb {D}(	heta _{\eta _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(	heta _{\varphi _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(	heta _{\psi _ i})_ X,  \] it is enough to treat the case where $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is monotone. Write the divisorial parts of $	heta _{\varphi _ i}$ and $	heta _{\varphi }$ as \[  \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m^ i[D_ m],\quad \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m[D_ m].  \] By theorem 6.2.29 , $a_ m^ i	o a_ m$ for each fixed $m$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is decreasing, then $a_ m^ i\leq a_ m$ for all $i,m$. The finite-tail argument in the proof of ( 11.6 ) then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi }ight\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi _ i}ight\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi }ight\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is increasing, then $a_ m\leq a_ m^ i\leq a_ m^1$. We first choose $N$ so that the tails of both $\sum _ m a_ m[D_ m]$ and $\sum _ m a_ m^1[D_ m]$ are at most $(\epsilon /3)\{ \omega \} $ in the pseudo-effective order. The convergence of the finitely many coefficients $a_ m^ i$, $m\leq N$, then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi _ i}ight\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi }ight\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}	heta _{\varphi _ i}ight\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. This proves ( 11.9 ). $\square$ Lemma 11.1.12 . Let $\pi \colon Xightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Consider non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$ currents $T,S$ on $X$ in the same cohomology class. If $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$, then $\pi _*T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi _*S$. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem B.1.6 and 6.1.18 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. By 7.3.10 , \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T,\quad \pi ^*\pi _*S=S+F_ S,  \] where $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ are effective $\pi $-exceptional divisors. Since $\{ T\} =\{ S\} $, the exceptional divisors $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ have the same cohomology class. Factoring $\pi $ into blow-ups and using proposition 11.1.1 at each step, the classes of $\pi $-exceptional prime divisors are linearly independent in the relative cohomology; hence $F_ T=F_ S$. It follows that \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}S+F_ S=\pi ^*\pi _*S.  \] Our assertion then follows from 6.1.18 . $\square$ Theorem 11.1.13 . Each big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ can be realized as $\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$. Furthermore, we may always assume that $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Note that $T$ is not unique. The current $T$ is necessarily non-divisorial. Proof. Fix a big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$. For each $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, we take a current with minimal singularities $T_ Y$ in $\mathbb {D}_ Y$. We claim that $\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)$ coincides with $\mathbb {D}$ up to the level of $Y$: For any modification $\pi '\colon Zightarrow X$ dominated by $\pi $ through a morphism $g\colon Yightarrow Z$, we have \[  \mathbb {D}_ Z=\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Z.  \] The notations are summarized in the following commutative diagram: 11.10  egin{equation} \label{eq:domi2} \gerbyimage{sgpt/e99b6d6e48f45d55c20e.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source} \end{equation} After unfolding the definitions, this means \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y).  \] Due to proposition 1.7.15 and proposition 3.2.12 , we know that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef and big. In particular, $T_ Y$ is non-divisorial, hence so is $g_*T_ Y$ by 1.7.16 . It follows from 7.3.10 that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(g_*T_ Y)=g_*T_ Y\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that 11.11  egin{equation} \label{eq:vol_unif_bound} \operatorname{vol}T_ Y\geq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0. \end{equation} Next we claim that the $P$-singularity types of the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ form a decreasing net. To see this, let us fix a diagram as ( 11.10 ). We need to show that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\preceq _ P \pi '_*T_ Z.  \] Since $T_ Z$ has minimal singularities, we have $g_*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} T_ Z$. In particular, 11.1.12 guarantees that $\pi _*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi '_*T_ Z$. But by corollary 7.3.12 and example 7.1.7 , both $\pi _*T_ Y$ and $\pi '_*T_ Z$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, so there is no difference between the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal{I}$-preorder in this case. Our assertion follows. Next observe that the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder and has a $d_ S$-limit as a consequence of ( 11.11 ) and corollary 6.2.13 . Take a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$ such that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}T.  \] It follows from proposition 11.1.11 that \[  \mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)	o \mathbb {D}(T).  \] Therefore, we conclude that \[  \mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}.  \] Thanks to theorem 11.1.10 , $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Write $T=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, then \[  T'\coloneqq 	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] is $\mathcal{I}$-good, non-divisorial and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}(T)$. $\square$ Corollary 11.1.14 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a b-divisor over $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\mathbb {D}$ is nef; for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Suppose that 1 holds. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Then we need to show that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Since modified nefness is a closed condition, after approximating $\mathbb {D}$ by nef Cartier b-divisors, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ itself is a nef Cartier b-divisor. We can then find a modification $\pi '\colon Zightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $ so that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by a nef class $\alpha $ on $Z$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is nothing but the pushforward of $\alpha $, and hence modified nef thanks to proposition 1.7.15 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . Suppose that 2 holds. We need to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to show that $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is nef for each $\epsilon >0$. After replacing $\mathbb {D}$ by the latter, we may further assume that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is big for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, and $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y$ has a uniform positive lower bound. In this case, the argument of theorem 11.1.13 shows that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some closed positive $(1,1)$-current in $\mathbb {D}_ X$. Therefore, $\mathbb {D}$ is nef, thanks to theorem 11.1.10 . $\square$ Let $\alpha $ be a modified nef class on $X$. We write $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )$ for the set of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T$ on $X$ with $T=\operatorname{Reg}T\in \alpha $ and $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Theorem 11.1.15 . There is a natural bijection from $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$ to the set of big and nef b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ with $\mathbb {D}_ X=\alpha $. Proof. Given $T\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$, we associate the b-divisor $\mathbb {D}(T)$. It is big and nef due to theorem 11.1.10 . This map clearly descends to $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$. This map is surjective by theorem 11.1.13 . Now we show that it is injective. Let $T,T'\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$. Assume that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}(T')$, we want to show that $T\sim _{\mathcal{I}} T'$. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$, it suffices to show that 11.12  egin{equation} \label{eq:nuTE} 
u (T,E)=
u (T',E). \end{equation} We may assume that $E$ is not a prime divisor on $X$, as otherwise both sides vanish. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers \[  Y\coloneqq X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}ightarrow \cdots ightarrow X_0\coloneqq X  \] so that $E$ is a prime divisor on $Y$, exceptional with respect to $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. Denote the composition by $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Thanks to proposition 11.1.1 , \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_ k,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_{k-1},\mathbb {R})\oplus \mathbb {R}\{ E_ k\} ,  \] where $E_ k=E$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. By induction, \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})\oplus  igoplus _{i=1}^{k} \mathbb {R} \{ E_ i\} ,  \] where $E_ i$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ iightarrow X_{i-1}$. Now by 7.3.10 , 11.13  egin{equation} \label{eq:RegpistarT} \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T=\pi ^*T-\sum _{i=1}^ k 
u (T,E_ i)[E_ i]. \end{equation} In particular, the cohomology class of $\operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T$ determines $
u (T,E)$. Hence, ( 11.12 ) follows. $\square$ Corollary 11.1.16 . The set of nef b-divisors over $X$ with root $\alpha $ can be naturally identified with \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} ight),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$ (with respect to the preorder of reverse domination), and given two Kähler forms $\omega \leq \omega '$ the transition map \[  \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}ightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}  \] is induced by the map $\mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )ightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')$ sending $T$ to $T+\omega '-\omega $. Proof. For each Kähler form $\omega $, theorem 11.1.15 identifies $\mathcal G(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal I}$ with the set of big and nef b-divisors whose root on $X$ is $\alpha +\{ \omega \} $. The transition map is exactly addition of $\mathbb D(\omega '-\omega )$. Passing to the inverse limit gives precisely nef b-divisors with root $\alpha $. $\square$ It is tempting to extend these results to more general currents, not necessarily non-divisorial ones. For this purpose, we introduce the following definition: Definition 11.1.17 . An augmented nef b-divisor over $X$ is a pair $(\mathbb {D},D)$, where $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$; $D$ is a formal sum \[  D=\sum _{E} c_ E E,\quad c_ E\in \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0},  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$, such that the following condition is satisfied: \[  \sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\}   \] is convergent as a sum in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. The cohomology class of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \mathbb {D}_ X+\sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R}).  \] The volume of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathbb {D},D)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Recall that we defined $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ as the set of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T\in \alpha $ in definition 1.7.3 . We introduce a further notation here: \[  \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}\coloneqq \left\{ T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha ): \operatorname{vol}T>0ight\} .  \] Corollary 11.1.18 . There is a canonical bijection between the following sets: The set $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$; the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with positive volume with cohomology class $\alpha $. More precisely, given a current $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$, we associate $(\mathbb {D},D)$ as follows: \[  \mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T),\quad D=\sum _ E 
u (T,E)E,  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$. Proof. This is a direct consequence of theorem 11.1.15 and Siu's decomposition 1.7.11 . $\square$ In fact, corollary 11.1.18 can also be reformulated in an elementary manner, without referring to b-divisors at all. Suppose that we are given a big cohomology class $\alpha $ on $X$ and a non-negative real number $c_ E$ for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$. A natural question is: When is there a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \alpha $ with positive volume such that $
u (T,E)=c_ E$ for every $E$? Then corollary 11.1.18 says that $T$ exists if and only if the following two conditions hold: \[  \lim _{\pi \colon Yightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\left( \pi ^*\alpha -\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\}  ight)>0 ootnotemark ,  \] Note. In particular, implicitly, the sum $\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\} $ converges in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$. where $\pi $ runs over all modifications of $X$; for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the class $ \pi ^*\alpha -\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\} $ is modified nef. Similarly, we have the following generalization of corollary 11.1.16 . Corollary 11.1.19 . There is a canonical bijection between the following two sets: The set of \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha +\omega )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} ight),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$; the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. Apply corollary 11.1.16 to the non-divisorial parts and use Siu's decomposition on $X$ to record the divisorial part. The convergence condition in definition 11.1.17 is exactly the condition that the roots of the non-divisorial parts converge to the prescribed cohomology class $\alpha $. $\square$ Corollary 11.1.20 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a Cartier b-divisor over $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 if and only if it is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 . Proof. We only handle the nontrivial implication. Assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 . We want to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 . After replacing $X$ by a realization of $\mathbb {D}$, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by $(X,\alpha )$ for some cohomology class $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. We first assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is big. Choose a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$. Now $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ means that for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the current $\pi ^*T$ is non-divisorial. In particular, $T$ has vanishing generic Lelong number along each prime divisor over $X$, see ( 11.13 ). Equivalently, $T$ has vanishing Lelong number everywhere. By Demailly's regularization theorem, a pseudo-effective class carrying a positive current with vanishing Lelong number at every point is nef. Hence $\alpha =\{ T\} $ is nef. In the general case, fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on the realization of $\mathbb {D}$. For every $\epsilon >0$, the Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is big and nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 , hence is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 by the big case. Thus $\alpha +\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ is nef for all $\epsilon >0$, and the closedness of the nef cone shows that $\alpha $ is nef. $\square$ Corollary 11.1.21 . Let $T$ and $T'$ be non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Suppose that $\{ T\} =\{ T'\} $. Then the following are equivalent: $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$; $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$. Proof. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers as in the proof of theorem 11.1.15 , so that $E$ appears as one of the exceptional prime divisors on the resulting model $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. By ( 11.13 ), the difference \[  \mathbb {D}(T')_ Y-\mathbb {D}(T)_ Y  \] is represented in the relative cohomology by \[  \sum _ i\left(
u (T,E_ i)-
u (T',E_ i)ight)\{ E_ i\} .  \] Using proposition 11.1.1 inductively, or equivalently the negativity lemma for exceptional classes, pseudo-effectivity of this exceptional class is equivalent to the non-negativity of all coefficients. Hence $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$ is equivalent to \[  
u (T,E)\geq 
u (T',E)  \] for every prime divisor $E$ over $X$, which is exactly $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$ by proposition 6.1.5 . $\square$ Corollary 11.1.22 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then there is a decreasing sequence of nef and big Cartier b-divisors $\mathbb {D}_ i$ over $X$ with limit $\mathbb {D}$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By theorem 11.1.13 , for each $i>0$, we can find a non-divisorial Kähler current $T_ i\in \mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ such that \[  \mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega ).  \] We observe that $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}$ have the same $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type. Indeed, applying corollary 11.1.21 to $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}+(i^{-1}-(i+1)^{-1})\omega $ shows that these two currents are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent; adding the smooth form does not change the singularity type. Let $(T_ i^ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $T_ i$ such that $T_ i^ j$ is a Kähler current in $\mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ for $j\geq j_0(i)$, and for each fixed $j$, the singularity type of $T_ i^ j$ is independent of $i$. Note that 2 is possible by using the Bergman kernel construction of the quasi-equisingular approximations, since the $T_ i$'s have the same multiplier ideals. For fixed $j$, the b-divisor \[  \mathbb {B}_ j\coloneqq \mathbb {D}(T_ i^ j)-i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )  \] is independent of $i$. Since the quasi-equisingular approximations are decreasing in $j$, the sequence $(\mathbb {B}_ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and proposition 11.1.11 gives $\mathbb {B}_ j	o \mathbb {D}$. It suffices to take $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {B}_{j_ i}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )=\mathbb {D}(T_ i^{j_ i})$, where $j_ i$ is chosen to be a sufficiently fast increasing sequence of positive integers with $j_ i\geq j_0(i)$. $\square$

title: Definition 11.1.9
text: Definition 11.1.9 . Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Given any modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we define 11.3 \begin{equation}  \mathbb {D}(T)_ Y\coloneqq \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T \right\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R}). \end{equation} We call $\mathbb {D}(T)$ the b-divisor of $T$ .

title: Theorem 11.1.10
text: Theorem 11.1.10 . Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef. Moreover, 11.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volDT} \operatorname{vol}T=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T). \end{equation} Proof. Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Step 1 . Reduce to the case where $T$ is a Kähler current. Note that $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is the Cartier b-divisor realized by $(X,\{ \omega \} )$. The b-divisors $\mathbb {D}(T+\epsilon \omega )=\mathbb {D}(T)+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ decrease to $\mathbb {D}(T)$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Hence, by 11.1.4 and proposition 7.3.4 , it suffices to prove our assertion with $T+\epsilon \omega $ in place of $T$. Step 2 . We prove the assertion under the additional assumption that $T$ has analytic singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a modification so that \[  \pi ^*T=[D]+R,  \] where $D$ is an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor on $Y$ and $R$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with locally bounded potentials. See theorem 1.6.7 for the existence of $\pi $. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is the nef Cartier b-divisor realized by $(\pi ,\{ R\} )$. Note that ( 11.4 ) is immediate in this case. Step 3 . We prove the assertion for a general Kähler current $T$. Next, take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ in the cohomology class of $T$ and write $T=\theta _{\varphi }$ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Since $T$ is a Kähler current, we choose the quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ so that, after discarding finitely many terms, each $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ is a Kähler current. This is possible by Demailly regularization, in the form used in the proof of theorem 7.1.1 . We claim that 11.5 \begin{equation} \label{eq:conv_bdiv_temp1} \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\to \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi ). \end{equation} By definition of this convergence, we need to establish the following: for every modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we have \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\right)\right\} \to \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )\right)\right\} .  \] This follows immediately from theorem 6.2.29 if $\operatorname{Sing}(\pi ^*T)$ has only finitely many components. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$. We want to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $j_0>0$ so that when $j\geq j_0$, 11.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Regpivarphij_conv_temp1} \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\right)\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )\right)\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega _ Y\} . \end{equation} Write the divisorial part of $\pi ^*\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi _ j$ and $\pi ^*\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi $ as \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i^ j [E_ i],\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i [E_ i].  \] Then $a_ i^ j\leq a_ i$. We can find an integer $N>0$ large enough so that, in the pseudo-effective order of cohomology classes, \[  \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }a_ i \{ E_ i\} \leq \frac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] By theorem 6.2.29 , we can take $j_0$ large enough so that for $j>j_0$, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{N}(a_ i-a_ i^ j)\{ E_ i\} \leq \frac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] Then ( 11.6 ) follows, and ( 11.5 ) is established. As a consequence, $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef and the volume can be computed using 11.1.4 : \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T)=\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}\left( \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)=\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)=\operatorname{vol}T.  \] Hence, ( 11.4 ) follows. $\square$
11.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volDT} \operatorname{vol}T=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T). \end{equation}
11.5 \begin{equation} \label{eq:conv_bdiv_temp1} \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\to \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi ). \end{equation}

11.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Regpivarphij_conv_temp1} \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\right)\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )\right)\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega _ Y\} . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 11.1.11
text: Proposition 11.1.11 . Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. If $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 11.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont1} \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to establish the following: 11.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont2} \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)_ Y\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right)_ Y. \end{equation} As a map from the pseudometric space $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ to the finite-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$, the continuity of $\mathbb {D}(\bullet )_ Y$ can be tested on sequences. Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume that $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a sequence and $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. It is enough to prove that every subsequence has a further subsequence for which ( 11.9 ) holds. By corollary 6.2.8 , $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Hence it suffices to prove the claim on $Y$, so we may assume that $\pi $ is the identity. Therefore, we are reduced to the following assertion: 11.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont3} \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i} \right\} \to \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi } \right\} . \end{equation} After adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may also assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. By theorem 6.2.27 , replacing all potentials by their $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes does not change the divisorial parts and preserves $d_ S$-convergence. The masses are then bounded from below along a tail, so after passing to a subsequence proposition 6.2.12 supplies increasing and decreasing envelopes $\eta _ i\leq \varphi _ i\leq \psi _ i$ which both converge to $\varphi $ in $d_ S$. Since \[  \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\eta _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\varphi _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\psi _ i})_ X,  \] it is enough to treat the case where $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is monotone. Write the divisorial parts of $\theta _{\varphi _ i}$ and $\theta _{\varphi }$ as \[  \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m^ i[D_ m],\quad \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m[D_ m].  \] By theorem 6.2.29 , $a_ m^ i\to a_ m$ for each fixed $m$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is decreasing, then $a_ m^ i\leq a_ m$ for all $i,m$. The finite-tail argument in the proof of ( 11.6 ) then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is increasing, then $a_ m\leq a_ m^ i\leq a_ m^1$. We first choose $N$ so that the tails of both $\sum _ m a_ m[D_ m]$ and $\sum _ m a_ m^1[D_ m]$ are at most $(\epsilon /3)\{ \omega \} $ in the pseudo-effective order. The convergence of the finitely many coefficients $a_ m^ i$, $m\leq N$, then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. This proves ( 11.9 ). $\square$
11.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont1} \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right). \end{equation}
11.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont2} \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)_ Y\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right)_ Y. \end{equation}
11.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Dcont3} \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i} \right\} \to \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi } \right\} . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 11.1.12
text: Lemma 11.1.12 . Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Consider non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$ currents $T,S$ on $X$ in the same cohomology class. If $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$, then $\pi _*T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi _*S$. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem B.1.6 and 6.1.18 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. By 7.3.10 , \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T,\quad \pi ^*\pi _*S=S+F_ S,  \] where $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ are effective $\pi $-exceptional divisors. Since $\{ T\} =\{ S\} $, the exceptional divisors $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ have the same cohomology class. Factoring $\pi $ into blow-ups and using proposition 11.1.1 at each step, the classes of $\pi $-exceptional prime divisors are linearly independent in the relative cohomology; hence $F_ T=F_ S$. It follows that \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}S+F_ S=\pi ^*\pi _*S.  \] Our assertion then follows from 6.1.18 . $\square$

title: Theorem 11.1.13
text: Theorem 11.1.13 . Each big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ can be realized as $\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$. Furthermore, we may always assume that $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. Fix a big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$. For each $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we take a current with minimal singularities $T_ Y$ in $\mathbb {D}_ Y$. We claim that $\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)$ coincides with $\mathbb {D}$ up to the level of $Y$: For any modification $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominated by $\pi $ through a morphism $g\colon Y\rightarrow Z$, we have \[  \mathbb {D}_ Z=\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Z.  \] The notations are summarized in the following commutative diagram: 11.10 \begin{equation} \label{eq:domi2} \gerbyimage{sgpt/e99b6d6e48f45d55c20e.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source} \end{equation} After unfolding the definitions, this means \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y).  \] Due to proposition 1.7.15 and proposition 3.2.12 , we know that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef and big. In particular, $T_ Y$ is non-divisorial, hence so is $g_*T_ Y$ by 1.7.16 . It follows from 7.3.10 that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(g_*T_ Y)=g_*T_ Y\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that 11.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:vol_unif_bound} \operatorname{vol}T_ Y\geq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0. \end{equation} Next we claim that the $P$-singularity types of the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ form a decreasing net. To see this, let us fix a diagram as ( 11.10 ). We need to show that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\preceq _ P \pi '_*T_ Z.  \] Since $T_ Z$ has minimal singularities, we have $g_*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} T_ Z$. In particular, 11.1.12 guarantees that $\pi _*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi '_*T_ Z$. But by corollary 7.3.12 and example 7.1.7 , both $\pi _*T_ Y$ and $\pi '_*T_ Z$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, so there is no difference between the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal{I}$-preorder in this case. Our assertion follows. Next observe that the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder and has a $d_ S$-limit as a consequence of ( 11.11 ) and corollary 6.2.13 . Take a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$ such that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}T.  \] It follows from proposition 11.1.11 that \[  \mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)\to \mathbb {D}(T).  \] Therefore, we conclude that \[  \mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}.  \] Thanks to theorem 11.1.10 , $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Write $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, then \[  T'\coloneqq \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] is $\mathcal{I}$-good, non-divisorial and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}(T)$. $\square$
11.10 \begin{equation} \label{eq:domi2} \gerbyimage{sgpt/e99b6d6e48f45d55c20e.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source} \end{equation}
11.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:vol_unif_bound} \operatorname{vol}T_ Y\geq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 11.1.14
text: Corollary 11.1.14 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a b-divisor over $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\mathbb {D}$ is nef; for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Suppose that 1 holds. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$. Then we need to show that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Since modified nefness is a closed condition, after approximating $\mathbb {D}$ by nef Cartier b-divisors, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ itself is a nef Cartier b-divisor. We can then find a modification $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $ so that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by a nef class $\alpha $ on $Z$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is nothing but the pushforward of $\alpha $, and hence modified nef thanks to proposition 1.7.15 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . Suppose that 2 holds. We need to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to show that $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is nef for each $\epsilon >0$. After replacing $\mathbb {D}$ by the latter, we may further assume that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is big for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, and $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y$ has a uniform positive lower bound. In this case, the argument of theorem 11.1.13 shows that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some closed positive $(1,1)$-current in $\mathbb {D}_ X$. Therefore, $\mathbb {D}$ is nef, thanks to theorem 11.1.10 . $\square$

title: Theorem 11.1.15
text:
Theorem 11.1.15 . There is a natural bijection from $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$ to the set of big and nef b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ with $\mathbb {D}_ X=\alpha $. Proof. Given $T\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$, we associate the b-divisor $\mathbb {D}(T)$. It is big and nef due to theorem 11.1.10 . This map clearly descends to $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$. This map is surjective by theorem 11.1.13 . Now we show that it is injective. Let $T,T'\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$. Assume that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}(T')$, we want to show that $T\sim _{\mathcal{I}} T'$. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$, it suffices to show that 11.12  egin{equation} \label{eq:nuTE} 
u (T,E)=
u (T',E). \end{equation} We may assume that $E$ is not a prime divisor on $X$, as otherwise both sides vanish. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers \[  Y\coloneqq X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}ightarrow \cdots ightarrow X_0\coloneqq X  \] so that $E$ is a prime divisor on $Y$, exceptional with respect to $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. Denote the composition by $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Thanks to proposition 11.1.1 , \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_ k,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_{k-1},\mathbb {R})\oplus \mathbb {R}\{ E_ k\} ,  \] where $E_ k=E$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. By induction, \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})\oplus  igoplus _{i=1}^{k} \mathbb {R} \{ E_ i\} ,  \] where $E_ i$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ iightarrow X_{i-1}$. Now by 7.3.10 , 11.13  egin{equation} \label{eq:RegpistarT} \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T=\pi ^*T-\sum _{i=1}^ k 
u (T,E_ i)[E_ i]. \end{equation} In particular, the cohomology class of $\operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T$ determines $
u (T,E)$. Hence, ( 11.12 ) follows. $\square$
11.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:nuTE} \nu (T,E)=\nu (T',E). \end{equation}
11.13 \begin{equation} \label{eq:RegpistarT} \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T=\pi ^*T-\sum _{i=1}^ k \nu (T,E_ i)[E_ i]. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 11.1.16
text: Corollary 11.1.16 . The set of nef b-divisors over $X$ with root $\alpha $ can be naturally identified with \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \right),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$ (with respect to the preorder of reverse domination), and given two Kähler forms $\omega \leq \omega '$ the transition map \[  \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\rightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}  \] is induced by the map $\mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )\rightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')$ sending $T$ to $T+\omega '-\omega $. Proof. For each Kähler form $\omega $, theorem 11.1.15 identifies $\mathcal G(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal I}$ with the set of big and nef b-divisors whose root on $X$ is $\alpha +\{ \omega \} $. The transition map is exactly addition of $\mathbb D(\omega '-\omega )$. Passing to the inverse limit gives precisely nef b-divisors with root $\alpha $. $\square$

title: Definition 11.1.17
text: Definition 11.1.17 . An augmented nef b-divisor over $X$ is a pair $(\mathbb {D},D)$, where $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$; $D$ is a formal sum \[  D=\sum _{E} c_ E E,\quad c_ E\in \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0},  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$, such that the following condition is satisfied: \[  \sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\}   \] is convergent as a sum in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. The cohomology class of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \mathbb {D}_ X+\sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R}).  \] The volume of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathbb {D},D)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \]

title: Corollary 11.1.18
text: Corollary 11.1.18 . There is a canonical bijection between the following sets: The set $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$; the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with positive volume with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. This is a direct consequence of theorem 11.1.15 and Siu's decomposition 1.7.11 . $\square$

title: Corollary 11.1.19
text: Corollary 11.1.19 . There is a canonical bijection between the following two sets: The set of \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha +\omega )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \right),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$; the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. Apply corollary 11.1.16 to the non-divisorial parts and use Siu's decomposition on $X$ to record the divisorial part. The convergence condition in definition 11.1.17 is exactly the condition that the roots of the non-divisorial parts converge to the prescribed cohomology class $\alpha $. $\square$

title: Corollary 11.1.20
text: Corollary 11.1.20 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a Cartier b-divisor over $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 if and only if it is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 . Proof. We only handle the nontrivial implication. Assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 . We want to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 . After replacing $X$ by a realization of $\mathbb {D}$, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by $(X,\alpha )$ for some cohomology class $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. We first assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is big. Choose a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$. Now $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ means that for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the current $\pi ^*T$ is non-divisorial. In particular, $T$ has vanishing generic Lelong number along each prime divisor over $X$, see ( 11.13 ). Equivalently, $T$ has vanishing Lelong number everywhere. By Demailly's regularization theorem, a pseudo-effective class carrying a positive current with vanishing Lelong number at every point is nef. Hence $\alpha =\{ T\} $ is nef. In the general case, fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on the realization of $\mathbb {D}$. For every $\epsilon >0$, the Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is big and nef in the sense of definition 11.1.8 , hence is nef in the sense of definition 11.1.7 by the big case. Thus $\alpha +\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ is nef for all $\epsilon >0$, and the closedness of the nef cone shows that $\alpha $ is nef. $\square$

title: Corollary 11.1.21
text:
Corollary 11.1.21 . Let $T$ and $T'$ be non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Suppose that $\{ T\} =\{ T'\} $. Then the following are equivalent: $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$; $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$. Proof. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers as in the proof of theorem 11.1.15 , so that $E$ appears as one of the exceptional prime divisors on the resulting model $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. By ( 11.13 ), the difference \[  \mathbb {D}(T')_ Y-\mathbb {D}(T)_ Y  \] is represented in the relative cohomology by \[  \sum _ i\left(
u (T,E_ i)-
u (T',E_ i)ight)\{ E_ i\} .  \] Using proposition 11.1.1 inductively, or equivalently the negativity lemma for exceptional classes, pseudo-effectivity of this exceptional class is equivalent to the non-negativity of all coefficients. Hence $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$ is equivalent to \[  
u (T,E)\geq 
u (T',E)  \] for every prime divisor $E$ over $X$, which is exactly $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$ by proposition 6.1.5 . $\square$

title: Corollary 11.1.22
text: Corollary 11.1.22 . Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then there is a decreasing sequence of nef and big Cartier b-divisors $\mathbb {D}_ i$ over $X$ with limit $\mathbb {D}$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By theorem 11.1.13 , for each $i>0$, we can find a non-divisorial Kähler current $T_ i\in \mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ such that \[  \mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega ).  \] We observe that $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}$ have the same $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type. Indeed, applying corollary 11.1.21 to $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}+(i^{-1}-(i+1)^{-1})\omega $ shows that these two currents are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent; adding the smooth form does not change the singularity type. Let $(T_ i^ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $T_ i$ such that $T_ i^ j$ is a Kähler current in $\mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ for $j\geq j_0(i)$, and for each fixed $j$, the singularity type of $T_ i^ j$ is independent of $i$. Note that 2 is possible by using the Bergman kernel construction of the quasi-equisingular approximations, since the $T_ i$'s have the same multiplier ideals. For fixed $j$, the b-divisor \[  \mathbb {B}_ j\coloneqq \mathbb {D}(T_ i^ j)-i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )  \] is independent of $i$. Since the quasi-equisingular approximations are decreasing in $j$, the sequence $(\mathbb {B}_ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and proposition 11.1.11 gives $\mathbb {B}_ j\to \mathbb {D}$. It suffices to take $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {B}_{j_ i}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )=\mathbb {D}(T_ i^{j_ i})$, where $j_ i$ is chosen to be a sufficiently fast increasing sequence of positive integers with $j_ i\geq j_0(i)$. $\square$

title: 11.2 Properties of the intersection product
text: 11.2 Properties of the intersection product Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Recall that the mixed volume of currents is studied in section 7.3 . Definition 11.2.1 . Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as \[  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n),  \] where $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents in $\mathbb {D}_{1,X},\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_{n,X}$ respectively such that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_{i}$. The definition makes sense thanks to theorem 11.1.13 . It does not depend on the choices of $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ since they are uniquely defined up to $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence, as proved in theorem 11.1.15 . Lemma 11.2.2 . The product in definition 11.2.1 is symmetric in its $n$ variables. Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n,\mathbb {D}'_1$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1+\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+\left(\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$. Then \[  \left(\lambda \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\lambda \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_1\leq \mathbb {D}'$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq \left(\mathbb {D}',\mathbb {D}_2,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Proof. 1 , 2 and 3 follow immediately from the corresponding results for mixed volumes, as proved in proposition 7.3.4 . 4 Take $\mathcal{I}$-good non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ and $T'$ so that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}'$. Furthermore, we may assume that the $T_ i$'s and $T'$ are Kähler currents by the perturbation argument. Let $(T_{i}^ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $T_ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$. It follows from theorem 6.2.17 that \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n=\lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] It suffices to show that for all $j\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j\leq \int _ X T'\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] Therefore, we have reduced to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have analytic singularities. After a resolution, we may assume that they have log singularities along $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors. By proposition 7.3.4 5 , we can further reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have bounded local potentials. Perturbing $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ by a Kähler form, we may further assume that $\{ T_2\} ,\ldots , \{ T_ n\} $ are Kähler classes. By proposition 7.3.4 4 , we finally reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ are Kähler forms. In this case, the assertion follows from the pseudo-effectivity of $\{ T'\} -\{ T_1\} $. $\square$ In general, we can extend the definition of the intersection product to nef b-divisors as follows: Definition 11.2.3 . Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as 11.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mixed_product_limit_def} \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$. Note that as $\epsilon \to 0+$, $\left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)$ is decreasing, as a consequence of 11.2.2 4 . Similarly, by 11.2.2 4 again, the definition is independent of the choice of $\omega $. Proposition 11.2.4 . The product in definition 11.2.3 is symmetric in its $n$ variables. Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n,\mathbb {D}'_1$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1+\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+\left(\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$. Then \[  \left(\lambda \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\lambda \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_1\leq \mathbb {D}'$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq \left(\mathbb {D}',\mathbb {D}_2,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}(T_1),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}(T_ n) \Bigr )= \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] Proof. 1 , 2 , 3 and 4 These are immediate consequences of the corresponding results in the big and nef case established in 11.2.2 . 5 By ( 7.21 ) and ( 11.14 ), we may assume that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are Kähler currents. In this case, the assertion follows from the definitions. $\square$ Lemma 11.2.5 . Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Fix a compact set $K\subseteq \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_{i,X}\in K$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then there is a constant $C$ depending only on $X,K,\{ \omega \} $ such that for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$, we have \[  0\leq \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr )-\left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq C\epsilon .  \] Proof. By 11.2.2 4 , the left-hand side is non-negative. For the upper bound, by the multi-linearity of the product proved in proposition 11.2.4 , we can rewrite the difference as a sum of $2^ n-1$ terms like \[  \epsilon ^{m} \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}(\omega )^{m}, \mathbb {D}_{i_1},\ldots , \mathbb {D}_{i_{n-m}} \Bigr ),  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. We need to show that these coefficients are uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on the given data. For this purpose, we add $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ to each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ and then replace $K$ by $K+\{ \omega \} $. Therefore, we reduce to the case where each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ is nef and big, and hence $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {D}(T_ i)$ for some $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes. Then we need to bound \[  \int _ X \omega ^ m\wedge T_{i_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{i_{n-m}}.  \] For this purpose, let $D\geq 0$ be the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} -\alpha $ is nef for any $\alpha \in K$. Then the integral is bounded by the cohomological intersection $\{ \omega \} ^ m\cap (D\{ \omega \} )^{n-m}$. Our assertion follows. $\square$ We first make a consistency check. Proposition 11.2.6 . Suppose that $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then \[  \left( \mathbb {D},\ldots ,\mathbb {D} \right)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Proof. Using 11.2.5 and 11.1.4 , we may easily reduce to the case where $\mathbb {D}$ is nef and big. In this case, take a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ in $\mathbb {D}_ X$ such that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}$. Then we need to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}=\operatorname{vol}T,  \] which is proved in theorem 11.1.10 . $\square$ Proposition 11.2.7 . Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\right)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, our assertion follows from proposition 7.3.8 . $\square$ Proposition 11.2.8 . The product in definition 11.2.3 is upper semicontinuous in the following sense. Suppose that $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ are nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 11.15 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limsupint_prod} \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right)\leq \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that the $\mathbb D_ i^ j$'s and the $\mathbb D_ i$'s are all big. Choose $\mathcal I$-good non-divisorial currents $T_ i^ j$ and $T_ i$ such that $\mathbb D(T_ i^ j)=\mathbb D_ i^ j$ and $\mathbb D(T_ i)=\mathbb D_ i$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and fix $\epsilon >0$. Since $\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j\to \mathbb D_{i,X}$, for all sufficiently large $j$ the class \[  \mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} -\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j  \] is Kähler. Choose a Kähler form $\chi _ i^ j$ in this class and set $S_ i^ j=T_ i^ j+\chi _ i^ j$. Then $S_ i^ j$ lies in the fixed class $\mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ and has the same divisorial Lelong numbers as $T_ i^ j$. Hence, by theorem 7.3.13 and proposition 7.3.4 2 , \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (T_1^ j,\ldots ,T_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (S_1^ j,\ldots ,S_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right).  \] Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\Bigl (\mathbb D_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \Bigl (\mathbb D_1+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega )\Bigr ).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ gives ( 11.15 ). Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then by 11.2.5 , for any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right) \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 11.2.9 . The product in definition 11.2.3 is continuous along decreasing nets in each variable. In other words, if $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) are decreasing nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$, then \[  \lim _{j\in J} \left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j\right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n\right).  \] Proof. This is a straightforward consequence of 11.2.2 4 and proposition 11.2.8 . $\square$ Remark 11.2.10 . The algebraic nef b-divisors are introduced by Dang–Favre [ DF20 ] , as their intersection theory. It is a straightforward application of the results proved in this section that our transcendental intersection theory coincides with theirs in the algebraic setting.

title: Proposition 11.2.6
text: Proposition 11.2.6 . Suppose that $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then \[  \left( \mathbb {D},\ldots ,\mathbb {D} \right)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Proof. title: Proposition 11.2.7
text: Proposition 11.2.7 . Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\right)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, our assertion follows from proposition 7.3.8 . $\square$

title: Proposition 11.2.8
text: Proposition 11.2.8 . The product in definition 11.2.3 is upper semicontinuous in the following sense. Suppose that $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ are nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 11.15 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limsupint_prod} \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right)\leq \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that the $\mathbb D_ i^ j$'s and the $\mathbb D_ i$'s are all big. Choose $\mathcal I$-good non-divisorial currents $T_ i^ j$ and $T_ i$ such that $\mathbb D(T_ i^ j)=\mathbb D_ i^ j$ and $\mathbb D(T_ i)=\mathbb D_ i$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and fix $\epsilon >0$. Since $\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j\to \mathbb D_{i,X}$, for all sufficiently large $j$ the class \[  \mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} -\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j  \] is Kähler. Choose a Kähler form $\chi _ i^ j$ in this class and set $S_ i^ j=T_ i^ j+\chi _ i^ j$. Then $S_ i^ j$ lies in the fixed class $\mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ and has the same divisorial Lelong numbers as $T_ i^ j$. Hence, by theorem 7.3.13 and proposition 7.3.4 2 , \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (T_1^ j,\ldots ,T_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (S_1^ j,\ldots ,S_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right).  \] Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\Bigl (\mathbb D_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \Bigl (\mathbb D_1+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega )\Bigr ).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ gives ( 11.15 ). Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then by 11.2.5 , for any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right) \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$
11.15 \begin{equation} \label{eq:limsupint_prod} \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right)\leq \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 11.2.9
text: Proposition 11.2.9 . The product in definition 11.2.3 is continuous along decreasing nets in each variable. In other words, if $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) are decreasing nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$, then \[  \lim _{j\in J} \left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j\right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n\right).  \] Proof. This is a straightforward consequence of 11.2.2 4 and proposition 11.2.8 . $\square$

title: Remark 11.2.10
text: Remark 11.2.10 . The algebraic nef b-divisors are introduced by Dang–Favre [ DF20 ] , as their intersection theory. It is a straightforward application of the results proved in this section that our transcendental intersection theory coincides with theirs in the algebraic setting.

title: 3 Applications
text:
3 Applications The three chapters of this part apply the singularity theory developed earlier to three rather different settings: big toric geometry, non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and partial Bergman kernels. They are largely independent of one another, and each uses a different part of the machinery built in the preceding chapters. chapter 12 extends the toric dictionary of chapter 5 from ample line bundles to big toric line bundles. In the big case, identifying the Newton body is no longer as simple as in the ample setting, and the behavior of potentials along toric strata becomes more delicate. The chapter establishes the toric-convex dictionary using the theory of partial Okounkov bodies developed in chapter 10 . chapter 13 develops a non-Archimedean pluripotential theory on compact Kähler manifolds. The basic objects are inverse systems of $\mathcal I$-model test curves, and the operations on test curves from section 9.4 provide the corresponding algebra of non-Archimedean potentials. The chapter constructs Duistermaat–Heckman measures and proves a comparison theorem identifying the resulting space with the Boucksom–Jonsson space of non-Archimedean psh metrics in the projective setting. chapter 14 proves the convergence of partial Bergman kernels. Given a singular $\theta $-psh potential, a closed non-pluripolar weighted subset $(K,v)$ and a Bernstein–Markov measure, the normalized partial Bergman measure converges weakly to the corresponding partial equilibrium measure. The proof combines the envelope theory of chapter 3 and the asymptotic Riemann–Roch theorem theorem 7.4.2 . It extends the theorem of Berman–Boucksom–Witt Nyström [ BBWN11 ] to the singular relative setting considered here. The prerequisites for the three chapters are different. The big toric chapter uses basic toric geometry, for which [ CLS11 ] and [ Fultor ] are standard references. The non-Archimedean chapter is best read with the Boucksom–Jonsson theory in mind, especially [ BJ22 ] . The Bergman kernel chapter is closest in spirit to [ BBWN11 ] . These references are not logically required for following the arguments, but they provide useful context. He is considered one of the greatest mathematicians of all time and a pioneer of several modern mathematical fields. He also played a key role in the development of special relativity, and was one of the first to understand the deep connection between mathematics and physics. , L'avenir des mathématiques

title: 12 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
search_title: Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: 12 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles This chapter extends the toric pluripotential theory of chapter 5 from ample toric line bundles to big toric line bundles. Let $L=\mathcal O_ X(D)$ be a big toric line bundle on a smooth projective toric variety $X$, and let $P_ D\subseteq M_{\mathbb R}$ be the polytope associated with the toric divisor $D$. In the ample case, $P_ D$ is a smooth lattice polytope and its faces correspond directly to toric strata. This direct correspondence breaks down. This is the main new feature of the chapter. The first goal is to recover a usable toric-convex dictionary in this more flexible setting. We begin by recalling the big toric setup, the Cartier data of $D$, and the stable base locus. We then compare the Newton body of a toric psh metric with its partial Okounkov body. The main computation, theorem 12.2.9 , identifies the partial Okounkov body of a toric singularity with its Newton body, up to the natural affine transformation determined by the chosen toric flag. This result is the bridge between the general Okounkov-body theory of chapter 10 and the explicit convex geometry of toric metrics. Once this comparison is established, several pluripotential-theoretic consequences follow. The Newton body computes non-pluripolar mass, describes Lelong numbers along toric divisors, and gives an explicit description of the potential with minimal singularities. In this way the abstract constructions of previous chapters become concrete convex-geometric statements in the toric setting. The second half of the chapter develops the full toric pluripotential theory in a big class. Toric $\theta $-psh potentials are identified with proper convex functions on $N_{\mathbb R}$ satisfying the appropriate growth condition determined by $P_ D$. Under this correspondence, sums, rooftop envelopes, suprema, decreasing limits and $P$-equivalence all have convex interpretations. We also describe toric subgeodesics, geodesics and the toric Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. The final sections study restriction and intersection theory in the toric setting. The trace operator along toric strata is computed by slicing Newton bodies, and its volume formula becomes a statement about the Euclidean volume of faces and slices. We also prove a mixed-volume formula for Newton bodies and recover the augmented base locus from the convex data. Throughout the chapter we use the notation and conventions of chapter 5 . The partial Okounkov body machinery of chapter 10 is used repeatedly.

Recall that $T_ c$ is the compact torus contained in $T(\mathbb {C})$. Consider a rational polyhedral fan $\Sigma $ in $N_{\mathbb {R}}$ corresponding to an $n$-dimensional smooth projective toric variety $X$. Let \[  D=\sum _{ho \in \Sigma (1)} a_{ho }D_{ho }  \] be a $T$-invariant integral big divisor on $X$. Let $P_ D\subseteq M_{\mathbb {R}}$ be the following polytope Note. Note that $P_ D$ is not necessarily a lattice polytope, see [ Example 10.5.4 , CLS11 ] . In fact, any rational polytope with positive volume can be realized in this manner. 12.1  egin{equation} \label{eq:bigPrep} P_ D=\left\{  m\in M_{\mathbb {R}}: \langle m,u_{ho }angle \geq -a_{ho }\quad  orall ho \in \Sigma (1)ight\} . \end{equation} Since we have assumed that $D$ is big, $P_ D$ is $n$-dimensional. Let $L=\mathcal{O}_ X(D)$. Note that replacing $D$ by a linearly equivalent divisor amounts to replacing $P_ D$ by an integral translation. Recall that for each $ho \in \Sigma (1)$, $u_{ho }$ denotes the ray generator of $ho $. Let $\{ m_{\sigma }\} _{\sigma \in \Sigma }$ denote the Cartier data associated with $D$. In other words, for each $\sigma \in \Sigma $, $m_{\sigma }\in M$ satisfies that \[  \langle m_{\sigma },u_{ho } angle =-a_{ho },\quad  orall ho \in \sigma (1).  \] The element $m_{\sigma }\in M$ is well-defined modulo 12.2  egin{equation} \label{eq:Msigmadef} M(\sigma )\coloneqq \sigma ^{\perp }\cap M, \end{equation} where \[  \sigma ^{\perp }\coloneqq \left\{  m\in M_{\mathbb {R}} : \langle m,uangle =0 \quad  orall u\in \sigma ight\} .  \] Moreover, if $	au $ is a face of $\sigma $, then 12.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:Cartierdatalowdim} m_{\sigma }\equiv m_{	au } \mod M(	au ). \end{equation} See [ Theorem 4.2.8 , CLS11 ] . In particular, for an $n$-dimensional $\sigma \in \Sigma $, the element $m_{\sigma }$ is uniquely determined. In general, for $\sigma \in \Sigma (n)$, one need not have $m_{\sigma }\in P_ D$. In fact, $m_{\sigma }\in P_ D$ for all $\sigma \in \Sigma (n)$ if and only if $D$ is base-point free. See [ Theorem 6.1.7 , CLS11 ] . Note that for any $n$-dimensional cone $\sigma $ in $\Sigma $ and any $ho \in \sigma (1)$, we have 12.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:mmsigpos} \langle m-m_{\sigma },u_{ho } angle \geq 0,\quad  orall m\in P_ D, \end{equation} as a consequence of ( 12.1 ) and the choice of $m_\sigma $. See [ Proposition 4.1.2 , CLS11 ] . Next consider a $T$-invariant irreducible subvariety $Y\subseteq X$. Since $X$ is smooth, so is $Y$. Let $\sigma $ be the cone in $\Sigma $ corresponding to $Y$. We observe that $\sigma $ corresponds to a (possibly empty) face $Q_{\sigma }$ of $P_ D$: 12.6  egin{equation} \label{eq:Qsigma} Q_{\sigma }=\left\{ m\in P_ D: \langle m,u_{ho }angle =-a_{ho }\quad  orall ho \in \sigma (1) ight\} . \end{equation} The dimension of $\sigma $ is not necessarily equal to the codimension of $Q$ as we will see in example 12.1.4 . We have the following characterization of the base locus of $D$. We are not aware of a direct reference; the result is likely folklore. Proposition 12.1.1 . The base locus $\operatorname{Bs}(D)$ (with the reduced complex structure) of $D$ is a toric-invariant (possibly reducible) subvariety given by the union of $V(	au )$, where $	au $ runs over elements in $\Sigma $ satisfying the following condition: 12.7  egin{equation} \label{eq:arhononcrit} a_{ho }+\langle m, u_{ho }angle >0\quad 	extup{for some }ho \in 	au (1) \end{equation} for each $m\in M\cap P_ D$. Here $V(	au )$ denotes the toric subvariety of $X$ corresponding to $	au $. In other words, \[  V(	au )= igcap _{ho \in 	au (1)} D_{ho }.  \] Proof. Recall that \[  \mathrm{H}^0(X,L)\cong  igoplus _{m\in M\cap P_ D} \mathbb {C}\chi ^ m.  \] See [ Proposition 4.3.3 , CLS11 ] for example. So we only need to understand the common zeros of $D+\operatorname{div}\chi ^ m$ for all $m\in M\cap P_ D$. But we know that \[  D+\operatorname{div}\chi ^ m=\sum _{ho \in \Sigma (1)} \left( a_{ho }+\langle m, u_{ho }angle ight) D_{ho }.  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$ Corollary 12.1.2 . The stable base locus (with the reduced complex structure) of $D$ is a toric-invariant (possibly reducible) subvariety given by the union of the $V(	au )$'s, where $	au $ runs over elements in $\Sigma $ satisfying ( 12.7 ) for each $m\in P_ D$. Geometrically, the condition means $Q_{	au }=\varnothing $. Proof. It follows from proposition 12.1.1 that the stable base locus of $D$ is given by the union of the $V(	au )$'s, where $	au $ runs over elements of $\Sigma $ satisfying ( 12.7 ) for all $m\in M_{\mathbb {Q}}\cap P_ D$. That is, \[  M_{\mathbb {Q}}\cap \left\{  m\in P_ D : a_{ho }+\langle m, u_{ho }angle =0\quad  orall ho \in 	au (1) ight\} =\varnothing .  \] Since the latter part is a rational polytope, this statement is equivalent to 12.8  egin{equation} \label{eq:PDcapvarnot} \left\{  m\in P_ D : a_{ho }+\langle m, u_{ho }angle =0\quad  orall ho \in 	au (1) ight\} =\varnothing . \end{equation} Our first assertion follows. $\square$ We will keep two examples in mind. Example 12.1.3 . In this case, $\Sigma $ is the fan in 12.1 consisting of three $2$-dimensional cones $\sigma _1$, $\sigma _2$ and $\sigma _3$; three $1$-dimensional cones $\sigma _4$, $\sigma _5$ and $\sigma _6$; one $0$-dimensional cone $\sigma _0$. 12.1 The fan $\Sigma $ of $\mathbb {P}^2$. The three rays $\sigma _4,\sigma _5,\sigma _6\in \Sigma (1)$ subdivide $N_{\mathbb {R}}$ into three full-dimensional cones $\sigma _1,\sigma _2,\sigma _3\in \Sigma (2)$; the origin is the unique cone of dimension zero. The fan $\Sigma $ is just the fan of $X=\mathbb {P}^2$. Under the orbit-cone correspondence, we have \[   egin{aligned}  D_{\sigma _1}=&  \{ [1:0:0]\} ,\quad D_{\sigma _2}=\{ [0:1:0]\} ,\quad D_{\sigma _3}=\{ [0:0:1]\} ,\  D_{\sigma _4}=&  \{ [0:X_1:X_2]:(X_1,X_2)
