title: Corollary 12.3.11
section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: Corollary 12.3.11 . Let $\varphi _0,\varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )\cap \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the following are equivalent: $\varphi _0\sim _ P \varphi _1$; there is a subgeodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. If these conditions are satisfied, let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Then $\varphi _ t\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )$ for all $t\in (0,1)$ and 12.67 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Glinear} G_{\varphi _ t}=(1-t)G_{\varphi _0}+tG_{\varphi _1}. \end{equation} Proof. The equivalence between 1 and 2 follows from a general fact theorem 6.1.23 . In the toric case, 2 $\implies $ 1 can also be argued more directly. Assume that these conditions are satisfied. Let $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in (0,1)}$ be the geodesic from $\varphi _0$ to $\varphi _1$. Since the geodesic is the upper envelope of toric subgeodesics, $\varphi _ t\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )$ for all $t\in (0,1)$. Let $\Psi '$ be the proper convex function on $M_{\mathbb {R}}\times \mathbb {R}$ defined by corollary 12.3.10 . Then $\Psi '$ is the minimum of all $\Psi $ satisfying ( 12.50 ). We claim that 12.68 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Psiptemp1} \Psi '(m,s)=G_{\varphi _0}(m)\lor \left(G_{\varphi _1}(m)+s\right). \end{equation} It suffices to show that the right-hand side is proper, namely, $G_{\varphi _0}\lor G_{\varphi _1}$ is not identically $\infty $. But recall that by proposition 4.1.6 , we have $\varphi _0\land \varphi _1\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Therefore, by proposition 12.3.4 , \[  G_{\varphi _0}\lor G_{\varphi _1}=G_{\varphi _0\land \varphi _1}\not\equiv \infty .  \] In particular, ( 12.68 ) follows. Now by construction, \[  G_{\varphi _ t}(m)=\inf _{s\in \mathbb {R}} \left( \Psi '(m,s)-st\right)=(1-t)G_{\varphi _0}(m)+tG_{\varphi _1}(m)  \] for all $t\in (0,1)$. So ( 12.67 ) follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 12.3.12
section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: Corollary 12.3.12 . There is a canonical bijection between the following sets: The set of $\ell \in \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$; The set of proper closed convex functions $g$ on $M_{\mathbb {R}}$ with $\overline{\operatorname{Dom}g}=\Delta (\theta ,\phi )$. Moreover, given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, then 12.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:geod_ray_G} G_{\ell _ t}=G_{\phi }+tg,\quad \forall t>0. \end{equation} Proof. First observe that given $g$ as in 2 , ( 12.69 ) indeed induces a geodesic ray in $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ thanks to corollary 12.3.11 . Therefore, we have a map from 2 to 1 . Conversely, given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, it follows from corollary 12.3.11 that $G_{\ell _ t}$ is linear in $t\geq 0$ after restriction to $\operatorname{Int}\{ G_{\phi }<\infty \} $. Let \[  g'(m)= \begin{cases}  G_{\ell _1}(m)-G_{\phi }(m),&  m\in \operatorname{Int}\{ G_{\phi }<\infty \} ;\\  \infty ,&  m\in M_{\mathbb {R}}\setminus \operatorname{Int}\{ G_{\phi }<\infty \} . \end{cases}  \] Note that for $m\in \operatorname{Int}\{ G_{\phi }<\infty \} $, we actually have \[  g'(m)=\lim _{t\to \infty }t^{-1}G_{\ell _ t}(m).  \] Hence, $g'$ is a proper convex function on $M_{\mathbb {R}}$. Define $g=\operatorname{cl}g'$. Then $g$ is a proper closed convex function on $M_{\mathbb {R}}$, and $\overline{\operatorname{Dom}g}=\Delta (\theta ,\phi )$. We have therefore a map from 1 to 2 . It remains to argue that this map is the converse of the preceding map from 2 to 1 . The non-trivial point is to verify ( 12.69 ) holds for the $g$ we just constructed. Fix $t>0$. We need to show that \[  G_{\ell _ t}=G_{\phi }+tg.  \] This holds on $\operatorname{Int}\{ G_{\phi }<\infty \} $ by corollary 12.3.11 and the definition of $g$, but then it holds everywhere thanks to proposition A.1.16 . Our assertion follows. $\square$

section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: 12.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:geod_ray_G} G_{\ell _ t}=G_{\phi }+tg,\quad \forall t>0. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 12.3.13
section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: Corollary 12.3.13 . Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and $g$ be the function as in corollary 12.3.12 . Then 12.72 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ellmax_temp1} \ell ^*_{\max }=-\inf _{M_{\mathbb {R}}} g, \end{equation} and for each $\tau <-\inf _{M_{\mathbb {R}}} g$, the function $\ell ^*_{\tau }$ is toric-invariant, and \[  G_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}(m)=\begin{cases}  G_{\phi }(m),& \textup{if }g(m)\leq -\tau ;\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}  \] In particular, for such $\tau $, \[  \Delta \left(\theta , \ell ^*_{\tau }\right)=\left\{ g\leq -\tau \right\} .  \] Proof. Fix $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }=\inf _{t>0} \left(\ell _ t-t\tau \right)  \] is clearly toric-invariant. Therefore, \[  F_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}=\inf _{t>0} \left(F_{\ell _ t}-t\tau \right).  \] Fix $m\in M_{\mathbb {R}}$. We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  G_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}(m)=&  \sup _{n\in N_{\mathbb {R}}}\left( \langle m, n\rangle -F_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}(n) \right)\\  =&  \sup _{t>0}\sup _{n\in N_{\mathbb {R}}}\left( \langle m, n\rangle - F_{\ell _ t}(n) +t\tau \right)\\  =& \sup _{t>0} \left(G_{\ell _ t}(m)+t\tau \right)\\  =&  G_{\phi }(m)+\sup _{t>0} t\left(g(m)+\tau \right)\\  =& \begin{cases}  G_{\phi }(m),& \textup{if }g(m)+\tau \leq 0;\\  \infty ,& \textup{otherwise}. \end{cases}\end{aligned}  \] Our assertions follow. $\square$

Corollary 12.3.15 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,	heta )$, we have 12.93  egin{equation} \label{eq:volTr_tor} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)=(\dim Y)!\operatorname{vol}_{\dim Y} \Bigl (\Delta (	heta ,\varphi )\cap Q_{\sigma }\Bigr ). \end{equation} Proof. If $
u (\varphi ,Y)>0$, then by corollary 12.2.11 , $\Delta (	heta ,\varphi )\cap Q_\sigma =\varnothing $. By convention the right-hand side of ( 12.93 ) is $0$, and the trace is not defined, so the left-hand side is $0$. Assume now that $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Take a toric-invariant ample line bundle $H$ on $X$ and a toric-invariant Kähler metric $\omega \in c_1(H)$. For $\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}$, write $Q_{\sigma ,\epsilon }$ for the face corresponding to $\sigma $ for the divisor $D+\epsilon H$, with the same convention on the Cartier datum along $\sigma $. Since $	heta _{\varphi }+\epsilon \omega $ is a toric Kähler current and $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$, its trace along $Y$ is defined and has positive volume. Hence theorem 12.3.14 gives \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon \omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta +\epsilon \omega }(\varphi )ight)= (\dim Y)!\operatorname{vol}_{\dim Y} \Bigl (\Delta (	heta +\epsilon \omega ,\varphi )\cap Q_{\sigma ,\epsilon }\Bigr ).  \] By A.3.7 , \[  \Delta (	heta +\epsilon \omega ,\varphi )=\Delta (	heta ,\varphi )+\epsilon P_ H.  \] We choose the Cartier datum of $D+\epsilon H$ along $\sigma $ to be the sum of the chosen datum of $D$ and $\epsilon $ times the chosen datum of $H$. With this convention, the face of $P_ D+\epsilon P_ H$ corresponding to $\sigma $ is $Q_\sigma +\epsilon Q_\sigma ^ H$. In particular, \[  \Delta (	heta +\epsilon \omega ,\varphi )\cap Q_{\sigma ,\epsilon }=(\Delta (	heta ,\varphi )\cap Q_{\sigma })+\epsilon Q^ H_{\sigma },  \] where $Q^ H_{\sigma }$ denotes the corresponding face of the polytope of $H$. Indeed, the defining inequalities along the rays of $\sigma $ are non-negative on both summands, so equality for their sum forces equality on each summand. By example 8.1.12 , the left-hand side converges to \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^	heta (\varphi )ight),  \] with the convention that this limit is $0$ when the trace in the limiting class is not defined. title: Theorem 12.3.18
section: 18.4 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: Theorem 12.3.18 . Take $T$-invariant big divisors $D_1,\ldots ,D_ n$ on $X$. Consider $T_ c$-invariant closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_ i$ in $c_1(\mathcal{O}_ X(D_ i))$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 12.94 \begin{equation} \label{eq:mixvol_pob} n! \operatorname{vol}\Bigl ( \Delta (T_1),\ldots ,\Delta (T_ n) \Bigr )=\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n \right). \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to prove the following assertion: 12.95 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Delta_add} \Delta (T_1+T_2)=\Delta (T_1)+\Delta (T_2).\footnotemark \end{equation} Note. This is slightly problematic when $n=1$, since $T_2$ is not defined stricto sensu . We take $D_2,T_2$ satisfying the same assumptions as $D_1,T_1$ in this case. In fact, assuming this, by induction, for each tuple of non-negative integers $C_1,\ldots ,C_ n$, we have \[  \Delta \left( \sum _{i=1}^ n C_ i T_ i \right)=\sum _{i=1}^ n C_ i \Delta (T_ i).  \] Comparing the volumes, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Delta \left( \sum _{i=1}^ n C_ i T_ i \right)=\sum _{i_1,\ldots ,i_ n=1}^ n C_{i_1}\cdots C_{i_ n} \operatorname{vol}\left(\Delta \left(T_{i_1}\right),\ldots ,\Delta \left(T_{i_ n}\right)\right).  \] On the other hand, by proposition 12.2.4 , the $\mathcal{I}$-goodness of toric singularities example 7.4.5 , and proposition 7.3.4 , we have \[  n! \operatorname{vol}\Delta \left( \sum _{i=1}^ n C_ i T_ i \right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( \sum _{i=1}^ n C_ i T_ i \right)=\sum _{i_1,\ldots ,i_ n=1}^ n C_{i_1}\cdots C_{i_ n} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_ n}\right).  \] Comparing the coefficients of the above two expressions, we conclude ( 12.94 ). It only remains to establish ( 12.95 ). For this purpose, we fix smooth $T_ c$-invariant Hermitian metrics $h_1$ and $h_2$ on $\mathcal{O}_ X(D_1)$ and $\mathcal{O}_ X(D_2)$ respectively. Correspondingly, take $h_1\otimes h_2$ as the reference Hermitian metric on $\mathcal{O}_ X(D_1+D_2)$. Write \[  \theta _1=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_1,\quad \theta _2=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_2.  \] We choose the rational section of $\mathcal O_ X(D_1+D_2)$ to be $s_{D_1}\otimes s_{D_2}$. With this choice and with the reference metric $h_1\otimes h_2$, the normalization ( 12.22 ) gives \[  F_{\theta _1+\theta _2}=F_{\theta _1}+F_{\theta _2}.  \] Thus \[  F_{\varphi _1+\varphi _2}=F_{\varphi _1}+F_{\varphi _2}.  \] Take $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta _ i)$ with $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=1,2$. Then $F_{\varphi _1}+F_{\varphi _2}$ is a candidate for $F_{\varphi _1+\varphi _2}$; see ( 12.23 ). Therefore, ( 12.95 ) follows from the equality of closed gradient images proved in A.3.7 . $\square$

title: 13 Non-Archimedean pluripotential theory
text: 13 Non-Archimedean pluripotential theory This chapter develops a non-Archimedean pluripotential theory for compact Kähler manifolds. In the projective setting, Boucksom and Jonsson constructed a space of non-Archimedean psh metrics on the Berkovich analytification of a polarized variety. Our approach starts instead from the analytic objects developed in the previous chapters: $\mathcal I$-model test curves and their operations. The resulting theory agrees with the Boucksom–Jonsson theory in the projective case. The guiding idea is the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. A geodesic ray can be encoded by a test curve, and the $\mathcal I$-model version of this construction retains precisely the multiplier-ideal information relevant to algebraic approximation. For a pseudo-effective class $\{ \theta \} $, we define a non-Archimedean potential as an inverse system of $\mathcal I$-model test curves in the big classes $\{ \theta +\omega \} $, where $\omega $ ranges over Kähler forms. The transition maps are given by the $\mathcal I$-envelope. After the definition, we develop the basic operations on non-Archimedean potentials. Sums, translations, maxima, suprema, infima and rescalings are induced from the corresponding operations on test curves. We also define the non-Archimedean volume and prove its basic monotonicity and continuity properties. The next part of the chapter constructs the Duistermaat–Heckman measure of a non-Archimedean potential based on the theory of Okounkov bodies developed in chapter 10 . It is defined through Okounkov test curves and is shown to be independent of the chosen flag. The final part compares this construction with the Boucksom–Jonsson theory. In the projective case, we define the analytification of our non-Archimedean potentials and prove that the resulting space is naturally identified with the Boucksom–Jonsson space of psh non-Archimedean metrics. A related approach has been developed independently by Mesquita-Piccione [ MP24 ] , where a Berkovich-like analytification of a compact Kähler manifold is constructed. The present chapter is logically based on the test-curve formalism of chapter 9 , especially the $\mathcal I$-model theory of section 9.3 and the operations of section 9.4 . It is largely independent of chapter 12 , chapter 14 , while the comparison with Boucksom–Jonsson uses the non-Archimedean theory recalled in section 13.4 .

title: 13.1 The definition of non-Archimedean metrics
text: 13.1 The definition of non-Archimedean metrics Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Let $\textup{Käh}(X)$ be the set of Kähler forms on $X$ with the partial order given as follows: We say $\omega \preceq \omega '$ if $\omega \geq \omega '$. Note that the partially ordered set $\textup{Käh}(X)$ is a directed set. Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Definition 13.1.1 . We define \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )=\varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\footnotemark  \] Note. The cumbersome projective limit can be avoided if instead of relying on the language of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, we use that of augmented nef b-divisors developed in definition 11.1.17 instead. But given the fact that these two formulations are completely equivalent to each other by corollary 11.1.19 , we just stick to the slightly more traditional language here. in the category of sets, where the transition maps are given as follows: Suppose that $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}$ and $\omega \geq \omega '$. Then the transition map is defined in proposition 9.3.6 : 13.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PItransPSHNApositive} P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ')_{>0}\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}. \end{equation} Note that the transition maps are compatible: \[  P_{\theta +\omega ''}[P_{\theta +\omega '}[\varphi ]_\mathcal {I}]_\mathcal {I}=P_{\theta +\omega ''}[\varphi ]_\mathcal {I},\quad \forall \,  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}  \] for $\omega \leq \omega '\leq \omega ''$, since both sides are $\mathcal{I}$-model and are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent to $\varphi $. Recall that $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is defined in definition 9.3.1 . In general, when we denote an element in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ by $\Gamma $, its component in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}$ ($\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$) will be written either as $\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }$ or as $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Note that $\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\max }$ is independent of the choice of $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. We denote this common value by $\Gamma _{\max }$. Remark 13.1.2 . Thanks to proposition 9.3.3 , for any other $\theta '$ representing $\{ \theta \} $, we have a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ').  \] Moreover, these bijections satisfy the cocycle condition. If we view the set of closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms representing $\{ \theta \} $ as a category with a unique morphism between any two objects, then we can define \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\{ \theta \} )=\varprojlim _{\theta } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ).  \] This definition is independent of the choice of the explicit representative of the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $. However, given the fact that our notation is already quite heavy, we stick to the set $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. The constructions below are independent of the choice of $\theta $ within its cohomology class. Proposition 13.1.3 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then given $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ with $\omega \geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]_{\mathcal{I}} = \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }.  \] Proof. Since for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 7.1.7 , it follows that \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Our assertion follows from proposition 3.1.28 and proposition 3.2.19 . $\square$ Proposition 13.1.4 . There is a natural injective map \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ),\quad \Gamma \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}.  \] In the sequel, we do not distinguish an element of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ from its image in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Note that given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, the value of $\Gamma _{\max }$ does not depend on whether we view it as an element of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ or of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Proof. The map is well-defined by the compatibility of the transition maps. It suffices to argue its injectivity. Suppose that $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for some Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then $\Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma '_{\max }$ and for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\Gamma '_{\tau }  \] by proposition 6.1.12 . It follows again from proposition 6.1.12 that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\Gamma '_{\tau }.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Definition 13.1.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define its volume as follows: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \coloneqq \lim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)} \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n\in [0,\infty ).  \] Observe that the net is decreasing, so the limit exists. Proposition 13.1.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }\right)^ n.  \] Proof. This follows from proposition 3.1.26 , corollary 3.1.27 and proposition 9.1.11 . $\square$ Lemma 13.1.7 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $0<t\leq 1$. Then for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  \leq {}& \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Proof. For $\sigma \in \{ -\infty ,\tau \} $, put \[  S_ t^\sigma =\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 13.1.3 , example 7.1.7 , proposition 3.1.6 , projecting $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }$ to the class $\theta +\omega $ does not change the total mass computed in the larger class. Thus \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\sigma }\right)^ n = \int _ X \left(S_ t^\sigma +(1-t)\omega \right)^ n.  \] Expanding the right-hand side and subtracting the two identities for $\sigma =-\infty $ and $\sigma =\tau $, we get \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  ={}& \sum _{a=0}^ n \binom {n}{a}(1-t)^{n-a} \left(\int _ X (S_ t^{-\infty })^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}-\int _ X (S_ t^\tau )^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}\right). \end{aligned}  \] Since $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\geq \Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }$, each summand is non-negative by the monotonicity theorem for mixed non-pluripolar products. Keeping only the term $a=n$ gives the desired inequality. $\square$ Lemma 13.1.8 . The image of the canonical injection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] is given by the set of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. Proof. By proposition 13.1.6 , every element in the image has positive volume. Conversely, take $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. We want to construct $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ representing $\Gamma $. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Define 13.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gamma'_tau} \Gamma '_{\tau }\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty }\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }. \end{equation} We claim that it suffices to show 13.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:theta_kinvomega_masslim_pos} \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n>0 \end{equation} for some $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. If this holds, then the argument of 9.1.3 implies that the same holds for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Then proposition 3.1.26 , proposition 3.2.18 guarantee that $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and represents $\Gamma $. It remains to argue ( 13.7 ). Let $\epsilon =\operatorname{vol}\Gamma >0$. Take $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ so that \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] Therefore, by 13.1.7 , for any $k\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] By the definition of $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma $, the first integral in the preceding line tends to $\epsilon $ as $k\to \infty $. Hence \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\geq \epsilon /2>0,  \] which proves ( 13.7 ). $\square$ Example 13.1.9 . Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We can define an associated non-Archimedean metric \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] as follows: $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$; for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$ and any $\tau <0$, we set \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi ,\theta +\omega }_{\tau }=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Such non-Archimedean metrics are called homogeneous non-Archimedean metrics. Observe that \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\varphi }=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] See proposition 7.3.4 and the footnote there. Definition 13.1.10 . Let $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. We define the map \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )  \] as follows: Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the element such that for any $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}.  \] It is straightforward to check that under the identification of proposition 13.1.4 , the map $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ extends the map ( 13.1 ). Proposition 13.1.11 . The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 together induce a bijection 13.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral2} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ). \end{equation} Proof. It is a tautology that the maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 are compatible with the transition maps. So the map ( 13.8 ) is well-defined. It is injective by the same argument as proposition 13.1.4 . We argue the surjectivity. By unfolding the definitions, an object in the target of ( 13.8 ) is an assignment: With each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we associate a family $(\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '})_{\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ satisfying: $\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega +\omega ')_{>0}$ for each $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$; for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega ''\geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''};  \] for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega \leq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega '+\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ',\omega ''}.  \] The preimage of such an object is given by the family $(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega })_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ given by \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\omega /2,\omega /2}.  \] The fact that the image of $\Gamma $ is as expected follows directly from the definitions. $\square$ With an almost identical argument involving proposition 3.1.26 , we get Proposition 13.1.12 . The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 and the injective maps proposition 13.1.4 together induce bijections 13.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ runs over either the partially ordered set of all smooth closed real positive $(1,1)$-forms with positive volume Note. This partially ordered set is not directed. on $X$ or $\textup{Käh}(X)$. Corollary 13.1.13 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then $\pi ^*$ induces a bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from proposition 13.1.12 . $\square$ It is immediate to verify that $\pi ^*$ in corollary 13.1.13 extends the map proposition 9.3.4 .

title: Definition 13.1.1
text: Definition 13.1.1 . We define \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )=\varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\footnotemark  \] Note. The cumbersome projective limit can be avoided if instead of relying on the language of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, we use that of augmented nef b-divisors developed in definition 11.1.17 instead. But given the fact that these two formulations are completely equivalent to each other by corollary 11.1.19 , we just stick to the slightly more traditional language here. in the category of sets, where the transition maps are given as follows: Suppose that $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}$ and $\omega \geq \omega '$. Then the transition map is defined in proposition 9.3.6 : 13.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PItransPSHNApositive} P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ')_{>0}\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}. \end{equation} Note that the transition maps are compatible: \[  P_{\theta +\omega ''}[P_{\theta +\omega '}[\varphi ]_\mathcal {I}]_\mathcal {I}=P_{\theta +\omega ''}[\varphi ]_\mathcal {I},\quad \forall \,  \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}  \] for $\omega \leq \omega '\leq \omega ''$, since both sides are $\mathcal{I}$-model and are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent to $\varphi $.

13.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PItransPSHNApositive} P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ')_{>0}\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}. \end{equation}

title: Remark 13.1.2
text: Remark 13.1.2 . Thanks to proposition 9.3.3 , for any other $\theta '$ representing $\{ \theta \} $, we have a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ').  \] Moreover, these bijections satisfy the cocycle condition. If we view the set of closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms representing $\{ \theta \} $ as a category with a unique morphism between any two objects, then we can define \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\{ \theta \} )=\varprojlim _{\theta } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ).  \] This definition is independent of the choice of the explicit representative of the cohomology class $\{ \theta \} $. However, given the fact that our notation is already quite heavy, we stick to the set $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. The constructions below are independent of the choice of $\theta $ within its cohomology class.

title: Proposition 13.1.3
text: Proposition 13.1.3 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then given $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ with $\omega \geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]_{\mathcal{I}} = \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }.  \] Proof. Since for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 7.1.7 , it follows that \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Our assertion follows from proposition 3.1.28 and proposition 3.2.19 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.1.4
text: Proposition 13.1.4 . There is a natural injective map \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ),\quad \Gamma \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}.  \] Proof. The map is well-defined by the compatibility of the transition maps. It suffices to argue its injectivity. Suppose that $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for some Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then $\Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma '_{\max }$ and for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\Gamma '_{\tau }  \] by proposition 6.1.12 . It follows again from proposition 6.1.12 that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\Gamma '_{\tau }.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Definition 13.1.5
text: Definition 13.1.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define its volume as follows: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \coloneqq \lim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)} \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n\in [0,\infty ).  \]

title: Proposition 13.1.6
text: Proposition 13.1.6 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }\right)^ n.  \] Proof. This follows from proposition 3.1.26 , corollary 3.1.27 and proposition 9.1.11 . $\square$

title: Lemma 13.1.7
text: Lemma 13.1.7 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $0<t\leq 1$. Then for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  \leq {}& \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Proof. For $\sigma \in \{ -\infty ,\tau \} $, put \[  S_ t^\sigma =\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 13.1.3 , example 7.1.7 , proposition 3.1.6 , projecting $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }$ to the class $\theta +\omega $ does not change the total mass computed in the larger class. Thus \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\sigma }\right)^ n = \int _ X \left(S_ t^\sigma +(1-t)\omega \right)^ n.  \] Expanding the right-hand side and subtracting the two identities for $\sigma =-\infty $ and $\sigma =\tau $, we get \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  ={}& \sum _{a=0}^ n \binom {n}{a}(1-t)^{n-a} \left(\int _ X (S_ t^{-\infty })^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}-\int _ X (S_ t^\tau )^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}\right). \end{aligned}  \] Since $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\geq \Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }$, each summand is non-negative by the monotonicity theorem for mixed non-pluripolar products. Keeping only the term $a=n$ gives the desired inequality. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.1.8
text: Lemma 13.1.8 . The image of the canonical injection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] is given by the set of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. Proof. By proposition 13.1.6 , every element in the image has positive volume. Conversely, take $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. We want to construct $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ representing $\Gamma $. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Define 13.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gamma'_tau} \Gamma '_{\tau }\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty }\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }. \end{equation} We claim that it suffices to show 13.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:theta_kinvomega_masslim_pos} \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n>0 \end{equation} for some $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. If this holds, then the argument of 9.1.3 implies that the same holds for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Then proposition 3.1.26 , proposition 3.2.18 guarantee that $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and represents $\Gamma $. It remains to argue ( 13.7 ). Let $\epsilon =\operatorname{vol}\Gamma >0$. Take $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ so that \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] Therefore, by 13.1.7 , for any $k\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] By the definition of $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma $, the first integral in the preceding line tends to $\epsilon $ as $k\to \infty $. Hence \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\geq \epsilon /2>0,  \] which proves ( 13.7 ). $\square$
13.6 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gamma'_tau} \Gamma '_{\tau }\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty }\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }. \end{equation}

13.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:theta_kinvomega_masslim_pos} \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n>0 \end{equation}

title: Example 13.1.9
text: Example 13.1.9 . Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We can define an associated non-Archimedean metric \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] as follows: $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$; for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$ and any $\tau <0$, we set \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi ,\theta +\omega }_{\tau }=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Such non-Archimedean metrics are called homogeneous non-Archimedean metrics. Observe that \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\varphi }=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] See proposition 7.3.4 and the footnote there.

title: Definition 13.1.10
text: Definition 13.1.10 . Let $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. We define the map \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )  \] as follows: Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the element such that for any $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}.  \]

title: Proposition 13.1.11
text: Proposition 13.1.11 . The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 together induce a bijection 13.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral2} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ). \end{equation} Proof. It is a tautology that the maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 are compatible with the transition maps. So the map ( 13.8 ) is well-defined. It is injective by the same argument as proposition 13.1.4 . We argue the surjectivity. By unfolding the definitions, an object in the target of ( 13.8 ) is an assignment: With each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we associate a family $(\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '})_{\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ satisfying: $\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega +\omega ')_{>0}$ for each $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$; for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega ''\geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''};  \] for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega \leq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega '+\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ',\omega ''}.  \] The preimage of such an object is given by the family $(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega })_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ given by \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\omega /2,\omega /2}.  \] The fact that the image of $\Gamma $ is as expected follows directly from the definitions. $\square$

13.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral2} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.1.12
text: Proposition 13.1.12 . The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 13.1.10 and the injective maps proposition 13.1.4 together induce bijections 13.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ runs over either the partially ordered set of all smooth closed real positive $(1,1)$-forms with positive volume Note. This partially ordered set is not directed. on $X$ or $\textup{Käh}(X)$.

13.9 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PSHNAprojlimigeneral} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ), \end{equation}

title: Corollary 13.1.13
text: Corollary 13.1.13 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then $\pi ^*$ induces a bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from proposition 13.1.12 . $\square$

title: 13.2 Operations on non-Archimedean metrics
text: 13.2 Operations on non-Archimedean metrics Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta ,\theta ',\theta ''$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. This section relies heavily on section 9.4 . We shall use the notions introduced in that section without further explanations. Definition 13.2.1 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. We say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if for some $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega } \leq \Gamma '{}^{\theta '+\omega }.  \] This notion is independent of the choice of $\omega $ thanks to 9.4.2 . Moreover, we have the following: Proposition 13.2.2 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. This follows immediately from 9.4.2 . $\square$ Observe that this definition coincides with the corresponding definition in definition 9.4.1 when $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proposition 13.2.3 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '.  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '{}^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is an immediate consequence of theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$ Definition 13.2.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +\Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\theta '+2\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+\Gamma '^{\theta '+\omega }.  \] This definition yields an element in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by 9.4.6 and it extends the definition in definition 9.4.3 by 9.4.6 as well. Proposition 13.2.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Suppose that $\omega ,\omega '$ are two smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.6 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.6 . The operation $+$ is commutative and associative: For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta '')$, we have \[  \Gamma +\Gamma '=\Gamma '+\Gamma ,\quad (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 9.4.5 . $\square$ Definition 13.2.7 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. We define $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +C \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+C.  \] It is obvious from definition 9.4.7 that $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. It is also obvious that this definition extends definition 9.4.7 . Proposition 13.2.8 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Suppose that $\omega $ is a smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma +C]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Proposition 13.2.9 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $C,C'\in \mathbb {R}$. Then $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+C)=(\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '$; $\Gamma +(C+C')=(\Gamma +C)+C'$. Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 9.4.8 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.10 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C).  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }=\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C)^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is obvious. $\square$ Definition 13.2.11 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma \lor \Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }\lor \Gamma '^{\theta +\omega }.  \] It follows from 9.4.12 that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and this definition extends the corresponding definition in definition 9.4.9 . Proposition 13.2.12 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.12 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.13 . The operation $\lor $ is commutative and associative. In particular, given a finite non-empty family $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we then define $\bigvee _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i$ in the obvious way. Proof. This is a direct consequence of corollary 9.4.11 . $\square$ Definition 13.2.14 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 13.10 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supPSHNAmaxfinite} \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }<\infty . \end{equation} Then we define $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] It follows immediately from 9.4.18 that $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and this definition extends definition 9.4.16 . Moreover, this definition clearly extends definition 13.2.11 as well. Proposition 13.2.15 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.18 . $\square$ We also have a non-Archimedean version of Choquet's lemma. Proposition 13.2.16 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then there exists a countable subfamily $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$. For each $m\geq 1$, proposition 9.4.19 gives a countable subfamily $I_ m\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I_ m}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Set $I'=\bigcup _{m\geq 1}I_ m$. This is countable. We claim that it works. Let $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$. Choose $m$ so large that $\omega '\geq m^{-1}\omega _0$. By proposition 13.2.15 and the compatibility of the transition maps, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}} =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{aligned}  \] Thus the two non-Archimedean metrics have the same component in every class $\theta +\omega '$, and the assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 13.2.17 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 9.4.20 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.18 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then 13.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:prop:vol_NA_incnet_cont} \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} Proof. The $\geq $ direction in ( 13.14 ) is a direct consequence of proposition 13.2.3 . It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Note that ( 13.14 ) holds when $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i>0$ for each $i\in I$, as a consequence of proposition 9.4.14 , corollary 6.2.9 and theorem 6.2.30 . In particular, for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega } \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] For our purpose, we need to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $\omega $ so that \[  \sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon .  \] We shall show that it is possible to choose $\omega $ so that the stronger statement holds: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon ,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Equivalently, we need to choose $\omega $ so that for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $X$ dominated by $\omega $, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }+\epsilon /2,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\Omega $ such that $\Omega \geq \theta +\omega _0$. It is enough to take $\omega =\delta \omega _0$ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. If $\omega '$ is dominated by $\omega $, then $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $. Set \[  T_ i\coloneqq \theta +\omega '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 9.1.11 , the potential $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }$ has the same $P$-singularity type in the class $\theta +\omega $ as $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }$. Hence its mass can be computed as \[  \int _ X\left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } =& \int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n-\int _ X T_ i^ n\\  =&  \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X T_ i^ a\wedge \left( \omega -\omega '\right)^{n-a}\\  \leq & \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X \Omega ^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}. \end{aligned}  \] In the last inequality we used the facts that $0\leq \omega -\omega '\leq \omega $ and $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . We can choose $\omega $ so that the right-hand side is less than $\epsilon /2$. Our assertion then follows. $\square$ Definition 13.2.19 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 13.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnetcontition} \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation} then we define $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have 13.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnettestcurdef} \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }. \end{equation} We observe that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}.  \] This follows from proposition 9.4.26 . Moreover, by 9.4.27 , we have $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, and this definition extends definition 9.4.25 . In general, \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)\leq \lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i  \] as a consequence of proposition 13.2.3 . But the reverse inequality fails in general. Proposition 13.2.20 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows from 9.4.27 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.21 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\leq \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 13.2.22 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \lambda \Gamma \right)^{\lambda \theta +\omega }=\lambda \Gamma ^{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }.  \] It follows immediately from 9.4.24 that $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ and this definition extends definition 9.4.21 . Proposition 13.2.23 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\lambda P_{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from 9.4.24 . $\square$ Proposition 13.2.24 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] If $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ), then \[  \lambda \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\inf _{i\in I}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. Everything except the last assertion follows from proposition 9.4.23 . The last assertion follows directly from the definition. $\square$ Proposition 13.2.25 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \lambda \Gamma \right)=\lambda ^ n \operatorname{vol}\Gamma .  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 13.2.26 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We say that the trace operator of $\Gamma $ along $Y$ is well-defined if \[  \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0  \] for all sufficiently negative $\tau $ and every $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. We define \[  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0\right\} .  \] Here $\omega $ is any Kähler form on $X$; this number is independent of the choice of $\omega $ by the compatibility of the transition maps. In this case, we define $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ Note. Here $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y$ is the normalization of $Y$. as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(\widetilde{Y})$, the component 13.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:TrYinPSHNAg0} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega )_{>0} \end{equation} is defined as follows: We let 13.24 \begin{equation} \label{eq:tracemax} \left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega } \right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }; \end{equation} for each $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than $\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }$, we define \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\left[ \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right) \right]_{\mathcal{I}},  \] where $\tilde{\omega }$ is an arbitrary Kähler form on $X$ such that $\omega \geq \tilde{\omega }|_{\widetilde{Y}}$. It follows from [ Proposition 3.6 , GK20 ] that $\widetilde{Y}$ is a normal Kähler space and hence $\tilde{\omega }$ exists. We observe that the choice of the trace operator $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right)$ is irrelevant since two different choices are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent. Moreover, ( 13.23 ) holds as a consequence of proposition 8.1.5 and proposition 8.2.1 . It is therefore clear that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$. Here when $\widetilde{Y}$ is not smooth, we understand $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ as the set of non-Archimedean metrics on a resolution of $\widetilde{Y}$, which is independent of the choice of the resolution by proposition 8.2.1 . See chapter B for more details. Proposition 13.2.27 . Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then all definitions in this section are invariant under pullback to $Y$. The meaning is clear in most cases. In the case of the trace operator, this means the following: Suppose that $Z\subseteq X$ is an analytic subset and $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ has non-trivial restriction to $Z$. Suppose that $Z$ is not contained in the non-isomorphism locus of $\pi $ so that the strict transform $W$ of $Z$ is defined. If we write $\Pi \colon W\rightarrow Z$ for the restriction of $\pi $ and $\widetilde{\Pi }\colon \widetilde{W}\rightarrow \widetilde{Z}$ the strict transform of $\Pi $, then we have \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )=\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma ).  \] The relevant notations are summarized in the following diagram: \[  \gerbyimage{sgpt/8370eb499968da6bf2d9.svg}{Mathematical diagram from the source}  \] Proof. We only prove the assertion for the trace operator, as the other proofs are similar. We shall use the notations above. Observe that for any closed positive smooth $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$ with positive mass, we have \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },Z\right)=0 \right\} ,  \] and \[  \begin{aligned}  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=& \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left((\pi ^*\Gamma )^{\pi ^*\theta +\pi ^*\omega }_{\tau },W\right)=0 \right\} \\  =& \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\pi ^*\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },W\right)=0 \right\} \\  =&  \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },Z\right)=0 \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Here we implicitly used proposition 13.1.12 . Therefore, \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Take a Kähler form $\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}$ (resp. $\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$) on $\widetilde{Z}$ (resp. $\widetilde{W}$). Take a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$ (resp. $\omega _ X$ on $X$) such that \[  \omega _{\widetilde{Z}}\geq \omega _ X|_{\widetilde{Z}},\quad \omega _{\widetilde{W}} \geq \omega _ Y|_{\widetilde{W}},\quad \omega _ Y \geq \pi ^*\omega _ X.  \] We want to show that, after projection to the common background $(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$, \[  P_{(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}\left[\widetilde{\Pi }^*\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Z}}+\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}}_\tau \right)\right]_{\mathcal I} \sim _ P \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)^{(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}_\tau .  \] Unfolding the definitions, we reduce to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z^{\theta +\omega _ X}\left( \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega _ X}_{\tau } \right)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}^{\pi ^*\theta +\omega _ Y}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma \right)^{\pi ^*\theta +\omega _ Y}_{\tau }\right).  \] Using proposition 8.2.1 , this is equivalent to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z\left( \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega _ X}_{\tau } \right)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma \right)^{\pi ^*\theta +\pi ^*\omega _ X}_{\tau }\right).  \] This is a consequence of 8.2.4 . $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.1
text: Definition 13.2.1 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. We say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if for some $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega } \leq \Gamma '{}^{\theta '+\omega }.  \]

title: Proposition 13.2.2
text: Proposition 13.2.2 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. This follows immediately from 9.4.2 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.3
text: Proposition 13.2.3 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '.  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '{}^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is an immediate consequence of theorem 2.4.8 . $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.4
text: Definition 13.2.4 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +\Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\theta '+2\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+\Gamma '^{\theta '+\omega }.  \]

title: Proposition 13.2.5
text: Proposition 13.2.5 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Suppose that $\omega ,\omega '$ are two smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.6 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.6
text: Proposition 13.2.6 . The operation $+$ is commutative and associative: For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta '')$, we have \[  \Gamma +\Gamma '=\Gamma '+\Gamma ,\quad (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 9.4.5 . $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.7
text: Definition 13.2.7 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. We define $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +C \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+C.  \]

title: Proposition 13.2.8
text: Proposition 13.2.8 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Suppose that $\omega $ is a smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma +C]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.9
text: Proposition 13.2.9 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $C,C'\in \mathbb {R}$. Then $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+C)=(\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '$; $\Gamma +(C+C')=(\Gamma +C)+C'$. Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 9.4.8 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.10
text: Proposition 13.2.10 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C).  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }=\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C)^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is obvious. $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.11
text: Definition 13.2.11 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma \lor \Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }\lor \Gamma '^{\theta +\omega }.  \]

title: Proposition 13.2.12
text: Proposition 13.2.12 . Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.12 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.13
text: Proposition 13.2.13 . The operation $\lor $ is commutative and associative. Proof. This is a direct consequence of corollary 9.4.11 . $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.14
text: Definition 13.2.14 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 13.10 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supPSHNAmaxfinite} \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }<\infty . \end{equation} Then we define $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \]
13.10 \begin{equation} \label{eq:supPSHNAmaxfinite} \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }<\infty . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.2.15
text: Proposition 13.2.15 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 9.4.18 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.16
text: Proposition 13.2.16 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then there exists a countable subfamily $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$. For each $m\geq 1$, proposition 9.4.19 gives a countable subfamily $I_ m\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I_ m}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Set $I'=\bigcup _{m\geq 1}I_ m$. This is countable. We claim that it works. Let $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$. Choose $m$ so large that $\omega '\geq m^{-1}\omega _0$. By proposition 13.2.15 and the compatibility of the transition maps, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}} =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{aligned}  \] Thus the two non-Archimedean metrics have the same component in every class $\theta +\omega '$, and the assertion follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.17
text: Proposition 13.2.17 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 9.4.20 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.18
text: Proposition 13.2.18 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then 13.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:prop:vol_NA_incnet_cont} \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} Proof. The $\geq $ direction in ( 13.14 ) is a direct consequence of proposition 13.2.3 . It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Note that ( 13.14 ) holds when $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i>0$ for each $i\in I$, as a consequence of proposition 9.4.14 , corollary 6.2.9 and theorem 6.2.30 . In particular, for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega } \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] For our purpose, we need to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $\omega $ so that \[  \sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon .  \] We shall show that it is possible to choose $\omega $ so that the stronger statement holds: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon ,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Equivalently, we need to choose $\omega $ so that for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $X$ dominated by $\omega $, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }+\epsilon /2,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\Omega $ such that $\Omega \geq \theta +\omega _0$. It is enough to take $\omega =\delta \omega _0$ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. If $\omega '$ is dominated by $\omega $, then $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $. Set \[  T_ i\coloneqq \theta +\omega '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 9.1.11 , the potential $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }$ has the same $P$-singularity type in the class $\theta +\omega $ as $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }$. Hence its mass can be computed as \[  \int _ X\left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } =& \int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n-\int _ X T_ i^ n\\  =&  \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X T_ i^ a\wedge \left( \omega -\omega '\right)^{n-a}\\  \leq & \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X \Omega ^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}. \end{aligned}  \] In the last inequality we used the facts that $0\leq \omega -\omega '\leq \omega $ and $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . We can choose $\omega $ so that the right-hand side is less than $\epsilon /2$. Our assertion then follows. $\square$

13.14 \begin{equation} \label{eq:prop:vol_NA_incnet_cont} \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation}

title: Definition 13.2.19
text: Definition 13.2.19 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 13.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnetcontition} \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation} then we define $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have 13.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnettestcurdef} \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }. \end{equation}
13.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnetcontition} \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation}
13.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:decnettestcurdef} \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }. \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.2.20
text: Proposition 13.2.20 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows from 9.4.27 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.21
text: Proposition 13.2.21 . Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 13.18 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\leq \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.22
text: Definition 13.2.22 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \lambda \Gamma \right)^{\lambda \theta +\omega }=\lambda \Gamma ^{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }.  \]

title: Proposition 13.2.23
text: Proposition 13.2.23 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\lambda P_{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from 9.4.24 . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.24
text: Proposition 13.2.24 .
