Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.10 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] If $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 13.18 ), then \[  \lambda \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\inf _{i\in I}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. Everything except the last assertion follows from proposition 9.4.23 . The last assertion follows directly from the definition. $\square$

title: Proposition 13.2.25
text: Proposition 13.2.25 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \lambda \Gamma \right)=\lambda ^ n \operatorname{vol}\Gamma .  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$

title: Definition 13.2.26
text: Definition 13.2.26 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We say that the trace operator of $\Gamma $ along $Y$ is well-defined if \[  \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0  \] for all sufficiently negative $\tau $ and every $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. We define \[  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0\right\} .  \] Here $\omega $ is any Kähler form on $X$; this number is independent of the choice of $\omega $ by the compatibility of the transition maps. In this case, we define $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ Note. Here $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y$ is the normalization of $Y$. as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(\widetilde{Y})$, the component 13.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:TrYinPSHNAg0} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega )_{>0} \end{equation} is defined as follows: We let 13.24 \begin{equation} \label{eq:tracemax} \left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega } \right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }; \end{equation} for each $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than $\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }$, we define \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\left[ \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right) \right]_{\mathcal{I}},  \] where $\tilde{\omega }$ is an arbitrary Kähler form on $X$ such that $\omega \geq \tilde{\omega }|_{\widetilde{Y}}$.

13.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:TrYinPSHNAg0} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega )_{>0} \end{equation}
13.24 \begin{equation} \label{eq:tracemax} \left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega } \right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }; \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.2.27
text:
Proposition 13.2.27 . Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then all definitions in this section are invariant under pullback to $Y$. Proof. We only prove the assertion for the trace operator, as the other proofs are similar. We shall use the notations above. Observe that for any closed positive smooth $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$ with positive mass, we have \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )ight)_{\max }=\left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )ight)_{\max }=\sup \left\{  	au <\Gamma _{\max }: 
u \left(\Gamma ^{	heta +\omega }_{	au },Zight)=0 ight\} ,  \] and \[   egin{aligned}  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )ight)_{\max }=& \sup \left\{  	au <\Gamma _{\max }: 
u \left((\pi ^*\Gamma )^{\pi ^*	heta +\pi ^*\omega }_{	au },Wight)=0 ight\} \  =& \sup \left\{  	au <\Gamma _{\max }: 
u \left(\pi ^*\Gamma ^{	heta +\omega }_{	au },Wight)=0 ight\} \  =&  \sup \left\{  	au <\Gamma _{\max }: 
u \left(\Gamma ^{	heta +\omega }_{	au },Zight)=0 ight\} . \end{aligned}  \] Here we implicitly used proposition 13.1.12 . Therefore, \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )ight)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )ight)_{\max }.  \] Let $	au \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Take a Kähler form $\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}$ (resp. $\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$) on $\widetilde{Z}$ (resp. $\widetilde{W}$). Take a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$ (resp. $\omega _ X$ on $X$) such that \[  \omega _{\widetilde{Z}}\geq \omega _ X|_{\widetilde{Z}},\quad \omega _{\widetilde{W}} \geq \omega _ Y|_{\widetilde{W}},\quad \omega _ Y \geq \pi ^*\omega _ X.  \] We want to show that, after projection to the common background $(\pi ^*	heta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$, \[  P_{(\pi ^*	heta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}\left[\widetilde{\Pi }^*\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )^{	heta |_{\widetilde{Z}}+\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}}_	au ight)ight]_{\mathcal I} \sim _ P \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )ight)^{(\pi ^*	heta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}_	au .  \] Unfolding the definitions, we reduce to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z^{	heta +\omega _ X}\left( \Gamma ^{	heta +\omega _ X}_{	au } ight)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}^{\pi ^*	heta +\omega _ Y}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma ight)^{\pi ^*	heta +\omega _ Y}_{	au }ight).  \] Using proposition 8.2.1 , this is equivalent to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z\left( \Gamma ^{	heta +\omega _ X}_{	au } ight)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma ight)^{\pi ^*	heta +\pi ^*\omega _ X}_{	au }ight).  \] This is a consequence of 8.2.4 . $\square$

title: 13.3 Duistermaat–Heckman measures
text: 13.3 Duistermaat–Heckman measures Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Definition 13.3.1 . Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma $ is defined as \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq n!\cdot \operatorname{DH}\left(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\right).  \] Recall that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$ is the Okounkov test curve defined in theorem 10.5.13 . See definition 10.5.9 for the definition of the Duistermaat–Heckman measure of an Okounkov test curve. Theorem 13.3.2 . Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ in definition 13.3.1 is independent of the choice of the smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Furthermore, for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, the following moment identity holds: 13.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc1} \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)=\Gamma _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Gamma +m\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\tau ^{m-1}\Bigl ( \operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau })-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma \Bigr )\, \mathrm{d}\tau , \end{equation} and 13.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc2} \int _{\mathbb {R}}\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=\operatorname{vol}\Gamma . \end{equation} For each $m\in \mathbb {N}$, $\int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)$ is indeed $n!$ times the $m$-th moment of the random variable $G[\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )]$, by definition 13.3.1 , definition 10.5.9 . Proof. We observe that ( 13.28 ) holds by the computations in proposition 10.5.10 and theorem 10.4.13 1 . It is independent of the choice of the flag. Furthermore, ( 13.29 ) follows immediately from theorem 10.4.13 1 . Assume first that $\Gamma $ is bounded. Since the Duistermaat–Heckman measure has bounded support in this case (cf. theorem 10.5.6 ), we conclude that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is uniquely determined. By translating the parameter, it suffices to treat the case $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Indeed, if $a=\Gamma _{\max }$ and \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \coloneqq \Gamma _{\tau +a},  \] then $\widetilde\Gamma _{\max }=0$, and the associated test function is translated by $a$. Consequently, \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=(x\mapsto x+a)_*\operatorname{DH}(\widetilde\Gamma ).  \] Thus independence of the flag and the moment identity for $\widetilde\Gamma $ imply the corresponding assertions for $\Gamma $. For each $\epsilon >0$, we define $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  \Gamma _{-\infty },& \text{ if }\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1},\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _{\tau }-\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty } \right],& \text{ if }\tau \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0\right). \end{cases}  \] Let us check that $\Gamma ^\epsilon $ is indeed an element of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . Since the $\Gamma _\tau $'s are $\mathcal I$-model, they are $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.7 ; hence \[  (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _\tau -\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty }  \] is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 7.2.1 . Therefore its $P$-envelope is also its $\mathcal I$-envelope, and the corresponding level is $\mathcal I$-model. The value at $-\infty $ is $\Gamma _{-\infty }$. Thus $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each fixed $\tau <0$, the argument of theorem 9.2.9 Step 3.3 gives \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau \searrow \Gamma _\tau \quad \textup{as }\epsilon \to 0+.  \] By proposition 3.1.26 and corollary 6.2.11 , this convergence is in $d_ S$. Hence theorem 10.4.13 4 gives \[  \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau )\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )  \] for every $\tau <0$. Since \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _{-\infty }=\Gamma _{-\infty }  \] for all $\epsilon $, the underlying convex body is fixed. Therefore 10.5.11 applies and gives \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^\epsilon )\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ).  \] It follows that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is independent of the choice of the flag. $\square$ More generally, when $X$ does not admit a smooth flag, we may choose a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ so that $Y$ admits a flag. We define 13.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DHmgeneral} \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq \operatorname{DH}(\pi ^*\Gamma ). \end{equation} It follows from theorem 10.4.13 5 that this measure is independent of the choice of $\pi $. Proposition 13.3.3 . Let \[  (\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}\subseteq \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Assume one of the following conditions holds: The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is decreasing and $\Gamma =\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i$. Assume that 13.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volGammalim} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is increasing and $\Gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then 13.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:contDHm} \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ). \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Assume 1 . Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] Since $\Gamma _\tau \leq \Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }$ for every $i$ and every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta .  \] By proposition 3.1.26 , the decreasing limit $\eta $ is model and \[  \int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Using ( 13.33 ), this equals \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n.  \] Since $\Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta $ and both potentials are model, proposition 6.1.4 gives \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\eta .  \] Thus \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] We want to derive ( 13.34 ) from 10.5.11 . It boils down to prove the following: For any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] For fixed $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potentials $\Gamma ^ i_\tau $ decrease to $\Gamma _\tau $. By proposition 3.1.26 , their masses converge to the mass of $\Gamma _\tau $; hence $\Gamma ^ i_\tau \xrightarrow {d_ S}\Gamma _\tau $ by corollary 6.2.11 . Applying the continuity of the partial Okounkov body map, theorem 10.4.13 4 , gives \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] The proof under the assumption 2 is similar. We only need to apply 10.5.12 instead of 10.5.11 . $\square$ Remark 13.3.4 . When $\{ \theta \} $ is a Hodge class and $\Gamma $ is induced by a test configuration as in example 9.3.9 and 9.3.10 , our Duistermaat–Heckman measure coincides with the more traditional definition of [ Section 3.2 , BHJ17 ] . This is explained in [ Remark 7.17 , Xia21 ] .

title: Definition 13.3.1
text: Definition 13.3.1 . Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma $ is defined as \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq n!\cdot \operatorname{DH}\left(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\right).  \]

title: Theorem 13.3.2
text: Theorem 13.3.2 . Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ in definition 13.3.1 is independent of the choice of the smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Furthermore, for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, the following moment identity holds: 13.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc1} \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)=\Gamma _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Gamma +m\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\tau ^{m-1}\Bigl ( \operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau })-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma \Bigr )\, \mathrm{d}\tau , \end{equation} and 13.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc2} \int _{\mathbb {R}}\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=\operatorname{vol}\Gamma . \end{equation} Proof. We observe that ( 13.28 ) holds by the computations in proposition 10.5.10 and theorem 10.4.13 1 . It is independent of the choice of the flag. Furthermore, ( 13.29 ) follows immediately from theorem 10.4.13 1 . Assume first that $\Gamma $ is bounded. Since the Duistermaat–Heckman measure has bounded support in this case (cf. theorem 10.5.6 ), we conclude that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is uniquely determined. By translating the parameter, it suffices to treat the case $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Indeed, if $a=\Gamma _{\max }$ and \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \coloneqq \Gamma _{\tau +a},  \] then $\widetilde\Gamma _{\max }=0$, and the associated test function is translated by $a$. Consequently, \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=(x\mapsto x+a)_*\operatorname{DH}(\widetilde\Gamma ).  \] Thus independence of the flag and the moment identity for $\widetilde\Gamma $ imply the corresponding assertions for $\Gamma $. For each $\epsilon >0$, we define $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  \Gamma _{-\infty },& \text{ if }\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1},\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _{\tau }-\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty } \right],& \text{ if }\tau \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0\right). \end{cases}  \] Let us check that $\Gamma ^\epsilon $ is indeed an element of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 3.1.24 . Since the $\Gamma _\tau $'s are $\mathcal I$-model, they are $\mathcal I$-good by example 7.1.7 ; hence \[  (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _\tau -\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty }  \] is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 7.2.1 . Therefore its $P$-envelope is also its $\mathcal I$-envelope, and the corresponding level is $\mathcal I$-model. The value at $-\infty $ is $\Gamma _{-\infty }$. Thus $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each fixed $\tau <0$, the argument of theorem 9.2.9 Step 3.3 gives \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau \searrow \Gamma _\tau \quad \textup{as }\epsilon \to 0+.  \] By proposition 3.1.26 and corollary 6.2.11 , this convergence is in $d_ S$. Hence theorem 10.4.13 4 gives \[  \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau )\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )  \] for every $\tau <0$. Since \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _{-\infty }=\Gamma _{-\infty }  \] for all $\epsilon $, the underlying convex body is fixed. Therefore 10.5.11 applies and gives \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^\epsilon )\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ).  \] It follows that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is independent of the choice of the flag. $\square$

13.28 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc1} \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)=\Gamma _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Gamma +m\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\tau ^{m-1}\Bigl ( \operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau })-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma \Bigr )\, \mathrm{d}\tau , \end{equation}
13.29 \begin{equation} \label{eq:momentDHmtc2} \int _{\mathbb {R}}\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=\operatorname{vol}\Gamma . \end{equation}
13.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:DHmgeneral} \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq \operatorname{DH}(\pi ^*\Gamma ). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.3.3
text: Proposition 13.3.3 . Let \[  (\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}\subseteq \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Assume one of the following conditions holds: The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is decreasing and $\Gamma =\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i$. Assume that 13.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volGammalim} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is increasing and $\Gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then 13.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:contDHm} \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ). \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Assume 1 . Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] Since $\Gamma _\tau \leq \Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }$ for every $i$ and every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta .  \] By proposition 3.1.26 , the decreasing limit $\eta $ is model and \[  \int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Using ( 13.33 ), this equals \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n.  \] Since $\Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta $ and both potentials are model, proposition 6.1.4 gives \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\eta .  \] Thus \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] We want to derive ( 13.34 ) from 10.5.11 . It boils down to prove the following: For any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] For fixed $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potentials $\Gamma ^ i_\tau $ decrease to $\Gamma _\tau $. By proposition 3.1.26 , their masses converge to the mass of $\Gamma _\tau $; hence $\Gamma ^ i_\tau \xrightarrow {d_ S}\Gamma _\tau $ by corollary 6.2.11 . Applying the continuity of the partial Okounkov body map, theorem 10.4.13 4 , gives \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] The proof under the assumption 2 is similar. We only need to apply 10.5.12 instead of 10.5.11 . $\square$
13.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:volGammalim} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation}
13.34 \begin{equation} \label{eq:contDHm} \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ). \end{equation}

title: Remark 13.3.4
text: Remark 13.3.4 . When $\{ \theta \} $ is a Hodge class and $\Gamma $ is induced by a test configuration as in example 9.3.9 and 9.3.10 , our Duistermaat–Heckman measure coincides with the more traditional definition of [ Section 3.2 , BHJ17 ] . This is explained in [ Remark 7.17 , Xia21 ] .

title: 13.4.1 A brief recap of Boucksom–Jonsson's theory
search_title: A brief recap of Boucksom–Jonsson's theory
text: 13.4.1 A brief recap of Boucksom–Jonsson's theory In this section, we briefly recall the non-Archimedean global pluripotential theory à la Boucksom–Jonsson [ BJ22 ] . Our presentation is selective, so the original paper remains the best companion for this section.

title: Valuations
text: None Valuations Let $X$ be an irreducible reduced variety over $\mathbb {C}$ of dimension $n$. We recall the Berkovich analytification $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ of $X$ with respect to the trivial valuation on $\mathbb {C}$. Definition 13.4.1 . A (real-valued) valuation on $X$ (or a valuation of $\mathbb {C}(X)$) is a map $v\colon \mathbb {C}(X)\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ satisfying the following conditions: For $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f)=\infty $ if and only if $f=0$; For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(fg)=v(f)+v(g)$; For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f+g)\geq v(f)\land v(g)$; For $c\in \mathbb {C}^{\times }$, $v(c)=0$. The set of valuations on $X$ is denoted by $X^{\mathrm{val}}$. The center of a valuation $v$ is the scheme-theoretic point $c=c(v)$ of $X$ such that $v\geq 0$ on $\mathcal{O}_{X,c}$ and $v>0$ on the maximal ideal $\mathfrak {m}_{X,c}$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X,c}$. The center is unique if it exists, and it exists if $X$ is proper. In the remainder of this section, we assume that $X$ is projective. As a set, $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ is the set of semi-valuations on $X$, in other words, real-valued valuations $v$ on irreducible reduced subvarieties $Y$ of $X$ that are trivial on $\mathbb {C}$. We call $Y$ the support of the semi-valuation $v$. In other words, \[  X^{\mathrm{An}}=\coprod _{Y} Y^{\mathrm{val}}.  \] We will write $v_{\mathrm{triv}}\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$ for the trivial valuation on $X$: $v_{\mathrm{triv}}(f)=0$ for any $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)^{\times }$. We endow $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ with the coarsest topology such that for any Zariski open subset $U\subseteq X$, the subset $U^{\mathrm{An}}$ of $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ consisting of semi-valuations whose supports meet $U$ is open; for each Zariski open subset $U\subseteq X$ and each $f\in \mathrm{H}^0(U,\mathcal{O}_ X)$ (here $\mathcal{O}_ X$ is the sheaf of regular functions), the map $|f|\colon U^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ sending $v$ to $\exp (-v(f))$ is continuous. See [ Berk93 ] for more details. We will be most interested in divisorial valuations. Recall that a divisorial valuation on $X$ is a valuation of the form $t\operatorname{ord}_ E$, where $t\in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}$ and $E$ is a prime divisor over $X$. The set of divisorial valuations on $X$ is denoted by $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. When $\mathbb {Q}_{>0}$ is replaced by $\mathbb {R}_{>0}$, we can similarly define a space $X^{\operatorname{div}}_{\mathbb {R}}$. Given any coherent ideal $\mathfrak {a}$ on $X$ and any $v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$, we define 13.35 \begin{equation} \label{eq:va} v(\mathfrak {a})\coloneqq \min \{ v(f):f\in \mathfrak {a}_{c(v)}\} \in [0,\infty ], \end{equation} where $c(v)$ is the center of the valuation $v$ on $X$. Given any valuation $v$ on $X$, the Gauss extension of $v$ is a valuation $\sigma (v)$ on $X\times \mathbb {A}^1$: 13.36 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gext} \sigma (v)\left(\sum _ i f_ i t^ i\right)\coloneqq \min _ i (v(f_ i)+i). \end{equation} Here $t$ is the standard coordinate on $\mathbb {A}^1=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb {C}[t]$. The key property is that when $v$ is a divisorial valuation, then so is $\sigma (v)$. See [ Lemma 4.2 , BHJ17 ] .

title: Definition 13.4.1
text: Definition 13.4.1 . A (real-valued) valuation on $X$ (or a valuation of $\mathbb {C}(X)$) is a map $v\colon \mathbb {C}(X)\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ satisfying the following conditions: For $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f)=\infty $ if and only if $f=0$; For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(fg)=v(f)+v(g)$; For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f+g)\geq v(f)\land v(g)$; For $c\in \mathbb {C}^{\times }$, $v(c)=0$.
13.35 \begin{equation} \label{eq:va} v(\mathfrak {a})\coloneqq \min \{ v(f):f\in \mathfrak {a}_{c(v)}\} \in [0,\infty ], \end{equation}
13.36 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gext} \sigma (v)\left(\sum _ i f_ i t^ i\right)\coloneqq \min _ i (v(f_ i)+i). \end{equation}

title: Non-Archimedean plurisubharmonic functions
text: None Non-Archimedean plurisubharmonic functions Let $X$ be an irreducible complex projective variety of dimension $n$ and $L$ be a holomorphic pseudo-effective $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle on $X$. Through the GAGA morphism $X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow X$ of ringed spaces, $L$ can be pulled back to an analytic line bundle $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ on $X$. The purpose of this section is to study the psh metrics on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$. We will follow the approach of [ BJ22 ] , which avoids the direct treatment of $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ itself. Following [ Definition 2.18 , BJ22 ] , we define $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$, the set of (rational) generically finite Fubini–Study functions $\phi \colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ that are of the following form: 13.37 \begin{equation}  \phi =\frac{1}{m}\max _ j \{ \log |s_ j|+\lambda _ j\} . \end{equation} Here $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ is an integer such that $L^ m$ is a line bundle, the $s_ j$'s are a finite collection of non-zero sections in $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m)$, and $\lambda _ j\in \mathbb {Q}$. We follow the convention of Boucksom–Jonsson by writing $\log |s_ j|(v)=-v(s_ j)$. Definition 13.4.2 ( [ Definition 4.1 , BJ22 ] ) . A plurisubharmonic metric (or psh metric for short) on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ is a function $\phi \colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ that is not identically $-\infty $, and is the pointwise limit of a decreasing net $(\phi _ i)_{i\in I}$, where $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L_ i^{\mathrm{An}})$ for some $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundles $L_ i$ on $X$ satisfying $c_1(L_ i)\to c_1(L)$ in $\mathrm{NS}^1(X)_{\mathbb {R}}$. The set of psh metrics on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. We endow $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ with the topology of pointwise convergence on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. This topology is Hausdorff as functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ are completely determined by their restriction on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$: Theorem 13.4.3 ( [ Theorem 4.22 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $\psi :X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be an usc function. Assume that $\phi \leq \psi $ on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. Then the same holds on $X^{\mathrm{An}}$. Proposition 13.4.4 ( [ Theorem 4.7 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $\phi ,\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then so is their pointwise maximum $\phi \lor \phi '$. Proposition 13.4.5 . Let $H$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Consider $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Assume that for each $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. This is a special case of [ (PSH2) , BJ22 ] on Page 45. Next we note that we may use sequences instead of nets in the definition of $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$: Theorem 13.4.6 ( [ Corollary 12.18 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $S$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a sequence of rational numbers $\varepsilon _ i\searrow 0$ and a decreasing sequence $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\varepsilon _ i S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that $\phi $ is the pointwise limit of $\phi _ i$, as $i\to \infty $. The space $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ inherits most of the expected properties of (Archimedean) psh functions ( [ Theorem 4.7 , BJ22 ] ). However, the following compactness result is not known: Conjecture 13.4.7 ( [ §5 , BJ22 ] ) . Assume that $X$ is unibranch. Then every bounded from above increasing net of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ converges in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. This prediction is equivalent to the so-called envelope conjecture [ Conjecture 5.14 , BJ22 ] : the regularized supremum of a bounded from above family of functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. See [ Theorem 5.11 , BJ22 ] for the proof of the equivalence. This conjecture is proved when $X$ is smooth and $L$ is nef in [ BJ22 ] . More recently, in [ BJ22b ] , Boucksom–Jonsson further established the case when $X$ is smooth and $L$ is pseudo-effective.

title: Definition 13.4.2
text: Definition 13.4.2 ( [ Definition 4.1 , BJ22 ] ) . A plurisubharmonic metric (or psh metric for short) on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ is a function $\phi \colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ that is not identically $-\infty $, and is the pointwise limit of a decreasing net $(\phi _ i)_{i\in I}$, where $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L_ i^{\mathrm{An}})$ for some $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundles $L_ i$ on $X$ satisfying $c_1(L_ i)\to c_1(L)$ in $\mathrm{NS}^1(X)_{\mathbb {R}}$.

title: Theorem 13.4.3
text: Theorem 13.4.3 ( [ Theorem 4.22 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $\psi :X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be an usc function. Assume that $\phi \leq \psi $ on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. Then the same holds on $X^{\mathrm{An}}$.

title: Proposition 13.4.4
text: Proposition 13.4.4 ( [ Theorem 4.7 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $\phi ,\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then so is their pointwise maximum $\phi \lor \phi '$.

title: Proposition 13.4.5
text: Proposition 13.4.5 . Let $H$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Consider $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Assume that for each $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$.

title: Theorem 13.4.6
text: Theorem 13.4.6 ( [ Corollary 12.18 , BJ22 ] ) . Let $S$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a sequence of rational numbers $\varepsilon _ i\searrow 0$ and a decreasing sequence $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\varepsilon _ i S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that $\phi $ is the pointwise limit of $\phi _ i$, as $i\to \infty $.

title: Conjecture 13.4.7
text: Conjecture 13.4.7 ( [ §5 , BJ22 ] ) . Assume that $X$ is unibranch. Then every bounded from above increasing net of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ converges in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$.

title: 13.4.2 The analytifications
text: 13.4.2 The analytifications Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n$. Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class.

title: The transcendental setting
text: None The transcendental setting Definition 13.4.8 . For $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define the analytification $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,0]$ as follows: 13.38 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphianv} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq -v(\varphi )=-\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right). \end{equation} By theorem 1.4.12 and Fekete's lemma, the limit in ( 13.38 ) exists. Note that we can also write 13.39 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphiAnalt} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\inf _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} -2^{-k}v\left( \mathcal{I}(2^ k\varphi )\right). \end{equation} When $v=t\operatorname{ord}_ E$ for some prime divisor $E$ over $X$, $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-t\nu (\varphi ,E)$ by proposition 1.4.13 . Definition 13.4.9 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define the analytification $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\operatorname{div}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ of $\Gamma $ as follows: For any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we define 13.40 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiandef} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation} Clearly, ( 13.40 ) is independent of the choice of $\omega $. Note that ( 13.40 ) can be equivalently written as \[  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)= \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)=\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)  \] with $(-\infty )^{\mathrm{An}}(v) = -\infty $ understood. Proposition 13.4.10 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\Gamma _{\max }\leq 0$. Let $\Psi $ be the complexification of $\Gamma ^*$. Then 13.41 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiansigma} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-\sigma (v)(\Psi )\quad \forall v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} See definition 4.1.12 for the definition of the complexification $\Psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X\times \Delta )$. Note that since $\Gamma _{\max }\leq 0$, by corollary 9.2.11 and theorem 1.2.9 , $\Psi $ extends uniquely to a quasi-psh function on $X\times \Delta $. Proof. Recall that \[  \Psi (x,\delta )=\sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }} (\Gamma _{\tau }(x)-\log |\delta |^2\tau )\quad \text{for }x\in X, \delta \in \Delta ^*.  \] By ( 13.36 ), we have $\sigma (v)(\log |\delta |^2)=1$ and $\sigma (v)(\Gamma _{\tau })=v(\Gamma _{\tau })$ for all $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$. So we have \[  \sigma (v)(\Gamma _\tau (x) - \log |\delta |^2 \tau ) = v(\Gamma _\tau ) - \tau .  \] Lastly, since $\sigma (v)$ is a divisorial valuation on $X \times \Delta $, by corollary 1.4.6 , we conclude ( 13.41 ). $\square$ Definition 13.4.11 . Let $N\in \mathbb {N}$, and $A_{0},\ldots ,A_ N$ be a finite collection of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\tau _0>\tau _1>\cdots >\tau _ N$ be finitely many real numbers. Then the piecewise linear curve $A=(A_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ associated with these data is the affine interpolation of these data: $A_{\tau _ i}=A_ i$ for $i=0,\ldots ,N$; $A_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$ for $\tau \leq \tau _ N$; for $t\in (0,1)$ and $i=0,\ldots ,N-1$, we have \[  A_{(1-t)\tau _ i+t\tau _{i+1}}=(1-t)A_{\tau _ i}+tA_{\tau _{i+1}};  \] $A_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ for $\tau >\tau _0$. The analytification of $A$ is the function $A^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ defined as follows: 13.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psianvlinear} A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \tau _0} (A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau )=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N} \left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right)\quad \forall v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation} We also say $A=(A_{\tau })_{\tau \leq \tau _0}$ is a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Remark 13.4.12 . Note that $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$ is upper semicontinuous, but not necessarily concave. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Then it can be inductively constructed as follows: For $\tau \in (\tau _0,\infty )$, we let $A'_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $; we set $A'_{\tau _0}=A_{\tau _0}$; define inductively for $j=0,\ldots ,N-1$ the following: For $\tau \in [\tau _{j+1},\tau _ j)$, we set \[  A'_{\tau }=\max _{i=j+1,\ldots ,N}\left( \frac{\tau _ j-\tau }{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A_{\tau _ i}+\frac{\tau -\tau _ i}{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A'_{\tau _ j} \right)\lor A'_{\tau _ j};  \] for $\tau \in (-\infty ,\tau _ N)$, we set $A'_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$. This construction is just a reformulation of the general formula proposition A.1.11 . In particular, $A'_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all $\tau \leq \tau _0$. Note that $A'$ is not necessarily piecewise linear. Lemma 13.4.13 . Let $A$ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Define $\tilde A$ by \[  \tilde{A}^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_{\tau }]_{\mathcal I}, \quad \omega \in \textup{Käh}(X),\  \tau <\tau _0.  \] Then $\tilde A\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, and 13.43 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psieqsiprime} A^{\mathrm{An}}=\tilde{A}^{\mathrm{An}}\quad \text{on }X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} Here $\tau _0$ is as in definition 13.4.11 . Proof. We continue to use the notations in definition 13.4.11 . The fact that $\tilde{A}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ follows from 13.4.12 and the cocycle property of the $\mathcal{I}$-projection. In order to prove ( 13.43 ), we fix $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$ and $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. The inductive construction in 13.4.12 uses only finite maxima and positive affine combinations of the potentials $A_{\tau _ i}$. On divisorial valuations, analytification commutes with both operations. Moreover, $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal I}$ does not change divisorial valuations. Hence \[  \tau \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_\tau ]_{\mathcal I}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)= (A'_\tau )^{\mathrm{An}}(v)  \] is the ordinary upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$. The Legendre-type supremum over $\tau $ is therefore unchanged by passing from $A$ to $A'$, which proves ( 13.43 ). $\square$

title: Definition 13.4.8
text: Definition 13.4.8 . For $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define the analytification $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,0]$ as follows: 13.38 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphianv} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq -v(\varphi )=-\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right). \end{equation}
13.38 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphianv} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq -v(\varphi )=-\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right). \end{equation}
13.39 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphiAnalt} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\inf _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} -2^{-k}v\left( \mathcal{I}(2^ k\varphi )\right). \end{equation}

title: Definition 13.4.9
text: Definition 13.4.9 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define the analytification $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\operatorname{div}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ of $\Gamma $ as follows: For any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we define 13.40 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiandef} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation}
13.40 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiandef} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.4.10
text: Proposition 13.4.10 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\Gamma _{\max }\leq 0$. Let $\Psi $ be the complexification of $\Gamma ^*$. Then 13.41 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiansigma} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-\sigma (v)(\Psi )\quad \forall v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} Proof. Recall that \[  \Psi (x,\delta )=\sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }} (\Gamma _{\tau }(x)-\log |\delta |^2\tau )\quad \text{for }x\in X, \delta \in \Delta ^*.  \] By ( 13.36 ), we have $\sigma (v)(\log |\delta |^2)=1$ and $\sigma (v)(\Gamma _{\tau })=v(\Gamma _{\tau })$ for all $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$. So we have \[  \sigma (v)(\Gamma _\tau (x) - \log |\delta |^2 \tau ) = v(\Gamma _\tau ) - \tau .  \] Lastly, since $\sigma (v)$ is a divisorial valuation on $X \times \Delta $, by corollary 1.4.6 , we conclude ( 13.41 ). $\square$
13.41 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psiansigma} \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-\sigma (v)(\Psi )\quad \forall v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation}

title: Definition 13.4.11
text: Definition 13.4.11 . Let $N\in \mathbb {N}$, and $A_{0},\ldots ,A_ N$ be a finite collection of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\tau _0>\tau _1>\cdots >\tau _ N$ be finitely many real numbers. Then the piecewise linear curve $A=(A_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ associated with these data is the affine interpolation of these data: $A_{\tau _ i}=A_ i$ for $i=0,\ldots ,N$; $A_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$ for $\tau \leq \tau _ N$; for $t\in (0,1)$ and $i=0,\ldots ,N-1$, we have \[  A_{(1-t)\tau _ i+t\tau _{i+1}}=(1-t)A_{\tau _ i}+tA_{\tau _{i+1}};  \] $A_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ for $\tau >\tau _0$. The analytification of $A$ is the function $A^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ defined as follows: 13.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psianvlinear} A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \tau _0} (A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau )=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N} \left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right)\quad \forall v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation}

13.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psianvlinear} A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \tau _0} (A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau )=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N} \left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right)\quad \forall v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation}

title: Remark 13.4.12
text: Remark 13.4.12 . Note that $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$ is upper semicontinuous, but not necessarily concave. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Then it can be inductively constructed as follows: For $\tau \in (\tau _0,\infty )$, we let $A'_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $; we set $A'_{\tau _0}=A_{\tau _0}$; define inductively for $j=0,\ldots ,N-1$ the following: For $\tau \in [\tau _{j+1},\tau _ j)$, we set \[  A'_{\tau }=\max _{i=j+1,\ldots ,N}\left( \frac{\tau _ j-\tau }{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A_{\tau _ i}+\frac{\tau -\tau _ i}{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A'_{\tau _ j} \right)\lor A'_{\tau _ j};  \] for $\tau \in (-\infty ,\tau _ N)$, we set $A'_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$. This construction is just a reformulation of the general formula proposition A.1.11 . In particular, $A'_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all $\tau \leq \tau _0$. Note that $A'$ is not necessarily piecewise linear.

title: Lemma 13.4.13
text: Lemma 13.4.13 . Let $A$ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Define $\tilde A$ by \[  \tilde{A}^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_{\tau }]_{\mathcal I}, \quad \omega \in \textup{Käh}(X),\  \tau <\tau _0.  \] Then $\tilde A\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, and 13.43 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psieqsiprime} A^{\mathrm{An}}=\tilde{A}^{\mathrm{An}}\quad \text{on }X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} Proof. We continue to use the notations in definition 13.4.11 . The fact that $\tilde{A}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ follows from 13.4.12 and the cocycle property of the $\mathcal{I}$-projection. In order to prove ( 13.43 ), we fix $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$ and $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. The inductive construction in 13.4.12 uses only finite maxima and positive affine combinations of the potentials $A_{\tau _ i}$. On divisorial valuations, analytification commutes with both operations. Moreover, $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal I}$ does not change divisorial valuations. Hence \[  \tau \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_\tau ]_{\mathcal I}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)= (A'_\tau )^{\mathrm{An}}(v)  \] is the ordinary upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$. The Legendre-type supremum over $\tau $ is therefore unchanged by passing from $A$ to $A'$, which proves ( 13.43 ). $\square$
13.43 \begin{equation} \label{eq:psieqsiprime} A^{\mathrm{An}}=\tilde{A}^{\mathrm{An}}\quad \text{on }X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation}

title: The algebraic setting
text: None The algebraic setting Let $L$ be a $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle on $X$ and $h$ be a Hermitian metric on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Lemma 13.4.14 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. After replacing $L$ with a sufficiently high power, we may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Take a very ample line bundle $H$ on $X$. By Siu's uniform global generation theorem [ Siu98 ] , [ Theorem 6.27 , Dem12 ] there exists $b>0$ large enough so that $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$ is globally generated for all $k>0$. Let $\{ s_ i\} _ i$ be a finite set of global sections that generate the sheaf $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$. Then \[  v(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))=\min _ i v(s_ i).  \] It follows that $v\mapsto -k^{-1}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right)$ lies in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\frac{b}{k}H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Using ( 13.39 ), we conclude that $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. $\square$ Lemma 13.4.15 . Let $\Gamma $ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. The result follows from ( 13.42 ), proposition 13.4.4 and 13.4.14 . $\square$ Lemma 13.4.16 . Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbb {C}$-algebra of finite type and $I$ be an ideal of $ R[t]$. If for any $a\in S^1$, $a^*I\subseteq I$, then $I$ is stable under the $\mathbb C^*$-action. Moreover, there are ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots \subseteq I_ m$ in $R$ so that 13.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Iexp} I=I_0 + I_1t+ \cdots + I_ m (t^ m). \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to argue that $I$ can be expanded as in ( 13.44 ). To see this, assume that $a\in I$. We can write $a=a_0+a_1t+\cdots +a_ mt^ m$ with $a_ i\in R$. Then our assumption implies that $\sum _ i a_ i \rho ^ i t^ i\in I$ as well for all $\rho \in S^1$. So by the Lagrange interpolation formula, $a_ it^ i\in I$ for all $i$. Therefore, we can write $I$ as $I_0+I_1t+I_2t^2+\cdots $ for some ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots $ in $R$. But as $R$ is noetherian, there is $m\geq 0$ so that $I_{m'}=I_ m$ for $m'>m$. ( 13.44 ) follows. $\square$ Lemma 13.4.17 . Let $X$ be a complex projective variety and $p:X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Assume that $\mathcal{I}$ is an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {C}$. Assume that $\mathcal{I}|_{X \times \mathbb C^*}=p^*\mathcal{J}$ for some coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal{J}$ on $X$. Then $\mathcal{I}$ is the analytification of an algebraic coherent ideal sheaf. Proof. Let $q:X\times (\mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} )\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Since $\mathbb C^* \subset \mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} $, we can glue $q^*\mathcal{J}$ with $\mathcal{I}$ to get an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {P}^1$. By the GAGA principle, this ideal sheaf is necessarily algebraic, hence so is its restriction to $X\times \mathbb {C}$. $\square$ Next we point out a version of Siu's uniform global generation lemma [ Siu88 ] that we will need in the proof of our next theorem: Lemma 13.4.18 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ such that $c_1(L) = \{ \theta \} $ and $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times \Delta , p_1^*\theta )$, where $\Delta $ is the unit disk. Let $G$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k>0$, depending only on $X$ and $G$, such that $p_1^*(G^ k \otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal I(m \Phi )$ is globally generated for all $m \in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Proof. The argument for this is exactly the same as the one in [ Lemma 5.6 , BBJ21 ] with Nadel's vanishing theorem replaced by the family version proved by Matsumura in [ Theorem 1.7 , Mat16 ] . $\square$ Proposition 13.4.19 . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential and $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ with $\sup _ X \ell _1\leq 0$. Let $\Phi $ be the complexification of $\ell $. Then the function \[  v\mapsto -\sigma (v)(\Phi ) \quad \text{for } v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}  \] admits a unique extension to an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. We may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 13.4.3 . Let $p_1\colon X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the projection. For each $t>0$, we have $\ell _ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, hence $\ell _ t\sim _ P\phi $ by theorem 3.1.9 and $\ell _ t\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\phi $ by corollary 6.1.9 . Thanks to proposition 1.4.17 and 8.5.11 , for each $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )|_{X\times \Delta ^*} = p_1^* \mathcal{I}(m\phi )|_{X\times \Delta ^*}.  \] In particular, $\mathcal{I}(m\Phi )$ admits an $S^1$-invariant coherent extension to $X\times \mathbb {C}$, obtained by gluing it with $p_1^*\mathcal{I}(m\phi )$ over $X\times \mathbb {C}^*$. From 13.4.16 and 13.4.17 , we get that 13.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ImPhiexp} \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )=\mathfrak {a}_0 +\mathfrak {a}_1 t+\cdots +\mathfrak {a}_{N-1} t^{N-1}+\mathfrak {a}_ N (t^ N)\, , \end{equation} where the $\mathfrak {a}_ i$'s are coherent ideal sheaves on $X$. Using 13.4.18 , there exists an ample line bundle $T$ over $X$ such that $p_1^* (T\otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )$ is globally generated, which is equivalent to $T\otimes L^ m\otimes \mathfrak {a}_ i$ being globally generated for all $i$. Note. In contrast with the case where $\phi $ is bounded, explored in [ BBJ21 ] , $\mathfrak {a}_ N \neq \mathcal{O}_ X$ in general. We define \[  \varphi _ m(v)\coloneqq -\frac{1}{m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(m\Phi ))=-\frac{1}{m}\min _ i (v(\mathfrak {a}_ i)+i),\quad v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}.  \] From the right-hand side of the formula, $\varphi _ m$ can be extended to an element in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+m^{-1}T)^{\mathrm{An}})$, which we denote by the same symbol. For $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  -\sigma (v)(\Phi )=\lim _{m\to \infty }-\frac{1}{2^ m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(2^ m\Phi ))=\lim _{m\to \infty }\varphi _{2^ m}(v)  \] and the right-hand side defines an element in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by definition, since $\{ \varphi _{2^ m}\} _ m$ is decreasing by the subadditivity of multiplier ideals theorem 1.4.12 . $\square$ Corollary 13.4.20 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$ defined in definition 13.4.9 admits a unique extension to $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. The extension will be denoted by the same notation $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$. Proof. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 13.4.3 . We may assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$ without loss of generality. When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, our assertion follows from proposition 13.4.19 and proposition 13.4.10 . In general, fix an ample line bundle $H$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(H)$. Then we know that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\left(\Gamma ^{m^{-1}\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})  \] for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by proposition 13.4.5 . $\square$

title: Lemma 13.4.14
text: Lemma 13.4.14 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. After replacing $L$ with a sufficiently high power, we may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Take a very ample line bundle $H$ on $X$. By Siu's uniform global generation theorem [ Siu98 ] , [ Theorem 6.27 , Dem12 ] there exists $b>0$ large enough so that $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$ is globally generated for all $k>0$. Let $\{ s_ i\} _ i$ be a finite set of global sections that generate the sheaf $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$. Using ( 13.39 ), we conclude that $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.4.15
text: Lemma 13.4.15 . Let $\Gamma $ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. The result follows from ( 13.42 ), proposition 13.4.4 and 13.4.14 . $\square$

title: Lemma 13.4.16
text: Lemma 13.4.16 . Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbb {C}$-algebra of finite type and $I$ be an ideal of $ R[t]$. If for any $a\in S^1$, $a^*I\subseteq I$, then $I$ is stable under the $\mathbb C^*$-action. Moreover, there are ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots \subseteq I_ m$ in $R$ so that 13.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Iexp} I=I_0 + I_1t+ \cdots + I_ m (t^ m). \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to argue that $I$ can be expanded as in ( 13.44 ). To see this, assume that $a\in I$. We can write $a=a_0+a_1t+\cdots +a_ mt^ m$ with $a_ i\in R$. Then our assumption implies that $\sum _ i a_ i \rho ^ i t^ i\in I$ as well for all $\rho \in S^1$. So by the Lagrange interpolation formula, $a_ it^ i\in I$ for all $i$. Therefore, we can write $I$ as $I_0+I_1t+I_2t^2+\cdots $ for some ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots $ in $R$. But as $R$ is noetherian, there is $m\geq 0$ so that $I_{m'}=I_ m$ for $m'>m$. ( 13.44 ) follows. $\square$
13.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Iexp} I=I_0 + I_1t+ \cdots + I_ m (t^ m). \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.4.17
text: Lemma 13.4.17 . Let $X$ be a complex projective variety and $p:X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Assume that $\mathcal{I}$ is an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {C}$. Assume that $\mathcal{I}|_{X \times \mathbb C^*}=p^*\mathcal{J}$ for some coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal{J}$ on $X$. Then $\mathcal{I}$ is the analytification of an algebraic coherent ideal sheaf. Proof. Let $q:X\times (\mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} )\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Since $\mathbb C^* \subset \mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} $, we can glue $q^*\mathcal{J}$ with $\mathcal{I}$ to get an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {P}^1$. By the GAGA principle, this ideal sheaf is necessarily algebraic, hence so is its restriction to $X\times \mathbb {C}$. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.4.18
text: Lemma 13.4.18 . Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ such that $c_1(L) = \{ \theta \} $ and $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times \Delta , p_1^*\theta )$, where $\Delta $ is the unit disk. Let $G$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k>0$, depending only on $X$ and $G$, such that $p_1^*(G^ k \otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal I(m \Phi )$ is globally generated for all $m \in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Proof. The argument for this is exactly the same as the one in [ Lemma 5.6 , BBJ21 ] with Nadel's vanishing theorem replaced by the family version proved by Matsumura in [ Theorem 1.7 , Mat16 ] . $\square$

title: Proposition 13.4.19
text: Proposition 13.4.19 . Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential and $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ with $\sup _ X \ell _1\leq 0$. Let $\Phi $ be the complexification of $\ell $. Then the function \[  v\mapsto -\sigma (v)(\Phi ) \quad \text{for } v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}  \] admits a unique extension to an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. We may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 13.4.3 . Let $p_1\colon X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the projection. For each $t>0$, we have $\ell _ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, hence $\ell _ t\sim _ P\phi $ by theorem 3.1.9 and $\ell _ t\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\phi $ by corollary 6.1.9 .
