From 13.4.16 and 13.4.17 , we get that 13.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ImPhiexp} \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )=\mathfrak {a}_0 +\mathfrak {a}_1 t+\cdots +\mathfrak {a}_{N-1} t^{N-1}+\mathfrak {a}_ N (t^ N)\, , \end{equation} where the $\mathfrak {a}_ i$'s are coherent ideal sheaves on $X$. Using 13.4.18 , there exists an ample line bundle $T$ over $X$ such that $p_1^* (T\otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )$ is globally generated, which is equivalent to $T\otimes L^ m\otimes \mathfrak {a}_ i$ being globally generated for all $i$. Note. In contrast with the case where $\phi $ is bounded, explored in [ BBJ21 ] , $\mathfrak {a}_ N \neq \mathcal{O}_ X$ in general. We define \[  \varphi _ m(v)\coloneqq -\frac{1}{m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(m\Phi ))=-\frac{1}{m}\min _ i (v(\mathfrak {a}_ i)+i),\quad v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}.  \] From the right-hand side of the formula, $\varphi _ m$ can be extended to an element in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+m^{-1}T)^{\mathrm{An}})$, which we denote by the same symbol. For $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  -\sigma (v)(\Phi )=\lim _{m\to \infty }-\frac{1}{2^ m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(2^ m\Phi ))=\lim _{m\to \infty }\varphi _{2^ m}(v)  \] and the right-hand side defines an element in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by definition, since $\{ \varphi _{2^ m}\} _ m$ is decreasing by the subadditivity of multiplier ideals theorem 1.4.12 . $\square$
13.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ImPhiexp} \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )=\mathfrak {a}_0 +\mathfrak {a}_1 t+\cdots +\mathfrak {a}_{N-1} t^{N-1}+\mathfrak {a}_ N (t^ N)\, , \end{equation}

title: Corollary 13.4.20
text: Corollary 13.4.20 . Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$ defined in definition 13.4.9 admits a unique extension to $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 13.4.3 . We may assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$ without loss of generality. When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, our assertion follows from proposition 13.4.19 and proposition 13.4.10 . In general, fix an ample line bundle $H$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(H)$. Then we know that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\left(\Gamma ^{m^{-1}\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})  \] for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by proposition 13.4.5 . $\square$

title: 13.4.3 The comparison theorem

text: 13.46 \begin{equation} \label{eq:analymap} \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}}),\quad \Gamma \mapsto \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation}
13.47 \begin{equation} \label{eq:proj_NA_an_invariance} \left( P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma \right]_{\mathcal{I}} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation}
13.48 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gammamax} \Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v_{\mathrm{triv}}), \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.4.21
text: Lemma 13.4.21 . The map ( 13.46 ) is order preserving. Moreover, suppose that $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfies that $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \Gamma '^{\mathrm{An}}$, then $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$. In particular, the map ( 13.46 ) is injective. Proof. The map ( 13.46 ) is order preserving by definition. Let us take $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \Gamma '^{\mathrm{An}}$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Let $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$ and $t \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}$. Then, using ( 13.40 ) and the homogeneity of divisorial valuations, we notice that 13.49 \begin{equation} \label{eq:legendre_NA} t \Gamma ^\mathrm{An}\left(t^{-1} v \right) = \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+ t \tau \right). \end{equation} A similar equality holds for $\Gamma '$. Therefore, by corollary A.2.4 , we have \[  \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \left(\Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. It follows that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }  \] by proposition 6.1.5 . Since both sides are $\mathcal{I}$-model, proposition 6.1.12 gives \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\leq \Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Hence $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ by the definition of the order. $\square$

13.49 \begin{equation} \label{eq:legendre_NA} t \Gamma ^\mathrm{An}\left(t^{-1} v \right) = \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+ t \tau \right). \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.4.22
text: Lemma 13.4.22 . Let $\phi \in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a piecewise linear curve $A$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\phi =A^{\mathrm{An}}$. In particular, $\phi $ is in the image of ( 13.46 ). Proof. Let us write 13.50 \begin{equation} \label{eq:phiintominversemax} \phi =\frac{1}{m}\max _{i=1,\ldots ,M} \left(\log |s_ i|+\lambda _ i\right), \end{equation} where $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $s_{1},\ldots , s_ M$ are a finite number of sections of $L^ m$ and $\lambda _1,\ldots ,\lambda _ M\in \mathbb {Q}$. Write $I_{\tau }$ for the set of $i$ such that $m^{-1}\lambda _ i=\tau $. We denote the finitely many $\tau $ so that $I_{\tau }$ is non-empty as $\tau _0> \cdots > \tau _ N$. For each $i=0,\ldots ,N$, we write \[  A_{\tau _ i}=\frac{1}{m}\max _{j\in I_{\tau _ i}} \log |s_ j|^2_{h^ m}.  \] We define $A$ as the piecewise linear curve associated with the $A_{\tau _ i}$'s and the $\tau _ i$'s. For every $v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$, \[  A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N}\left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right) =\frac{1}{m}\max _{j=1,\ldots ,M}\left(\log |s_ j|(v)+\lambda _ j\right)=\phi (v),  \] where we used the convention $\log |s_ j|(v)=-v(s_ j)$. The final assertion follows from 13.4.13 and theorem 13.4.3 . $\square$
13.50 \begin{equation} \label{eq:phiintominversemax} \phi =\frac{1}{m}\max _{i=1,\ldots ,M} \left(\log |s_ i|+\lambda _ i\right), \end{equation}

title: Proposition 13.4.23
text: Proposition 13.4.23 . Let $(\Gamma _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that ( 13.18 ) is satisfied. Then \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i}^{\mathrm{An}}.  \] Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We need to show that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i}^{\mathrm{An}}.  \] Therefore, after replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega $, we may assume that $\Gamma _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$ and $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Fix $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$. By theorem 13.4.3 , it suffices to prove that 13.51 \begin{equation} \label{eq:anpreinf1} \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \left(\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)= \adjustlimits \inf _{i\in I}\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation} Write $\Gamma =\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _ i$. We first compare the two sides inside the Legendre-type supremum. If $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, then by the definition of the infimum test curve, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }.  \] The net $(\Gamma _{i,\tau })_ i$ decreases to $\Gamma _{\tau }$. By 9.4.27 , $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is stable under $P_{\theta }[\bullet ]$. Hence proposition 3.1.26 gives convergence of the masses, and corollary 6.2.11 yields \[  \Gamma _{i,\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S}\Gamma _{\tau }.  \] Hence theorem 6.2.29 gives \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v),\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] If $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$, then $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $, and also $\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }\equiv -\infty $, since $\Gamma _{\max }=\inf _ i(\Gamma _ i)_{\max }$. Thus the same equality holds for $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$ as well, with value $-\infty $. The possible endpoint $\tau =\Gamma _{\max }$ does not affect the supremum: for any test curve $\Lambda $ and any $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  \sup _{\tau \leq \Lambda _{\max }}\left(\Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right) =\sup _{\tau < \Lambda _{\max }}\left(\Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right),  \] because $\Lambda _{\Lambda _{\max }}\leq \Lambda _{\tau }$ for $\tau <\Lambda _{\max }$, hence \[  \Lambda _{\Lambda _{\max }}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\Lambda _{\max } \leq \Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\Lambda _{\max }  \] and we let $\tau \nearrow \Lambda _{\max }$. Consequently, in ( 13.51 ) we may replace $\left(\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$ by $\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$ inside the supremum. The equality then follows from proposition A.2.10 applied to the closed convex functions $-\Gamma _{i,\bullet }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$. $\square$

13.51 \begin{equation} \label{eq:anpreinf1} \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \left(\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)= \adjustlimits \inf _{i\in I}\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation}

title: Theorem 13.4.24
text: Theorem 13.4.24 . The map ( 13.46 ) is an order preserving bijection. Proof. The map ( 13.46 ) is an order preserving injection by 13.4.21 . It remains to prove that it is surjective. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. We want to construct $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. Let $H$ be an ample line bundle and $(\epsilon _ i)_ i$ be a decreasing sequence of rational numbers with limit $0$, $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\epsilon _ i H)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that \[  \phi =\inf _{i>0}\phi _ i.  \] The existence of these data is guaranteed by theorem 13.4.6 . Fix a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(H)$. Thanks to 13.4.22 , we can find $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ i \omega )$ with $(\Gamma ^ i)^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi _ i$. It follows from 13.4.21 that \[  \Gamma ^ i\geq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ i\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i+1} \right]_{\mathcal{I}} \geq \Gamma ^{i+1}.  \] Therefore, for any $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$, after discarding finitely many $i$ so that $\omega '\geq \epsilon _ i\omega $, the sequence $(P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}})_ i$ is decreasing. This does not change its infimum. We let \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}=\inf _{i\gg 1}P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ').  \] Note that the infimum is defined thanks to ( 13.48 ). It follows from proposition 13.4.23 that \[  \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi .  \] From this, we conclude that for $\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ with $\omega '\leq \omega ''$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega ''}\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega ''}.  \] Indeed, both sides have analytification $\phi $, by ( 13.47 ) and ( 13.46 ). The injectivity part of 13.4.21 gives our assertion. It follows that $(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '})_{\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ defines an element $\Gamma $ in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. $\square$

title: Theorem 13.4.25
text: Theorem 13.4.25 . Under the bijection theorem 13.4.24 , the operations on the space $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ defined in section 13.2 all correspond to the corresponding operations on $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ in Boucksom–Jonsson's theory.

title: Theorem 13.4.26
text: Theorem 13.4.26 . Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. Consider an element $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with well-defined restriction to $Y$. Then 13.52 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Tracena} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}=\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first reduce to the positive mass case. Choose a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and set $\widehat{\Gamma }=P_{\theta +\omega _0}[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega _0$ and $\Gamma $ by $\widehat{\Gamma }$ does not change $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$, by ( 13.47 ); it also only replaces $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )$ by the corresponding $\mathcal{I}$-projection on $\widetilde{Y}$, whose analytification is unchanged. Hence we may assume that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Let $\phi =\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. By 13.4.27 , $\phi (v_{Y,\mathrm{triv}})\neq -\infty $. Take an ample line bundle $S$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(S)$. Write $\phi $ as the decreasing limit of a sequence $(\phi ^{i})_ i$ of elements in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+i^{-1}S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ as in theorem 13.4.6 . Take $\Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +i^{-1}\omega )$ such that $\Gamma ^{i,\mathrm{An}}=\phi ^{i}$. Note that by 13.1.8 , $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +i^{-1}\omega )_{>0}$. Write $\widehat{\Gamma }^ i\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and $\widehat{\Gamma }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Applying proposition 13.4.23 to the decreasing sequence $(\widehat{\Gamma }^ i)_ i$ and then using the injectivity in 13.4.21 , we get $\inf _ i\widehat{\Gamma }^ i=\widehat{\Gamma }$. Hence, by the componentwise definition of this infimum, for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \inf _{i\in \mathbb {N}}\widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau }=\widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }.  \] Now proposition 3.1.26 and corollary 6.2.11 give \[  \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S} \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }.  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. By 13.4.27 again, each $\widehat{\Gamma }^{i}$ has non-trivial restriction to $Y$. By proposition 8.2.2 , for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $\widetilde{Y}$ satisfying $\omega '\geq \omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}$ we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau } \right)\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }\right)  \] for any $\tau <(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma ))_{\max }$. Thanks to theorem 6.2.29 , for every $c\operatorname{ord}_ F\in Y^{\operatorname{div}}$ and every such $\tau $, \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau } \right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\inf _{i\geq 1}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau } \right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F).  \] Applying proposition A.2.10 to the Legendre transforms in $\tau $, and using again that $\mathcal{I}$-projection does not change analytification, we get \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\inf _{i\geq 1}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma ^ i)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F).  \] Since also $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _ i \Gamma ^{i,\mathrm{An}}$, it suffices to prove ( 13.52 ) with $\Gamma ^ i$ in place of $\Gamma $. In other words, we have reduced to the case where $\phi \in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $L$ is big. Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. By 13.4.22 , we can find a concave curve $(\Gamma '_{\tau })_{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}$ such that $\Gamma '_{\tau }$ is a generalized Fubini–Study metric for each $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$ and such that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }].  \] Here the second equality follows from example 7.1.6 , since generalized Fubini–Study metrics have analytic singularities. With the convention that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(-\infty )=-\infty $ and $(-\infty )^{\mathrm{An}}\equiv -\infty $, it follows that for any $c\operatorname{ord}_ F\in \widetilde{Y}^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \phi |_{Y^{\mathrm{An}}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=& \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\Gamma '_{\tau }{}^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\left(\Gamma '_{\tau }|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma '_{\tau })^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma _{\tau })^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F). \end{aligned}  \] The third equality follows from example 8.1.10 , since $\Gamma '_{\tau }$ has analytic singularities. The fourth equality follows from $\Gamma _{\tau }=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }]$, proposition 8.2.1 and corollary 6.1.9 . It remains to justify the second line. Namely, we want to show that for any generalized Fubini–Study metric $\varphi $ whose restriction to $\widetilde{Y}$ is not identically $-\infty $, we have 13.58 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphiAncordF} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\left(\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F). \end{equation} We can immediately reduce to the case where $\varphi $ is a Fubini–Study metric, and then to the case \[  \varphi =\log |s|_{h_0}^2,  \] where $s$ is a holomorphic section of $L$, not vanishing identically on $Y$, in which case ( 13.58 ) is obvious. $\square$
13.52 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Tracena} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}=\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}. \end{equation}
13.58 \begin{equation} \label{eq:varphiAncordF} \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\left(\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F). \end{equation}

title: Lemma 13.4.27
14 Partial Bergman kernels
text: 14 Partial Bergman kernels The classical Bergman kernel of a Hermitian line bundle $L$ on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ encodes, through its asymptotic expansion as the tensor power $L^ k$ goes to infinity, deep geometric information about the underlying metric. This chapter develops the corresponding partial Bergman kernel. The word partial refers to the fact that we only use sections cut out by an ideal, typically the multiplier ideal of an auxiliary psh weight on a closed subset $K\subseteq X$. The main result is the convergence theorem theorem 14.3.7 . Given a $\theta $-psh potential $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, a closed non-pluripolar weighted subset $(K,v)$, and a Bernstein–Markov measure $\mu $, the normalized partial Bergman measures on $X$ converge weakly to the partial equilibrium measure of $(K,v,\varphi )$ as $k\to \infty $. This is the relative version of the theorem of Berman–Boucksom–Witt Nyström [ BBWN11 ] , corresponding to the case $\varphi =V_\theta $. The assumptions are essentially the mildest ones under which the statement makes sense. The first part of the chapter introduces the relative envelope operators. In section 14.1 we define the relative $P$-envelope $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)$ and the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$ by replacing the constraint $\eta \leq 0$ in the usual $P$- and $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes with the constraint $\eta |_ K\leq v$. We establish their basic properties, including monotonicity, mass-preservation, and the relation with the envelope operators of chapter 3 . The second part develops the equilibrium theory associated with a weighted subset $(K,v)$. In section 14.2 we show that the Monge–Ampère measure $\theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$ is carried by the contact locus $\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=v\} \subseteq K$, which justifies the name partial equilibrium measure . The chapter concludes in section 14.3 with the proof of the weak convergence of partial Bergman measures towards this partial equilibrium.

title: 14.1 Partial envelopes
text: 14.1 Partial envelopes Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $K \subseteq X$ be a closed non-pluripolar set. Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Definition 14.1.1 . Given a function $f\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we introduce the relative $P$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 14.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Similarly, we define the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 14.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphivI} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} By $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, we mean that there is a pluripolar set $S\subseteq X$ so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. In general the upper envelope in ( 14.1 ) or ( 14.2 ) may be identically $\infty $. Observe that when $f$ is bounded from below, neither envelope is identically $-\infty $. The envelopes contain essentially all envelope operators that we have studied in this book: Example 14.1.2 . When $K=X$ and $f=0$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] When $K=X$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ](f).  \] These definitions reduce to the envelopes studied in chapter 3 . On the other hand, when $\varphi =V_{\theta }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) & =P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\\ & =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \begin{array}{l} \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere} \end{array} \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] In an even more special case where $\varphi =V_{\theta }$ and $K=X$, we find that \[  P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](f)=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere}\Bigr \} .  \] This is nothing but $P_{\theta }(f)$ as we studied in definition 2.4.12 . Proposition 14.1.3 . Let $f,g\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be functions and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then we have the following: We have \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] assume that $f$ is bounded from above, then \[  \begin{aligned}  \left.P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\  \left. P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere}; \end{aligned}  \] suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] if $f\leq g$, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](g),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(g);  \] for any $t \in (0,1)$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f),\\  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f). \end{aligned}  \] Proof. 1 This follows from $\eta \preceq \varphi \Rightarrow \eta \preceq _{\mathcal I}\varphi $. 2 This follows from proposition 1.2.5 and 1.5.5 . 3 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 4 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 5 If $\eta ,\eta '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ are such that \[  \begin{split} & \eta |_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad \eta '|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\ & \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta '\preceq \psi , \end{split}  \] then for $t\in (0,1)$, \[  \left.\left(t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\right)\right|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad t\eta +(1-t)\eta ' \preceq t\varphi +(1-t)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\leq P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f).  \] Since $\eta $ and $\eta '$ are arbitrary, the first inequality follows. The second follows from the same argument. $\square$ Similar to the usual envelopes studied in chapter 3 , the $P$-partial envelopes are well-behaved only when $\varphi $ has positive mass. Lemma 14.1.4 . Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ is bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ptheta_partial_pos_mass} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} In other words, in this situation, in the definition ( 14.1 ), we may restrict to only those $\eta $ with positive mass. Proof. By our assumption, we can find $C>0$ so that $\varphi |_ K-C\leq f$. Then if $\eta $ is a candidate in ( 14.1 ), $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate, and $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Therefore, $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate for the right-hand side of ( 14.11 ). The equality ( 14.11 ) follows. $\square$ Note that in the most important cases, we can actually replace the condition $\eta \leq f$ quasi-everywhere in ( 14.1 ) by everywhere. Lemma 14.1.5 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaK_new_def} \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. Both $\geq $ directions in ( 14.12 ) are trivial. Conversely, let $\eta $ be a candidate in ( 14.11 ). Let $S\subseteq X$ be a pluripolar set so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. We now claim that we can choose $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\chi |_ S\equiv -\infty $ and $\chi \leq \eta $. Assume this for the moment. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, we have \[  (1-\delta )\eta |_ K+\delta \chi |_ K\leq f,\quad (1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi \preceq \varphi .  \] Hence, $(1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 14.12 ). Letting $\delta \to 0+$, we conclude that $\eta $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 14.12 ) and hence, ( 14.12 ) follows. It remains to construct $\chi $. Since $\varphi $ has positive mass, the class $\{ \theta \} $ is big. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\rho }\geq 2\epsilon _0\omega _0$ for some $\epsilon _0>0$. By theorem 1.1.17 , there is a quasi-psh function $q$ such that $q|_ S\equiv -\infty $. Choose $A>0$ so that $A\omega _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. For $a>0$ small enough, $\rho +aq\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and still has pole $-\infty $ on $S$. Replacing $\rho $ by $\rho +aq$, we may therefore assume that $\rho |_ S\equiv -\infty $. Since $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>0$, fixing such a $\rho $ and taking $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, we have \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }}+\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Thus, by proposition 3.1.15 and theorem 3.1.18 , we have \[  \Bigl (\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }\Bigr ) \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] It suffices to define this function as $\chi $. $\square$ Corollary 14.1.6 . Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is bounded, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there is a constant $C=C(\sup _ K f,K,X)>0$ such that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq C.  \] Proof. Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, 1.5.5 then gives a constant $C>0$, depending only on $\sup _ K f$, $K$ and $X$, such that every $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere satisfies $\eta \leq C$ on $X$. This applies to the candidates defining both envelopes. Hence both candidate families are locally uniformly bounded above, so their upper semicontinuous suprema are genuine $\theta $-psh functions. By proposition 14.1.3 2 , both envelopes are dominated by $f$ quasi-everywhere on $K$. Applying 1.5.5 once more gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(f)\leq C.  \] $\square$ Proposition 14.1.7 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Proof. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be such that $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then $\eta \preceq _ P \psi $, and thanks to corollary 6.1.22 for any $C>0$, we have $\eta \land (\psi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. But then $\eta \land (\psi +C)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f)$, and we find \[  \eta \land (\psi +C)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] By corollary 6.1.22 again, we get \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\psi ](\eta )\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Our assertion follows now from 14.1.4 . $\square$ Corollary 14.1.8 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. We first apply proposition 14.1.7 , \[  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\right](f)\\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split}  \] Next observe that by 14.1.4 , the latter can also be written as \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} .  \] Next we apply 14.1.5 ; the remaining statements follow. $\square$ Corollary 14.1.9 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be $\mathcal{I}$-good. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)=P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Proof. In fact, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, a potential $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ if and only if $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi $. Therefore, our assertion follows from corollary 14.1.8 and ( 14.2 ). $\square$ Next, we make the following observations about the singularity types of our envelopes: Lemma 14.1.10 . Let $f \colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We have 14.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv_singtype} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first prove the $P$-part of ( 14.21 ). If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta \leq 0$, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 14.1 ), and hence, \[  \eta +\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] It follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that \[  \eta |_ K\leq f,\quad \eta \preceq \varphi .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, by 1.5.5 we can find $C=C(\sup _ K f,K, X)>0$ so that $\eta \leq C$. Hence $\eta -C$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and hence \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By 14.1.5 , this implies that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f) \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ] + C.  \] The proof of the $\mathcal{I}$-part is similar, but we spell it out since this comparison will be used below. If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \leq 0$ and $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in ( 14.2 ). Hence \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+\inf _ K f\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a candidate in ( 14.2 ). Since $K$ is non-pluripolar and $f$ is bounded, the same compactness estimate gives a constant $C>0$, independent of $\eta $, such that $\eta \leq C$. Then $\eta -C\leq 0$ and $\eta -C\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. By corollary 6.1.11 , \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Taking the upper envelope over all such $\eta $ gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Corollary 14.1.11 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiveq} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Take any $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, then \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f).  \] Therefore, \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right).  \] So we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 14.22 ). For the reverse direction, take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Then $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 14.1.3 . Hence \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] By corollary 14.1.8 , the $\geq $ direction in ( 14.22 ) follows. $\square$

title: Definition 14.1.1
text: Definition 14.1.1 . Given a function $f\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we introduce the relative $P$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 14.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Similarly, we define the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 14.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphivI} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

14.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

14.2 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphivI} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Example 14.1.2
text: Example 14.1.2 . When $K=X$ and $f=0$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] When $K=X$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ](f).  \] These definitions reduce to the envelopes studied in chapter 3 . On the other hand, when $\varphi =V_{\theta }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) & =P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\\ & =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \begin{array}{l} \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere} \end{array} \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] In an even more special case where $\varphi =V_{\theta }$ and $K=X$, we find that \[  P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](f)=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere}\Bigr \} .  \] This is nothing but $P_{\theta }(f)$ as we studied in definition 2.4.12 .

title: Proposition 14.1.3
text: Proposition 14.1.3 . Let $f,g\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be functions and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then we have the following: We have \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] assume that $f$ is bounded from above, then \[  \begin{aligned}  \left.P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\  \left. P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere}; \end{aligned}  \] suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] if $f\leq g$, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](g),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(g);  \] for any $t \in (0,1)$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f),\\  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f). \end{aligned}  \] Proof. 1 This follows from $\eta \preceq \varphi \Rightarrow \eta \preceq _{\mathcal I}\varphi $. 2 This follows from proposition 1.2.5 and 1.5.5 . 3 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 4 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 5 If $\eta ,\eta '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ are such that \[  \begin{split} & \eta |_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad \eta '|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\ & \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta '\preceq \psi , \end{split}  \] then for $t\in (0,1)$, \[  \left.\left(t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\right)\right|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad t\eta +(1-t)\eta ' \preceq t\varphi +(1-t)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\leq P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f).  \] Since $\eta $ and $\eta '$ are arbitrary, the first inequality follows. The second follows from the same argument. $\square$

title: Lemma 14.1.4
text: Lemma 14.1.4 . Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ is bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ptheta_partial_pos_mass} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Proof. By our assumption, we can find $C>0$ so that $\varphi |_ K-C\leq f$. Then if $\eta $ is a candidate in ( 14.1 ), $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate, and $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Therefore, $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate for the right-hand side of ( 14.11 ). The equality ( 14.11 ) follows. $\square$

14.11 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Ptheta_partial_pos_mass} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 14.1.5
text: Lemma 14.1.5 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaK_new_def} \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. Both $\geq $ directions in ( 14.12 ) are trivial. Conversely, let $\eta $ be a candidate in ( 14.11 ). Let $S\subseteq X$ be a pluripolar set so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. We now claim that we can choose $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\chi |_ S\equiv -\infty $ and $\chi \leq \eta $. Assume this for the moment. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, we have \[  (1-\delta )\eta |_ K+\delta \chi |_ K\leq f,\quad (1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi \preceq \varphi .  \] Hence, $(1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 14.12 ). Letting $\delta \to 0+$, we conclude that $\eta $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 14.12 ) and hence, ( 14.12 ) follows. It remains to construct $\chi $. Since $\varphi $ has positive mass, the class $\{ \theta \} $ is big. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\rho }\geq 2\epsilon _0\omega _0$ for some $\epsilon _0>0$. By theorem 1.1.17 , there is a quasi-psh function $q$ such that $q|_ S\equiv -\infty $. Choose $A>0$ so that $A\omega _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. For $a>0$ small enough, $\rho +aq\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and still has pole $-\infty $ on $S$. Replacing $\rho $ by $\rho +aq$, we may therefore assume that $\rho |_ S\equiv -\infty $. Since $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>0$, fixing such a $\rho $ and taking $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, we have \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }}+\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Thus, by proposition 3.1.15 and theorem 3.1.18 , we have \[  \Bigl (\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }\Bigr ) \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] It suffices to define this function as $\chi $. $\square$

14.12 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaK_new_def} \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation}

title: Corollary 14.1.6
text: Corollary 14.1.6 . Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is bounded, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there is a constant $C=C(\sup _ K f,K,X)>0$ such that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq C.  \] Proof. Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, 1.5.5 then gives a constant $C>0$, depending only on $\sup _ K f$, $K$ and $X$, such that every $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere satisfies $\eta \leq C$ on $X$. This applies to the candidates defining both envelopes. Hence both candidate families are locally uniformly bounded above, so their upper semicontinuous suprema are genuine $\theta $-psh functions. By proposition 14.1.3 2 , both envelopes are dominated by $f$ quasi-everywhere on $K$. Applying 1.5.5 once more gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(f)\leq C.  \] $\square$

title: Proposition 14.1.7
text: Proposition 14.1.7 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Proof. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be such that $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then $\eta \preceq _ P \psi $, and thanks to corollary 6.1.22 for any $C>0$, we have $\eta \land (\psi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. But then $\eta \land (\psi +C)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f)$, and we find \[  \eta \land (\psi +C)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] By corollary 6.1.22 again, we get \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\psi ](\eta )\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Our assertion follows now from 14.1.4 . $\square$

title: Corollary 14.1.8
text: Corollary 14.1.8 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. We first apply proposition 14.1.7 , \[  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\right](f)\\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split}  \] Next observe that by 14.1.4 , the latter can also be written as \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} .  \] Next we apply 14.1.5 ; the remaining statements follow. $\square$

title: Corollary 14.1.9
text: Corollary 14.1.9 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be $\mathcal{I}$-good. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)=P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Proof. In fact, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, a potential $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ if and only if $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi $. Therefore, our assertion follows from corollary 14.1.8 and ( 14.2 ). $\square$

title: Lemma 14.1.10
text: Lemma 14.1.10 . Let $f \colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We have 14.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv_singtype} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first prove the $P$-part of ( 14.21 ). If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta \leq 0$, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 14.1 ), and hence, \[  \eta +\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] It follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that \[  \eta |_ K\leq f,\quad \eta \preceq \varphi .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, by 1.5.5 we can find $C=C(\sup _ K f,K, X)>0$ so that $\eta \leq C$. Hence $\eta -C$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and hence \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By 14.1.5 , this implies that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f) \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ] + C.  \] The proof of the $\mathcal{I}$-part is similar, but we spell it out since this comparison will be used below. If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \leq 0$ and $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in ( 14.2 ). Hence \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+\inf _ K f\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a candidate in ( 14.2 ). Since $K$ is non-pluripolar and $f$ is bounded, the same compactness estimate gives a constant $C>0$, independent of $\eta $, such that $\eta \leq C$. Then $\eta -C\leq 0$ and $\eta -C\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. By corollary 6.1.11 , \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Taking the upper envelope over all such $\eta $ gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

14.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiv_singtype} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 14.1.11
text: Corollary 14.1.11 . Let $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiveq} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Take any $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, then \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f).  \] Therefore, \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right).  \] So we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 14.22 ). For the reverse direction, take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Then $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 14.1.3 . Hence \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] By corollary 14.1.8 , the $\geq $ direction in ( 14.22 ) follows. $\square$
14.22 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphiveq} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation}

title: 14.2 Partial equilibrium measures
text:
14.2 Partial equilibrium measures Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Definition 14.2.1 . A weighted subset of $X$ is a pair $(K,v)$ consisting of a closed non-pluripolar subset $K\subseteq X$ and a function $v\in C^0(K)$. The next result motivates our terminology to call the measures $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](f)}^ n$ the partial equilibrium measures of our context: Lemma 14.2.2 . Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 14.23  egin{equation} \label{eq:intXminusKthetan_vanish} \int _{X\setminus K}	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0,\quad \int _ K \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K
eq vight\} }	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0. \end{equation} More precisely, we have 14.24  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPKuv} 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=vight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n. \end{equation} Here $\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K
eq v\} $ and $\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=v\} $ are understood as consisting of points of $K$ satisfying these constraints. Proof. Step 1 . We first prove ( 14.23 ) when $\varphi = V_{	heta }$. Let $S\subseteq X$ be a proper analytic subset, such that $V_{	heta }$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus S$. Such $S$ exists by 2.4.6 . Fix holomorphic balls $B\Subset B'\Subset X\setminus S$. By proposition 1.2.3 and 14.1.5 , we can take an increasing sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that \[  \eta _ j
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad \eta _ j|_ K\leq v	extup{ for all }j\geq 1.  \] Note that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)\sim V_{	heta }$ by 14.1.10 . Take $C>0$ so that \[  \left.\left( P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v) ight)ight|_ K-C\leq v.  \] Then we may replace $\eta _ j$ by $\eta _ j\lor (P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)-C)$ and assume that $\eta _ j\sim V_{	heta }$ for each $j$. In particular, $\eta _ j$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus S$. For each $j\geq 1$, let $\gamma _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be the balayage of $\eta _ j$ on $B$, defined in proposition 1.5.9 . Note that $(\gamma _ j)_ j$ is increasing due to proposition 1.2.15 . For the first equality in ( 14.23 ), we may assume that $B\Subset X\setminus (S \cup K)$. It suffices to show that $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n$ does not charge $B$. Since $B$ lies outside $K$ by assumption, we also have $\gamma _ j|_ K=\eta _ j|_ K \leq v$ for all $j\geq 1$. In particular, $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. It follows that $\gamma _ j 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$ almost everywhere as well. Testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$ and using theorem 2.4.7 , we find that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$, as desired. We next prove the second equality in ( 14.23 ). The proof is essentially the same as that of 2.4.13 . It suffices to show that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge the set $K\cap \{ P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K<v\} $. Let $x\in (X\setminus S) \cap K$ be a point such that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)(x)<v(x)-\epsilon $ for some $\epsilon >0$. We may assume that $x\in B$ and $B'$ is small enough, so that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_{\overline{B'}}<v(x)-\epsilon $. $v|_{\overline{B'}\cap K}>v(x)-\epsilon $. By 1 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{\partial B}\leq v(x)-\epsilon $, hence by proposition 1.2.15 , $\gamma _ j|_ B\leq v(x)-\epsilon $. By 2 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{B\cap K}\leq v|_{B\cap K}$. On the other hand, $\gamma _ j|_{K\setminus B}=\eta _{j}|_{K\setminus B}\leq v|_{K\setminus B}$. Therefore, $\gamma _ j|_ K\leq v$. It follows again that $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Therefore, we conclude as in the previous paragraph that $\gamma _ j
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Thus, testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$, we conclude that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$ again by theorem 2.4.7 . Step 2 . We handle the general case. By corollary 14.1.11 , \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ]\left(P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight).  \] Now corollary 3.1.8 gives \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=vight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where in the second inequality we have used Step 1. Hence ( 14.24 ) follows, and a fortiori ( 14.23 ) follows as well. $\square$ Corollary 14.2.3 . Let $v\in C^0(K)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 14.27  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetandoesnotcharge1}  egin{aligned}  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)<vight\} }	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}=&  0,\  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)<vight\} }	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=&  0. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Proof. The first equation in ( 14.27 ) follows from 14.2.2 . For the second, it suffices to observe that \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)=P_{	heta ,K}\left[P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}ight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)=P_{	heta ,K}\left[P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}ight](v)  \] by corollary 14.1.9 . $\square$ Definition 14.2.4 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, we define the partial equilibrium energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }\colon C^0(K)ightarrow \mathbb {R}$ as follows: given $v \in C^0(K)$, we set 14.30  egin{equation}  \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)\coloneqq E_{	heta }^{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight). \end{equation} Recall that the energy $E_{	heta }^{P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}$ functional is defined in definition 3.1.35 . Note that by 14.1.10 , we have \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }\left(X,	heta ;P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}ight),  \] so $\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)\in \mathbb {R}$. Proposition 14.2.5 . Let $v,f \in C^0(K)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then $\mathbb {R}
i t \mapsto \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf)$ is differentiable and 14.31  egin{equation} \label{eq:ddtI}  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf) = \int _ K f\,  	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)} \end{equation} for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$. Proof. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model by replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Note that it suffices to prove ( 14.31 ) at $t=0$, which is equivalent to 14.32  egin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_1} \lim _{t	o 0} rac{E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)}{t}=\int _ K f\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} It suffices to prove the right derivative at $0$ for an arbitrary $f$; applying the same argument to $-f$ then gives the left derivative. In other words, we need to prove that 14.33  egin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_2} \lim _{t	o 0+} rac{E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)}{t}=\int _ K f\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} We first reduce the proof of ( 14.33 ) to the case $f\leq 0$. Assume that this case is known. Choose $A\in \mathbb R$ such that $f-A\leq 0$ on $K$. Since for any $t>0$, \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\Bigl ( v+t(f-A) \Bigr )= P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf)-tA,  \] then we have \[  \int _ K f\,  	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=\int _ K (f-A)\,  	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}+A\int _ X 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] By ( 3.71 ), for any $t>0$, \[  E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\Bigl (P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\left(v+t(f-A)ight)\Bigr )=E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-tA\int _ X	heta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] So the limit in ( 14.33 ) exists and is equal to the left-hand side of ( 14.33 ) with $f-A$ in place of $f$ plus $A\int _ X	heta _{\varphi }^ n$. So ( 14.33 ) for $f-A$ implies the desired formula for $f$ in view of 14.1.10 and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Hence we may assume that $f\leq 0$. Fix $t>0$. Set \[  \eta _ t\coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf),\quad \eta _0\coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v).  \] By the comparison principle ( 3.59 ) and proposition 3.1.45 , we find \[   egin{aligned}  E_{	heta }^{\varphi }(\eta _ t)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }(\eta _0) ={}&  rac{1}{n+1}\sum _{i=0}^ n\int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\,  	heta _{\eta _ t}^ i\wedge 	heta _{\eta _0}^{n-i}\  \leq {}&  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, 	heta _{\eta _0}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] By 14.2.2 and corollary 14.1.9 , the measure $	heta _{\eta _0}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, and the measure $	heta _{\eta _ t}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $. On $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, we have $\eta _ t\leq v+tf=\eta _0+tf$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\leq tf.  \] On $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $, we have $\eta _0\leq v$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\geq tf.  \] It follows that \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, 	heta _{\eta _0}^ n \leq t\int _ K f\, 	heta _{\eta _0}^ n  \] and \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, 	heta _{\eta _ t}^ n \geq t\int _ K f\, 	heta _{\eta _ t}^ n.  \] Thus, letting $t	o 0+$, we get the inequality \[  \varlimsup _{t	o 0+} rac{E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)}{t}\leq \int _ K f\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Similarly, for $t>0$, we have \[   egin{aligned} & E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)-P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n\  \geq &  t\int _ K f\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $t	o 0+$, we find \[  \varliminf _{t	o 0+} rac{E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)ight)-E_{	heta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)}{t}\geq \int _ K f\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Here we used the following elementary continuity consequence: \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)-t\| f\| _{C^0(K)} \leq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) \leq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)  \] for $t>0$, and hence $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$ almost everywhere when $t	o 0+$. Next we claim that \[  \int _ K f\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}\leq \lim _{t	o 0+} \int _ K f\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n.  \] Choose a continuous extension $	ilde f\in C^0(X)$ of $f$. Since 14.2.2 , corollary 14.1.9 show that all the measures appearing here are carried by $K$, the integrals over $K$ against $f$ are the same as the integrals over $X$ against $	ilde f$. Thus corollary 2.4.9 applies. We conclude ( 14.32 ). $\square$ Lemma 14.2.6 . Assume that $\{ 	heta \} $ represents a big cohomology class. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a weighted subset $(K,v)$ of $X$. There exists a uniformly bounded increasing sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ and a uniformly bounded decreasing sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$, such that 14.39  egin{equation} \label{eq:unf_bd_vj} \sup _ X |v_ j^-|\leq C,\quad \sup _ X |v_ j^+|\leq C \end{equation} for some constant $C$ depending only on $\| v\| _{C^0(K)}$, $X$, $K$ and $	heta +\omega $. Furthermore, for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and any $\delta \in [0,1]$ we have the following: We have \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v_ j^+) \searrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v),  \] and \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j) 
earrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)  \] almost everywhere. Suppose in addition that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, then \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^-)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v),\quad \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^+)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Step 1 . First we construct $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Let \[  C_{K,v} \coloneqq \sup \left\{ \sup _ X \eta : \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega ), \eta |_ K \leq vight\} .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, we have $C_{K,v} \in \mathbb {R}$ by 1.5.5 . Set \[  M_{K,v}\coloneqq \max \{ C_{K,v}+1,\sup _ K v\} .  \] Now define $\widetilde v \colon X 	o \mathbb {R}$ as \[  \widetilde{v}(x)=\left\{   egin{aligned}  v(x),& \quad x\in K;\  M_{K,v},& \quad x\in X\setminus K. \end{aligned} ight.  \] Since $M_{K,v}\geq \sup _ K v$, the function $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous. Therefore there exists an increasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^-_ j 
earrow \widetilde v$ and \[  \| v_ j^-\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| 	ilde{v}\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] The right-hand side can clearly be bounded by a constant as in ( 14.39 ). Step 2 . We construct $(v_ j^+)_ j$. Since \[  h \coloneqq P_{	heta + \omega ,K}[V_{	heta +\omega }](v) \lor \left(\inf _ K v -1ight)  \] is usc, there exists a decreasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^+_ j \searrow h$. We may guarantee that \[  \| v^+_ j\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| h\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] Note that $\inf _ K v-1\leq h\leq C_{K,v} \lor (\inf _ K v-1)$. So ( 14.39 ) is satisfied. Step 3 . We finish the proof. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\delta \in [0,1]$. Note that 2 follows from corollary 14.1.9 , 14.1.10 , proposition 3.1.47 and 1 . Let us prove 1 . Step 3.1 . We prove 1 for $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Observe that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)$ is increasing in $j\geq 1$, and \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)\leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] We claim that 14.42  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetapdeltaomega_temp1} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight) 
earrow P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)\quad 	extup{a.e.}. \end{equation} Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )$ be a potential such that $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq v$. Take some $\epsilon >0$. Then, since $\eta $ is upper semicontinuous, $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous and $\eta < \epsilon +\widetilde v$, compactness gives $j_0>0$ such that $\eta < \epsilon + v^-_ j$ for $j \geq j_0$. Hence, \[  \eta \leq \epsilon +P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)  \] for $j\geq j_0$. Therefore, \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)+\epsilon .  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, we find \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight).  \] Since $\eta $ is arbitrary, ( 14.42 ) follows. Step 3.2 . We prove 1 for $(v^+_ j)_ j$. Note that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^+_ j)$ is decreasing in $j$, and 14.43  egin{equation} \label{eq:defchilimPthetadeltaomega} \chi \coloneqq \lim _{j	o \infty } P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_ jight) \geq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} In particular, $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )_{>0}$, since $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)$ has the same singularity types as $P_{	heta + \delta \omega }[\varphi ]$ by 14.1.10 . Observe that \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v_ j^+ight)\leq v_ j^+  \] for all $j\geq 1$, since $v_ j^+$ is continuous. Thus, $\chi \leq h$. On the other hand, $h|_ K\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. So in particular, $\chi |_{K}\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. On the other hand, \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_1ight)\sim _ P \varphi  \] by 14.1.10 . Hence, by corollary 14.1.8 , \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] Therefore, ( 14.43 ) is an equality. $\square$ Proposition 14.2.7 . Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then the following hold: If $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 14.44  egin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphij1} P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} If $\varphi _ j 
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere then \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) 	extup{ a.e.}.  \] Proof. We only give the proof for the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes; the proof for the relative $P$-envelopes is identical, replacing $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ by $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ and using corollary 14.1.8 for the final candidate condition. Set \[  \eta _ j\coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad \eta \coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] By 14.1.10 , $d_ S(\eta _ j,P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ and $d_ S(\eta ,P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ for all $j$. Moreover, theorem 6.2.27 gives \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] in case 1 , and the same convergence holds in case 2 by corollary 6.2.9 and theorem 6.2.27 . Consequently, $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta $ in both cases. Assume first that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is decreasing and $\eta _ j\geq \eta $. Let $\eta _\infty \coloneqq \inf _ j \eta _ j$. The Monge–Ampère masses of $\eta _ j$ converge to the mass of $\eta $, by the preceding $d_ S$-convergence and theorem 6.2.17 . Since $\eta _ j\geq \eta _\infty \geq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ X	heta _{\eta _\infty }^ n=\int _ X	heta _\eta ^ n.  \] Hence $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta _\infty $ by corollary 6.2.11 . The uniqueness of the $d_ S$-limit gives $d_ S(\eta _\infty ,\eta )=0$. Since $\eta _\infty \geq \eta $, proposition 6.2.4 implies $\eta _\infty \sim _ P \eta $. In particular, $\eta _\infty \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 6.1.9 . The condition $\eta _\infty \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere is inherited from the $\eta _ j$'s, so $\eta _\infty $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. Thus $\eta _\infty \leq \eta $, and the reverse inequality was already observed. This proves the $\mathcal{I}$-part of 1 . Assume next that $\varphi _ j
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is increasing and $\eta _ j\leq \eta $. Put $	ilde\eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}_ j \eta _ j$. By corollary 14.1.6 and corollary 6.2.9 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}	ilde\eta $. The $d_ S$-convergence above therefore gives $d_ S(	ilde\eta ,\eta )=0$, hence $	ilde\eta \sim _ P \eta $ by proposition 6.2.4 . In particular, $	ilde\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 6.1.9 . Also $	ilde\eta \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 1.2.5 . Hence $	ilde\eta $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$, so $	ilde\eta \leq \eta $. Since $\eta _ j\leq \eta $ for all $j$, this proves $\eta _ j
earrow \eta $ almost everywhere. $\square$

title: Definition 14.2.1
text: Definition 14.2.1 . A weighted subset of $X$ is a pair $(K,v)$ consisting of a closed non-pluripolar subset $K\subseteq X$ and a function $v\in C^0(K)$.

title: Lemma 14.2.2
text:
Lemma 14.2.2 . Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 14.23  egin{equation} \label{eq:intXminusKthetan_vanish} \int _{X\setminus K}	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0,\quad \int _ K \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K
eq vight\} }	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0. \end{equation} More precisely, we have 14.24  egin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPKuv} 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=vight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n. \end{equation} Proof.
