earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad \eta _ j|_ K\leq v	extup{ for all }j\geq 1.  \] Note that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)\sim V_{	heta }$ by 14.1.10 . Take $C>0$ so that \[  \left.\left( P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v) ight)ight|_ K-C\leq v.  \] Then we may replace $\eta _ j$ by $\eta _ j\lor (P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)-C)$ and assume that $\eta _ j\sim V_{	heta }$ for each $j$. In particular, $\eta _ j$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus S$. For each $j\geq 1$, let $\gamma _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be the balayage of $\eta _ j$ on $B$, defined in proposition 1.5.9 . Note that $(\gamma _ j)_ j$ is increasing due to proposition 1.2.15 . For the first equality in ( 14.23 ), we may assume that $B\Subset X\setminus (S \cup K)$. It suffices to show that $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n$ does not charge $B$. Since $B$ lies outside $K$ by assumption, we also have $\gamma _ j|_ K=\eta _ j|_ K \leq v$ for all $j\geq 1$. In particular, $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. It follows that $\gamma _ j 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$ almost everywhere as well. Testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$ and using theorem 2.4.7 , we find that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$, as desired. We next prove the second equality in ( 14.23 ). The proof is essentially the same as that of 2.4.13 . It suffices to show that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge the set $K\cap \{ P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K<v\} $. Let $x\in (X\setminus S) \cap K$ be a point such that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)(x)<v(x)-\epsilon $ for some $\epsilon >0$. We may assume that $x\in B$ and $B'$ is small enough, so that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_{\overline{B'}}<v(x)-\epsilon $. $v|_{\overline{B'}\cap K}>v(x)-\epsilon $. By 1 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{\partial B}\leq v(x)-\epsilon $, hence by proposition 1.2.15 , $\gamma _ j|_ B\leq v(x)-\epsilon $. By 2 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{B\cap K}\leq v|_{B\cap K}$. On the other hand, $\gamma _ j|_{K\setminus B}=\eta _{j}|_{K\setminus B}\leq v|_{K\setminus B}$. Therefore, $\gamma _ j|_ K\leq v$. It follows again that $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Therefore, we conclude as in the previous paragraph that $\gamma _ j
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Thus, testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$, we conclude that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$ again by theorem 2.4.7 . Step 2 . We handle the general case. By corollary 14.1.11 , \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ]\left(P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight).  \] Now corollary 3.1.8 gives \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=vight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where in the second inequality we have used Step 1. Hence ( 14.24 ) follows, and a fortiori ( 14.23 ) follows as well. $\square$

14.23 \begin{equation} \label{eq:intXminusKthetan_vanish} \int _{X\setminus K}\theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0,\quad \int _ K \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K\neq v\right\} }\theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n=0. \end{equation}

14.24 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetaPKuv} \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](v)|_ K=v\right\} }\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](v)}^ n. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 14.2.3
text: Corollary 14.2.3 . Let $v\in C^0(K)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.27 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetandoesnotcharge1} \begin{aligned}  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)<v\right\} }\theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}=&  0,\\  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)<v\right\} }\theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=&  0. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Proof. The first equation in ( 14.27 ) follows from 14.2.2 . For the second, it suffices to observe that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)=P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)=P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right](v)  \] by corollary 14.1.9 . $\square$

14.27 \begin{equation} \label{eq:thetandoesnotcharge1} \begin{aligned}  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)<v\right\} }\theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}=&  0,\\  \int _{(X\setminus K)\cup \left\{ P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)<v\right\} }\theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=&  0. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

title: Definition 14.2.4
text: Definition 14.2.4 . Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we define the partial equilibrium energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }\colon C^0(K)\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ as follows: given $v \in C^0(K)$, we set 14.30 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)\coloneqq E_{\theta }^{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 14.2.5
text: Proposition 14.2.5 . Let $v,f \in C^0(K)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\mathbb {R}\ni t \mapsto \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf)$ is differentiable and 14.31 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ddtI} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf) = \int _ K f\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)} \end{equation} for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$. Proof. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model by replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Note that it suffices to prove ( 14.31 ) at $t=0$, which is equivalent to 14.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_1} \lim _{t\to 0}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} It suffices to prove the right derivative at $0$ for an arbitrary $f$; applying the same argument to $-f$ then gives the left derivative. In other words, we need to prove that 14.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_2} \lim _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} We first reduce the proof of ( 14.33 ) to the case $f\leq 0$. Assume that this case is known. Choose $A\in \mathbb R$ such that $f-A\leq 0$ on $K$. Since for any $t>0$, \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\Bigl ( v+t(f-A) \Bigr )= P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf)-tA,  \] then we have \[  \int _ K f\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=\int _ K (f-A)\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}+A\int _ X \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] By ( 3.71 ), for any $t>0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\Bigl (P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\left(v+t(f-A)\right)\Bigr )=E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-tA\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] So the limit in ( 14.33 ) exists and is equal to the left-hand side of ( 14.33 ) with $f-A$ in place of $f$ plus $A\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$. So ( 14.33 ) for $f-A$ implies the desired formula for $f$ in view of 14.1.10 and the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 . Hence we may assume that $f\leq 0$. Fix $t>0$. Set \[  \eta _ t\coloneqq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf),\quad \eta _0\coloneqq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v).  \] By the comparison principle ( 3.59 ) and proposition 3.1.45 , we find \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\varphi }(\eta _ t)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }(\eta _0) ={}& \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{i=0}^ n\int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\,  \theta _{\eta _ t}^ i\wedge \theta _{\eta _0}^{n-i}\\  \leq {}&  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] By 14.2.2 and corollary 14.1.9 , the measure $\theta _{\eta _0}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, and the measure $\theta _{\eta _ t}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $. On $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, we have $\eta _ t\leq v+tf=\eta _0+tf$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\leq tf.  \] On $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $, we have $\eta _0\leq v$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\geq tf.  \] It follows that \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n \leq t\int _ K f\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n  \] and \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n \geq t\int _ K f\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n.  \] Thus, letting $t\to 0+$, we get the inequality \[  \varlimsup _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}\leq \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Similarly, for $t>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)-P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n\\  \geq &  t\int _ K f\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $t\to 0+$, we find \[  \varliminf _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}\geq \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Here we used the following elementary continuity consequence: \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)-t\| f\| _{C^0(K)} \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)  \] for $t>0$, and hence $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) \nearrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$ almost everywhere when $t\to 0+$. Next we claim that \[  \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}\leq \lim _{t\to 0+} \int _ K f\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n.  \] Choose a continuous extension $\tilde f\in C^0(X)$ of $f$. Since 14.2.2 , corollary 14.1.9 show that all the measures appearing here are carried by $K$, the integrals over $K$ against $f$ are the same as the integrals over $X$ against $\tilde f$. Thus corollary 2.4.9 applies. We conclude ( 14.32 ). $\square$
14.31 \begin{equation} \label{eq:ddtI} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf) = \int _ K f\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)} \end{equation}

14.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_1} \lim _{t\to 0}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation}

14.33 \begin{equation} \label{eq:to_prove_2} \lim _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 14.2.6
text:
Lemma 14.2.6 . Assume that $\{ 	heta \} $ represents a big cohomology class. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a weighted subset $(K,v)$ of $X$. There exists a uniformly bounded increasing sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ and a uniformly bounded decreasing sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$, such that 14.39  egin{equation} \label{eq:unf_bd_vj} \sup _ X |v_ j^-|\leq C,\quad \sup _ X |v_ j^+|\leq C \end{equation} for some constant $C$ depending only on $\| v\| _{C^0(K)}$, $X$, $K$ and $	heta +\omega $. Furthermore, for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and any $\delta \in [0,1]$ we have the following: We have \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v_ j^+) \searrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v),  \] and \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j) 
earrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)  \] almost everywhere. Suppose in addition that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, then \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^-)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v),\quad \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^+)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Step 1 . First we construct $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Let \[  C_{K,v} \coloneqq \sup \left\{ \sup _ X \eta : \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega ), \eta |_ K \leq vight\} .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, we have $C_{K,v} \in \mathbb {R}$ by 1.5.5 . Set \[  M_{K,v}\coloneqq \max \{ C_{K,v}+1,\sup _ K v\} .  \] Now define $\widetilde v \colon X 	o \mathbb {R}$ as \[  \widetilde{v}(x)=\left\{   egin{aligned}  v(x),& \quad x\in K;\  M_{K,v},& \quad x\in X\setminus K. \end{aligned} ight.  \] Since $M_{K,v}\geq \sup _ K v$, the function $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous. Therefore there exists an increasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^-_ j 
earrow \widetilde v$ and \[  \| v_ j^-\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| 	ilde{v}\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] The right-hand side can clearly be bounded by a constant as in ( 14.39 ). Step 2 . We construct $(v_ j^+)_ j$. Since \[  h \coloneqq P_{	heta + \omega ,K}[V_{	heta +\omega }](v) \lor \left(\inf _ K v -1ight)  \] is usc, there exists a decreasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^+_ j \searrow h$. We may guarantee that \[  \| v^+_ j\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| h\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] Note that $\inf _ K v-1\leq h\leq C_{K,v} \lor (\inf _ K v-1)$. So ( 14.39 ) is satisfied. Step 3 . We finish the proof. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\delta \in [0,1]$. Note that 2 follows from corollary 14.1.9 , 14.1.10 , proposition 3.1.47 and 1 . Let us prove 1 . Step 3.1 . We prove 1 for $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Observe that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)$ is increasing in $j\geq 1$, and \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)\leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] We claim that 14.42  egin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetapdeltaomega_temp1} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight) 
earrow P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)\quad 	extup{a.e.}. \end{equation} Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )$ be a potential such that $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq v$. Take some $\epsilon >0$. Then, since $\eta $ is upper semicontinuous, $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous and $\eta < \epsilon +\widetilde v$, compactness gives $j_0>0$ such that $\eta < \epsilon + v^-_ j$ for $j \geq j_0$. Hence, \[  \eta \leq \epsilon +P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)  \] for $j\geq j_0$. Therefore, \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)+\epsilon .  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, we find \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight).  \] Since $\eta $ is arbitrary, ( 14.42 ) follows. Step 3.2 . We prove 1 for $(v^+_ j)_ j$. Note that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^+_ j)$ is decreasing in $j$, and 14.43  egin{equation} \label{eq:defchilimPthetadeltaomega} \chi \coloneqq \lim _{j	o \infty } P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_ jight) \geq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} In particular, $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )_{>0}$, since $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)$ has the same singularity types as $P_{	heta + \delta \omega }[\varphi ]$ by 14.1.10 . Observe that \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v_ j^+ight)\leq v_ j^+  \] for all $j\geq 1$, since $v_ j^+$ is continuous. Thus, $\chi \leq h$. On the other hand, $h|_ K\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. So in particular, $\chi |_{K}\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. On the other hand, \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_1ight)\sim _ P \varphi  \] by 14.1.10 . Hence, by corollary 14.1.8 , \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] Therefore, ( 14.43 ) is an equality. $\square$
14.39 \begin{equation} \label{eq:unf_bd_vj} \sup _ X |v_ j^-|\leq C,\quad \sup _ X |v_ j^+|\leq C \end{equation}

14.42 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Pthetapdeltaomega_temp1} P_{\theta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ j\right) \nearrow P_{\theta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)\quad \textup{a.e.}. \end{equation}

14.43 \begin{equation} \label{eq:defchilimPthetadeltaomega} \chi \coloneqq \lim _{j\to \infty } P_{\theta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_ j\right) \geq P_{\theta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 14.2.7
text:
Proposition 14.2.7 . Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then the following hold: If $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 14.44  egin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphij1} P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} If $\varphi _ j 
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere then \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) 	extup{ a.e.}.  \] Proof. We only give the proof for the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes; the proof for the relative $P$-envelopes is identical, replacing $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ by $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ and using corollary 14.1.8 for the final candidate condition. Set \[  \eta _ j\coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad \eta \coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] By 14.1.10 , $d_ S(\eta _ j,P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ and $d_ S(\eta ,P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ for all $j$. Moreover, theorem 6.2.27 gives \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] in case 1 , and the same convergence holds in case 2 by corollary 6.2.9 and theorem 6.2.27 . Consequently, $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta $ in both cases. Assume first that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is decreasing and $\eta _ j\geq \eta $. Let $\eta _\infty \coloneqq \inf _ j \eta _ j$. The Monge–Ampère masses of $\eta _ j$ converge to the mass of $\eta $, by the preceding $d_ S$-convergence and theorem 6.2.17 . Since $\eta _ j\geq \eta _\infty \geq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 2.4.8 gives \[  \int _ X	heta _{\eta _\infty }^ n=\int _ X	heta _\eta ^ n.  \] Hence $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta _\infty $ by corollary 6.2.11 . The uniqueness of the $d_ S$-limit gives $d_ S(\eta _\infty ,\eta )=0$. Since $\eta _\infty \geq \eta $, proposition 6.2.4 implies $\eta _\infty \sim _ P \eta $. In particular, $\eta _\infty \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 6.1.9 . The condition $\eta _\infty \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere is inherited from the $\eta _ j$'s, so $\eta _\infty $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. Thus $\eta _\infty \leq \eta $, and the reverse inequality was already observed. This proves the $\mathcal{I}$-part of 1 . Assume next that $\varphi _ j
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is increasing and $\eta _ j\leq \eta $. Put $	ilde\eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}_ j \eta _ j$. By corollary 14.1.6 and corollary 6.2.9 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}	ilde\eta $. The $d_ S$-convergence above therefore gives $d_ S(	ilde\eta ,\eta )=0$, hence $	ilde\eta \sim _ P \eta $ by proposition 6.2.4 . In particular, $	ilde\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 6.1.9 . Also $	ilde\eta \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 1.2.5 . Hence $	ilde\eta $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$, so $	ilde\eta \leq \eta $. Since $\eta _ j\leq \eta $ for all $j$, this proves $\eta _ j
earrow \eta $ almost everywhere. $\square$

14.44 \begin{equation} \label{eq:PthetaKvarphij1} P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) \searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) \searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation}

title: 14.3 Quantization of partial equilibrium measures
text: 14.3 Quantization of partial equilibrium measures Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$, and let $h$ be a Hermitian metric on $L$. Set $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Let $(T,h_ T)$ be a Hermitian line bundle on $X$.

title: 14.3.1 Bernstein–Markov measures
text: 14.3.1 Bernstein–Markov measures Let $K\subseteq X$ be a closed non-pluripolar subset, and $v\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be a measurable function. Definition 14.3.1 . Let $\mu $ be a Borel probability measure on $K$. We introduce the following functions on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), with values possibly equal to $\infty $: 14.45 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Nkvmu_norm} \begin{aligned}  N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \coloneqq &  \left(\int _ K h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \mathrm{e}^{-kv} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2},\\  N^ k_{v,K}(s) \coloneqq &  \sup _{K\setminus \{ v=-\infty \} } \left( h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Observe that if $\mu $ puts no mass on $\{ v=-\infty \} $ then we always have 14.48 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Nkinfcomp} N^ k_{v,\mu }(s)\leq N^ k_{v,K}(s). \end{equation} We start with the following elementary observation: Lemma 14.3.2 . Let $v_1,v_2\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be two measurable functions such that $v_1\leq v_2$; $\{ v_1=-\infty \} =\{ v_2=-\infty \} $. Then for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), we have \[  N_{v_1,K}^ k(s)\geq N_{v_2,K}^ k(s).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from the definition ( 14.45 ). $\square$ Definition 14.3.3 . Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. A Borel probability measure $\mu $ on $K$ is Bernstein–Markov with respect to $(K,v)$ if for each $\epsilon >0$, there is a constant $C_\epsilon >0$ such that 14.49 \begin{equation} \label{eq:BM} N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k} N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \end{equation} for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ and any $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We write $\mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ for the set of Bernstein–Markov measures with respect to $(K,v)$. As pointed out in [ BBWN11 ] , any volume form on $X$ is Bernstein–Markov with respect to $(X,v)$, with $v \in C^\infty (X)$. Proposition 14.3.4 . Assume that $(K,v)$ is a weighted subset of $X$. Then $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. For any $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. Proof. 1 As $v$ is bounded, $N^ k_{v,K}$ is clearly finite on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. In order to show that it is a norm, it suffices to show that for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$, $N^ k_{v,K}(s)=0$ implies that $s=0$. In fact, we have $s|_ K=0$, hence $s=0$ by the connectedness of $X$ and the assumption that $K$ is non-pluripolar. 2 As $v$ is bounded, clearly $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is finite and satisfies the triangle inequality. Non-degeneracy follows from the fact that $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm and ( 14.49 ). $\square$

text: Lemma 14.3.2 . Let $v_1,v_2\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be two measurable functions such that $v_1\leq v_2$; $\{ v_1=-\infty \} =\{ v_2=-\infty \} $. Then for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), we have \[  N_{v_1,K}^ k(s)\geq N_{v_2,K}^ k(s).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from the definition ( 14.45 ). $\square$

title: 14.3.2 Partial Bergman kernels
text:
14.3.2 Partial Bergman kernels In this section, we fix a weighted subset $(K,v)$ of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Definition 14.3.5 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, we introduce the partial Bergman kernels of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) as follows: For any $k\geq 1$, we introduce 14.50  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }(x) \coloneqq \sup \left\{ h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}(x):s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight),ight.\  \left. N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \leq 1 ight\} ,\quad x\in K. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We extend $B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }$ to the whole $X$ by setting it to be $0$ outside $K$. The partial Bergman measures of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) are defined as 14.53  egin{equation}   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \coloneqq  rac{n!}{k^ n} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \, \mathrm{d}\mu \end{equation} for each $k\geq 1$. Remark 14.3.6 . Recall that in the definition of $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$, the singular metric $\varphi $ only appears through the conditions $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The pointwise norm used to define $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$ and $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is defined via $v$ not $\varphi $. This leads to the following seemingly paradoxical consequence, if $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }\leq  eta ^ k_{v,\psi ,\mu }\quad  orall \, k\geq 1.  \] We shall apply this consequence without further mention in the sequel. Observe that \[  \int _ X  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }= rac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight).  \] In particular, 14.54  egin{equation} \label{eq:betaint_conv} \lim _{k	o \infty }\int _ X  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }=\operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _{\varphi }ight)=\int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \end{equation} by theorem 7.4.2 and 14.1.10 . The goal of this section is to improve this result to the convergence of the Bergman kernels themselves: Theorem 14.3.7 . Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then 14.55  egin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconvgeneral}  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty . \end{equation} The proof will be given at the end of this subsection. We shall prove a few preliminaries at first. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that \[  \int _ X \omega ^ n = 1.  \] Proposition 14.3.8 . Assume here that $K=X$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. If $v \in C^\infty (X)$, then 14.56  egin{equation} \label{eq:pbmconvanaly}  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty . \end{equation} Proof. The equality part in ( 14.56 ) follows from corollary 14.1.9 . It remains to prove the weak convergence. Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n})_ k$. In view of ( 14.54 ), it suffices to show that 14.57  egin{equation} \label{eq:muleq_temp1} 	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n. \end{equation} We can obtain an upper bound of $	au $ via the observation: \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq  eta ^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n}.  \] After replacing $\varphi $ by $V_{	heta }$, the corresponding problem is handled by [ Theorem 1.2 , Ber11 ] , giving us \[   eta ^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n} ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n \quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty ,  \] where the last identity is due to proposition 3.1.21 . We obtain that 14.58  egin{equation} \label{eq:Bergmanmeasure} 	au \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n. \end{equation} Now observe that it suffices to show that 14.59  egin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp1} 	au \left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} =0. \end{equation} Assuming this, then ( 14.58 ) further gives \[  	au \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)= vight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n= 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n,  \] where the equality follows from proposition 3.1.21 , and ( 14.57 ) follows. It now remains to argue ( 14.59 ). Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Observe that \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) \sim \varphi  \] for all $\epsilon \geq 0$ by 14.1.10 and proposition 3.2.15 . The family $P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)$ is decreasing as $\epsilon 	o 0+$. Let \[  \chi \coloneqq \inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Then $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ since $\chi \geq P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)$. Moreover $\chi \leq v$ and $\chi \preceq \varphi $. Hence \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Thus, equality holds, and \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)\searrow P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] In other words, \[  \left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} = igcup _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}}\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} .  \] So in order to show ( 14.59 ), we may fix $\epsilon >0$ and argue that 14.60  egin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp2} 	au \left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} =0. \end{equation} Let $k\geq 1$, and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(k\varphi ))$ be a section such that $N^ k_{v,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1$. Then by [ Lemma 4.1 , Ber11 ] , there exists $C>0$ such that \[  h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv} \leq B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq B^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n} \leq k^ n C.  \] This implies that \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \leq v +  rac{\log C }{k} + n  rac{\log k}{ k }.  \] We define $\varphi _ k$ as in proposition 1.8.13 . Take $\alpha _ k
earrow 1$ as in proposition 1.8.13 . After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $X$. After replacing $\alpha _ k$ by a subsequence, we also have $\alpha _ k\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\epsilon \omega )$ for all $k>0$, and $\alpha _ k\varphi \searrow \varphi $. Then \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\preceq \varphi _ k\preceq \alpha _ k\varphi .  \] We notice that $ rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X, 	heta + \epsilon \omega )$ for all $k \geq k_0(\epsilon )$. Indeed, \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}\left(X,	heta + k^{-1} c_1(T,h_ T)ight)  \] by proposition 1.8.4 . In particular, \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)- rac{\log C}{k}-n rac{\log k}{k}\leq P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v).  \] Now taking supremum over all candidates $s$, we obtain that 14.61  egin{equation} \label{eq:smooth_Berg_est} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq C k^ n \mathrm{e}^{k \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v)-vight)},\quad k \geq k_0. \end{equation} Now we prove ( 14.60 ). First observe that $\alpha _ k\varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 6.2.14 . Thus, by proposition 14.2.7 , \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) \searrow P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)  \] and we get that \[   igcup _{k=1}^{\infty }\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) < vight\} =\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} .  \] It suffices to show that $	au $ does not put mass on the set $\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v\} $ for each fixed $m$. Fix a positive rational $\delta >0$, it suffices to show that $	au $ puts no mass on $F\coloneqq \{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v-\delta \} $. Note that $F$ is open, and ( 14.61 ) gives $ eta ^\ell _{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n}(F)	o 0$. Therefore, $	au $ puts no mass on $F$ as well, proving ( 14.60 ). $\square$ Definition 14.3.9 . Take $k\geq 1$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, let $\operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ be the space of norms on the vector space $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi } \colon \operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )) 	o \mathbb R$ be the partial Donaldson functional : 14.62  egin{equation}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(H) =  rac{n!}{k^{n+1}} \log  rac{\operatorname{vol}\{ s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) : H(s) \leq 1\} }{\operatorname{vol}\left\{ s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) : N^ k_{0,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1ight\} }, \end{equation} where $\operatorname{vol}$ is a Lebesgue measure on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The normalization does not matter. Proposition 14.3.10 . Let $w,w' \in C^0(X)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then 14.63  egin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure} \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) ight)= \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation} In particular, 14.64  egin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure2} \lim _{k	o \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 14.3.4 , for any $k\geq 1$, $N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}$ and $N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 14.63 ) make sense. We first assume that $w,w'\in C^\infty (X)$. To start, we make the following observation: \[   egin{aligned}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})& = \int _0^1  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\omega ^ n})\, \mathrm{d}t\ &  = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \,  eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\,  \mathrm{d}t. \end{aligned}  \] The second equality follows from differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}$: \[   rac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathcal L_{k,\varphi } \left(N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}ight)=\int _ X (w-w')\,  eta ^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}.  \] By proposition 14.3.8 , we have \[  \lim _{k	o \infty }\int _ X (w-w') \,  eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}=\int _ X (w-w')\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n.  \] By theorem 7.4.2 , we have \[   igl |\int _ X (w-w') eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n} igr | \leq C \sup _ X |w - w'|.  \] Hence, by the dominated convergence theorem we obtain that \[   egin{aligned}  \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})ight) & = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n \, \mathrm{d}t\ &  = \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line we have used proposition 14.2.5 . This proves ( 14.63 ) for smooth weights. For general $w,w'\in C^0(X)$, choose smooth functions $w_ j,w'_ j$ converging uniformly to $w,w'$, respectively. If $\| w_ j-w\| _{C^0}\leq \delta _ j$, then \[  \mathrm{e}^{-k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}\leq N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n}\leq \mathrm{e}^{k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n},  \] and hence \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})ight| \leq  rac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)\delta _ j.  \] The same estimate holds for $w'_ j$ and $w'$. Moreover, proposition 14.2.5 shows that the energy side is Lipschitz with respect to the uniform norm of the weight. Letting first $k	o \infty $ in the smooth case, and then $j	o \infty $, proves ( 14.63 ) for continuous weights. Equation ( 14.64 ) again follows by taking $w'=0$. $\square$ Lemma 14.3.11 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 14.69  egin{equation} \label{eq:Bern_Mark_implies} \lim _{k	o \infty }  ig ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu }) ig ) = 0\, . \end{equation} Proof. By ( 14.48 ) and ( 14.49 ), for every $\epsilon >0$ and all $k\geq 1$, \[  N^ k_{v,\mu }\leq N^ k_{v,K}\leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}N^ k_{v,\mu }.  \] The corresponding unit balls therefore satisfy inclusions with radii differing by at most the factor $C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}$. Taking logarithmic volumes and multiplying by $n!k^{-n-1}$ gives \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })ight| \leq  rac{2n!}{k^{n+1}} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)(\log C_\epsilon +\epsilon k).  \] The right-hand side has limsup at most $2\epsilon \operatorname{vol}(	heta _\varphi )$ by theorem 7.4.2 . Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$ proves ( 14.69 ). $\square$ Corollary 14.3.12 . Let $w \in C^0(X)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k	o \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w).  \] Proof. This follows from 14.3.11 and proposition 14.3.10 : indeed $\omega ^ n \in \mathrm{BM}(X,0)$, hence $\omega ^ n\in \mathrm{BM}(X,w)$ as $w$ is bounded. $\square$ It would be helpful to consider the following auxiliary functions: \[   egin{aligned}  P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)\coloneqq &  \sup \Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \eta |_ K \leq v 	extup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} ,\  P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\coloneqq &  \sup \Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ): \eta |_ K \leq v 	extup{ and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{aligned}  \] We note the following maximum principles that follow from the above definitions: Lemma 14.3.13 . Let $v\in C^0(K)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, and $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then 14.72  egin{equation} \label{eq:max_princ} \sup _ K (\eta -v) = \sup _{\{ \eta 
eq -\infty \} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)=\sup _{\left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty ight\} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight). \end{equation} Proof. We prove the first equality first. We write $S=\{ \eta =-\infty \} $. By definition, $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K\leq v$, so \[  \left.\left(\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)ight|_{K\setminus S}\geq \eta |_{K\setminus S}-v|_{K\setminus S}\, .  \] This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \leq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight).  \] Conversely, observe that $\sup _ K(\eta -v)>-\infty $ as $K$ is non-pluripolar. It follows that $\eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)$. Hence, 14.73  egin{equation} \label{eq:etaminussupK_temp1} \eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)\leq P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \geq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight),  \] finishing the proof of the first identity in ( 14.72 ). In order to prove the latter identity, observe that \[  \left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) =-\infty ight\}  \subseteq S  \] as a consequence of ( 14.73 ). On $\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty \} \cap S$, we have $\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)=-\infty $. Hence the last equality of ( 14.72 ) also follows. $\square$ Proposition 14.3.14 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$, $(K',v')$ be two weighted subsets of $X$. Then 14.74  egin{equation} \label{eq:LkdiffconvtoI} \lim _{k	o \infty } \left( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v',K'}) ight) = \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)-\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K'}^{\varphi }(v'). \end{equation} In particular, 14.75  egin{equation} \label{eq:Lkconv} \lim _{k	o \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v). \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 14.3.4 , for any $k>0$, $N^ k_{v,K}$ and $N^ k_{v',K'}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 14.74 ) make sense. Moreover, ( 14.75 ) is just a special case of ( 14.74 ) for $K'=X$ and $v'= 0$. To prove ( 14.74 ) it is enough to show that for any fixed $w \in C^\infty (X)$ we have 14.76  egin{equation} \label{eq:inproofLdiffsmw} \lim _{k	o \infty }  ig ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})  ig ) = \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) - \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} For $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, $	heta _{(1-\epsilon )\varphi }$ is still a Kähler current. Let us fix such $\epsilon $, along with an arbitrary $\epsilon ' \in (0,1)$. Let $(v^-_{j})_ j$ and $(v^+_{j})_ j$ be the sequences of smooth functions constructed in 14.2.6 for the data $(K,v)$. By proposition 1.8.13 there exists $k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ') \in \mathbb N$ such that \[   rac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi ,  \] and $ rac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta + \epsilon '\omega )$ for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$, as long as $k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ')$. In particular, 14.3.13 gives that \[   egin{aligned}  N^ k_{P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v,K}(s),\  N^ k_{P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s),\  N^ k_{P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s). \end{aligned}  \] As \[  P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-) \leq P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v) \leq P'_{	heta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),  \] where the second inequality follows from 14.2.6 and the fact that $P'=P$ for the global continuous obstacles $v_ j^\pm $. By 14.3.2 we have \[  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s) \leq N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s), \quad s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T \otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )), k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] Composing with $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }$ we arrive at \[  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})\, , \quad k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] For any $j>0$, by corollary 14.3.12 we get \[   egin{aligned}  \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^-_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)=&  \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k	o \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\  \leq &  \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\  =&  \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^+_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{aligned}  \] Using 14.2.6 , we can let $j 	o \infty $ to arrive at \[   egin{split}  \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w) & \leq \varliminf _{k	o \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\ & \leq \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})ight)\ &  \leq \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{split}  \] Hence, ( 14.76 ) follows. $\square$ Corollary 14.3.15 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })= \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Our claim follows from proposition 14.3.14 and 14.3.11 . $\square$ Proposition 14.3.16 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty .  \] Proof. For $w\in C^0(X)$, let $f_ k,g\colon \mathbb {R}ightarrow \mathbb {R}$ ($k\geq 1$) be defined as \[  f_ k(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }),\quad g(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tw).  \] By corollary 14.3.15 , for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } f_ k(t)= g(t).  \] Here we use that $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v+tw)$ for all fixed $t$, which follows from $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ and the boundedness of $tw$ on $K$. Note that $f_ k$ is concave by Hölder's inequality. For each $k$, the function $f_ k$ is differentiable and \[  f_ k'(0)=\int _ X w\,  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] This follows by differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }$. The function $g$ is differentiable at $0$ by proposition 14.2.5 , with \[  g'(0)=\int _ K w\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v)}.  \] Applying A.5.3 to the convex functions $-f_ k$ and $-g$ gives \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } f_ k'(0)=g'(0),  \] which is equivalent to $ eta ^ k_{v, \varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$, by proposition 14.2.5 . $\square$ Proposition 14.3.17 . Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ is such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 14.88  egin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconv1}  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as } k	o \infty . \end{equation} Proof. Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$. We claim that 14.89  egin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmuleq} 	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that this claim implies the conclusion. In fact, by theorem 7.4.2 , we have equality of the total masses, so equality holds in ( 14.89 ). As $	au $ is an arbitrary cluster point of the sequence $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$, we get ( 14.88 ). It remains to prove ( 14.89 ). Let $(\varphi _ j)$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. We may assume that $	heta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for all $j\geq 1$. By corollary 7.1.10 , we know that \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] The quasi-equisingular approximation is decreasing, so applying the decreasing case of proposition 14.2.7 to the limit $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, and using the definition of the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope, we get \[  P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] In particular, 14.90  egin{equation} \label{eq:inproofeqmass} \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \leq  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu }  \] for any $k \geq 1$. As $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, by proposition 14.3.16 , \[  	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,  \] for any $j \geq 1$ fixed. By ( 14.90 ) and the semicontinuity theorem theorem 2.4.7 , we have \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ nightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n  \] as $j	o \infty $. Therefore, ( 14.89 ) follows. $\square$ Proof of theorem 14.3.7 . By 14.1.10 and proposition 3.2.8 , the three potentials below have the same multiplier ideals. Hence \[   egin{aligned}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(kP_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})ight)\ & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I\left(kP_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)ight). \end{aligned}  \] This allows us to replace $\varphi $ with $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. By 2.4.19 , there exists a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $\varphi _ j
earrow \varphi $ a.e. and $	heta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for each $j\geq 1$. This gives \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu } \leq  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$. Then by proposition 14.3.17 , \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq 	au .  \] By proposition 14.2.7 and corollary 2.4.9 , we have \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n.  \] Hence, 14.93  egin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmulower} 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq 	au . \end{equation} A comparison of total masses using ( 14.54 ) gives that equality holds in ( 14.93 ). As $	au $ is arbitrary, we obtain ( 14.55 ). $\square$ Remark 14.3.18 . The results in this chapter can also be reformulated as the large deviation principle of a determinantal point process on $X$ using the Gärtner–Ellis theorem exactly as in [ Ber14 ] . We do not pursue this reformulation here.

title: Definition 14.3.5
text: Definition 14.3.5 . For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we introduce the partial Bergman kernels of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) as follows: For any $k\geq 1$, we introduce 14.50 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }(x) \coloneqq \sup \left\{ h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}(x):s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right),\right.\\  \left. N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \leq 1 \right\} ,\quad x\in K. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We extend $B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }$ to the whole $X$ by setting it to be $0$ outside $K$. The partial Bergman measures of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) are defined as 14.53 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \coloneqq \frac{n!}{k^ n} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \, \mathrm{d}\mu \end{equation} for each $k\geq 1$.

title: Remark 14.3.6
text: Remark 14.3.6 . Recall that in the definition of $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$, the singular metric $\varphi $ only appears through the conditions $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The pointwise norm used to define $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$ and $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is defined via $v$ not $\varphi $. This leads to the following seemingly paradoxical consequence, if $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }\leq \beta ^ k_{v,\psi ,\mu }\quad \forall \, k\geq 1.  \] We shall apply this consequence without further mention in the sequel.

14.54 \begin{equation} \label{eq:betaint_conv} \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }=\operatorname{vol}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right)=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \end{equation}

title: Theorem 14.3.7
text: Theorem 14.3.7 . Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 14.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconvgeneral} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof of theorem 14.3.7 . By 14.1.10 and proposition 3.2.8 , the three potentials below have the same multiplier ideals. Hence \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(kP_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})\right)\\ & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I\left(kP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\right). \end{aligned}  \] This allows us to replace $\varphi $ with $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. By 2.4.19 , there exists a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ j\nearrow \varphi $ a.e. and $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for each $j\geq 1$. This gives \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu } \leq \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$. Then by proposition 14.3.17 , \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq \tau .  \] By proposition 14.2.7 and corollary 2.4.9 , we have \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n.  \] Hence, 14.93 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmulower} \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq \tau . \end{equation} A comparison of total masses using ( 14.54 ) gives that equality holds in ( 14.93 ). As $\tau $ is arbitrary, we obtain ( 14.55 ). $\square$
14.55 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconvgeneral} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 14.3.8
text: Proposition 14.3.8 . Assume here that $K=X$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. If $v \in C^\infty (X)$, then 14.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbmconvanaly} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=\theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof. The equality part in ( 14.56 ) follows from corollary 14.1.9 . It remains to prove the weak convergence. Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n})_ k$. In view of ( 14.54 ), it suffices to show that 14.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muleq_temp1} \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n. \end{equation} We can obtain an upper bound of $\tau $ via the observation: \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq \beta ^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n}.  \] After replacing $\varphi $ by $V_{\theta }$, the corresponding problem is handled by [ Theorem 1.2 , Ber11 ] , giving us \[  \beta ^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n} \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n \quad \textup{as }k\to \infty ,  \] where the last identity is due to proposition 3.1.21 . We obtain that 14.58 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Bergmanmeasure} \tau \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n. \end{equation} Now observe that it suffices to show that 14.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp1} \tau \left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation} Assuming this, then ( 14.58 ) further gives \[  \tau \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)= v\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n= \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n,  \] where the equality follows from proposition 3.1.21 , and ( 14.57 ) follows. It now remains to argue ( 14.59 ). Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Observe that \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) \sim \varphi  \] for all $\epsilon \geq 0$ by 14.1.10 and proposition 3.2.15 . The family $P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)$ is decreasing as $\epsilon \to 0+$. Let \[  \chi \coloneqq \inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Then $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ since $\chi \geq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)$. Moreover $\chi \leq v$ and $\chi \preceq \varphi $. Hence \[  \chi \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Thus, equality holds, and \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)\searrow P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] In other words, \[  \left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =\bigcup _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}}\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} .  \] So in order to show ( 14.59 ), we may fix $\epsilon >0$ and argue that 14.60 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp2} \tau \left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation} Let $k\geq 1$, and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(k\varphi ))$ be a section such that $N^ k_{v,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1$. Then by [ Lemma 4.1 , Ber11 ] , there exists $C>0$ such that \[  h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv} \leq B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq B^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n} \leq k^ n C.  \] This implies that \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \leq v + \frac{\log C }{k} + n \frac{\log k}{ k }.  \] We define $\varphi _ k$ as in proposition 1.8.13 . Take $\alpha _ k\nearrow 1$ as in proposition 1.8.13 . After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $X$. After replacing $\alpha _ k$ by a subsequence, we also have $\alpha _ k\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon \omega )$ for all $k>0$, and $\alpha _ k\varphi \searrow \varphi $. Then \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\preceq \varphi _ k\preceq \alpha _ k\varphi .  \] We notice that $\frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X, \theta + \epsilon \omega )$ for all $k \geq k_0(\epsilon )$. Indeed, \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}\left(X,\theta + k^{-1} c_1(T,h_ T)\right)  \] by proposition 1.8.4 . In particular, \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)-\frac{\log C}{k}-n\frac{\log k}{k}\leq P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v).  \] Now taking supremum over all candidates $s$, we obtain that 14.61 \begin{equation} \label{eq:smooth_Berg_est} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq C k^ n \mathrm{e}^{k \left(P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v)-v\right)},\quad k \geq k_0. \end{equation} Now we prove ( 14.60 ). First observe that $\alpha _ k\varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 6.2.14 . Thus, by proposition 14.2.7 , \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) \searrow P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)  \] and we get that \[  \bigcup _{k=1}^{\infty }\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) < v\right\} =\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} .  \] It suffices to show that $\tau $ does not put mass on the set $\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v\} $ for each fixed $m$. Fix a positive rational $\delta >0$, it suffices to show that $\tau $ puts no mass on $F\coloneqq \{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v-\delta \} $. Note that $F$ is open, and ( 14.61 ) gives $\beta ^\ell _{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n}(F)\to 0$. Therefore, $\tau $ puts no mass on $F$ as well, proving ( 14.60 ). $\square$

14.56 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbmconvanaly} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=\theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation}
14.57 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muleq_temp1} \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n. \end{equation}
14.58 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Bergmanmeasure} \tau \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n. \end{equation}
14.59 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp1} \tau \left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation}
14.60 \begin{equation} \label{eq:muP0_temp2} \tau \left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation}

14.61 \begin{equation} \label{eq:smooth_Berg_est} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq C k^ n \mathrm{e}^{k \left(P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v)-v\right)},\quad k \geq k_0. \end{equation}

title: Definition 14.3.9
text: Definition 14.3.9 . Take $k\geq 1$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, let $\operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ be the space of norms on the vector space $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi } \colon \operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )) \to \mathbb R$ be the partial Donaldson functional : 14.62 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(H) = \frac{n!}{k^{n+1}} \log \frac{\operatorname{vol}\{ s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) : H(s) \leq 1\} }{\operatorname{vol}\left\{ s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) : N^ k_{0,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1\right\} }, \end{equation} where $\operatorname{vol}$ is a Lebesgue measure on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The normalization does not matter.

title: Proposition 14.3.10
text: Proposition 14.3.10 . Let $w,w' \in C^0(X)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then 14.63 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure} \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) \right)= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation} In particular, 14.64 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure2} \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 14.3.4 , for any $k\geq 1$, $N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}$ and $N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 14.63 ) make sense. We first assume that $w,w'\in C^\infty (X)$. To start, we make the following observation: \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})& = \int _0^1 \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\omega ^ n})\, \mathrm{d}t\\ &  = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, \beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\,  \mathrm{d}t. \end{aligned}  \] The second equality follows from differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}$: \[  \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathcal L_{k,\varphi } \left(N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}\right)=\int _ X (w-w')\, \beta ^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}.  \] By proposition 14.3.8 , we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X (w-w') \, \beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}=\int _ X (w-w')\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n.  \] By theorem 7.4.2 , we have \[  \bigl |\int _ X (w-w')\beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\bigr | \leq C \sup _ X |w - w'|.  \] Hence, by the dominated convergence theorem we obtain that \[  \begin{aligned}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})\right) & = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n \, \mathrm{d}t\\ &  = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line we have used proposition 14.2.5 . This proves ( 14.63 ) for smooth weights. For general $w,w'\in C^0(X)$, choose smooth functions $w_ j,w'_ j$ converging uniformly to $w,w'$, respectively. If $\| w_ j-w\| _{C^0}\leq \delta _ j$, then \[  \mathrm{e}^{-k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}\leq N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n}\leq \mathrm{e}^{k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n},  \] and hence \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})\right| \leq \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\delta _ j.  \] The same estimate holds for $w'_ j$ and $w'$. Moreover, proposition 14.2.5 shows that the energy side is Lipschitz with respect to the uniform norm of the weight. Letting first $k\to \infty $ in the smooth case, and then $j\to \infty $, proves ( 14.63 ) for continuous weights. Equation ( 14.64 ) again follows by taking $w'=0$. $\square$

14.63 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure} \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) \right)= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation}
14.64 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LdiffonXsmoothmeasure2} \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 14.3.11
text: Lemma 14.3.11 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 14.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Bern_Mark_implies} \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\big ) = 0\, . \end{equation} Proof. By ( 14.48 ) and ( 14.49 ), for every $\epsilon >0$ and all $k\geq 1$, \[  N^ k_{v,\mu }\leq N^ k_{v,K}\leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}N^ k_{v,\mu }.  \] The corresponding unit balls therefore satisfy inclusions with radii differing by at most the factor $C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}$. Taking logarithmic volumes and multiplying by $n!k^{-n-1}$ gives \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\right| \leq \frac{2n!}{k^{n+1}} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)(\log C_\epsilon +\epsilon k).  \] The right-hand side has limsup at most $2\epsilon \operatorname{vol}(\theta _\varphi )$ by theorem 7.4.2 . Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ proves ( 14.69 ). $\square$
14.69 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Bern_Mark_implies} \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\big ) = 0\, . \end{equation}

title: Corollary 14.3.12
text: Corollary 14.3.12 . Let $w \in C^0(X)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w).  \] Proof. This follows from 14.3.11 and proposition 14.3.10 : indeed $\omega ^ n \in \mathrm{BM}(X,0)$, hence $\omega ^ n\in \mathrm{BM}(X,w)$ as $w$ is bounded. $\square$

title: Lemma 14.3.13
text:
Lemma 14.3.13 . Let $v\in C^0(K)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, and $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then 14.72  egin{equation} \label{eq:max_princ} \sup _ K (\eta -v) = \sup _{\{ \eta 
eq -\infty \} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)=\sup _{\left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty ight\} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight). \end{equation} Proof. We prove the first equality first. We write $S=\{ \eta =-\infty \} $. By definition, $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K\leq v$, so \[  \left.\left(\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)ight|_{K\setminus S}\geq \eta |_{K\setminus S}-v|_{K\setminus S}\, .  \] This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \leq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight).  \] Conversely, observe that $\sup _ K(\eta -v)>-\infty $ as $K$ is non-pluripolar. It follows that $\eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)$. Hence, 14.73  egin{equation} \label{eq:etaminussupK_temp1} \eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)\leq P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \geq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight),  \] finishing the proof of the first identity in ( 14.72 ). In order to prove the latter identity, observe that \[  \left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) =-\infty ight\}  \subseteq S  \] as a consequence of ( 14.73 ). On $\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty \} \cap S$, we have $\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)=-\infty $. Hence the last equality of ( 14.72 ) also follows. $\square$

14.72 \begin{equation} \label{eq:max_princ} \sup _ K (\eta -v) = \sup _{\{ \eta \neq -\infty \} } \left(\eta - P'_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)\right)=\sup _{\left\{ P'_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)\neq -\infty \right\} } \left(\eta - P'_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)\right). \end{equation}
14.73 \begin{equation} \label{eq:etaminussupK_temp1} \eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)\leq P'_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 14.3.14
text: Proposition 14.3.14 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$, $(K',v')$ be two weighted subsets of $X$. Then 14.74 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LkdiffconvtoI} \lim _{k\to \infty } \left( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v',K'}) \right) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K'}^{\varphi }(v'). \end{equation} In particular, 14.75 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Lkconv} \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v). \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 14.3.4 , for any $k>0$, $N^ k_{v,K}$ and $N^ k_{v',K'}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 14.74 ) make sense. Moreover, ( 14.75 ) is just a special case of ( 14.74 ) for $K'=X$ and $v'= 0$. To prove ( 14.74 ) it is enough to show that for any fixed $w \in C^\infty (X)$ we have 14.76 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofLdiffsmw} \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X}) \big ) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} For $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, $\theta _{(1-\epsilon )\varphi }$ is still a Kähler current. Let us fix such $\epsilon $, along with an arbitrary $\epsilon ' \in (0,1)$. Let $(v^-_{j})_ j$ and $(v^+_{j})_ j$ be the sequences of smooth functions constructed in 14.2.6 for the data $(K,v)$. By proposition 1.8.13 there exists $k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ') \in \mathbb N$ such that \[  \frac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi ,  \] and $\frac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta + \epsilon '\omega )$ for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$, as long as $k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ')$. In particular, 14.3.13 gives that \[  \begin{aligned}  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v,K}(s),\\  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s),\\  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s). \end{aligned}  \] As \[  P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-) \leq P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v) \leq P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),  \] where the second inequality follows from 14.2.6 and the fact that $P'=P$ for the global continuous obstacles $v_ j^\pm $. By 14.3.2 we have \[  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s) \leq N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s), \quad s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T \otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )), k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] Composing with $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }$ we arrive at \[  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})\, , \quad k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] For any $j>0$, by corollary 14.3.12 we get \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^-_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)=&  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  =&  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^+_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{aligned}  \] Using 14.2.6 , we can let $j \to \infty $ to arrive at \[  \begin{split}  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w) & \leq \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\ & \leq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\ &  \leq \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{split}  \] Hence, ( 14.76 ) follows. $\square$

14.74 \begin{equation} \label{eq:LkdiffconvtoI} \lim _{k\to \infty } \left( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v',K'}) \right) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K'}^{\varphi }(v'). \end{equation}
14.75 \begin{equation} \label{eq:Lkconv} \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v). \end{equation}

14.76 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofLdiffsmw} \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X}) \big ) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation}

title: Corollary 14.3.15
text: Corollary 14.3.15 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Our claim follows from proposition 14.3.14 and 14.3.11 . $\square$

title: Proposition 14.3.16
text: Proposition 14.3.16 . Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=\theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty .  \] Proof. For $w\in C^0(X)$, let $f_ k,g\colon \mathbb {R}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ ($k\geq 1$) be defined as \[  f_ k(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }),\quad g(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tw).  \] By corollary 14.3.15 , for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } f_ k(t)= g(t).  \] Here we use that $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v+tw)$ for all fixed $t$, which follows from $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ and the boundedness of $tw$ on $K$. Note that $f_ k$ is concave by Hölder's inequality. For each $k$, the function $f_ k$ is differentiable and \[  f_ k'(0)=\int _ X w\, \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] This follows by differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }$. The function $g$ is differentiable at $0$ by proposition 14.2.5 , with \[  g'(0)=\int _ K w\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v)}.  \] Applying A.5.3 to the convex functions $-f_ k$ and $-g$ gives \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } f_ k'(0)=g'(0),  \] which is equivalent to $\beta ^ k_{v, \varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$, by proposition 14.2.5 . $\square$

title: Proposition 14.3.17
text: Proposition 14.3.17 . Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 14.88 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconv1} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\quad \textup{as } k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof. Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$. We claim that 14.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmuleq} \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that this claim implies the conclusion. In fact, by theorem 7.4.2 , we have equality of the total masses, so equality holds in ( 14.89 ). As $\tau $ is an arbitrary cluster point of the sequence $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$, we get ( 14.88 ). It remains to prove ( 14.89 ). Let $(\varphi _ j)$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for all $j\geq 1$. By corollary 7.1.10 , we know that \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] The quasi-equisingular approximation is decreasing, so applying the decreasing case of proposition 14.2.7 to the limit $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, and using the definition of the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope, we get \[  P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] In particular, 14.90 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofeqmass} \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \leq \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu }  \] for any $k \geq 1$. As $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, by proposition 14.3.16 , \[  \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,  \] for any $j \geq 1$ fixed. By ( 14.90 ) and the semicontinuity theorem theorem 2.4.7 , we have \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n  \] as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, ( 14.89 ) follows. $\square$
14.88 \begin{equation} \label{eq:pbkconv1} \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\quad \textup{as } k\to \infty . \end{equation}
14.89 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmuleq} \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation}

14.90 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofeqmass} \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation}
14.93 \begin{equation} \label{eq:inproofmulower} \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq \tau . \end{equation}

title: Remark 14.3.18
text: Remark 14.3.18 . The results in this chapter can also be reformulated as the large deviation principle of a determinantal point process on $X$ using the Gärtner–Ellis theorem exactly as in [ Ber14 ] . We do not pursue this reformulation here.
