title: Lemma 1.6.10
text: Lemma 1.6.10 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain and $S\subset \Omega $ a closed set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Let $a,b$ be plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ and locally bounded off $S$, with $\{ a=-\infty \} =S$. If $a\leq b+C$ near $S$ for some finite constant $C$, then, as positive Radon measures, \[  \mathbf1_ S(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n_{\mathrm{full}} \leq \mathbf1_ S(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}.  \] If $a-b$ is bounded near $S$, equality holds. Proof. Fix a compact set $E\subset S$ and $\varepsilon >0$, and put $w_ c=\max \{ b-c,(1+\varepsilon )a\} $ for $c>0$. Since $a=-\infty $ on the compact set $E$, upper semicontinuity gives a neighborhood of $E$ on which $a<-(C+c)/\varepsilon $ and $a\leq b+C$. Off $S$, on this neighborhood, $b-c-(1+\varepsilon )a\geq -C-c-\varepsilon a>0$, while on $S$ the second branch of the maximum equals $-\infty $. Thus $w_ c=b-c$ near $E$, and locality on open sets gives $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ c)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}(E)=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}(E)$. As $c\to \infty $, the functions $w_ c$ decrease to $(1+\varepsilon )a$. Theorem 1.6.9 applies to every $w_ c$ with the same set $S$, so their full measures converge weakly to $(1+\varepsilon )^ n(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}$. Since the mass of a compact set is upper semicontinuous under weak convergence of positive measures, we obtain \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}(E) \leq (1+\varepsilon )^ n(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^ n_{\mathrm{full}}(E).  \] Here we apply the semicontinuity after multiplying the measures by a fixed nonnegative cutoff function with compact support, equal to one near $E$; both masses on $E$ are finite by the theorem. Letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ and applying inner regularity to all compact sets $E\subset S$ gives the asserted inequality of measures. If $a-b$ is bounded near $S$, then also $\{ b=-\infty \} =S$, so the roles of $a$ and $b$ can be interchanged, and equality follows. $\square$

title: 1.6.3 Sobolev regularity at divisorial poles
text:
1.6.3 Sobolev regularity at divisorial poles For a potential that is a convex function of $\log |f|$, with $f$ holomorphic, the growth of the convex function at $-\infty $ determines which derivatives are integrable near the divisor of $f$. The gradient and the classical Laplacian have different thresholds. Moreover, the distributional Laplacian keeps a measure on the divisor unless the slope of the convex function tends to zero. Let $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a sufficiently small neighborhood of $0$, and let $f
ot\equiv 0$ be a holomorphic function on $U$ with $f(0)=0$. Write \[  f=g\prod _{j=1}^ N h_ j^{m_ j},\qquad m_0=\min _ jm_ j,  \] where $g$ is a holomorphic unit and the $h_ j$ are distinct irreducible germs represented on $U$. Fix a convex nondecreasing function $\chi \in C^2(({-\infty },A])$ and shrink $U$ so that $\log |f|<A-1$. Set $v=\chi (\log |f|)$ off $Z=\{ f=0\} $; this function is plurisubharmonic and bounded above, and we extend it across $Z$ by lemma 1.3.7 . In this subsection, gradients, Laplacians, Sobolev spaces and the volume form $\mathrm dV$ are the real Euclidean ones. Write $|\partial f|^2=\sum _ j|\partial f/\partial z_ j|^2$, so that $|
abla |f||=|\partial f|$ off $Z$. Lemma 1.6.11 . After shrinking $U$, there is a constant $C>0$ such that \[  |\partial f|\leq C|f|^{1-1/m_0}\quad 	ext{on }U\setminus Z.  \] For each compact set $K\subset U$, there are $C_ K,r_ K>0$ with \[  \int _{K\cap \{ |f|=r\} }|\partial f|\, \mathrm dS\leq C_ Kr \qquad (0<r<r_ K),  \] where $\mathrm dS$ is the Euclidean surface measure on the real hypersurface $\{ |f|=r\} $. In particular, for every nonnegative measurable function $\Psi $, \[  \int _{K\cap \{ 0<|f|<r_ K\} }\Psi (|f|)|\partial f|^2\, \mathrm dV \leq C_ K\int _0^{r_ K}\Psi (r)r\, \mathrm dr.  \] Proof. Shrink $U$ so that $|h_ j|\leq 1$ and the unit $g$, its inverse and the first derivatives of $g$ and of all $h_ j$ are bounded. For each $j$, $|f|^{1/m_0}\leq C|h_ j|^{m_ j/m_0}\leq C|h_ j|$. Logarithmic differentiation of the factorization therefore gives \[   rac{|\partial f|}{|f|} \leq C\left(1+\sum _ j|h_ j|^{-1}ight) \leq C|f|^{-1/m_0},  \] which proves the first bound. For small $\zeta \in \mathbb C$, let $\mu _\zeta $ be the Euclidean volume measure of the fiber divisor $\{ f=\zeta \} $, counted with multiplicity. As $\zeta 	o 0$, we have $\log |f-\zeta |	o \log |f|$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$: by the local compactness theorem recalled at the beginning of section 1.4 , it suffices to identify subsequential limits, and the convergence is locally uniform off $Z$, which identifies every such limit and excludes convergence to $-\infty $. The Poincaré–Lelong formula therefore gives weak convergence of the fiber currents, and hence of their Euclidean trace measures. Pairing with a fixed nonnegative cutoff function equal to one near $K$ shows that $\sup _{|\zeta |<r_ K}\mu _\zeta (K)<\infty $ for some $r_ K>0$. The critical locus of $f$ has finitely many local components, and $f$ is constant on each of them. After shrinking $U$, every remaining critical component passes through $0$, where $f$ vanishes. Thus the small nonzero fibers are smooth. On $\{ |f|=r\} $, the coarea formula for the map $f$ to the circle of radius $r$ gives \[  \int _{K\cap \{ |f|=r\} }|\partial f|\, \mathrm dS =\int _{|\zeta |=r}\mu _\zeta (K)\, \mathrm dS(\zeta ) \leq C_ Kr.  \] The coarea formula for the function $|f|$, together with $|
abla |f||=|\partial f|$, proves the last inequality. The same formulas hold in dimension one, where the fiber volume is the counting measure. $\square$ Proposition 1.6.12 . For each $2\leq p<\infty $, \[  v\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \int _{-\infty }^ A|\chi '(s)|^ p \mathrm e^{(2-p)s/m_0}\, \mathrm ds<\infty .  \] In this case, the weak gradient of $v$ is the zero extension of $\chi '(\log |f|)
abla \log |f|$ from $U\setminus Z$. Proof. At a smooth point of a component of multiplicity $m_0$, outside the other components, multiplying the defining function of the component by a holomorphic $m_0$-th root of the remaining unit gives a normal coordinate $w_1$ with $f=w_1^{m_0}$. Coordinate changes with bounded derivatives and Jacobians preserve local first-order Sobolev integrability. With $r=|w_1|$ and $s=m_0\log r$, polar integration of the classical gradient gives, up to fixed positive factors, \[  \int _0^{r_0}|\chi '(m_0\log r)|^ p r^{1-p}\, \mathrm dr = rac1{m_0}\int _{-\infty }^{m_0\log r_0} |\chi '(s)|^ p\mathrm e^{(2-p)s/m_0}\, \mathrm ds.  \] Such smooth points occur in every neighborhood of $0$. This proves necessity, since changing the finite upper endpoint does not affect convergence. For sufficiency, put \[  s_\varepsilon =	frac 12\log (|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2), \qquad v_\varepsilon =\chi (s_\varepsilon ).  \] For small $\varepsilon >0$, these are $C^2$ plurisubharmonic functions decreasing to $v$. By convexity, $|\chi (s)|\leq C(1+|s|)$ for $s\leq A$, so the local exponential integrability of $\log |f|$, recalled in [ SGPT ] , gives convergence in every local $L^ p$ space with $p<\infty $. By the chain rule, \[  |
abla v_\varepsilon | =\chi '(s_\varepsilon )  rac{|f|}{|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2}|\partial f|.  \] Apply lemma 1.6.11 with the coarea formula, keeping two powers of $|\partial f|$ for the level estimate and bounding the other $p-2$ powers by the first inequality of the lemma. The local integral of $|
abla v_\varepsilon |^ p$ over $K\cap \{ 0<|f|<r_ K\} $ is then bounded by \[  C\int _0^{r_ K} |\chi '(	frac 12\log (r^2+\varepsilon ^2))|^ p  rac{r^{p+(p-2)(1-1/m_0)+1}}{(r^2+\varepsilon ^2)^ p} \, \mathrm dr.  \] With $s=	frac 12\log (r^2+\varepsilon ^2)$, we have $\mathrm ds=r\, \mathrm dr/(r^2+\varepsilon ^2)$ and $r\leq (r^2+\varepsilon ^2)^{1/2}$, so this is at most \[  C\int _{-\infty }^ A|\chi '(s)|^ p \mathrm e^{(2-p)s/m_0}\, \mathrm ds.  \] The integral over the part where $|f|\geq r_ K$ is uniformly bounded as well. Weak compactness in Sobolev spaces and the local $L^ p$ convergence therefore show that $v\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Its weak gradient agrees with the classical one off $Z$, and $Z$ has Lebesgue measure zero, which proves the final assertion. $\square$ Proposition 1.6.13 . Let $G$ be the zero extension of $\chi ''(\log |f|)|
abla \log |f||^2$ from $U\setminus Z$, and put $\ell =\lim _{s	o -\infty }\chi '(s)$. For each $1\leq p<\infty $, \[  G\in L^ p_{\mathrm{loc}}(U) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \int _{-\infty }^ A|\chi ''(s)|^ p \mathrm e^{2(1-p)s/m_0}\, \mathrm ds<\infty .  \] In the sense of distributions, \[  \Delta v=G+\ell \, \Delta \log |f|,  \] where $\Delta \log |f|$ is a positive measure carried by the divisor of $f$. In particular, $\Delta v$ is represented by a locally $L^ p$ function exactly when $\ell =0$ and the integral above is finite. Proof. The limit $\ell \geq 0$ exists because $\chi '$ is nonnegative and nondecreasing. Near a smooth point of a component of multiplicity $m_0$, outside the other components, the coordinate reduction to $f=w_1^{m_0}$ makes the positive complex Hessian of $v$ off $Z$ a single factor in the normal direction. Its Euclidean traces in the two coordinate systems are uniformly comparable, so polar integration gives necessity. In general, $G=\chi ''(\log |f|)|\partial f|^2/|f|^2$ off $Z$. The coarea formula and lemma 1.6.11 , now bounding the remaining $2p-2$ powers of $|\partial f|$ by the first inequality of the lemma, give \[  \int _{K\cap \{ 0<|f|<r_ K\} }G^ p\, \mathrm dV \leq C\int _0^{r_ K}|\chi ''(\log r)|^ p r^{-1-2(p-1)/m_0}\, \mathrm dr.  \] The substitution $s=\log r$ proves sufficiency. For $p=1$ the integral is always finite, since $\int _{-\infty }^ A\chi ''=\chi '(A)-\ell $. For the distributional identity, use $s_\varepsilon $ and $v_\varepsilon $ from the preceding proof. Direct differentiation gives \[   egin{aligned}  \Delta v_\varepsilon & =\chi ''(s_\varepsilon )  rac{|f|^2|\partial f|^2}{(|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2)^2} +\chi '(s_\varepsilon )\Delta s_\varepsilon ,\  \Delta s_\varepsilon & = rac{2\varepsilon ^2|\partial f|^2}{(|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2)^2}. \end{aligned}  \] Off $Z$, the first term tends locally uniformly to $G$. By the level estimate of lemma 1.6.11 and the same substitution, its integral over $K\cap \{ |f|<r_0\} $ is at most \[  C\int _{-\infty }^{ rac12\log (r_0^2+\varepsilon ^2)} \chi ''(s)\, \mathrm ds.  \] This bound tends to zero if we first let $\varepsilon 	o 0$ and then $r_0	o 0$, so the first term converges to $G$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The positive measures $\Delta s_\varepsilon $ converge weakly to $\Delta \log |f|$, with locally bounded masses, and the Poincaré–Lelong formula shows that this limit is a measure supported on $Z$. On $\{ |f|<r_0\} $, \[  0\leq \chi '(s_\varepsilon )-\ell \leq \chi '(	frac 12\log (r_0^2+\varepsilon ^2))-\ell ,  \] while $\Delta s_\varepsilon 	o 0$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\{ |f|\geq r_0\} $. Taking the same successive limits shows that $(\chi '(s_\varepsilon )-\ell )\Delta s_\varepsilon 	o 0$ weakly. Since $v_\varepsilon 	o v$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, passing to the limit in the formula for $\Delta v_\varepsilon $ gives the identity. If $\ell >0$, the measure $\ell \, \Delta \log |f|$ is nonzero and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure; uniqueness of the Lebesgue decomposition therefore proves the final criterion. $\square$ Example 1.6.14 . Shrink $U$ so that $\log |f|<-2$, and let $0<a<1$. Then the plurisubharmonic function \[  v_ a=-(-\log |f|)^ a  \] has $\Delta v_ a\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, while \[  v_ a\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad a<	frac 12.  \] It belongs to no $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $p>2$ and to no $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Proof. Here $\chi (s)=-(-s)^ a$ is of class $C^2$ on $(-\infty ,-1]$, so the preceding propositions apply with $A=-1$. Moreover, $\chi '(s)=a(-s)^{a-1}$ and $\chi ''(s)=a(1-a)(-s)^{a-2}$, so $\ell =0$. The two propositions give the assertion about the Laplacian and the first-order thresholds. At $a=1/2$, the first-order integral diverges logarithmically; for $p>2$, its exponential factor forces divergence. For second derivatives, take a smooth point of a component of multiplicity $m$, outside the other components, with a normal coordinate $w_1$ such that $f=w_1^ m$. Write $F(r)=\chi (m\log r)$ with $r=|w_1|$. The real second derivative of $v_ a$ in the unit direction tangent to the circles $|w_1|=r$ equals $F'(r)/r=m\chi '(m\log r)/r^2$. Thus the integral of its absolute value over the normal disk is bounded below, up to a fixed positive factor, by \[  \int _0^{r_0}\chi '(m\log r) rac{\mathrm dr}{r} = rac1m\int _{-\infty }^{m\log r_0}\chi '(s)\, \mathrm ds =+\infty .  \] Hence the classical Hessian of $v_ a$ off the divisor is not locally integrable, whereas local integrability is necessary for $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Since smooth coordinate changes preserve this Sobolev class, the argument is complete. $\square$

title: Lemma 1.6.11
text: Lemma 1.6.11 . For small $\zeta \in \mathbb C$, let $\mu _\zeta $ be the Euclidean volume measure of the fiber divisor $\{ f=\zeta \} $, counted with multiplicity. The Poincaré–Lelong formula therefore gives weak convergence of the fiber currents, and hence of their Euclidean trace measures. On $\{ |f|=r\} $, the coarea formula for the map $f$ to the circle of radius $r$ gives \[  \int _{K\cap \{ |f|=r\} }|\partial f|\, \mathrm dS =\int _{|\zeta |=r}\mu _\zeta (K)\, \mathrm dS(\zeta ) \leq C_ Kr.  \] The coarea formula for the function $|f|$, together with $|\nabla |f||=|\partial f|$, proves the last inequality. The same formulas hold in dimension one, where the fiber volume is the counting measure. $\square$

title: Proposition 1.6.13
text: Proposition 1.6.13 . Let $G$ be the zero extension of $\chi ''(\log |f|)|\nabla \log |f||^2$ from $U\setminus Z$, and put $\ell =\lim _{s\to -\infty }\chi '(s)$. For each $1\leq p<\infty $, \[  G\in L^ p_{\mathrm{loc}}(U) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \int _{-\infty }^ A|\chi ''(s)|^ p \mathrm e^{2(1-p)s/m_0}\, \mathrm ds<\infty .  \] In the sense of distributions, \[  \Delta v=G+\ell \, \Delta \log |f|,  \] where $\Delta \log |f|$ is a positive measure carried by the divisor of $f$. In particular, $\Delta v$ is represented by a locally $L^ p$ function exactly when $\ell =0$ and the integral above is finite. Proof. The limit $\ell \geq 0$ exists because $\chi '$ is nonnegative and nondecreasing. Near a smooth point of a component of multiplicity $m_0$, outside the other components, the coordinate reduction to $f=w_1^{m_0}$ makes the positive complex Hessian of $v$ off $Z$ a single factor in the normal direction. Its Euclidean traces in the two coordinate systems are uniformly comparable, so polar integration gives necessity. In general, $G=\chi ''(\log |f|)|\partial f|^2/|f|^2$ off $Z$. The coarea formula and lemma 1.6.11 , now bounding the remaining $2p-2$ powers of $|\partial f|$ by the first inequality of the lemma, give \[  \int _{K\cap \{ 0<|f|<r_ K\} }G^ p\, \mathrm dV \leq C\int _0^{r_ K}|\chi ''(\log r)|^ p r^{-1-2(p-1)/m_0}\, \mathrm dr.  \] The substitution $s=\log r$ proves sufficiency. For $p=1$ the integral is always finite, since $\int _{-\infty }^ A\chi ''=\chi '(A)-\ell $. For the distributional identity, use $s_\varepsilon $ and $v_\varepsilon $ from the preceding proof. Direct differentiation gives \[  \begin{aligned}  \Delta v_\varepsilon & =\chi ''(s_\varepsilon ) \frac{|f|^2|\partial f|^2}{(|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2)^2} +\chi '(s_\varepsilon )\Delta s_\varepsilon ,\\  \Delta s_\varepsilon & =\frac{2\varepsilon ^2|\partial f|^2}{(|f|^2+\varepsilon ^2)^2}. \end{aligned}  \] Off $Z$, the first term tends locally uniformly to $G$. By the level estimate of lemma 1.6.11 and the same substitution, its integral over $K\cap \{ |f|<r_0\} $ is at most \[  C\int _{-\infty }^{\frac12\log (r_0^2+\varepsilon ^2)} \chi ''(s)\, \mathrm ds.  \] This bound tends to zero if we first let $\varepsilon \to 0$ and then $r_0\to 0$, so the first term converges to $G$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The positive measures $\Delta s_\varepsilon $ converge weakly to $\Delta \log |f|$, with locally bounded masses, and the Poincaré–Lelong formula shows that this limit is a measure supported on $Z$. On $\{ |f|<r_0\} $, \[  0\leq \chi '(s_\varepsilon )-\ell \leq \chi '(\tfrac 12\log (r_0^2+\varepsilon ^2))-\ell ,  \] while $\Delta s_\varepsilon \to 0$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\{ |f|\geq r_0\} $. Taking the same successive limits shows that $(\chi '(s_\varepsilon )-\ell )\Delta s_\varepsilon \to 0$ weakly. Since $v_\varepsilon \to v$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, passing to the limit in the formula for $\Delta v_\varepsilon $ gives the identity. If $\ell >0$, the measure $\ell \, \Delta \log |f|$ is nonzero and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure; uniqueness of the Lebesgue decomposition therefore proves the final criterion. $\square$

title: 1.6.4 Spherical Monge–Ampère measures
text: 1.6.4 Spherical Monge–Ampère measures A bounded radial maximum gives a measure concentrated on a real hypersurface. This supplies singular measures that still give zero mass to pluripolar sets. Lemma 1.6.15 . For $r>0$, let $\sigma _ r$ be the normalized Euclidean surface measure on $\{ |z|=r\} \subset \mathbb C^ n$. Then \[  \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log \max \{ |z|^2,r^2\} \bigr )^ n=\sigma _ r.  \] In particular, $\sigma _ r$ does not charge pluripolar sets. Proof. Write $t=\log |z|^2$ and approximate $\max \{ t,\log r^2\} $ uniformly by smooth convex increasing functions $F_\epsilon (t)$ whose derivatives equal zero below $\log r^2-\epsilon $ and one above $\log r^2+\epsilon $. Their compositions with $t$ extend smoothly across zero. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t$ has rank $n-1$ off zero, the chain rule gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F_\epsilon (t))^ n =n(F_\epsilon ')^{n-1}F_\epsilon ''\, \mathrm dt\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t \wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t)^{n-1}.  \] The integral of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t)^{n-1}$ over each sphere is one. Indeed, $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t$ integrates to one on the Hopf circle, and the induced form on $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log (1+|w|^2)$; its top power has density $(n-1)!\pi ^{-(n-1)}(1+|w|^2)^{-n}$ on the affine chart, whose integral is one. Thus each displayed radial measure has total mass $\int ( (F_\epsilon ')^ n)'\, \mathrm dt=1$. Its support shrinks to the sphere, and its rotation invariance identifies the limit as $\sigma _ r$. Uniform bounded-potential convergence identifies that limit with the product in the statement. Non-pluripolarity follows from theorem 1.6.1 . $\square$

title: Lemma 1.6.15
text: Lemma 1.6.15 . For $r>0$, let $\sigma _ r$ be the normalized Euclidean surface measure on $\{ |z|=r\} \subset \mathbb C^ n$. Then \[  \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log \max \{ |z|^2,r^2\} \bigr )^ n=\sigma _ r.  \] In particular, $\sigma _ r$ does not charge pluripolar sets. Proof. Write $t=\log |z|^2$ and approximate $\max \{ t,\log r^2\} $ uniformly by smooth convex increasing functions $F_\epsilon (t)$ whose derivatives equal zero below $\log r^2-\epsilon $ and one above $\log r^2+\epsilon $. Their compositions with $t$ extend smoothly across zero. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t$ has rank $n-1$ off zero, the chain rule gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F_\epsilon (t))^ n =n(F_\epsilon ')^{n-1}F_\epsilon ''\, \mathrm dt\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t \wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t)^{n-1}.  \] The integral of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}t)^{n-1}$ over each sphere is one. Indeed, $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}t$ integrates to one on the Hopf circle, and the induced form on $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log (1+|w|^2)$; its top power has density $(n-1)!\pi ^{-(n-1)}(1+|w|^2)^{-n}$ on the affine chart, whose integral is one. Thus each displayed radial measure has total mass $\int ( (F_\epsilon ')^ n)'\, \mathrm dt=1$. Its support shrinks to the sphere, and its rotation invariance identifies the limit as $\sigma _ r$. Uniform bounded-potential convergence identifies that limit with the product in the statement. Non-pluripolarity follows from theorem 1.6.1 . $\square$

title: 1.6.5 Measure concentration under integrable convergence
text: 1.6.5 Measure concentration under integrable convergence Decreasing approximation controls Bedford–Taylor products, but convergence of the potentials in $L^1$ alone does not. If plurisubharmonic functions tend to zero in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and are locally uniformly bounded, the range estimate ( 1.4 ) shows that their Monge–Ampère measures tend to zero. Without a common bound, smooth bounded potentials that tend to zero, even in capacity, can have Monge–Ampère measures converging to a point mass. Lemma 1.6.16 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain. Suppose that $u_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ tend to zero in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ and satisfy $\sup _ j\| u_ j\| _{L^\infty (K)}<\infty $ for every compact set $K\subset \Omega $. Then $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n(K)\to 0$ for every such $K$. Proof. Fix concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset B_1\Subset \Omega $, and put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. If $\psi $ is a nonnegative smooth cutoff function supported in $B_1$ and equal to one near $\overline B$, integration by parts gives \[  0\leq \int _ B\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\wedge \beta ^{n-1} \leq \int _{B_1}u_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge \beta ^{n-1} \leq C\| u_ j\| _{L^1(B_1)}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Choose $M>0$ with $|u_ j|\leq M$ on $B$ for all $j$, and apply the first estimate in ( 1.4 ) to $u_ j+M$, whose values lie in $[0,2M]$. It bounds the top-degree mass of $B'$ by $C(2M)^{n-1}$ times the trace integral over $B$, which tends to zero; for $n=1$ the trace estimate itself suffices. Covering $K$ by finitely many such balls proves the lemma. $\square$ The construction uses a regularized maximum of a small multiple of a logarithm in one variable and a potential in the remaining variables. Its Monge–Ampère measure can be computed exactly by integration over circles in the first variable, and this will keep its top-degree mass fixed while the logarithmic coefficient tends to zero. Lemma 1.6.17 . Let $n\geq 2$, let $U\subset \mathbb C^{n-1}$ be a domain, and let $v$ be a smooth plurisubharmonic function on $U$. Fix $\varepsilon ,R,\eta >0$ and $A\in \mathbb R$. Let $\chi _\eta $ be the convolution of $t\mapsto \max (t,0)$ with a smooth even probability density supported in $[-\eta ,\eta ]$, and put \[  \begin{split}  q(\zeta )& =\varepsilon \log (|\zeta |^2/R^2),\qquad T(\zeta ,z')=v(z')-A-q(\zeta ),\\  h(\zeta ,z')& =q(\zeta )+\chi _\eta (T(\zeta ,z')) \end{split}  \] for $\zeta \ne 0$. Then $h$ extends to a smooth plurisubharmonic function on $\mathbb C\times U$. Set \[  w_\eta (t)=n\chi _\eta '(t)^{n-1}\chi _\eta ''(t),\qquad r_ t(z')=R\exp \bigl ((v(z')-A-t)/(2\varepsilon )\bigr ).  \] The function $w_\eta $ is nonnegative, supported in $[-\eta ,\eta ]$, and has integral one. For every $f\in C_ c(\mathbb C\times U)$, 1.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:smooth-ridge-transverse-integral} \begin{split}  \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n =\varepsilon \int _ U\biggl [\int _{-\eta }^{\eta }w_\eta (t) \int _0^{2\pi }f(r_ t(z')\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\vartheta },z') \frac{\mathrm d\vartheta }{2\pi }\, \mathrm dt\biggr ] (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-1}. \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. By convexity, $0\leq \chi _\eta '\leq 1$ and $\chi _\eta ''\geq 0$. The function $\chi _\eta $ vanishes on $(-\infty ,-\eta ]$ and equals $t$ on $[\eta ,\infty )$. Since $T\to +\infty $ as $\zeta \to 0$, we have $h=v-A$ near each point with $\zeta =0$, which gives the smooth extension. Off the hyperplane $\{ \zeta =0\} $, the function $q$ is pluriharmonic and \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h=\chi _\eta '(T)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v +\chi _\eta ''(T)\, \mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T\geq 0.  \] The second summand has rank at most one, and the first has rank at most $n-1$. Hence \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n=n\chi _\eta '(T)^{n-1}\chi _\eta ''(T) \, \mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-1}.  \] The last factor has top degree in the variables $z'$, so the derivatives of $v$ in $\mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T$ contribute nothing. Write $s=\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$. In polar coordinates, $\mathrm dq=\varepsilon \, \mathrm ds$ and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q=\varepsilon \, \mathrm d\vartheta /(2\pi )$. At fixed $z'$, the change of variables from $s$ to $t=v-A-\varepsilon s$ gives ( 1.19 ). There is no contribution near $\zeta =0$, where $h=v-A$ and the form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ has rank at most $n-1$. Finally, $w_\eta $ is the derivative of $(\chi _\eta ')^ n$, whose values at $-\eta $ and $\eta $ are zero and one. $\square$ Proposition 1.6.18 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain and $a\in \Omega $. For every $c>0$, there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $ such that \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\longrightarrow 0\quad (1\leq p<\infty ), \qquad (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n\longrightarrow c\delta _ a \quad \text{vaguely}.  \] The same sequence tends to zero in local capacity. Here the norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure, and vague convergence means convergence against every compactly supported continuous test function. Proof. Translate $a$ to the origin and write $z=(\zeta ,z')\in \mathbb C\times \mathbb C^ m$, $m=n-1$. It suffices to construct measures of mass one and then multiply the potentials by $c^{1/n}$. For $\delta >0$, put $H_\delta (z')=\log (|z'|^2+\delta ^2)$. With $s=|z'|^2$, the complex Hessian of $H_\delta $ has the eigenvalue $(s+\delta ^2)^{-1}$ with multiplicity $m-1$ in the directions orthogonal to $z'$ and the eigenvalue $\delta ^2(s+\delta ^2)^{-2}$ in the radial direction. Taking the determinant and integrating in polar coordinates gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m= \frac{m!}{\pi ^ m}\frac{\delta ^2}{(|z'|^2+\delta ^2)^{m+1}} \, \mathrm d\lambda _{2m}, \qquad \int _{|z'|<b}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m =\left(\frac{b^2}{b^2+\delta ^2}\right)^ m,  \] where $\lambda _{2m}$ is Lebesgue measure. These probability measures tend to $\delta _0$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$, since their mass outside each ball about the origin tends to zero. Choose $R>\max (1,\sup _\Omega |\zeta |)$ and a ball $P\subset \mathbb C^ m$ containing the projection of $\Omega $ to the $z'$ variables. Set \[  \begin{gathered} \delta _ j=\varepsilon _ j=j^{-1},\qquad \eta _ j=j^{-2}, \qquad v_ j=\varepsilon _ j^{-1/m}H_{\delta _ j},\\ A_ j=\sup _ Pv_ j+2\varepsilon _ j\log (Rj). \end{gathered}  \] Apply lemma 1.6.17 on $\mathbb C\times \mathbb C^ m$ to these data, and let $u_ j=h_ j-\eta _ j$, where $h_ j$ is the resulting function. The convolution satisfies $0\leq \chi _{\eta _ j}(t)-\max (t,0)\leq \eta _ j$, and $q+\max (T,0)=\max (q,v_ j-A_ j)$. Both branches of this maximum are negative on $\Omega $, so \[  \varepsilon _ j\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)-\eta _ j \leq u_ j\leq 0.  \] Each $u_ j$ is smooth and bounded on $\Omega $, since the second branch $v_ j-A_ j$ is bounded below on the bounded set $P$. The logarithm has finite $L^ p(\Omega )$ norm for every finite $p$, by polar integration on a fixed polydisk containing $\Omega $. Hence $u_ j\to 0$ in all these norms. Let $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ be concentric balls, and let $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$. Since $|u_ j|\leq \varepsilon _ j|\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)|+\eta _ j$, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate applied to $\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$, together with the range estimate ( 1.4 ) for the constant term, gives \[  \int _{B'}|u_ j|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n\leq C_ B(\varepsilon _ j+\eta _ j),  \] where $C_ B$ depends on the fixed balls and the logarithm but not on $j$ or $w$. Restricting the integral to $B'\cap \{ |u_ j|>t\} $, dividing by $t>0$ and taking the supremum over $w$ shows that the capacity of $B'\cap \{ |u_ j|>t\} $ relative to $B$ tends to zero. In ( 1.19 ), the factor $\varepsilon _ j(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ m$ equals $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m$. For $z'\in P$ and $|t|\leq \eta _ j$, the radii satisfy \[  r_ t(z')\leq j^{-1}\exp (\eta _ j/(2\varepsilon _ j)) \leq \mathrm e^{1/2}/j.  \] Extend $f\in C_ c(\Omega )$ by zero to $\mathbb C^ n$. Outside the projection of $\operatorname {supp}f$ to the $z'$ variables, both $f(r_ t\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\vartheta },z')$ and $f(0,z')$ vanish. On this projection, the uniform continuity of $f$ and the bound on the radii make their difference tend to zero uniformly. Since the weights $w_{\eta _ j}(t)\, \mathrm dt$ and $\mathrm d\vartheta /(2\pi )$ and the measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m$ all have total mass one, it follows that \[  \int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n -\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f(0,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m \longrightarrow 0.  \] The second integral tends to $f(0)$, which proves the asserted vague limit. $\square$ Each approximating measure has a smooth density and charges no pluripolar set, whereas the limit is a point mass. By lemma 1.6.16 , the potentials therefore have no common lower bound on some compact set. Thus convergence in capacity is compatible with concentration of the Monge–Ampère measures once common local bounds are lost.

title: 1.6.6 Adding a prescribed local measure
text:
1.6.6 Adding a prescribed local measure The concentration in proposition 1.6.18 can be produced on top of a given bounded potential $b$ and repeated, so as to add an arbitrary prescribed measure to $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Adding a perturbation $h$ to $b$ creates the mixed terms $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r$. A mixed Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate controls them, provided that the lower-degree currents of $h$ are kept small. Lemma 1.6.19 . Fix the data $n,U,v,\varepsilon ,R,\eta ,\chi _\eta $ of lemma 1.6.17 , and write $h_ A$ for the smooth plurisubharmonic function $h$ of that lemma, regarded as a function of $A$. Put $D=\{ 0\} 	imes U$, and write $[D]$ for the current of integration over this hypersurface. Then, for every $1\leq r\leq n$, \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\longrightarrow \varepsilon [D]\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1} \quad 	ext{as currents on }\mathbb C	imes U,\  A	o \infty .  \] The product on the right is integration of the restriction of the smooth form $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1}$ over $D$. Proof. Write $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$, $q=\varepsilon \log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$ and $T_ A=v-A-q$. The rank-one calculation in the proof of lemma 1.6.17 gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r=\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^ rS^ r +r\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(T_ A) \, \mathrm dT_ A\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T_ A\wedge S^{r-1}  \] off $D$; since $h_ A$ is smooth and $D$ has measure zero, this formula determines the current. Fix a smooth compactly supported test form. On the projection of its support to $U$, the function $v$ and its derivatives are bounded. Hence the support of $\chi _\eta '(T_ A)$ lies in $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $, where $s_ A=C\exp (-A/(2\varepsilon ))$ and $C$ depends only on this compact set and the fixed data. The coefficients involving $v$ and $\chi _\eta $ are bounded at the fixed parameters, so the first summand has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$. In the second summand, the term with two derivatives of $v$ also has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$, and the two cross terms have pairing $O(s_ A)$: the derivative of $q$ in the $\zeta $ direction has size $O(|\zeta |^{-1})$, and its area integral over the disk $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $ is $O(s_ A)$. It remains to integrate the term containing $\mathrm dq\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q$. The logarithmic change of the radial variable used for ( 1.19 ) leaves the factor $\varepsilon $ and the probability weight \[  r\chi _\eta '(t)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(t)\, \mathrm dt, \qquad -\eta \leq t\leq \eta .  \] Only the component of the test form in the $z'$ directions enters this term, and on the shrinking circles its coefficients tend uniformly to their values at $\zeta =0$. Integration in the angle therefore gives, in the limit, exactly the pairing with $\varepsilon [D]\wedge S^{r-1}$. This proves the convergence in every degree. $\square$ Lemma 1.6.20 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, let $K$ and $L$ be compact subsets of $\Omega $ with $K$ contained in the interior $L^\circ $ of $L$, and put $ eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $, and let $T$ be a smooth positive closed $(r,r)$-form, $1\leq r<n$. Then \[  \int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge T \leq C_{K,L,n}(1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{n-r} \int _ L T\wedge  eta ^{n-r}.  \] Proof. Put $M=1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Cover $K$ by finitely many balls whose larger concentric balls have closures in $L^\circ $. Replacing $b$ by $b+M$, which has the same Hessian and takes values in $[0,2M]$ on $L$, we may assume $0\leq b\leq 2M$ there. For nested cutoff functions $\psi $, integration by parts against closed forms gives \[  \int \psi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge W =\int b\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge W \leq CM \int _{\operatorname {supp}\psi } eta \wedge W,  \] where $W$ is $T$ multiplied by the remaining positive closed factors. Apply this successively to the $n-r$ Hessians of $b$. For bounded $b$, the integrations by parts are justified by local decreasing regularization and theorem 1.6.1 , with one common bound on the range. Summing over the finite cover gives the asserted constant. $\square$ Proposition 1.6.21 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain, let $b\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty (\Omega )$, $a\in \Omega $ and $c>0$. Given finitely many $f_ i\in C_ c(\Omega )$ and numbers $	au ,t>0$, there is a smooth bounded plurisubharmonic function $h\leq 0$ on $\Omega $ such that \[   egin{gathered} \| h\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}t\quad (1\leq p<\infty ),\ \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h))^ n-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n igr ) -cf_ i(a)ight|<	au \quad 	ext{for every }i. \end{gathered}  \] For concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ and every $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$, it also satisfies \[  \int _{B'}|h|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n\leq C_{B',B,\Omega }t.  \] These constants are independent of $b,a,c$, the test functions and the tolerances. Proof. We take for $h$ a function from lemma 1.6.17 whose top-degree measure approximates $c\delta _ a$ and whose lower-degree currents are small; lemma 1.6.20 then controls the mixed terms. u _ j-

title: Lemma 1.6.19
text: Lemma 1.6.19 . Fix the data $n,U,v,\varepsilon ,R,\eta ,\chi _\eta $ of lemma 1.6.17 , and write $h_ A$ for the smooth plurisubharmonic function $h$ of that lemma, regarded as a function of $A$. Put $D=\{ 0\} \times U$, and write $[D]$ for the current of integration over this hypersurface. title: Lemma 1.6.20
text: Lemma 1.6.20 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, let $K$ and $L$ be compact subsets of $\Omega $ with $K$ contained in the interior $L^\circ $ of $L$, and put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $, and let $T$ be a smooth positive closed $(r,r)$-form, $1\leq r<n$. Then \[  \int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge T \leq C_{K,L,n}(1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{n-r} \int _ L T\wedge \beta ^{n-r}.  \] Proof. Put $M=1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Cover $K$ by finitely many balls whose larger concentric balls have closures in $L^\circ $. For nested cutoff functions $\psi $, integration by parts against closed forms gives \[  \int \psi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge W =\int b\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge W \leq CM \int _{\operatorname {supp}\psi }\beta \wedge W,  \] where $W$ is $T$ multiplied by the remaining positive closed factors. Apply this successively to the $n-r$ Hessians of $b$. For bounded $b$, the integrations by parts are justified by local decreasing regularization and theorem 1.6.1 , with one common bound on the range. Summing over the finite cover gives the asserted constant. $\square$

title: 1.6.7 Full cluster sets at the zero potential
search_title: Full cluster sets at the zero potential
text:
1.6.7 Full cluster sets at the zero potential Theorem 1.6.22 prescribes one limit of the Monge–Ampère measures, but a single sequence of potentials can have many subsequential limits. In fact, every vaguely closed set of measures is the set of all subsequential limits for a suitable sequence of potentials tending to zero. For a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, write $\mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ for the set of positive Radon measures on $\Omega $, including zero and measures of infinite total mass, with the vague topology defined by integration against $C_ c(\Omega )$. Lemma 1.6.23 . There are real functions $f_ i\in C_ c^\infty (\Omega )$ such that \[  d_ v(\alpha , eta )=\sum _{i\geq 1}2^{-i}  rac{\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha - eta )ight|}{1+\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha - eta )ight|}  \] is a metric inducing the vague topology on $\mathcal M_+(\Omega )$. This metric space is separable. Proof. Choose relatively compact open sets $U_\ell $ exhausting $\Omega $, with $\overline U_\ell \subset U_{\ell +1}$. For each $\ell $, choose a countable uniformly dense subset of $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ consisting of smooth compactly supported functions, extended by zero to $\Omega $; such families exist because $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ is separable and its elements can be approximated uniformly by smooth functions. Add a nonnegative smooth compactly supported cutoff function equal to one near $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and enumerate the union of all these functions as $(f_ i)$. Call the maps $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega f_ i\, \mathrm d\alpha $ the coordinates. If positive measures converge to a fixed measure in every coordinate, the cutoff coordinates give common mass bounds on each $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and uniform approximation then gives convergence against every $g\in C_ c(\Omega )$. The same argument, applied near a fixed measure, shows that $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega g\, \mathrm d\alpha $ is continuous for the topology generated by the coordinates: bound the relevant cutoff coordinate on a neighborhood, choose one smooth test that is uniformly close to $g$, and shrink the neighborhood using the coordinate of that test. Thus the coordinates generate exactly the vague topology, and they separate measures. The function $s\mapsto s/(1+s)$ is increasing and subadditive on $[0,\infty )$. Applying it to the triangle inequalities for the coordinates gives the triangle inequality for $d_ v$, and $d_ v$ is positive on distinct measures because the coordinates separate them. Each coordinate is continuous for this metric, and the tails of the series are uniformly small, so the metric induces exactly the topology generated by the coordinates. Finally, the finite atomic measures with nonnegative rational weights at points of a fixed countable dense subset of $\Omega $ form a countable dense family. To approximate a measure in finitely many coordinates, partition a compact neighborhood of the supports of the corresponding tests into sets on which all these tests have small oscillation, place an atom in each set of nonzero mass, and then perturb its location and weight. Only the finite mass of that compact neighborhood is used, and the remaining tail of the metric is arbitrarily small. $\square$ The metric controls limits along corresponding subsequences: if $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ and one of the sequences converges vaguely to a fixed measure along a subsequence, then, by the triangle inequality, so does the other. Without common local mass bounds, however, $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ need not imply that $\int g(\alpha _ j- eta _ j)	o 0$ for every $g\in C_ c(\Omega )$. For example, fix $a\in \Omega $, a unit vector $e$, and numbers $r_ j\downarrow 0$ with $a+r_ je\in \Omega $, and put \[  \alpha _ j=r_ j^{-1/2}\delta _{a+r_ je},\qquad  eta _ j=r_ j^{-1/2}\delta _ a.  \] For every smooth compactly supported test, the difference of the two integrals is $O(r_ j^{1/2})$, so $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ because the tails of the series are small. On the other hand, if $\chi \in C_ c^\infty (\Omega )$ equals one near $a$, the continuous test function $g(z)=\chi (z)|z-a|^{1/2}$ gives $\int g(\alpha _ j- eta _ j)=1$ for all large $j$. Theorem 1.6.24 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain. A set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ is vaguely closed if and only if there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $, tending to zero in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$: \[  F=\left\{ \mu \in \mathcal M_+(\Omega ):\  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j_ k})^ n\longrightarrow \mu 	ext{ vaguely for some }j_1<j_2<\cdots ight\} .  \] The empty set is allowed. Proof. In a metric space, the full cluster set of a sequence is the intersection of the closures of its tails: a point of this intersection can be approximated within $1/k$ at an index larger than the preceding one, successively for $k=1,2,\ldots $. The full cluster set is therefore closed, and lemma 1.6.23 proves necessity. For sufficiency, suppose first that $F$ is nonempty and closed. A subset of a separable metric space is separable, so we may choose a dense sequence $\mu _1,\mu _2,\ldots $ in $F$, repetitions allowed. Concatenating the finite lists $(\mu _1)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2,\mu _3)$, and so on, we obtain a sequence $(
u _ j)$ in which every $\mu _ k$ appears arbitrarily late. Hence every point of $F$ is the limit of a subsequence, and since $F$ is closed, no other subsequential limit occurs. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 1.6.23 , and perform the finite atomic construction from the proof of theorem 1.6.22 separately for each $j$, with background zero, target $
u _ j$ and tests $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$. Thus we approximate $
u _ j$ in these coordinates by a finite atomic measure with error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, apply proposition 1.6.21 successively with $t=	au =(jN_ j)^{-1}$; if it has none, take $u_ j=0$. The resulting smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ satisfy \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] On every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the bounds of that proposition for test measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$, with $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ and $0\leq w\leq 1$, also sum to $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$. Dividing by a positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. These estimates require neither convergence of the targets $
u _ j$ nor a common local mass bound for them. Splitting the series defining the metric after its first $j$ terms gives \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Consequently, the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences, and hence the same full cluster set $F$. $\square$ For subharmonic functions on a planar domain, by contrast, $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ convergence to zero forces $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j	o 0$ in the sense of distributions, and positivity, tested against compactly supported cutoff functions, then gives vague convergence to zero. title: Lemma 1.6.23
text: Lemma 1.6.23 . There are real functions $f_ i\in C_ c^\infty (\Omega )$ such that \[  d_ v(\alpha ,\beta )=\sum _{i\geq 1}2^{-i} \frac{\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha -\beta )\right|}{1+\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha -\beta )\right|}  \] is a metric inducing the vague topology on $\mathcal M_+(\Omega )$. This metric space is separable. Proof. Choose relatively compact open sets $U_\ell $ exhausting $\Omega $, with $\overline U_\ell \subset U_{\ell +1}$. For each $\ell $, choose a countable uniformly dense subset of $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ consisting of smooth compactly supported functions, extended by zero to $\Omega $; such families exist because $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ is separable and its elements can be approximated uniformly by smooth functions. Add a nonnegative smooth compactly supported cutoff function equal to one near $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and enumerate the union of all these functions as $(f_ i)$. Call the maps $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega f_ i\, \mathrm d\alpha $ the coordinates. If positive measures converge to a fixed measure in every coordinate, the cutoff coordinates give common mass bounds on each $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and uniform approximation then gives convergence against every $g\in C_ c(\Omega )$. The same argument, applied near a fixed measure, shows that $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega g\, \mathrm d\alpha $ is continuous for the topology generated by the coordinates: bound the relevant cutoff coordinate on a neighborhood, choose one smooth test that is uniformly close to $g$, and shrink the neighborhood using the coordinate of that test. Thus the coordinates generate exactly the vague topology, and they separate measures. The function $s\mapsto s/(1+s)$ is increasing and subadditive on $[0,\infty )$. Applying it to the triangle inequalities for the coordinates gives the triangle inequality for $d_ v$, and $d_ v$ is positive on distinct measures because the coordinates separate them. Each coordinate is continuous for this metric, and the tails of the series are uniformly small, so the metric induces exactly the topology generated by the coordinates. Finally, the finite atomic measures with nonnegative rational weights at points of a fixed countable dense subset of $\Omega $ form a countable dense family. To approximate a measure in finitely many coordinates, partition a compact neighborhood of the supports of the corresponding tests into sets on which all these tests have small oscillation, place an atom in each set of nonzero mass, and then perturb its location and weight. Only the finite mass of that compact neighborhood is used, and the remaining tail of the metric is arbitrarily small. $\square$

title: Theorem 1.6.24
text:
Theorem 1.6.24 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain. A set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ is vaguely closed if and only if there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $, tending to zero in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$: \[  F=\left\{ \mu \in \mathcal M_+(\Omega ):\  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j_ k})^ n\longrightarrow \mu 	ext{ vaguely for some }j_1<j_2<\cdots ight\} .  \] The empty set is allowed. Proof. In a metric space, the full cluster set of a sequence is the intersection of the closures of its tails: a point of this intersection can be approximated within $1/k$ at an index larger than the preceding one, successively for $k=1,2,\ldots $. The full cluster set is therefore closed, and lemma 1.6.23 proves necessity. For sufficiency, suppose first that $F$ is nonempty and closed. A subset of a separable metric space is separable, so we may choose a dense sequence $\mu _1,\mu _2,\ldots $ in $F$, repetitions allowed. Concatenating the finite lists $(\mu _1)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2,\mu _3)$, and so on, we obtain a sequence $(
u _ j)$ in which every $\mu _ k$ appears arbitrarily late. Hence every point of $F$ is the limit of a subsequence, and since $F$ is closed, no other subsequential limit occurs. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 1.6.23 , and perform the finite atomic construction from the proof of theorem 1.6.22 separately for each $j$, with background zero, target $
u _ j$ and tests $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$. Thus we approximate $
u _ j$ in these coordinates by a finite atomic measure with error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, apply proposition 1.6.21 successively with $t=	au =(jN_ j)^{-1}$; if it has none, take $u_ j=0$. The resulting smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ satisfy \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] On every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the bounds of that proposition for test measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$, with $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ and $0\leq w\leq 1$, also sum to $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$. Dividing by a positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. These estimates require neither convergence of the targets $
u _ j$ nor a common local mass bound for them. Splitting the series defining the metric after its first $j$ terms gives \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Consequently, the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences, and hence the same full cluster set $F$. $\square$

title: 1.6.8 Cluster sets at a bounded background

text:
1.6.8 Cluster sets at a bounded background Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, $n\geq 1$, and let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $. If potentials approach $b$ from below in local capacity, every limit of their Monge–Ampère measures must dominate $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Truncation at a fixed distance below $b$ provides a common bound, and plurifine locality keeps the measure outside the small set where the truncation changes the potential. Lemma 1.6.25 . Let $b,u_ j$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $ with $u_ j\leq b$ and $u_ j	o b$ in local capacity. Then, for every nonnegative $f\in C_ c(\Omega )$, \[  \liminf _{j	o \infty }\int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n \geq \int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n.  \] In particular, every vague subsequential limit of $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n$ dominates $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Proof. First suppose that $f$ is supported in $B'$, where $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ are concentric balls. Put $v_ j=\max (u_ j,b-1)$ and $E_ j=\{ u_ j\leq b-1\} $. The functions $v_ j$ lie between $b-1$ and $b$ and tend to $b$ in local capacity. Because of their common bounds, the continuity of bounded products recalled in section 1.6 gives $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n	o (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ vaguely on $B$. With $R=\sup _ B b-\inf _ B b+1$, the capacity bound for bounded potentials gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f) \leq R^ n\operatorname {cap}(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f,B) \longrightarrow 0,  \] where the limit holds because $E_ j\subset \{ |u_ j-b|>1/2\} $. On the plurifine open Borel set $\{ u_ j>b-1\} $ we have $v_ j=u_ j$, so theorem 1.6.1 shows that the two measures agree there. By positivity, \[  \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n \geq \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n -\| f\| _\infty (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f).  \] Taking the lower limit proves the assertion for such $f$. For a general $f$, use a finite nonnegative partition of unity subordinate to a cover of its support by such balls. Applying the inequality along a vaguely convergent subsequence proves the final assertion. $\square$ Theorem 1.6.26 . Assume that $\Omega $ is bounded, $n\geq 2$, and $b\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty (\Omega )$. For a set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$, the following are equivalent: $F$ is vaguely closed and every $\mu \in F$ satisfies $\mu \geq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$; there are bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq b$ on $\Omega $, converging to $b$ in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$. The empty set is allowed. If $b$ is smooth, every $u_ j$ in the second condition can be chosen smooth. Proof. If the second condition holds, lemma 1.6.25 gives the measure inequality, and the full cluster set is closed in the metrizable vague topology by the argument at the beginning of the proof of theorem 1.6.24 . Conversely, assume the first condition. If $F$ is nonempty, the concatenation of a dense sequence used in the proof of theorem 1.6.24 gives measures $
u _ j\in F$ whose full vague cluster set is $F$. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral at least $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, $
u _ j-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ is a positive Radon measure. Let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 1.6.23 . For each $j$, approximate the excess $
u _ j-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ against $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$ by a positive finite atomic measure, with each error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, perform the construction from the proof of theorem 1.6.22 , starting at $b$ and using $	au =t=(jN_ j)^{-1}$ for each atom; if it has none, take $u_ j=b$. Summing the estimates of proposition 1.6.21 gives \[  \| u_ j-b\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] For every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the same construction bounds the integral of $|u_ j-b|$ over $B'$ against $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$ by $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$, for every $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$. Dividing by a fixed positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. Each $u_ j$ is bounded and lies below $b$, and it is smooth when $b$ is smooth. One sequence serves all finite $p$, and no common local mass bound on the $
u _ j$ is needed. The error in the first $j$ coordinates and the tail of the series yield \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] By the remark following lemma 1.6.23 , the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences. Hence their full vague cluster sets coincide. $\square$ For example, on the unit ball the function $b=|z|^2-1$ has nonzero Monge–Ampère measure. For every point $a$ of the ball, the theorem allows the cluster sets $\{ (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n\} $, $\{ (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+\delta _ a\} $ and the empty set, but it excludes $\{ 0\} $; this exclusion relies on the convergence in local capacity. In dimension one, $L^1$ convergence alone forces $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j	o \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b$ vaguely, so the full cluster set is always $\{ \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\} $.
