title: 4.6.4 Ample comparison quotients on Hirzebruch surfaces
search_title: Ample comparison quotients on Hirzebruch surfaces
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: 4.6.4 Ample comparison quotients on Hirzebruch surfaces To apply corollary 4.6.18 , we need ample vector bundles whose duals are close to a split bundle $F_1\oplus F_2$ with $\deg _{\Theta _ s}F_ s>0$ for suitable test forms $\Theta _ s$. The split bundle $F_1^*\oplus F_2^*$ is not ample itself: otherwise its quotient line bundles $F_ s^*$ would be ample, hence carry positively curved metrics, and each $F_ s$ would have negative degree for every test form. The ample bundles must therefore be obtained by deformation. On a Hirzebruch surface we choose a split bundle $E_0=L_1\oplus L_2$ whose dual summands have positive degree for suitable Kähler forms, and we construct an ample bundle $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ with the same Chern classes as a quotient of a trivial bundle. Both bundles belong to the family of bundles with these Chern classes that are prioritary for the ruling. This family is irreducible, which will allow us to find ample bundles in every neighborhood of $E_0$. Let $e\geq 0$ be an integer, and let \[  X=\mathbb F_ e=\mathbb P_{\mathbb P^1}(\mathcal O\oplus \mathcal O(e)), \qquad \pi :X\longrightarrow \mathbb P^1,  \] be the Hirzebruch surface, where the projective bundle parametrizes lines. Write $S$ for the section defined by the subbundle $\mathcal O(e)$ and $f$ for a fiber of $\pi $, called a ruling fiber; we identify line bundles with divisor classes and write $\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)$. The normal bundle of $S$ is $\mathcal O(-e)$, so \[  S^2=-e,\qquad S\cdot f=1,\qquad f^2=0.  \] The dual of the tautological line bundle is $\mathcal O_ X(S)$. A line bundle of degree zero on the ruling fibers is pulled back from $\mathbb P^1$: its direct image has rank one, and the evaluation map from the pullback of the direct image is an isomorphism on each fiber. Consequently $\operatorname {Pic}(X)=\mathbb ZS\oplus \mathbb Zf$. Lemma 4.6.19 . For integers $a\geq 0$ and $b$, \[  \pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)= \bigoplus _{i=0}^ a\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(b-ie), \qquad R^1\pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)=0.  \] A class $aS+bf$ is effective exactly when $a,b\geq 0$. If $a\geq 1$ and $b>ae$, its line bundle is very ample. In particular, \[  H=S+(3e+1)f, \qquad H^2=5e+2, \qquad h^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(H))=5e+4.  \] The canonical class is $K_ X=-2S-(e+2)f$. Proof. Over a trivializing chart of the base, sections of $\mathcal O_ X(aS)$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree $a$ in the fiber coordinates. Their transition law gives \[  \pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS)= \operatorname {Sym}^ a(\mathcal O\oplus \mathcal O(-e)),  \] and twisting by the base gives the formula. The first cohomology of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(a)$ on each fiber vanishes, which gives the assertion on the higher direct image. If $a<0$, restriction to a general ruling fiber excludes a nonzero section. For $a\geq 0$, the direct-image formula gives a nonzero section exactly when $b\geq 0$. Suppose that $a\geq 1$ and $b>ae$. All line bundles in the direct image then have degree at least one. Fiber polynomials of degree $a$ separate points and tangent directions within a fiber. To separate points over different base points, choose a fiber monomial that is nonzero at the first point and a coefficient section vanishing at the second base point but not at the first. At any point, choose such a nonzero monomial and a coefficient section with a simple zero at its base point; the resulting global section vanishes there, has nonzero derivative in a prescribed base direction and has zero vertical derivative. The complete linear system therefore separates points and first jets, so it defines an embedding. The formulas for $H^2$ and $h^0(H)$ follow from the intersection numbers and from the direct image $\mathcal O(3e+1)\oplus \mathcal O(2e+1)$. Finally, the relative Euler sequence gives $K_{X/\mathbb P^1}=-2S-ef$, and adding the pullback of the canonical class of $\mathbb P^1$ proves the last identity. $\square$ Put \[  L_1=\mathcal O_ X(5S-f),\qquad L_2=\mathcal O_ X(-S+(12e+5)f),\qquad E_0=L_1\oplus L_2.  \] Their Chern classes satisfy \[  c_1(E_0)=4H,\qquad c_2(E_0)=65e+26=13H^2.  \] An ample bundle with these Chern classes can be constructed as a quotient of a trivial bundle. The main point of the proof is to make the fibers of the associated map to projective space finite, which requires excluding common curves of the defining sections uniformly over the projective parameter. Proposition 4.6.20 . There exist linearly independent sections $a_0,\ldots ,a_3$ of $\mathcal O_ X(H)$ with no common zero. For any such quadruple and a general quadruple $b_0,\ldots ,b_3$ of sections of $\mathcal O_ X(3H)$, the sequence \[  0\longrightarrow \mathcal O_ X(-H)\oplus \mathcal O_ X(-3H) \xrightarrow {(a,b)}\mathcal O_ X^{\oplus 4} \longrightarrow E_{\mathrm{amp}}\longrightarrow 0  \] has a locally free ample cokernel $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ of rank two, with $c_1(E_{\mathrm{amp}})=4H$ and $c_2(E_{\mathrm{amp}})=13H^2$. Here general means outside a proper Zariski-closed subset of the space of quadruples. Proof. Step 1: the quadruple $a$. Since $\mathcal O_ X(H)$ is globally generated, a common zero at a fixed point imposes four independent linear conditions on a quadruple $a$. The incidence variety of quadruples with a common zero at some point of the surface therefore has codimension at least two in the space of quadruples, and its image there is closed by properness. Linear independence is also a nonempty open condition, because $h^0(H)\geq 4$, and the two open conditions intersect. Fix such an $a$ and write \[  V=H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H))^{\oplus 4},\qquad N=\dim V.  \] Step 2: local freeness. At a fixed point $x$, the map $(a,b)$ drops rank exactly when $b(x)$ is proportional to the nonzero vector $a(x)$. Since evaluation on $V$ is surjective, this is a condition of codimension three. Its incidence over $X$ has dimension at most $N-1$, and its image in $V$ is closed. Outside that image the cokernel is locally free of rank two. Step 3: the map to projective space. Dualizing the sequence identifies $E_{\mathrm{amp}}^*$ with a subbundle of $(\mathbb C^4)^*\otimes \mathcal O_ X$. This inclusion defines a proper morphism \[  q_ b:\mathbb P(E_{\mathrm{amp}}^*)\longrightarrow \mathbb P((\mathbb C^4)^*), \qquad \mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_{\mathrm{amp}}^*)}(1) =q_ b^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1).  \] For $w=[w_0:\cdots :w_3]$, its fiber is the common zero scheme of \[  s_ w=\sum _ iw_ i a_ i\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(H)), \qquad t_ w=\sum _ iw_ i b_ i\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H)).  \] Linear independence of $a$ gives $s_ w\neq 0$ for every $w$. Step 4: no common curves. A nonzero effective subdivisor $D$ of $\operatorname {div}(s_ w)$ has class $uS+vf$, where \[  u\in \{ 0,1\} ,\qquad 0\leq v\leq 3e+1, \qquad (u,v)\neq (0,0).  \] Write $|D|=\mathbb P H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(D))$ for the complete linear system. For each of these finitely many classes $D_0$, let $T_{D_0}$ parametrize the triples $(w,[\sigma ],[\tau ])$ with \[  [\sigma ]\in |D_0|,\qquad [\tau ]\in |H-D_0|, \qquad [s_ w]=[\sigma \tau ].  \] Since products of nonzero sections are nonzero, this is a closed projective parameter scheme. Its fiber over $w$ consists of the finitely many effective subdivisors of the fixed divisor $\operatorname {div}(s_ w)$, counted with their possible multiplicities. Thus $\dim T_{D_0}\leq 3$. Vanishing on a nonzero effective divisor $D$ imposes at least four independent conditions on $H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H))$. Indeed, choose an integral curve $C$ in its support. Very ampleness gives sections $r_0,r_1$ of $\mathcal O_ X(H)$ with nonconstant ratio on $C$. The four cubic monomials in their restrictions are linearly independent, since a linear relation would make the nonconstant ratio algebraic over $\mathbb C$, hence constant. For fixed $(w,[\sigma ],[\tau ])$, the map $V\to H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H))$, $b\mapsto t_ w$, is surjective. The condition that $t_ w$ vanish on $D=\operatorname {div}(\sigma )$ therefore has codimension at least four in $V$. This condition is closed in families: the universal multiplication map \[  H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H-D_0))\otimes \mathcal O_{|D_0|}(-1) \longrightarrow H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(3H))\otimes \mathcal O_{|D_0|}  \] is injective on fibers, so its image is a subbundle, and the condition is the vanishing of the image of $t_ w$ in the quotient bundle. Its incidence over $T_{D_0}$ has dimension at most $N-1$, and its image in $V$ is closed. Step 5: conclusion. Choose $b$ outside these finitely many proper closed images and outside the image of Step 2. Then $s_ w$ and $t_ w$ have no common curve for any $w$, so every fiber of $q_ b$ is finite. A proper morphism with finite fibers is finite, and the pullback of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1)$ by a finite morphism is ample; hence $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is ample. Finally, the Whitney formula gives \[  c(E_{\mathrm{amp}})=\frac1{(1-H)(1-3H)}=1+4H+13H^2.  \] $\square$ A vector bundle $E$ on $X$ is called prioritary for the ruling if $\operatorname {Ext}^2_ X(E,E(-f))=0$. Since all ruling fibers are linearly equivalent, this condition does not depend on the chosen fiber, and by Serre duality it is equivalent to \[  \operatorname {Hom}_ X(E,E(K_ X+f))=0.  \] Prioritary bundles of fixed rank and Chern classes form an irreducible family, by the theorem of Walter recalled in 4.6.6 . Lemma 4.6.21 . Both $E_0$ and $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ are prioritary for the ruling. Proof. Write $D=K_ X+f=-2S-(e+1)f$. The summands of $\operatorname {End}(E_0)(D)$ have classes \[  D,\quad D,\quad 4S-(13e+7)f,\quad -8S+(11e+5)f.  \] Each has a negative coefficient in the basis $S,f$, so by lemma 4.6.19 none of them has a nonzero section. This proves the required vanishing of $\operatorname {Hom}$ for $E_0$. Precomposition with the surjection $\mathcal O_ X^4\to E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ gives an injection \[  \operatorname {Hom}(E_{\mathrm{amp}},E_{\mathrm{amp}}(D)) \hookrightarrow H^0(X,E_{\mathrm{amp}}(D))^4.  \] Twist the defining sequence by $D$. Its middle term has no sections. For $j=1,3$, Serre duality and the formula of lemma 4.6.19 give \[  \begin{aligned}  H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(D-jH))& =H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(jH-f))^*,\\  \pi _*\mathcal O_ X(jH-f)& =\bigoplus _{i=0}^ j\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(j(3e+1)-1-ie). \end{aligned}  \] The higher direct image vanishes, and every degree in this sum is at least $j(2e+1)-1\geq 0$. Hence all these first cohomology groups vanish, and the long exact sequence of the twisted sequence gives $H^0(X,E_{\mathrm{amp}}(D))=0$. This proves the vanishing of $\operatorname {Hom}$ for $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$. $\square$ Proposition 4.6.22 . For $F_ s=L_ s^*$, $s=1,2$, there are Kähler forms $\eta _ s$ with $\deg _{\eta _ s}F_ s=1$. Consequently, the split bundle $E_0^*=F_1\oplus F_2$ satisfies the hypotheses of theorem 4.6.4 . Proof. The integral classes \[  A_1=6S+(6e+1)f,\qquad A_2=S+(13e+6)f  \] are very ample by lemma 4.6.19 . Pullbacks of normalized Fubini–Study forms under the corresponding embeddings give Kähler forms $\eta _ s$ representing $c_1(\mathcal O_ X(A_ s))$. A direct computation of intersection numbers gives \[  c_1(L_1)\cdot A_1=-1,\qquad c_1(L_2)\cdot A_2=-1,  \] so the degrees of the duals are equal to one. Since $n=2$, the closed positive $(1,1)$-forms $\eta _ s$ are admissible test forms $\Theta _ s$ in theorem 4.6.4 . $\square$

title: Lemma 4.6.19
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Lemma 4.6.19 . For integers $a\geq 0$ and $b$, \[  \pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)= \bigoplus _{i=0}^ a\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(b-ie), \qquad R^1\pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)=0.  \] A class $aS+bf$ is effective exactly when $a,b\geq 0$. If $a\geq 1$ and $b>ae$, its line bundle is very ample. In particular, \[  H=S+(3e+1)f, \qquad H^2=5e+2, \qquad h^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(H))=5e+4.  \] The canonical class is $K_ X=-2S-(e+2)f$. Proof. Over a trivializing chart of the base, sections of $\mathcal O_ X(aS)$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree $a$ in the fiber coordinates. Their transition law gives \[  \pi _*\mathcal O_ X(aS)= \operatorname {Sym}^ a(\mathcal O\oplus \mathcal O(-e)),  \] and twisting by the base gives the formula. The first cohomology of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(a)$ on each fiber vanishes, which gives the assertion on the higher direct image. If $a<0$, restriction to a general ruling fiber excludes a nonzero section. For $a\geq 0$, the direct-image formula gives a nonzero section exactly when $b\geq 0$. Suppose that $a\geq 1$ and $b>ae$. All line bundles in the direct image then have degree at least one. Fiber polynomials of degree $a$ separate points and tangent directions within a fiber. To separate points over different base points, choose a fiber monomial that is nonzero at the first point and a coefficient section vanishing at the second base point but not at the first. At any point, choose such a nonzero monomial and a coefficient section with a simple zero at its base point; the resulting global section vanishes there, has nonzero derivative in a prescribed base direction and has zero vertical derivative. title: 4.6.5 Stable extensions approaching the split comparison bundle
search_title: Stable extensions approaching the split comparison bundle
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
4.6.5 Stable extensions approaching the split comparison bundle The bundles near $E_0$ that we construct will also be slope-stable for a fixed polarization. The split bundle $E_0$ is unstable, and the ample bundle $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ need not be stable. Nonsplit extensions of $L_2$ by $L_1$ have the same Chern classes as $E_0$, are stable, and converge to $E_0$ as the extension class tends to zero; they are not ample, however. The next subsection combines them with $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$. Keep the Hirzebruch surface $X=\mathbb F_ e$, its ruling and the line bundles of 4.6.4 . Thus \[  L_1=\mathcal O_ X(5S-f),\qquad L_2=\mathcal O_ X(-S+(12e+5)f),\qquad E_0=L_1\oplus L_2.  \] We use the very ample polarization $P=4H-f=4S+(12e+3)f$. For a torsion-free coherent sheaf $E$ of positive rank on $X$, put \[  \deg _ PE=c_1(E)\cdot P, \qquad \mu _ P(E)=\frac{\deg _ PE}{\operatorname {rank}E}.  \] A vector bundle $V$ is $\mu _ P$-stable if $\mu _ P(M)<\mu _ P(V)$ for every coherent subsheaf $M\subset V$ with $0<\operatorname {rank}M<\operatorname {rank}V$. Since $\mu _ P(L_2)>\mu _ P(E_0)$ by the computation below, the split bundle $E_0$ is not $\mu _ P$-stable. Proposition 4.6.23 . The extension space has dimension \[  \dim \operatorname {Ext}^1_ X(L_2,L_1)=105e+35.  \] Every nonsplit extension \[  0\longrightarrow L_1\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow {q}L_2 \longrightarrow 0  \] is a locally free, $\mu _ P$-stable bundle with $c_1(V)=4H$ and $c_2(V)=13H^2$. Proof. Extensions of line bundles are locally free: the quotient is free on a small trivializing neighborhood, so the sequence splits there. Their classes form \[  \operatorname {Ext}^1_ X(L_2,L_1) =H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(6S-(12e+6)f)).  \] By lemma 4.6.19 , the higher direct image of this line bundle vanishes and its direct image is the sum of the seven line bundles $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-12e-6-ie)$, $0\leq i\leq 6$. Their first cohomology groups have total dimension \[  \sum _{i=0}^6(12e+5+ie)=105e+35>0.  \] The Chern classes follow from the extension sequence. Direct computations of intersection numbers give \[  \mu _ P(L_1)=40e+11,\qquad \mu _ P(V)=40e+14, \qquad \mu _ P(L_2)=40e+17.  \] It suffices to test line-bundle subsheaves $M\hookrightarrow V$. Indeed, a rank-one torsion-free subsheaf on a smooth surface has a line bundle as its double dual, and its inclusion extends across the finitely many missing points by Hartogs extension in local bundle frames. The extended map remains injective and has the same first Chern class. This argument does not require the quotient to be locally free. If the composite $M\to L_2$ is zero, then $M$ maps nontrivially into $L_1$, so $\deg _ P M\leq \mu _ P(L_1)<\mu _ P(V)$. Otherwise its zero divisor $D$ is effective and $M=L_2(-D)$. If $D=0$, the composite is an isomorphism and its inverse splits $q$, contrary to the hypothesis. Hence $D\neq 0$, and \[  \deg _ P M=\mu _ P(V)+3-D\cdot P.  \] Every effective class is $aS+bf$ with $a,b\geq 0$, and \[  S\cdot P=8e+3,\qquad f\cdot P=4.  \] For $e\geq 1$, every nonzero effective divisor has $P$-degree at least four, which proves the strict slope inequality. For $e=0$, the only nonzero effective class of $P$-degree at most three is $S$. A lift of multiplication by a nonzero section $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(S))$ from $L_2(-S)$ to $V$ would make the pullback of the nonzero extension class vanish. That pullback is the image of the class under the map \[  H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(6S-6f)) \xrightarrow {\  \cdot s\  }H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(7S-6f)).  \] On $X=\mathbb P^1\times \mathbb P^1$, order the factors so that $\mathcal O_ X(S)=\mathcal O(1,0)$ and $\mathcal O_ X(f)=\mathcal O(0,1)$. The Künneth formula identifies this map with \[  \bigl [H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(6)) \xrightarrow {\  \cdot s\  }H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(7))\bigr ] \otimes \operatorname {Id}_{H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-6))}.  \] Multiplication by a nonzero section is injective on global sections, and tensoring with a vector space preserves injectivity. Thus the nonzero extension class cannot pull back to zero. This excludes the possible equality of slopes and proves stability also for $e=0$. $\square$ Proposition 4.6.24 . Every extension of $L_2$ by $L_1$, including the split extension, is prioritary for the ruling and is not ample. Its restriction to every ruling fiber is $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(5)\oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. Proof. Put $D=K_ X+f=-2S-(e+1)f$. The four line bundles $L_ i^*\otimes L_ j(D)$ have classes \[  D,\quad D,\quad 4S-(13e+7)f,\quad -8S+(11e+5)f.  \] Each has a negative coefficient in the basis $S,f$, and hence no nonzero section. Applying $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(L_ i,\cdot )$ to the extension twisted by $D$ gives $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(L_ i,V(D))=0$ for $i=1,2$. Applying $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(\cdot ,V(D))$ to the original extension then gives $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(V,V(D))=0$. By Serre duality this is the prioritary condition $\operatorname {Ext}^2_ X(V,V(-f))=0$. Restriction to a ruling fiber is exact, because the quotient is locally free. The restricted line bundles have degrees five and minus one, and the restricted extension splits, since $\operatorname {Ext}^1_{\mathbb P^1}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O(5)) =H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(6))=0$. The quotient of negative degree on this curve excludes ampleness. $\square$ Proposition 4.6.25 . On the smooth bundle underlying $E_0$ there is a holomorphic one-parameter family of Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial _ t=\bar\partial _0+tA$, $t\in \mathbb C$, such that for $t\ne 0$ the holomorphic bundle defined by $\bar\partial _ t$ is $\mu _ P$-stable and prioritary, but not ample. As $t\to 0$, these operators converge to $\bar\partial _0$ in the $C^ m$ norm for every integer $m\geq 0$. Proof. Choose a nonzero extension class and a smooth Dolbeault representative $\eta \in \Omega ^{0,1}(X,L_2^*\otimes L_1)$ of it, so that $\bar\partial \eta =0$. On the smooth direct sum, set \[  A=\begin{pmatrix} 0

& \eta 

\\ 0

& 0

\end{pmatrix}.  \] The covariant Dolbeault derivative of $A$ is zero and $A\wedge A=0$, so $\bar\partial _ t^2=0$. Adding the Dolbeault operator of the base $\mathbb C$ of the parameter $t$ also gives an integrable operator on $X\times \mathbb C$, because the family depends holomorphically on $t$. This defines a holomorphic family of bundles whose extension class is $t[\eta ]$. It is nonsplit for $t\neq 0$, so the two preceding propositions apply. For a fixed smooth background connection and fixed metrics, \[  \| \bar\partial _ t-\bar\partial _0\| _{C^ m} =|t|\, \| A\| _{C^ m}\longrightarrow 0,  \] and the norm $\| A\| _{C^ m}$ is finite for every $m$ because $X$ is compact. $\square$ Thus stability and ampleness have been realized separately in the prioritary family of $E_0$: the nonsplit extensions are stable but not ample, while $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is ample. The deformation argument of theorem 4.6.30 joins the stable locus to the ample one and provides stable ample bundles arbitrarily close to $E_0$.

Hence $D\neq 0$, and \[  \deg _ P M=\mu _ P(V)+3-D\cdot P.  \] Every effective class is $aS+bf$ with $a,b\geq 0$, and \[  S\cdot P=8e+3,\qquad f\cdot P=4.  \] For $e\geq 1$, every nonzero effective divisor has $P$-degree at least four, which proves the strict slope inequality. For $e=0$, the only nonzero effective class of $P$-degree at most three is $S$. A lift of multiplication by a nonzero section $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_ X(S))$ from $L_2(-S)$ to $V$ would make the pullback of the nonzero extension class vanish. That pullback is the image of the class under the map \[  H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(6S-6f)) \xrightarrow {\  \cdot s\  }H^1(X,\mathcal O_ X(7S-6f)).  \] On $X=\mathbb P^1\times \mathbb P^1$, order the factors so that $\mathcal O_ X(S)=\mathcal O(1,0)$ and $\mathcal O_ X(f)=\mathcal O(0,1)$. The Künneth formula identifies this map with \[  \bigl [H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(6)) \xrightarrow {\  \cdot s\  }H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(7))\bigr ] \otimes \operatorname {Id}_{H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-6))}.  \] Multiplication by a nonzero section is injective on global sections, and tensoring with a vector space preserves injectivity. Thus the nonzero extension class cannot pull back to zero. This excludes the possible equality of slopes and proves stability also for $e=0$. $\square$

title: Proposition 4.6.24
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Proposition 4.6.24 . Every extension of $L_2$ by $L_1$, including the split extension, is prioritary for the ruling and is not ample. Its restriction to every ruling fiber is $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(5)\oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. Proof. Put $D=K_ X+f=-2S-(e+1)f$. The four line bundles $L_ i^*\otimes L_ j(D)$ have classes \[  D,\quad D,\quad 4S-(13e+7)f,\quad -8S+(11e+5)f.  \] Each has a negative coefficient in the basis $S,f$, and hence no nonzero section. Applying $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(L_ i,\cdot )$ to the extension twisted by $D$ gives $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(L_ i,V(D))=0$ for $i=1,2$. Applying $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(\cdot ,V(D))$ to the original extension then gives $\operatorname {Hom}_ X(V,V(D))=0$. By Serre duality this is the prioritary condition $\operatorname {Ext}^2_ X(V,V(-f))=0$. Restriction to a ruling fiber is exact, because the quotient is locally free. The restricted line bundles have degrees five and minus one, and the restricted extension splits, since $\operatorname {Ext}^1_{\mathbb P^1}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O(5)) =H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(6))=0$. The quotient of negative degree on this curve excludes ampleness. $\square$

title: Proposition 4.6.25
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
Proposition 4.6.25 . On the smooth bundle underlying $E_0$ there is a holomorphic one-parameter family of Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial _ t=\bar\partial _0+tA$, $t\in \mathbb C$, such that for $t\ne 0$ the holomorphic bundle defined by $\bar\partial _ t$ is $\mu _ P$-stable and prioritary, but not ample. As $t\to 0$, these operators converge to $\bar\partial _0$ in the $C^ m$ norm for every integer $m\geq 0$. Proof. Choose a nonzero extension class and a smooth Dolbeault representative $\eta \in \Omega ^{0,1}(X,L_2^*\otimes L_1)$ of it, so that $\bar\partial \eta =0$. On the smooth direct sum, set \[  A=\begin{pmatrix} 0

& \eta 

\\ 0

& 0

\end{pmatrix}.  \] The covariant Dolbeault derivative of $A$ is zero and $A\wedge A=0$, so $\bar\partial _ t^2=0$. Adding the Dolbeault operator of the base $\mathbb C$ of the parameter $t$ also gives an integrable operator on $X\times \mathbb C$, because the family depends holomorphically on $t$. This defines a holomorphic family of bundles whose extension class is $t[\eta ]$. It is nonsplit for $t\neq 0$, so the two preceding propositions apply. For a fixed smooth background connection and fixed metrics, \[  \| \bar\partial _ t-\bar\partial _0\| _{C^ m} =|t|\, \| A\| _{C^ m}\longrightarrow 0,  \] and the norm $\| A\| _{C^ m}$ is finite for every $m$ because $X$ is compact. $\square$

title: 4.6.6 Deforming to stable ample bundles
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
4.6.6 Deforming to stable ample bundles We keep the Hirzebruch surface $X=\mathbb F_ e$ and the data $H,P,L_1,L_2,E_0$ of 4.6.4 , 4.6.5 . The ample quotient $E_{\mathrm{amp}}$ and a nonsplit extension are two prioritary bundles with the same Chern classes as $E_0$; the former is ample and the latter is stable. Prioritary bundles with these invariants form an irreducible family in which ampleness and stability are open conditions, so bundles with both properties are dense in the family, and in particular they accumulate at $E_0$. We first prove the required openness assertions for algebraic families. Throughout this subsection, $T$ denotes a smooth complex algebraic variety. A flat family is a coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ on $X	imes T$ that is flat over $T$, and its fiber $\mathcal E_ t$ at $t\in T$ is its restriction to $X	imes \{ t\} $. Lemma 4.6.26 . If a flat family $\mathcal E$ has a locally free fiber at $t_0\in T$, then $\mathcal E$ is a vector bundle on $X	imes T'$ for some Zariski-open neighborhood $T'$ of $t_0$. Proof. At a point of $X	imes \{ t_0\} $, lift a local basis of the fiber to $\mathcal E$. By Nakayama's lemma, the resulting map from a free module of finite rank is surjective near that point. Tensor its kernel sequence with the residue field of $t_0$. Flatness over $T$ makes the first Tor term zero, so the kernel restricts to the kernel of the chosen isomorphism on the fiber, namely zero, and Nakayama's lemma shows that the kernel vanishes near that point. Thus $\mathcal E$ is locally free near every point of the central fiber. The locus where $\mathcal E$ is not locally free is closed. Since the projection $X	imes T	o T$ is proper, the image of that locus is closed and misses $t_0$, and we remove this image. $\square$ Lemma 4.6.27 . For a vector bundle $\mathcal E$ on $X	imes T$, the parameters $t$ for which $\mathcal E_ t$ is ample form a Zariski-open subset of $T$. Proof. Put $Y=\mathbb P_{X	imes T}(\mathcal E^*)$, with the line convention, and let $p:Y	o T$ be the projection, a projective flat morphism. Write $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_ Y(1)$. If $\mathcal E_{t_0}$ is ample, then $\mathcal L_{t_0}$ is ample. Choose $k$ so that its $k$th power is very ample and has vanishing higher cohomology. By Serre vanishing, semicontinuity, and cohomology and base change, after shrinking $T$ around $t_0$ the sheaf $\mathcal V=p_*\mathcal L^ k$ is locally free and commutes with restriction to fibers. After a further shrinking, the evaluation map $p^*\mathcal V	o \mathcal L^ k$ is surjective: its cokernel vanishes on the central fiber, and the image of its support under the proper map $p$ is closed and misses $t_0$. Evaluation gives a proper morphism \[  g:Y\longrightarrow \mathbb P_ T(\mathcal V^*), \qquad g^*\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal L^ k,  \] whose restriction to the central fiber is a closed immersion. The locus where $g$ is quasi-finite is open; its complement has closed image in $T$ by properness and misses $t_0$, so after a further shrinking $g$ is proper and quasi-finite, hence finite. For a finite morphism, pushforward commutes with base change. The cokernel of \[  \mathcal O_{\mathbb P_ T(\mathcal V^*)}\longrightarrow g_*\mathcal O_ Y  \] therefore vanishes on the central fiber, and its support projects to a closed subset of $T$ missing $t_0$. After removing that subset, the map is surjective, so $g$ is a closed immersion. Consequently $\mathcal L^ k$ is very ample on every fiber, and $\mathcal E_ t$ is ample there. $\square$ Lemma 4.6.28 . For a family $\mathcal E$ of rank-two vector bundles on $X	imes T$ whose fibers have a fixed first Chern class, the parameters $t$ for which $\mathcal E_ t$ is $\mu _ P$-stable form a Zariski-open subset of $T$. Proof. Fix a stable fiber at $t_0$ and put $
u =c_1(\mathcal E_ t)\cdot P/2$, which is independent of $t$. Choose $k\geq 1$ such that $\mathcal E_{t_0}^*(kP)$ is globally generated and has vanishing higher cohomology. The argument with Serre vanishing, base change and evaluation used in the previous proof gives, over a neighborhood of $t_0$, maps \[  \mathcal E_ t\longrightarrow \mathcal O_ X(kP)^{\oplus N}  \] that are injective on every fiber. By the double-dual argument for rank-one subsheaves in the proof of proposition 4.6.23 , a destabilizing subsheaf of $\mathcal E_ t$ yields a nonzero map from a line bundle $M=\mathcal O_ X(aS+bf)$ with $\deg _ P M\geq 
u $. At least one component of its composite with the injection above is nonzero, and since effective classes have nonnegative coefficients, \[  a\leq 4k,\qquad b\leq (12e+3)k.  \] Since $\deg _ P M=(8e+3)a+4b$, the inequality $\deg _ PM\geq 
u $ also gives \[  a\geq  rac{
u -4(12e+3)k}{8e+3}, \qquad b\geq  rac{
u -4k(8e+3)}4.  \] Only finitely many integral pairs $(a,b)$ satisfy these four bounds. For each such pair with $\deg _ P M\geq 
u $, semicontinuity makes the set \[  \{ t:H^0(X,\mathcal E_ t\otimes M^*)
eq 0\}   \] closed, and it does not contain $t_0$. Conversely, a nonzero map from such an $M$ is injective as a map of sheaves and violates stability. Thus the set of parameters with unstable fibers is, on this neighborhood, exactly the finite union of these closed subsets, and removing the union proves the claim. $\square$ Lemma 4.6.29 . Let $T$ be smooth and irreducible, let $U\subset T$ be a nonempty Zariski-open subset, and let $\mathcal E$ be a vector bundle on $X	imes T$. For every $t_0\in T$, there are points $t_ j\in U$ tending to $t_0$ in the analytic topology, together with smooth complex-linear identifications of the bundles underlying $\mathcal E_{t_ j}$ and $\mathcal E_{t_0}$, under which the Dolbeault operators of the fibers converge in the $C^ m$ norm for every integer $m\geq 0$. The dual operators converge in the same sense. Proof. The proper algebraic closed subset $T\setminus U$ has empty interior in the analytic topology. In an analytic coordinate ball $B$ around $t_0$, choose $t_ j\in U\cap B$ with $t_ j	o t_0$. Choose a smooth complex connection on $\mathcal E|_{X	imes B}$. Parallel transport along radial paths in $B$, keeping $x\in X$ fixed, gives identifications \[  \Phi _ t:\mathcal E_{t_0}^{\mathrm{sm}}\longrightarrow \mathcal E_ t^{\mathrm{sm}},\qquad \Phi _{t_0}=\operatorname {id},  \] depending smoothly on $(x,t)$, where the superscript $\mathrm{sm}$ denotes the underlying smooth complex bundle. These identifications need not be holomorphic. Transport the Dolbeault operators by these maps and write \[   ar\partial _ t=\Phi _ t^{-1} ar\partial _{\mathcal E_ t}\Phi _ t, \qquad A_ t= ar\partial _ t- ar\partial _{\mathcal E_{t_0}}.  \] Since both operators satisfy the same Leibniz rule, $A_ t$ is an endomorphism-valued $(0,1)$-form. Its coefficients are smooth in $(x,t)$, and $A_{t_0}=0$. Fix background metrics and a smooth connection on the central bundle. Compactness of $X$ and continuity of every finite collection of derivatives give \[  \| A_{t_ j}\| _{C^ m(X)}\longrightarrow 0 \qquad 	ext{for every integer }m\geq 0.  \] The dual identifications are $(\Phi _ t^{-1})^*$. In transported dual frames the perturbation is $-A_ t^{\mathsf T}$, so the same convergence holds for the dual Dolbeault operators. $\square$ We use Walter's theorem on prioritary stacks: on a birationally ruled surface, a nonempty stack of prioritary torsion-free sheaves with fixed rank $r\geq 2$ and fixed numerical Chern classes is smooth and irreducible. Here prioritary means that $\operatorname {Ext}^2(E,E(-f))=0$ for every ruling fiber $f$; on $X$ all ruling fibers are linearly equivalent. The theorem concerns the full prioritary stack and has no semistability hypothesis. Theorem 4.6.30 . For every $e\geq 0$, there are integrable Dolbeault operators on the smooth bundle underlying $E_0$ that converge to its split operator in every $C^ m$ norm, $m\geq 0$, and define ample $\mu _ P$-stable bundles of rank two with $c_1=4H$ and $c_2=13H^2$. The induced dual operators converge to the split dual operator in every $C^ m$ norm. Proof. Let $\mathcal P$ be the prioritary stack with invariants $(2,4H,13H^2)$. It contains $E_0$ by proposition 4.6.24 , and Walter's theorem makes it smooth and irreducible. Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal S$ be the loci of ample and of $\mu _ P$-stable vector bundles in $\mathcal P$. They are open by the three preceding family lemmas, which apply on smooth local charts of $\mathcal P$; the first lemma allows restriction to locally free families near a point given by a vector bundle. The ample bundle of proposition 4.6.20 is prioritary by lemma 4.6.21 , so $\mathcal A$ is nonempty. A nonsplit extension is stable and prioritary by proposition 4.6.23 , proposition 4.6.24 , so $\mathcal S$ is nonempty. By irreducibility, $\mathcal U=\mathcal A\cap \mathcal S$ is nonempty and dense. Choose a smooth local chart $q:T	o \mathcal P$ of finite type over $\mathbb C$, with a point $t_0$ representing $E_0$, and let $\mathcal E$ be the corresponding flat family on $X	imes T$. Fix an identification $\mathcal E_{t_0}\simeq E_0$. The variety $T$ is smooth because the stack and the chart are smooth. Shrink $T$ to an irreducible neighborhood of $t_0$ and use lemma 4.6.26 to make $\mathcal E$ a vector bundle on the whole product. The inverse image $q^{-1}(\mathcal U)$ is dense: every nonempty open $T'\subset T$ has nonempty open image $q(T')$ under the smooth map $q$, and this image meets $\mathcal U$. Apply lemma 4.6.29 to this dense open set. Each transported operator defines a bundle isomorphic to the corresponding ample stable fiber. The fixed invariants of the stack give its Chern classes, and the lemma also gives the convergence of the dual operators. $\square$ Corollary 4.6.31 . For every $e\geq 0$, there is an ample $\mu _ P$-stable bundle $E$ of rank two on $X$ with $c_1(E)=4H$ and $c_2(E)=13H^2$ that admits no smooth strongly pseudoconvex squared Finsler metric with semipositive Kobayashi curvature. Proof. By proposition 4.6.22 , the two line summands of $E_0^*$ have positive degrees with respect to suitable test forms. The preceding theorem gives an ample stable bundle $E$ whose dual Dolbeault operator is as close to the split dual operator in $C^4$ as required. Apply corollary 4.6.18 to $F=E^*$. $\square$

title: 4.6.7 A fixed Stein hypersurface for all Finsler metrics
search_title: A fixed Stein hypersurface for all Finsler metrics
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
4.6.7 A fixed Stein hypersurface for all Finsler metrics Corollary 4.6.31 shows that no Finsler metric on $E$ has semipositive Kobayashi curvature, but it does not locate the failure. For a single metric, a point where the curvature is not semipositive gives a local hypersurface through that point on which the metric has a nondegenerate critical point with many positive Levi directions. Holomorphic approximation on a Stein manifold allows one hypersurface to serve for all metrics at once. In this subsection, $X$ is a connected smooth projective variety of dimension $n\geq 1$, and $E	o X$ is an algebraic vector bundle of rank $r\geq 2$, viewed as a holomorphic bundle. We use the squared Finsler metrics and the convention for Kobayashi curvature of 4.6.3 . A compact subset $K$ of a Stein manifold $Y$ is holomorphically convex if it coincides with its holomorphic hull $\{ y\in Y:|f(y)|\leq \sup _ K|f|	ext{ for all }f\in \mathcal O(Y)\} $. We use the classical Oka–Weil theorem in the following form: a function holomorphic near a holomorphically convex compact subset of a Stein manifold can be approximated uniformly there by global holomorphic functions. We also use polynomial Runge approximation in one variable on a union of two disjoint closed disks. Lemma 4.6.32 . Let $K,L$ be holomorphically convex compact subsets of a Stein manifold $Y$. If a global holomorphic function maps them into disjoint closed disks in $\mathbb C$, then $K\cup L$ is holomorphically convex. Proof. Write $h$ for the function and $\Delta _ K,\Delta _ L$ for the disks. Their union is polynomially convex, so testing with polynomials in $h$ shows that $h$ maps the holomorphic hull of $K\cup L$ into $\Delta _ K\cup \Delta _ L$. Suppose that $p
otin K\cup L$ and $h(p)\in \Delta _ K$. Holomorphic convexity of $K$ gives $a\in \mathcal O(Y)$ with $|a(p)|>\sup _ K|a|$. Choose polynomials tending uniformly to one on $\Delta _ K$ and to zero on $\Delta _ L$. Their compositions with $h$, multiplied by $a$, converge to $a$ at $p$ and on $K$, and to zero on $L$. A sufficiently good approximation therefore separates $p$ from $K\cup L$. The case $h(p)\in \Delta _ L$ is identical, with $K$ and $L$ interchanged. Thus no point outside $K\cup L$ belongs to its hull. $\square$ Lemma 4.6.33 . Let $U$ be a connected smooth affine variety and let $q\geq 0$ be an integer. Put $B=U	imes \mathbb C^*	imes \mathbb C^ q$, with coordinates $(x,t,s)$, and for $\lambda \in \mathbb C^*$ let $d_\lambda (x,t,s)=(x,\lambda t,\lambda s)$. For each $j\geq 1$, let $C_ j\subset B$ be a holomorphically convex compact set, let $g_ j$ be holomorphic near $C_ j$, and let $\delta _ j>0$. Suppose that $t(C_ j)$ lies in the disk $|t-t_ j|\leq |t_ j|/4$ for some $t_ j
eq 0$. Then there are $\lambda _ j\in \mathbb C^*$ and $f\in \mathcal O(B)$ such that \[  \sup _{d_{\lambda _ j}(C_ j)} |f-\lambda _ j g_ j\circ d_{\lambda _ j}^{-1}|<|\lambda _ j|\delta _ j \qquad (j\geq 1).  \] Proof. Choose an exhaustion $(L_ j)_{j\geq 0}$ of the affine, hence Stein, manifold $B$ by holomorphically convex compact sets with $L_ j\subset \operatorname {int}L_{j+1}$. We construct $f_ j\in \mathcal O(B)$ and compact sets $K_ j$ inductively, starting with $f_0=0$ and $K_0=L_0$. At stage $j\geq 1$, choose $M>0$ with $t(K_{j-1})\subset \{ |t|\leq M\} $, and choose $R>4M/3$. Oka–Weil approximation gives $f_ j\in \mathcal O(B)$ with \[  \sup _{K_{j-1}}|f_ j-f_{j-1}|<\epsilon _ j, \qquad \sup _{C_ j}|f_ j-g_ j|<\epsilon _ j, \qquad \epsilon _ j=2^{-j-2}\min (1,\delta _1,\ldots ,\delta _ j).  \] Let $K_ j$ be a member of the fixed exhaustion containing $K_{j-1}\cup C_ j\cup L_ j$ in its interior. The interiors of the sets $K_ j$ exhaust $B$, and the summable errors make $f_ j$ converge locally uniformly to some $f\in \mathcal O(B)$. For a fixed $j$, every later approximation controls its error on $C_ j$, since $C_ j\subset K_{m-1}$ for $m>j$. Consequently \[  \sup _{C_ j}|f-g_ j| \leq \sum _{m\geq j}\epsilon _ m \leq 2^{-j-1}\delta _ j<\delta _ j.  \] Returning to the original notation gives the stated tolerances. $\square$ Theorem 4.6.34 . Suppose that $E$ admits no smooth strongly pseudoconvex squared Finsler metric with semipositive Kobayashi curvature. We seek $\mathcal S$ as a graph $w=f(x,t,s)$ over $B$; such a graph avoids the zero section because $t
e 0$. Step 2: a local test for one metric. Fix a candidate metric $G$. Since its Kobayashi curvature is not semipositive, its horizontal Schur complement has a positive direction somewhere. This condition is open, so it holds at a point $v_0=(x_0,w_0,t_0,s_0)$ with $x_0\in U$, $t_0
eq 0$ and $G_ w(v_0)
eq 0$. eq 0$, the space $K$ is the graph of a linear map defined on $T_{b_0}^{1,0}B$, where $b_0=(x_0,t_0,s_0)$. Keep this first jet of $g$ fixed and vary its quadratic jet. The mixed second derivatives of $F$ do not change, while in local coordinates $z$ on $B$ the pure second derivatives satisfy \[  F_{\alpha  eta }(b_0)=A_{\alpha  eta }+G_ w(v_0)g_{\alpha  eta }(b_0),  \] where $A$ is fixed. Since $G_ w(v_0)
e 0$, we can prescribe the pure quadratic part of $F$ to be $	au \operatorname {Re}\sum _\alpha z_\alpha ^2$, whose real Hessian has eigenvalues $\pm 2	au $. eq 0\} $ of $E^	imes $. Every candidate metric belongs to some $\mathcal V_ j$, so its restriction to $\mathcal S$ has the required nondegenerate critical point. title: Lemma 4.6.32
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Lemma 4.6.32 . Let $K,L$ be holomorphically convex compact subsets of a Stein manifold $Y$. If a global holomorphic function maps them into disjoint closed disks in $\mathbb C$, then $K\cup L$ is holomorphically convex. Proof. Write $h$ for the function and $\Delta _ K,\Delta _ L$ for the disks. Their union is polynomially convex, so testing with polynomials in $h$ shows that $h$ maps the holomorphic hull of $K\cup L$ into $\Delta _ K\cup \Delta _ L$. Suppose that $p\notin K\cup L$ and $h(p)\in \Delta _ K$. Holomorphic convexity of $K$ gives $a\in \mathcal O(Y)$ with $|a(p)|>\sup _ K|a|$. Choose polynomials tending uniformly to one on $\Delta _ K$ and to zero on $\Delta _ L$. Their compositions with $h$, multiplied by $a$, converge to $a$ at $p$ and on $K$, and to zero on $L$. A sufficiently good approximation therefore separates $p$ from $K\cup L$. The case $h(p)\in \Delta _ L$ is identical, with $K$ and $L$ interchanged. Thus no point outside $K\cup L$ belongs to its hull. $\square$

title: 4.6.8 Concave neighborhoods and dual norms
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
4.6.8 Concave neighborhoods and dual norms A relatively compact neighborhood $\Omega $ of the zero section of a vector bundle $E$ determines a norm on $E^*$, the support function $\xi \mapsto \max _{v\in \overline\Omega \cap E_ x}|\xi (v)|$ of its fibers. If the boundary of $\Omega $ is sufficiently concave in the horizontal directions, holomorphic sections touching the boundary from inside show that this support norm has plurisubharmonic square, and supporting balls give it uniform convexity in the fibers. Consequently, when the dual norms are obstructed as in theorem 4.6.4 , such neighborhoods cannot exist. In terms of exhaustion functions, this bounds the convexity of the complement of the zero section in the projective completion of $E$. In this subsection, $E	o X$ is a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r\geq 1$, and $n\geq 1$. Fix a smooth Hermitian metric $k$ on $E$, with real inner product $k_{\mathbb R}=\operatorname {Re}k$ and dual norm $|\cdot |_{k^*}$. For a smooth real function $f$, write $\mathcal L_ f$ for its complex Hessian. Let $\Omega $ be an open set with smooth boundary, defined near $\partial \Omega $ by $f<0$ with $\mathrm df
e 0$ on $\partial \Omega $. We say that $\partial \Omega $ has at least $n$ negative Levi directions if, at every boundary point, $\mathcal L_ f$ has at least $n$ negative eigenvalues on $\ker \partial f$. Lemma 4.6.36 . Fix $\delta ,B>0$. On a finite-dimensional Hermitian vector space, put \[  s_ c(\xi )=|\xi (c)|+\delta |\xi |  \] for covectors $\xi $ and vectors $c$ with $|c|\leq B$. There is $\gamma >0$, depending only on $\delta $ and $B$, such that $s_ c^2-\gamma |\xi |^2$ is real convex for every such $c$. Proof. For $0<	au \leq 1$, replace $s_ c$ by the norm \[  s_{c,	au }(\xi )=\sqrt{|\xi (c)|^2+	au |\xi |^2}+\delta |\xi |,  \] which is smooth off zero. Its Lipschitz constant is at most $L=\sqrt{B^2+1}+\delta $, uniformly in $c$ and $	au $. All derivatives below are real derivatives on the dual space. At $\xi 
e 0$, set $u=\xi /|\xi |$ and decompose a vector as $w=\alpha u+b$ with $b$ orthogonal to $u$ for the real inner product. Write $s=s_{c,	au }$ and $A=\mathrm ds_\xi (w)$. Since the first summand of $s$ is convex and $s\geq \delta |\xi |$, \[  D^2s(w,w)\geq \delta  rac{|b|^2}{|\xi |},\qquad D^2(s^2)(w,w)\geq 2A^2+2\delta ^2|b|^2.  \] Homogeneity gives $\mathrm ds_\xi (u)=s(\xi )/|\xi |\geq \delta $. Since $|\mathrm ds_\xi (b)|\leq L|b|$, we have \[  |w|^2\leq  rac{2A^2}{\delta ^2} +\left(1+ rac{2L^2}{\delta ^2}ight)|b|^2.  \] Take $\gamma =\delta ^4/(\delta ^2+2L^2)$. Then $\gamma \leq \delta ^2/2$ and $\gamma (1+2L^2/\delta ^2)=\delta ^2$, so $D^2(s^2)(w,w)\geq 2\gamma |w|^2$. The homogeneous function $s^2-\gamma |\xi |^2$ of degree two extends as a $C^1$ function at zero with differential zero. Its restriction to every real line is convex, including at zero, because its second derivative is nonnegative away from zero and its first derivatives match there. Thus it is convex on the whole space. Finally, \[  0\leq s_{c,	au }(\xi )-s_ c(\xi )\leq \sqrt	au \, |\xi |,  \] and the locally uniform limit as $	au \downarrow 0$ proves the assertion with the same $\gamma $. $\square$ Theorem 4.6.37 . Suppose that a relatively compact neighborhood $\Omega \Subset E$ of the zero section has smooth boundary with at least $n$ negative Levi directions. Then \[  p(x,\xi )=\max _{v\in \overline\Omega \cap E_ x}|\xi (v)|  \] is a continuous complex norm on $E^*$ whose square $Q=p^2$ is plurisubharmonic on the total space of $E^*$. For some $\gamma >0$, each function $Q(x,\cdot )-\gamma |\cdot |_{k^*}^2$ is real convex. If $E$ is ample, $E^*$ also admits a smooth complex norm with strictly plurisubharmonic square off the zero section. Proof. Step 1: basic bounds. Put $A_ x=\overline\Omega \cap E_ x$. By compactness of $X$ there are $0<a_0<b_0$ such that, in every fiber, the closed $k$-ball of radius $a_0$ is contained in $\Omega $ and $\overline\Omega $ lies in the open ball of radius $b_0$. The maximum defining $p$ is attained, and \[  a_0|\xi |_{k^*}\leq p(x,\xi )\leq b_0|\xi |_{k^*}.  \] As a supremum of absolute values of linear functionals, $p$ is complex homogeneous and satisfies the triangle inequality. Step 2: support points. Fix $\xi _0
e 0$ and a maximizing point $v_0\in A_{x_0}$. It lies on $\partial \Omega $, since at an interior point a small vertical displacement would increase $|\xi _0(v)|$. Multiply $\xi _0$ by a complex number of modulus one to obtain $\eta $ with $\eta (v_0)=p(x_0,\xi _0)=a>0$. Then $\ell =\operatorname {Re}\eta $ satisfies $\ell \leq a$ on $A_{x_0}$. Choose a smooth defining function $f$ near the boundary, with $\Omega =\{ f<0\} $ and $\mathrm df
e 0$ there. Let $V=T^{1,0}_{v_0}E_{x_0}$ be the vertical tangent space and $T=\ker \partial f(v_0)$. Choose an $n$-dimensional complex subspace $W\subset T$ on which $\mathcal L_ f$ is negative definite. We first show that the vertical differential $\mathrm d_ vf(v_0)$ is nonzero. Otherwise $V\subset T$, and counting dimensions gives $W\cap V
e \{ 0\} $. A vector in this intersection has negative vertical Levi form, and the two corresponding real directions show that the real vertical Hessian of $f$ has a negative direction. Its negative cone is open, hence contains a direction $w$ with $\ell (w)>0$. Since the vertical first derivative vanishes, Taylor expansion gives $f(v_0+tw)<0$ for small $t>0$, contradicting $\ell \leq a$ on $A_{x_0}$. The boundary of $A_{x_0}$ is therefore smooth at $v_0$. Since the supporting functional $\ell $ attains its maximum on $A_{x_0}$ there, \[  \mathrm d_ vf(v_0)=c\, \mathrm d\ell ,\qquad c>0;  \] the sign follows because an inward direction along which $\ell $ increases would contradict the maximality. On the affine hyperplane $\{ \ell =a\} $ of the fiber, the restriction of $f$ has a local minimum zero at $v_0$: a point there with $f<0$ would allow an additional displacement increasing $\ell $ within $\Omega $. The real vertical Hessian of $f$ is thus nonnegative on $\ker \mathrm d\ell $. Consequently $\mathcal L_ f$ is nonnegative on the complex space $V\cap T$, of dimension $r-1$. Hence $W\cap V=\{ 0\} $, and the projection $W	o T^{1,0}_{x_0}X$ is an isomorphism. Step 3: plurisubharmonicity. In local coordinates $z$ centered at $x_0$, choose a holomorphic section $\sigma _0$ through $v_0$ with tangent space $W$. The function $f\circ \sigma _0$ has zero first derivative and negative definite mixed Hessian. Its quadratic expansion is \[  f(\sigma _0(z))=\sum H_{\alpha  ar eta }z_\alpha  ar z_ eta +2\operatorname {Re}P(z)+O(|z|^3),  \] where $P$ is a holomorphic quadratic polynomial. Choose a vertical vector $b$ with $\partial _ vf(b)=1$, and replace $\sigma _0$ by $\sigma =\sigma _0-bP$. This preserves the first jet and cancels the pure quadratic part. Thus, after shrinking the chart, \[  f(\sigma (z))\leq -\epsilon |z|^2, \qquad \sigma (0)=v_0,  \] for some $\epsilon >0$. In particular $\sigma (z)\in A_ z$ throughout the chart. Compactness of $\overline\Omega $ makes $p$ upper semicontinuous: for convergent covectors, the corresponding maximizing vectors have a subsequence whose limit lies in the limiting fiber of $\overline\Omega $. The supporting section gives the opposite inequality $p(z,\xi )\geq |\xi (\sigma (z))|$, with equality at $(x_0,\xi _0)$. Therefore $p$ is continuous off the zero section, and its upper bound gives continuity at zero. The holomorphic pairing $\xi (\sigma (z))$ is nonzero near the contact point, and its logarithmic absolute value is a pluriharmonic function lying below $\log p$ and equal to it at $(x_0,\xi _0)$. The mean-value property on small holomorphic disks therefore gives the submean inequality for $\log p$ at every point off the zero section. Thus $\log p$, and then $Q=\exp (2\log p)$ by Jensen's inequality, are plurisubharmonic there. At the zero section the continuous nonnegative function $Q$ vanishes, so its submean inequality on disks also holds there. Step 4: uniform convexity in the fibers. Consider all maximizing triples $(x,\xi ,v)$ with $|\xi |_{k^*}=1$. They form a compact set, since $p$ is continuous, and by Step 2 the vertical differential $\mathrm d_ vf$ does not vanish at these support points. Thus there are uniform constants $m>0$, $ho >0$ and $C\geq 1$ such that, for vertical vectors $w$, \[  |\mathrm d_ vf|\geq m,\qquad f(v+w)\leq \mathrm d_ vf(w)+C|w|_ k^2\quad (|w|_ k\leq ho ).  \] Choose $0<\delta <\min \{ a_0/2,ho /2,m/(2C)\} $. At a support point, write $N$ for the outward real vertical unit normal and set $c=v-\delta N$. If $|w+\delta N|_ k\leq \delta $, then \[  k_{\mathbb R}(w,N)\leq - rac{|w|_ k^2}{2\delta },\qquad f(v+w)\leq -\left( rac{m}{2\delta }-Cight)|w|_ k^2\leq 0.  \] All these points lie in the neighborhood where $f$ is defined, so the closed ball $\overline B_ k(c,\delta )$ is contained in $A_ x$. The support function of this ball is $s_ c(\xi )=|\xi (c)|+\delta |\xi |_{k^*}\leq p(x,\xi )$. For a maximizing covector of unit norm, with its phase normalized as in Step 2, the real part $\operatorname {Re}\eta $ has real dual norm one and its metric dual vector is $N$. Hence $\operatorname {Re}\eta (N)=1$, and since $|\eta (N)|\leq 1$, also $\eta (N)=1$. We obtain $\eta (c)=a-\delta >0$, and therefore $s_ c(\xi )=a$. Homogeneity now gives \[  Q(x,\xi )=\sup _ c s_ c(\xi )^2,  \] where $c$ ranges over the centers of the supporting balls in the fiber. Every such center satisfies $|c|_ k\leq b_0+\delta $, so by lemma 4.6.36 all the functions $s_ c^2-\gamma |\xi |_{k^*}^2$ are convex for the same $\gamma >0$. Their supremum is finite, and it proves the asserted strong convexity of $Q$. Step 5: smoothing. Finally, if $E$ is ample, proposition 4.6.12 gives the smooth strictly plurisubharmonic homogeneous function on $E^*$ required in proposition 4.6.9 , and applying that proposition to $Q$ gives the smooth norm. $\square$ For a complex manifold of dimension $N$ and an integer $1\leq q\leq N$, we say that the manifold is $q$-convex if it has a smooth real exhaustion function with at least $N-q+1$ positive Levi eigenvalues outside a compact set; here an exhaustion function is one whose sublevel sets are compact. A $q$-convex manifold is also $q'$-convex for $q\leq q'\leq N$. We call such integers $q$ the smooth convexity indices of the manifold, and the smallest of them, when one exists, its least smooth convexity index . Lemma 4.6.38 . Let $Y$ be a complex manifold of dimension $N$, and let $Z\subset Y$ be a closed complex submanifold of dimension $D\geq 1$. If the least smooth convexity index of $Z$ is $\kappa \leq D$, then every smooth convexity index of $Y$ is at least $\kappa $. Proof. Suppose that $Y$ is $p$-convex for an integer $1\leq p<\kappa $. Then a smooth exhaustion function $\psi $ has at least $N-p+1$ positive Levi eigenvalues outside a compact set $K\subset Y$. Its restriction to the closed submanifold $Z$ is an exhaustion function, since its sublevel sets are closed subsets of the compact sublevel sets of $\psi $, and $K\cap Z$ is compact. At a point of $Z\setminus K$, choose a complex subspace $P\subset T^{1,0}Y$ of dimension $N-p+1$ on which the Levi form of $\psi $ is positive definite. Then \[  \dim _{\mathbb C}(P\cap T^{1,0}Z)\geq (N-p+1)+D-N=D-p+1.  \] The Levi form of $\psi |_ Z$ is the restriction of the Levi form of $\psi $, since the inclusion is holomorphic, so it has at least $D-p+1$ positive eigenvalues. Since $p<\kappa \leq D$, this shows that $Z$ is $p$-convex, which contradicts the definition of $\kappa $. $\square$ In the following results, projectivizations parametrize complex lines. Corollary 4.6.39 . Suppose that $E$ is ample and that $E^*$ admits no smooth complex norm with plurisubharmonic square off the zero section. Then the complement \[  Z\setminus Y,\qquad Z=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X\oplus E), \quad Y=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X),  \] is not $r$-convex. Proof. The chart of $Z$ where the $\mathcal O_ X$-coordinate is nonzero is identified with the total space of $E$, and $Y$ is its zero section. Suppose that $Z\setminus Y$ is $r$-convex. Since $\dim Z=n+r$, a smooth exhaustion function $\psi $ then has at least $n+1$ positive Levi eigenvalues outside a compact set $K$. Choose a relatively compact disk-bundle neighborhood $D\Subset E$ of $Y$. The set $Z\setminus D$ is compact and disjoint from $Y$. Choose a regular value $c$ of $\psi $ greater than its maximum on $Z\setminus D$ and on $K$. Since $\{ \psi \leq c\} $ is compact in $Z\setminus Y$, the set $\Omega =\{ \psi >c\} \cup Y$ is an open neighborhood of $Y$. Its closure is a compact subset of $D$, and its boundary is the regular level set $\{ \psi =c\} $. The defining function $f=c-\psi $ has at least $n+1$ negative Levi eigenvalues there. Restriction to the complex tangent hyperplane removes at most one negative direction, leaving at least $n$. Since $E$ is ample, theorem 4.6.37 produces a smooth complex norm on $E^*$ with plurisubharmonic square, a contradiction. $\square$ Corollary 4.6.40 . For every $e\geq 0$, there is an ample rank-two bundle $E$ on the Hirzebruch surface $X=\mathbb F_ e$ such that $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X\oplus E)\setminus \mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X)$ is not $2$-convex. The bundle may be chosen with the slope-stability and Chern classes of theorem 4.6.30 . Proof. Use theorem 4.6.30 to choose $E$ whose dual Dolbeault operator lies in the $C^4$ neighborhood of theorem 4.6.4 ; the split dual bundle satisfies the hypotheses of that theorem by proposition 4.6.22 . Thus $E^*$ admits no smooth complex norm with plurisubharmonic square, and corollary 4.6.39 with $r=2$ gives the assertion. $\square$

title: Lemma 4.6.36
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Lemma 4.6.36 . Fix $\delta ,B>0$. On a finite-dimensional Hermitian vector space, put \[  s_ c(\xi )=|\xi (c)|+\delta |\xi |  \] for covectors $\xi $ and vectors $c$ with $|c|\leq B$. There is $\gamma >0$, depending only on $\delta $ and $B$, such that $s_ c^2-\gamma |\xi |^2$ is real convex for every such $c$. Proof. For $0<\tau \leq 1$, replace $s_ c$ by the norm \[  s_{c,\tau }(\xi )=\sqrt{|\xi (c)|^2+\tau |\xi |^2}+\delta |\xi |,  \] which is smooth off zero. Its Lipschitz constant is at most $L=\sqrt{B^2+1}+\delta $, uniformly in $c$ and $\tau $. All derivatives below are real derivatives on the dual space. At $\xi \ne 0$, set $u=\xi /|\xi |$ and decompose a vector as $w=\alpha u+b$ with $b$ orthogonal to $u$ for the real inner product. Write $s=s_{c,\tau }$ and $A=\mathrm ds_\xi (w)$. Since the first summand of $s$ is convex and $s\geq \delta |\xi |$, \[  D^2s(w,w)\geq \delta \frac{|b|^2}{|\xi |},\qquad D^2(s^2)(w,w)\geq 2A^2+2\delta ^2|b|^2.  \] Homogeneity gives $\mathrm ds_\xi (u)=s(\xi )/|\xi |\geq \delta $. Since $|\mathrm ds_\xi (b)|\leq L|b|$, we have \[  |w|^2\leq \frac{2A^2}{\delta ^2} +\left(1+\frac{2L^2}{\delta ^2}\right)|b|^2.  \] Take $\gamma =\delta ^4/(\delta ^2+2L^2)$. Then $\gamma \leq \delta ^2/2$ and $\gamma (1+2L^2/\delta ^2)=\delta ^2$, so $D^2(s^2)(w,w)\geq 2\gamma |w|^2$. The homogeneous function $s^2-\gamma |\xi |^2$ of degree two extends as a $C^1$ function at zero with differential zero. Its restriction to every real line is convex, including at zero, because its second derivative is nonnegative away from zero and its first derivatives match there. Thus it is convex on the whole space. Finally, \[  0\leq s_{c,\tau }(\xi )-s_ c(\xi )\leq \sqrt\tau \, |\xi |,  \] and the locally uniform limit as $\tau \downarrow 0$ proves the assertion with the same $\gamma $. $\square$

title: Theorem 4.6.37
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
Theorem 4.6.37 . Suppose that a relatively compact neighborhood $\Omega \Subset E$ of the zero section has smooth boundary with at least $n$ negative Levi directions. Then \[  p(x,\xi )=\max _{v\in \overline\Omega \cap E_ x}|\xi (v)|  \] is a continuous complex norm on $E^*$ whose square $Q=p^2$ is plurisubharmonic on the total space of $E^*$. For some $\gamma >0$, each function $Q(x,\cdot )-\gamma |\cdot |_{k^*}^2$ is real convex. If $E$ is ample, $E^*$ also admits a smooth complex norm with strictly plurisubharmonic square off the zero section. Proof. Step 1: basic bounds. Put $A_ x=\overline\Omega \cap E_ x$. By compactness of $X$ there are $0<a_0<b_0$ such that, in every fiber, the closed $k$-ball of radius $a_0$ is contained in $\Omega $ and $\overline\Omega $ lies in the open ball of radius $b_0$. The maximum defining $p$ is attained, and \[  a_0|\xi |_{k^*}\leq p(x,\xi )\leq b_0|\xi |_{k^*}.  \] As a supremum of absolute values of linear functionals, $p$ is complex homogeneous and satisfies the triangle inequality. Step 2: support points. Fix $\xi _0
e 0$ and a maximizing point $v_0\in A_{x_0}$. It lies on $\partial \Omega $, since at an interior point a small vertical displacement would increase $|\xi _0(v)|$. Multiply $\xi _0$ by a complex number of modulus one to obtain $\eta $ with $\eta (v_0)=p(x_0,\xi _0)=a>0$. Then $\ell =\operatorname {Re}\eta $ satisfies $\ell \leq a$ on $A_{x_0}$. Choose a smooth defining function $f$ near the boundary, with $\Omega =\{ f<0\} $ and $\mathrm df
e 0$ there. Let $V=T^{1,0}_{v_0}E_{x_0}$ be the vertical tangent space and $T=\ker \partial f(v_0)$. Choose an $n$-dimensional complex subspace $W\subset T$ on which $\mathcal L_ f$ is negative definite. We first show that the vertical differential $\mathrm d_ vf(v_0)$ is nonzero. Otherwise $V\subset T$, and counting dimensions gives $W\cap V
e \{ 0\} $. A vector in this intersection has negative vertical Levi form, and the two corresponding real directions show that the real vertical Hessian of $f$ has a negative direction. Its negative cone is open, hence contains a direction $w$ with $\ell (w)>0$. Since the vertical first derivative vanishes, Taylor expansion gives $f(v_0+tw)<0$ for small $t>0$, contradicting $\ell \leq a$ on $A_{x_0}$. The boundary of $A_{x_0}$ is therefore smooth at $v_0$. Since the supporting functional $\ell $ attains its maximum on $A_{x_0}$ there, \[  \mathrm d_ vf(v_0)=c\, \mathrm d\ell ,\qquad c>0;  \] the sign follows because an inward direction along which $\ell $ increases would contradict the maximality. On the affine hyperplane $\{ \ell =a\} $ of the fiber, the restriction of $f$ has a local minimum zero at $v_0$: a point there with $f<0$ would allow an additional displacement increasing $\ell $ within $\Omega $. The real vertical Hessian of $f$ is thus nonnegative on $\ker \mathrm d\ell $. Consequently $\mathcal L_ f$ is nonnegative on the complex space $V\cap T$, of dimension $r-1$. In local coordinates $z$ centered at $x_0$, choose a holomorphic section $\sigma _0$ through $v_0$ with tangent space $W$. The function $f\circ \sigma _0$ has zero first derivative and negative definite mixed Hessian. Its quadratic expansion is \[  f(\sigma _0(z))=\sum H_{\alpha  ar eta }z_\alpha  ar z_ eta +2\operatorname {Re}P(z)+O(|z|^3),  \] where $P$ is a holomorphic quadratic polynomial. Choose a vertical vector $b$ with $\partial _ vf(b)=1$, and replace $\sigma _0$ by $\sigma =\sigma _0-bP$. This preserves the first jet and cancels the pure quadratic part. Thus, after shrinking the chart, \[  f(\sigma (z))\leq -\epsilon |z|^2, \qquad \sigma (0)=v_0,  \] for some $\epsilon >0$. In particular $\sigma (z)\in A_ z$ throughout the chart. Compactness of $\overline\Omega $ makes $p$ upper semicontinuous: for convergent covectors, the corresponding maximizing vectors have a subsequence whose limit lies in the limiting fiber of $\overline\Omega $. The supporting section gives the opposite inequality $p(z,\xi )\geq |\xi (\sigma (z))|$, with equality at $(x_0,\xi _0)$. Therefore $p$ is continuous off the zero section, and its upper bound gives continuity at zero. The holomorphic pairing $\xi (\sigma (z))$ is nonzero near the contact point, and its logarithmic absolute value is a pluriharmonic function lying below $\log p$ and equal to it at $(x_0,\xi _0)$. The mean-value property on small holomorphic disks therefore gives the submean inequality for $\log p$ at every point off the zero section. Thus $\log p$, and then $Q=\exp (2\log p)$ by Jensen's inequality, are plurisubharmonic there. At the zero section the continuous nonnegative function $Q$ vanishes, so its submean inequality on disks also holds there. Step 4: uniform convexity in the fibers. Consider all maximizing triples $(x,\xi ,v)$ with $|\xi |_{k^*}=1$. They form a compact set, since $p$ is continuous, and by Step 2 the vertical differential $\mathrm d_ vf$ does not vanish at these support points. Thus there are uniform constants $m>0$, $ho >0$ and $C\geq 1$ such that, for vertical vectors $w$, \[  |\mathrm d_ vf|\geq m,\qquad f(v+w)\leq \mathrm d_ vf(w)+C|w|_ k^2\quad (|w|_ k\leq ho ).  \] Choose $0<\delta <\min \{ a_0/2,ho /2,m/(2C)\} $. At a support point, write $N$ for the outward real vertical unit normal and set $c=v-\delta N$. If $|w+\delta N|_ k\leq \delta $, then \[  k_{\mathbb R}(w,N)\leq - rac{|w|_ k^2}{2\delta },\qquad f(v+w)\leq -\left( rac{m}{2\delta }-Cight)|w|_ k^2\leq 0.  \] All these points lie in the neighborhood where $f$ is defined, so the closed ball $\overline B_ k(c,\delta )$ is contained in $A_ x$. The support function of this ball is $s_ c(\xi )=|\xi (c)|+\delta |\xi |_{k^*}\leq p(x,\xi )$. For a maximizing covector of unit norm, with its phase normalized as in Step 2, the real part $\operatorname {Re}\eta $ has real dual norm one and its metric dual vector is $N$. Hence $\operatorname {Re}\eta (N)=1$, and since $|\eta (N)|\leq 1$, also $\eta (N)=1$. We obtain $\eta (c)=a-\delta >0$, and therefore $s_ c(\xi )=a$. Homogeneity now gives \[  Q(x,\xi )=\sup _ c s_ c(\xi )^2,  \] where $c$ ranges over the centers of the supporting balls in the fiber. Every such center satisfies $|c|_ k\leq b_0+\delta $, so by lemma 4.6.36 all the functions $s_ c^2-\gamma |\xi |_{k^*}^2$ are convex for the same $\gamma >0$. Their supremum is finite, and it proves the asserted strong convexity of $Q$. Step 5: smoothing. Finally, if $E$ is ample, proposition 4.6.12 gives the smooth strictly plurisubharmonic homogeneous function on $E^*$ required in proposition 4.6.9 , and applying that proposition to $Q$ gives the smooth norm. $\square$

title: 4.6.9 Curvature and projective complement exhaustions
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text:
4.6.9 Curvature and projective complement exhaustions Corollary 4.6.39 excludes $r$-convexity of the complement of the zero section in the projective completion, but it does not decide which larger indices occur. Upper bounds come from curvature. The reciprocal of the squared norm of a Hermitian metric is an exhaustion near the removed zero section, and every positive direction of the curvature, evaluated at a fiber vector, contributes a positive Levi eigenvalue. For a stable bundle of positive Gauduchon degree, the Hermitian–Einstein metric provides such a direction at every fiber vector. In this subsection, $E	o X$ is a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r\geq 1$, $n\geq 1$, and $h$ is a smooth Hermitian metric on $E$. In a holomorphic frame, write the matrix of $h$ as $M$, using column vectors and an inner product linear in its first argument, so that $h(v,v)=v^*Mv$. Put \[  F_ h= ar\partial (M^{-1}\partial M) =\sum _{\alpha , eta }F_{\alpha  ar eta }\, \mathrm dz_\alpha \wedge \mathrm d ar z_ eta , \qquad R_ h(u, ar u)=\sum _{\alpha , eta }F_{\alpha  ar eta }u_\alpha  ar u_ eta .  \] For $v\in E_ x$, the real $(1,1)$-form $\alpha _{h,v}=\mathrm i\, h(F_ hv,v)$ has the Hermitian coefficient form $u\mapsto h(R_ h(u, ar u)v,v)$. For a Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$, the mean curvature of $h$ is the $h$-Hermitian endomorphism $K_{\omega ,h}=\Lambda _\omega (\mathrm iF_ h)$, where $\Lambda _\omega $ denotes contraction with $\omega $, so that $\Lambda _\omega ( eta )\, \omega ^ n=n eta \wedge \omega ^{n-1}$ for $(1,1)$-forms $ eta $. The curvature $F_ h$ is unscaled: for a line bundle, the curvature $-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log h$ of section 4.6 is $\mathrm iF_ h/(2\pi )$. Use the line convention for projectivization and put \[  U_ E=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X\oplus E)\setminus \mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X).  \] The chart $[1:v]$ identifies the total space of $E$ with an open subset of $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X\oplus E)$, in which $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X)$ is the zero section; thus $U_ E$ contains $E^	imes $. Its complex dimension is $n+r$. Convexity is understood in the sense of the smooth exhaustions of 4.6.8 . Lemma 4.6.41 . Put $G(v)=h(v,v)$ and $ho =G^{-1}$ on $E^	imes $. In a holomorphic frame that is unitary and Chern-normal at $x$, meaning that $M(x)$ is the identity and the first derivatives of $M$ vanish at $x$, the complex Hessian of $ho $ at $(x,v)$ is \[  \mathcal L_ho (u,w) = rac{h(R_ h(u, ar u)v,v)}{G^2} - rac{|w|_ h^2}{G^2} + rac{2|h(w,v)|^2}{G^3}, \qquad u\in T_ x^{1,0}X,\quad w\in E_ x,  \] where $(u,w)$ are the horizontal and vertical components of a tangent vector. There are no mixed horizontal–vertical terms, and the vertical block has exactly one positive and $r-1$ negative eigenvalues. Proof. Such a frame is obtained by a constant change of frame making it unitary at $x$, followed by a holomorphic change of frame, linear in the coordinates, that cancels $\partial M$. Then $F_{\alpha  ar eta }=-\partial _\alpha \partial _{ ar eta }M$ at $x$. The horizontal first derivatives of $G$ and its mixed horizontal–vertical second derivatives vanish. The horizontal complex Hessian of $G$ is $-h(R_ h(u, ar u)v,v)$, its vertical complex Hessian is $|w|_ h^2$, and its vertical first derivative in the direction $w$ is $h(w,v)$. Apply \[  \partial  ar\partial (G^{-1}) =2G^{-3}\partial G\wedge  ar\partial G-G^{-2}\partial  ar\partial G.  \] The vertical block equals $G^{-1}>0$ at $w=v$ and equals $-|w|_ h^2/G^2$ when $w\perp _ h v$. These two subspaces are orthogonal for the vertical block, which proves the statement about its eigenvalues. $\square$ Theorem 4.6.42 . Let $s$ be an integer with $0\leq s\leq n$. Suppose that for every $x\in X$ and every $0
e v\in E_ x$, the coefficient form of $\alpha _{h,v}$ has at least $s$ positive eigenvalues. Then $U_ E$ is $(n+r-s)$-convex. Proof. By lemma 4.6.41 , the horizontal block of $\mathcal L_ho $ has at least $s$ positive eigenvalues and the vertical block has one. Their direct sum thus has at least $s+1$ positive eigenvalues at every point of $E^	imes $. Choose $\epsilon >0$ and a smooth function $\chi :[0,+\infty )	o [0,1]$ equal to one on $[0,\epsilon ]$ and to zero on $[2\epsilon ,+\infty )$. Define \[  \psi ([1:v])= rac{\chi (G(v))}{G(v)}\quad (v
e 0),  \] and extend $\psi $ by zero on the divisor at infinity $\mathbb P(E)$. This extension is smooth. Indeed, near a point $[0:v]$ with $v
e 0$, use a local representative $[u:v]$ in a projective chart. On its intersection with the affine chart, $G(v/u)=h(v,v)/|u|^2$ tends to infinity as $u	o 0$, so $\chi (G)$ vanishes in a neighborhood of the point. The function $\psi $ tends to infinity near the removed zero section. Since the ambient projective bundle is compact, every sublevel set of $\psi $ is compact in $U_ E$: it is closed there and cannot accumulate on the removed section. Put $D=\{ G<\epsilon \} \subset E$, including the zero section, and $K=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_ X\oplus E)\setminus D$. Then $K$ is a compact subset of $U_ E$, and $\psi =ho $ on $U_ E\setminus K$. Thus the exhaustion $\psi $ has at least $s+1$ positive Levi eigenvalues outside a compact set. In dimension $n+r$, this is $(n+r-s)$-convexity. $\square$ Taking $s=0$ gives $(n+r)$-convexity for every bundle. For $s=1$, the curvature hypothesis is precisely RC-positivity of the metric, as in definition 4.11.1 . A positive definite mean curvature provides such a direction by taking a trace. To apply this to stable bundles, we extend the degree of line bundles of section 4.6 to vector bundles through their determinants. Definition 4.6.43 . For a Gauduchon form $\omega $ on $X$, define \[  \deg _\omega E=\deg _{\omega ^{n-1}}\det E =\int _ X rac{\mathrm i\operatorname {tr}F_ h}{2\pi }\wedge \omega ^{n-1}, \qquad \mu _\omega (E)= rac{\deg _\omega E}{r}.  \] For a nonzero torsion-free coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$, use the determinant line bundle $\det \mathcal F=( igwedge ^{\operatorname {rank}\mathcal F}\mathcal F)^{**}$ to define its degree and slope. The bundle $E$ is $\omega $-slope-stable if $\mu _\omega (\mathcal F)<\mu _\omega (E)$ for every coherent subsheaf $\mathcal F\subset E$ with $0<\operatorname {rank}\mathcal F<r$ and torsion-free quotient. If $\det h'=\mathrm e^ f\det h$, the two curvature representatives differ by $-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$, whose integral against $\omega ^{n-1}$ vanishes by lemma 2.1.1 . Thus the degree depends only on the Bott–Chern class $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(E)$ of the closed form $\mathrm i\operatorname {tr}F_ h/(2\pi )$, and it is the pairing of this class with $\omega ^{n-1}$. The Hopf example in example 4.6.55 shows that the de Rham first Chern class of $E$ does not determine the degree. Corollary 4.6.44 . If $K_{\omega ,h}$ is positive definite for a Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$, then $U_ E$ is $(n+r-1)$-convex. This holds, in particular, when $\omega $ is Gauduchon, $E$ is $\omega $-slope-stable, and $\deg _\omega E>0$. Proof. For $v
e 0$, the trace of $\alpha _{h,v}$ with respect to $\omega $ is $h(K_{\omega ,h}v,v)>0$, and a Hermitian form with positive trace has a positive eigenvalue. Apply theorem 4.6.42 with $s=1$. Under the Gauduchon and stability hypotheses, the classical existence theorem for Hermitian–Einstein metrics on stable bundles gives a metric $h$ with $K_{\omega ,h}=\lambda \operatorname {Id}_ E$, where $\lambda $ is a constant. Taking the trace and integrating the contraction identity gives \[  r\lambda \int _ X\omega ^ n =n\int _ X\operatorname {tr}(\mathrm iF_ h)\wedge \omega ^{n-1} =2\pi n\deg _\omega E>0.  \] Here $\operatorname {tr}F_ h= ar\partial \partial \log \det M$, so $\mathrm i\operatorname {tr}F_ h/(2\pi )$ represents $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(E)$. Thus $\lambda >0$, and the first assertion applies. $\square$ Corollary 4.6.45 . For every $e\geq 0$, there is a stable ample rank-two bundle $E$ on $X=\mathbb F_ e$ as in corollary 4.6.40 for which $U_ E$ is $3$-convex but not $2$-convex. Its least smooth convexity index is three. Proof. Use the ruling section $S$ and fiber $f$ of lemma 4.6.19 , and put $H=S+(3e+1)f$ and $P=4H-f$. title: Lemma 4.6.41
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Lemma 4.6.41 . Put $G(v)=h(v,v)$ and $\rho =G^{-1}$ on $E^\times $. In a holomorphic frame that is unitary and Chern-normal at $x$, meaning that $M(x)$ is the identity and the first derivatives of $M$ vanish at $x$, the complex Hessian of $\rho $ at $(x,v)$ is \[  \mathcal L_\rho (u,w) =\frac{h(R_ h(u,\bar u)v,v)}{G^2} -\frac{|w|_ h^2}{G^2} +\frac{2|h(w,v)|^2}{G^3}, \qquad u\in T_ x^{1,0}X,\quad w\in E_ x,  \] where $(u,w)$ are the horizontal and vertical components of a tangent vector. There are no mixed horizontal–vertical terms, and the vertical block has exactly one positive and $r-1$ negative eigenvalues. Proof. Such a frame is obtained by a constant change of frame making it unitary at $x$, followed by a holomorphic change of frame, linear in the coordinates, that cancels $\partial M$. Then $F_{\alpha \bar\beta }=-\partial _\alpha \partial _{\bar\beta }M$ at $x$. The horizontal first derivatives of $G$ and its mixed horizontal–vertical second derivatives vanish. The horizontal complex Hessian of $G$ is $-h(R_ h(u,\bar u)v,v)$, its vertical complex Hessian is $|w|_ h^2$, and its vertical first derivative in the direction $w$ is $h(w,v)$. e 0),  \] and extend $\psi $ by zero on the divisor at infinity $\mathbb P(E)$. This extension is smooth. Indeed, near a point $[0:v]$ with $v

title: Definition 4.6.43
topic: Hermitian geometry, torsion, and Gauduchon duality
text: Definition 4.6.43 . For a Gauduchon form $\omega $ on $X$, define \[  \deg _\omega E=\deg _{\omega ^{n-1}}\det E =\int _ X\frac{\mathrm i\operatorname {tr}F_ h}{2\pi }\wedge \omega ^{n-1}, \qquad \mu _\omega (E)=\frac{\deg _\omega E}{r}.  \] For a nonzero torsion-free coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$, use the determinant line bundle $\det \mathcal F=(\bigwedge ^{\operatorname {rank}\mathcal F}\mathcal F)^{**}$ to define its degree and slope. title: Corollary 4.6.44

text: Corollary 4.6.44 . If $K_{\omega ,h}$ is positive definite for a Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$, then $U_ E$ is $(n+r-1)$-convex.
