title: 12.6 Continuous products, envelopes and domination
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.6 Continuous products, envelopes and domination Uniform admissible approximation allows us to define the mixed Hessian products. Their local bounds retain the derivatives of the Hermitian background; closedness of the background is not required. Proposition 12.6.1 . For continuous admissible $u_1,\ldots ,u_ k$, $1\leq k\leq m$, the current \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k) \wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] is well defined as the limit of uniform smooth admissible approximations. It is positive, local, and continuous when its potentials converge uniformly. Its local masses are bounded in terms of uniform bounds on the potentials. In particular $H_ m(u)$ is a positive Radon measure. Proof. 12.5.1 , 12.5.2 provide the smooth approximations without using any continuous Hessian product or domination input. For a smooth admissible $u$ put $\sigma =\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Since $\mathrm d\sigma =\mathrm d\omega $, the coefficients of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi \sigma ^{r-1}\wedge \omega ^{n-r})$ are sums of smooth test factors paired with powers $\sigma ^ q$, $q\leq r-1$, where $\chi $ is a fixed cutoff. The absolute-form lemma and integration by parts give the Chern–Levine–Nirenberg bound by induction on $r\leq m$: \[  \int _ K\sigma ^ r\wedge \omega ^{n-r} \leq C_{K,U,\omega }(1+\| u\| _{L^\infty (U)})^ r.  \] At the induction step write $\sigma ^ r=\omega \wedge \sigma ^{r-1} +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \sigma ^{r-1}$, integrate the second term against $\chi $, and move $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to $\chi \sigma ^{r-1}\omega ^{n-r}$. The resulting powers have degrees $r-1,r-2,r-3$, with negative powers absent, and the induction applies on nested slightly larger compact sets. Mixed masses reduce to the single potential average, by positivity of the expansion of its power. Positive mixed currents have total variation controlled by these trace masses. To prove independence, telescope the difference between two smooth mixed products whose potentials have a common uniform bound. Each term paired with a fixed smooth complementary test is \[  \int \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ a-v_ a)\wedge T\wedge \eta =\int (u_ a-v_ a)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(T\wedge \eta ),  \] where $T$ is a product of the remaining admissible factors and $\omega ^{n-m}$. The identity $\mathrm d(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)=\mathrm d\omega $ and its $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ analogue show that derivatives of $T$ introduce only fixed metric derivatives; every term has at most $k-1<m$ admissible factors. The absolute mixed-form bound and the mass estimate just proved bound the variation of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(T\wedge \eta )$ uniformly. Consequently the pairing difference is at most $C_\eta \max _ a\| u_ a-v_ a\| _\infty $. The same construction with an arbitrary complementary smooth test also defines the signed products of fewer than $m$ factors without the factor $\omega ^{n-m}$: their variation is bounded by the absolute-form lemma. These products justify the metric-derivative terms above. This proves that all approximations have the same limit and that the products are continuous in the uniform topology. Positivity passes from the smooth mixed products. Using a test supported in an open set on which two limiting potentials coincide proves locality by the same estimate on a smaller neighborhood of its support. $\square$ Write $H_ m(u)$ for the measure with every potential equal to $u$. Locality and uniform continuity of these products give comparison on a contact set. Lemma 12.6.2 . If $u\leq v$ are continuous admissible functions and the remaining $m-1$ factors are fixed continuous admissible functions, then on $\{ u=v\} $ the mixed measure with first factor $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is at most the one with first factor $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$. In particular $\mathbf1_{\{ u=v\} }H_ m(u)\leq \mathbf1_{\{ u=v\} }H_ m(v)$. Proof. Write $M(w)$ for the mixed measure with first potential $w$. Positivity and locality give, for $t>0$, \[  M(\max (v,u+t))\geq \mathbf1_{\{ v>u+t\} }M(v)+\mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }M(u).  \] The first indicators increase to $\mathbf1_{\{ v>u\} }$ as $t\downarrow 0$, and the potentials on the left converge uniformly to $v$. Integrate against nonnegative continuous tests and pass to the limit. Subtract the first restricted measure to obtain the claimed contact inequality. Replacing one factor at a time proves the pure-power claim and the analogous contact inequalities for all mixed powers. $\square$ For a continuous real obstacle $h$, define $P(h)$ to be the supremum of continuous admissible functions bounded above by $h$. Constants make the family nonempty. The penalty construction also proves that this supremum is continuous and its Hessian measure lies on the contact set. Lemma 12.6.3 . The function $P(h)$ is continuous and admissible, and $H_ m(P(h))$ is supported on $\{ P(h)=h\} $. Moreover $\| P(h_1)-P(h_2)\| _\infty \leq \| h_1-h_2\| _\infty $. Proof. For smooth $h$, use the penalty solutions $w_ N$ in 12.5.2 . Its maximum argument applies to every continuous admissible competitor $v\leq h$, with an error depending on $h$ and $N$, and not on $v$. Taking their supremum gives \[  P(h)-E_ N-2M_ N/N\leq w_ N\leq P(h),  \] where the error tends to zero. Thus $P(h)$ is their uniform limit and is continuous and admissible. On every compact subset of $\{ P(h)<h\} $ the penalty densities $b e^{N(w_ N-h)}$ tend uniformly to zero. Product continuity implies the contact support assertion. Adding constants to competitors gives the stated Lipschitz bound. Approximate a continuous $h$ uniformly by smooth obstacles. Their envelopes converge uniformly to $P(h)$, proving continuity and admissibility. Any compact subset of $\{ P(h)<h\} $ also lies outside the contact sets of all sufficiently close smooth obstacles; product continuity gives the support assertion for $h$. $\square$ The obstacle also bounds discontinuous competitors. Their upper-test admissibility suffices for the penalty estimate, so allowing them does not change the continuous envelope of a smooth obstacle. Proposition 12.6.4 . For every smooth real obstacle $h$, the envelope $P(h)$ equals the pointwise supremum of all bounded admissible functions below $h$. Proof. The solutions $w_ N$ of 12.5.4 are continuous admissible competitors, so $w_ N\leq P(h)$. For each bounded admissible $u\leq h$, the same lemma gives \[  u\leq w_ N+E_ N+2M_ N/N\leq P(h)+E_ N+2M_ N/N.  \] Let $N\to \infty $ for this fixed obstacle and fixed $b$. Thus $P(h)$ dominates every bounded competitor. Since $P(h)$ itself is a bounded competitor, it equals their supremum. $\square$ The trace test in ( 12.1 ) gives $L_\omega u\geq -n$, where $L_\omega u=n\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge \omega ^{n-1}/\omega ^ n$. We use the classical normalized Green estimate 12.3 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-normalized-l1} \int _ X(\sup _ Xu-u)\omega ^ n\leq C_\omega \end{equation} for continuous admissible $u$. The stationary probability of $L_\omega $ has a smooth positive density equivalent to $\omega ^ n$. The positive measure $L_\omega u+n$ has stationary mass $n$, so the Green-kernel estimate gives this bound. It is a linear elliptic input, and does not assert compactness for a nonlinear Hessian measure. To use envelopes in domination, we must first exclude a potential with zero total Hessian mass. Lemma 12.6.5 . Every continuous admissible $u$ satisfies $\int _ X H_ m(u)>0$. Proof. Suppose this integral is zero. For $s>0$ put $w=\max (u,\min _ Xu+s)$ and $U=\{ u<\min _ Xu+s\} $. The open set $U$ is nonempty, $0\leq w-u\leq s$, and $w=u$ outside it. Set $\sigma _ u=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$, $\sigma _ w=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$, and $\mu _ q=\sigma _ u^ q\wedge \sigma _ w^{m-q}\wedge \omega ^{n-m}$. The contact lemma gives $\mathbf1_{X\setminus U}\mu _ q\geq \mathbf1_{X\setminus U}\mu _ m$, for $0\leq q\leq m$. For $q<m$ the telescoping identity is \[  \mu _ q-\mu _ m=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w-u)\wedge T_ q,\qquad T_ q=\sigma _ u^ q\wedge \sum _{r=0}^{m-q-1}\sigma _ w^ r\wedge \sigma _ u^{m-q-1-r} \wedge \omega ^{n-m}.  \] Integration by parts on $X$ therefore gives \[  \int _ U(\mu _ q-\mu _ m)\leq \int _ X(\mu _ q-\mu _ m) =\int _ X(w-u)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q.  \] This identity follows first for smooth approximants and then by uniform product continuity. The derivatives of $T_ q$ contain only fixed metric derivatives and products of at most $m-1$ admissible factors, so the absolute-form lemma makes $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q$ a measure of uniformly controlled variation. Uniform convergence also justifies its continuous weight. On $U$, locality gives $\sigma _ w=\omega $ and thus \[  |\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q|\leq C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mu _ r.  \] The constant depends only on the metric and $m,n$, and not on $u$ or $s$. Consequently \[  \sum _{q=0}^ m\int _ U\mu _ q \leq (m+1)\int _ U H_ m(u)+Cms\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r.  \] For sufficiently small $s$, absorption and $H_ m(u)=0$ force all these nonnegative integrals to vanish. But $\mu _0=\omega ^ n$ on the nonempty open set $U$, a contradiction. $\square$ The envelope of a stretched difference now converts vanishing of a restricted measure into an order relation. The linear bound ( 12.3 ) prevents these envelopes from tending to $-\infty $ on an open set. Proposition 12.6.6 . If continuous admissible $u,v$ satisfy $\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(u)=0$, then $u\geq v$. Proof. Replace $v$ by $\max (u,v)$, so $u\leq v$. For $b>1$ put $p_ b=P(bu-(b-1)v)$ and $z_ b=b^{-1}p_ b+(1-b^{-1})v\leq u$. On the contact set $C_ b=\{ p_ b=bu-(b-1)v\} $ one has $z_ b=u$; the contact inequality and polarized positivity give \[  \mathbf1_{C_ b}b^{-m}H_ m(p_ b) \leq \mathbf1_{C_ b}H_ m(z_ b) \leq \mathbf1_{C_ b}H_ m(u).  \] The envelope measure is supported on $C_ b$ and has positive mass. It vanishes on $C_ b\cap \{ u<v\} $ by the hypothesis, so some point of $C_ b\cap \{ u=v\} $ exists. Hence $\sup _ Xp_ b\geq \inf _ Xv$, while $p_ b\leq u$. The estimate ( 12.3 ) is consequently uniform for $p_ b$. On the open set $E_ a=\{ u<v-a\} $, for $a>0$, one has $p_ b\leq v-ba$, and therefore \[  C_\omega \geq \int _ X(\sup _ Xp_ b-p_ b)\omega ^ n \geq (ba-\operatorname {osc}_ Xv)\int _{E_ a}\omega ^ n.  \] Letting $b\to \infty $ gives zero volume for $E_ a$. Since it is open it is empty, and $a\downarrow 0$ gives $u\geq v$. $\square$ Proposition 12.6.7 . If continuous admissible $u,v$ satisfy \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(u)\leq c\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(v),\qquad 0\leq c<1,  \] then $u\geq v$. Proof. Choose $b>1$ so that $(1-b^{-1})^ m>c$, and put $p=P(bu-(b-1)v)$ and $z=b^{-1}p+(1-b^{-1})v\leq u$. On $C=\{ p=bu-(b-1)v\} $ the contact comparison gives \[  \mathbf1_ C\bigl (b^{-m}H_ m(p)+(1-b^{-1})^ mH_ m(v)\bigr ) \leq \mathbf1_ C H_ m(u).  \] Restricting to $\{ u<v\} $ and using the hypothesis shows that $H_ m(p)$ vanishes on $C\cap \{ u<v\} $. Its support lies in $C$, where $p<v$ is equivalent to $u<v$. Thus $H_ m(p)$ vanishes on $\{ p<v\} $. The preceding domination proposition gives $p\geq v$. Since $p\leq bu-(b-1)v$, it follows that $u\geq v$. $\square$ Strict domination yields the comparison needed for the proper equations. Lemma 12.6.8 . For continuous admissible $u,v$ and $a>0$, if \[  e^{-av}H_ m(v)\geq e^{-au}H_ m(u),  \] then $u\geq v$. Proof. Fix $\delta >0$. On $\{ u<v-\delta \} $, the assumed inequality gives \[  H_ m(u)\leq e^{a(u-v)}H_ m(v) \leq e^{-a\delta }H_ m(v-\delta ).  \] The constant $e^{-a\delta }$ is strictly smaller than one, so 12.6.7 applied to $u$ and $v-\delta $ gives $u\geq v-\delta $. Letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.6.1
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.6.1 . For continuous admissible $u_1,\ldots ,u_ k$, $1\leq k\leq m$, the current \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k) \wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] is well defined as the limit of uniform smooth admissible approximations. Each term paired with a fixed smooth complementary test is \[  \int \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ a-v_ a)\wedge T\wedge \eta =\int (u_ a-v_ a)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(T\wedge \eta ),  \] where $T$ is a product of the remaining admissible factors and $\omega ^{n-m}$. These products justify the metric-derivative terms above. This proves that all approximations have the same limit and that the products are continuous in the uniform topology. Positivity passes from the smooth mixed products. Using a test supported in an open set on which two limiting potentials coincide proves locality by the same estimate on a smaller neighborhood of its support. $\square$

text: Lemma 12.6.3 . The function $P(h)$ is continuous and admissible, and $H_ m(P(h))$ is supported on $\{ P(h)=h\} $. Moreover $\| P(h_1)-P(h_2)\| _\infty \leq \| h_1-h_2\| _\infty $. Proof. For smooth $h$, use the penalty solutions $w_ N$ in 12.5.2 . Its maximum argument applies to every continuous admissible competitor $v\leq h$, with an error depending on $h$ and $N$, and not on $v$. Taking their supremum gives \[  P(h)-E_ N-2M_ N/N\leq w_ N\leq P(h),  \] where the error tends to zero. Thus $P(h)$ is their uniform limit and is continuous and admissible. text: Proposition 12.6.4 . For every smooth real obstacle $h$, the envelope $P(h)$ equals the pointwise supremum of all bounded admissible functions below $h$. Proof. The solutions $w_ N$ of 12.5.4 are continuous admissible competitors, so $w_ N\leq P(h)$. title: Lemma 12.6.5
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.6.5 . Every continuous admissible $u$ satisfies $\int _ X H_ m(u)>0$. Proof. Suppose this integral is zero. For $s>0$ put $w=\max (u,\min _ Xu+s)$ and $U=\{ u<\min _ Xu+s\} $. The open set $U$ is nonempty, $0\leq w-u\leq s$, and $w=u$ outside it. Set $\sigma _ u=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$, $\sigma _ w=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$, and $\mu _ q=\sigma _ u^ q\wedge \sigma _ w^{m-q}\wedge \omega ^{n-m}$. The contact lemma gives $\mathbf1_{X\setminus U}\mu _ q\geq \mathbf1_{X\setminus U}\mu _ m$, for $0\leq q\leq m$. For $q<m$ the telescoping identity is \[  \mu _ q-\mu _ m=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w-u)\wedge T_ q,\qquad T_ q=\sigma _ u^ q\wedge \sum _{r=0}^{m-q-1}\sigma _ w^ r\wedge \sigma _ u^{m-q-1-r} \wedge \omega ^{n-m}.  \] Integration by parts on $X$ therefore gives \[  \int _ U(\mu _ q-\mu _ m)\leq \int _ X(\mu _ q-\mu _ m) =\int _ X(w-u)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q.  \] This identity follows first for smooth approximants and then by uniform product continuity. The derivatives of $T_ q$ contain only fixed metric derivatives and products of at most $m-1$ admissible factors, so the absolute-form lemma makes $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q$ a measure of uniformly controlled variation. Uniform convergence also justifies its continuous weight. On $U$, locality gives $\sigma _ w=\omega $ and thus \[  |\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q|\leq C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mu _ r.  \] The constant depends only on the metric and $m,n$, and not on $u$ or $s$. Consequently \[  \sum _{q=0}^ m\int _ U\mu _ q \leq (m+1)\int _ U H_ m(u)+Cms\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r.  \] For sufficiently small $s$, absorption and $H_ m(u)=0$ force all these nonnegative integrals to vanish. But $\mu _0=\omega ^ n$ on the nonempty open set $U$, a contradiction. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.6.6
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.6.6 . If continuous admissible $u,v$ satisfy $\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(u)=0$, then $u\geq v$. Proof. Replace $v$ by $\max (u,v)$, so $u\leq v$. For $b>1$ put $p_ b=P(bu-(b-1)v)$ and $z_ b=b^{-1}p_ b+(1-b^{-1})v\leq u$. On the contact set $C_ b=\{ p_ b=bu-(b-1)v\} $ one has $z_ b=u$; the contact inequality and polarized positivity give \[  \mathbf1_{C_ b}b^{-m}H_ m(p_ b) \leq \mathbf1_{C_ b}H_ m(z_ b) \leq \mathbf1_{C_ b}H_ m(u).  \] The envelope measure is supported on $C_ b$ and has positive mass. It vanishes on $C_ b\cap \{ u<v\} $ by the hypothesis, so some point of $C_ b\cap \{ u=v\} $ exists. Hence $\sup _ Xp_ b\geq \inf _ Xv$, while $p_ b\leq u$. The estimate ( 12.3 ) is consequently uniform for $p_ b$. On the open set $E_ a=\{ u<v-a\} $, for $a>0$, one has $p_ b\leq v-ba$, and therefore \[  C_\omega \geq \int _ X(\sup _ Xp_ b-p_ b)\omega ^ n \geq (ba-\operatorname {osc}_ Xv)\int _{E_ a}\omega ^ n.  \] Letting $b\to \infty $ gives zero volume for $E_ a$. Since it is open it is empty, and $a\downarrow 0$ gives $u\geq v$. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.6.7
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.6.7 . If continuous admissible $u,v$ satisfy \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(u)\leq c\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(v),\qquad 0\leq c<1,  \] then $u\geq v$. Proof. Choose $b>1$ so that $(1-b^{-1})^ m>c$, and put $p=P(bu-(b-1)v)$ and $z=b^{-1}p+(1-b^{-1})v\leq u$. On $C=\{ p=bu-(b-1)v\} $ the contact comparison gives \[  \mathbf1_ C\bigl (b^{-m}H_ m(p)+(1-b^{-1})^ mH_ m(v)\bigr ) \leq \mathbf1_ C H_ m(u).  \] Restricting to $\{ u<v\} $ and using the hypothesis shows that $H_ m(p)$ vanishes on $C\cap \{ u<v\} $. Its support lies in $C$, where $p<v$ is equivalent to $u<v$. Thus $H_ m(p)$ vanishes on $\{ p<v\} $. The preceding domination proposition gives $p\geq v$. Since $p\leq bu-(b-1)v$, it follows that $u\geq v$. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.6.8
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.6.8 . For continuous admissible $u,v$ and $a>0$, if \[  e^{-av}H_ m(v)\geq e^{-au}H_ m(u),  \] then $u\geq v$. Proof. Fix $\delta >0$. On $\{ u<v-\delta \} $, the assumed inequality gives \[  H_ m(u)\leq e^{a(u-v)}H_ m(v) \leq e^{-a\delta }H_ m(v-\delta ).  \] The constant $e^{-a\delta }$ is strictly smaller than one, so 12.6.7 applied to $u$ and $v-\delta $ gives $u\geq v-\delta $. Letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ proves the assertion. $\square$

title: 12.7 Continuous equations and regularity
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.7 Continuous equations and regularity The proper equation is stable in the uniform norm, so its smooth solutions extend to continuous data. This also identifies the limit of the auxiliary equations with a prescribed continuous weak solution. Proposition 12.7.1 . Let $a>0$ and let smooth $H_ j$ converge uniformly to a continuous $H$. The smooth solutions of $H_ m(w_ j)=e^{aw_ j+H_ j}\omega ^ n$ converge uniformly to the unique continuous admissible solution of $H_ m(w)=e^{aw+H}\omega ^ n$. For two continuous data $H_1,H_2$, the corresponding solutions satisfy \[  \| w_1-w_2\| _\infty \leq a^{-1}\| H_1-H_2\| _\infty .  \] They also satisfy $-\max _ XH/a\leq w\leq -\min _ XH/a$. Proof. Smooth solutions exist by 12.5.1 . At a maximum of $w_1-w_2$, monotonicity of the smooth Hessian operator gives $e^{aw_1+H_1}\leq e^{aw_2+H_2}$. Hence $a(w_1-w_2)\leq H_2-H_1$ there. Exchanging the functions gives the stated norm estimate for smooth data. Thus a uniformly convergent sequence of smooth data gives a uniformly Cauchy sequence of solutions. Its limit is admissible by the linear distributional inequalities, and 12.6.1 passes the equation to the limit. The bounds follow from those for the smooth solutions. Taking limits in the smooth norm estimate proves it for continuous data. Finally, 12.6.8 in both directions gives uniqueness among continuous admissible solutions. $\square$ For smooth positive densities depending on the potential, the estimate of section 12.3 gives complex-Hessian bounds independent of derivatives of the prescribed approximation. The elliptic extension then upgrades the continuous solution to a classical one. Theorem 12.7.2 . If $\varphi $ is continuous and admissible on $X$, $f(x,t)$ is smooth on a neighborhood of its bounded range, and \[  H_ m(\varphi )=e^{f(x,\varphi )}\omega ^ n,  \] then $\varphi $ is smooth. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $v_ j\to \varphi $ uniformly, by 12.5.2 . Their values lie in a fixed compact interval on which $f$ is smooth. Put $h(x,t)=-t+f(x,t)$ and solve \[  H_ m(u_ j)=e^{u_ j+h(x,v_ j)}\omega ^ n.  \] The preceding stability proposition shows that $u_ j$ converges uniformly to a continuous admissible $u$ satisfying \[  e^{-u}H_ m(u)=e^{-\varphi +f(x,\varphi )}\omega ^ n =e^{-\varphi }H_ m(\varphi ).  \] 12.6.8 , applied in both directions, gives $u=\varphi $. The zero-order bounds for $u_ j$ are uniform. Fix $M$ bounding them and choose $B>\| \varphi \| _\infty +1$. Extend $h$ smoothly away from a neighborhood of the range of $\varphi $ to $X\times [-B-1,B+1]$; this does not change the equations for large $j$. The tolerance $\varepsilon $ in 12.3.6 depends on these bounds and on $h$, without derivatives of the smooth comparison function. Choose a fixed smooth $\widetilde\varphi $ with $\| \widetilde\varphi -\varphi \| _\infty <\varepsilon /2$ and $\| \widetilde\varphi \| _\infty \leq B$. For large $j$, $\| v_ j-\widetilde\varphi \| _\infty <\varepsilon $. 12.3.7 then gives uniform gradient and complex-Hessian bounds for $u_ j$, independent of derivatives of $v_ j$. 12.4.1 yields $\varphi \in W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p$, and $\varphi \in C^{1,\alpha }$ for every $\alpha <1$. 12.4.4 makes $\varphi $ a continuous viscosity solution of the concave uniformly elliptic extension, with right-hand side $e^{f(x,\varphi )/m}$. This right-hand side is Hölder. The analytic estimate in section 12.4 therefore gives $\varphi \in C^{2,\beta }$, for some $\beta >0$. The operator agrees with the original Hessian root on the attained compact cone set; the now classical equation thus has smooth dependence on $x,\varphi $ and its complex Hessian, and is uniformly elliptic there. Difference quotients and interior Schauder estimates give $C^{3,\beta }$; iteration proves smoothness. The estimate applies directly to the viscosity limit. $\square$ The proper equation can now be solved when its exponent depends smoothly on the unknown potential, provided that constant barriers bound the desired range and the dependence is strictly increasing. Theorem 12.7.3 . Let $A<B$ and let $f$ be smooth on a neighborhood of $X\times [A,B]$. Suppose that, for every $x\in X$, \[  f(x,A)\leq 0\leq f(x,B),\qquad 0<\kappa \leq \partial _ t f(x,t)\leq L\quad (A\leq t\leq B).  \] There is a unique continuous admissible solution with values in $[A,B]$ of \[  H_ m(w)=e^{f(x,w)}\omega ^ n.  \] This solution is smooth and strictly admissible. Proof. Choose $a\geq L$ and let $\mathcal C=\{ v\in C(X):A\leq v\leq B\} $, a complete subset of $C(X)$ in the uniform norm. For $v\in \mathcal C$ put $H_ v(x)=f(x,v(x))-av(x)$ and let $T(v)$ be the continuous proper solution with exponent $aT(v)+H_ v$, furnished by 12.7.1 . The function $f(x,t)-at$ is nonincreasing in $t$, so \[  -aB\leq f(x,B)-aB\leq H_ v(x) \leq f(x,A)-aA\leq -aA.  \] The zero-order bounds in that proposition give $A\leq T(v)\leq B$. The mean-value theorem also gives \[  \| H_ v-H_ z\| _\infty \leq (a-\kappa )\| v-z\| _\infty , \qquad \| T(v)-T(z)\| _\infty \leq (1-\kappa /a)\| v-z\| _\infty .  \] Since $0\leq 1-\kappa /a<1$, the contraction theorem gives a unique fixed point $w\in \mathcal C$. It is admissible because it equals $T(w)$, and its equation is exactly the stated equation. Every continuous admissible solution in this interval is a fixed point, by uniqueness of the continuous proper equation with its prescribed $H_ w$. This proves uniqueness in the stated class. 12.7.2 makes $w$ smooth. Its form lies in the closed $m$-cone and has positive $m$th symmetric polynomial; Maclaurin's inequalities then put it in the open cone. Thus it is strictly admissible. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.7.1
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.7.1 . Let $a>0$ and let smooth $H_ j$ converge uniformly to a continuous $H$. The smooth solutions of $H_ m(w_ j)=e^{aw_ j+H_ j}\omega ^ n$ converge uniformly to the unique continuous admissible solution of $H_ m(w)=e^{aw+H}\omega ^ n$. For two continuous data $H_1,H_2$, the corresponding solutions satisfy \[  \| w_1-w_2\| _\infty \leq a^{-1}\| H_1-H_2\| _\infty .  \] They also satisfy $-\max _ XH/a\leq w\leq -\min _ XH/a$. Proof. Smooth solutions exist by 12.5.1 . At a maximum of $w_1-w_2$, monotonicity of the smooth Hessian operator gives $e^{aw_1+H_1}\leq e^{aw_2+H_2}$. Hence $a(w_1-w_2)\leq H_2-H_1$ there. Exchanging the functions gives the stated norm estimate for smooth data. Thus a uniformly convergent sequence of smooth data gives a uniformly Cauchy sequence of solutions. Its limit is admissible by the linear distributional inequalities, and 12.6.1 passes the equation to the limit. The bounds follow from those for the smooth solutions. Taking limits in the smooth norm estimate proves it for continuous data. Finally, 12.6.8 in both directions gives uniqueness among continuous admissible solutions. $\square$

title: Theorem 12.7.2
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Theorem 12.7.2 . If $\varphi $ is continuous and admissible on $X$, $f(x,t)$ is smooth on a neighborhood of its bounded range, and \[  H_ m(\varphi )=e^{f(x,\varphi )}\omega ^ n,  \] then $\varphi $ is smooth. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $v_ j\to \varphi $ uniformly, by 12.5.2 . Their values lie in a fixed compact interval on which $f$ is smooth. Put $h(x,t)=-t+f(x,t)$ and solve \[  H_ m(u_ j)=e^{u_ j+h(x,v_ j)}\omega ^ n.  \] The preceding stability proposition shows that $u_ j$ converges uniformly to a continuous admissible $u$ satisfying \[  e^{-u}H_ m(u)=e^{-\varphi +f(x,\varphi )}\omega ^ n =e^{-\varphi }H_ m(\varphi ).  \] 12.6.8 , applied in both directions, gives $u=\varphi $. The zero-order bounds for $u_ j$ are uniform. Fix $M$ bounding them and choose $B>\| \varphi \| _\infty +1$. Extend $h$ smoothly away from a neighborhood of the range of $\varphi $ to $X\times [-B-1,B+1]$; this does not change the equations for large $j$. The tolerance $\varepsilon $ in 12.3.6 depends on these bounds and on $h$, without derivatives of the smooth comparison function. Choose a fixed smooth $\widetilde\varphi $ with $\| \widetilde\varphi -\varphi \| _\infty <\varepsilon /2$ and $\| \widetilde\varphi \| _\infty \leq B$. For large $j$, $\| v_ j-\widetilde\varphi \| _\infty <\varepsilon $. 12.3.7 then gives uniform gradient and complex-Hessian bounds for $u_ j$, independent of derivatives of $v_ j$. 12.4.1 yields $\varphi \in W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p$, and $\varphi \in C^{1,\alpha }$ for every $\alpha <1$. 12.4.4 makes $\varphi $ a continuous viscosity solution of the concave uniformly elliptic extension, with right-hand side $e^{f(x,\varphi )/m}$. This right-hand side is Hölder. The analytic estimate in section 12.4 therefore gives $\varphi \in C^{2,\beta }$, for some $\beta >0$. The operator agrees with the original Hessian root on the attained compact cone set; the now classical equation thus has smooth dependence on $x,\varphi $ and its complex Hessian, and is uniformly elliptic there. Difference quotients and interior Schauder estimates give $C^{3,\beta }$; iteration proves smoothness. The estimate applies directly to the viscosity limit. $\square$

title: 12.8 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
search_title: Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.8 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents The decreasing approximation of bounded admissible potentials supplies limits that uniform approximation cannot reach. A bounded potential can multiply a current with measure coefficients, so one can apply $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to the resulting current. Repeating this operation requires bounds on every coefficient, rather than only on the trace of a positive mixed measure. The absolute-form estimate provides these bounds below degree $m$; at degree $m$, positivity is obtained after wedging with $\omega ^{n-m}$. All bounded potentials have their canonical upper semicontinuous representatives from ( 12.2 ). Their pointwise values will be used when multiplying measure coefficients. For a real current $T$ of order zero, write $\| T\| _ K$ for the sum of the total variations of its coefficients on a compact coordinate set $K$. Fix $K\Subset U$ in a coordinate chart. Different fixed coordinate frames give equivalent local bounds. Lemma 12.8.1 . If $u$ is bounded admissible, then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ has signed Radon measure coefficients. For $K\Subset U$ contained in a coordinate chart, \[  \| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\| _ K\leq C_{K,U,\omega }(1+\| u\| _{L^\infty (X)}).  \] Proof. Choose smooth strictly admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ by 12.5.5 , and put $\sigma _ j=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. After discarding finitely many terms, $\| u_ j\| _\infty \leq \| u\| _\infty +1$. Indeed, the increasing open sets $\{ u_ j<\sup _ Xu+1\} $ cover $X$, and compactness gives a single index whose open set is all of $X$; the lower bound follows from $u_ j\geq u$. The closed $m$-cone lies in the closed $2$-cone. In an $\omega $-unitary frame, its eigenvalues satisfy \[  \sum _ i\lambda _ i^2\leq (\operatorname {tr}\sigma _ j)^2, \qquad \operatorname {tr}\sigma _ j\geq 0.  \] Thus every coefficient of $\sigma _ j$ is bounded by its trace. The degree-one Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate in 12.6.1 , applied to these smooth functions, bounds the integral of that trace on $K$ by $C(1+\| u\| _\infty )$. Subtracting the fixed smooth $\omega $ gives the same bound for the coefficient variations of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. Bounded convergence gives $u_ j\to u$ in local $L^1$, and therefore $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\to \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ in distributions. The uniform coefficient bounds show that this limit has measure coefficients with the asserted bound. $\square$ Set $D_0=1$. For an ordered list $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ of bounded admissible potentials, define recursively 12.4 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-bounded-recursion} D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p) =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\bigl (u_ pD_{p-1}(u_1,\ldots ,u_{p-1})\bigr ). \end{equation} The next result justifies the bounded multiplication at every step up to $p=m$. Proposition 12.8.2 . For $1\leq p<m$, the recursion defines a real closed current of order zero and bidegree $(p,p)$. If $M=\max _ a\| u_ a\| _{L^\infty (X)}$, then \[  \| D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)\| _ K \leq C_{K,U,\omega ,p}(1+M)^ p.  \] For $p=m$, it defines a real closed distributional current. For any smooth admissible sequences $u_ a^{j_ a}\downarrow u_ a$ with a common uniform bound, one has 12.5 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-bounded-iterated-limit} D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p) =\lim _{j_ p\to \infty }\cdots \lim _{j_1\to \infty } \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1^{j_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p^{j_ p} \end{equation} in distributions. The index $j_1$ tends to infinity first. Below degree $m$, all these limits have locally uniformly bounded coefficient variations. Proof. The case $p=1$ is the preceding lemma. Suppose the assertions hold through degree $p-1<m$. Since $u_ p$ is bounded Borel and $D_{p-1}$ has measure coefficients, their product is well defined. Applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ gives a real current that is both $\mathrm d$- and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$-closed. For a fixed smooth complementary test form $\eta $, dominated convergence against the fixed signed measures gives \[  \begin{aligned}  \langle D_ p,\eta \rangle & =\langle u_ pD_{p-1},\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta \rangle \\ & =\lim _{j_ p\to \infty } \langle u_ p^{j_ p}D_{p-1},\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta \rangle . \end{aligned}  \] With $j_ p$ fixed, the inductive iterated limit for $D_{p-1}$ can be paired with the smooth form $u_ p^{j_ p}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta $. Integration by parts for the smooth closed factors identifies the resulting pairing with the smooth product on the right of ( 12.5 ). This proves that identity also when $p=m$. For $p<m$, expand the smooth product using $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ a^{j_ a}=\sigma _ a^{j_ a}-\omega $. A term with $q$ admissible factors, $0\leq q\leq p$, has the form \[  \sigma _{a_1}^{j_{a_1}}\wedge \cdots \wedge \sigma _{a_ q}^{j_{a_ q}}\wedge \omega ^{p-q}.  \] Every such $q$ is strictly less than $m$. Apply 12.1.5 to each coefficient test, and then the smooth mass estimate from 12.6.1 to the potential sum. The term $q=0$ is the fixed smooth form $\omega ^ p$. For $q\geq 1$, the sum of its admissible forms is $q(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\bar u)$, where $\bar u$ is their average and $\| \bar u\| _\infty \leq M+1$. The result is a coefficient variation bound $C(1+M)^ p$, after choosing the approximations with norm at most $M+1$ as in the preceding proof. For arbitrary uniformly bounded approximations the same argument uses their common bound. The bounds survive each distributional limit, proving that $D_ p$ has order zero and the stated estimate. This completes the induction. No coefficient bound for the unwedged degree-$m$ current is used or asserted. $\square$ For a subset $I=\{ i_1<\cdots <i_ q\} \subset \{ 1,\ldots ,p\} $, write $D_ I=D_ q(u_{i_1},\ldots ,u_{i_ q})$, with $D_\varnothing =1$. Define the shifted current and its mixed positive current by 12.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-bounded-shifted-current} R_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p) =\sum _{I\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,p\} }\omega ^{p-|I|}\wedge D_ I, \qquad Q_ p=R_ p\wedge \omega ^{n-m}. \end{equation} Below degree $m$, $R_ p$ has measure coefficients. At degree $m$ it is initially a distributional current. Its positive wedge $Q_ m$ is nevertheless a measure. Put $M=\max _ a\| u_ a\| _{L^\infty (X)}$. Theorem 12.8.3 . For $1\leq p\leq m$, $Q_ p$ is a positive current of order zero, and \[  \int _ KQ_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq C_{K,U,\omega ,p}(1+M)^ p.  \] It is the iterated limit, in the order of ( 12.5 ), of \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1^{j_1})\wedge \cdots \wedge (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p^{j_ p})\wedge \omega ^{n-m}.  \] In particular $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure. These currents are local in the canonical potentials and independent of the chosen approximations for the fixed ordering. When all potentials are continuous, $Q_ p$ equals the continuous mixed product of 12.6.1 . Proof. Expand the smooth shifted product over its subsets. Applying ( 12.5 ) to each subset, in its inherited ordering, gives ( 12.8 ). The absent indices have no effect on a subset's limit. Each smooth product is positive: pairing with a decomposable strongly positive complementary test appends $m-p$ nonnegative rank-one $(1,1)$-forms, and polarized Gårding positivity applies. The smooth mixed mass bound is uniform in all indices. Distributional limits preserve positivity and the local trace bound at every step. Positive currents have order zero, so this gives the assertions for $Q_ p$, including the top-degree measure. The recursion uses only bounded multiplication of canonical values and local distributional differentiation. It is therefore local. Its definition contains no approximation choices, so the proved limit is independent of those choices while the ordering is fixed. For continuous potentials, the approximations converge uniformly by Dini's theorem. The telescoping estimate in 12.6.1 is uniform in all remaining indices and shows that their iterated limit is the same continuous mixed product. This also proves permutation invariance in the continuous case. $\square$ The shifted currents are not closed. Their derivatives can be stated without multiplying a discontinuous function by a distribution of positive order. This is the torsion identity needed before considering integration by parts with bounded weights. Proposition 12.8.4 . Write $R_{p-1}^{\widehat a}$ for the shifted current obtained by omitting $u_ a$, in the inherited order, and use two hats for two omissions. Put $R_0=1$. For $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm dR_ p& =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}R_ p& =\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}R_ p& =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a} +2\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a<b}R_{p-2}^{\widehat a\widehat b}. \end{aligned}  \] The last sum is absent for $p=1$. All currents on the right have order zero. If all but at most one potential are smooth, $R_ p$ is independent of the ordering and is the ordinary product of the smooth factors with $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Proof. Every $D_ I$ is both $\mathrm d$- and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$-closed. Differentiating ( 12.8 ) therefore gives \[  \mathrm dR_ p=\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _ I(p-|I|)\omega ^{p-|I|-1}\wedge D_ I,  \] with zero terms omitted. The coefficient $p-|I|$ counts the omitted indices outside $I$, which proves the first formula; the second is identical with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ in place of $\mathrm d$. Apply $\mathrm d$ to the second formula. Each pair of omitted indices occurs twice, and $-\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \mathrm d\omega =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ because both forms have odd degree three. This gives the displayed $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ formula, with every background derivative retained. If all but one potential are smooth, applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to the bounded potential times a smooth closed product gives its $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ wedged with that product. At later smooth steps, closedness again makes the recursion ordinary smooth multiplication. This is independent of the position of the bounded potential, and the subset expansion gives the last assertion. $\square$ Local capacity arguments naturally concern functions whose unshifted Hessian lies in the cone. On a coordinate ball $U$, call a bounded canonical function $f$ $m$-subharmonic relative to $\omega $ if \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f\wedge \gamma _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \gamma _{m-1} \wedge \omega ^{n-m}\geq 0  \] for all smooth $\gamma _ i\in \Gamma _ m(\omega )$. Equivalently, its local upper tests $q$ satisfy $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}$. The same Hermitian form $\omega $ is used here and in the chapter's shifted admissibility. Lemma 12.8.5 . Let $U$ be a coordinate ball compactly contained in a holomorphic chart. There is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic $\rho $ on a neighborhood of $\overline U$ such that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $ and, for every bounded admissible $u$ on $X$, $u+\rho $ is $m$-subharmonic relative to $\omega $ on $U$. Adding $\rho $ to the approximations in 12.5.5 gives uniformly bounded smooth decreasing approximations in this local class. Proof. Take $\rho =C|z|^2$ in the chart. On the fixed compact set $\overline U$, a sufficiently large $C$ gives $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $. An upper test $q$ for $u+\rho $ at $x$ gives the upper test $q-\rho $ for $u$ there. Hence \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(q-\rho ))+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho -\omega ) \in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )},  \] since the second summand is positive and the cone is preserved by adding nonnegative forms. Smooth addition preserves the canonical representative. The same identity applies pointwise to every smooth admissible approximation. Adding a fixed smooth function preserves pointwise decrease and convergence, and its bounded norm on $\overline U$ preserves the common local bound. $\square$ The correction is a local inclusion of classes. It leaves the metric in the cone tests unchanged. Although $\tau =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho $ is closed, $\tau -\omega $ has derivative $-\mathrm d\omega $, so the background terms in the preceding torsion identity remain present. In particular, $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+\rho )+(\omega -\tau )$. Comparison of the unshifted Hessians of the corrected functions must therefore account for this smooth remainder. Example 12.8.6 . On the unit ball in $\mathbb C^3$, put $\beta _ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z_ j|^2$, $\beta =\sum _{j=1}^3\beta _ j$ and \[  u=-\tfrac 12\sum _{j=1}^3|z_ j|^2, \qquad v=-\tfrac 45|z_1|^2.  \] Both $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ and $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are strictly positive, but \[  (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta > (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta , \qquad (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta <(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta .  \] Thus shifted Hessian order does not imply unshifted Hessian order, even for smooth potentials with positive perturbed forms. Proof. The eigenvalues of the two perturbed forms relative to $\beta $ are $(\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12)$ and $(\tfrac 15,1,1)$. For a diagonal form with relative eigenvalues $\lambda _1,\lambda _2, \lambda _3$, its second Hessian is $(\lambda _1\lambda _2+\lambda _1\lambda _3+\lambda _2\lambda _3)\beta ^3/3$. Consequently the shifted measures of $u,v$ are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $\tfrac 7{15}\beta ^3$, while their unshifted expressions are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $0$. Their unshifted traces are negative, so neither original function belongs to the local unshifted class. Adding $\sum _ j|z_ j|^2$ gives an exact correction in this constant closed background. An exact correction $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho =\omega $ is impossible where $\mathrm d\omega \ne 0$. $\square$ The iterated limit fixes the order of the potentials. Symmetry and simultaneous convergence require control of discontinuous weights against varying coefficient measures. The next section supplies the first-Hessian estimate for 12.9.5 ; the local Hessian capacities in section 12.10 give the control in the remaining degrees.

text: Theorem 12.8.3 . For $1\leq p\leq m$, $Q_ p$ is a positive current of order zero, and \[  \int _ KQ_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq C_{K,U,\omega ,p}(1+M)^ p.  \] It is the iterated limit, in the order of ( 12.5 ), of \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1^{j_1})\wedge \cdots \wedge (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p^{j_ p})\wedge \omega ^{n-m}.  \] In particular $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure. These currents are local in the canonical potentials and independent of the chosen approximations for the fixed ordering. When all potentials are continuous, $Q_ p$ equals the continuous mixed product of 12.6.1 . Proof. Expand the smooth shifted product over its subsets. Applying ( 12.5 ) to each subset, in its inherited ordering, gives ( 12.8 ). The absent indices have no effect on a subset's limit. Each smooth product is positive: pairing with a decomposable strongly positive complementary test appends $m-p$ nonnegative rank-one $(1,1)$-forms, and polarized Gårding positivity applies. The smooth mixed mass bound is uniform in all indices. Distributional limits preserve positivity and the local trace bound at every step. Positive currents have order zero, so this gives the assertions for $Q_ p$, including the top-degree measure. The recursion uses only bounded multiplication of canonical values and local distributional differentiation. It is therefore local. Its definition contains no approximation choices, so the proved limit is independent of those choices while the ordering is fixed. For continuous potentials, the approximations converge uniformly by Dini's theorem. The telescoping estimate in 12.6.1 is uniform in all remaining indices and shows that their iterated limit is the same continuous mixed product. This also proves permutation invariance in the continuous case. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.8.4
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.8.4 . Write $R_{p-1}^{\widehat a}$ for the shifted current obtained by omitting $u_ a$, in the inherited order, and use two hats for two omissions. Put $R_0=1$. For $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm dR_ p& =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}R_ p& =\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}R_ p& =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a} +2\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a<b}R_{p-2}^{\widehat a\widehat b}. \end{aligned}  \] The last sum is absent for $p=1$. All currents on the right have order zero. If all but at most one potential are smooth, $R_ p$ is independent of the ordering and is the ordinary product of the smooth factors with $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Proof. Every $D_ I$ is both $\mathrm d$- and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$-closed. Differentiating ( 12.8 ) therefore gives \[  \mathrm dR_ p=\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _ I(p-|I|)\omega ^{p-|I|-1}\wedge D_ I,  \] with zero terms omitted. The coefficient $p-|I|$ counts the omitted indices outside $I$, which proves the first formula; the second is identical with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ in place of $\mathrm d$. Apply $\mathrm d$ to the second formula. Each pair of omitted indices occurs twice, and $-\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \mathrm d\omega =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ because both forms have odd degree three. This gives the displayed $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ formula, with every background derivative retained. If all but one potential are smooth, applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to the bounded potential times a smooth closed product gives its $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ wedged with that product. At later smooth steps, closedness again makes the recursion ordinary smooth multiplication. This is independent of the position of the bounded potential, and the subset expansion gives the last assertion. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.8.5
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.8.5 . Let $U$ be a coordinate ball compactly contained in a holomorphic chart. There is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic $\rho $ on a neighborhood of $\overline U$ such that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $ and, for every bounded admissible $u$ on $X$, $u+\rho $ is $m$-subharmonic relative to $\omega $ on $U$. Adding $\rho $ to the approximations in 12.5.5 gives uniformly bounded smooth decreasing approximations in this local class. Proof. Take $\rho =C|z|^2$ in the chart. On the fixed compact set $\overline U$, a sufficiently large $C$ gives $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $. An upper test $q$ for $u+\rho $ at $x$ gives the upper test $q-\rho $ for $u$ there. Hence \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(q-\rho ))+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho -\omega ) \in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )},  \] since the second summand is positive and the cone is preserved by adding nonnegative forms. Smooth addition preserves the canonical representative. The same identity applies pointwise to every smooth admissible approximation. Adding a fixed smooth function preserves pointwise decrease and convergence, and its bounded norm on $\overline U$ preserves the common local bound. $\square$

title: Example 12.8.6
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Example 12.8.6 . On the unit ball in $\mathbb C^3$, put $\beta _ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z_ j|^2$, $\beta =\sum _{j=1}^3\beta _ j$ and \[  u=-\tfrac 12\sum _{j=1}^3|z_ j|^2, \qquad v=-\tfrac 45|z_1|^2.  \] Both $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ and $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are strictly positive, but \[  (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta > (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta , \qquad (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta <(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta .  \] Thus shifted Hessian order does not imply unshifted Hessian order, even for smooth potentials with positive perturbed forms. Proof. The eigenvalues of the two perturbed forms relative to $\beta $ are $(\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12)$ and $(\tfrac 15,1,1)$. For a diagonal form with relative eigenvalues $\lambda _1,\lambda _2, \lambda _3$, its second Hessian is $(\lambda _1\lambda _2+\lambda _1\lambda _3+\lambda _2\lambda _3)\beta ^3/3$. Consequently the shifted measures of $u,v$ are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $\tfrac 7{15}\beta ^3$, while their unshifted expressions are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $0$. Their unshifted traces are negative, so neither original function belongs to the local unshifted class. Adding $\sum _ j|z_ j|^2$ gives an exact correction in this constant closed background. An exact correction $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho =\omega $ is impossible where $\mathrm d\omega \ne 0$. $\square$

12.9 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors To multiply a varying coefficient measure by a bounded potential, weak convergence of the measures is not enough. We first control the sets on which a potential can be discontinuous. The linear trace of an admissible form supplies this control through Sobolev capacity. Its Gauduchon multiplier must be chosen in the conformal class of $\omega $, since an admissible form need not be positive in every tangent direction. Choose $ho >0$ by theorem 4.1.2 and put \[  T=ho \omega ^{n-1},\qquad \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0,\qquad A=\int _ X\omega \wedge T>0.  \] Write $H^1(X)=W^{1,2}(X,\mathbb R)$ and use the equivalent Sobolev norm \[  \| f\| _{H^1}^2=\int _ Xf^2\omega ^ n+ \int _ X\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge T.  \] For an open set $G\subset X$ define \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G) =\inf \{ \| f\| _{H^1}^2:f\in H^1(X),\  f\geq 1 	ext{ almost everywhere on }G\} ,  \] and for an arbitrary set $E$ take the infimum over open $G\supset E$. Thus this capacity is defined by Sobolev energy; it is distinct from an $m$-Hessian capacity. Truncation allows $0\leq f\leq 1$ in the infimum for open sets. Lemma 12.9.1 . The capacity $\operatorname {Cap}_1$ is countably subadditive. For a smooth real $f$ and $a>0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(\{ |f|>a\} )\leq a^{-2}\| f\| _{H^1}^2.  \] If a positive Radon measure $\mu $ satisfies $|\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d\mu |\leq C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$ for every smooth real $\phi $, then for every Borel set $E$, \[  \mu (E)\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}.  \] Proof. For open $G_ i$ choose Sobolev functions $0\leq f_ i\leq 1$ equal to one almost everywhere on $G_ i$, with a summably small excess in their squared norms over the capacity infima. The Sobolev chain rule gives \[  \| \max _{i\leq N}f_ i\| _{H^1}^2\leq \sum _{i\leq N}\| f_ i\| _{H^1}^2.  \] Indeed, almost everywhere the gradient of the maximum is the gradient of an active function, and the squared value is bounded by the sum of the squared values. If the sum is finite, these maxima converge in $L^2$, are bounded in $H^1$, and have a weak $H^1$ limit equal to one almost everywhere on $ igcup _ iG_ i$. Lower semicontinuity proves subadditivity for open sets. Taking open supersets proves it for arbitrary sets. If the sum is infinite there is nothing to prove. The level-set estimate follows by testing with $\min \{ 1,|f|/a\} $ and the same Sobolev chain rule. Fix a compact $K\subset G$ and a Sobolev competitor $0\leq f\leq 1$ for the open set $G$. Positive local mollification and a partition of unity give smooth nonnegative $f_\epsilon 	o f$ in $H^1$ that satisfy $f_\epsilon \geq 1$ on $K$ for small $\epsilon $: every convolution ball meeting $K$ then lies in $G$, where $f=1$ almost everywhere. The assumed estimate gives $\mu (K)\leq C\lim _\epsilon \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}=C\| f\| _{H^1}$. Take the infimum over $f$ and then the supremum over compact $K\subset G$ to obtain the estimate for $G$. Outer regularity and open supersets give it for every Borel $E$. $\square$ Lemma 12.9.2 . Every bounded admissible $u$ belongs to $H^1(X)$. Its trace \[  \mu _ u=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)\wedge T  \] is a positive Radon measure of total mass $A$. If $\| u\| _\infty \leq M$, then \[  \| u\| _{H^1}\leq C(1+M),\qquad \mu _ u(E)\leq C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}  \] for every Borel $E$. On each fixed relatively compact coordinate chart, the total variation of every coefficient of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is also bounded on $E$ by $C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$. Proof. First let $u$ be smooth admissible. The first-cone inequality gives $\mu _ u\geq 0$, since $T$ is conformal to $\omega ^{n-1}$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0$ gives $\mu _ u(X)=A$. Applying distributional Stokes to $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u^2)$ yields the energy identity \[  \int _ X\mathrm du\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm d\mu _ u+\int _ Xu\omega \wedge T \leq 2MA.  \] Together with the $L^2$ bound this controls $\| u\| _{H^1}$. For bounded admissible $u$, choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ by 12.5.5 , discard a finite initial segment, and take $\| u_ j\| _\infty \leq M+1$ as in 12.8.1 . Bounded convergence gives strong $L^2$ convergence. The energy bound gives weak $H^1$ compactness, and every weak cluster point agrees with $u$ in $L^2$; thus the entire sequence converges weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. This proves the Sobolev bound. The trace measures converge weakly to $\mu _ u$, preserving positivity and total mass. For any smooth real $\phi $, the first-order Stokes identity is \[  \int _ X\phi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ X\mathrm d\phi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T +\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge \mathrm dT.  \] It remains valid for $u\in H^1$ by smooth Sobolev approximation. Both terms are bounded by $C\| u\| _{H^1}\| \phi \| _{H^1}$; the background term $\int \phi \omega \wedge T$ is bounded by $C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$. The preceding capacity lemma gives the bound for $\mu _ u$. In particular the derivative $\mathrm dT$ has not been discarded. For a smooth admissible approximant, write the eigenvalues of $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame as $\lambda _ i$. Since $m\geq 2$, \[  \sum _ i\lambda _ i^2\leq \left(\sum _ i\lambda _ iight)^2, \qquad \sum _ i\lambda _ i\geq 0.  \] Consequently every coefficient of this form is dominated by its trace. On a fixed coordinate chart this bounds the coefficient variations of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ by $C(\mu _{u_ j}+\omega ^ n)$. Passing to the weak measure limits of 12.8.1 gives the same domination by $C(\mu _ u+\omega ^ n)$. Finally $\int _ E\omega ^ n\leq \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)$ and $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)\leq \| 1\| _{H^1}^2$ absorb the smooth term into the claimed square-root estimate. $\square$ Lemma 12.9.3 . Every bounded canonical admissible potential is continuous on the complement of an open set of arbitrarily small $\operatorname {Cap}_1$. The same open set can be chosen for any countable family of such potentials. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$. By the preceding lemma these functions converge weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. Mazur's lemma gives finite convex combinations $w_ N$ of terms with $j\geq N$ such that \[  \| w_ N-u\| _{H^1}\leq 8^{-N}.  \] Because $u\leq w_ N\leq u_ N$, they converge pointwise to the canonical function $u$, not just to an unspecified almost-everywhere representative. Put \[  G_{N_0}= igcup _{N\geq N_0} \{ |w_{N+1}-w_ N|>2^{-N}\} .  \] The capacity tools imply \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G_{N_0}) \leq \sum _{N\geq N_0}4^ N\| w_{N+1}-w_ N\| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\sum _{N\geq N_0}16^{-N}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Outside $G_{N_0}$, the successive differences form a uniformly summable series. Thus $w_ N$ converge uniformly there and their limit $u$ is continuous on that closed set. For a countable family, choose the exceptional open sets with capacities less than $\epsilon 2^{-i}$ and take their union. Countable subadditivity proves the last assertion. $\square$ Proposition 12.9.4 . Suppose $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded canonical admissible potentials with a common uniform bound. Then \[  v_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\longrightarrow v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u  \] weakly as currents with signed measure coefficients. The same conclusion holds for $v_ j\mu _{u_ j}	o v\mu _ u$. Proof. Bounded convergence gives $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1$. Their complex Hessians therefore converge in distributions. The preceding coefficient bounds are uniform, so this is weak convergence of each signed coefficient measure against continuous compactly supported tests. The trace measures also converge weakly. Every one of these measures has total variation bounded by $C_ M\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$ on a Borel set $E$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. Quasicontinuity supplies an open $G$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_1(G)<\epsilon $ on whose complement $v$ and every $v_ j$ are continuous. Dini's theorem on the compact set $X\setminus G$ gives uniform convergence there. Extend $v|_{X\setminus G}$ to a continuous function $F$ on $X$ with the same uniform bound, by Tietze's theorem. For any one of the signed coefficient measures $
u _ j	o 
u $ and a fixed continuous compactly supported test $\psi $, subtract $F
u _ j$ and $F
u $. The resulting error is at most \[  C_{M,\psi } igl (\| v_ j-v\| _{X\setminus G} +\epsilon ^{1/2} igr ).  \] The term with $F$ converges by weak measure convergence. First let $j	o \infty $ and then $\epsilon \downarrow 0$. This proves the assertion for the Hessian coefficients and for the positive trace measures. $\square$ Theorem 12.9.5 . For two bounded admissible potentials $u,v$, the recursive current $D_2(u,v)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)$ is symmetric in its arguments. If $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded admissible sequences with a common uniform bound, then \[  D_2(u_ j,v_ j)\longrightarrow D_2(u,v)  \] in distributions. Their shifted positive currents \[  Q_2(u,v)= igl (\omega ^2+\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u +\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v+D_2(u,v) igr )\wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] converge weakly as positive currents. For $m=2$ these are positive Radon measures. For $m>2$, the unwedged $D_2$ also converges weakly as a current with measure coefficients. Proof. For smooth admissible approximations $u_ k\downarrow u$ and $v_ k\downarrow v$, the weighted convergence proposition gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)\longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u).  \] The smooth current on the left is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ and is symmetric. Applying the same argument in the opposite order proves $D_2(u,v)=D_2(v,u)$. For the bounded sequences in the statement, weighted convergence followed by $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ gives the asserted simultaneous distributional limit. The displayed subset expansion is the current of 12.8.3 with $p=2$. Its lower-degree terms converge weakly, so its whole distributional limit is $Q_2(u,v)$. Positivity and the uniform local mass bounds turn this into weak convergence of currents of order zero. When $m>2$, the same conclusion for $D_2$ follows from the uniform coefficient bounds below degree $m$ in 12.8.2 . $\square$ The capacity estimate depends on using a first Hessian. A product of two Hessians can already charge a set of zero Sobolev capacity. Lemma 12.9.6 . Let $E$ be a compact subset of a smooth real submanifold of codimension two contained in a coordinate chart. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. Proof. It suffices to treat a compact subset of a submanifold chart, since finitely many such subsets cover $E$ and the capacity is subadditive. Choose real coordinates $(s,t)$ there, with $t\in \mathbb R^2$ and the submanifold given by $t=0$. Choose $0\leq \eta \leq 1$ smooth, supported in this chart and equal to one near the compact subset. Put $r=|t|$. For $0<\epsilon <1/2$ define \[  h_\epsilon (r)=  egin{cases}  1,& 0\leq r\leq \epsilon ^2,\  \displaystyle  rac{\log (\epsilon /r)}{\log (1/\epsilon )}, & \epsilon ^2<r<\epsilon ,\  0,& r\geq \epsilon . \end{cases}  \] The Sobolev function $f_\epsilon =\eta h_\epsilon $ equals one on an open neighborhood of that subset. On the fixed compact coordinate set the Sobolev norm is equivalent to the Euclidean one. Integration in the two normal variables gives \[  \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\left(\epsilon ^2+ \int _{\epsilon ^2}^{\epsilon }  rac{\mathrm dr}{r\log (1/\epsilon )^2}ight) =C\left(\epsilon ^2+ rac1{\log (1/\epsilon )}ight) \longrightarrow 0.  \] The derivatives of $\eta $ contribute at most $C\epsilon ^2$. Taking the infimum over open neighborhoods proves the assertion. $\square$ Example 12.9.7 . There are bounded continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potentials $u,v$ and a compact Borel set $E$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0,\qquad \int _ E Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2}>0.  \] Consequently the first-Hessian capacity estimate does not extend to this positive two-factor measure, even within the continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic subclass. Proof. Choose holomorphic coordinates $z_ j=x_ j+\mathrm i y_ j$ and a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\chi $ supported in the chart and equal to one on a smaller coordinate box. Extend \[  u=a\chi |x_1|,\qquad v=a\chi |x_2|  \] by zero outside the chart. These functions are globally continuous and bounded. To check their curvature, replace $|x_ j|$ by $g_\delta (x_ j)=(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{1/2}$, with $0<\delta \leq 1$. The Hessian of $\chi g_\delta $ has the nonnegative term $\chi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta $; all its remaining terms are uniformly bounded forms, since $g_\delta $ and $g_\delta '$ are uniformly bounded on the fixed support. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi g_\delta )\geq -C\omega $ with $C$ independent of $\delta $. Choosing $a>0$ sufficiently small gives $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\chi g_\delta )\geq \omega /2$ for both coordinates. Their decreasing limits $u,v$ are therefore $\omega $-plurisubharmonic and admissible. On the box where $\chi =1$, set $\alpha _ j= rac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }\mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j$. The book's normalization gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta (x_ j)=	frac 12g_\delta ''(x_ j)\alpha _ j, \qquad g_\delta ''(x_ j) = rac{\delta ^2}{(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{3/2}} \longrightarrow 2\delta _{\{ x_ j=0\} }.  \] The measures $g_\delta ^{\prime \prime }(t)\, \mathrm dt$ have mass two, while their mass outside any fixed neighborhood of zero tends to zero. The two smooth factors depend on distinct real variables, so their product is an approximate identity in $(x_1,x_2)$ and converges to the tensor-product measure. By 12.9.5 , locally \[  D_2(u,v)=a^2\delta _{\{ x_1=0\} }\delta _{\{ x_2=0\} } \alpha _1\wedge \alpha _2.  \] Choose $E$ to be a compact piece of $\{ x_1=x_2=0\} $ inside this box with nonempty relative interior. The preceding lemma gives $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. On this box, the positive measure $D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}$ has strictly positive mass on $E$, since $\omega $ is strictly positive. The smooth term $\omega ^ n$ and the two single-Hessian terms in the expansion \[  Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2} =\omega ^ n+\omega ^{n-1}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v) +D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}  \] have zero mass on $E$: each single-Hessian term is absolutely continuous in the other normal real variable. Hence the asserted mass is strictly positive. A bound by $C\operatorname {Cap}_1(F)^ b$ for all Borel $F$, with any $b>0$, would contradict this choice of $E$. $\square$ The preceding Sobolev-capacity estimate therefore cannot be iterated to control higher-degree coefficient measures. A local Hessian capacity supplies that control in the next section.

title: Lemma 12.9.3
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.9.3 . Every bounded canonical admissible potential is continuous on the complement of an open set of arbitrarily small $\operatorname {Cap}_1$. The same open set can be chosen for any countable family of such potentials. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$. By the preceding lemma these functions converge weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. Mazur's lemma gives finite convex combinations $w_ N$ of terms with $j\geq N$ such that \[  \| w_ N-u\| _{H^1}\leq 8^{-N}.  \] Because $u\leq w_ N\leq u_ N$, they converge pointwise to the canonical function $u$, not just to an unspecified almost-everywhere representative. Put \[  G_{N_0}=\bigcup _{N\geq N_0} \{ |w_{N+1}-w_ N|>2^{-N}\} .  \] The capacity tools imply \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G_{N_0}) \leq \sum _{N\geq N_0}4^ N\| w_{N+1}-w_ N\| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\sum _{N\geq N_0}16^{-N}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Outside $G_{N_0}$, the successive differences form a uniformly summable series. Thus $w_ N$ converge uniformly there and their limit $u$ is continuous on that closed set. For a countable family, choose the exceptional open sets with capacities less than $\epsilon 2^{-i}$ and take their union. Countable subadditivity proves the last assertion. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.9.4
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text:
Proposition 12.9.4 . Suppose $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded canonical admissible potentials with a common uniform bound. Then \[  v_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\longrightarrow v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u  \] weakly as currents with signed measure coefficients. The same conclusion holds for $v_ j\mu _{u_ j}	o v\mu _ u$. Proof. Bounded convergence gives $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1$. Their complex Hessians therefore converge in distributions. The preceding coefficient bounds are uniform, so this is weak convergence of each signed coefficient measure against continuous compactly supported tests. The trace measures also converge weakly. Every one of these measures has total variation bounded by $C_ M\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$ on a Borel set $E$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. Quasicontinuity supplies an open $G$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_1(G)<\epsilon $ on whose complement $v$ and every $v_ j$ are continuous. Dini's theorem on the compact set $X\setminus G$ gives uniform convergence there. Extend $v|_{X\setminus G}$ to a continuous function $F$ on $X$ with the same uniform bound, by Tietze's theorem. For any one of the signed coefficient measures $
