First let $j	o \infty $ and then $\epsilon \downarrow 0$. This proves the assertion for the Hessian coefficients and for the positive trace measures. $\square$

title: Theorem 12.9.5
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Theorem 12.9.5 . For two bounded admissible potentials $u,v$, the recursive current $D_2(u,v)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)$ is symmetric in its arguments. If $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded admissible sequences with a common uniform bound, then \[  D_2(u_ j,v_ j)\longrightarrow D_2(u,v)  \] in distributions. Their shifted positive currents \[  Q_2(u,v)=\bigl (\omega ^2+\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u +\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v+D_2(u,v)\bigr )\wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] converge weakly as positive currents. For $m=2$ these are positive Radon measures. For $m>2$, the unwedged $D_2$ also converges weakly as a current with measure coefficients. Proof. For smooth admissible approximations $u_ k\downarrow u$ and $v_ k\downarrow v$, the weighted convergence proposition gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)\longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u).  \] The smooth current on the left is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ and is symmetric. Applying the same argument in the opposite order proves $D_2(u,v)=D_2(v,u)$. For the bounded sequences in the statement, weighted convergence followed by $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ gives the asserted simultaneous distributional limit. The displayed subset expansion is the current of 12.8.3 with $p=2$. Its lower-degree terms converge weakly, so its whole distributional limit is $Q_2(u,v)$. Positivity and the uniform local mass bounds turn this into weak convergence of currents of order zero. When $m>2$, the same conclusion for $D_2$ follows from the uniform coefficient bounds below degree $m$ in 12.8.2 . $\square$

title: Lemma 12.9.6
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.9.6 . Let $E$ be a compact subset of a smooth real submanifold of codimension two contained in a coordinate chart. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. Proof. It suffices to treat a compact subset of a submanifold chart, since finitely many such subsets cover $E$ and the capacity is subadditive. Choose real coordinates $(s,t)$ there, with $t\in \mathbb R^2$ and the submanifold given by $t=0$. Choose $0\leq \eta \leq 1$ smooth, supported in this chart and equal to one near the compact subset. Put $r=|t|$. For $0<\epsilon <1/2$ define \[  h_\epsilon (r)= \begin{cases}  1,& 0\leq r\leq \epsilon ^2,\\  \displaystyle \frac{\log (\epsilon /r)}{\log (1/\epsilon )}, & \epsilon ^2<r<\epsilon ,\\  0,& r\geq \epsilon . \end{cases}  \] The Sobolev function $f_\epsilon =\eta h_\epsilon $ equals one on an open neighborhood of that subset. On the fixed compact coordinate set the Sobolev norm is equivalent to the Euclidean one. Integration in the two normal variables gives \[  \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\left(\epsilon ^2+ \int _{\epsilon ^2}^{\epsilon } \frac{\mathrm dr}{r\log (1/\epsilon )^2}\right) =C\left(\epsilon ^2+\frac1{\log (1/\epsilon )}\right) \longrightarrow 0.  \] The derivatives of $\eta $ contribute at most $C\epsilon ^2$. Taking the infimum over open neighborhoods proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Example 12.9.7
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Example 12.9.7 . There are bounded continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potentials $u,v$ and a compact Borel set $E$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0,\qquad \int _ E Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2}>0.  \] Consequently the first-Hessian capacity estimate does not extend to this positive two-factor measure, even within the continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic subclass. Proof. Choose holomorphic coordinates $z_ j=x_ j+\mathrm i y_ j$ and a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\chi $ supported in the chart and equal to one on a smaller coordinate box. Extend \[  u=a\chi |x_1|,\qquad v=a\chi |x_2|  \] by zero outside the chart. These functions are globally continuous and bounded. To check their curvature, replace $|x_ j|$ by $g_\delta (x_ j)=(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{1/2}$, with $0<\delta \leq 1$. The Hessian of $\chi g_\delta $ has the nonnegative term $\chi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta $; all its remaining terms are uniformly bounded forms, since $g_\delta $ and $g_\delta '$ are uniformly bounded on the fixed support. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi g_\delta )\geq -C\omega $ with $C$ independent of $\delta $. Choosing $a>0$ sufficiently small gives $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\chi g_\delta )\geq \omega /2$ for both coordinates. Their decreasing limits $u,v$ are therefore $\omega $-plurisubharmonic and admissible. On the box where $\chi =1$, set $\alpha _ j=\frac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }\mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d\bar z_ j$. The book's normalization gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta (x_ j)=\tfrac 12g_\delta ''(x_ j)\alpha _ j, \qquad g_\delta ''(x_ j) =\frac{\delta ^2}{(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{3/2}} \longrightarrow 2\delta _{\{ x_ j=0\} }.  \] The measures $g_\delta ^{\prime \prime }(t)\, \mathrm dt$ have mass two, while their mass outside any fixed neighborhood of zero tends to zero. The two smooth factors depend on distinct real variables, so their product is an approximate identity in $(x_1,x_2)$ and converges to the tensor-product measure. By 12.9.5 , locally \[  D_2(u,v)=a^2\delta _{\{ x_1=0\} }\delta _{\{ x_2=0\} } \alpha _1\wedge \alpha _2.  \] Choose $E$ to be a compact piece of $\{ x_1=x_2=0\} $ inside this box with nonempty relative interior. The preceding lemma gives $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. On this box, the positive measure $D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}$ has strictly positive mass on $E$, since $\omega $ is strictly positive. The smooth term $\omega ^ n$ and the two single-Hessian terms in the expansion \[  Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2} =\omega ^ n+\omega ^{n-1}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v) +D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}  \] have zero mass on $E$: each single-Hessian term is absolutely continuous in the other normal real variable. Hence the asserted mass is strictly positive. A bound by $C\operatorname {Cap}_1(F)^ b$ for all Borel $F$, with any $b>0$, would contradict this choice of $E$. $\square$

title: 12.10 Local capacities and decreasing products
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text:
12.10 Local capacities and decreasing products The codimension-two example shows why Sobolev capacity cannot control a product of Hessians. Local capacities built from smooth Hessian measures give the stronger control needed for the recursive currents. Their quasicontinuity estimate comes from an energy variation in which the derivatives of the background remain present. Work on a coordinate ball $U$ with compact closure in a holomorphic chart, with the restriction of $\omega $. For a smooth function in the local unshifted class of 12.8.5 , put \[  \Lambda _ s(f)=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ s\wedge \omega ^{n-s},\qquad 0\leq s\leq m,  \] where $\Lambda _0(f)=\omega ^ n$. The local mass and gradient estimates needed for the capacity use ordinary smooth products. Lemma 12.10.1 . Fix $K\Subset U$ and $M<\infty $. For smooth local $m$-subharmonic $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with $|f_ i|\leq M$, $0\leq q\leq m$, their mixed trace has mass at most a constant depending only on $K,U,\omega ,m,M$. If also $f$ is smooth in this class and $|f|\leq M$, then, for $q\leq m-1$, \[  \int _ K\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \omega ^{n-q-1}\leq C.  \] Proof. For one potential and a nonnegative compactly supported cutoff $\chi $, closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$ gives \[  \int \chi (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ q\omega ^{n-q} =\int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^{q-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi \omega ^{n-q}).  \] For $q\geq 1$, the absolute-form estimate 12.1.5 applies at degree $q-1<m$. Nested cutoffs and induction, starting with volume, therefore bound the left side by $C M^ q$; replacing $M$ by $1+M$ includes $M=0$. For mixed factors, positivity of every term in the expansion of $(\sum _ i\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i)^ q\omega ^{n-q}$ bounds the mixed trace by a fixed multiple of the single trace for $\sum _ i f_ i$. This proves the first assertion, including its degree-zero convention. Replace $f$ by $f+M$, so that $0\leq f\leq 2M$ without changing its gradient or Hessian. The identity \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(f^2)=2f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f+2\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f  \] also shows that $f^2$ belongs to the local cone. Wedge with the remaining $q$ Hessians and $\omega ^{n-q-1}$. The first term on the right is nonnegative, and the mixed mass estimate applied to $f^2$ and the other potentials bounds the second term. The degree used is $q+1\leq m$. A cutoff equal to one on $K$ gives the stated local estimate. $\square$ Definition 12.10.2 . For Borel $E\subset U$ define the smooth capacity \[  c_ s(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E \Lambda _ s(a): a\in C^\infty (U),\  -1\leq a\leq 0, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}ight\} ,  \] for $0\leq s\leq m$. Its outer-open version is \[  c_ s^*(E)=\inf \{ c_ s(G):E\subset G\subset U,\  G	ext{ open}\} .  \] A function on a compact $K\Subset U$ is quasicontinuous for this capacity if, for every $\epsilon >0$, it is continuous on $K\setminus G$ for some open $G\subset U$ with $c_ s(G)<\epsilon $. In particular $c_0(E)=\int _ E\omega ^ n$. Each $c_ s$ is monotone, countably subadditive and continuous under increasing unions. For the last assertion, the supremum over competitors commutes with the increasing supremum over sets. Local smooth mass bounds make it finite on compact subsets. The outer capacity $c_ s^*$ is monotone and countably subadditive and agrees with $c_ s$ on open sets. The capacities control mixed traces for smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with a common bound. Choose a fixed smooth strictly plurisubharmonic $b$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\geq \omega $ on $U$. For $q\leq s$, choose constants $B$ and $L\geq 1$ so that $(f_1+\cdots +f_ q+b-B)/L$ lies in $[-1,0]$. Both constants depend only on the common bound and the fixed data. Positivity of the smooth binomial expansion gives 12.15  egin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:smooth-capacity-bound} (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1+\cdots +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q)^ q\omega ^{n-q} \leq C \Lambda _ s igl ((	extstyle \sum _ i f_ i+b-B)/L igr ). \end{equation} For $q=0$ the left side is $\omega ^ n$; the same argument applies. Indeed, replacing any of the $s-q$ factors $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b$ by $\omega $ subtracts a nonnegative mixed trace. Thus every such mixed trace, and every coefficient of a smooth product of $q<m$ Hessians, is dominated on Borel sets by $C c_ s$. The latter assertion follows from the absolute mixed-form estimate. Lemma 12.10.3 . Let $0\leq q\leq m-1$ and let $S$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form in $\overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}$ pointwise. Put $T=S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$. For smooth real $f$ and nonnegative Borel weights $a$, supported on a fixed compact set, \[  \left|\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge Tight| \leq C\left(\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega \wedge Tight)^{1/2} \left(\int a\, \omega ^2\wedge Tight)^{1/2}.  \] The corresponding inequality with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm d\omega $ holds as well. For a mixed product of $q$ cone forms in place of $S^ q$, it suffices to sum these bounds over the finitely many subset sums of its factors. Proof. For $q\leq m-2$, diagonalize $S$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame. Every diagonal coefficient of $S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$ is a positive multiple of $S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ for two omitted coordinates. This is nonnegative by deleted-coordinate positivity, because $q+2\leq m$. The form is a nonnegative sum of simple positive coordinate forms. For one such simple form, only the remaining complex two-plane contributes to a complementary wedge. The coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ are uniformly bounded in unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Its wedge with $\mathrm df$ is consequently bounded by a constant times the gradient norm on that plane. The wedges with $\omega ^2$ and with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega $ give, up to fixed positive constants, one and the square of that norm. Pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz over the simple summands, followed by integral Cauchy–Schwarz with weight $a$, proves the estimate. Conjugation gives the other estimate. For $q=m-1$, at one point choose an $\omega $-unitary coframe $e_ i$ that diagonalizes $S$. Put $\epsilon _ i=\mathrm i e_ i\wedge  ar e_ i$ and $\Omega =\epsilon _1\cdots \epsilon _ n$, so that $\omega =\sum _ i\epsilon _ i$ and $S=\sum _ i\lambda _ i\epsilon _ i$. Writing $B_{ij}=S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ and $D_ i=S_{q;i}(\lambda )$, ordinary wedge expansion gives \[  S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2} =q!(n-q-2)!\sum _{i<j}B_{ij} \prod _{k
otin \{ i,j\} }\epsilon _ k.  \] Only the remaining two-plane contributes to its wedge with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $. If $\partial f=\sum _ i f_ i e_ i$, its absolute density relative to $\Omega $ is bounded by \[  C\sum _{i<j}(|f_ i|+|f_ j|)|B_{ij}|.  \] The constant bounds the tensor coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ in all unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Diagonalization is only pointwise; no derivative of this moving frame is taken. 12.1.6 and finite Cauchy–Schwarz bound this sum by \[  C\sum _ i|f_ i|\sqrt{D_ i}\sum _ j\sqrt{D_ j} \leq C\left(\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ iight)^{1/2} \left(\sum _ iD_ iight)^{1/2}.  \] Here $\sum _ iD_ i=(n-q)S_ q(\lambda )$. Moreover \[   egin{aligned}  S^ q\omega ^{n-q}& =q!(n-q)!S_ q(\lambda )\Omega ,\  \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge S^ q\omega ^{n-q-1} & =\kappa q!(n-q-1)!\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\, \Omega , \end{aligned}  \] where $\kappa =1/(2\pi )$ by the book's $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ normalization. These two densities are nonnegative. Thus the pointwise torsion density is bounded by a constant times their geometric mean. Multiplication by $a$ and integral Cauchy–Schwarz give the assertion, including the cases where either density vanishes. The other wedge is conjugate up to a fixed sign, which does not affect its absolute value. For $q\geq 1$, use the exact polarization identity \[  q!\, \alpha _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \alpha _ q =\sum _{J\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,q\} } (-1)^{q-|J|}\left(\sum _{i\in J}\alpha _ iight)^ q.  \] Every nonempty subset sum remains in the cone. Applying the single power estimate to each term and taking absolute values proves the mixed assertion. At $q=0$ use the single term $S^0=1$. No Cauchy–Schwarz assertion for an arbitrary weakly positive $(n-2,n-2)$-form is needed. $\square$ Lemma 12.10.4 . Let $f_ j$ be uniformly bounded smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions with $f_ j\downarrow f$, and fix a smaller concentric ball $V\Subset U$. There are uniformly bounded smooth local functions $v_ j\downarrow v$ which equal $f_ j$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$ and equal one fixed strictly plurisubharmonic $\psi $ on one fixed boundary collar. Moreover $v=f$ near $\overline V$ and $v=\psi $ on that collar. Proof. Write $U=\{ |z|<R\} $ and $|f_ j|\leq M$. Take $\psi =A(|z|^2-R^2)+b$, with $b>M+2$ and then $A$ so large that $\psi <-M-2$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$. It exceeds $M+2$ on a fixed sufficiently thin boundary collar. Use the regularized maximum $M_\epsilon $ constructed in 12.1.7 . Choose $0<\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ with $\epsilon _ j<1$, and put $v_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(f_ j,\psi )$. The lemma preserves the local unshifted cone condition. Its two monotonicities give $v_ j\downarrow \max (f,\psi )=v$, and the fixed gaps give the two asserted regions of exact equality. The bounds \[  \max (f_ j,\psi )\leq v_ j\leq \max (f_ j,\psi )+\epsilon _ j/2  \] give a common bound. In particular all differences $v_ k-v_ j$ have support in one fixed compact subset of $U$. $\square$ Proposition 12.10.5 . For the localized sequence in the preceding lemma and $0\leq s\leq m$, \[  c_ s\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} \longrightarrow 0 \qquad (\delta >0).  \] Consequently a uniformly bounded smooth decreasing local sequence has a quasicontinuous pointwise limit on every compact subset of $U$, for each $c_ s^*$ as well as $c_ s$, $0\leq s\leq m$. Proof. The assertion for $s=0$ follows by bounded convergence for volume. Induct on $s$, assuming it for $s-1$, and put $q=s-1$ and $	heta =\omega ^{n-s}$. For $j\geq k$ let $h=v_ k-v_ j\geq 0$. The support of $h$ lies in one fixed compact set $K_0\Subset U$. Smooth capacity domination and the induction hypothesis give, uniformly over all bounded local smooth mixed potentials, 12.18  egin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:lower-weight} \int h\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_1\cdots \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_ q\omega ^{n-q} \longrightarrow 0\quad (k	o \infty ). \end{equation} To see this, split at $h=\delta $. On $\{ h\leq \delta \} $ the mass bound gives $C\delta $. On the remaining set use $h\leq v_ k-v$, the capacity bound and the induction hypothesis. Let $k$ tend to infinity before $\delta \downarrow 0$. For $q=0$ this is the volume estimate. Constants are uniform in $j\geq k$ and all potentials with the fixed common bound. Consider the real smooth energy \[  E_ s(w)=\int _ U w(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ s	heta , \qquad w_ t=v_ j+t h,\quad 0\leq t\leq 1.  \] The energies $E_ s(v_ j)$ are bounded: on the fixed collar the integrand is fixed, and the remaining compact set has a uniform smooth mass bound. Since $h$ vanishes near the boundary, integration by parts and closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t$ give the exact identity 12.19  egin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:energy-variation}  egin{split}   rac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}E_ s(w_ t) & =(s+1)\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ s	heta \ & \quad +s\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q  igl (\mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}	heta -\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t\wedge \mathrm d	heta +w_ t\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}	heta  igr ). \end{split} \end{equation} Here \[   egin{aligned}  \mathrm d	heta & =(n-s)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1},\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}	heta & =(n-s)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1}\ & \quad +(n-s)(n-s-1)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-2}, \end{aligned}  \] and the analogous $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ formula holds. A zero scalar coefficient means that its term is absent. The two first-order terms in ( 12.19 ) tend uniformly to zero by 12.10.3 , the uniform local gradient bound, and ( 12.18 ). The last term has the same property by the absolute-form estimate at degree $q<m$. More explicitly, the first torsion integral is bounded by \[  C\left(\int h\, \mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t \wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q-1}ight)^{1/2} \left(\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q}ight)^{1/2}.  \] The first factor is bounded since $h$ has a common bound and 12.10.1 applies; the second tends to zero by ( 12.18 ). Conjugation handles the other first-order term. Thus, with $e_ k\downarrow 0$ after taking a tail supremum, \[  E_ s(v_ k)-E_ s(v_ j)=(s+1)\Delta _{kj}+r_{kj}, \quad \Delta _{kj}=\int _0^1\int h\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\, \mathrm dt\geq 0, \quad |r_{kj}|\leq e_ k.  \] It follows that $E_ s(v_ j)\leq E_ s(v_ k)+e_ k$ for $j\geq k$. Taking a subsequence $k$ approaching the liminf shows that the bounded energy sequence converges. Hence $\Delta _{kj}	o 0$ uniformly for $j\geq k$. Positivity of the binomial expansion $\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\geq (1-t)^ s \Lambda _ s(v_ j)$ then gives 12.25  egin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:self-weight} \int h\Lambda _ s(v_ j)\longrightarrow 0 \quad 	ext{uniformly for }j\geq k. \end{equation} It remains to replace each Hessian factor by a capacity competitor. For any smooth $-1\leq a\leq 0$ in the local cone, put \[  I_\ell =\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell }	heta , \qquad \eta _\ell =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell -1}, \quad 0\leq \ell <s.  \] First-order Stokes, with every metric derivative retained, gives \[  I_\ell =-\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell 	heta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d	heta .  \] The second term is $o(1)$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Use finite polarization in 12.10.3 ; each subset sum has a uniform local gradient bound and its lower trace is controlled by ( 12.18 ). The form $\eta _\ell 	heta $ is positive of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$: a complementary nonnegative rank-one form completes a polarized product of $s\leq m$ cone forms. Its associated Hermitian gradient pairing is nonnegative, so Cauchy–Schwarz and the uniform gradient bound for $a$ give \[  I_\ell \leq C F_\ell (h)^{1/2}+o(1), \qquad F_\ell (h)=\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell 	heta .  \] Another exact first-order Stokes identity gives \[  F_\ell (h)= I_{\ell +1} -\int h\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \eta _\ell 	heta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d	heta \leq I_{\ell +1}+o(1).  \] The dropped term is nonnegative. For the last term the same polarized torsion estimate applies: its first gradient factor is uniformly bounded because $h=v_ k-v_ j$, and its second factor tends to zero by ( 12.18 ); here $h^2\leq C h$ and the gradient energy of the difference is at most twice the sum of those of $v_ k$ and $v_ j$ for every positive single-power gradient pairing. Starting with ( 12.25 ) at $I_ s$, finite backward induction gives $I_0	o 0$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Chebyshev's inequality now yields $c_ s\{ v_ k-v_ j>\delta \} \leq \delta ^{-1}\sup _ a I_0$. These sets increase to $\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} $ as $j	o \infty $. Continuity of $c_ s$ under increasing unions proves the induction. For any one $0\leq s\leq m$, choose $k_ N$ so that the open sets $G_ N=\{ v_{k_ N}-v>2^{-N}\} $ satisfy $c_ s(G_ N)<\epsilon 2^{-N}$, $N\geq 1$. They are open because $v$ is upper semicontinuous and $v_{k_ N}$ is smooth. On $U\setminus  igcup _ NG_ N$ these smooth functions converge uniformly to the pointwise limit $v$. Hence $v$ is continuous there. The union has capacity less than $\epsilon $. Boundary localization transfers this conclusion to $f$ on each smaller compact set. Open sets have the same outer capacity, which also proves the assertion for $c_ s^*$. $\square$ Lemma 12.10.6 . Every bounded admissible potential on $X$ is locally quasicontinuous for each smooth capacity $c_ s^*$, $0\leq s\leq m$. For $0\leq p<m$, each coefficient measure $
u $ of the ordered $D_ p$ satisfies \[  |
u |(E)\leq C c_{m-1}^*(E),\qquad E\subset K\Subset U,  \] uniformly when its global potentials have one common bound. The assertion at $p=0$ means the volume coefficient of $D_0=1$. Proof. The global decreasing approximation and 12.8.5 provide bounded smooth local approximations to $u+ho $. The preceding proposition makes its canonical pointwise limit quasicontinuous. Subtracting the smooth $ho $ preserves quasicontinuity. For smooth approximations write $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+ho )-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho $ and expand the product. Each term has $q\leq p<m$ local cone factors and fixed smooth complementary factors. The absolute-form estimate and ( 12.15 ), with $s=m-1$, bound each coefficient variation by $C c_{m-1}$ on Borel sets. The constants depend only on the common bound and local data. Take the iterated limits of 12.8.2 on a slightly larger compact neighborhood of $K$. Lower semicontinuity of signed measure variation on open sets preserves these estimates at each limit. For any open $G\supset E$, intersect with a fixed open neighborhood of $K$ having compact closure in $U$; this gives $|
u |(E)\leq Cc_{m-1}(G)$. Taking the infimum proves the outer estimate. No simultaneous rough product or rough diagonal polynomial expansion is used. $\square$ Lemma 12.10.7 . Fix $0\leq s\leq m$ and the outer smooth capacity $c_ s^*$ on $U$. Let signed Radon measures $

Their open union $G$ has $c_ s(G)<\epsilon $, and every function is continuous on the compact set $A=K\setminus G$. Dini's theorem gives $b_ i^ j	o b_ i$ uniformly on $A$ for each $i$. Weak convergence is applied to $\phi g$ on the whole measure. $\square$ Theorem 12.10.8 . For uniformly bounded admissible potentials $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ on $X$, the currents $D_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j)$ converge to $D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$ in distributions for $p\leq m$, and weakly with measure coefficients for $p<m$. These currents are symmetric in their potentials. For $p<m$ the coefficient convergence also holds after multiplication by a uniformly bounded decreasing admissible weight. The positive shifted currents $Q_ p$ converge weakly for $p\leq m$; $Q_ m$ converges as a positive Radon measure. At degree $m$, the convergence assertion for $D_ m$ is distributional. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. Degree zero is constant. Suppose the result holds for $D_{p-1}$, which has measure coefficients since $p-1<m$. The preceding two lemmas, applied coefficientwise with weight $u_ p^ j$, give convergence of $u_ p^ jD_{p-1}(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_{p-1}^ j)$. Applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves distributional convergence at degree $p$. For $p<m$, the uniform coefficient bounds in 12.8.2 upgrade this to weak convergence of measures, by smooth approximation of compactly supported continuous tests. The same weighted lemma gives the additional weighted conclusion. For each fixed list choose simultaneous smooth decreasing global approximations. Their smooth raw Hessian wedges are symmetric. The convergence just proved identifies their limit with $D_ p$ in any ordering, proving symmetry without an exchange of previously unproved iterated limits. The subset expansion for $R_ p$ uses fixed smooth powers of $\omega $, so its distributional convergence and symmetry follow from those of $D_ I$. Its wedge $Q_ p$ is positive with uniform local masses by 12.8.3 . Distributional convergence and these mass bounds imply weak convergence as an order-zero positive current, including the Radon measure conclusion at $p=m$. A partition of unity on a finite coordinate cover proves the global assertions. $\square$ The coefficient bound for raw currents uses only $c_{m-1}$. For the positive shifted products, $c_ m$ also controls their trace at top degree. This allows an additional bounded weight in every Hessian degree. Lemma 12.10.9 . On $K\Subset U$, the positive shifted currents $Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$, $1\leq p\leq m$, for globally bounded admissible potentials have trace and coefficient variations bounded on Borel $E\subset K$ by $C c_ m^*(E)$. The constants are uniform when all potentials have a common bound. Proof. First take smooth potentials, put $\sigma _ i=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, and choose the fixed local correction $	au =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho \geq 2\omega $. Then $ eta _ i=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+ho )=\sigma _ i+(	au -\omega )$ lies in the same local cone. Since $	au -\omega \geq 0$, mixed positivity gives \[  0\leq \int _ E Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq \int _ E eta _1\cdots  eta _ p\omega ^{n-p} \leq C c_ m(E),\qquad E\subset K.  \] Here $Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p}=\sigma _1\cdots \sigma _ p\omega ^{n-p}$. The last bound follows from smooth mixed-trace domination at $s=m$ for the bounded corrected potentials and a normalized bounded sum with a fixed strictly plurisubharmonic function. Positivity of $Q_ p$ bounds each of its coefficient variations on the compact coordinate set by a fixed multiple of its trace measure. For bounded potentials choose the smooth decreasing global approximations already established in the chapter. The joint convergence in 12.10.8 identifies their positive-current limit with the previously constructed $Q_ p$. On a compact neighborhood of $K$ inside $U$, lower semicontinuity on open sets preserves trace and coefficient variation estimates. For an arbitrary open $G\supset E$ intersect with a fixed relatively compact neighborhood of $K$ before taking this limit; its capacity is at most $c_ m(G)$. Therefore every such trace or variation measure $\mu $ satisfies $\mu (E)\leq Cc_ m(G)$. Infimize over $G$ to obtain the asserted outer-open bound. The constants of the smooth estimates are independent of the approximation index. The argument does not multiply a rough current of positive order or use an unproved rough diagonal polynomial expansion. $\square$ Theorem 12.10.10 . Suppose $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ are bounded canonical global admissible potentials with common bounds. Then, for $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  a_ j Q_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j) \longrightarrow a Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)  \] weakly as currents with measure coefficients. At $p=m$ this is weak convergence of weighted Radon measures. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. By 12.10.8 , every coefficient measure of the positive shifted currents converges weakly and has a uniform local variation bound. 12.10.9 strengthens this to domination by $C c_ m^*$ on Borel sets. 12.10.6 makes the canonical weights $a_ j$ and $a$ quasicontinuous for this capacity. Apply 12.10.7 with $s=m$ to each coefficient, and then use a finite partition of unity. At $p=m$, $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure, so this also gives the stated weighted measure convergence. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.10.1
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.10.1 . Fix $K\Subset U$ and $M<\infty $. For smooth local $m$-subharmonic $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with $|f_ i|\leq M$, $0\leq q\leq m$, their mixed trace has mass at most a constant depending only on $K,U,\omega ,m,M$. If also $f$ is smooth in this class and $|f|\leq M$, then, for $q\leq m-1$, \[  \int _ K\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \omega ^{n-q-1}\leq C.  \] Proof. For one potential and a nonnegative compactly supported cutoff $\chi $, closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$ gives \[  \int \chi (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ q\omega ^{n-q} =\int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^{q-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi \omega ^{n-q}).  \] For $q\geq 1$, the absolute-form estimate 12.1.5 applies at degree $q-1<m$. Nested cutoffs and induction, starting with volume, therefore bound the left side by $C M^ q$; replacing $M$ by $1+M$ includes $M=0$. For mixed factors, positivity of every term in the expansion of $(\sum _ i\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i)^ q\omega ^{n-q}$ bounds the mixed trace by a fixed multiple of the single trace for $\sum _ i f_ i$. This proves the first assertion, including its degree-zero convention. Replace $f$ by $f+M$, so that $0\leq f\leq 2M$ without changing its gradient or Hessian. The identity \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(f^2)=2f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f+2\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f  \] also shows that $f^2$ belongs to the local cone. Wedge with the remaining $q$ Hessians and $\omega ^{n-q-1}$. The first term on the right is nonnegative, and the mixed mass estimate applied to $f^2$ and the other potentials bounds the second term. The degree used is $q+1\leq m$. A cutoff equal to one on $K$ gives the stated local estimate. $\square$

title: Definition 12.10.2
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Definition 12.10.2 . For Borel $E\subset U$ define the smooth capacity \[  c_ s(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E \Lambda _ s(a): a\in C^\infty (U),\  -1\leq a\leq 0, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}\right\} ,  \] for $0\leq s\leq m$. Its outer-open version is \[  c_ s^*(E)=\inf \{ c_ s(G):E\subset G\subset U,\  G\text{ open}\} .  \] A function on a compact $K\Subset U$ is quasicontinuous for this capacity if, for every $\epsilon >0$, it is continuous on $K\setminus G$ for some open $G\subset U$ with $c_ s(G)<\epsilon $.

title: Lemma 12.10.3
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.10.3 . Let $0\leq q\leq m-1$ and let $S$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form in $\overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}$ pointwise. Put $T=S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$. For smooth real $f$ and nonnegative Borel weights $a$, supported on a fixed compact set, \[  \left|\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge T\right| \leq C\left(\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega \wedge T\right)^{1/2} \left(\int a\, \omega ^2\wedge T\right)^{1/2}.  \] The corresponding inequality with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm d\omega $ holds as well. For a mixed product of $q$ cone forms in place of $S^ q$, it suffices to sum these bounds over the finitely many subset sums of its factors. Proof. For $q\leq m-2$, diagonalize $S$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame. Every diagonal coefficient of $S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$ is a positive multiple of $S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ for two omitted coordinates. This is nonnegative by deleted-coordinate positivity, because $q+2\leq m$. The form is a nonnegative sum of simple positive coordinate forms. For one such simple form, only the remaining complex two-plane contributes to a complementary wedge. The coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ are uniformly bounded in unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Its wedge with $\mathrm df$ is consequently bounded by a constant times the gradient norm on that plane. The wedges with $\omega ^2$ and with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega $ give, up to fixed positive constants, one and the square of that norm. Pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz over the simple summands, followed by integral Cauchy–Schwarz with weight $a$, proves the estimate. Conjugation gives the other estimate. For $q=m-1$, at one point choose an $\omega $-unitary coframe $e_ i$ that diagonalizes $S$. Put $\epsilon _ i=\mathrm i e_ i\wedge \bar e_ i$ and $\Omega =\epsilon _1\cdots \epsilon _ n$, so that $\omega =\sum _ i\epsilon _ i$ and $S=\sum _ i\lambda _ i\epsilon _ i$. Writing $B_{ij}=S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ and $D_ i=S_{q;i}(\lambda )$, ordinary wedge expansion gives \[  S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2} =q!(n-q-2)!\sum _{i<j}B_{ij} \prod _{k\notin \{ i,j\} }\epsilon _ k.  \] Only the remaining two-plane contributes to its wedge with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $. If $\partial f=\sum _ i f_ i e_ i$, its absolute density relative to $\Omega $ is bounded by \[  C\sum _{i<j}(|f_ i|+|f_ j|)|B_{ij}|.  \] The constant bounds the tensor coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ in all unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Diagonalization is only pointwise; no derivative of this moving frame is taken. 12.1.6 and finite Cauchy–Schwarz bound this sum by \[  C\sum _ i|f_ i|\sqrt{D_ i}\sum _ j\sqrt{D_ j} \leq C\left(\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\right)^{1/2} \left(\sum _ iD_ i\right)^{1/2}.  \] Here $\sum _ iD_ i=(n-q)S_ q(\lambda )$. Moreover \[  \begin{aligned}  S^ q\omega ^{n-q}& =q!(n-q)!S_ q(\lambda )\Omega ,\\  \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge S^ q\omega ^{n-q-1} & =\kappa q!(n-q-1)!\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\, \Omega , \end{aligned}  \] where $\kappa =1/(2\pi )$ by the book's $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ normalization. These two densities are nonnegative. Thus the pointwise torsion density is bounded by a constant times their geometric mean. Multiplication by $a$ and integral Cauchy–Schwarz give the assertion, including the cases where either density vanishes. The other wedge is conjugate up to a fixed sign, which does not affect its absolute value. For $q\geq 1$, use the exact polarization identity \[  q!\, \alpha _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \alpha _ q =\sum _{J\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,q\} } (-1)^{q-|J|}\left(\sum _{i\in J}\alpha _ i\right)^ q.  \] Every nonempty subset sum remains in the cone. Applying the single power estimate to each term and taking absolute values proves the mixed assertion. At $q=0$ use the single term $S^0=1$. No Cauchy–Schwarz assertion for an arbitrary weakly positive $(n-2,n-2)$-form is needed. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.10.4
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.10.4 . Let $f_ j$ be uniformly bounded smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions with $f_ j\downarrow f$, and fix a smaller concentric ball $V\Subset U$. There are uniformly bounded smooth local functions $v_ j\downarrow v$ which equal $f_ j$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$ and equal one fixed strictly plurisubharmonic $\psi $ on one fixed boundary collar. Moreover $v=f$ near $\overline V$ and $v=\psi $ on that collar. Proof. Write $U=\{ |z|<R\} $ and $|f_ j|\leq M$. Take $\psi =A(|z|^2-R^2)+b$, with $b>M+2$ and then $A$ so large that $\psi <-M-2$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$. It exceeds $M+2$ on a fixed sufficiently thin boundary collar. Use the regularized maximum $M_\epsilon $ constructed in 12.1.7 . Choose $0<\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ with $\epsilon _ j<1$, and put $v_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(f_ j,\psi )$. The lemma preserves the local unshifted cone condition. Its two monotonicities give $v_ j\downarrow \max (f,\psi )=v$, and the fixed gaps give the two asserted regions of exact equality. The bounds \[  \max (f_ j,\psi )\leq v_ j\leq \max (f_ j,\psi )+\epsilon _ j/2  \] give a common bound. In particular all differences $v_ k-v_ j$ have support in one fixed compact subset of $U$. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.10.5
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Proposition 12.10.5 . For the localized sequence in the preceding lemma and $0\leq s\leq m$, \[  c_ s\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} \longrightarrow 0 \qquad (\delta >0).  \] Consequently a uniformly bounded smooth decreasing local sequence has a quasicontinuous pointwise limit on every compact subset of $U$, for each $c_ s^*$ as well as $c_ s$, $0\leq s\leq m$. Proof. The assertion for $s=0$ follows by bounded convergence for volume. Induct on $s$, assuming it for $s-1$, and put $q=s-1$ and $\theta =\omega ^{n-s}$. For $j\geq k$ let $h=v_ k-v_ j\geq 0$. The support of $h$ lies in one fixed compact set $K_0\Subset U$. Smooth capacity domination and the induction hypothesis give, uniformly over all bounded local smooth mixed potentials, 12.18 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:lower-weight} \int h\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_1\cdots \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_ q\omega ^{n-q} \longrightarrow 0\quad (k\to \infty ). \end{equation} To see this, split at $h=\delta $. On $\{ h\leq \delta \} $ the mass bound gives $C\delta $. On the remaining set use $h\leq v_ k-v$, the capacity bound and the induction hypothesis. Let $k$ tend to infinity before $\delta \downarrow 0$. For $q=0$ this is the volume estimate. Constants are uniform in $j\geq k$ and all potentials with the fixed common bound. Consider the real smooth energy \[  E_ s(w)=\int _ U w(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ s\theta , \qquad w_ t=v_ j+t h,\quad 0\leq t\leq 1.  \] The energies $E_ s(v_ j)$ are bounded: on the fixed collar the integrand is fixed, and the remaining compact set has a uniform smooth mass bound. Since $h$ vanishes near the boundary, integration by parts and closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t$ give the exact identity 12.19 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:energy-variation} \begin{split}  \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}E_ s(w_ t) & =(s+1)\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ s\theta \\ & \quad +s\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q \bigl (\mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\theta -\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t\wedge \mathrm d\theta +w_ t\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\theta \bigr ). \end{split} \end{equation} Here \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm d\theta & =(n-s)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1},\\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\theta & =(n-s)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1}\\ & \quad +(n-s)(n-s-1)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-2}, \end{aligned}  \] and the analogous $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ formula holds. A zero scalar coefficient means that its term is absent. The two first-order terms in ( 12.19 ) tend uniformly to zero by 12.10.3 , the uniform local gradient bound, and ( 12.18 ). The last term has the same property by the absolute-form estimate at degree $q<m$. More explicitly, the first torsion integral is bounded by \[  C\left(\int h\, \mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t \wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q-1}\right)^{1/2} \left(\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q}\right)^{1/2}.  \] The first factor is bounded since $h$ has a common bound and 12.10.1 applies; the second tends to zero by ( 12.18 ). Conjugation handles the other first-order term. Thus, with $e_ k\downarrow 0$ after taking a tail supremum, \[  E_ s(v_ k)-E_ s(v_ j)=(s+1)\Delta _{kj}+r_{kj}, \quad \Delta _{kj}=\int _0^1\int h\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\, \mathrm dt\geq 0, \quad |r_{kj}|\leq e_ k.  \] It follows that $E_ s(v_ j)\leq E_ s(v_ k)+e_ k$ for $j\geq k$. Taking a subsequence $k$ approaching the liminf shows that the bounded energy sequence converges. Hence $\Delta _{kj}\to 0$ uniformly for $j\geq k$. Positivity of the binomial expansion $\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\geq (1-t)^ s \Lambda _ s(v_ j)$ then gives 12.25 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian:self-weight} \int h\Lambda _ s(v_ j)\longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{uniformly for }j\geq k. \end{equation} It remains to replace each Hessian factor by a capacity competitor. For any smooth $-1\leq a\leq 0$ in the local cone, put \[  I_\ell =\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell }\theta , \qquad \eta _\ell =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell -1}, \quad 0\leq \ell <s.  \] First-order Stokes, with every metric derivative retained, gives \[  I_\ell =-\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell \theta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d\theta .  \] The second term is $o(1)$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Use finite polarization in 12.10.3 ; each subset sum has a uniform local gradient bound and its lower trace is controlled by ( 12.18 ). The form $\eta _\ell \theta $ is positive of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$: a complementary nonnegative rank-one form completes a polarized product of $s\leq m$ cone forms. Its associated Hermitian gradient pairing is nonnegative, so Cauchy–Schwarz and the uniform gradient bound for $a$ give \[  I_\ell \leq C F_\ell (h)^{1/2}+o(1), \qquad F_\ell (h)=\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell \theta .  \] Another exact first-order Stokes identity gives \[  F_\ell (h)= I_{\ell +1} -\int h\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \eta _\ell \theta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d\theta \leq I_{\ell +1}+o(1).  \] The dropped term is nonnegative. For the last term the same polarized torsion estimate applies: its first gradient factor is uniformly bounded because $h=v_ k-v_ j$, and its second factor tends to zero by ( 12.18 ); here $h^2\leq C h$ and the gradient energy of the difference is at most twice the sum of those of $v_ k$ and $v_ j$ for every positive single-power gradient pairing. Starting with ( 12.25 ) at $I_ s$, finite backward induction gives $I_0\to 0$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Chebyshev's inequality now yields $c_ s\{ v_ k-v_ j>\delta \} \leq \delta ^{-1}\sup _ a I_0$. These sets increase to $\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} $ as $j\to \infty $. Continuity of $c_ s$ under increasing unions proves the induction. For any one $0\leq s\leq m$, choose $k_ N$ so that the open sets $G_ N=\{ v_{k_ N}-v>2^{-N}\} $ satisfy $c_ s(G_ N)<\epsilon 2^{-N}$, $N\geq 1$. They are open because $v$ is upper semicontinuous and $v_{k_ N}$ is smooth. On $U\setminus \bigcup _ NG_ N$ these smooth functions converge uniformly to the pointwise limit $v$. Hence $v$ is continuous there. The union has capacity less than $\epsilon $. Boundary localization transfers this conclusion to $f$ on each smaller compact set. Open sets have the same outer capacity, which also proves the assertion for $c_ s^*$. $\square$

Lemma 12.10.6 . Every bounded admissible potential on $X$ is locally quasicontinuous for each smooth capacity $c_ s^*$, $0\leq s\leq m$. For $0\leq p<m$, each coefficient measure $
u $ of the ordered $D_ p$ satisfies \[  |
u |(E)\leq C c_{m-1}^*(E),\qquad E\subset K\Subset U,  \] uniformly when its global potentials have one common bound. The assertion at $p=0$ means the volume coefficient of $D_0=1$. Proof. The global decreasing approximation and 12.8.5 provide bounded smooth local approximations to $u+ho $. The preceding proposition makes its canonical pointwise limit quasicontinuous. Subtracting the smooth $ho $ preserves quasicontinuity. For smooth approximations write $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+ho )-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho $ and expand the product. Each term has $q\leq p<m$ local cone factors and fixed smooth complementary factors. The absolute-form estimate and ( 12.15 ), with $s=m-1$, bound each coefficient variation by $C c_{m-1}$ on Borel sets. The constants depend only on the common bound and local data. Take the iterated limits of 12.8.2 on a slightly larger compact neighborhood of $K$. Lower semicontinuity of signed measure variation on open sets preserves these estimates at each limit. For any open $G\supset E$, intersect with a fixed open neighborhood of $K$ having compact closure in $U$; this gives $|
u |(E)\leq Cc_{m-1}(G)$. Taking the infimum proves the outer estimate. No simultaneous rough product or rough diagonal polynomial expansion is used. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.10.7
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text:
Lemma 12.10.7 . Fix $0\leq s\leq m$ and the outer smooth capacity $c_ s^*$ on $U$. Let signed Radon measures $
u _ j	o 
u $ weakly have uniformly bounded local variations, with all variations dominated on compact subsets by $C c_ s^*$. Suppose, for $1\leq i\leq \ell $, that bounded Borel functions $b_ i^ j\downarrow b_ i$ have one common bound and every member of these countable families is locally quasicontinuous for this capacity. title: Theorem 12.10.8
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Theorem 12.10.8 . For uniformly bounded admissible potentials $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ on $X$, the currents $D_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j)$ converge to $D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$ in distributions for $p\leq m$, and weakly with measure coefficients for $p<m$. These currents are symmetric in their potentials. For $p<m$ the coefficient convergence also holds after multiplication by a uniformly bounded decreasing admissible weight. The positive shifted currents $Q_ p$ converge weakly for $p\leq m$; $Q_ m$ converges as a positive Radon measure. At degree $m$, the convergence assertion for $D_ m$ is distributional. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. Degree zero is constant. Suppose the result holds for $D_{p-1}$, which has measure coefficients since $p-1<m$. The preceding two lemmas, applied coefficientwise with weight $u_ p^ j$, give convergence of $u_ p^ jD_{p-1}(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_{p-1}^ j)$. Applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves distributional convergence at degree $p$. For $p<m$, the uniform coefficient bounds in 12.8.2 upgrade this to weak convergence of measures, by smooth approximation of compactly supported continuous tests. The same weighted lemma gives the additional weighted conclusion. For each fixed list choose simultaneous smooth decreasing global approximations. Their smooth raw Hessian wedges are symmetric. The convergence just proved identifies their limit with $D_ p$ in any ordering, proving symmetry without an exchange of previously unproved iterated limits. The subset expansion for $R_ p$ uses fixed smooth powers of $\omega $, so its distributional convergence and symmetry follow from those of $D_ I$. Its wedge $Q_ p$ is positive with uniform local masses by 12.8.3 . Distributional convergence and these mass bounds imply weak convergence as an order-zero positive current, including the Radon measure conclusion at $p=m$. A partition of unity on a finite coordinate cover proves the global assertions. $\square$

title: Lemma 12.10.9
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Lemma 12.10.9 . On $K\Subset U$, the positive shifted currents $Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$, $1\leq p\leq m$, for globally bounded admissible potentials have trace and coefficient variations bounded on Borel $E\subset K$ by $C c_ m^*(E)$. The constants are uniform when all potentials have a common bound. Proof. First take smooth potentials, put $\sigma _ i=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, and choose the fixed local correction $\tau =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $. Then $\beta _ i=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+\rho )=\sigma _ i+(\tau -\omega )$ lies in the same local cone. Since $\tau -\omega \geq 0$, mixed positivity gives \[  0\leq \int _ E Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq \int _ E\beta _1\cdots \beta _ p\omega ^{n-p} \leq C c_ m(E),\qquad E\subset K.  \] Here $Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p}=\sigma _1\cdots \sigma _ p\omega ^{n-p}$. The last bound follows from smooth mixed-trace domination at $s=m$ for the bounded corrected potentials and a normalized bounded sum with a fixed strictly plurisubharmonic function. Positivity of $Q_ p$ bounds each of its coefficient variations on the compact coordinate set by a fixed multiple of its trace measure. For bounded potentials choose the smooth decreasing global approximations already established in the chapter. The joint convergence in 12.10.8 identifies their positive-current limit with the previously constructed $Q_ p$. On a compact neighborhood of $K$ inside $U$, lower semicontinuity on open sets preserves trace and coefficient variation estimates. For an arbitrary open $G\supset E$ intersect with a fixed relatively compact neighborhood of $K$ before taking this limit; its capacity is at most $c_ m(G)$. Therefore every such trace or variation measure $\mu $ satisfies $\mu (E)\leq Cc_ m(G)$. Infimize over $G$ to obtain the asserted outer-open bound. The constants of the smooth estimates are independent of the approximation index. The argument does not multiply a rough current of positive order or use an unproved rough diagonal polynomial expansion. $\square$

title: Theorem 12.10.10
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: Theorem 12.10.10 . Suppose $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ are bounded canonical global admissible potentials with common bounds. Then, for $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  a_ j Q_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j) \longrightarrow a Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)  \] weakly as currents with measure coefficients. At $p=m$ this is weak convergence of weighted Radon measures. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. By 12.10.8 , every coefficient measure of the positive shifted currents converges weakly and has a uniform local variation bound. 12.10.9 strengthens this to domination by $C c_ m^*$ on Borel sets. 12.10.6 makes the canonical weights $a_ j$ and $a$ quasicontinuous for this capacity. Apply 12.10.7 with $s=m$ to each coefficient, and then use a finite partition of unity. At $p=m$, $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure, so this also gives the stated weighted measure convergence. $\square$

title: 12.11 Locality and maxima of bounded potentials
search_title: Locality and maxima of bounded potentials
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.11 Locality and maxima of bounded potentials Where one bounded admissible potential is strictly larger than another, the maximum has the same positive Hessian current as the larger potential. These strict comparison sets need not be open. Quasicontinuity gives cutoffs whose products with the approximating currents converge, allowing smooth locality to pass to these sets. Proposition 12.11.1 . Let $u,v$ be bounded admissible, put $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, and fix $1\leq p\leq m$. For any bounded admissible $t_2,\ldots ,t_ p$, \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u>v\} }Q_ p(w,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p) =\mathbf1_{\{ u>v\} }Q_ p(u,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p).  \] The equality is coefficientwise as currents with measure coefficients. The corresponding equality on $\{ v>u\} $ follows by exchanging $u,v$. Proof. Choose smooth uniformly bounded decreasing approximations of all the potentials by 12.5.5 . Construct $w_ j$ by 12.1.7 . Work on one compact coordinate test set. Fix $\delta >0$ and a smooth $\chi _\delta :\mathbb R\to [0,1]$ that vanishes for $s\leq \delta /2$ and equals one for $s\geq \delta $. For $j$ large enough that $\epsilon _ j<\delta /2$, ordinary smooth locality gives \[  \chi _\delta (u_ j-v_ j)Q_ p(w_ j,t_2^ j,\ldots ,t_ p^ j) =\chi _\delta (u_ j-v_ j)Q_ p(u_ j,t_2^ j,\ldots ,t_ p^ j).  \] Indeed, wherever the weight is nonzero, $w_ j=u_ j$ on an open neighborhood. The equality elsewhere follows from its zero weight. Both sequences of positive currents converge by 12.10.8 ; every coefficient variation is uniformly dominated by $C c_ m^*$ by 12.10.9 . The potentials and their limits are quasicontinuous by 12.10.6 . Apply 12.10.7 with $s=m$ and $F(x,y)=\chi _\delta (x-y)$ to the real and imaginary parts of each coefficient. Passing to the limit gives the same identity with $u,v,w,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p$. Choose the cutoffs so that $\chi _\delta (s)\to \mathbf1_{\{ s>0\} }$ pointwise as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Dominated convergence against the fixed finite coefficient variations on the test set gives the asserted restriction. A partition of unity proves it globally. $\square$ On the contact set, a positive constant shift gives a strict comparison before the limit is taken. Decreasing the shift then recovers that set by dominated convergence for a fixed measure. Theorem 12.11.2 . Let $u,v$ be bounded admissible. Fix $1\leq r\leq m$ and bounded admissible $z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}$. Define the positive Radon measure \[  \mu _ r(t)=Q_ m(\underbrace{t,\ldots ,t}_{r},z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}).  \] For $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, \[  \mu _ r(w)\geq \mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }\mu _ r(u) +\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }\mu _ r(v).  \] The inequality with $u,v$ exchanged also holds. Proof. Symmetry and 12.11.1 , applied to the $r$ slots, give $\mu _ r(w)=\mu _ r(v)$ on $\{ u<v\} $ and $\mu _ r(w)=\mu _ r(u)$ on $\{ u>v\} $. To include the contact set, put $w_\epsilon =\max \{ u+\epsilon ,v\} $. Strict locality and invariance under addition of constants give \[  \mu _ r(w_\epsilon )\geq \mathbf1_{\{ u+\epsilon >v\} }\mu _ r(u).  \] The invariance follows from the smooth products and their joint decreasing limits. As $\epsilon \downarrow 0$, $w_\epsilon \downarrow w$, so the left side converges weakly to $\mu _ r(w)$. Against any nonnegative continuous compactly supported test function, the right side converges by dominated convergence for the fixed measure $\mu _ r(u)$ to $\mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }\mu _ r(u)$. This proves the measure inequality on the contact set as well as on $\{ u>v\} $. On its disjoint complement $\{ u<v\} $, the already proved equality supplies $\mu _ r(v)$. Restricting the positive measures to these two Borel sets and adding gives the assertion. Exchanging $u,v$ gives its other form. $\square$ Convex rescaling also supplies a positive background term in the measure. Lemma 12.11.3 . For bounded admissible $v$, $0\leq \alpha \leq 1$ and a real constant $b$, the function $v_\alpha =\alpha v+b$ is bounded admissible and \[  H_ m(v_\alpha )\geq \alpha ^ m H_ m(v)+(1-\alpha )^ m\omega ^ n.  \] Proof. Take smooth decreasing uniformly bounded admissible $v_ j\downarrow v$. Cone convexity makes $\alpha v_ j+b$ admissible because \[  \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\alpha v_ j+b) =\alpha (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)+(1-\alpha )\omega .  \] For $\alpha >0$, an upper test $q$ for $\alpha v+b$ gives the upper test $(q-b)/\alpha $ for $v$. The same convex combination of forms therefore proves admissibility of the limit. For $\alpha =0$ the potential is constant. The pointwise decreasing limit has the displayed canonical affine values. Expand the smooth top product. Every mixed term is positive by polarized Gårding positivity. Keeping the two extreme terms gives \[  H_ m(\alpha v_ j+b)\geq \alpha ^ m H_ m(v_ j) +(1-\alpha )^ m\omega ^ n.  \] Joint decreasing convergence from 12.10.8 passes this inequality against each nonnegative continuous test to the asserted inequality of positive Radon measures. $\square$ The weighted limits also pass integration by parts against metric derivatives. A truncation just above the infimum then excludes zero Hessian mass for a bounded potential. Lemma 12.11.4 . Put $k=m-1$ and $\ell =n-m$. For bounded admissible $t_1,\ldots ,t_ k$, let $T=R_ k(t_1,\ldots ,t_ k)\wedge \omega ^\ell $. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ is a signed Radon measure. If bounded admissible $t_ i^ j\downarrow t_ i$ have a common bound, these measures converge weakly, also after multiplication by any continuous function of finitely many uniformly bounded decreasing admissible potentials. Proof. The subset definition and the torsion formulas in 12.8.4 give, in distributions, \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T={}& \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \left(\sum _{a=1}^ kR_{k-1}^{\widehat a}\omega ^\ell +\ell R_ k\omega ^{\ell -1}\right)\\ & +2\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a<b}R_{k-2}^{\widehat a\widehat b}\omega ^\ell \\ & +2\ell \, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ kR_{k-1}^{\widehat a}\omega ^{\ell -1}\\ & +\ell (\ell -1)\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge R_ k\omega ^{\ell -2}. \end{aligned}  \] The sum with two hats is absent when $k=1$, and the last term is absent when $\ell =1$. Every factor $R_ r$ has degree $r\leq k<m$, so its coefficients are signed measures. Expanding each $R_ r$ over subsets expresses the displayed measure as fixed smooth forms wedged with raw currents $D_ p$ of degrees $p\leq m-1$. 12.10.6 therefore bounds its variation locally by $C c_{m-1}^*$, uniformly under common bounds on the potentials. Joint convergence follows from 12.10.8 applied to this expansion. All the canonical weights are quasicontinuous for $c_{m-1}^*$. 12.10.7 , with $s=m-1$, thus proves the weighted assertion coefficientwise on a finite coordinate cover. A partition of unity gives it on $X$. The term involving $R_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^\ell )$ retains degree $m-1$; the argument requires no coefficient estimate in degree $m$. $\square$ Proposition 12.11.5 . Every bounded admissible potential $u$ has \[  \int _ X H_ m(u)>0.  \] No differential identities for powers of $\omega $ are required. Proof. Suppose instead that $H_ m(u)=0$. Fix $s>0$, set $c=\inf _ Xu+s$, and put $w=\max \{ u,c\} $. The upper semicontinuity of $u$ makes $U=\{ u<c\} $ open, and the definition of the infimum makes it nonempty. Moreover $0\leq w-u\leq s$ and this difference is zero outside $U$. The maximum is bounded admissible with its canonical pointwise values by 12.1.7 . For $0\leq q\leq m$, define the positive Radon measures \[  \mu _ q=Q_ m(\underbrace{u,\ldots ,u}_{q}, \underbrace{w,\ldots ,w}_{m-q}).  \] Thus $\mu _ m=H_ m(u)=0$. For $q<m$, let $T_ q$ be the sum of $m-q$ currents with $q+r$ slots equal to $u$ and $m-q-1-r$ slots equal to $w$, for $0\leq r<m-q$, each of degree $m-1$ and wedged with $\omega ^{n-m}$. In smooth notation this is \[  T_ q=\sum _{r=0}^{m-q-1} (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{q+r} (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^{m-q-1-r}\omega ^{n-m}.  \] Here each displayed product denotes the symmetric shifted current $R_{m-1}$ of ( 12.8 ), wedged with $\omega ^{n-m}$. Choose smooth bounded admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ and the regularized maxima $w_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(u_ j,c)\downarrow w$, where $\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, as in 12.1.7 . Both lists have a common bound. The smooth polynomial identity and Stokes' theorem on the compact manifold give \[  \int _ X(\mu _ q^ j-\mu _ m^ j) =\int _ X(w_ j-u_ j)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q^ j.  \] Joint decreasing convergence passes the left side to its limit. The preceding lemma, with $F(x,y)=y-x$ and the decreasing lists $u_ j,w_ j$, passes the right side to its limit. Hence \[  \int _ X\mu _ q=\int _ X(w-u)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q.  \] The difference of the two decreasing sequences need not itself decrease; the continuous two-variable weight is essential here. On the open set $U$, the potential $w$ is constant. Locality of the raw recursion therefore sets every factor $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ to zero there, so that its shifted factors become $\omega $. The formula in the preceding lemma expresses $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q|_ U$ as finitely many smooth metric-derivative forms wedged with powers of $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ of degrees at most $m-1$. Use smooth admissible approximations to $u$ and the constant $c$ in these local expressions; their limits are the same restricted currents. For those smooth approximations, the absolute mixed-form estimate 12.1.5 bounds each such term by a constant times the corresponding positive trace, and therefore by $C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mu _ r$ on $U$ after taking joint limits. More explicitly, a term with $r$ factors is bounded by $C(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ r\omega ^{n-r}$; this is $C\mu _ r$ on $U$. Against compactly supported nonnegative tests in $U$, weak convergence and lower semicontinuity of total variation preserve the estimate. Exhaustion gives the measure inequality \[  \mathbf1_ U|\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q| \leq C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mathbf1_ U\mu _ r.  \] Here $C$ depends only on $\omega ,m,n$, not on $u$ or $s$; a fixed finite coordinate cover bounds all the smooth metric coefficients. Since $w-u$ vanishes outside $U$, positivity gives \[  \int _ U\mu _ q\leq \int _ X\mu _ q \leq Cs\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r \qquad (0\leq q<m).  \] Summing these $m$ inequalities and choosing $s>0$ with $mCs<1$ forces $\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r=0$. But locality gives $\mu _0=\omega ^ n$ on the nonempty open set $U$, whose volume is positive. This contradiction proves the result. $\square$

More explicitly, a term with $r$ factors is bounded by $C(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ r\omega ^{n-r}$; this is $C\mu _ r$ on $U$. Exhaustion gives the measure inequality \[  \mathbf1_ U|\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q| \leq C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mathbf1_ U\mu _ r.  \] Here $C$ depends only on $\omega ,m,n$, not on $u$ or $s$; a fixed finite coordinate cover bounds all the smooth metric coefficients. Since $w-u$ vanishes outside $U$, positivity gives \[  \int _ U\mu _ q\leq \int _ X\mu _ q \leq Cs\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r \qquad (0\leq q<m).  \] Summing these $m$ inequalities and choosing $s>0$ with $mCs<1$ forces $\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r=0$. But locality gives $\mu _0=\omega ^ n$ on the nonempty open set $U$, whose volume is positive. This contradiction proves the result. $\square$

title: 12.12 Hessian mass and global comparison
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.12 Hessian mass and global comparison The maximum inequality compares measures on complementary Borel sets. Integrating it leaves a difference of total masses. The recursive currents express this difference through the complex Hessians of the background powers, extending the mass calculation of chapter 2 to bounded admissible potentials. Their vanishing characterizes the unmodified comparison principle. When they do not vanish, a small sublevel set limits the change made by the maximum; the resulting torsion error can still be absorbed after rescaling the upper potential. For bounded admissible $t_1,\ldots ,t_ m$, put \[  \mathcal M_ m(t_1,\ldots ,t_ m)=\int _ XQ_ m(t_1,\ldots ,t_ m), \qquad H_ m(t)=Q_ m(t,\ldots ,t).  \] Here $H_ m(t)$ is a finite positive Radon measure and $\mathcal M_ m$ is the total mass of a mixed positive measure, by 12.8.3 . For a nonempty subset $I=\{ i_1<\cdots <i_ q\} \subset \{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $, put $i(I)=i_ q$ and $I^-=I\setminus \{ i_ q\} $. Use $D_{I^-}$ for the recursive current with those ordered inputs, with $D_\varnothing =1$. Lemma 12.12.1 . For every bounded admissible list, 12.32 \begin{equation} \label{eq:hessian-bounded-mass-expansion} \mathcal M_ m(t_1,\ldots ,t_ m) =\int _ X\omega ^ n+ \sum _{\varnothing \ne I\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,m\} } \int _ X t_{i(I)}D_{I^-}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^{n-|I|}). \end{equation} Every integral on the right is an integral of bounded canonical values against signed measure coefficients. Proof. Expand $Q_ m$ using ( 12.8 ). The term for $I$ pairs $D_ I$ with the smooth form $\omega ^{n-|I|}$. By ( 12.4 ), \[  \langle D_ I,\omega ^{n-|I|}\rangle =\langle t_{i(I)}D_{I^-},\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^{n-|I|})\rangle .  \] Since $|I^-|\leq m-1$, 12.8.2 gives measure coefficients for $D_{I^-}$; their bounded product with $t_{i(I)}$ is well defined. Thus the displayed pairing is exactly the integral in the sum, and is finite on compact $X$. The empty subset contributes $\int _ X\omega ^ n$. $\square$ Let $\mu _ r$ be the repeated-slot mixed measure from 12.11.2 , for fixed $r$ and $z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}$. The total-mass difference below therefore has the explicit expression ( 12.32 ) for the two indicated lists. Proposition 12.12.2 . If $u,v$ are bounded admissible and $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, then \[  \int _{\{ u<v\} }\mathrm d\mu _ r(v) \leq \int _{\{ u<v\} }\mathrm d\mu _ r(u) +\int _ X\mathrm d\mu _ r(w)-\int _ X\mathrm d\mu _ r(u).  \] Proof. Set $E=\{ u<v\} $. The contact-set version of 12.11.2 gives \[  \mu _ r(w)\geq \mathbf1_{X\setminus E}\mu _ r(u) +\mathbf1_ E\mu _ r(v).  \] All these measures are finite and positive. Integrating on $X$ and using $\mu _ r(u)(X\setminus E)=\mu _ r(u)(X)-\mu _ r(u)(E)$ gives exactly the assertion. No boundary or closed-background hypothesis enters this calculation. $\square$ The unmodified global comparison principle holds precisely when the powers occurring in this mass formula are $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-closed. Only the powers $n-m,\ldots ,n-1$ occur at Hessian degree $m$. Theorem 12.12.3 . The following conditions are equivalent: $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^{n-q})=0$ for every $1\leq q\leq m$; $\int _ XH_ m(u)$ is independent of the smooth admissible potential $u$; $\mathcal M_ m(t_1,\ldots ,t_ m)=\int _ X\omega ^ n$ for every bounded admissible list; every pair of bounded admissible $u,v$ satisfies \[  \int _{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(v)\leq \int _{\{ u<v\} }H_ m(u).  \] Under these conditions, for every $1\leq r\leq m$ and every fixed bounded admissible list $z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}$, one also has \[  \int _{\{ u<v\} }\mathrm d\mu _ r(v) \leq \int _{\{ u<v\} }\mathrm d\mu _ r(u).  \] Proof. The first condition implies the third by ( 12.32 ). The third implies the second by taking all inputs equal to a smooth potential. To prove that the second implies the first, fix any smooth real $f$. For all sufficiently small real $t$ of either sign, $\omega +t\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$ is positive, so $tf$ is strictly admissible. The polynomial \[  \int _ X(\omega +t\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ m\wedge \omega ^{n-m} =\sum _{q=0}^ m\binom mq t^ q \int _ X(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ q\wedge \omega ^{n-q}  \] is constant on an interval. Consequently every coefficient with $q\geq 1$ vanishes. Polarizing that coefficient by replacing $f$ with $\sum _{a=1}^ q s_ af_ a$ gives \[  \int _ X\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \omega ^{n-q}=0  \] for all smooth real $f_ a$. Integration by parts in the first factor, using lemma 2.1.1 , gives \[  \int _ Xf_1\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^{n-q})=0.  \] Since $f_1$ is arbitrary, the smooth top-degree form paired with it vanishes pointwise. At each point the other complex Hessians can be prescribed by real quadratic functions times a cutoff. Complexifying this multilinear identity gives all coordinate $(q-1,q-1)$-forms, as in the proof of theorem 2.2.2 . They detect every coefficient of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^{n-q})$, so that form vanishes. When $q=1$, there are no other Hessians and the same conclusion follows directly from the arbitrariness of $f_1$. Under the third condition, $\mu _ r(w)$ and $\mu _ r(u)$ have the same total mass. 12.12.2 proves the mixed comparison assertion, and $r=m$ gives the fourth condition. Finally, suppose the fourth condition holds and fix smooth admissible $u,v$. Choose $C$ so large that $u<v+C$ everywhere. Constant invariance gives $H_ m(v+C)=H_ m(v)$, so comparison gives $\int _ XH_ m(v)\leq \int _ XH_ m(u)$. Exchanging $u,v$ gives equality, which is the second condition. $\square$ The same varying background that obstructs Monge–Ampère comparison also obstructs comparison at each intermediate Hessian degree. Example 12.12.4 . Let $X=(\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+\mathrm i\mathbb Z))^ n$, with $z_ j=x_ j+\mathrm i y_ j$, and put \[  \beta _ j=\frac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d\bar z_ j, \qquad b=2+\cos (2\pi x_1), \qquad \omega =\beta _1+b\beta _2+\sum _{j=3}^ n\beta _ j.  \] For $|t|<\pi ^{-2}$ the potential $u_ t=t\cos (2\pi x_1)$ is smooth strictly admissible, and, with $B_ n=\int _ X\beta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \beta _ n$, \[  \int _ X H_ m(u_ t)=n!\left(2-\frac{m\pi ^2t}{2n}\right)B_ n.  \] Thus every $-\pi ^{-2}<t<0$, together with a constant $C>|t|$, gives a pair $u=0$, $v=u_ t+C$ that violates the unmodified global comparison inequality. Proof. As in example 2.3.1 , $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ t=-\pi ^2t\cos (2\pi x_1)\beta _1$. The coefficient of $\beta _1$ in $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ t$ is strictly positive in the stated range, and all the other coefficients are positive. Since $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ t)^2=0$, expansion gives \[  H_ m(u_ t)=\omega ^ n+m\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ t\wedge \omega ^{n-1} =n!b\left(1-\frac mn\pi ^2t\cos (2\pi x_1)\right) \beta _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \beta _ n.  \] The period averages of $b$ and $b\cos (2\pi x_1)$ are respectively $2$ and $1/2$, proving the mass formula. For $t<0$ this mass is strictly larger than $\int _ XH_ m(0)=2n!B_ n$. Meanwhile $C>|t|$ gives $\{ 0<u_ t+C\} =X$, so the comparison inequality for this pair would assert the opposite ordering of these masses. $\square$

title: 12.12.1 Modified comparison
topic: Local Monge–Ampère theory and Hessian equations
text: 12.12.1 Modified comparison On a sublevel set just above the infimum of a difference, the maximum changes the lower potential by at most a prescribed small number. Integration by parts then expresses the mass defect through this small difference and a torsion measure. Mixed lower-degree traces control its variation. Rescaling the upper potential adds a positive background term that relates these traces to the top Hessian measure. For bounded admissible $u,V$, use the notation \[  \sigma _ u=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u,\qquad M_{p,q}=\sigma _ u^ p\sigma _ V^ q\omega ^{n-p-q} \quad (0\leq p+q\leq m).  \] These expressions denote the positive mixed measure $Q_ m$ with $p$ slots equal to $u$, $q$ slots equal to $V$ and the remaining slots equal to the constant zero. In particular $M_{0,0}=\omega ^ n$.  For $p+q\leq m-1$, put \[  T_{p,q}=\sigma _ u^ p\sigma _ V^ q\omega ^{n-p-q-1}.  \] This denotes $R_{m-1}$ with the same nonconstant slots and zero in its other slots, wedged with $\omega ^{n-m}$. Lemma 12.12.5 . Let $u,V$ be bounded admissible, $b$ a real constant and $s>0$. Suppose $0\leq \max \{ u,V+b\} -u\leq s$. Set $E=\{ u<V+b\} $ and $b_{p,q}=M_{p,q}(E)$. There is a constant $C$, depending only on $X,\omega ,m,n$, such that \[  b_{p,q+1}\leq b_{p+1,q} +Cs\sum _{a+d\leq p+q}b_{a,d} \qquad (p+q\leq m-1).  \] For $q=0$, the error can instead be bounded by $Cs(b_{p,0}+b_{p-1,0}+b_{p-2,0})$, with negative indices zero. Proof. First estimate the torsion of $T_{p,q}$, writing $r=p+q$. For smooth admissible potentials, the product rule expresses $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}$ as a sum of fixed smooth metric forms wedged with products of $\sigma _ u,\sigma _ V$ of degrees $r,r-1,r-2$. The terms of degree $r$ come from differentiating the background power; they cannot be discarded. Indeed, $\mathrm d\sigma _ u=\mathrm d\sigma _ V=\mathrm d\omega $, $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\sigma _ u=\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\sigma _ V=\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sigma _ u=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sigma _ V=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $. Every term therefore contains either $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $ or $\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $, with its product-rule multiplicity and the appropriate remaining background power. Terms with negative numbers of factors are absent. All variable degrees are at most $r<m$. Apply 12.1.5 to each term. Expanding the resulting positive power of the sum of its variable factors gives the pointwise bound \[  |\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}|\leq C\sum _{a+d\leq r}M_{a,d}.  \] For $q=0$ every variable factor is $\sigma _ u$, so the sharper bound is $C(M_{p,0}+M_{p-1,0}+M_{p-2,0})$. The constant bounds fixed metric coefficients on a finite coordinate cover and the finitely many multiplicities; it is independent of the potentials and their bounds. Choose uniformly bounded smooth decreasing approximations to $u,V$. By 12.11.4 , the torsion measures converge weakly; by 12.10.8 , all positive measures in these bounds also converge weakly. Against nonnegative continuous tests, lower semicontinuity of total variation preserves both bounds. They are consequently inequalities of measures and may be restricted to the Borel set $E$. Put $w=\max \{ u,V+b\} $ and $h=w-u$. The mixed maximum theorem 12.11.2 , with one moving slot and the fixed slots defining $T_{p,q}$, gives \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)T_{p,q} \geq \mathbf1_ E\sigma _ VT_{p,q} +\mathbf1_{X\setminus E}\sigma _ uT_{p,q}.  \] All products here are the corresponding positive mixed measures. After integration, this implies \[  b_{p,q+1}\leq b_{p+1,q} +\int _ X\bigl ((\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)-\sigma _ u\bigr )T_{p,q}.  \] Regularized maxima of the smooth decreasing approximations give a uniformly bounded decreasing smooth list $w_ j\downarrow w$. Stokes' theorem on compact $X$ gives for these lists \[  \int _ X\bigl ((\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j)-\sigma _{u_ j}\bigr )T_{p,q}^ j =\int _ X(w_ j-u_ j)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}^ j.  \] Joint decreasing convergence passes the positive mixed measures on the left to their limits. The continuous two-variable weight $F(x,y)=y-x$ in 12.11.4 passes the right side to $\int _ Xh\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}$. No monotonicity of $w_ j-u_ j$ is needed. Since $h$ is zero outside $E$ and $0\leq h\leq s$, \[  \int _ Xh\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}\leq s|\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_{p,q}|(E).  \] The torsion bounds prove both assertions. The argument never passes a varying measure to a weak limit after restriction to $E$. $\square$ Theorem 12.12.6 . There is $C\geq 1$, depending only on $X,\omega ,m,n$, with the following property. For bounded admissible $u,v$ and $0<\alpha <1$, put $\eta =1-\alpha $, $V=\alpha v$ and $S=\inf _ X(u-V)$. For $0<s<\eta ^3/C$, let $E_ s=\{ u<V+S+s\} $. Then \[  \int _{E_ s}H_ m(V) \leq \left(1+\frac{Cs}{\eta ^ m}\right) \int _{E_ s}H_ m(u).  \] No differential identity for a power of $\omega $ is assumed. Proof. Use the mixed measures above on $E_ s$, writing $b_{p,q}=M_{p,q}(E_ s)$ and $a_ k=b_{k,0}$. The definition of $S$ gives $0\leq \max \{ u,V+S+s\} -u\leq s$, so 12.12.5 applies. Repeatedly moving a $V$ slot to a $u$ slot gives, for $p+q=r$, \[  b_{p,q}\leq a_ r+C_1s\sum _{d=0}^{r-1}A_ d, \qquad A_ d=\max _{a+b=d}b_{a,b},\qquad 1\leq r\leq m.  \] Here there are at most $m$ moves, and the multiplicity $d+1$ in the lower-degree sum is absorbed in $C_1$. For $0<s\leq 1$, induction on $r$ shows \[  A_ r\leq a_ r+K_ rs\sum _{k<r}a_ k.  \] In fact $A_0=a_0$, and one may take $K_ r=C_1(1+\sum _{1\leq d<r}K_ d)$: insert the earlier bounds in the displayed recurrence and use $s^2\leq s$. Thus, for a constant $C_2$ depending only on the setting, \[  b_{0,m}\leq a_ m+C_2s\sum _{k<m}a_ k.  \] It remains to control the lower diagonal masses by $a_ m$. The identity $\sigma _ V=\alpha \sigma _ v+\eta \omega $ and mixed positivity give $b_{k,1}\geq \eta a_ k$; this identity and inequality pass from smooth approximations by joint convergence. The diagonal assertion of 12.12.5 gives \[  \eta a_ k\leq a_{k+1} +C_3s(a_ k+a_{k-1}+a_{k-2})\qquad (0\leq k<m),  \] with $a_{-1}=a_{-2}=0$. Set $B_ k=\eta ^{m-k}a_ k$ for $0\leq k\leq m$, and set $B_{-1}=B_{-2}=0$. Multiplying by $\eta ^{m-k-1}$ and using $0<\eta <1$ gives \[  B_ k\leq B_{k+1} +\delta (B_ k+B_{k-1}+B_{k-2}), \qquad \delta =C_3s\eta ^{-3}.  \] For $M=\max _{0\leq k<m}B_ k$, summing from any $j<m$ through $m-1$ gives $B_ j\leq B_ m+3m\delta M$. If $s<\eta ^3/(6mC_3)$, it follows that $M\leq 2B_ m$. Consequently \[  a_ k\leq 2\eta ^{-(m-k)}a_ m\quad (k<m),\qquad \sum _{k<m}a_ k\leq 2m\eta ^{-m}a_ m.  \] Choose $C\geq \max \{ 1,6mC_3,2mC_2\} $. Then the asserted range for $s$ supplies every preceding restriction, and substitution in the bound for $b_{0,m}$ proves the theorem. No division by $a_ m$ occurs, so zero top mass on $E_ s$ is included. $\square$
