Ordered contact on each part gives \[  \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{p_{j,N}}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mu _{p_{j,N}} \leq \sum _{\ell =j}^ N I_\ell \leq 2^{1-j}.  \] Only integrals of nonnegative functions occur here, so the estimate holds even if a rooftop has infinite mass. As $N	o \infty $, $p_{j,N}\downarrow p_ j$; as $j	o \infty $, the $p_ j$ increase, and their regularized limit $p$ is not identically $-\infty $. Both monotone limits hold in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 . Moreover $h\leq p\leq u\leq \varphi +C$, where $p\leq u$ follows from the almost-everywhere convergence of the extracted $u_ j$. Thus $p\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Apply lemma 6.3.1 , first as $N	o \infty $ and then as $j	o \infty $, with the bounded quasi-continuous weights in the preceding estimate. These weights converge in capacity because the exponential is Lipschitz on a common upper half-line. We obtain \[  \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^ p-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mu _ p=0, \qquad \mu _ p(\{ p<u\} )=0.  \] The second equality follows off the poles, which the extended measures ignore. The zero-domination lemma lemma 31.2.2 now gives $p=u$; no finiteness of $\mu _ p$ is needed. Finally, the upper envelopes $U_ j=(\sup _{\ell \geq j}u_\ell )^*$ decrease to $u$, by theorem 1.4.2 and the almost-everywhere convergence. Applying lemma 1.8.12 to $p_ j\uparrow u$ and $U_ j\downarrow u$, the inequalities $p_ j\leq u_ j\leq U_ j$ give convergence in capacity along this subsequence, and hence for the original sequence. $\square$

text: Proposition 31.3.2 . Suppose $u_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and, for a fixed $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and a constant $C$, \[  h\leq u_ j\leq \varphi +C,\qquad u_ j\longrightarrow u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\quad \hbox{in }L^1(X).  \] If \[  I_ j:=\int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{u_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mu _{u_ j}\longrightarrow 0,  \] then $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $u_ j\to u$ in capacity. section: 12.5 Relative equations under positive lower mass
text:
31.3.1 Convergence under a fixed measure The extraction lemma provides the lower envelope required by the integral criterion. The same fixed measure then controls the measures of deep sublevel sets, so convergence in capacity passes to the Monge–Ampère measures themselves. Theorem 31.3.3 . Suppose $u_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $u_ j	o u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ in $L^1(X)$, and $\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u $ for a fixed finite non-pluripolar measure $
u $. Then \[  u\in \mathcal E_\varphi , \qquad u_ j\longrightarrow u	ext{ in capacity}, \qquad \mu _{u_ j}ightharpoonup \mu _ u\leq 
u .  \] Proof. Start with an arbitrary subsequence. By lemma 31.3.1 , a further subsequence has a common lower envelope $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, and $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Inequality ( 31.2 ) and Hartogs' lemma give a common upper bound $u_ j\leq \varphi +C$. After a common translation, assume $u_ j,u\leq 0$. Since $\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u $, lemma 1.23.1 gives \[  \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{u_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mathrm{d}\mu _{u_ j} \leq \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{u_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mathrm{d}
u \longrightarrow 0.  \] Thus proposition 31.3.2 gives convergence in capacity along this subsequence. For the measures themselves, the common lower bound gives \[  \mu _{u_ j}(\{ u_ j\leq -T\} ) \leq 
u (\{ h\leq -T\} )\longrightarrow 0 \quad \hbox{uniformly in }j,  \] since $
u $ is finite and does not charge the pole set of $h
ot\equiv -\infty $. The tail criterion for smooth backgrounds, theorem 7.6.1 , therefore gives $\mu _{u_ j}ightharpoonup \mu _ u$, and weak limits preserve domination by the fixed finite measure $
u $. Every subsequence of the original sequence has a further subsequence with these conclusions and the same limit $u$, so both convergences hold for the original sequence. $\square$

title: 31.4 Moving bounded carrier measures
section: 12.5 Relative equations under positive lower mass
text: 31.4 Moving bounded carrier measures In the approximation scheme of section 31.6 , the measures of the approximating solutions are dominated by Monge–Ampère measures of uniformly bounded $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potentials $\psi _ j$, which vary with $j$. For a bounded $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potential $\psi $, write $\omega _\psi =\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi $. A single dominating measure is then unavailable, but an exponential domination $\mu _{u_ j}\leq A\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u_ j}\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n$ still provides a common lower envelope. A smaller-background potential and a strict big potential give comparison functions whose constants are uniform in $j$. If every $u_ j$ has the ordinary singularity type of $\varphi $, smaller-background comparison gives the same construction even when $v_-(\theta )=0$. Convergence of the potentials $\psi _ j$ in capacity then identifies the limiting equation. Proposition 31.4.1 . Fix $A,\lambda >0$, $C\in \mathbb R$ and $L\geq 0$. For $j\geq 1$, suppose that $u_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $u_ j\leq \varphi +C$, and 31.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:exponential-bounded-reference-domination} \mu _{u_ j}\leq A \mathrm{e}^{\lambda u_ j}\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n, \qquad \psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega ),\qquad \| \psi _ j\| _\infty \leq L. \end{equation} Assume either $v_-(\theta )>0$ or $u_ j\sim \varphi $ for every $j$. Then \[  h=P_\theta \left(\inf _ j u_ j\right)\in \mathcal E_\varphi .  \] No convergence of $\psi _ j$ or $u_ j$ is assumed, and in the second alternative the constants in $u_ j\sim \varphi $ need not be uniform in $j$. Proof. Translate all $u_ j$ by one constant so that $u_ j\leq \varphi \leq 0$; this changes $A$ by a fixed factor. Translate each $\psi _ j$ so that it takes values in $[-2L,0]$; this does not change its measure. Set $q=P_{\varepsilon \theta }(\varphi )$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $a>0$ such that \[  q\leq \varphi , \qquad \rho \leq 0,\qquad \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq a\omega .  \] Here $q\not\equiv -\infty $ by the model condition, and $\rho $ exists because $\theta $ is big. Fix $0<\delta <(1-\varepsilon )a$. For a fixed real $b\geq 1$, put $r_{j,b}=Q_ b(u_ j,\varphi )$. The stretching lemma puts it in $\mathcal E_\varphi $, and $r_{j,b}\leq u_ j\leq 0$. Contact support and positivity imply \[  \mu _{r_{j,b}} \leq b^ n\mathbf1_{D_{j,b}}\mu _{u_ j}, \qquad D_{j,b}=\{ b^{-1}r_{j,b}+(1-b^{-1})\varphi =u_ j\} .  \] On this contact set, $\varphi \leq 0$ gives $u_ j\leq r_{j,b}/b$. Thus ( 31.7 ) yields 31.8 \begin{equation} \label{eq:stretched-exponential-domination} \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda r_{j,b}/b}\mu _{r_{j,b}} \leq b^ n A\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n, \end{equation} where the weights are evaluated off the pluripolar pole sets. Choose $C_ b\geq 0$ so large that \[  \delta ^ n\exp (\lambda C_ b/b)\geq b^ n A,  \] and define \[  s_{j,b}=q+(1-\varepsilon )\rho +\delta \psi _ j-C_ b.  \] This is a $\theta $-plurisubharmonic function, not identically $-\infty $, since \[  \begin{split}  \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}s_{j,b} & = (\varepsilon \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q) +(1-\varepsilon )(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho ) +\delta \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ j\\ & \geq \delta \omega _{\psi _ j}. \end{split}  \] Consequently $\mu _{s_{j,b}}\geq \delta ^ n\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n$: this inequality holds away from the poles by the local positive product inequality, and then globally because the bounded reference measure does not charge pluripolar sets. Also $s_{j,b}\leq -C_ b$ and $s_{j,b}\preceq \varphi $. Together with ( 31.8 ), we conclude \[  \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda s_{j,b}/b}\mu _{s_{j,b}} \geq b^ n A\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n \geq \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda r_{j,b}/b}\mu _{r_{j,b}}.  \] If $v_-(\theta )>0$, apply corollary 31.2.4 with first potential $r_{j,b}$ and second potential $s_{j,b}$. It gives $r_{j,b}\geq s_{j,b}$. In the second alternative, $r_{j,b}\sim \varphi $: if $u_ j\geq \varphi -K_ j$, the potential $\varphi -bK_ j$ is a competitor for $r_{j,b}$. Hence the smaller-background envelope $P_{\varepsilon \theta }(r_{j,b})$ is not identically $-\infty $, and $s_{j,b}\preceq r_{j,b}$. Therefore corollary 14.1.3 also gives $r_{j,b}\geq s_{j,b}$, without a lower-mass hypothesis. Since $\psi _ j\geq -2L$, we now have a lower bound independent of $j$: \[  H_ b=q+(1-\varepsilon )\rho -2\delta L-C_ b \leq r_{j,b}.  \] The potential $H_ b$ is $\theta $-plurisubharmonic and not identically $-\infty $. By the definition of $r_{j,b}$, therefore, \[  b^{-1}H_ b+(1-b^{-1})\varphi \leq u_ j \quad \hbox{for every }j.  \] For $b=1$ this shows that the infimum envelope $h$ is not identically $-\infty $. For general $b$, the left side is a competitor for $h$, so it lies below $h$; it is thus a competitor in the defining condition of the relative class for $b$. text: Proposition 31.4.1 . Fix $A,\lambda >0$, $C\in \mathbb R$ and $L\geq 0$. For $j\geq 1$, suppose that $u_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $u_ j\leq \varphi +C$, and 31.7 \begin{equation} \label{eq:exponential-bounded-reference-domination} \mu _{u_ j}\leq A \mathrm{e}^{\lambda u_ j}\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n, \qquad \psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega ),\qquad \| \psi _ j\| _\infty \leq L. \end{equation} Assume either $v_-(\theta )>0$ or $u_ j\sim \varphi $ for every $j$. Then \[  h=P_\theta \left(\inf _ j u_ j\right)\in \mathcal E_\varphi .  \] Proof. Translate all $u_ j$ by one constant so that $u_ j\leq \varphi \leq 0$; this changes $A$ by a fixed factor. Translate each $\psi _ j$ so that it takes values in $[-2L,0]$; this does not change its measure. Set $q=P_{\varepsilon \theta }(\varphi )$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $a>0$ such that \[  q\leq \varphi , \qquad \rho \leq 0,\qquad \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq a\omega .  \] Here $q\not\equiv -\infty $ by the model condition, and $\rho $ exists because $\theta $ is big. Fix $0<\delta <(1-\varepsilon )a$. For a fixed real $b\geq 1$, put $r_{j,b}=Q_ b(u_ j,\varphi )$. The stretching lemma puts it in $\mathcal E_\varphi $, and $r_{j,b}\leq u_ j\leq 0$. Contact support and positivity imply \[  \mu _{r_{j,b}} \leq b^ n\mathbf1_{D_{j,b}}\mu _{u_ j}, \qquad D_{j,b}=\{ b^{-1}r_{j,b}+(1-b^{-1})\varphi =u_ j\} .  \] On this contact set, $\varphi \leq 0$ gives $u_ j\leq r_{j,b}/b$. Also $s_{j,b}\leq -C_ b$ and $s_{j,b}\preceq \varphi $. Together with ( 31.8 ), we conclude \[  \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda s_{j,b}/b}\mu _{s_{j,b}} \geq b^ n A\omega _{\psi _ j}^ n \geq \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda r_{j,b}/b}\mu _{r_{j,b}}.  \] If $v_-(\theta )>0$, apply corollary 31.2.4 with first potential $r_{j,b}$ and second potential $s_{j,b}$. It gives $r_{j,b}\geq s_{j,b}$. In the second alternative, $r_{j,b}\sim \varphi $: if $u_ j\geq \varphi -K_ j$, the potential $\varphi -bK_ j$ is a competitor for $r_{j,b}$. Hence the smaller-background envelope $P_{\varepsilon \theta }(r_{j,b})$ is not identically $-\infty $, and $s_{j,b}\preceq r_{j,b}$. Therefore corollary 14.1.3 also gives $r_{j,b}\geq s_{j,b}$, without a lower-mass hypothesis. Since $\psi _ j\geq -2L$, we now have a lower bound independent of $j$: \[  H_ b=q+(1-\varepsilon )\rho -2\delta L-C_ b \leq r_{j,b}.  \] The potential $H_ b$ is $\theta $-plurisubharmonic and not identically $-\infty $. By the definition of $r_{j,b}$, therefore, \[  b^{-1}H_ b+(1-b^{-1})\varphi \leq u_ j \quad \hbox{for every }j.  \] For $b=1$ this shows that the infimum envelope $h$ is not identically $-\infty $. For general $b$, the left side is a competitor for $h$, so it lies below $h$; it is thus a competitor in the defining condition of the relative class for $b$. title: 31.7 Normalization at exponent zero
section: 12.5 Relative equations under positive lower mass
text: 31.7 Normalization at exponent zero In this section the background is a Hermitian form $h$ on $X$ with $v_-(h)>0$, and the reference is zero; thus $\theta =h$ and $\varphi =0$ in the notation of the chapter, and $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,h,0)$ is the minimal envelope class. Let $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ be nonzero. Recall from ( 14.101 ) that the subsolution threshold $b_ h(f)$ is the limit of the normalizing constants of the truncations $\min (f,k)$; by theorem 14.27.2 , it is the largest $a\geq 0$ for which some $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,h)$ satisfies $\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(u)\geq af\, \mathrm{d}V$. We show that $b_ h(f)$ is exactly the scalar of the normalized equation in the minimal envelope class: scalar comparison bounds every subsolution coefficient by this scalar. Dominated continuity also identifies the equation satisfied by every limit of normalized greatest exponential solutions; whether these limits coincide is a question about the potentials. Corollary 31.7.1 . Let $h$ be a Hermitian form on $X$ with $v_-(h)>0$, and let $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ be nonzero. There is $v\in \mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,h,0)$ such that \[  \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(v)=b_ h(f)f\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] The number $b_ h(f)>0$ is the unique positive scalar for which this equation has a solution in that envelope class. For $\lambda >0$, let $u_\lambda $ be the greatest solution of $\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(u_\lambda )=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u_\lambda }f\, \mathrm{d}V$ from theorem 14.34.1 , and set $v_\lambda =u_\lambda -\sup _ Xu_\lambda $. Each $u_\lambda $ belongs to $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,h,0)$. If $\lambda _ j\downarrow 0$ and $v_{\lambda _ j}\to v$ in $L^1$, then the convergence holds in capacity, and $v$ belongs to the same envelope class and satisfies the equation above. Proof. By theorem 31.5.1 , applied with $\theta =h$, there are $c>0$ and $w\in \mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,h,0)$ with $\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(w)=cf\, \mathrm{d}V$. If $s\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,h)$ satisfies $\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(s)\geq af\, \mathrm{d}V$ with $a>0$, then \[  \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(w) \leq \frac ca\, \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(s).  \] Every $h$-plurisubharmonic $s$ satisfies $s\preceq 0$, so the scalar assertion of corollary 31.2.4 , with reference zero, gives $c/a\geq 1$. Taking the maximum over all subsolution coefficients $a$, theorem 14.27.2 yields $b_ h(f)\leq c$. The reverse inequality holds because $w$ itself is a subsolution with coefficient $c$. The same argument identifies the scalar of every solution in this envelope class with $b_ h(f)$. For $\lambda >0$, theorem 31.5.1 also gives a solution $s_\lambda $ of the exponential equation in the envelope class. Since $s_\lambda $ is in particular a subsolution, the greatest-solution property gives $s_\lambda \leq u_\lambda $. Upward stability (proposition 13.4.2 ) places $u_\lambda $ and its translate $v_\lambda $ in that class. Write $c_\lambda =\exp (\lambda \sup _ Xu_\lambda )$. By corollary 14.34.2 , $c_\lambda \to b_ h(f)>0$ and \[  \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_ h(v_\lambda ) =c_\lambda \mathrm{e}^{\lambda v_\lambda }f\, \mathrm{d}V \longrightarrow b_ h(f)f\, \mathrm{d}V \quad \text{in total variation}.  \] Since $v_\lambda \leq 0$ and $c_\lambda $ stays bounded for small $\lambda $, these measures are dominated by one finite non-pluripolar measure $C f\, \mathrm{d}V$. Applying theorem 31.3.3 to the given $L^1$-convergent sequence $v_{\lambda _ j}$, we obtain class membership, convergence in capacity and the equation for its limit. $\square$ By theorem 1.4.2 , every sequence $\lambda _ j\downarrow 0$ has a subsequence along which $v_{\lambda _ j}$ converges in $L^1$. The corollary identifies the equation of every such limit; the examples below show that this equation alone need not determine the normalized potential.

title: 31.7.1 Nonuniqueness in the minimal envelope class

section: 12.5 Relative equations under positive lower mass
text:
31.7.1 Nonuniqueness in the minimal envelope class In this subsection the manifold and the background are no longer fixed. The examples of 11.9.1 are smooth solutions on projective manifolds with nonclosed Hermitian backgrounds. Comparison with a Kähler form shows that these backgrounds have both positive lower mass and bounded mass, and smooth potentials belong to the minimal envelope class. Thus even both mass bounds together allow several normalized solutions with the same scalar. Corollary 31.7.2 . In every complex dimension $n\geq 3$, there are a projective manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, a smooth nonclosed Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$, and a nonzero finite non-pluripolar measure $
u $ on $X$ such that \[  0<v_-(\omega )\leq v_+(\omega )<+\infty ,  \] but the equation \[  \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\omega (u)=c
u , \qquad u\in \mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,\omega ,0), \qquad \sup _ Xu=0,  \] has at least two smooth solutions. The only positive constant for which it has a solution is $c=1$. Relative to a Kähler volume form on $X$, the measure $
u $ has a real analytic density, positive off two connected smooth real hypersurfaces and vanishing quadratically along them. Proof. Use the form and the two potentials of 11.9.1 . Since the manifold is projective, lemma 21.4.1 gives bounded mass. Fix a Kähler form $\Omega $ on $X$ and choose $\varepsilon >0$ with $\varepsilon \Omega \leq \omega $. Lower-volume monotonicity, theorem 30.1.1 , applied to the zero potential in both backgrounds, gives \[  v_-(\omega )\geq v_-(\varepsilon \Omega ) =\varepsilon ^ n\int _ X\Omega ^ n>0.  \] Here the potentials of the same ordinary type as zero are exactly the bounded ones, so these lower volumes are the infima defining $v_-$. The two smooth potentials belong to $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,\omega ,0)$ by proposition 13.4.2 , and their extended measures are the ordinary top powers. Their common measure $
u $ is finite and does not charge pluripolar sets. The construction gives $c=1$, and corollary 31.2.4 shows that no other positive scalar is possible. The density and its zero set were computed in 11.9.1 . $\square$

title: 32 Big backgrounds under bounded mass
text: 32 Big backgrounds under bounded mass Let $X$ be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$, let $\theta $ be a smooth big real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, not necessarily closed or semipositive, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. As in chapter 31 , we solve the equations $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}\mu $, $\lambda >0$, and $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=c\mu $, $c>0$, for an arbitrary nonzero finite non-pluripolar measure $\mu $, with $u$ in the relative class of $\varphi $. We replace the smaller-background model condition used there by upper and positive lower mass bounds. Throughout this chapter we make two standing assumptions. First, $X$ has the bounded mass property of definition 6.5.1 : $v_+(\omega )<+\infty $ for one, and hence every, Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$ (proposition 6.5.2 ). Second, $\varphi $ satisfies ( 30.10 ): it is an ordinary model, $P_\theta [\varphi ]=\varphi $ (definition 1.19.4 ), and its lower singularity volume is positive. Recall from definition 13.3.1 that the lower and upper volumes $\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (u)$ and $\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (u)$ are the infimum and the supremum of $\int _ X\mathrm{MA}_\theta (v)$ over all $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $v\sim u$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega $ for capacity and a smooth positive volume form $\mathrm{d}V$. The two assumptions give the two bounds needed for approximation: every member of the relative class of $\varphi $ has Monge–Ampère mass at least $\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi )>0$ and at most $\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi )<\infty $. With these bounds, first moments relative to a reference prevent collapse and keep limits in the relative class, while higher moments control convergence against a smoothed measure. This first gives solutions in the class of the potential $V_\theta $ with minimal singularities. To pass to the reference $\varphi $, we project a solution in the relative class of $V_\theta $ onto the relative class of $\varphi $. The projection keeps only part of the exponentially weighted measure, but weighted addition can fill any remaining deficit; maximizing the weighted mass therefore gives the required equation. The same contact estimates keep limits in the relative class when the model reference varies in the volume comparison of section 30.6 . For general finite non-pluripolar data the solutions lie in the relative full-mass class; for $L^ p$ densities, a stronger moment estimate shows that they differ from $\varphi $ by a bounded function. A positive exponent determines the solution uniquely; at exponent zero only the scalar is unique. For $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, write \[  \mathcal E_\varphi =\mathcal E_{\mathrm{vol}}(X,\theta ,\varphi ) =\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,\theta ,\varphi ), \qquad \theta _ a=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a,\qquad \mu _ a=\mathrm{MA}_\theta (a).  \] Here $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{vol}}(X,\theta ,\varphi )$ is the relative full-mass class of definition 30.2.3 , consisting of the $u\preceq \varphi $ with $\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (u)=\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi )$; $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,\theta ,\varphi )$ is the relative envelope class of definition 13.4.1 ; and the two classes coincide by theorem 30.2.4 . As in definition 1.12.1 , $u\preceq v$ means $u\leq v+C$ for a constant $C$, and $u\sim v$ means $u\preceq v\preceq u$. The measure $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (a)$ is the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure of theorem 6.1.2 ; it is finite by proposition 6.5.3 . Put \[  \ell =\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi )>0, \qquad M=\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi )<\infty .  \] By theorem 30.2.4 , every $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfies 32.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:big-relative-mass-interval} \ell \leq \mu _ u(X)\leq M. \end{equation} We use the stretching envelopes $Q_ b(u,w)=P_\theta (bu-(b-1)w)$ introduced before definition 13.4.1 , the rooftop envelopes $P_\theta (u_1,\ldots ,u_ N)=P_\theta (\min _ iu_ i)$, and $V_\theta =P_\theta (0)$ (section 1.19 ). For $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, proposition 13.4.5 gives $P_\theta [a]=\varphi $, and hence, as in ( 31.2 ), \[  a-\sup _ Xa\leq \varphi .  \] We refer to this inequality as the envelope identity. Finally, zero domination refers to theorem 30.3.1 with coefficient zero: if $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $v\preceq \varphi $ and $\mu _ u(\{ u<v\} )=0$, then $u\geq v$.
32.1 \begin{equation} \label{eq:big-relative-mass-interval} \ell \leq \mu _ u(X)\leq M. \end{equation}

title: 32.1 Equations for finite measures
text: 32.1 Equations for finite measures A positive exponent determines a unique solution in the relative class. At exponent zero, the equation determines its positive scalar, but normalized potentials may still differ, as in corollary 31.7.2 . Theorem 32.1.1 . For every nonzero finite non-pluripolar measure $\mu $ on $X$: There are $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and a unique $c>0$ such that $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=c\mu $. For each $\lambda >0$ there is a unique $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}\mu $. If $\mu =f\, \mathrm{d}V$ with $0\leq f\in L^ p(\mathrm{d}V)$ for some $p>1$, the solutions in both parts may be taken with $u\sim \varphi $. Part (1) is theorem 32.7.2 , part (2) is theorem 32.7.1 , and the assertion for $L^ p$ densities is corollary 32.8.3 . The standing assumptions also give $v_-(\omega )>0$. Indeed, choose $C>0$ with $\theta \leq C\omega $. Since $\varphi \preceq 0$, theorem 30.1.1 gives \[  0<\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\varphi ) \leq \underline{\operatorname {vol}}_{C\omega }(0) =C^ n v_-(\omega ).  \]

title: Theorem 32.1.1
text: Theorem 32.1.1 . For every nonzero finite non-pluripolar measure $\mu $ on $X$: There are $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and a unique $c>0$ such that $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=c\mu $. For each $\lambda >0$ there is a unique $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}\mu $. If $\mu =f\, \mathrm{d}V$ with $0\leq f\in L^ p(\mathrm{d}V)$ for some $p>1$, the solutions in both parts may be taken with $u\sim \varphi $.

The proof compares rooftop masses with the fixed measure of a potential of the same type as $w$ whose mass is close to the upper volume $M$. For a real number $t$, write $t_+=\max (t,0)$. Suppose $u_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $u_ j\leq w$, and \[  K:=\sup _ j\int _ X(w-u_ j)\, \mu _{u_ j}<+\infty .  \] Then $\sup _ Xu_ j$ is bounded below. If $u_ j	o u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ in $L^1(X)$, then $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. The same conclusions hold if $u_ j\leq w$ is replaced by a common upper bound $u_ j\leq \varphi +C$ and the integral is replaced by $\int _ X(w-u_ j)_+\, \mu _{u_ j}$. Proof. We first treat the case $u_ j\leq w$. Since $\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (w)=M$, we may choose $w'\sim w$ with $\mu _{w'}(X)>M-\ell /2$. Translate $w'$ so that $w'\leq w$, and put $p_ j=P_	heta (u_ j,w')$. These rooftops belong to $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Contact support and ordered contact imply 32.3  egin{equation} \label{eq:big-energy-roof-bound} \int _ X(w'-p_ j)\, \mu _{p_ j} \leq \int _ X(w-u_ j)\, \mu _{u_ j}\leq K. \end{equation} Indeed, the integrand vanishes on the contact part $\{ p_ j=w'\} $, and on the remaining contact part $p_ j=u_ j<w'\leq w$. We shall use the following estimate for maxima. If $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $a\leq w'$, and $t>0$, then 32.4  egin{equation} \label{eq:big-energy-max-bound} \mu _ a(\{ a>w'-t\} ) \leq \mu _{w'}(\{ a>w'-t\} )+M-\mu _{w'}(X). \end{equation} To see this, put $m=\max (a,w'-t)$. It has the ordinary singularity type of $w'$, so $\mu _ m(X)\leq M$. On $\{ a>w'-t\} $, locality gives $\mu _ m=\mu _ a$. On the complementary set, where $m=w'-t$, ordered contact gives $\mu _ m\geq \mu _{w'}$. Integrating over the two sets proves ( 32.4 ). Suppose that a subsequence had $\sup _ Xu_ j	o -\infty $; then also $\sup _ Xp_ j	o -\infty $. Splitting the mass of $p_ j$ at the level $w'-s$, $s>0$, and using ( 32.3 ) and ( 32.4 ), we obtain \[  \ell \leq \mu _{p_ j}(X) \leq  rac Ks+\mu _{w'}(\{ p_ j>w'-s\} )+M-\mu _{w'}(X).  \] For fixed $s$, the middle term tends to zero as $j	o \infty $, since $w'$ is finite off a pluripolar set and $\mu _{w'}$ is finite and non-pluripolar. Letting $j	o \infty $ and then $s	o \infty $ gives $\ell \leq M-\mu _{w'}(X)<\ell /2$, a contradiction. This proves the first assertion. Now suppose $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1$. Then $u\leq w\preceq \varphi $. Fix $b>1$ and suppose that $Q_ b(u,w)\equiv -\infty $. Since $w-w'$ is bounded, translating competitors by a constant shows that $Q_ b(u,w')\equiv -\infty $ as well. ot\equiv -\infty $. ot\equiv -\infty $ for every $b>1$. Consequently the decreasing sequence has a limit \[  p_ j=P_	heta \left(\inf _{k\geq j}u_ kight)  \] that is not identically $-\infty $, and the same proposition puts $p_ j$ in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The increasing sequence $p_ j$ has a regularized limit $p$, which belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by upward stability, since $p_1\leq p\leq u\preceq \varphi $. The inequality $p\leq u$ follows from the almost-everywhere convergence of the extracted sequence. Both $p_{j,N}\downarrow p_ j$ and $p_ j\uparrow p$ hold in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 , since $p_1
ot\equiv -\infty $ is a common lower bound. Apply lemma 6.3.1 to ( 32.5 ), with the bounded weights $\min (1,|p_{j,N}-u|)$ and then $\min (1,|p_ j-u|)$. title: Lemma 32.3.3
text: Lemma 32.3.3 . Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfy $u\sim V$ and $u\leq V$. Let $\chi :\mathbb R_{\leq 0}\to \mathbb R_{\leq 0}$ be increasing and concave, with $\chi (0)=0$ and $\chi '\geq 1$, and assume that $\chi $ is $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals. Set \[  b=V+\chi (u-V),\qquad p=P_\theta (b),  \] where the obstacle $b$ is defined off the pole set of $V$ and is set equal to $-\infty $ on that set. Then $p\sim V$ and \[  \mu _ p\leq \mathbf1_{\{ p=b\} }\chi '(u-V)^ n\mu _ u.  \] The measures and contact sets in this inequality may be restricted to the complement of the pole set of any fixed strict analytic barrier for $\theta $, that is, of any $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq a\omega $ for some $a>0$. Proof. The difference $u-V$ is bounded, so $V-C\leq b\leq u\leq V$ for some constant $C$. Hence $p\sim V$. The obstacle is quasi-continuous: away from sets of arbitrarily small capacity, $u$ and $V$ are finite and continuous, and their difference has a fixed bounded range. The general contact theorem theorem 14.7.4 therefore applies. Choose a strict analytic barrier $\rho $ and translate it so that $\rho \leq V$; put $\Omega =X\setminus \{ \rho =-\infty \} $. On this open set $u$, $V$ and $p$ are locally bounded. Let $\tau =\chi ^{-1}$; then $\tau $ is convex and $0<\tau '\leq 1$. By lemma 1.7.9 , the function \[  w=V+\tau (p-V)  \] is $\theta $-plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ and satisfies \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (w)\geq \tau '(p-V)^ n\mu _ p.  \] Since $p\leq w\leq V$ on $\Omega $, the removability lemma lemma 1.3.7 extends $w$ across the analytic set $X\setminus \Omega $, preserving its smooth lower curvature bound. The inequality $p\leq b$ implies $w\leq u$, with equality on $D=\{ p=b\} $. Ordered contact gives \[  \mathbf1_ D\tau '(p-V)^ n\mu _ p \leq \mathbf1_ D\mathrm{MA}_\theta (w) \leq \mathbf1_ D\mu _ u.  \] On $D$ the derivative $\tau '(p-V)$ equals $1/\chi '(u-V)$. Together with contact support for $p$, this proves the claim on $\Omega $. The analytic set $X\setminus \Omega $ is not charged by the non-pluripolar measures involved. $\square$

title: Corollary 32.4.3
text: Corollary 32.4.3 . Suppose that $X$ has the bounded mass property and $v_-(\omega )>0$. Then $\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (V_\theta )>0$ for every smooth big real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$; hence the preceding theorem applies to every such $\theta $. Proof. Choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _\rho \geq a\omega $ for some $a>0$. Then $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta -a\omega )$. Volume addition (proposition 30.1.2 ), followed by monotonicity in the singularities (theorem 30.1.1 ), gives \[  0<a^ n v_-(\omega ) =\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_{a\omega }(0) \leq \underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (\rho ) \leq \underline{\operatorname {vol}}_\theta (V_\theta ).  \] In the addition step the big background is $a\omega $, and the added positive current is $(\theta -a\omega )_\rho $. title: 32.5 Relative projection and supersolutions
text:
32.5 Relative projection and supersolutions To pass from the minimal class to the reference $\varphi $, we project a solution $z\in \mathcal E_ V$ onto $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The projection is the increasing limit $P_	heta [\varphi ](z)$ of the rooftops $P_	heta (\varphi +C,z)$ as $C	o \infty $, in the notation of lemma 30.3.3 . The small stretches of lemma 30.4.1 first show that the rooftop $P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $ and has the full upper volume of $\varphi $. Contact support then bounds the measure of the projection by the measure of $z$ on the set where the two coincide. The argument uses only that the reference of $z$ lies above $\varphi $, so we formulate it for an arbitrary ordinary model above $\varphi $; this will also allow the reference to vary. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ satisfy $P_	heta [\eta ]=\eta \geq \varphi $, and write $\mathcal E_\eta =\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,	heta ,\eta )$. Proposition 32.5.1 . For every $z\in \mathcal E_\eta $, the rooftop $P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Proof. First suppose $z\leq \eta $; recall also that $\varphi \leq \eta \leq 0$. For $b>1$ sufficiently close to one, lemma 30.4.1 gives \[  h_ b=Q_ b(\varphi ,\eta )\leq \varphi ,  \] which is not identically $-\infty $. Set $a=1-b^{-1}$. The stretching lemma lemma 13.4.3 , now applied in $\mathcal E_\eta $, gives $z_{1/a}=Q_{1/a}(z,\eta )\in \mathcal E_\eta $. The potential \[  k_ a=a z_{1/a}+(1-a)h_ b  \] lies below both $\varphi $ and $z$. Indeed, $z_{1/a}\leq \eta $ and $(1-a)h_ b+a\eta \leq \varphi $ give the first bound, while $h_ b\leq \eta $ and $a z_{1/a}+(1-a)\eta \leq z$ give the second. Thus $p=P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $. Volume addition and monotonicity give \[  (1-a)^ n\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (h_ b) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (k_ a) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (p) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\varphi ).  \] As $b\downarrow 1$, we have $a\downarrow 0$, and the first term tends to the last by lemma 30.4.1 . The upper volumes of $p$ and $\varphi $ are therefore equal. Since $p\leq \varphi $, theorem 30.2.4 gives $p\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. For general $z$, the envelope identity in $\mathcal E_\eta $ gives $z-\sup _ Xz\leq \eta $. Set $S=\max (\sup _ Xz,0)$. The preceding case gives $P_	heta (\varphi ,z-S)\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, and \[  P_	heta (\varphi ,z-S)\leq P_	heta (\varphi ,z)\leq \varphi .  \] Upward stability finishes the proof. $\square$ Proposition 32.5.2 . Let $z\in \mathcal E_\eta $ and let $Q=P_	heta [\varphi ](z)= igl (\lim _{C	o \infty }P_	heta (\varphi +C,z) igr )^*$ be its projection onto the relative class of $\varphi $. Then $Q\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $Q\leq z$, and \[  \mu _ Q\leq \mathbf1_{\{ Q=z\} }\mu _ z.  \] Proof. For $C\geq 0$ put $p_ C=P_	heta (\varphi +C,z)$. The preceding proposition gives $p_0\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Since $p_0\leq p_ C\preceq \varphi $, upward stability gives $p_ C\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. The envelope identity, together with $p_ C\leq z$, yields the uniform bound \[  p_ C\leq \varphi +\sup _ Xp_ C\leq \varphi +\sup _ Xz.  \] Consequently the increasing regularized limit $Q$ is not identically $-\infty $, belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ and is at most $z$. The monotone convergence holds in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 . Finally, lemma 30.3.3 , applied with $u=\varphi $ and $w=z$, gives 32.13  egin{equation} \label{eq:big-projection-contact-tail} \mu _ Q\leq \mathbf1_{\{ Q=z\} }\mu _ z. \end{equation} $\square$ Corollary 32.5.3 . u $, there is $Q\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that \[  0

title: 32.5.1 Varying model references
text:
32.5.1 Varying model references We now let the reference vary. Recall from definition 30.6.1 the comparison \[  d_	heta (u,v)=2\, \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\max (u,v)) -\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (u)-\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (v)  \] and, for $\delta >0$, the set $\mathcal M_\delta (	heta )$ of ordinary models $u=P_	heta [u]$ with $\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (u)\geq \delta $. For models $\varphi _ j	o \varphi $ in this comparison, theorem 30.7.3 provides increasing lower models whose upper volumes approach that of $\varphi $. Projecting finite families of potentials onto these lower models makes their rooftops comparable. To keep the limit in the relative class of $\varphi $, domination of the measures is needed only where the potentials lie below one fixed member of that class; domination on all of $X$ gives, in addition, convergence in capacity and convergence of the measures. Theorem 32.5.4 . Let $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathcal M_\delta (	heta )$ for some $\delta >0$, with $d_	heta (\varphi _ j,\varphi )	o 0$. Suppose $u_ j\in \mathcal E_{\varphi _ j}$, $u_ j	o u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ in $L^1(X)$, and $\chi \in \mathcal E_\varphi $. If one finite non-pluripolar measure $
u $ satisfies \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u_ j\leq \chi \} }\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u ,  \] then $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Moreover, after extraction and relabeling, the potentials \[  \psi _ j=P_	heta \left(\inf _{l\geq j}\varphi _ light),\qquad h_ j=P_	heta \left(\inf _{l\geq j}u_ light)  \] satisfy $\psi _ j\in \mathcal M_{\delta /2}(	heta )$ and $h_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$. If $\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u $ on $X$, the original sequence converges to $u$ in capacity and $\mu _{u_ j}ightharpoonup \mu _ u$. Proof. We first construct the lower models $\psi _ j$, then a common lower bound for rooftops of the $u_ l$ in the classes $\mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, and finally treat domination on all of $X$. By Hartogs' lemma, $u_ j$, $u$ and $\chi $ have a common upper bound; translate them to be nonpositive. The envelope identity then gives $u_ j\leq \varphi _ j$. Since $\varphi _ j	o \varphi $ in $L^1$ by proposition 30.6.3 , it follows that $u\leq \varphi $. Put $\Lambda =
u +\mu _\chi $. Using lemma 1.23.1 , extract a subsequence along which $u_ j	o u$ almost everywhere for smooth volume and \[  I_ j:=\int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{u_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mathrm{d}\Lambda \leq 2^{-j}.  \] Apply theorem 30.7.3 to extract further, keeping these estimates, and obtain increasing models $w_ j\leq \varphi _ j,\varphi $ with lower volume at least $\delta /2$ and $d_	heta (w_ j,\varphi )	o 0$. For $l\geq j$ we have $w_ j\leq w_ l\leq \varphi _ l$. Hence $\psi _ j$ is not identically $-\infty $, and \[  w_ j\leq \psi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] The upper bound follows by passing to the $L^1$ limit in $\psi _ j\leq \varphi _ l$ as $l	o \infty $. Monotonicity of the ordinary envelope gives $P_	heta [\psi _ j]\leq \varphi _ l$ for all $l\geq j$, so $\psi _ j$ is an ordinary model. It increases with $j$, has lower volume at least $\delta /2$, and 32.14  egin{equation} \label{eq:varying-reference-volume-limit} \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\psi _ j) \longrightarrow \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\varphi ). \end{equation} Set $g_ j=P_	heta [\psi _ j](\chi )$. Proposition 32.5.2 , with $(\varphi ,\eta )$ replaced by $(\psi _ j,\varphi )$, gives $g_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, $g_ j\leq \chi $ and $\mu _{g_ j}\leq \mu _\chi $. Moreover $g_ j$ increases with $j$. For $N\geq j$, consider \[  q_{j,N}=P_	heta (g_ j,u_ j,\ldots ,u_ N).  \] For each $l\geq j$, the projection $P_	heta [\psi _ j](u_ l)$ belongs to $\mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$ by the same proposition, now with upper reference $\varphi _ l$. The finite rooftop of these projections and $g_ j$ lies below $q_{j,N}$. Since $q_{j,N}\leq g_ j$, the finite-rooftop proposition and upward stability give $q_{j,N}\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, and hence $\mu _{q_{j,N}}(X)\geq \delta /2$. Partition the contact set of $q_{j,N}$ into disjoint pieces, one for each obstacle. On a piece where $q_{j,N}=u_ l$, we have $u_ l\leq g_ j\leq \chi $, so the hypothesis bounds the measure there by $
u $. On the piece where $q_{j,N}=g_ j$, the measure is bounded by $\mu _{g_ j}\leq \mu _\chi $. Consequently $\mu _{q_{j,N}}\leq \Lambda $. Put $F_ j=\min (\mathrm{e}^ u,\mathrm{e}^{g_ j})$. On the $u_ l$ piece, \[  |\mathrm{e}^{q_{j,N}}-F_ j|\leq |\mathrm{e}^{u_ l}-\mathrm{e}^ u|.  \] On the $g_ j$ piece, $g_ j=q_{j,N}\leq u_ N$, so the error is $(\mathrm{e}^{g_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u)_+\leq |\mathrm{e}^{u_ N}-\mathrm{e}^ u|$. u $ and $\mu _\chi $ of $\Lambda $, so together they contribute at most $I_ N$. title: 32.6 Weighted measure addition
text: 32.6 Weighted measure addition Given $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$, we look for $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v$. This weighted addition is used in section 32.7 to enlarge the weighted measure of a supersolution. The measure $\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda v}\mu _ v$ can have infinite mass, so we approximate the inputs while keeping a common lower bound in $\mathcal E_\varphi $ for the approximate solutions. This bound gives convergence in capacity, even when the approximate solutions have different ordinary types, and localizes the limiting equation away from deep sublevel sets. Exponentially weighted measures are defined off the pole sets and assigned zero mass there. Lemma 32.6.1 . Let $a_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ have a common upper bound and converge in $L^1(X)$ to $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $a\preceq \varphi $. Suppose there is $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that $h\leq a_ j$ for every $j$. If, for some $\lambda >0$, \[  \int _ X|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ j}\longrightarrow 0,  \] then $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $a_ j\to a$ in capacity. Proof. By lemma 1.3.3 , the lower bound passes to the limit, so $h\leq a\preceq \varphi $, and upward stability gives $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Start with any subsequence and extract a further one along which the integrals in the hypothesis are at most $2^{-j}$ and $a_ j\to a$ almost everywhere for smooth volume. The finite rooftops \[  p_{j,N}=P_\theta (a_ j,\ldots ,a_ N)  \] are not identically $-\infty $ because $h$ is a competitor. Partitioning their contact sets according to the first obstacle touched gives \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{p_{j,N}} \leq \sum _{k=j}^ N\int _ X|a_ k-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ k} \leq 2^{1-j}.  \] No relative-class assertion about these finite rooftops is needed. Their decreasing limits $p_ j=P_\theta (\inf _{k\geq j}a_ k)$ are at least $h$, and the almost-everywhere convergence gives $p_ j\leq a$. Hence the $p_ j$ and their increasing regularized limit $p$ lie in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The limits in $N$ and then in $j$ hold in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 , since $h$ is a common lower bound. Apply the weighted lower semicontinuity lemma 6.3.1 twice, to the bounded weights $\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}$ and their limits. These weights converge in capacity: discard deep sublevel sets of $h$ and $a$, and use continuity on the remaining finite ranges. We obtain \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _ p=0.  \] The exponential is positive off a pluripolar set, which $\mu _ p$ does not charge. Hence $\mu _ p(\{ p<a\} )=0$, and zero domination gives $p=a$. The upper envelopes $(\sup _{k\geq j}a_ k)^*$ decrease to $a$, and squeezing proves convergence in capacity along this subsequence. Since the initial subsequence was arbitrary, the convergence holds for the original sequence. $\square$ The next lemma treats exponent one; the general exponent in theorem 32.6.3 follows by rescaling the background and the potentials. Lemma 32.6.2 . Let $u,v,\sigma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be nonpositive, with $u,v\preceq \varphi $, and let $t_ j\uparrow \infty $. Each of the sequences $u_ j$, $v_ j$ is either constant, equal to $u$, respectively $v$, for every $j$, or given by the truncations \[  u_ j=\max (u,\sigma -t_ j),\qquad v_ j=\max (v,\sigma -t_ j).  \] Suppose that the Monge–Ampère masses of the $u_ j$ and $v_ j$ are uniformly bounded. Fix $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and let $a_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfy \[  \mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-u_ j}\mu _{u_ j}+\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-v_ j}\mu _{v_ j}, \qquad h\leq a_ j\leq \min (u_ j,v_ j).  \] If $a_ j\to a$ in $L^1(X)$, then $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, the convergence holds in capacity, and \[  a\leq \min (u,v),\qquad \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] The measure on the right is finite, even when $\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v$ has infinite total mass. Proof. Since $u_ j$ and $v_ j$ decrease to $u$ and $v$, the bounds give $h\leq a\leq \min (u,v)\preceq \varphi $, so $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. After discarding finitely many indices we may assume $t_ j\geq 0$, so all potentials $a_ j,a$ are nonpositive. Let $E_ j$ be the intersection of the sets $\{ u>\sigma -t_ j\} $ and $\{ v>\sigma -t_ j\} $, taken only for those inputs that are truncated; a constant sequence imposes no condition. On $E_ j$, locality gives $\mu _{u_ j}=\mu _ u$ and $\mu _{v_ j}=\mu _ v$. Since $a,a_ j\leq u_ j,v_ j$, we have \[  \mathrm{e}^ a\mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{(a+a_ j)/2}(\mu _{u_ j}+\mu _{v_ j}).  \] If $x\notin E_ j$, then one truncated input and its truncation are at most $-t_ j$ at $x$, so $a_ j(x),a(x)\leq -t_ j$. Moreover $|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^{(a+a_ j)/4}$ is bounded by an absolute constant, since $a_ j,a\leq 0$. Thus 32.16 \begin{equation} \label{eq:big-addition-weighted-error} \int _ X|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^ a\, \mu _{a_ j} \leq \int _ X|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^{(a+a_ j)/2}(\mu _ u+\mu _ v) +C \mathrm{e}^{-t_ j/2}. \end{equation} The assumed uniform mass bound is used only in the last term. The fixed measure $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$ is finite by bounded mass. Lemma 1.23.1 , applied to $\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}$ and $\mathrm{e}^ a$, shows that $a_ j\to a$ in measure for $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$, since $a$ is finite almost everywhere for this non-pluripolar measure. The integrand in the first term of ( 32.16 ) is uniformly bounded and tends to zero in measure, so its integral tends to zero. Lemma 32.6.1 now gives convergence in capacity. When a subsequence is taken, the corresponding truncation levels $t_ j$ are kept. To identify the equation, fix $T>0$ and choose a continuous nondecreasing function $g_ T:[-\infty ,0]\to [0,1]$ that vanishes on $[-\infty ,-2T]$ and equals one on $[-T,0]$, such that $g_ T\uparrow 1$ at finite points as $T\to \infty $. Put $\chi _ T=g_ T(h)$. Since $h\leq a\leq u,v$, both $u$ and $v$ exceed $-2T$ on $\{ \chi _ T>0\} $. Therefore, once $t_ j>2T$, every truncated input agrees there with its limit, and \[  \chi _ T\mu _{a_ j} =\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v).  \] Choose a Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $. On the left-hand side, replace $a_ j$ by $\max (a_ j,-2T)$, which does not change $\chi _ T\mu _{a_ j}$ because $\chi _ T$ vanishes where $a_ j\leq -2T$, and expand the bounded product as \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max (a_ j,-2T))^ n =\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nk (\Omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max (a_ j,-2T))^ k\wedge (\theta -\Omega )^{n-k}.  \] Bounded capacity continuity with the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\chi _ T$ therefore gives convergence to $\chi _ T\mu _ a$, after testing against a continuous function. The uncut product may be signed, but its terms have uniformly capacity-controlled total variations. On the right-hand side, $\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{-u}$ and $\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{-v}$ are bounded by $\mathrm{e}^{2T}$. Fixed-measure exponential convergence therefore gives convergence in total variation to $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^ a(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v)$. Let $T\to \infty $. The limiting right-hand side is at most $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$, because $a\leq u,v$. Both sides ignore the pole set of $h$, so the cutoff identities prove the global equation and the finiteness of its right-hand side. $\square$

title: 32.6.1 Ordinary types and bounded carriers
text:
32.6.1 Ordinary types and bounded carriers We first solve the weighted addition equation when one input has the ordinary type of $\varphi $, or a measure dominated by the Monge–Ampère measure of a bounded potential. In both cases first moments control the rooftops of the approximating solutions, and these rooftops give the common lower bound required by lemma 32.6.2 . title: 32.7.2 Arbitrary weighted sums
text: 32.7.2 Arbitrary weighted sums With existence for general measures available, weighted addition extends to arbitrary $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Truncating the exponential weights gives finite data, which theorem 32.7.1 solves. A first-moment estimate prevents collapse of these solutions, and a rooftop involving their limit localizes the equation before the limit can be compared with the inputs. Theorem 32.7.4 . For every $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$, there is a unique $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfying \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v.  \] Moreover $a\leq \min (u,v)$ and $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Proof. By the scaling used in theorem 32.6.3 , it suffices to take $\lambda =1$. For positive integers $j$, let \[  \tau _ j=\mathrm{e}^{-\max (u,-j)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\max (v,-j)}\mu _ v.  \] These are nonzero finite non-pluripolar measures, and they increase with $j$. Only the weights are truncated; the functions $\max (u,-j)$ and $\max (v,-j)$ need not be $\theta $-plurisubharmonic. Theorem 32.7.1 gives $a_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}\tau _ j$. Since $\tau _ j$ increases, exponential order implies that $a_ j$ decreases. Set $r=P_\theta (u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. On $\{ a_ j<r\} $, one has $r\leq u,v$ and \[  (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-\max (u,-j)}\leq (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-r}\leq \mathrm{e}^{-1},  \] with the same inequality for $v$. Consequently \[  \int _ X(r-a_ j)_+\, \mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{-1}\bigl (\mu _ u(X)+\mu _ v(X)\bigr ).  \] Also $a_ j\leq a_1\leq \varphi +\sup _ Xa_1$. The one-sided first-moment criterion of proposition 32.3.1 , with fixed reference $r$, bounds $\sup _ Xa_ j$ from below. Thus the decreasing sequence has an $L^1$ limit $a\not\equiv -\infty $, and the same criterion puts $a$ in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. We identify the equation before comparing $a$ with the inputs. The rooftop \[  q=P_\theta (a,u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi  \] lies below $a_ j$, $a$, $u$ and $v$. For $T>0$, let $\chi _ T=g_ T(q)$, with $g_ T$ as in the proof of lemma 32.6.2 : a continuous nondecreasing cutoff that vanishes where $q\leq -2T$, equals one where $q\geq -T$, and increases to one off the pole set of $q$ as $T\to \infty $. On $\{ \chi _ T>0\} $ both inputs exceed $-2T$. Hence, for $j>2T$, 32.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:unrestricted-addition-cutoff} \chi _ T\mu _{a_ j} =\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{a_ j}(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v). \end{equation} The factors $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-u}$ and $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-v}$ are bounded by $\mathrm{e}^{2T}$. Since $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $a_ j\leq \sup _ Xa_1$, dominated convergence against the fixed measure $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$ gives convergence in total variation of the right-hand sides to the corresponding expression with $a$. For the left-hand side, $a_ j\to a$ in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 . Choose a Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $, and replace $a_ j$ by $b_ j=\max (a_ j,-2T)$ before forming bounded products. The $b_ j$ are uniformly bounded $\Omega $-plurisubharmonic functions converging in capacity. The expansion \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ n =\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nk(\Omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ k \wedge (\theta -\Omega )^{n-k}  \] and bounded capacity continuity apply against the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\chi _ T$. Where $\chi _ T\ne 0$ no potential is truncated, so locality gives convergence to $\chi _ T\mu _ a$. In this way the possibly signed bounded product is handled before the cutoff is inserted. Thus ( 32.21 ) holds in the limit. Let $T\to \infty $. Both sides ignore the poles of $q$, so monotone convergence gives \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] Since $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, this also shows that the weighted right-hand side is finite. For $\varepsilon >0$, the equation implies \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ u \leq \mathrm{e}^{-\varepsilon }\mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ a.  \] Strict domination, theorem 30.3.1 , gives $u\geq a-\varepsilon $, and letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ gives $u\geq a$. Similarly $v\geq a$, so $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Two solutions have the same exponentially weighted measure, so corollary 30.3.2 , applied in both directions, gives uniqueness. $\square$ Corollary 32.7.5 . For fixed $\lambda >0$, write $u\star _\lambda v$ for the solution $a$ in the theorem. This operation on $\mathcal E_\varphi $ is commutative and associative, and, for $c\in \mathbb R$, \[  (u+c)\star _\lambda (v+c)=(u\star _\lambda v)+c, \qquad u\star _\lambda u=u-\lambda ^{-1}\log 2.  \] Proof. Put $F_\lambda (u)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda u}\mu _ u$, with zero mass on the poles. The theorem says that $F_\lambda (u\star _\lambda v)=F_\lambda (u)+F_\lambda (v)$. By corollary 30.3.2 , the map $F_\lambda $ is injective on $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Commutativity and associativity therefore follow from those of addition of positive measures, including measures of infinite total mass. Finally, $F_\lambda (u+c)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda c}F_\lambda (u)$, which together with injectivity gives both identities. $\square$

title: Theorem 32.7.4
text: Theorem 32.7.4 . For every $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$, there is a unique $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfying \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v.  \] Moreover $a\leq \min (u,v)$ and $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Proof. By the scaling used in theorem 32.6.3 , it suffices to take $\lambda =1$. For positive integers $j$, let \[  \tau _ j=\mathrm{e}^{-\max (u,-j)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\max (v,-j)}\mu _ v.  \] These are nonzero finite non-pluripolar measures, and they increase with $j$. Only the weights are truncated; the functions $\max (u,-j)$ and $\max (v,-j)$ need not be $\theta $-plurisubharmonic. Theorem 32.7.1 gives $a_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}\tau _ j$. Since $\tau _ j$ increases, exponential order implies that $a_ j$ decreases. Set $r=P_\theta (u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. On $\{ a_ j<r\} $, one has $r\leq u,v$ and \[  (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-\max (u,-j)}\leq (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-r}\leq \mathrm{e}^{-1},  \] with the same inequality for $v$. Consequently \[  \int _ X(r-a_ j)_+\, \mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{-1}\bigl (\mu _ u(X)+\mu _ v(X)\bigr ).  \] Also $a_ j\leq a_1\leq \varphi +\sup _ Xa_1$. The one-sided first-moment criterion of proposition 32.3.1 , with fixed reference $r$, bounds $\sup _ Xa_ j$ from below. Thus the decreasing sequence has an $L^1$ limit $a\not\equiv -\infty $, and the same criterion puts $a$ in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. We identify the equation before comparing $a$ with the inputs. The rooftop \[  q=P_\theta (a,u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi  \] lies below $a_ j$, $a$, $u$ and $v$. For $T>0$, let $\chi _ T=g_ T(q)$, with $g_ T$ as in the proof of lemma 32.6.2 : a continuous nondecreasing cutoff that vanishes where $q\leq -2T$, equals one where $q\geq -T$, and increases to one off the pole set of $q$ as $T\to \infty $. On $\{ \chi _ T>0\} $ both inputs exceed $-2T$. Hence, for $j>2T$, 32.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:unrestricted-addition-cutoff} \chi _ T\mu _{a_ j} =\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{a_ j}(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v). \end{equation} The factors $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-u}$ and $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-v}$ are bounded by $\mathrm{e}^{2T}$. Since $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $a_ j\leq \sup _ Xa_1$, dominated convergence against the fixed measure $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$ gives convergence in total variation of the right-hand sides to the corresponding expression with $a$. For the left-hand side, $a_ j\to a$ in capacity by lemma 1.8.12 . Choose a Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $, and replace $a_ j$ by $b_ j=\max (a_ j,-2T)$ before forming bounded products. The $b_ j$ are uniformly bounded $\Omega $-plurisubharmonic functions converging in capacity. The expansion \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ n =\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nk(\Omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ k \wedge (\theta -\Omega )^{n-k}  \] and bounded capacity continuity apply against the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\chi _ T$. Where $\chi _ T\ne 0$ no potential is truncated, so locality gives convergence to $\chi _ T\mu _ a$. In this way the possibly signed bounded product is handled before the cutoff is inserted. Thus ( 32.21 ) holds in the limit. Let $T\to \infty $. Both sides ignore the poles of $q$, so monotone convergence gives \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] Since $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, this also shows that the weighted right-hand side is finite. For $\varepsilon >0$, the equation implies \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ u \leq \mathrm{e}^{-\varepsilon }\mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ a.  \] Strict domination, theorem 30.3.1 , gives $u\geq a-\varepsilon $, and letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ gives $u\geq a$. Similarly $v\geq a$, so $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Two solutions have the same exponentially weighted measure, so corollary 30.3.2 , applied in both directions, gives uniqueness. $\square$
32.21 \begin{equation} \label{eq:unrestricted-addition-cutoff} \chi _ T\mu _{a_ j} =\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{a_ j}(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v). \end{equation}

title: Corollary 32.7.5
text: Corollary 32.7.5 . For fixed $\lambda >0$, write $u\star _\lambda v$ for the solution $a$ in the theorem. This operation on $\mathcal E_\varphi $ is commutative and associative, and, for $c\in \mathbb R$, \[  (u+c)\star _\lambda (v+c)=(u\star _\lambda v)+c, \qquad u\star _\lambda u=u-\lambda ^{-1}\log 2.  \] Proof. Put $F_\lambda (u)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda u}\mu _ u$, with zero mass on the poles. The theorem says that $F_\lambda (u\star _\lambda v)=F_\lambda (u)+F_\lambda (v)$. By corollary 30.3.2 , the map $F_\lambda $ is injective on $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Commutativity and associativity therefore follow from those of addition of positive measures, including measures of infinite total mass. Finally, $F_\lambda (u+c)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda c}F_\lambda (u)$, which together with injectivity gives both identities. $\square$

title: 32.8 Relative boundedness for  data
text: 32.8 Relative boundedness for $L^ p$ data If the datum has finite moments of sufficiently high order against normalized $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions, every normalized $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ whose measure is dominated by the datum differs from $\varphi $ by a bounded function. We work directly with $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $: truncating $u$ against $\varphi -j$ would introduce a contact measure that need not be controlled by the datum. Envelopes with concave obstacles, as in lemma 32.3.3 , keep this domination and give a differential inequality for the distribution of $\varphi -u$. Lemma 32.8.1 . Let $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $u\leq \varphi $, and let $\chi :\mathbb R_{\leq 0}\to \mathbb R_{\leq 0}$ be increasing and concave, with $\chi (0)=0$. Suppose that $\chi $ is $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals and that, for a finite constant $L\geq 1$, \[  1\leq \chi '\leq L.  \] Then the envelope \[  p=P_\theta (\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi ))  \] belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $, and \[  \mu _ p\leq \mathbf1_{\{ p=\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )\} } \chi '(u-\varphi )^ n\mu _ u.  \] Here the obstacle and the contact set are defined off the pluripolar set where $u-\varphi $ is undefined, which all these measures ignore. Proof. For $t\leq 0$, the bounds on $\chi '$ give $Lt\leq \chi (t)\leq t$. Thus \[  Q_ L(u,\varphi )\leq p\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] The lower potential belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by lemma 13.4.3 , so $p$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by upward stability. The obstacle is finite and quasi-continuous off the poles, so the contact theorem theorem 14.7.4 applies. Let $\tau =\chi ^{-1}$. It is convex, with $L^{-1}\leq \tau '\leq 1$. We justify the transformation \[  w=\varphi +\tau (p-\varphi )  \] without assuming that $\varphi $ is locally bounded on some open set. On a coordinate ball choose a smooth function $q$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. The functions \[  p_ m=\max (p,q-m),\qquad \varphi _ m=\max (\varphi ,q-m)  \] are locally bounded $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions on the ball, and $p_ m\leq \varphi _ m$. Lemma 1.7.9 applies to $w_ m=\varphi _ m+\tau (p_ m-\varphi _ m)$ and gives \[  \theta _{w_ m}\geq 0,\qquad \mu _{w_ m}\geq \tau '(p_ m-\varphi _ m)^ n\mu _{p_ m}.  \] The function $(s,t)\mapsto t+\tau (s-t)$ on $\{ s\leq t\} $ is nondecreasing in each variable. Consequently $w_ m$ decreases as $m$ increases. Since $p\leq p_ m\leq w_ m\leq \varphi _ m$, the limit is not identically $-\infty $ on the ball. Off the poles it equals $w$. The local limits therefore agree on overlaps after regularization and define a global $\theta $-plurisubharmonic function. On $D_ m=\{ p>q-m\} $, neither $p$ nor $\varphi $ is truncated. Thus $w_ m=w$ there, and plurifine locality transfers the product inequality to $D_ m$. These sets exhaust the complement of the poles of $p$ in the ball. Since all products ignore the discarded pluripolar set, \[  \mu _ w\geq \tau '(p-\varphi )^ n\mu _ p.  \] The obstacle bound $p\leq \varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )$ gives $w\leq u$, with equality on the contact set of $p$. Ordered contact, the identity $\tau '(p-\varphi )=1/\chi '(u-\varphi )$ on that set, and contact support of $\mu _ p$ prove the assertion. $\square$ Proposition 32.8.2 . Let $\mu $ be a finite non-pluripolar measure. Suppose that, for some real $m>2n+1$, \[  A_ m:=\sup _{\substack {v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\\ \sup _ Xv=0}} \int _ X(-v)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu <\infty .  \] There is a finite constant $C$, depending only on $n,\ell ,M,m,\mu (X)$ and $A_ m$, such that every $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\sup _ Xu=0$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ satisfies \[  \varphi -C\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] Proof. As in proposition 32.3.4 , we build a concave weight from the distribution of $\varphi -u$ and apply the preceding lemma. The moment bound on $\mu $ now yields a differential inequality for this weight, which bounds the depth of $\varphi -u$ under $\mu _ u$. The envelope identity gives $u\leq \varphi \leq 0$. Put $x=\varphi -u$, defined off the poles, and $N=2n+1$. Since $x\leq -u$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $, Hölder's inequality gives the uniform first-moment bound \[  B:=\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u \leq \int _ X(-u)\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq \mu (X)^{1-1/m}A_ m^{1/m}=:A_1.  \] Let $H(t)=\mu _ u(\{ x>t\} )$ and $T=\sup \{ t\geq 0:H(t)>0\} $, with $T=0$ if this set is empty; at this point $T$ may be infinite. If $T<\infty $, zero domination applied to $u$ and $\varphi -t$ for $t>T$ gives $u\geq \varphi -T$. It is therefore enough to bound $T$. We may assume $T>1$, and we choose any $S$ with $1<S<T$. Define, for $t\geq 0$, \[  g(t)= \begin{cases}  ((1+t)^{3/2}H(t))^{-1},& 0\leq t\leq S,\\  (1+t)^{-3/2},& t>S, \end{cases} \qquad F(t)=1+\int _0^ t g(s)\, \mathrm{d}s,  \] and set $W(t)=\int _0^ t F(s)^{1/N}\, \mathrm{d}s$ and $\chi (-t)=-W(t)$. Since $H(S)>0$, $F$ is bounded on the whole half-line, although its bound may depend on $S$ and $u$. It is locally Lipschitz and nondecreasing. Hence $\chi $ has bounded derivative, is increasing and concave, and satisfies the hypotheses of the preceding lemma. Also $W(t)\geq t$ and $W(t)\leq tF(t)^{1/N}$. Since $H(t)\leq M$, Tonelli's theorem gives a bound independent of $S$ and $u$: \[  \int _ X F(x)\, \mu _ u =\mu _ u(X)+\int _0^\infty g(t)H(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \leq 3\max (1,M)=:K.  \] Let $p=P_\theta (\varphi -W(x))\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, the envelope of the preceding lemma for this $\chi $. On its contact set the lemma bounds its measure by $F(x)^{n/N}\mu _ u$. Hence, using $N=2n+1$ and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, \[  \begin{split}  \int _ X(\varphi -p)^{1/2}\, \mu _ p & \leq \int _ X x^{1/2}F(x)^{(n+1/2)/N}\, \mu _ u\\ & \leq \left(\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \left(\int _ XF(x)\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \leq \sqrt{KB}. \end{split}  \] The identity $P_\theta [p]=\varphi $ implies $p-\sup _ Xp\leq \varphi $. Since $p\leq \varphi \leq 0$ and $\mu _ p(X)\geq \ell $, the last integral is at least $\ell \sqrt{-\sup _ Xp}$. Consequently \[  0\leq -\sup _ Xp\leq KA_1/\ell ^2=:D.  \] Using $W(x)\leq \varphi -p\leq -p$, and applying the moment hypothesis to $p-\sup _ Xp$, we obtain 32.26 \begin{equation} \label{eq:big-model-weight-moment} \int _ XW(x)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq 2^{m-1}\bigl (A_ m+D^ m\mu (X)\bigr )<C_0, \end{equation} where we choose $C_0=1+2^{m-1}(A_ m+D^ m\mu (X))$. This constant is independent of $S$ and $u$. For $0<t\leq S$, Chebyshev's inequality and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ give \[  H(t)\leq C_0W(t)^{-m}, \qquad F'(t)\geq \frac{W(t)^ m}{C_0(1+t)^{3/2}} \quad \text{for almost every }t.  \] Since $W'=F^{1/N}$, the derivative of $(W')^{N+1}$ is at least \[  \frac{N+1}{NC_0}\,  \frac{W^ mW'}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] All functions being differentiated are absolutely continuous on compact intervals. Integrating from $0$ to $t$ and using $W(0)=0$ gives \[  (W'(t))^{N+1} \geq \frac{N+1}{NC_0(m+1)} \frac{W(t)^{m+1}}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] In particular \[  W'(t)\geq c_0(1+t)^{-\gamma }W(t)^\kappa , \quad \gamma =\frac{3}{2(N+1)}<1,\quad \kappa =\frac{m+1}{N+1}>1,  \] with $c_0>0$ independent of $S$ and $u$. Integrating the derivative of $W^{1-\kappa }$ over $[1,S]$ yields \[  (\kappa -1)c_0\int _1^ S(1+t)^{-\gamma }\, \mathrm{d}t \leq W(1)^{1-\kappa }-W(S)^{1-\kappa }\leq 1,  \] because $W(1)\geq 1$. Since the integral on the left diverges as $S\to \infty $, every $S<T$ is bounded by a constant independent of $S$ and $u$, and hence so is $T$. The zero-domination argument at the beginning of the proof now gives $u\geq \varphi -C$. The case $T\leq 1$, which includes $B=0$, was covered there as well. $\square$ Corollary 32.8.3 . Let $0\leq f\in L^ p(X,\mathrm{d}V)$, with $p>1$ and $\int _ Xf\, \mathrm{d}V>0$. For $\lambda >0$, the solution in theorem 32.7.1 of \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}f\, \mathrm{d}V  \] satisfies $u\sim \varphi $. Every normalized solution in $\mathcal E_\varphi $ of \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=cf\, \mathrm{d}V,\qquad c>0,  \] also satisfies $u\sim \varphi $. In particular, both existence statements hold in the ordinary singularity type of $\varphi $. Proof. Lemma 1.5.1 , applied in a Hermitian background dominating $\theta $, gives uniform moments of every finite order against $\mathrm{d}V$ for normalized $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions. Hölder's inequality therefore implies, for every finite $m$, \[  \sup _{\substack {v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\\ \sup _ Xv=0}} \int _ X(-v)^ m f\, \mathrm{d}V<\infty .  \] Choose $m>2n+1$. For the solution of the exponential equation, set $S=\sup _ Xu$ and $v=u-S$. Then $v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $\sup _ Xv=0$, and \[  \mu _ v=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}f\, \mathrm{d}V \leq \mathrm{e}^{\lambda S}f\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] The preceding proposition, applied to this fixed dominating measure, shows that $v$, and hence $u$, has the ordinary type of $\varphi $. For the normalized equation, apply the proposition to the measure $cf\, \mathrm{d}V$. $\square$
